# 02b. Theory campaign history: every result, conjecture, counterexample and refutation, campaign start to method meeting

Archive document 02b (part "B" of the theory documentation). Source thread: T3 thread "New BVS Headquarters" (`5e38497d-7dfd-48f9-88e9-b21895922f58`), 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-04. Scope: transcript positions about 88 to 1110, that is, from the start of the theory campaign (credits, Wave 1) to the method decision that preceded the method meeting. The final v3.1 method and the final paper-1 list (cards M1 to M8 and the supplement cards, archive IDs TH01 to TH20, CJ01 to CJ27, DR, LIM) are documented elsewhere (part "A"). This part uses only the ID blocks TH101+, LM101+, CJ101+, RF101+, CE101+.

Nothing in this document is adopted. Every "PROVED" is the author's status word; the exact status words and the checkers (same-family Claude verifier "SF", cross-family Astra reviewer "XF", Lean) are recorded per item. Statuses are copied, never upgraded.

## 0. How to read this document

### 0.1 ID prefixes

| Prefix | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| TH | theorem, proposition or corollary (proved, or proved under named inputs, or "PROVED (candidate)"; includes pre-campaign PROVED-LOCKED theorems) | status word per item |
| LM | lemma (including implementation and bookkeeping lemmas) | |
| CJ | conjecture, hypothesis, named condition, open problem, proposed target | pre-campaign conjectures T05, T24, T26 ... and hypotheses H24, EXP', PW2 ... live here |
| RF | a claim shown FALSE, refuted or retired (the claim itself, quoted, with the refutation and the replacement) | |
| CE | a counterexample (the concrete construction or numbers) | cross-referenced from RF entries |

Every ID is followed in the text by the native name(s), for example `TH265 (Theorem A)`. The authoritative lookup table is `ID_REGISTRY.md (part B)` (one row per ID, plus an alias index mapping every native label used in the sources to an ID).
Native labels in the sources collide (W8-SYNTH section 4.15: "Theorem A/B/C", "Lemma S", "Lemma M", "Prop M", "Lemma U", "Lemma 0", "CE1", "W'", "Theorem W", "(e')"); the archive IDs resolve the collisions. A `⟦name⟧` that could not be resolved is printed as `name [unresolved cross-reference]`.

### 0.3 Status vocabulary (campaign PROTOCOL.md, `campaign/PROTOCOL.md`)

<!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 1.000) from `campaign/PROTOCOL.md`; that file is authoritative -->
> Honest status words only. Use exactly these: PROVED (a complete proof you checked line by line), PROOF SKETCH (the crux is identified and the steps are plausible, but not every step is verified), COUNTEREXAMPLE (with a reproducible script or explicit construction), CONJECTURE, and OPEN. Never upgrade a status. A proof here is a **candidate**: it is not reviewed and not adopted. Review happens later, by other model families.

Other words used by the sources (THEORY.md section 0, REGISTRY_v2 header):
- PROVED-LOCKED: a row of `Docs/Theory/proofs/LOCKED_PROOFS.md`, statement and proof frozen by hash, always "not adopted" (Felipe's adoption decision never taken).
- CONDITIONAL: a locked theorem whose hypotheses (H24, PW2, EXP', VIS, NL_eta, NL_avg, H2, H3, BASIN, COVER, exposure/occurrence conditions) are assumed, not proved.
- PARTLY PROVED: only named parts locked.
- PROVED-UNDER: "PROVED given/under named inputs" (REGISTRY_v2 author-status class).
- REFEREE: a repair or counterexample supplied by a cross-family referee without a PROVED label.
- SF ("same-family"): a Claude run (Opus or Fable) checked a Claude run. XF ("cross-family"): an Astra review (A-REV1 to A-REV9, run on Codex/OpenAI). Verdict tags: VERIFIED, VERIFIED* (verified after a repair or with a stated qualification), GAP, ERROR. A re-review never raises an earlier adverse code on the original text; repaired texts carry the re-review verdict (REGISTRY_v2 header).
- Repairs: `[APPLIED]` (a campaign run has written the fix) / `[PENDING]`. W6-FIXREV1 and W6-FIXREV2 repairs are same-family and were later re-reviewed by A-REV5 (and A-REV6 to A-REV9 for later repairs).

- `T38-RECORD/REGISTRY_v2.md` (431 named results, 49 flagged sub-claims, 26 conflicts) and `T38-RECORD/LOCKABLE_v2.md` (55 strict lockable candidates). Source of statuses and SF/XF verdicts.
- `W8-SYNTH/SYNTHESIS.md` (snapshot of 2026-11-02 20:15-20:40 UTC; it predates A-REV5 to A-REV9 and the API wave; its own caveats are noted where they matter) and `campaign/LEDGER.md`.
- Each branch's REPORT.md / PROOF.md / STATEMENTS for the exact statements; `MEET-THM/REGISTRY_PAPER1.md` for the final-card mapping ("feeds").

# PART I. THEMES

## Theme 0: PRE — the pre-campaign theory set (T01-T39), hypotheses and selection records as they stood at campaign start

Summary: This theme records what the theory looked like on 2026-11-02, when the HQ thread ("New BVS Headquarters") started the campaign, and the pre-campaign claims that the campaign later refuted or corrected. Everything below is taken verbatim from the main-branch documentation of commit `c4ef0dc` ("Transfer", 1,283 files, pushed to GitHub at [pos 263]), snapshot `branch_snapshots/main@c4ef0dc/Docs/`: `THEORY.md` (master table and sections 0-5), `THEORY_PRIORITIES.md`, `Theory/one_pagers/T01..T39.md`, `Theory/proofs/LOCKED_PROOFS.md` and the per-theorem `STATEMENT.md` files, `Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md` (assumption inventory) and `Theory/theorems/Txx_*.md`, `Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/` (PROPOSAL, FABLE_REVIEW, ASTRA_REVIEW, FROZEN_LIST, `new_conjectures/T37..T39`), `Theory/DROPPED.md`, `Theory/FAILED_ATTEMPTS.md` and `History/selection_campaign_2026-10-13/FAILED_ATTEMPTS.md`, plus `campaign/HQ/SR_AUDIT.md` and the E-SPINE amendments (PR #1).

Status at campaign start (THEORY.md sections 0 and 2, verbatim figures): of T01-T36, 12 are proved in all parts (T01, T02, T03, T04, T06, T07, T09, T10, T12, T13, T15, T21), 8 partly proved (T11, T14, T20, T22, T23, T31 core; T25, T27 secondary), 16 not proved; T37, T38, T39 are new conjectures (not proved); 19 register rows give 21 theorem entries; nothing is adopted ('adoption is Felipe's decision', never answered). The statuses used are PROVED-LOCKED, CONDITIONAL, PARTLY PROVED, CONJECTURED (not proved), DROPPED (two senses: dropped from the paper selection vs dropped as a conjecture).

Timeline (positions): the HQ thread first reviewed the transferred repo at [pos 119] (it lists the open hypotheses H24, EXP', PW2, BASIN, H2/H3 as the likely campaign targets); at [pos 150], [pos 156] and [pos 178] it learned of T37-T39, of the frozen paper targets and of the p >> n data showing that the literal T37 fails; Felipe gave the go-ahead at [pos 180]; the campaign protocol and task files were written at [pos 190]-[pos 197]; Wave 1 (five Opus 5.5 routine runs: W1-T37R, W1-T24G, W1-T38E, W1-T03R, W1-EXP) was queued at [pos 233]-[pos 238] for 16:01-16:05 UTC on 2026-11-02 (the first, W1-T24G, pushed at about 16:20 UTC [pos 263]; the others started 16:56-17:01 UTC [pos 286]) and reported at [pos 296], [pos 327], [pos 342], [pos 355]; the Wave-1 results on the pre-campaign hypotheses (H24 false, T03 restated, the T02 sharper cutoff impossible) were reported at [pos 342] and [pos 355] and independently checked at [pos 370]. The 'tempering is needed' spine claim was refuted by W7-SEP and corrected through the E-SPINE pull request ([pos 796], [pos 800], [pos 805], [pos 807], [pos 850]). The pre-campaign set is the baseline against which all later themes state their results.

How this theme is organised: Part A = the 20 locked or partly proved T-items (TH101-TH120); Part B = the 16 unproved conjectures T05..T36 (CJ101-CJ116); Part C = the three new conjectures T37-T39 as written on 2026-10-28 (CJ117-CJ119); Part D = hypotheses and named conditions (CJ120-CJ130); Part E = pre-campaign claims later refuted or corrected (RF101-RF120); Part F = counterexamples named before the campaign (CE101-CE110); Appendix = the FROZEN_LIST / PROPOSAL / FABLE_REVIEW / ASTRA_REVIEW selection records, the E-SPINE amendments, the recorded-but-not-ID'd returnable ideas. LM101-LM130 are unused (no lemma-level result is registered separately; T-items with paper role 'Supplement lemma' are kept as TH because the brief locks T-items as TH or CJ). Convention: every 'Statement (verbatim)' block is copied by a script from the cited file; one-pager statements are the one-pagers' own 'Faithful condensation' of the STATEMENT.md files, which remain authoritative; where the STATEMENT.md was needed for exactness (T01, T02, T21, T22(iii), T23, T27(i), T25(iv), hypotheses) an excerpt is quoted as well. Names in doubled brackets are cross-theme references to be resolved by the lead.

### TH101 — T01 — Contrast reduction and mixed-rate transfer (old label A0 = T1)  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/STATEMENT.md`, `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/PROOF_v3.tex`; condensation used here: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T01.md` (the STATEMENT.md is authoritative; the one-pager says 'Faithful condensation'); positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]
- Status at campaign start (verbatim, one-pager line 2):
  > PROVED-LOCKED (all parts, wave 3); not adopted (adoption is Felipe's decision)  | Rank: core (lemma) | Paper role: Supplement lemma (of Thm 1)
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T01 | Contrast reduction and mixed-rate transfer (A0 = T1) | core | PROVED-LOCKED (all parts; wave 3) | Supplement lemma (of Thm 1) | `proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/` | G, R (regime); external review queued |
- Statement (verbatim, one-pager 'Statement' section):
  > Source: proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/STATEMENT.md section 2 (T01); theorems/T01_A0_contrast_reduction.md (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
  > - (i) Identity (every valid input, deterministic): the v3 joint posterior of (S, theta_S, v) = (S, s_y beta_S, s_y^2 sigma^2) equals the contrast-model posterior at inverse-gamma rate b = b0 s_y^2, and m(S) = c_n(s_y) m^c_{b0 s_y^2}(S) with c_n(s) = s^(n-1) Gamma(0.51)/(sqrt(2 pi b0) Gamma(0.01)). Hence BF(S), pi(S) and Z are the contrast-model quantities at that rate; z^c_S = s_y z_S and Q^c_S = s_y^2 Q_S; and v | S, y ~ IG(nu, b0 s_y^2 + Q^c_S/2), theta_S | v, S, y ~ N_k(n H_S^-1 z^c_S, n v H_S^-1).
  > - (ii) Envelope (deterministic): for 0 < b1 <= b <= b2 and kappa12 = (b2/b1)^0.51, kappa12^-1 m^c_{b2}(S) <= m^c_b(S) <= kappa12 m^c_{b1}(S) for every S and every y_c; for every event E, kappa12^-1 I_{b2}(E) <= I_b(E) <= kappa12 I_{b1}(E), so Pi_b(E) <= kappa12^2 I_{b1}(E)/Z^c_{b2}.
  > - (iii) Scale event, under G and R: s_y^2 - (sigma*^2 + ||mu||^2/(n-1)) = O_P(n^-1/2), P0(B_n) -> 1 for B_n = {sigma*^2/2 <= s_y^2 <= 2(sigma*^2+M)+1}; and eps_c = U^T eps ~ N_{n-1}(0, sigma*^2 I) exactly, y_c = X_c theta* + eps_c.
  > - (iv) Rate derivative: d/db log[m^c_b(S)/m^c_b(S')] = 2 nu (Q^c_S - Q^c_S') / ((2b + Q^c_S)(2b + Q^c_S')).
  > - (T) Transfer rule. (a) Mixed-endpoint transfer: on B_n, Pi(E | y) <= kappa^2 I_{b-}(E)/Z^c_{b+}, with b- = b0 sigma*^2/2, b+ = b0(2(sigma*^2+M)+1), kappa = (b+/b-)^0.51; so a bound I_{b-}(E_n)/Z^c_{b+} <= eps_n transfers at cost kappa^2. (b) Same-rate bounds do not transfer: a worst case over inputs (b1: no data-free implication between bounds at two distinct fixed rates; b2: witnesses inside B_n where a same-rate bound at b- or b+ does not bound the v3 posterior by any constant).
- Full statement of record, excerpt of `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/STATEMENT.md` from '2. T01' (verbatim):
  > ## 2. T01
  >
  > **(i) [identity; every valid input, deterministic].** The joint transformed posterior of (S, θ_S, v) equals Π_{b₀s_y²}, the posterior of the contrast model at rate b = b₀s_y² (the rate evaluated at the observed s_y), and for every S ∈ Ω
  > m(S) = c_n(s_y) · m^c_{b₀s_y²}(S),  c_n(s) = s^{n−1}Γ(0.51)/(√(2πb₀)Γ(0.01)).
  > Hence BF(S) = m^c_{b₀s_y²}(S)/m^c_{b₀s_y²}(∅), π(S) = ϖ(S)m^c_{b₀s_y²}(S)/Z^c_{b₀s_y²}, and Z = c_n(s_y) Z^c_{b₀s_y²}. Moreover z_S^c = s_y z_S, Q_S^c = s_y²Q_S, and under the joint transformed posterior
  > v | S, y ~ IG(ν, b₀s_y² + Q_S^c/2),  θ_S | v, S, y ~ N_k(nH_S⁻¹z_S^c, nvH_S⁻¹).
  >
  > **(ii) [envelope; deterministic].** Let 0 < b₁ ≤ b ≤ b₂ be any numbers and κ₁₂ = (b₂/b₁)^{0.51}. For every S ∈ Ω and every y_c ∈ ℝ^{n−1}:
  > κ₁₂⁻¹m^c_{b₂}(S) ≤ m^c_b(S) ≤ κ₁₂ m^c_{b₁}(S).
  > For every measurable parameter event E: κ₁₂⁻¹I_{b₂}(E) ≤ I_b(E) ≤ κ₁₂ I_{b₁}(E); consequently Π_b(E) ≤ κ₁₂² I_{b₁}(E)/Z^c_{b₂}. (The original writes b₋, b₊, κ here; the letters are changed only because b₋, b₊, κ denote the specific constants of §1 elsewhere. With b₁ = b₋, b₂ = b₊ one has κ₁₂ = κ.)
  >
  > **(iii) [scale event].** Under G and R: s_y² − (σ*² + ‖μ‖²/(n−1)) = O_{P₀}(n^{−1/2}) and P₀(𝓑_n) → 1. Also ε_c := Uᵀε ~ N_{n−1}(0, σ*²I_{n−1}) exactly, and y_c = X_cθ* + ε_c.
  >
  > **(iv) [rate derivative; fixed contrast data].** For S, S′ ∈ Ω and b > 0:
  > ∂_b log[m^c_b(S)/m^c_b(S′)] = 2ν(Q_S^c − Q_{S′}^c)/((2b + Q_S^c)(2b + Q_{S′}^c)).
  >
  > **(T) [transfer rule].**
  > (a) *Mixed-endpoint transfer.* With b₋, b₊, κ, 𝓑_n as in §1: on 𝓑_n, for every measurable parameter event E,
  > Π(E | y) ≤ κ² I_{b₋}(E)/Z^c_{b₊} ≤ κ² I_{b₋}(E)/(ϖ(S₀) m^c_{b₊}(S₀))
  > (the last step when S₀ ∈ Ω), where Π(· | y) is the joint transformed v3 posterior and the right-hand sides are computed from y_c at the fixed rates b₋ (numerator) and b₊ (denominator). Consequently, under G and R, if I_{b₋}(E_n)/Z^c_{b₊} ≤ ε_n with P₀-probability → 1 (resp. = O_{P₀}(ε_n)), then Π(E_n | y) ≤ κ²ε_n with P₀-probability → 1 (resp. = O_{P₀}(ε_n)).
  > (b) *Same-rate bounds do not transfer (a worst case over inputs, not a statement about P₀).*
  > (b1) For any fixed rates 0 < r₁ < r₂ there are valid inputs (n → ∞, p = 1) with Π_{r₁}({S = {1}}) → 1 and Π_{r₂}({S = {1}}) → 0 (so Π_{r₁}({S = ∅}) → 0 and Π_{r₂}({S = ∅}) → 1). Hence, for distinct fixed rates b ≠ b′, there is no function g with g(x) → 0 as x ↓ 0, independent of n and the data, such that Π_{b′}(E) ≤ g(Π_b(E)) for all valid inputs and all events E. (Its inputs have s_y² → 0, so they lie outside 𝓑_n for large n; (b2) is the version on 𝓑_n.)
  > (b2) Fix any σ*² > 0 and M ≥ 0 (hence b₋, b₊), and any s² with σ*²/2 < s² < 2(σ*²+M)+1. There are valid inputs with p = 2 and s_y² = s² for every n ≥ 4 (so 𝓑_n holds for every n) such that, for E = {S = {1}}, Π_{b₋}(E) → 0 while Π(E | y) → 1 as n → ∞; and there are valid inputs with the same properties such that, for E′ = {S = {1,2}}, Π_{b₊}(E′) → 0 while Π(E′ | y) → 1. Hence, for b ∈ {b₋, b₊}, there is no constant C, independent of n and of the data, such that Π(E | y) ≤ C·Π_b(E) for all valid inputs in 𝓑_n and all events E.
  > (Proof discipline, not a mathematical claim: the proofs never treat ε or ε_c as N(0, σ*²I) conditionally on s_y or on 𝓑_n.)
- Assumptions / hypotheses (verbatim, one-pager):
  > - (i), (ii), (iv): none beyond a valid input (n >= 3, no constant column, non-constant y).
  > - (iii) and (T): G (fixed design, Gaussian errors) and R (s0 fixed, p <= n^A, ||mu||^2/n <= M, lambda_min(R_S0) >= phi0^2, s0 <= K eventually). No SE, no beta-min, no H-xx. EX-A for exact arithmetic.

  > PROVED-LOCKED (all parts, wave 3), with H-T02 as hypothesis (closed by T02(i)); not adopted (adoption is Felipe's decision)  | Rank: core ((i) double-log fallback secondary) | Paper role: Supplement remark
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T04 | Contraction without beta-min (A3 = T4) | core | PROVED-LOCKED (all parts; wave 3; hypothesis H-T02) | Supplement remark | `proofs/T04_A3_contraction/` | SE, DX; external review queued |
- Statement (verbatim, one-pager 'Statement' section):
  > Source: proofs/T04_A3_contraction/STATEMENT.md section 3 (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
  > - There is a constant C depending only on (sigma*^2, M, phi0, A) such that, in R1 under G, R and H-T02 ('-> 0' means in P0-probability), with l_n = log(p v n), eps_2^2 = (s0+1) l_n^2 / n, eps_1^2 = (s0+1) l_n / n, d* = s0 + ceil(s0 (2A+1)):
  > - (i) fallback (secondary): Pi-dagger(||X theta - mu||^2/n > C eps_2^2 | y) -> 0.
  > - (ii) under SE in addition: Pi(|S| > d* | y) -> 0; Pi-dagger(||X theta - mu||^2/n > C eps_1^2 | y) -> 0; Pi-dagger(||theta - theta*||^2 > C eps_1^2/phi0^2 | y) -> 0.
  > - (iii) for every deterministic u_n -> infinity: Pi-dagger(|v/sigma*^2 - 1| > C[eps_n^2 + u_n/sqrt(n)] | y) -> 0, with eps_n = eps_2,n under G, R and eps_1,n under SE in addition.
  > - (iv) under SE and DX: Pi-dagger(||D_x^-1 (theta - theta*)||^2 > C eps_1^2/(phi0^2 d-^2) | y) -> 0.
  > - Not claimed: beta-min; out-of-sample, intercept-posterior or random-design Hellinger results.
- Assumptions / hypotheses (verbatim, one-pager):
  > - R1, G, R; H-T02 (= T02(i)); SE for (ii), (iv) and the sharper part of (iii); DX (min raw column SD >= d- > 0) for (iv).

### TH105 — T06 — Identifiability and exact ties (old label A5 = T-ID)  [proposition]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/STATEMENT.md`, `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/PROOF_v2.tex`; condensation used here: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T06.md` (the STATEMENT.md is authoritative; the one-pager says 'Faithful condensation'); positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]
- Status at campaign start (verbatim, one-pager line 2):
  > PROVED-LOCKED (all parts, wave 3); (ii)(b) conditional on H-T03 (= T03(i)); not adopted (adoption is Felipe's decision)  | Rank: core (proposition) | Paper role: Supplement remark (one sentence of T06(i) goes into Prop 1)
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T06 | Identifiability and exact ties (A5 = T-ID) | core | PROVED-LOCKED (all parts; wave 3); (ii)(b) uses H-T03 | Supplement remark (one sentence of T06(i) goes into Prop 1) | `proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/` | H-T03 for (ii)(b); NIS / DUP where stated; external review queued |
- Statement (verbatim, one-pager 'Statement' section):
  > Source: proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/STATEMENT.md section 1 (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
  > - (i) Exact ties. (a) For S, S' in Omega: F_S = F_S' on the contrast sphere iff X_S X_S^T = X_S' X_S'^T (outer products agree); then |S| = |S'| and F(S) = F(S') for every response. (b) If span(X_S) = span(X_S') but the outer products differ, the score functions differ somewhere; such feasible pairs exist at every n >= 4 (p = 4), never when K = 1. (c) Under G, P0-a.s. every exact tie F(S) = F(S') has equal outer products; under G and NIS, P0(there exist S != S' in Omega with F(S) = F(S')) = 0.
  > - (ii) Fallback without NIS. (a) Deterministic: on {pi(S0) > 1/2}, S0 in Omega and argmax F = {S0}, so S-dagger = S0 for every tie rule. (b) Conditional on H-T03 (T03(i): 1 - pi(S0) = O_P(r_n)): P0(pi(S0) > 1/2) -> 1.
  > - (iii) Duplicates and weak separation. (a)-(b) Under DUP(a), the transposition tau of i, j preserves size and F; PIP_i = PIP_j and pi(S) < 1/2 for S containing exactly one of i, j. (c) Two-point bound: for any selector delta, max_k P_k(delta != S_k) >= (1/2) sum_k P_k(delta != S_k) >= Phi(-||m1 - m2||/(2 sigma*)); location-invariant selectors: >= Phi(-||mu1 - mu2||/(2 sigma*)). (d) No uniform recovery over classes containing pairs with ||mu1 - mu2||/sigma_n -> 0 (liminf sup error >= 1/2). (e) The near-duplicate report (components of |r_ij| >= 1 - 1e-10) is a warning only: F_{A+i} = F_{A+j} iff |r_ij| = 1, and exact-tie pairs with max |r_ij| <= 1/sqrt(2) exist for every n >= 4 (p = 4).
- Assumptions / hypotheses (verbatim, one-pager):
  > - Valid input; G for the probabilistic parts; NIS for (i)(c); DUP(a) for (iii)(a)-(d); H-T03 (= T03(i) conclusion, only as pi(S0) -> 1) for (ii)(b); 'mean-matched' pairs for the all-selector version of (iii)(c)-(d).
- LOCKED_PROOFS.md register row(s) (verbatim; hashes there are the freeze record):
  > | **T06 and T07** (identifiability and exact ties; size-only ranking ceiling and Bayes decisions) | T06: two models tie exactly iff their projection matrices X_S X_S' agree; a fallback gives the HPM equal to S0 when pi(S0) > 1/2; with duplicate columns two supports are indistinguishable, and a two-point bound shows uniform recovery is impossible. T07: no size-only prior can fix a within-size ranking error; the 0-1 loss is minimised by the HPM and the Hamming loss by the median-probability model; the PIP error bounds the excess risk. | `T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior\STATEMENT.md`<br>`ba3279b7f5a1ed9027e38f4975910d7cde83ac9a2927efe6bb1b48c936f0c14c` | `T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior\proof\PROOF_v2.tex`<br>`fc6291c6999e1c157e6f43603aa97e62655b8e84111ad831b59cb1b51c28f804` | **H-T03** (= T03(i) conclusion; used only for T06(ii)(b); now in this register under T03's regime assumptions). ### TH106 — T07 — Size-only ranking ceiling and Bayes decisions (old label A6 = T5-C)  [proposition]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/STATEMENT.md`, `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/PROOF_v2.tex`; condensation used here: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T07.md` (the STATEMENT.md is authoritative; the one-pager says 'Faithful condensation'); positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]
- Status at campaign start (verbatim, one-pager line 2):
  > PROVED-LOCKED (all parts, wave 3); not adopted (adoption is Felipe's decision)  | Rank: core (proposition) | Paper role: JRSS-B Prop 1 (HPM is the Bayes rule for exact recovery; a size-only prior cannot fix a same-size swap); Biometrika: remark
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T07 | Size-only ranking ceiling and Bayes decisions (A6 = T5-C) | core | PROVED-LOCKED (all parts; wave 3) | JRSS-B Prop 1; Biometrika remark | `proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/` | external review queued |
- Statement (verbatim, one-pager 'Statement' section):
  > Source: proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/STATEMENT.md section 2 (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
  > - (i) Ceiling: for every response and every positive size-only prior w~, {S-dagger_w~ = S0} is contained in {S*_{s0} = S0}, where S*_k is the least element of argmax over |S| = k of m(S). So on a within-size ranking error no positive size-only prior yields S0.
  > - (ii) Bayes decisions: (a) 0-1 loss on supports: posterior risk 1 - pi(a); the minimisers are exactly argmax F, and S-dagger is one. (b) Hamming loss: MPM = {j : PIP_j > 1/2} minimises the risk over all subsets (unique iff no PIP_j = 1/2). (c) Capped: the top-l PIPs inside {PIP_j > 1/2}, l = min(K, N+), minimise Hamming risk over Omega.
  > - (iii) Target vs reported: (a) S-hat = S-dagger iff S-dagger is in the scored set; S-hat minimises posterior 0-1 loss iff the scored set meets argmax F. (b) {S-hat = S0} and {S*_{s0} != S0} implies S*_{s0} is not scored. (c) For any PIP estimate p-hat, 0 <= risk_H(a-hat) - risk_H(a_opt) <= 2 sum_{j in a-hat symmetric-difference a_opt} |p-hat_j - PIP_j| <= 2 ||p-hat - PIP||_1; MPM-hat = MPM iff p-hat_j > 1/2 <=> PIP_j > 1/2 for all j.
  > - The control of scoring and estimation events is not part of this result (it is the subject of T21, T23, T26).
- Assumptions / hypotheses (verbatim, one-pager):
  > - Positive marginal likelihood m; a fixed total tie order; no statistical assumption for (i)-(iii)(c).

### TH115 — T21 — Composition theorem for the reported HPM (old label T14-H)  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/STATEMENT.md`, `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/PROOF_v3.tex`; condensation used here: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T21.md` (the STATEMENT.md is authoritative; the one-pager says 'Faithful condensation'); positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]; later [pos 342]; [pos 370]
- Status at campaign start (verbatim, one-pager line 2):
  > PROVED-LOCKED (C1 and routes (a)-(f), wave 2) + CONDITIONAL on open hypotheses: H24 (route (e)) and the route-specific occurrence / exposure conditions; not adopted (adoption is Felipe's decision)  | Rank: core (theorem; route (e) medium confidence) | Paper role: JRSS-B Thm 4; Biometrika Thm 4 (route (e) now supplied by Thm 3, i.e. T37 or T24)
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T21 | Composition theorem for the reported HPM (T14-H) | core | PROVED-LOCKED (C1, routes (a)-(f); wave 2); CONDITIONAL on H24 (route e), exposure/occurrence conditions | JRSS-B Thm 4; Biometrika Thm 4 | `proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/` | H24; exposure / occurrence conditions; P(U) -> 0 |
- Statement (verbatim, one-pager 'Statement' section):
  > Source: proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/STATEMENT.md; theorems/T21_T14H_HPM_composition.md (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
  > - (C1) P(U or S-hat != S0) <= P(U) + 2 E0[delta1] + P(not U, S0 not in the scored set), where U = no usable HPM output, delta1 = 1 - pi(S0). The method fails to report the truth only if no output exists, or the posterior has at most half its mass on the truth, or the truth was never scored (INVENTORY D).
  > - Routes (a)-(f) bound the last term: (a) fresh iid final draws: P(S0 not scored) <= P(F^c, S0 not in S_cal) + E[1_F 1{S0 not in S_cal} (1 - pi0(S0))^Q_f]; (b) Gibbs execution (SR scores S0 when X_pre-j minus j equals S0 minus j); (c) swap exposure (probability 1/[k(p-k)] per execution; P(no hit) <= delta + (1-b)^D); (d) tables and scans (S0 inside a block is table-scored; a completed scan from a flip/swap neighbour scores it, T20(ii)); (e) terminal repair under T24: P(no truth score in H rounds) <= (1 - a_n)^H + H eta_n; (f) exact enumeration branch (S-hat = S-dagger).
  > - The statement also records that the previous version was changed by a Claude audit fix (E1, E3; PROOF_v3).
- Full statement of record, excerpt of `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/STATEMENT.md` from '3. Conclusions' (verbatim):
  > ## 3. Conclusions
  >
  > **(C1)** For every such n and data law,
  >
  >     P(U or Shat != S0) <= P(U) + 2 E0 delta1 + P(U^c, S0 not in Sscr).
  >
  > Under H03 the middle term tends to zero. If P(U)->0 and any applicable discovery bound below tends to zero, recovery probability tends to one. The finite bounds, and not merely the name of a route, specify the needed occurrence/exposure conditions.
  >
  > **(a) Fresh iid draws.** Under EX-S, CAL and full operational execution,
  >
  >     P(S0 not in Sscr)
  >     <= P(Fcal^c, S0 not in Scal)
  >        + E[1_Fcal 1_{S0 not in Scal} (1-pi0(S0))^Q_f].
  >
  > The second term is at most E[1_Fcal 1_{S0 not in Scal} exp(-Q_f pi0(S0))]. If the first term vanishes and, for every finite M, P(Fcal, Q_f pi0(S0)<=M)->0, then discovery failure tends to zero. This is the precise meaning of intensity diverging 'on launched runs'; conditional divergence given Fcal, when defined, is sufficient as well.
  >
  > If s0>=1 is fixed, i in S0, and Stilde0=S0 minus {i} has pi0(Stilde0)>=c>0 (Stilde0 need not be the start mode), H10 gives pi0(S0)>=c r_{s0-1} and
  >
  >     Q_f pi0(S0) >= 4 c s0 N_e(T+L+5)/[(2p-s0)sqrt(n+1)].
  >
  > This guaranteed lower-bound intensity has scale N_e(T+L+5)/(p sqrt(n)) for fixed s0,c. Under actual budgets it diverges whenever p<=C sqrt(n) for a fixed C, including the boundary because L grows logarithmically. If the start-mass event holds only with probability tending to one, add its failure probability. This is a sufficient range, not a necessary range: this lower bound supplies no proof of failure above it. No two-sided law from the unproved T27 is used.
  >
  > **(b) Gibbs execution.** If, before discovery, an actual Gibbs execution satisfies X_pre-j minus {j}=S0 minus {j}, SR scores S0. Let E_G be the event that such an execution occurs before discovery. Then {S0 not in Sscr} is contained in E_G^c. Thus P(U^c,E_G^c)->0 is sufficient for the discovery term in C1. Occupancy of a round-start state alone is not the execution-time condition.
  >
  > **(c) Swap execution.** A size-k proxy is S=(S0 minus {l}) union {j}, where l in S0, j not in S0, and 1<=k=s0<p. At each actual uniform-swap execution in such a proxy before the first truth score, the conditional probability of proposing and scoring S0 is b=1/[k(p-k)]. Let O be the number of these actual opportunities before discovery or the end of the run. For deterministic integer D>=0 and delta>=0,
  >
  >     P(S0 not in Sscr, O<D)<=delta
  >     implies P(S0 not in Sscr)<=delta+(1-b)^D.
  >
  > Use (1-b)^0=1, including b=1. The same statement may be conditioned on data or pre-run information, with D fixed under that conditioning. No independence of opportunities, or conditioning on their future count, is required. PX means such exposure is sufficiently large: for some omega_n->infinity, P(S0 not in Sscr, O<ceil(omega_n k(p-k)))->0. It yields discovery. ONE (a start-mode flip or same-block proxy relation) alone specifies no such count and is not substituted for PX.
  >
  > For a neighbour swap at that proxy the probability is 1/[k|N(j) minus S|] if the actual required edge l in N(j) is present, and zero if absent. A deterministic lower bound b_* in (0,1], valid at every counted neighbour-swap opportunity before discovery, can replace b. A random b_* may be used in the conditional version when it is measurable with respect to the information conditioned on and bounds every subsequent counted opportunity. Unconditional averaging then requires the corresponding expectation of (1-b_*)^D. A same-block description alone does not replace the actual edge condition.
  >
  > **(d) Tables and scans.** If S0 is contained in some C_b and that table is constructed, S0 is table-scored. If a completed local scan has a feasible flip-or-swap neighbour of S0 as its centre, it scores S0, whether or not any move budget remains. Let E_TS be the event that at least one such table construction or completed scan occurs. Then P(U^c,S0 not in Sscr)<=P(U^c,E_TS^c); vanishing of the latter suffices. No schedule-success assumption is needed if tables or calibration already supply the score.
  >
  > **(e) Terminal repair.** Under H24 and SR, select an eligible particle (state in R_d) using only the available past at a terminal-round boundary. Future randomness for that particle is fresh and its next H rounds, at temperature one and without intervening resampling, execute; H>=0 is fixed given the selection past. Conditional on that past and the data, on eligibility, let M_H be the event that S0 not in Sscr when those H rounds end. Then
  >
  >     P(M_H | available past) <= (1-a_n)^H+H eta_n.
  >
  > For an availability event A measurable at selection, the unconditional failure bound is P(A^c)+E[1_A min{1,(1-a_n)^H+H eta_n}]. The truth already being scored only improves the bound. For final-run repair put A_F=Fcal intersect {an eligible particle is available at the chosen terminal boundary}; then a sharper whole-run bound is
  >
  >     P(S0 not in Sscr) <= P(Fcal^c,S0 not in Scal)
  >        + P(Fcal, no eligible particle at that boundary)
  >        + E[1_{A_F} min{1,(1-a_n)^H+H eta_n}].
  >
  > Thus the nonlaunch term is retained. Pilot repair uses its forward filtration at the selection boundary, never conditioning on the subsequently constructed grid or final calibration record. With H=L+4, fixed s0,d, H24's asymptotic inputs and vanishing availability/nonlaunch terms imply discovery. For arbitrary H the sufficient repair condition is Ha_n->infinity and H eta_n->0 in probability on availability. These are HPM scoring guarantees, not PIP accuracy guarantees.
  >
  > **(f) Exact branch.** If sum_{k=0}^K binom(p,k)<=(5H0+4N0)p and the exact enumeration completes under EX-A, Sscr=Omega, Shat=Sdagger, and the evidence and primary PIPs are the exact finite sums Z and sum_{S:j in S} exp(F(S))/Z. Every fixed p eventually satisfies this branch inequality as n->infinity. Actual completion remains a separate operational requirement; truth recovery additionally uses H03 through C1.
- Assumptions / hypotheses (verbatim, one-pager):
  > - H03 (= T03(i) conclusion; closed by T03 in its regime), H10 (= T10(i) addition floor; used only in (a)'s one-deletion corollary; closed by T10), H24 (T24 terminal-repair inputs K1(x,{S0}) >= a_n and one-round exit probability <= eta_n on R_d, plus a_n >= c_n/2 and (L+4) eta_n -> 0; used only in (e); OPEN since T24 is not proved).
  > - Also P(U) -> 0 and route-specific occurrence or exposure conditions (PX, ONE, E_G, E_TS, availability of an eligible particle). EX-A, EX-S, CAL, SR.

- Statement (verbatim, one-pager 'Statement' section):
  > Source: proofs/T22_T16_start_aggregation/STATEMENT.md and proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/STATEMENT.md; theorems/T22_T16_start_aggregation.md (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
  > - PROVED-LOCKED (wave 1, parts (i), (ii), (iv-a), (iv-b) deterministic for every data realisation; (ii) and (iv) assume S0 in Omega, i.e. s0 <= K): with aggregation quantities q_n, e_n for a feasible reference S (size s): (i) if q_n < 1 then pi0(S) >= (1 - q_n)^(s+1) / (1 + e_n)^s and 1 - pi0(S) <= (s+1) q_n/(1 - q_n) + s e_n (also q_n <= u_n). (ii-a) pi0(S0) = pi0(S) [w(s0)/w(s)] prod_b r_b(S0 cap C_b)/r_b(S cap C_b) exactly; (ii-b) if S is contained in S0, pi0(S0)/pi0(S) >= prod_{j=0}^{s0-s-1} r_{s+j}. (iv-a) for 0 <= phi <= 1, 1/q_phi(S0) - 1 <= R0^(1-phi) R1^phi <= max(R0, R1); (iv-b) hence inf_phi q_phi(S0) >= min{pi0(S0), pi(S0)}: the bridge keeps mass on S0 at every temperature. (iv-c) is a conditional probabilistic consequence: if P0(S0 in Omega) -> 1, 1 - pi(S0) -> 0 (T03's conclusion) and 1 - pi0(S0) -> 0 (T22(iii)'s conclusion), then sup_phi [1 - q_phi(S0)] -> 0 in probability.
  > - PROVED-LOCKED but CONDITIONAL (wave 2, part (iii), folder T22iii_T16_start_aggregation, PROOF_v2): under G, R, within-block SE, VIS, NL_eta, the rate condition NL_avg(kappa) and EXP' (log[r_b(T+l)/r_b(T)] = -(1/2) log(n+1) - nu log(1 - x_{T,l}) + R with max |R| = O_P(1)): q_n <= u_n = O_P(2^B sqrt(log n) n^-kappa), e_n = o_P(n^-m) for every fixed m, and 1 - pi0(S0) = O_P(2^B sqrt(log n) n^-kappa + e_n). A weaker o_P(log n) remainder gives the exponent form.
  > - CONJECTURED (not proved): (v) block-orthogonal (BO) case: with SE, bounded signal energy and BM-infinity the projection argument supplies VIS; the score conclusion still needs EXP.
- Full statement of record, excerpt of `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/STATEMENT.md` from '4. Precise conclusion: part (iii)' (verbatim):
  > ## 4. Precise conclusion: part (iii)
  >
  > Under Sections 1–2 with the strict EXP′ remainder and any fixed κ satisfying the rate condition:
  >
  > 1. q_n ≤ u_n = O_{P₀}(2^B √(log n) n^(−κ)).
  > 2. For every fixed m>0, e_n = o_{P₀}(n^(−m)).
  > 3. 1−π₀(S₀) = O_{P₀}(2^B √(log n) n^(−κ)+e_n); in particular π₀(S₀) → 1 in P₀-probability.
  >
  > The random-scale O_{P₀} in item 3 means the ratio to the positive displayed scale is bounded in probability. It also follows that 1−π₀(S₀)=O_{P₀}(2^B√(log n)n^(−κ)).
  >
  > Under the weaker EXP′ variant, item 1 becomes: for some ξ_n=o_{P₀}(1),
  >
  >     q_n ≤ u_n ≤ 2^B√(log n)n^(−κ+ξ_n)
  >
  > on events of probability tending to one. Item 2 is unchanged, and item 3 becomes, for some ζ_n=o_{P₀}(1),
  >
  >     1−π₀(S₀) ≤ 2^B√(log n)n^(−κ+ζ_n)+s₀e_n
  >
  > on events of probability tending to one; concentration still follows. Exact zero leakage permits κ=1/2 in both variants.

- Full statement of record, excerpt of `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T23_T18_basin_prefix/STATEMENT.md` from '3. Conclusions' (verbatim):
  > ## 3. Conclusions
  >
  > (ii-a) **Pathwise RB bound.** On every realisation of the final run, for each island r,
  >   max_j |PIP̂_{rj} − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ B̄_r + max_j |o_j(S₀,1) − 1{j ∈ S₀}|.
  >   If S₀ ∉ Ω, the method does not define o_j(S₀, 1); it may then be given any real value, and the inequality holds for every such choice, because every path state lies in Ω and so B̄_r = 1.
  >
  > (ii-b) **Truth term.** If S₀ ∈ Ω, then max_j |o_j(S₀,1) − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ u_π. (If S₀ ∉ Ω, u_π = +∞ and the bound is trivial.)
  >
  > (ii-c) **Expectation bound for the primary PIP.** Under BASIN,
  >   E_𝓒 max_j |PIP̂_j − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ δ + (1−a)^{⌊L/r₀⌋} + (L+4)(η+ρ) + u_π =: 𝓑_n.
  >
  > (ii-d) **MPM.** P_𝓒(MPM̂ ≠ S₀) ≤ 2𝓑_n.
  >
  > The bounds use no independence between particles and no union bound over the p coordinates.

  > - PROVED-LOCKED, (i) start-mass law under cancellation (a conditional implication): if along a chain S^(0) subset ... subset S^(c) = S0 of c feasible single additions each table ratio is n^-1/2 e^{O_P(1)} jointly (H2), and the starting model keeps normalised start mass pi0(S^(0)) >= c0 with probability -> 1 (H3), then log pi0(S0) + c log p + (c/2) log n = O_P(1), i.e. pi0(S0) = p^-c n^-c/2 exp(O_P(1)). For c = 0 the conclusion is log pi0(S0) = O_P(1).
  > - CONJECTURED (not locked): (ii) budget exponent beta = max(1, a) - c(a + 1/2) for p ~ n^a (iid discovery tends to certainty if beta > 0, to zero if beta < 0); (iii) scales [max(n,p) log n]^-1 and [max(n,p) log^2 n]^-1; (iv) without the two-sided law T10 gives only a lower bound.
  > - Must not be combined with T22(iii) on one sequence (different regimes).
- Full statement of record, excerpt of `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T27i_T20C_cancellation_budget/STATEMENT.md` from 'Exact conclusion' (verbatim):
  > ## Exact conclusion
  >
  >     log pi_0(S_0)+c log p+(c/2)log n=O_{P_0}(1),
  >
  > equivalently pi_0(S_0)=p^(-c)n^(-c/2)exp{O_{P_0}(1)}. Here O_{P_0}(1) means tightness: for each epsilon>0 a finite M and N exist such that P_0{|Z_n|>M}<epsilon for n>=N. The positive mass multiplier and its reciprocal are both tight.
  >
  > **Empty-chain extension:** if c=0, S^(0)=S_0, H2 is vacuous (empty maximum zero), and the conclusion is log pi_0(S_0)=O_{P_0}(1), with empty products one and empty sums zero.
- Assumptions / hypotheses (verbatim, one-pager):
  > - H1 (fixed feasible completion chain; a definition), H2 (sequential ratio law, jointly two-sided O_P(1) remainders; assumed statistical input), H3 (normalised reference-mass lower bound; assumed statistical input), H4 (EX-A, EX-S, CAL, successful final execution). G / R, Gaussianity, eigenvalue or beta-min assumptions are NOT used to derive H2 or H3.

- Statement as written in the theorem file (verbatim; sections 'Definitions used', 'Assumptions', 'Precise statement'):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.991) from `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/T05_A4_orthogonal_threshold.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > [Definitions used]
  > Global HPM S†; D_S, Q_S, z_j (00_COMMON §1). λ_n = (n−1)b_n²/σ*²; τ_n = log n + 2 log((2p_n − s₀)/s₀). Φ = standard normal cdf. "Known-size, known-noise selector": the top-s₀ absolute-statistic selector that knows s₀ and σ*.
  > [Assumptions]
  > G, R (project); ORTH (project benchmark: G = (n−1)I_p, so p ≤ n−1; fixed 1 ≤ s₀ < p; equal magnitudes b_n on S₀; b_n²/σ*² bounded). No beta-min. Not a p > n result.
  > [Precise statement]
  > Under G, R, ORTH:
  > (i) [exact identities] D_S = n^{|S|} and Q_S = yᵀy − n⁻¹Σ_{j∈S}z_j². The exact addition log-odds are log[(k+1)/(2p−k−1)] − ½ log n + ν log[(0.02+Q_S)/(0.02+Q_S−z_j²/n)].
  > (ii) [threshold] If √λ_n − √τ_n → c ∈ [−∞, ∞], then P₀(S† = S₀) → Φ(c)^{s₀}.
  > (iii) [gap] If p_n − s₀ → ∞, every signal sequence with √λ_n − √(2 log(p_n−s₀)) → ∞ and √τ_n − √λ_n → ∞ is recovered by the known-size, known-noise selector with probability → 1 while v3's global HPM fails with probability → 1. Such sequences exist, since τ_n − 2 log(p_n−s₀) = log n + 2 log(2/s₀) + o(1); e.g. λ_n = (1−ε)τ_n with 0 < ε < 1/(1+2A); at p ≍ n^a the gap is [√(1+2a) − √(2a)]√(log n) to leading order. No minimax theorem is adopted.

  > [Definitions used]
  > Reflected elementary kernels K_e^W(x, A) = K_e(x, A∩W) + K_e(x, Wᶜ)1_A(x); reflected round; the reflected comparator run (iid q₀(·|W) starts, full initial normaliser m(∅)Z̄₀, same frozen grid and weights G_t); r_W = q₁(W)/q₀(W); first mismatch time τ; original Gibbs rewards o_j(·,1); μ_j^W := π(·|W)(o_j(·,1)) (00_COMMON §2; inventory CPL-E, CPL-H/RB).
  > [Assumptions]
  > EX-A, EX-S, CAL; CPL-E, CPL-H or the RB condition when transferring the corresponding output.
  > [Precise statement]
  > Fix nonempty W ⊆ Ω given 𝓒.
  > (i) Each K_e^W is q_φ(·|W)-reversible; the random-order reflected round is invariant and self-adjoint. The comparator's evidence has EẐ_r^W = Z·r_W (not Zq₁(W)).
  > (ii) [coupling] Couple each full initial draw with its conditional-W counterpart (agreeing when the full draw lies in W); while populations agree, share resampling and transition randomness. Up to the horizon relevant to the output, the failure probability satisfies h ≤ 4Nq₀(Wᶜ) + Σ_{r,i,e}E[1{τ > e⁻}K_e(X_{ri,e⁻}, Wᶜ)] (accepted exits at first occurrence; resampling causes no mismatch while populations and weights agree).
  > (iii) [transfer] For any statistic U measurable from coupled variables: |P(U ∈ A) − P(U^W ∈ A)| ≤ h. Under CPL-E: P(Ẑ/Z > x) ≤ h_E + r_W/x for x > 0. Evidence needs coupling only through its last weight evaluation; PIPs need the measured paths and the same reward function (or a reward-discrepancy allowance); HPM needs every scored proposal and scan. Rejecting an outside transition does not suppress its score.
  > (iv) [rewards] If original Gibbs rewards are retained in the reflected run, E[Ẑ_r^W PIP̂_{rj}^{W,orig}] = Z r_W μ_j^W, where in general μ_j^W ≠ π(j ∈ S | W), but |μ_j^W − PIP_j| ≤ π(Wᶜ).
  > (v) [hazard floor] For a boundary addition with hazard ≥ h_k, the stopped first-exit opportunities obey T11(iv), including P(failure) ≥ h_kEO. No blanket impossibility of coupling follows from a large union-bound upper bound or from a small stationary outside mass alone.

(i) Each K_e^W is q_phi(.|W)-reversible, the reflected round is invariant; the comparator's evidence has mean Z r_W, r_W = q_1(W)/q_0(W). (ii) Coupling failure h <= 4 N q_0(W^c) + sum E[1{tau > e-} K_e(X, W^c)]. (iii) Transfer: |P(U in A) - P(U^W in A)| <= h; under CPL-E, P(Z-hat/Z > x) <= h_E + r_W/x. (iv) Reward identity E[Z-hat_r^W PIP-hat^{W,orig}] = Z r_W mu_j^W with |mu_j^W - PIP_j| <= pi(W^c). (v) Hazard floor: a boundary addition with hazard >= h_k obeys T11(iv).

  > 𝓡_d = {U∪P : U ⊆ S₀, P ⊆ [p]∖S₀, |P| ≤ d}, fixed d ≥ 1, s₀+d ≤ K; Λ_n^all = max_{T∈𝓡_d}Σ_{l∉S₀∪T}o_l(T,1); ξ_n (EXIT_d); g_n^±, g_n = min(g_n^+, g_n^−) (GAIN_d; an empty family has minimum +∞); D = 2^{s₀+d}; c_n = 1/(s₀+d+B+2)!; ρ_* (T23); a_n := [c_n{1 − (s₀+d)e^{−g_n}} − DΛ_n^all − ρ_*]_+; η_n := min{1, (B+3)DΛ_n^all + ξ_n}.
  > [Assumptions]
  > EX-A, EX-S, SR; fixed s₀, d; LK_d, EXIT_d, GAIN_d (new); T03's hypotheses for truth stability; CAL for final-run use; pilot use requires the pilot's forward filtration; statistical verification uniform before selecting a state.
  > [Precise statement]
  > (i) inf_{x∈𝓡_d}K₁(x, S₀) ≥ a_n and sup_{x∈𝓡_d}P_x(first exit from 𝓡_d during one round) ≤ η_n. Under T03 and the inventory's logarithmic leakage/exit limits, (L+4)(η_n + ρ_*) → 0; since B ≤ 16, c_n has a fixed positive lower bound, and GAIN_d gives a_n ≥ c_n/2 eventually with probability → 1.
  > (ii) [HPM repair] For a particle in 𝓡_d selected from the available past: P(no truth score in H terminal rounds) ≤ (1−a_n)^H + Hη_n; with H = L+4 this is a discovery route needing neither HIT nor ONE. Availability of an eligible particle and operational execution are separate.
  > (iii) [PIP repair] T23 applies with r₀ = 1, a = a_n, η = η_n, ρ = ρ_*, plus a vanishing expected stage-T fraction outside 𝓡_d (independently or via T15).
  > (iv) [gain sub-conjectures] Under G, R, SE, BM-∞ a uniform projection-gain argument is proposed to derive g_n^+ → ∞ for fixed d (conversion to exact integrated log-score gains is an obligation); for d = 1, T03's global margin gives g_n^− → ∞; for d ≥ 2 a favourable single deletion from every proper truth superset remains an explicit GAIN_d assumption.
  > The v2 slot constants 1/(s₀!d!) and the treatment of EXIT_d as internal-change control are withdrawn (internal non-Gibbs moves can change the greedy maximiser without exiting 𝓡_d).

  > [Definitions used]
  > Hidden set 𝓜 as in T28; S†; first score time τ of 𝓜 over chronological opportunities with hazards p_e; stopped count O; μ_j^W = π(·|W)(o_j(·,1)) (T17(iv)); falling factorial (p+B+2)_h; h = |T Δ S₀|.

These quantified conditions replace distance or "protection" classifications.

This is polynomial accessibility, not discovery at the actual budget. Under T24's hypotheses and eligible occupancy, T24 instead gives high-probability discovery and excludes the corresponding MISS-H instance.

  > [Definitions used]

  > [Precise statement]

  > (ii) [obstruction] If ρ(a, D(b−u)2^{−60}) < 0.9 (STIFF), every positive tested endpoint fails and the construction cannot accept any step toward b. A gap condition alone is insufficient. Multi-state versions need their own mass and moment conditions.
  > (iii) [range bound] range(d) ≤ [(J_max + 1)ν + K] log(n+1). The former bound (n+K) log(n+1) fails (selecting one signal-aligned duplicate per actual block accumulates the same fit gain repeatedly in the table product); the former "unreachable below n ≈ 10¹⁷" cutoff is withdrawn. Actual production failure additionally needs a candidate set attaining the obstruction and passing preflight; the proxy-deletion production construction remains UNVERIFIED.

### CJ117 — T37 — Finite-n truth dominance and deterministic greedy repair (new conjecture, added 2026-10-28)  [conjecture]
- Source (authoritative, as written 2026-10-28): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/new_conjectures/T37_truth_dominance_greedy_repair.md`; condensation: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T37.md`; positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]; [pos 355]; [pos 370]
- Status at campaign start (verbatim, one-pager line 2):
  > CONJECTURED (not proved); NEW, added 2026-10-28 to fill the finite-n repair hole  | Rank: core (new) | Paper role: JRSS-B Thm 3 (new primary route; T24 kept as the Gibbs-path alternative; whichever closes first becomes Thm 3); Biometrika Thm 3
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T37 | Finite-n truth dominance and deterministic greedy repair (new, 2026-10-28) | core (new) | CONJECTURED (not proved); new 2026-10-28 | JRSS-B Thm 3 (new primary route); Biometrika Thm 3 | none (statement: `PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/new_conjectures/`) | whole statement |
- Statement (verbatim, the full new_conjectures file as written 2026-10-28):
  > # T37: Finite-n truth dominance and deterministic greedy repair
  >
  > **Status:** NEW conjecture, added 2026-10-28 to fill the "finite-n repair" hole. Source: `../FABLE_REVIEW.md` §2, adopted by HQ. Methodology SMC-BVS v3.0. Read with `../../theorems/00_COMMON.md`.
  >
  > **Category / rank:** core. Primary repair route for the paper's repair theorem; the Gibbs-path route T24 is the alternative.
  >
  > ## Definitions used
  > - **Local search:** the production local search. It scores every feasible flip and swap of the centre, moves to the best strict improvement, takes at most ℓ moves, and ends with a final certifying scan.
  > - **Near-truth region:** 𝓡_d = {U ∪ P : U ⊆ S₀, P ⊆ S₀ᶜ, |P| ≤ d}, with s₀ + d ≤ K.
  > - **Gains:** g(S, l) = F(S+l) − F(S) and h(S, j) = F(S−j) − F(S); swap gains are defined in the same way.
  > - **TD(d, m), truth dominance with margin m ≥ 0:**
  >   - for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊉ S₀, some missing true variable j has g(S, j) ≥ m + the gain of every other feasible move at S;
  >   - for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊋ S₀, some extra l has h(S, l) ≥ m + the gain of every other move;
  >   - at S₀, every move has gain ≤ −m.
  >
  > ## Assumptions
  > EX-A; fixed design X and truth S₀. Clause (ii) adds G; clause (iii) adds R, SE and BM-∞, with s₀ and d fixed.
  >
  > ## Precise statement
  > - **(i) Deterministic.** Assume TD(d, 0) with strict inequalities. Then from any centre S ∈ 𝓡_d, the local search with ℓ ≥ |S Δ S₀| moves monotonically to S₀ in exactly |S Δ S₀| moves, scores S₀, and reports `local_certified` at S₀. The path never leaves 𝓡_d. Hence S₀ ∈ 𝒮, and Ŝ = S₀ whenever π(S₀) > ½ (T21).
  > - **(ii) Finite n.** Under G, for fixed X, P₀(TD(d, m) fails) is at most the sum, over the ≤ 2^{s₀} C(p, d)(p + s₀p) distinct move comparisons, of P₀(a single score difference falls below m).
  >   - Each term is a one- or two-dimensional non-central Gaussian event.
  >   - Its non-centrality is (n−1)δ²_{T,l}/σ*², and its penalty is ½ log(n+1) + log[(2p−k−1)/(k+1)].
  > - **(iii) Corollary indexed by n.** Assume s₀ and d are fixed, ℓ_n = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ ≥ s₀ + d eventually, and G, R, SE and BM-∞ hold.
  >   - Then the bound in (ii) → 0, so TD(d, 0) holds with probability → 1.
  >   - Clause (i) then becomes an unconditional repair route that replaces GAIN_d, LK_d and EXIT_d.
  >
  > ## Why it should be true
  > Each gain is a monotone function of one residual projection u_{T,l}ᵀy (two for swaps).
  > - Adding a missing true variable j gains the full non-centrality (n−1)‖(P_{T+j} − P_T)μ‖².
  > - Its look-alike l captures only the r² fraction of the same signal.
  > - Once S₀ ⊆ S, every null variable has zero leakage and pays the size penalty.
  >
  > So the greedy order is "truths in, then extras out". That is T24's prescribed path without the randomness. The margin (n−1)θ²(1−r²)/(2σ²) between a true variable and its look-alike is also the proposed mechanism behind SMC-BVS's advantage in correlated designs (S3–S6 at c = 0.5).
  >
  > ## Proof route
  > - **(i):** induction on |S Δ S₀|, using TD.
  > - **(ii):**
  >   1. Write each comparison as a difference of quadratic forms in contrast coordinates (T01).
  >   2. Bound the log-ratio of the IG marginal by a Gaussian exponent, using bounded-Q_S Taylor control (as in T02's hint).
  >   3. Apply a union bound.
  > - **(iii):** plug in T03's beta-min margin.
  >
  > ## Main risks
  > - **Loose union bound.** The 2^{s₀} union in (ii) makes the finite-n number loose at s₀ = 14 (about 10 nats). A dependence-aware bound along the actual greedy path is the research part.
  > - **Move cap below the needed distance.** At n = 200, ℓ = 10 < s₀ + d = 15. The finite-n clause therefore needs either the one-extra-scan rule or a centre within 10 moves of S₀; state this.
  > - **Eligibility is not covered.** T37 does not deliver an eligible centre: some local-search centre must lie in 𝓡_d. That is T38's job.
- Fable's original proposal (verbatim, FABLE_REVIEW.md section 2, 'New conjecture T37'):
  > ### New conjecture T37: finite-n truth dominance and deterministic greedy repair
  >
  > **Setting and assumptions.** EX-A; the production local search (scan every feasible flip and swap of the centre, move to the best strict improvement, at most ℓ moves, final certifying scan). Fixed design X, truth S₀, 𝓡_d = {U ∪ P : U ⊆ S₀, P ⊆ S₀ᶜ, |P| ≤ d}, s₀ + d ≤ K. Gains g(S, l) = F(S+l) − F(S), h(S, j) = F(S−j) − F(S), swap gains likewise. **TD(d, m)** (truth dominance with margin m ≥ 0): for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊉ S₀, some missing true variable j has g(S, j) ≥ m + every other feasible move's gain at S; for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊋ S₀, some extra l has h(S, l) ≥ m + every other move's gain; at S₀ every move has gain ≤ −m. For (ii) add G.
  >
  > **Statement.** (i) [deterministic] Under TD(d, 0) with strict inequalities, from any centre S ∈ 𝓡_d the local search with ℓ ≥ |S Δ S₀| moves monotonically to S₀ in exactly |S Δ S₀| moves, scores S₀, and reports local_certified at S₀; hence S₀ ∈ 𝒮, and Ŝ = S₀ whenever π(S₀) > ½ (T21, T11(vii)). The path never leaves 𝓡_d. (ii) [finite n] Under G, for fixed X, P₀(TD(d, m) fails) ≤ Σ over the ≤ 2^{s₀} C(p, d)(p + s₀p) distinct move comparisons of P₀(a single score difference falls below m), each a one- or two-dimensional non-central Gaussian event with explicit non-centrality (n−1)δ²_{T,l}/σ*² and penalty ½ log(n+1) + log[(2p−k−1)/(k+1)]. (iii) [corollary, n-indexed] With s₀, d fixed and ℓ_n = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ ≥ s₀ + d eventually, under G, R, SE and BM-∞ the bound in (ii) → 0, so TD(d, 0) holds with probability → 1 and (i) is an unconditional repair route replacing GAIN_d, LK_d and EXIT_d.
  >
  > **Why true.** Each gain is a monotone function of one residual projection u_{T,l}ᵀy (two for swaps). Adding a missing true j at T ⊆ S₀ ∪ P gains the full non-centrality (n−1)‖(P_{T+j} − P_T)μ‖²; its look-alike l captures only the r² fraction of the same signal; once S₀ ⊆ S every null has zero leakage and pays the penalty. So the greedy order is "truths in, then extras out", which is T24's prescribed path without the randomness.
  >
  > **Proof route.** (i) by induction on |S Δ S₀| using TD. (ii) write each comparison as a quadratic-form difference in contrast coordinates (T01), bound the ν log-ratio of the IG marginal by a Gaussian exponent using the bounded-Q_S Taylor control from T02's hint, union bound. (iii) plug T03's beta-min margin.
  >
  > **Main risk.** The 2^{s₀} union in (ii) makes the finite-n number loose at s₀ = 14 (≈ 10 nats); a dependence-aware bound along the actual greedy path is the research part. Also ℓ = 10 < s₀ + d = 15 at n = 200, so the finite-n clause needs the one-extra-scan rule or a centre within 10 moves; say so. Nothing here is false as stated.
  >
  > **Where it fits.** Thm 4 (repair) in both journals; its (ii) is the paper's one finite-n statement and the mechanism behind the S3–S6 advantage; its failure event is the within-size swap of T07.

- Statement (verbatim, the full new_conjectures file as written 2026-10-28):
  > # T38: Two-regime consistency of the reported HPM (main theorem)
  >
  > **Status:** NEW conjecture, added 2026-10-28. It is a composite statement written by HQ from:
  > - Fable's Change A (`../FABLE_REVIEW.md` §1);
  > - Astra's delivery critique (`../ASTRA_REVIEW.md` §1–2).
  >
  > It replaces T26(iii) as the paper's main HPM theorem. Read with `../../theorems/00_COMMON.md`.
  >
  > **Category / rank:** core; the headline theorem.
  >
  > ## Why it is needed
  > T26 reaches the HPM through start concentration (T22(iii)). That regime does not need the sampler. In the masked regime (T27) the start gives the truth vanishing mass, and T26 says nothing. Both consultants found the same gap: **a repair theorem (T24 or T37) repairs an eligible particle or centre, but it does not deliver one.** The main theorem must contain the delivery step.
  >
  > ## Setting and assumptions
  > - **Asymptotic setting.** A triangular array with s₀ fixed, p_n ≤ n^A, B ≤ 16 and K_n = ⌊n/2⌋. The v3 budgets N_n, ℓ_n, L_n and T_n are indexed by n, as in master §I.8.
  > - **One statistical family.** All statistical premises must hold *jointly*, for the actual data-dependent block partition, on one family of designs.
  > - **Optional method tweak LS0.** Also run the local search from the start mode S̃₀.
  >   - It is deterministic and costs about ℓ·p extra scores.
  >   - It can be added after the fact to existing fits: the HPM is the best model ever scored, so extra scoring can only raise the reported HPM's score.
  >   - It is needed only if eligibility cannot be proved otherwise.
  >
  > ## Precise statement
  > By T21,
  >
  > P(no output or Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≤ P(U) + 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)] + P(Uᶜ, S₀ ∉ 𝒮),
  >
  > and T03 sends the middle term to 0. The discovery term P(Uᶜ, S₀ ∉ 𝒮) → 0 in each of two regimes:
  >
  > - **(a) Favourable regime.** Under T22(iii)'s hypotheses (EXP′, VIS, NL), Q_f π₀(S₀) → ∞. The fresh iid start draws then score S₀ by T11(iii).
  > - **(b) Masked regime.** π₀(S₀) may vanish as in T27, but the start puts mass π₀(𝓡_d) ≥ b_n on the near-truth region. This follows from T22(i) with a reference S° ∈ 𝓡_d, which need not be S₀. Then one of two routes applies:
  >   - **(b1)** TD(d, 0) holds with probability → 1 (T37), and some local-search centre lies in 𝓡_d with probability → 1. Either the best-scored model before the final search lies in 𝓡_d, or the start mode S̃₀ does and LS0 is used.
  >   - **(b2)** T24's conditions hold, and a particle in 𝓡_d is available at the terminal rounds.
  > - **(c) Cost corollary.** The expected number of score evaluations is polynomial: O(N_n T_n (p + B + 2) + ℓ_n p) under the declared budgets. Arithmetic costs follow from T32.
  >
  > Hence P(Ŝ = S₀) → 1 − limsup P(U).
  >
  > ## Not claimed
  > - Evidence or PIP accuracy in the masked regime. Those are T26(i)–(ii), favourable regime only.
  > - Any result about fits selected for having completed.
  > - Comparative superiority over other methods.
  >
  > ## Main risks
  > - **Eligibility in the masked regime.** Showing that the best-scored model, or S̃₀, lands in 𝓡_d.
  > - **Compatibility.** T22(i)'s reference bounds may not be compatible with T27's masking hypotheses on the same family.
  > - **Move budget.** At n = 200, ℓ_n is smaller than s₀ + d.
  > - **Fallback.** If (b) fails for the original method, use T39, the explicit repair-track extension.
- Fable's Change A (verbatim, FABLE_REVIEW.md section 1):
  > **Change A (matters most): Thm 6 = T26 is the wrong main theorem as written.** T26 reaches the HPM through clause (iii): start concentration makes an initial π₀ draw equal S₀ with probability → 1. A referee will ask why the SMC bridge, Gibbs rounds and local search exist, since the block-wise start already solves the problem. In the only regime where the sampler does work (the masked regime of T27, start mass p⁻ᶜ n⁻ᶜ/²), T26 says nothing. Its hypothesis list (G, R, SE, BM, VIS, NL_avg, EXP, OP-a, OP-s, CAL) is also the longest in the pool and the likeliest to be judged unverifiable.
  >
  > Restate the main theorem as a **two-regime HPM theorem** whose proof uses the moves:
  > - HPM part: for budgets indexed by n, P(Ŝ ≠ S₀ or no output) ≤ P(U) + o(1), where in the favourable regime (T22(iii)) the truth is scored by the iid start draws (T11(iii)), and in the masked regime (T27 chain, π₀(S^{(0)}) ≥ c₀) a start draw lands in 𝓡_d and the terminal repair (Thm 4) scores S₀; T21 composes; T03 supplies π(S₀) > ½.
  > - Evidence and PIP part: T26(i)–(ii) as stated, favourable regime only, with EXP named as a hypothesis.
  >
  > What this gains: the theorem then explains the method's *design*, not just its output, and the masked regime is exactly where the simulations show SMC-BVS beating the coordinate-wise competitors (S3–S6 at c = 0.5; S1 is a tie with SSL).

T26 establishes accuracy when the start already concentrates on the truth; it does not complete the masked-start repair argument.** These are different regimes, not consecutive links in one proof.

### CJ119 — T39 — Independent start-to-terminal scoring tracks with an explicit budget (contingency) (new contingency conjecture, added 2026-10-28; Astra's C37)  [conjecture]
- Source (authoritative, as written 2026-10-28): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/new_conjectures/T39_independent_repair_tracks.md`; condensation: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T39.md`; positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]; [pos 355]
- Status at campaign start (verbatim, one-pager line 2):
  > CONJECTURED (not proved); NEW contingency target; requires a METHOD EXTENSION (not run in the 2,400 fits)  | Rank: contingency (new) | Paper role: Contingency target only (use if T38(b) cannot be proved for the original method)
- Master-table row (THEORY.md section 2, verbatim):
  > | T39 | Independent start-to-terminal scoring tracks with an explicit budget (contingency) (new, 2026-10-28; Astra C37) | contingency (new) | CONJECTURED (not proved); new contingency (method extension) | Contingency target only | none (statement: `PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/new_conjectures/`) | whole statement (method extension) |
- Statement (verbatim, the full new_conjectures file as written 2026-10-28):
  > # T39: Independent start-to-terminal scoring tracks with an explicit budget (contingency)
  >
  > **Status:** NEW conjecture, added 2026-10-28 as a **contingency target**. Source: Astra's C37 (`../ASTRA_REVIEW.md` §2), renumbered T39.
  >
  > **Category / rank:** contingency. Use it only if T38(b) cannot be proved for the original method.
  >
  > **Method change.** This is a genuine algorithm extension. The existing 2,400 fits did not run it, and it would need separately labelled validation runs.
  >
  > ## Setting and assumptions
  > - **Repair tracks.** The exact target, the actual block start and the terminal hybrid kernel, plus M independent *scoring-only* repair tracks.
  >   - Each track starts from an exact π₀ draw and runs h rounds at φ = 1.
  >   - Their scores update the reported HPM. They do not feed the SMC particles, calibration, evidence or PIPs.
  >   - They use separate random streams, and all budgets are fixed before they run.
  > - **Data event.** On a data event G_n with probability ≥ 1 − δ_n:
  >   - π₀(𝓡_d) ≥ b_n > 0;
  >   - inf_{x∈𝓡_d} K₁(x, S₀) ≥ a_n > 0;
  >   - sup_{x∈𝓡_d} P_x(one-round first exit) ≤ η_n.
  > - **Sources of the bounds.** T24 or T37 supplies a_n and η_n. T22(i) supplies b_n from a reference in 𝓡_d, which need not be S₀.
  >
  > ## Precise statement
  > Let s_n = 1 − (1−a_n)^h − hη_n > 0.
  >
  > **Miss probability.** Conditional on data in G_n, for the potential uninterrupted tracks,
  >
  > P(S₀ never scored) ≤ (1 − b_n s_n)^M ≤ e^{−M b_n s_n}.
  >
  > **Budget.** Each track uses at most 1 + 2mh score evaluations, where m = p + B + 2. Choose:
  > - h = ⌈log 4 / a_n⌉, with hη_n ≤ 1/4;
  > - M = ⌈2 b_n⁻¹ log(1/ε_n)⌉.
  >
  > The miss probability is then ≤ ε_n.
  >
  > **Error bound.** Together with T21,
  >
  > P(no usable output or wrong HPM) ≤ P(U) + 2E₀[1−π(S₀)] + δ_n + ε_n.
  >
  > **Polynomial cost.** If b_n ≥ n^{−r}, a_n ≥ n^{−s} and η_n = o(a_n), the expected cost of discovery is C_setup + O(p n^{r+s}) score evaluations.
  >
  > ## Main risks
  > - **The value lies in the inputs.** The probability argument is elementary. The research work is a compatible statistical family with useful b_n and a_n, ideally one where T27 holds, so that direct iid discovery is expensive, while b_n and a_n stay bounded below.
  > - **T24's factorial constant** may make the guarantee impractical.
  > - **Role of tempering.** If the tracks explain essentially all of the selection gain, the paper must say what tempering contributes.
- Astra's original proposal C37 (verbatim, ASTRA_REVIEW.md section 2):
  > ### C37: Independent start-to-terminal scoring with an explicit budget
  >
  > **Setting and assumptions.** Retain the exact target, actual block start and terminal hybrid kernel. Add M independent *scoring-only repair tracks*: each starts from an exact π₀ draw and executes h rounds at φ = 1. Their scores update the reported HPM, but do not feed the SMC particles, calibration, evidence or PIP calculations. Use separate random streams and budgets fixed before these tracks run.
  >
  > On a data event $G_n$ of probability at least $1-\delta_n$, assume deterministic bounds
  >
  > \[
  > \pi_0(\mathcal R_d)\ge b_n>0,\qquad
  > \inf_{x\in\mathcal R_d}K_1(x,S_0)\ge a_n>0,\qquad
  > \sup_{x\in\mathcal R_d}P_x(\text{one-round first exit})\le\eta_n.
  > \]
  >
  > T24 supplies the last two bounds. For the first, T22(i) can supply $b_n$ from a reference $S^\circ\in\mathcal R_d$, using bounds on its aggregation quantities. **That reference need not be S₀**: do not impose start concentration on the truth in the masking regime. All statistical premises must hold jointly for the actual partition.
  >
  > **Precise statement.** Write $s_n=1-(1-a_n)^h-h\eta_n>0$. Conditional on data in $G_n$, for the potential uninterrupted tracks,
  >
  > \[
  > P(S_0\text{ never scored})\le(1-b_ns_n)^M\le e^{-Mb_ns_n}.
  > \]
  >
  > With $m=p+B+2$, each track uses at most $1+2mh$ score evaluations. An indefinitely continued sequence of tracks therefore has expected score count until the first truth score at most
  >
  > \[
  > C_{\rm setup}+\frac{1+2mh}{b_ns_n}.
  > \]
  >
  > The first truth score is an analysis stopping time, not an implementable stopping rule. The implemented bank uses fixed M. Choose $h=\lceil\log(4)/a_n\rceil$, require $h\eta_n\le1/4$, and take $M=\lceil2b_n^{-1}\log(1/\epsilon_n)\rceil$. Then the miss probability is at most ε_n. T21 yields
  >
  > \[
  > P(\text{no usable output or wrong HPM})
  > \le P(U)+2E_0[1-\pi(S_0)]+\delta_n+\epsilon_n.
  > \]
  >
  > If $b_n\ge n^{-r}$, $a_n\ge n^{-s}$, and $\eta_n=o(a_n)$, expected discovery costs $C_{\rm setup}+O(pn^{r+s})$ score evaluations. Arithmetic cost additionally includes T32's per-score and start-sampling costs.
  >
  > **Why plausible / proof route.** Condition on entering the basin, apply T24's survival-and-repair bound, multiply independent track failure probabilities, then sum a geometric tail. Use T22's normalized reference bound and T32 for the remaining inputs. The substantive proof work is a compatible statistical family, ideally one satisfying T27 where direct iid discovery is expensive but $b_n,a_n$ stay bounded below.
  >
  > **Main risk.** The probability calculation is elementary; without that family and useful constants this is only bookkeeping. T24's factorial entrance constant may make the guarantee impractical. The tracks are a genuine algorithm extension, requiring separately labelled validation; the existing 2,400 fits did not run them. If they explain essentially all selection gains, the paper must also address what tempering contributes.
  >
  > **Paper placement.** Immediately after T24 and before T21; no claim of PIP/evidence accuracy from these tracks. This is the only new conjecture I recommend.

  > - M independent scoring-only repair tracks, each started from an exact pi0 draw and run h rounds at phi = 1; their scores update the reported HPM but feed neither the SMC particles, calibration, evidence nor PIPs; separate streams; budgets fixed beforehand. On a data event G_n of probability >= 1 - delta_n: pi0(R_d) >= b_n, inf_{x in R_d} K_1(x, S0) >= a_n, sup_{x in R_d} P_x(one-round first exit) <= eta_n (a_n, eta_n from T24 or T37; b_n from T22(i)).
  > - With s_n = 1 - (1 - a_n)^h - h eta_n > 0: P(S0 never scored | G_n) <= (1 - b_n s_n)^M <= exp(-M b_n s_n). Each track uses at most 1 + 2mh score evaluations (m = p + B + 2); choosing h = ceil(log 4 / a_n) with h eta_n <= 1/4 and M = ceil(2 b_n^-1 log(1/eps_n)) gives miss probability <= eps_n. With T21: P(no usable output or wrong HPM) <= P(U) + 2 E0[1 - pi(S0)] + delta_n + eps_n. If b_n >= n^-r, a_n >= n^-s, eta_n = o(a_n), expected discovery cost is C_setup + O(p n^(r+s)) score evaluations.

### CJ122 — PW2 (one-step second-moment bound for the actual particle system)  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T25iv_T19_crossing_evidence/STATEMENT.md` section 'PW2 hypothesis and conclusion'; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md` section 3; positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]
- Status at campaign start: OPEN hypothesis: 'Not proved for the actual method. The optional partial work in T25iv_T19_crossing_evidence/helpers/OPTIONAL_PW2.md is unreviewed' (LOCKED_PROOFS.md section B). Audit finding E5: T25(iv) is equivalent to the PW2 recursion and adds no control beyond it.
- Statement (verbatim, T25(iv) STATEMENT.md; PW2 hypothesis and conclusion):
  > Let a_t and nu_t, 1<=t<=T, be finite nonnegative upper-bound constants, fixed given c (they may depend on the data, calibration and N). This spells out the rate-coefficient/slack convention in PW2. Assume PW2 for every t:
  >
  > E_c[W_{t-1}^2 { (qhat_{t-1}(g_t))^2 - 1 }]
  > <= (a_t/N) E_c[W_{t-1}^2] + nu_t.
  >
  > Then, with an empty product equal to 1,
  >
  > B_T := product_{t=1}^T (1+a_t/N) - 1
  > + sum_{s=1}^T nu_s product_{t=s+1}^T (1+a_t/N)
  >
  > satisfies Var_c(W_T) <= B_T.
  >
  > For four final islands r=1,...,4, let W_{r,T}=Zhat_{r,T}/Z and W_pool=(1/4)sum_r W_{r,T}=Zhat/Z. When PW2 holds with the same bounds for each island, Var_c(W_pool) <= B_T/4. This divides the **whole** bound, including the slack sum, by four; N remains N_e, not 4N_e.
  >
  > The constants need not be uniform over calibrations for this conditional statement. No RET, OCC, COVER, BW2, or BW_W premise is used to establish PW2 here. No statement about measured constants is a hypothesis of the theorem.
- 00_COMMON row (verbatim):
  > | PW2 | With W_t = Ẑ_t/Z_t: E[W²_{t−1}{(q̂_{t−1}g_t)² − 1}] ≤ (a_t/N)EW²_{t−1} + ν_t with controlled slack. | New research obligation |

### CJ123 — BASIN(R, r0, a, eta, rho, delta) (basin condition)  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T23_T18_basin_prefix/STATEMENT.md` section 2; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md` section 3; positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]
- Status at campaign start: OPEN hypothesis: 'Not proved. Its statistical instances are T23(iii)-(v), not in the register' (LOCKED_PROOFS.md section B). Used for T23(ii-c), (ii-d).
- Statement (verbatim, T23 STATEMENT.md section 2):
  > - **BASIN(𝓡, r₀, a, η, ρ, δ)**, given 𝓒: 𝓡 ⊆ Ω with S₀ ∈ 𝓡; an integer r₀ ≥ 1; numbers a, η, ρ ∈ [0,1], δ ≥ 0, such that
  >   - (entrance) K₁^{r₀}(x, {S₀}) ≥ a for every x ∈ 𝓡;
  >   - (basin exit) for every x ∈ 𝓡, the probability that a round started at x has some state outside 𝓡 on its path X⁽¹⁾, …, X⁽ᵐ⁾ is ≤ η;
  >   - (truth departure) the probability that a round started at S₀ has some state ≠ S₀ on its path X⁽¹⁾, …, X⁽ᵐ⁾ is ≤ ρ;
  >   - (initial occupancy) for every island r, E_𝓒[ N⁻¹ Σ_i 1{X_{i,0} ∉ 𝓡} ] ≤ δ.
- Readings fixed in the statement (verbatim, section 5):
  > 1. **ρ is the whole-round departure probability from S₀.** The theorem file says "truth prefix-departure ≤ ρ" and, in (iii), bounds ρ by summing first-departure probabilities over all p + B + 2 labels of a round. B_{i,h} counts a departure anywhere in the round. The whole-round reading is the one consistent with both.
  > 2. **η is the one-round first-exit probability from 𝓡,** maximised over starts in 𝓡 (path version). The proof uses only its consequence K₁(x, 𝓡ᶜ) ≤ η for x ∈ 𝓡, so the end-of-round version would also suffice.
  > 3. **Terminal rounds have no resampling** (the method resamples after every reweighting; there is no reweighting at φ = 1 after stage T). Particle identities persist through the L + 4 terminal rounds.
  > 4. **δ is per island** (islands are i.i.d. given 𝓒 under EX-S and CAL, so a bound for one island holds for all).
  > 5. "MPM error" means the event MPM̂ ≠ S₀.
- 00_COMMON row (verbatim):
  > | BASIN(𝓡, r₀, a, η, ρ, δ) | Given 𝓒: 𝓡 ∋ S₀; inf_{x∈𝓡}K₁^{r₀}(x, S₀) ≥ a; one-round basin first exit ≤ η; truth prefix-departure ≤ ρ; expected stage-T outside fraction ≤ δ. | New abstract conditions |

### CJ124 — COVER(W, eps_C) and pool avoidance  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T13_T10_restricted_ESS/STATEMENT.md`; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md` section 3; positions: [pos 119]
- Status at campaign start: Explicit premise of T13 clauses (ii), (iii), (iv); not a theorem to be proved but a condition that the actual run may or may not satisfy ('Coverage on [0,1] alone is not enough').
- Definition (verbatim, T13 STATEMENT.md section 0):
  > - **COVER(W, ε_C)**, for nonempty W ⊆ Ω, a grid, and **0 ≤ ε_C < 1**: q_ψ(W) ≥ 1 − ε_C for every ψ ∈ 𝓔_grid.
- Where it is a premise: T13 (ii) (verbatim, T13 STATEMENT.md section 1):
  > **(ii) Coverage corollary.**
  > (a) Let 0 ≤ ε_C < 1. If (u, v) is accepted and a(u) ≥ 1 − ε_C and a(w) ≥ 1 − ε_C, then 1 + χ²(q_v ‖ q_u) ≤ 10/(9(1 − ε_C)²).
  > (b) Assume EX-A. Let (φ_t)_{t=0}^T be the output of a successful candidate-grid construction run with candidate set V (in particular the frozen grid of a calibration, paired with the V of the construction that produced it). Then every interval (φ_{t−1}, φ_t) is accepted; its evaluation points φ_{t−1}, φ_t, w_t lie in 𝓔_grid; and if COVER(V, ε_C) holds, then 1 + χ²(q_{φ_t} ‖ q_{φ_{t−1}}) ≤ 10/(9(1 − ε_C)²) for every t = 1, …, T.
  > (c) Coverage on [0, 1] alone does not supply the hypothesis of (a) when w_t > 1: there is a method-class witness with grid T = 1 (φ₀ = 0, φ₁ = 1, w₁ = 2) such that, with ε_C = 0.1, the interval (0, 1) is accepted and q_ψ(V) ≥ 1 − ε_C for every ψ ∈ [0, 1], but q_{w₁}(V) < 1 − ε_C and 1 + χ²(q₁ ‖ q₀) > 10/(9(1 − ε_C)²).
  > (d) The largest w_t is not automatically the worst coverage point: there is a method-class witness with grid T = 2 (both intervals accepted) such that the minimum of ψ ↦ q_ψ(V) over 𝓔_grid is attained only at φ₀, not at max_t w_t, and the minimum over {w₁, …, w_T} is not attained at max_t w_t.
- Pool avoidance (verbatim, T13 STATEMENT.md section 1 (iv)(a)):
  > (a) Let V = V(𝒫) be of the method's form. If 𝒫 ∩ 𝓜 = ∅ (pool avoidance), then V ∩ 𝓜 = ∅. Pool avoidance holds, in particular, when calibration never scores 𝓜 and every member of 𝒫 was scored by the calibration or belongs to an inherited set of scored models (tables, leaders carried across tiers) that is assumed to avoid 𝓜.
- 00_COMMON row (verbatim):
  > | COVER(W, ε_C) | q_ψ(W) ≥ 1 − ε_C at every ψ ∈ 𝓔_grid. | New full-space coverage |

### CJ125 — H1-H4 of T27(i), in particular H2 (sequential ratio law) and H3 (normalised reference-mass lower bound)  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T27i_T20C_cancellation_budget/STATEMENT.md` section 'Every premise'; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/LOCKED_PROOFS.md` section B; positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 355]
- Status at campaign start: H2 and H3: OPEN statistical inputs ('Statistical inputs, not proved'); H1 is a definition; H4 collects EX-A, EX-S, CAL and successful execution (LOCKED_PROOFS.md section B).
- Statement (verbatim, T27(i) STATEMENT.md 'Every premise'):
  > H1. **Fixed feasible completion chain.** Fix integers s>=0 and c>=1. There is a specified data-measurable chain S^(0) subset ... subset S^(c)=S_0 with |S^(0)|=s and S^(i+1)=S^(i) union {l_i}, l_i not in S^(i), for i=0,...,c-1. Every state is feasible and |S_0|=s+c<=K eventually. Deterministic chains are included. Let b_i be the block of l_i and T_i=S^(i) intersect C_{b_i}.
  >
  > H2. **Joint sequential ratio law, assumed statistical input.** For this specified chain,
  >
  >     E_{n,i}=log[r_{b_i}(T_i union {l_i})/r_{b_i}(T_i)]+(1/2)log n,
  >     max_{0<=i<c}|E_{n,i}|=O_{P_0}(1).
  >
  > This is two-sided log tightness jointly at the successive states. A data-selected chain must itself satisfy this premise; no uniform guarantee over all selection rules is asserted. The remainders need not be independent. Cancellation at an initial table state alone does not assert H2.
  >
  > H3. **Normalized reference-mass lower bound, assumed statistical input.** A deterministic constant c_0 in (0,1] satisfies P_0{pi_0(S^(0))>=c_0}->1. This premise includes the full capped composite normalizer. A lower bound on an unnormalized table product does not replace it.
  >
  > H4. **Retained operational assumptions.** EX-A: exact scores, convolutions, probabilities, comparisons. EX-S: independent ideal uniform streams with the method's stream separation. CAL: calibration uses streams 0-9 only, final streams 10-13 are fresh and independent of calibration, and escalation precedes final randomness. Successful final execution: the final run completes its frozen schedule. These are retained as the theorem file's operational setting; the mass implication uses the exact start definition and H1-H3 and is independent of final-run randomness. No probability-of-completion assertion is added. In particular no stochastic-order statement conditioned on completion or diagnostics is claimed.
  >
  > The scaling p asymptotic to n^a is retained, although the mass implication itself only needs p>=s+c and fixed s,c. G/R, Gaussianity, eigenvalue or beta-min assumptions are not silently used to derive H2 or H3.

### CJ127 — VIS (visibility), NL_eta (leakage bound), NL_avg(kappa) (rate condition) and the 00_COMMON variants TL, TL_avg  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T22iii_T16_start_aggregation/STATEMENT.md` section 2; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md` section 3; positions: [pos 119]; [pos 156]; [pos 355]
- Status at campaign start: OPEN design/regime conditions, not proved: 'Regime or design conditions, not proved' (LOCKED_PROOFS.md section B). THEORY.md 5.3: 'VIS and NL_eta are doubtful; EXP', NL_avg and BM-infinity are unknown'.
- Statement (verbatim, T22(iii) STATEMENT.md section 2: VIS, NL_eta):
  > **VIS.** There is a deterministic M_n^V → ∞ such that for every b and T ⊆ C_b with U_b* ⊄ T,
  >
  >     ‖(P_{T∪U_b*}−P_T)μ‖² ≥ M_n^V v_T log n.
  >
  > **NL_η.** For a fixed 0 ≤ η < (√(2A+1)−√(2A))², every (b,T,l) ∈ L_n satisfies δ_{T,l}² ≤ ησ² log n. If L_n is empty this condition is vacuous.
- Rate parameter NL_avg(kappa) (verbatim, T22(iii) STATEMENT.md section 2):
  > **Rate parameter (NL_avg(κ)).** Fix ε₀ > 0 and h_n = √(2(A+ε₀)log n). For a leakage comparison put
  >
  >     E_{T,l} = min{δ_{T,l}²/(2Δ_T),
  >                    δ_{T,l}²/(2v_T)+|δ_{T,l}|σh_n/v_T},
  >
  > with E_{T,l}=0 if δ_{T,l}=0 (if Δ_T=0 then δ_{T,l}=0). The asserted rate holds for every fixed κ>0 for which, eventually, when p>s₀,
  >
  >     (p−s₀)⁻¹ Σ_{l∉S₀} max_{U*_{b(l)}⊆T⊆C_{b(l)}∖{l}} exp(E_{T,l})
  >        ≤ n^(1/2−κ).                                      [NL_avg(κ)]
  >
  > For p=s₀ use no average condition. In particular NL_η supplies this condition for any ε₀>0 and κ>0 satisfying
  >
  >     κ ≤ 1/2 − η/2 − √(2η(A+ε₀)).
  >
  > The strict threshold on η guarantees such positive choices. Equivalently, when η>0, every 0<κ<1/2−η/2−√(2Aη) is supplied by a sufficiently small fixed ε₀>0. Exact zero leakage (η=0) permits κ=1/2. NL_avg is the source theorem's rate condition, with NL_η additionally ensuring the small-partial-R² regime for EXP′.
- Leakage quantities (verbatim, 00_COMMON section 2):
