### CJ128 — SR (both Gibbs configurations are scored) and GUARD (stop-only resource coupling)  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md` section 3 (SR); `campaign/HQ/SR_AUDIT.md`; `W2-BOOK/PROOF.md` section 0.1 (GUARD); `T38-RECORD/REGISTRY_v2.md` D (implementation facts); positions: [pos 540]; [pos 542]; [pos 551]; [pos 580]
- Status at campaign start: SR: declared reading 'Scoring reading of M sections 6.5, 6.10 (to be confirmed by Felipe)' (00_COMMON). It is an implementation hypothesis, not an H-xx label. GUARD: did not exist before the campaign (introduced by W2-BOOK).
- SR as declared before the campaign (00_COMMON row, verbatim):
  > | SR | Each Gibbs update evaluates both feasible configurations (incl. the current one); both count as scored. | Scoring reading of M §§6.5, 6.10 (to be confirmed by Felipe) |
- SR in T21 (verbatim, T21 STATEMENT.md section 1):
  > SR means both feasible configurations given X_pre-j minus {j} are evaluated and counted as scored.
- HQ's SR audit of 2026-11-02 (campaign/HQ/SR_AUDIT.md, verbatim):
  > # SR audit: "both Gibbs configurations count as scored" (HQ, 2026-11-02)
  >
  > **Verdict: SR holds in the deployed engine (code v2.1 core in `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/cpp/`).** Felipe delegated this confirmation to HQ.
  >
  > ## What SR asserts
  > Every model that a Gibbs step at coordinate j looks at, namely the current state S and the flipped state S Δ {j}, is a scored model. In particular it reaches the HPM store, the same as any other evaluated model. The proofs that lean on SR are D2 (W1-T38E), Theorem B and its corollaries (W1-T24G), T21 routes (d)/(e′), and T38.
  >
  > ## Evidence (file:line)
  > 1. `v3_engine.h:113–132`, `step_gibbs`:
  >    - it calls `held(P, ME_GIBBS_HELD)` on the current state;
  >    - for a feasible flip, it builds `tmpQ = S Δ {j}` and calls `eval(tmpQ, ME_GIBBS_FLIP)` **before** the accept draw. The flipped configuration is therefore evaluated whether or not the move is taken, and the comment at :112 states SR explicitly;
  >    - an infeasible addition (|S| = K and j ∉ S) is not evaluated. This is consistent with SR's "feasible configurations".
  > 2. `v3_engine.h:87–100`, `eval`: every evaluation with `emit = true` (the default) calls `led->event(...)` with `is_fresh = fresh || !cache`. **No call site passes `emit = false`** (grep over `cpp/`).
  > 3. `v3_ledger.h`, `Ledger::event`: `offer_stores → offer_hpm` runs on fresh evaluations. Cache hits and held states are not re-offered, because they were offered when first evaluated in the same run context:
  >    - the cache is inserted only inside `eval`, which always emits;
  >    - an evicted model is re-evaluated as fresh and offered again, which is harmless;
  >    - the HPM tie rule (`hpm_better`) applies.
  > 4. **Every state a particle can enter is evaluated on entry:**
  >    - initial draws: `eval(P[i], ME_INIT)` (:289–291);
  >    - Gibbs flips: `P = tmpQ` after `eval` (:131);
  >    - uniform and neighbour swaps, and independence moves: `eval` then `P = tmpQ` (:158, :179, :186–191).
  >
  >    So a `held` current state has always been offered before.
  > 5. **Calibration → final run.** Calibration runs in its own context, `CalState`, with its own cache and ledger (`v3_core.cpp:553–582`). Its scored models and its HPM are passed through `frozen$inherited` (`v3_calib.R:155, 168`) and offered to the final run's stores and HPM with provenance "inherited" (`v3_core.cpp:409–421`). The reported HPM is therefore the best over calibration plus the final run.
  >
  > ## Caveats (stated, not defects)
  > - **SR covers the *logical* scored set.** "Scored" in the theorems means "offered to the HPM store at least once in the fit". That is what the code does.
  > - **LS0 must follow the same discipline:** emit its centre S̃₀ through `eval` (a score event) before searching (the W3-VT38E caveat).
  > - **This is HQ's read of the code, not an independent audit.** W5-LOCKBOOK includes a GUARD/OUT/SR code audit; its verdict supersedes this note if they differ.
  >
  > ## Decision recorded
  > **LS0: APPROVED by Felipe (2026-11-02), conditional on O-LS0's data check.** O-LS0 must show that on the 2,400 regenerated datasets LS0 changes few or no reported HPMs, never turns a correct report into an incorrect one beyond posterior-mode corrections, and costs a negligible amount of compute.
  > - Presentation: as part of the method (a final local search from both the best-scored model and the start mode), with T38 + LS0 as the main theorem and the no-LS0 version as a conditional remark.
  > - Implementation: emit the centre, use the HPM tie rule, label mechanisms; whether to run to certification is decided with O-LS0's data.
- GUARD as stated by W2-BOOK on 2026-11-02 (campaign origin, not pre-campaign; verbatim, W2-BOOK/PROOF.md):
  > **Hypothesis GUARD (stop-only coupling).** On 𝒢^c, st = st̄, and every reported output equals the corresponding
  > component of R̄.
  >
  > *Basis for GUARD.* It is an implementation fact, read from the code on 2026-11-02. It is not a theorem.
  > - `Scripts/SMC_BVS/core/cpp/v3_runtime.h`: `RuntimeGuard::check` reads `std::chrono::steady_clock` only. It consumes
  >   no random number and changes no setting.
  > - `v3_engine.h` (around line 335): the check runs after every bridge stage of an island. On a stop, the island returns
  >   `partial`.
  > - `v3_core.cpp` `cpp_final_run`: the islands run sequentially, island r on `seed_stream(seed, 9+r)`. A partial island
  >   sets `resource_limit`. After the four islands and the final local search there is one more check, and a stop there
  >   also sets `resource_limit`.
  > - The preflight reads (n, p, K, N_e, allocation) and, on the exact branch, a timing measurement. It reads no stream.
  >
  > On 𝒢^c no check fired, so the computation is the uninterrupted one. A same-seed replay at a larger allocation (the
  > D61 reproduction spot-check) is the empirical test of GUARD: on completed fits it should give bitwise-identical
  > outputs.
  >
  > **Finality.** GUARD says nothing about the law of 𝒢 given R̄. That law is unknown and design dependent.
- Registry code rows (REGISTRY_v2 section D, verbatim):
  > | `GUARD` | Stop-only resource guard: on 𝒪 every reported output equals the potential uninterrupted run's. | W2-BOOK (code reading of v3_runtime.h, v3_engine.h, v3_core.cpp); W5-LOCKBOOK audit in progress, no REPORT; A-REV5: RuntimeGuard::check reads elapsed/operation time, uses no RNG and no statistical setting (supports the stop-only coupling); A-REV8 E2: diagnostics differ, so the transfer holds for statistical outputs only | IMPLEMENTATION FACT — statistical stop-only coupling supported by two cross-family code readings (A-REV5, A-REV8); literal 'every output equals' ERROR (A-REV4, A-REV8) |
  > | `SR` | Both Gibbs configurations (held and flipped) are scored and offered to the HPM store. | HQ SR_AUDIT.md (holds in engine, file:line evidence); W3-VT38E, W2-VT24G agree; A-REV7: SR_AUDIT 'substantively correct'; its blanket 'no call passes emit = false' is too strong (v3_core.cpp:447,610,657 pass false for already-scored HPM centres) | IMPLEMENTATION FACT — HQ read, confirmed in substance by a cross-family reading (A-REV7) |
- W5-LOCKBOOK audit lemma IMPL-GUARD (verbatim):
  > **Lemma IMPL-GUARD.** For every input, seed and clock path: if the fit's status is not `resource_limit`, then the
  > status and every *statistical* output of the fit (HPM, its F and provenance, near-tie list, top/leader stores,
  > Ẑ_r, Ẑ, 0.05Ẑ, primary PIPs, MPM, flags E1–E3/low-ESS/local_limit/near_tie_truncated, `local_certified`, score
  > counters, the frozen object 𝓒 and the calibration archive) are those of R̄. Only the fields `timings`, `seconds_*`,
  > `runtime_guard` and `peak_memory_kb` (operational metadata) can differ. On 𝒢, the fit returns
  > `estimates_available = FALSE` and `hpm_incomplete = TRUE`.

- Depends on: CJ130 (EX-A, EX-S, CAL)

### CJ129 — TD(d, m) (truth dominance with margin m) and the near-truth region R_d  [hypothesis]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/new_conjectures/T37_truth_dominance_greedy_repair.md` (definitions); `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/FABLE_REVIEW.md` section 2; positions: [pos 156]; [pos 178]; [pos 355]
- Status at campaign start: Conditional definition inside the new conjecture T37: a deterministic condition to be shown to hold w.p. -> 1. Preliminary data of 2026-11-02: TD held strictly in 0 of 95 sampled cases (THEORY_PRIORITIES.md section 5; see CE103).
- Definition as written 2026-10-28 (verbatim, T37 file 'Definitions used'):
  > - **Local search:** the production local search. It scores every feasible flip and swap of the centre, moves to the best strict improvement, takes at most ℓ moves, and ends with a final certifying scan.
  > - **Near-truth region:** 𝓡_d = {U ∪ P : U ⊆ S₀, P ⊆ S₀ᶜ, |P| ≤ d}, with s₀ + d ≤ K.
  > - **Gains:** g(S, l) = F(S+l) − F(S) and h(S, j) = F(S−j) − F(S); swap gains are defined in the same way.
  > - **TD(d, m), truth dominance with margin m ≥ 0:**
  >   - for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊉ S₀, some missing true variable j has g(S, j) ≥ m + the gain of every other feasible move at S;
  >   - for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊋ S₀, some extra l has h(S, l) ≥ m + the gain of every other move;
  >   - at S₀, every move has gain ≤ −m.
- Fable's original wording (verbatim, FABLE_REVIEW.md section 2):
  > **Setting and assumptions.** EX-A; the production local search (scan every feasible flip and swap of the centre, move to the best strict improvement, at most ℓ moves, final certifying scan). Fixed design X, truth S₀, 𝓡_d = {U ∪ P : U ⊆ S₀, P ⊆ S₀ᶜ, |P| ≤ d}, s₀ + d ≤ K. Gains g(S, l) = F(S+l) − F(S), h(S, j) = F(S−j) − F(S), swap gains likewise. **TD(d, m)** (truth dominance with margin m ≥ 0): for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊉ S₀, some missing true variable j has g(S, j) ≥ m + every other feasible move's gain at S; for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊋ S₀, some extra l has h(S, l) ≥ m + every other move's gain; at S₀ every move has gain ≤ −m. For (ii) add G.
- Registry D 'Retired / refuted statements' row (verbatim):

#### Part E. Pre-campaign claims later refuted, corrected or dropped

### RF101 — Literal T37: truth dominance TD(d, m) and clause (i), as written on 2026-10-28  [refuted claim]
- Source (claim as written before the campaign): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/new_conjectures/T37_truth_dominance_greedy_repair.md`; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/PAPER_SELECTION_20261028/FABLE_REVIEW.md` section 2; `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/THEORY_PRIORITIES.md` Thm 3 and section 5; positions: [pos 150]; [pos 156]; [pos 178]; [pos 355]; [pos 370]
- The claim as written 2026-10-28 (verbatim; new_conjectures/T37: Definitions used):
  > - **Local search:** the production local search. It scores every feasible flip and swap of the centre, moves to the best strict improvement, takes at most ℓ moves, and ends with a final certifying scan.
  > - **Near-truth region:** 𝓡_d = {U ∪ P : U ⊆ S₀, P ⊆ S₀ᶜ, |P| ≤ d}, with s₀ + d ≤ K.
  > - **Gains:** g(S, l) = F(S+l) − F(S) and h(S, j) = F(S−j) − F(S); swap gains are defined in the same way.
  > - **TD(d, m), truth dominance with margin m ≥ 0:**
  >   - for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊉ S₀, some missing true variable j has g(S, j) ≥ m + the gain of every other feasible move at S;
  >   - for every S ∈ 𝓡_d with S ⊋ S₀, some extra l has h(S, l) ≥ m + the gain of every other move;
  >   - at S₀, every move has gain ≤ −m.
- The claim as written 2026-10-28 (verbatim; new_conjectures/T37: Precise statement):
  > - **(i) Deterministic.** Assume TD(d, 0) with strict inequalities. Then from any centre S ∈ 𝓡_d, the local search with ℓ ≥ |S Δ S₀| moves monotonically to S₀ in exactly |S Δ S₀| moves, scores S₀, and reports `local_certified` at S₀. The path never leaves 𝓡_d. Hence S₀ ∈ 𝒮, and Ŝ = S₀ whenever π(S₀) > ½ (T21).
  > - **(ii) Finite n.** Under G, for fixed X, P₀(TD(d, m) fails) is at most the sum, over the ≤ 2^{s₀} C(p, d)(p + s₀p) distinct move comparisons, of P₀(a single score difference falls below m).
  >   - Each term is a one- or two-dimensional non-central Gaussian event.
  >   - Its non-centrality is (n−1)δ²_{T,l}/σ*², and its penalty is ½ log(n+1) + log[(2p−k−1)/(k+1)].
  > - **(iii) Corollary indexed by n.** Assume s₀ and d are fixed, ℓ_n = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ ≥ s₀ + d eventually, and G, R, SE and BM-∞ hold.
  >   - Then the bound in (ii) → 0, so TD(d, 0) holds with probability → 1.
  >   - Clause (i) then becomes an unconditional repair route that replaces GAIN_d, LK_d and EXIT_d.
- Fable's own risk assessment when proposing it (verbatim, FABLE_REVIEW.md section 2):
  > **Main risk.** The 2^{s₀} union in (ii) makes the finite-n number loose at s₀ = 14 (≈ 10 nats); a dependence-aware bound along the actual greedy path is the research part. Also ℓ = 10 < s₀ + d = 15 at n = 200, so the finite-n clause needs the one-extra-scan rule or a centre within 10 moves; say so. Nothing here is false as stated.
- Pre-campaign data already flagging it (verbatim, THEORY_PRIORITIES.md section 5, 2026-11-02):
  > - **T37's literal truth-dominance condition fails generically.**
  >   - In the d = 0 audit, TD held strictly in 0 of 95 sampled cases (partial sample of 196); S₀ was a strict local maximum in about half.
  >   - The "toward S₀" variant is **open**: in this partial audit it did not separate from the literal one.
  >   - This matches the low-p finding (D18) that the literal TD fails whenever a swap bringing in a missing truth is available.
- HQ's pre-campaign summary (verbatim, [pos 178]):
  > - **The literal form of T37 fails** whenever a swap that brings in a missing true variable is available (decision D18).
- Refutation, registry D 'Retired / refuted statements' row (verbatim):

  > W7-SEP (`theory/W7-SEP` · `REPORT.md` §1, §5; `PROOF.md` §4.2) tested the planned claim that "start-only methods fail; the tempering bridge is needed". On the paper's own masked family LH, that claim is **false**.
  > - **Proposition GU (greedy universality)** is PROVED (candidate; not XF reviewed; it uses W4-T38FULL Lemma M, which is same-family VERIFIED only). Its setting: exact-Gram designs with an isolated relevant set R, SE on R and fixed signals. Its conclusion: the production local search, started at **any** C ⊆ R, reaches, scores and certifies S₀ with probability → 1, in a bounded number of moves.
  > - **Corollary GU-LH** (COUNTEREXAMPLE to the task's claim (a), by proof). On LH, start-only discovery plus the production local search (that is, LS0) scores S₀ with probability → 1. The same held numerically in 386/386 replicates.
  > - W7-SEP §1 item 4: on LH there is **no separation between the tempering bridge and a single greedy search from the start mode**.
- What remains true (verbatim, AMENDMENTS_20261102.md):
  > ### What is still true, and is the defensible claim
  > **Moving off the start is needed.**
  > - iid start draws alone fail in the masked regime: T27(i); R-T20(i).
  > - W7-SEP Theorem SEP(A)/(B) (PROVED, candidate) makes this sharp on LH. iid discovery, and one-shot importance reweighting, need Q* = p^c n^{c/2} draws.
  >
  > **v3's moves provide the move off the start.** Each of the following is a sufficient discovery route; none is shown to be uniquely necessary:
  > - bridge Gibbs flips;
  > - the terminal rounds (O-BGIBBS Theorem BG3: PROVED for the original method on LH with p fixed; Prop. LH-lock is a PROOF SKETCH);
  > - the local search, including LS0 (W7-SEP Prop. GU; T38(b1-LH)).
  >
  > **The bridge's own role** is to produce calibrated evidence and PIPs (T12, T26) and the HPM ledger.
- Registry D row (verbatim):
  > | 'Tempering / the sampler is needed for discovery in the masked regime' | W7-SEP Prop. GU / Cor. GU-LH: one greedy search from the start mode suffices on LH; no bridge-vs-search separation | 'moving off the start is needed' (E-SPINE; T38-RECORD v3 Remark 6) |
- HQ's announcement (verbatim, [pos 796]):
  > - **A spine claim was refuted:** W7-SEP showed that "tempering is needed" is false on our own family. The defensible version is "moving off the start is needed".
- Replaced by: 'moving off the start is needed' (E-SPINE; T38-RECORD v3 Remark 6): TH380 (SEP-A) / TH382 (SEP-B) (iid discovery and one-shot importance reweighting need Q* = p^c n^(c/2) draws), TH388 (SEP-GU) Prop. GU and Cor. GU-LH (W7-SEP, Theme 11), TH258 (OBG-BG3) terminal Gibbs rounds (O-BGIBBS).
- Status history: planned spine claim of the HQ campaign ([pos 717]: 'proof that the bridge is needed') -> W7-SEP tested it and found it false on LH (Prop. GU PROVED candidate; A-REV7 VERIFIED as a greedy best-neighbour theorem, A-REV9 GAP because Lemma M not re-audited there) -> HQ [pos 796] -> E-SPINE PR #1 ([pos 805], [pos 850]) amends the main docs (not merged at the time).

### CE103 — Pre-campaign data: literal truth dominance TD(d,0) held strictly in 0 of 95 sampled cases; 541 fits with search centre in R_2 but never S0  [counterexample]
- Source: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/THEORY_PRIORITIES.md` section 5 (2026-11-02, preliminary); positions: [pos 150]; [pos 178]
- Verbatim (THEORY_PRIORITIES.md section 5, bullets):
  > - **The HPM is delivered by the Gibbs/swap moves, not by the local search.**
  >   - About 98% of fresh scores come from Gibbs flips (≈ 1.7% neighbour swaps); the final local search repaired 0 fits.
  >   - In 541 fits the search centre was in 𝓡₂ but not S₀, and it never returned S₀.
  >   - This questions T37's premise that the *local search* is the repair route at n = 200, and favours a Gibbs-path route (T24-type) or a restated T37.
  > - **All misses are posterior misses, none are search misses.** Every completed wrong HPM has F(S₀) ≤ F(HPM) (565 posterior misses, 6 no-output, 0 search misses).
  >   - At c = 1 they are mostly supersets of S₀.
  >   - At c = 0.5 they are mostly same-size swaps and subsets.
  >   - This points the open work at the **statistical half** (T03/T02 restatement, T07's swap ceiling) rather than at discovery.
  > - **T37's literal truth-dominance condition fails generically.**
  >   - In the d = 0 audit, TD held strictly in 0 of 95 sampled cases (partial sample of 196); S₀ was a strict local maximum in about half.
  >   - The "toward S₀" variant is **open**: in this partial audit it did not separate from the literal one.
  >   - This matches the low-p finding (D18) that the literal TD fails whenever a swap bringing in a missing truth is available.

### CE107 — P8: counterexample to the T22(iv) 'existence of usable upper bounds' claim  [counterexample]
- Source: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/DROPPED.md`; possibly related legacy `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/legacy_pre_v3/elementary_III/PROOF.md` Example 2.3a; positions: pre-campaign; [pos 114]
- Verbatim (DROPPED.md):
  > - T22(iv) existence claim for usable upper bounds: false as stated (P8 counterexample). LF.
- Possibly the same P8 (legacy pre-v3 project, verbatim, elementary_III/PROOF.md Example 2.3a):
  > **Example 2.3a (the literal (iii) fails with ties, or without $U\ge Z$).** Let $n=p=1$, $X=(1)$ (standardised: $\|x_1\|^2=1=n$), $y=0$ and $k_{\max}=1$. Then $Q_\emptyset=Q_{\{1\}}=0$ and $D_{\{1\}}=h(1)=\tfrac32$ (Lemma 2.1(a) with $G_{\{1\}}=(1)$), so $m(\{1\})=m(\emptyset)\sqrt{2/3}$.
  > (a) *Ties.* Take $w(0)=1$ and $w(1)=\sqrt{3/2}$. Then $p(\emptyset)m(\emptyset)=p(\{1\})m(\{1\})$: both models are global maximisers, and with the order $\emptyset\prec\{1\}$ the global HPM is $\emptyset$. Take $V=\{\emptyset,\{1\}\}$, $U=Z$ and $\hat S=\{1\}\in\arg\max_V$. The hypothesis $U-Z_V=0<p(\hat S)m(\hat S)$ holds, but $\hat S$ is not the global HPM. Theorem 2.3's conclusion does hold: $\hat S$ is a global maximiser, and the HPM over $V$, which is $\emptyset$, is the global HPM.
  > (b) *$U<Z$.* Take $w(0)=w(1)=1$, so that $p(\emptyset)m(\emptyset)>p(\{1\})m(\{1\})>0$ and the global HPM is $\emptyset$. Take $V=\{\{1\}\}$, $\hat S=\{1\}$ and $U=Z_V<Z$. Then $U-Z_V=0<p(\hat S)m(\hat S)$, but $\hat S$ is not even a global maximiser. So the $U$ of (iii) must be the $U\ge Z$ of (ii).
  > (Both found by the round-1 reviewers; checked numerically in the script.)
- Refutes / bounds: RF109.
- Status: named counterexample 'P8'; whether it is the legacy Example 2.3a is not stated in the sources.
- Notes / UNCERTAIN: **UNCERTAIN:** DROPPED.md says '(P8 counterexample)' without a file; the legacy elementary_III Proposition P8 (certificates and a universal evidence bound) has a literal-(iii) counterexample (Example 2.3a) that may or may not be meant. Both are quoted; do not assume equality.

> ## The hole, and how it is filled
>
> Both reviewers found the same hole: a guarantee that a near-truth particle is *delivered* and *repaired* with an explicit, finite budget. T24 and T26 alone do not provide it. The fill:
> - **T37**, a finite-n repair through the existing local search (Fable);
> - **T38**, a main theorem that contains the delivery step (HQ's synthesis of both reviews);
> - **T39** as the fallback (Astra).
>
> New statements are in `new_conjectures/`.
>
> **Rejected as targets** (both reviewers):
> - a comparative superiority theorem over SuSiE or SSL (the competitors' fixed points are intractable, and a toy comparison invites attack). The correlated-design mechanism is instead made explicit by T37's look-alike margin (n−1)θ²(1−r²)/(2σ²);
> - PIP calibration;
> - robustness to misspecification;
> - minimax optimality.
>
> ## Restatement notes for the campaign
>
> **Common setting:**
> - a triangular array with s₀ fixed (14 in our study), p_n ≤ n^A and B ≤ 16, so s₀ = ⌊√n⌋ is not covered;
> - separate the potential uninterrupted run from the output-available event, and never condition on observed completion;
> - **prove compatible premises jointly**: one statistical family must satisfy every premise used in T38, not each conditional statement separately (Astra).
>
> **Per target:**
> - **T03 / T02.**
>   - Replace T02(i)'s geometric tail 2^−m with the exact BB(1,p) tail. This cuts m_n from about 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p), so SE on sets of size ≤ m_n + s₀ ≤ K becomes meaningful at n = 200 (Fable).
>   - Restrict SE to the comparison unions actually used.
>   - Use BM-∞ or an unnamed constant C in place of M*.
>   - Neither change yields a useful finite-n frequentist error rate.
> - **T22.**
>   - Prove EXP, visibility and leakage for the actual partition dependent on X.
>   - For T38(b), use the deterministic reference bound (the reference may differ from S₀) instead of concentration on the truth.
>   - Failure points: normalised mass and uniform score remainders.
> - **T27.**
>   - Replace the assumed ratio law with a bounded-leakage condition along the chain (Fable), as a two-sided law with a controlled multiplier (Astra).
>   - The exponent depends on the budget; recompute it when budgets change.
> - **T37.**
>   - The 2^{s₀} union is loose at s₀ = 14; a bound along the greedy path is the research part.
>   - ℓ = 10 < s₀ + d = 15 at n = 200, so use the extra-scan rule or a closer centre.
> - **T24 (alternative).**
>   - Evaluate LK only at states that contain S₀, and charge look-alike additions to d.
>   - Replace the 1/(s₀+d+B+2)! full-ordering constant with a progress argument of one correct step per round.
>   - Failure point: EXIT under internal non-Gibbs moves.
> - **T38.**
>   - Eligibility in the masked regime: show the best-scored model lands in 𝓡_d, or use tweak LS0 (local search also from the start mode; can be added to existing fits after the fact).
>   - Check compatibility of T22(i) with T27.
>   - The cost corollary comes from T32.
> - **T26 (i)–(ii).**
>   - Require (T_n+1)Δ_n → 0 and (L_n+4)ρ*_n → 0.
>   - Remove the secondary PIP.
>   - Make no claims about the masked regime.
> - **T12.**
>   - Freeze everything before the final randomness.
>   - Use the islandwise product identity; it is NOT an identity for pooled Ẑ × primary pooled PIP.
>   - Drop the secondary PIP; validate floating point separately.
> - **T21.** Keep P(U) and the non-launch terms. "Scored" includes rejected proposals.
>
> ## Suggested campaign order (both reviewers)
>
> 1. **T37.** Cheap and finite-n; feeds Thm 3 and T38.
> 2. **T02(i) tail sharpening and the T03 restatement.**
> 3. **T22(i)/(iii) and T27** on one compatible family, starting with EXP in the block-orthogonal benchmark.
> 4. **T38** (composition, plus eligibility).
> 5. **T24**, only if T37 fails; **T39** only if T38(b) fails.
> 6. **Bookkeeping restatements:** T12, T21, T26(i)–(ii), T07, the T05 remark.

> # HQ proposal: theorems for a JRSS-B / Biometrika paper (2026-10-28)
>
> **Felipe's premise.** Assume every conjecture T01–T36 is provable. Assumptions may be modified, the methodology may get minor tweaks (for example budget sequences indexed by n), and statements may be restated. The target is JRSS-B, or at least Biometrika. The main text should carry 5–10 results, chosen for the highest return on investment.
>
> **Story.** What SMC-BVS reports is consistent, and the reason is that the truth gets *scored*, not that the sampler converges. The reported HPM is the best model ever scored.
>
> ## Main-text selection (8)
>
> | Paper # | Conjecture | Role | Proof work left |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | Thm 1 | T03 (with T02 and T01 as lemmas) | The posterior concentrates on the truth | Restate on the capped space (|S| ≤ K + s0) so the SE premise is not impossible at finite n; s0 fixed |
> | Prop 1 | T07 | The HPM is the Bayes rule for exact recovery; no size-only prior can repair a within-size ranking error | None |
> | Thm 2 | T22 | The composite start puts provable mass on, or near, the truth; it concentrates in the favourable regime | Finish (iii) |
> | Thm 3 | T27 | Masking lower bound: the start gives the truth only about p^-d n^-d/2 mass, so the start alone can fail | Finish |
> | Thm 4 | T24 | Terminal repair: from a near-truth particle, the final rounds score the truth with high probability | All |
> | Thm 5 | T21 | Composition: P(wrong report) ≤ P(no output) + 2E[posterior mass off the truth] + P(truth never scored) | None (T24 supplies H24) |
> | Thm 6 | T26 | Main theorem: the reported HPM, the PIPs and the evidence estimate Ẑ are all consistent under budgets indexed by n | All (it composes the others) |
> | Prop 2 | T12 | The evidence estimate is unbiased, and so is Ẑ·PIP, for the frozen run | None |
>
> - **Biometrika cut (5):** Thm 1, Prop 1, Thm 4, Thm 5, Thm 6. T22 and T12 become remarks.
> - **Supplement lemmas:** T01, T02, T09, T10, T11, T13, T14, T15, T20, T23.
> - **Remarks:** T04, T06, T31, T32, T33, T34.
> - **Dropped:** T05, T08, T16, T17, T18, T19, T25, T28, T29, T30, T35, T36.

> ## Known context
>
> - **Empirical results** (`04_Reports_and_Presentations/STATUS_BRIEFING_20261028/BRIEFING.md` §4):
>   - At c = 1, SMC-BVS trails SuSiE, SSL, the horseshoe and SSL-RS by 2–6 points; its misses are mostly the truth plus extra variables.
>   - At c = 0.5, SMC-BVS leads clearly, by 11–34 points (paired) over the Bayesian competitors.

> # Fable 5.1 review of HQ's paper selection (2026-10-28)
>
> Consultant: Fable 5.1 (independent of the second consultant). Inputs: PROPOSAL.md, BRIEFING §2/§4/§5, THEORY_INVENTORY, theorem files T01–T36, THEOREM_MAP. Read-only; no jobs run.
>
> **Verdict in one line: ENDORSE WITH CHANGES.** The story (consistency because the truth is *scored*) is right and sellable. Two of the eight need restating before the campaign, the pool is missing one type of result (a finite-n repair guarantee), and I propose one new conjecture to fill it.
>
> ---
>
> ## 1. Critique of the selection
>
> **Change A (matters most): Thm 6 = T26 is the wrong main theorem as written.** T26 reaches the HPM through clause (iii): start concentration makes an initial π₀ draw equal S₀ with probability → 1. A referee will ask why the SMC bridge, Gibbs rounds and local search exist, since the block-wise start already solves the problem. In the only regime where the sampler does work (the masked regime of T27, start mass p⁻ᶜ n⁻ᶜ/²), T26 says nothing. Its hypothesis list (G, R, SE, BM, VIS, NL_avg, EXP, OP-a, OP-s, CAL) is also the longest in the pool and the likeliest to be judged unverifiable.
>
> Restate the main theorem as a **two-regime HPM theorem** whose proof uses the moves:
> - HPM part: for budgets indexed by n, P(Ŝ ≠ S₀ or no output) ≤ P(U) + o(1), where in the favourable regime (T22(iii)) the truth is scored by the iid start draws (T11(iii)), and in the masked regime (T27 chain, π₀(S^{(0)}) ≥ c₀) a start draw lands in 𝓡_d and the terminal repair (Thm 4) scores S₀; T21 composes; T03 supplies π(S₀) > ½.
> - Evidence and PIP part: T26(i)–(ii) as stated, favourable regime only, with EXP named as a hypothesis.
>
> What this gains: the theorem then explains the method's *design*, not just its output, and the masked regime is exactly where the simulations show SMC-BVS beating the coordinate-wise competitors (S3–S6 at c = 0.5; S1 is a tie with SSL).
>
> **Change B: Thm 4 (repair) should have a deterministic, finite-n route.** T24's repair constant c_n = 1/(s₀+d+B+2)! is 1/31! at s₀ = 14, and LK_d fails in correlated designs at states missing a true variable (a look-alike of the missing variable has leakage δ² ≈ (n−1)θ²r², so it is *more* attractive than most nulls). I propose T37 (§2) as the primary repair route: greedy best-improvement local search, which the method already runs three times, reaches S₀ from any 𝓡_d centre under a checkable "truth-dominance" condition, with a finite-n Gaussian bound on that condition. Keep T24 as the Gibbs-path alternative; whichever closes first is Thm 4, the other goes to the supplement. T37 is cheaper to prove and gives numbers at n = 200 for S1–S3.
>
> **Change C: T27 (Thm 3) is a Proposition, merged with T22 as "the start: upper and lower bounds".** Together they say "the start finds the truth in the favourable regime and provably cannot in the masked one", which is the motivation for the sampler in two sentences. Separate theorem status overstates T27, which is a corollary of T10/T11/T22 given the ratio law.
>
> **Keep unchanged:** T03 (Thm 1, with T01/T02 as lemmas), T07 (Prop 1), T21 (Thm 5), T12 (Prop 2; fold T31(i)'s Markov bound into it as one sentence so the reported 95% bound is covered).
>
> **Two cheap additions, not main-text items.** (a) Do not drop T05: clause (iii) says the g-prior + BB(1,p) HPM loses a √log n factor to the oracle selector under orthogonal design. Referees from the Castillo–van der Vaart school know this; a supplement remark pre-empts it and explains the S1 parity with SSL at c = 0.5. (b) One sentence of T06(i) next to Prop 1: exact ties and near-duplicates are a ceiling for every method (S4).
>
> **Biometrika cut (5):** Thm 1 (T03), Prop 1 (T07), Thm 4 (T37 or T24), Thm 5 (T21), Thm 6 (two-regime HPM, with evidence/PIP consistency as a remark). T22/T27 become one remark; T12 one remark. Same shape as HQ's cut, with Changes A and B applied.
>
> ---
>
> ## 2. Holes
>
> **Weak-signal advantage over SuSiE and SSL.** No theorem in the pool, and I recommend *not* conjecturing a comparative one: it would need SuSiE's variational fixed points or SSL's coordinate-ascent path, which no campaign will close, and a toy comparison invites attack. The data say the advantage is a *correlated-design* advantage (S1 at c = 0.5: 79 vs 80), so the honest mechanism statement is: exact joint scoring separates a true variable from a look-alike by a margin of order (n−1)θ²(1−r²)/(2σ²), and the only unfixable error is the within-size swap (T07). T37 makes that margin explicit. Pair it with the same-target comparator the briefing already recommends (MCMC on the same posterior).
>
> **Finite-n guarantee.** The real hole: every discovery route is asymptotic or conditional on abstract codes (LK, EXIT, GAIN, BASIN, HIT). T37 fills it.
>
> **Computational complexity.** Not a hole. Budgets are polynomial by construction (N₀ = max(2500, n, p), T_e = O(log² n), p scores per round), so "polynomial expected cost to score the truth" is a one-line corollary of Thm 6; state it as such.
>
> **Lower bound / optimality.** T05(iii) is the only optimality-type fact and it is negative; disclose it (§1). Minimax is out of scope.
>
> **PIP calibration and misspecification.** T23 stays pathwise and conditional; Regime L is the answer, not a theorem. For non-Gaussian errors, note in Limitations that scores depend on y only through projections, so sub-Gaussian extensions are routine but not done.
>
> [... section 'New conjecture T37' quoted in CJ117 ...]
>
> ## 3. Restatement notes for each selected theorem
>
> - **Thm 1, T03 (+T01, T02).** Replace the 2^{−m} geometric size tail in T02(i) by the exact BB(1,p) tail (ratio ≈ k/2p, not ½); m_n drops from ≈ 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p), which makes SE on sets of size ≤ m_n + s₀ ≤ K meaningful at n = 200. Replace M_* by an unnamed C in θ² ≥ C σ² (log n + log p)/n, or use BM-∞. s₀ fixed, p ≤ n^A, K_n = ⌊n/2⌋. Failure point: uniform Gaussian-maximum control over C(p, k) subsets with the (n+1)^{−1/2} determinant penalty. Optional upgrade if T03 closes fast: s₀ → ∞ with s₀ log p = o(n), statistical half only.
> - **Prop 1, T07.** None. Add the T06(i) tie sentence and name the look-alike swap as the within-size error.
> - **Prop 2 (start), T22 + T27.** T22(iii): state EXP as a hypothesis and prove it in the BO benchmark (T22(v)) where VIS is derivable; B_n ≤ 16 makes 2^B a constant, so the union is over p blocks. T27: replace the assumed ratio law by a bounded-leakage condition |δ_{T,l}| ≤ Cσ* along the chain, from which n^{−1/2}e^{O_P(1)} follows via the (n+1)^{−1/2} determinant factor. Failure point: the composite normaliser in T27(i) (the hint's warning).
> - **Thm 4, T37 / T24.** T37 as above. T24 if attempted: evaluate LK_d only at states containing S₀ (zero leakage) and charge look-alike additions at incomplete states to the budget d; replace the full-ordering event (1/(s₀+d+B+2)!) by a one-correct-Gibbs-step-per-round progress argument, giving (1−c′)^{H/(s₀+d)} with c′ ≈ 1/(B+3); H_n = L_n + 4 is already n-indexed. Failure point: EXIT_d bounding a non-Gibbs undo of a just-made correct step.
> - **Thm 5, T21.** None mathematically. State (C1) with routes (a), (d), (e′ = T37) only; make U explicit and report P(U) empirically (6/2,400).
> - **Thm 6, two-regime HPM + evidence/PIP.** Compose T22(iii)+T11(iii) [favourable] and T27+T37 [masked] through T21 and T03. Methodology tweak needed for the masked regime: an eligible centre must be the best scored model; guarantee it either by proving F(S^{(0)}) > sup_{S ∉ 𝓡_d} F(S) w.h.p. (T02/T03-type, asymptotic) or by a minor tweak, running the local search also from the start mode S̃₀ (deterministic, ≈ ℓ·p extra scores, no change to the sampler). Evidence/PIP clause: n-index Δ_n(T_n + 1) → 0 via T22(iv); failure point is EXP. Polynomial-cost corollary attached.
> - **Prop 3, T12 (+T31(i)).** Restate for the run as designed to finish with a separate output-available event; drop the secondary-PIP clause. No risk.

> # Independent design review for HQ — 28 October 2026
>
> Read: PROPOSAL.md; BRIEFING.md §§2, 4–5; THEORY_INVENTORY.md; 00_COMMON.md, T01–T36 and THEOREM_MAP.md. This review accepts Felipe's provability premise. No other consultant's answer was consulted; no jobs were run.
>
> ## 1. Critique of the selection
>
> The proposed story is strong, but its central implication is incomplete: **T24 repairs an eligible particle; it does not deliver that particle. T26 establishes accuracy when the start already concentrates on the truth; it does not complete the masked-start repair argument.** These are different regimes, not consecutive links in one proof.
>
> I recommend one replacement, keeping eight main-text results:
>
> - **Move T07 to the decision-rule discussion**, with its proof in the supplement. Its distinction between exact-support and Hamming loss matters, but posterior decision theory and cancellation of a common size prior offer little standalone novelty. Moreover, size-prior retuning *can* affect the observed truth-plus-extras errors.
> - **Add C37 below**, joining start mass, repair and an explicit discovery budget. This answers the referee's substantive question: where does the repairable particle come from, and what does obtaining and repairing it cost?
> - **Keep T26, but label it a favorable-start corollary.** Its evidence/PIP conclusions are valuable, especially because the actual method reports these quantities. Do not advertise them for the masked regime merely because T24 discovers the truth there.
> - **Keep T27 as a route-specific lower bound.** It explains why iid start proposals can be insufficient; it is neither a lower bound for the hybrid sampler nor evidence of computational optimality.
> - **Keep T12, correcting the proposed shorthand.** The identity is islandwise, $E[\widehat Z_r\widehat{\mathrm{PIP}}_{rj}]=Z\mathrm{PIP}_j$, hence also for the average of these products. It is generally **not** an identity for pooled evidence times the primary, equally pooled PIP.
>
> For **Biometrika's five**, choose **T03, T22, T24, C37, T21**. This preserves the target–start–repair–budget–reported-selection argument. Put T27's contrast in the text with its theorem in the supplement; move T12 and T26 there too. HQ's cut retains two composition results while demoting the start analysis that supplies their substantive content.
>
> ## 2. Holes and one new conjecture
>
> The pool contains most necessary *types* of mathematics. The important hole is an explicit, compatible start-to-repair guarantee with finite budgets. Merely assuming eligibility, or increasing unspecified budgets until convergence occurs, does not fill it. C37 offers a small methodology extension that removes the need to prove survival of a repairable particle through the entire tempering/resampling system.
>
> Other candidate directions have lower priority:
>
> - **Weak-signal advantage:** no universal superiority theorem over SuSiE or SSL is justified. Their priors, approximations, optimization and decisions differ. Exact HPM optimality is a posterior-risk statement, not frequentist dominance. Even SMC's HPM–PIP gap may include PIP estimation error. A controlled comparison would need a precisely specified competitor and matched target before blaming approximation.
> - **Finite n:** T21 and T24 already provide finite-budget inequalities, but useful numerical constants and a statistical error bound remain necessary. Removing the impossible SE premise alone does not make n = 200 informative.
> - **Complexity and lower bounds:** attach T32's arithmetic costs to C37. “Polynomial for fixed sparsity” alone is weak: exhaustive search through supports of bounded size is already polynomial. The gain must be an improved dependence on p or a demonstrated repair-versus-iid separation. Restore **T05 to the supplement**: its sharp threshold and oracle gap honestly delimit the chosen target, although ORTH excludes p > n. Do not claim minimax optimality.
> - **PIP calibration:** T23/T26 concern accuracy and eventual 0/1 recovery, not frequentist calibration of intermediate PIPs. That is a separate project. Misspecification robustness is likewise worthwhile but not essential to this paper's stated selection contribution; T04 is not such a robustness theorem.
>
> [... section 'C37' quoted in CJ119 ...]
>
> ## 3. Restatement notes for the eight selected results
>
> Common convention: use a triangular array with fixed s₀ (e.g. 14), $p_n\le n^A$, and B ≤ 16. This does not cover a growing-sparsity generator $s_0=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$. Distinguish the uninterrupted process from output availability; never condition identities on observed completion.
>
> - **T03.** Retain Ω with cap K_n; restrict SE to the comparison unions actually used, bounded by $\min\{p_n,\min(K_n,m_n)+s_0\}$, and recheck cap-boundary comparisons. First use BM-∞ with $M_n\log n/n\to0$; then sharpen constants. Neither a feasible SE condition nor an $O_P$ posterior rate supplies a useful finite-n frequentist error rate.
> - **T22.** Prove EXP and visibility/leakage bounds for the actual X-dependent partition. Require $2^{B_n}\sqrt{\log n}\,n^{-\kappa}\to0$ for truth concentration; for C37 use the deterministic reference bound instead. Normalized mass, response scaling and uniform score remainders are the failure points.
> - **T27.** State a two-sided sequential law with a controlled reciprocal random multiplier and normalized reference mass. Recompute discovery from $Q_n p_n^{-c}n^{-c/2}$, where c counts masked additions, whenever budgets change; the published exponent is budget-specific. Initial marginal cancellation alone does not establish sequential cancellation.
> - **T24.** Require $h_na_n\to\infty$ and $h_n\eta_n\to0$ for a single long track; PIP claims additionally need prefix stability and population occupancy. For C37 short restarted tracks, use its explicit h_n/M_n choices. Derive LK/EXIT/GAIN jointly; internal swaps, multiple-extra deletions and the factorial constant remain dangerous.
> - **C37.** Use predetermined h_n, M_n, fresh streams and independent tracks, with $b_n,a_n,\eta_n$ justified on one event. Budget sequences must use declared bounds, not the unknown truth. Keep scoring-only information separate from SMC estimation; include setup, sampling and operational failures.
> - **T21.** Retain P(U), nonlaunch and scoring-failure terms; insert C37's explicit bound or a separately verified original-method route. No independence between statistical and computational failures is needed. “Scored” must include rejected proposals; discovering truth cannot cure a posterior ranking error.
> - **T26.** Keep the no-switch regime explicit: require $(T_n+1)\Delta_n\to0$ and $(L_n+4)\rho_{*,n}\to0$. Polylogarithmic budgets suffice only when those deficits decay polynomially; prove schedule/resource availability separately. Remove secondary PIPs. Increasing N_n alone does not repair these premises or establish masked-regime evidence accuracy.
> - **T12.** Freeze calibration, grid, budgets and escalation before final randomness. Arbitrary finite n-indexed budgets preserve the ideal islandwise identities; state the averaged-product identity correctly. Remove the obsolete secondary estimator and exclude completion/flag conditioning. Floating-point evidence needs separate validation.
>
> ## 4. Verdict
>
> **ENDORSE WITH CHANGES.** Final main-text eight: **T03, T22, T27, T24, C37, T21, T26, T12**. Biometrika five: **T03, T22, T24, C37, T21**. T07 becomes a decision-rule remark; T05 returns in the supplement. The proof campaign should prioritize compatible start-and-repair assumptions, not merely prove each conditional statement separately.

**A5. THEORY.md section 0 ('How to read this'), verbatim**

> ## 0. How to read this
>
> **Status vocabulary** (used exactly, never upgraded):
>
> | Term | Meaning |
> |---|---|
> | PROVED-LOCKED | The result is a row of `proofs/LOCKED_PROOFS.md`: statement file and final proof file are frozen with the SHA-256 recorded there. Always followed by the review depth and by "not adopted". |
> | CONDITIONAL | The locked theorem carries open hypotheses that are assumed, not proved (H24, PW2, EXP', VIS, NL_eta, NL_avg, H2, H3, BASIN, COVER, exposure and occurrence conditions). The hypothesis is always named. |
> | PARTLY PROVED | Only named parts are locked. The other parts are CONJECTURED. |
> | CONJECTURED (not proved) | Every item of the 36 that is not in the register, and T37, T38, T39. |
> | DROPPED | Two different senses, always distinguished: dropped from the paper selection (FROZEN_LIST) versus dropped as a conjecture (DROPPED.md). A theorem can be partly proved and dropped from the paper (T25(iv)). |
>
> **Review depth by wave.** Wave 1 (10 results): Opus 5.5 lead; Astra #1 (Stage A); Astra #2 plus Opus 5.5 xhigh (Stage B); campaign review (Stage C) by Fable 5.1 (high) plus Astra xhigh. Wave 2 (4 results): Astra lead, two independent Sol 6.1 (high) reviewers, Astra xhigh closing review, Claude Opus audit. Wave 3 (5 folders, 7 theorem numbers): Opus 5.5 lead, two independent Opus 5.5 xhigh reviewers, statement checker where noted; the external (OpenAI) review is queued; no wave-level Fable campaign review is recorded and none is claimed.
>
> **Locked is not adopted.** "Locked" means the statement and proof files named in the register are frozen and have passed their audits. "Adopted" means Felipe has accepted the result into the paper's theory. No result is adopted; the adoption of the 21 locked entries is an open decision of Felipe (section 5).
>
> **Standing idealisations** (hypotheses only where a STATEMENT.md lists them; they are not H-xx labels): EX-A exact arithmetic; EX-S ideal independent uniform random streams; CAL calibration uses streams 0-9 only and the final run uses fresh streams 10-13; EXEC local-search scans are completed.
>
> **n = 200.** The study design is n = 200, p = 500 or 1000. Every statistical theorem is an asymptotic statement; the numbers it gives at n = 200 are mostly not informative (section 5.3). > ## 1. The spine: "moving off the start is needed", not "tempering is needed"
>
> ### The finding
> W7-SEP (`theory/W7-SEP` · `REPORT.md` §1, §5; `PROOF.md` §4.2) tested the planned claim that "start-only methods fail; the tempering bridge is needed". On the paper's own masked family LH, that claim is **false**.
> - **Proposition GU (greedy universality)** is PROVED (candidate; not XF reviewed; it uses W4-T38FULL Lemma M, which is same-family VERIFIED only). Its setting: exact-Gram designs with an isolated relevant set R, SE on R and fixed signals. Its conclusion: the production local search, started at **any** C ⊆ R, reaches, scores and certifies S₀ with probability → 1, in a bounded number of moves.
> - **Corollary GU-LH** (COUNTEREXAMPLE to the task's claim (a), by proof). On LH, start-only discovery plus the production local search (that is, LS0) scores S₀ with probability → 1. The same held numerically in 386/386 replicates.
> - W7-SEP §1 item 4: on LH there is **no separation between the tempering bridge and a single greedy search from the start mode**.
>
> ### What is still true, and is the defensible claim
> **Moving off the start is needed.**
> - iid start draws alone fail in the masked regime: T27(i); R-T20(i).
> - W7-SEP Theorem SEP(A)/(B) (PROVED, candidate) makes this sharp on LH. iid discovery, and one-shot importance reweighting, need Q* = p^c n^{c/2} draws.
>
> **v3's moves provide the move off the start.** Each of the following is a sufficient discovery route; none is shown to be uniquely necessary:
> - bridge Gibbs flips;
> - the terminal rounds (O-BGIBBS Theorem BG3: PROVED for the original method on LH with p fixed; Prop. LH-lock is a PROOF SKETCH);
> - the local search, including LS0 (W7-SEP Prop. GU; T38(b1-LH)).
>
> **The bridge's own role** is to produce calibrated evidence and PIPs (T12, T26) and the HPM ledger.
>
> ### Consistent facts
> - **S-ELS** (`theory/S-ELS` · `REPORT.md` §1, §3), on the 2,394 completed fits:
>   - the final local search made **0 moves** in every fit;
>   - every error is a posterior miss (565), with **0 search misses**;
>   - S₀ was scored in every completed fit.
> - **O-BGIBBS** (`theory/O-BGIBBS` · `REPORT.md` §1 · Theorem BG3): the original method's terminal Gibbs rounds score S₀ on LH, for fixed p.
>

> ## 2. Other 2026-11-02 campaign decisions that change the frozen wording
>
> ### 2.1 LS0 is effective (part of the method)
> Felipe approved LS0 on 2026-11-02, conditional on O-LS0's data check. The check passed:
> - source: `theory/O-LS0` @ 02348e2 · `REPORT.md` §1; `theory_campaign/LEDGER.md`, 20:33 UTC;
> - LS0 changed the reported HPM in **0 of 2,394** completed fits;
> - exact recovery is unchanged: 1,119/1,200 at c = 1 and 710/1,200 at c = 0.5;
> - the cost is under 0.1% of a fit.
>
> So the approval is effective. Where the frozen documents say "optional tweak", "addable after the fact" or "if needed", read "part of the method".
>
> Corrected cost: LS0 costs 1 + (ℓ+1)·max_k[p + k(p−k)] scores (W6-FIXREV1; ≈ 1.7·10⁵ at p = 1,000), not "about ℓ·p".
>
> Caveat (O-LS0 §1 item 6): most T38(b1) premises fail at n = 200, so LS0's theoretical value is asymptotic.
>
> ### 2.2 The common-σ² start is rejected
> Two runs show that it floods the start in study-like designs, even with the oracle σ²:
> - `theory/O-DILUTE` · `REPORT.md` §5: "Do not adopt it."

> If any start change is considered later, the candidate is residualised tables, and F-SIGMA's free post hoc Step 0 comes first. No main-branch document proposed the common-σ² start, so no main text changes.
>

> Source: W8-SYNTH §1, Decision 3, and §4.13.
> - **Beta-min** fails by **at least 43×**, not "about 100×". The 100× figure predates T03♯. Sources: F-REFINE, W6-FIXREV2, F-REFEREE.

## Theme 1: STAT, the statistical target and concentration (Theorem 1 / T03-sharp, the exact BB(1,p) tail, Prop D, Prop 1, T05, the literature verdicts)

Summary: This theme collects everything the campaign produced or relied on about the exact posterior $\pi$ of the shipped target (ridge unit-information slab, $\mathrm{IG}(0.01,0.01)$ variance, BB(1,p) size prior capped at $K=\min(p,\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$): posterior concentration and selection consistency (final name: **Theorem 1 = T03-sharp**, with the lemmas T01 and T02), the exact Beta-Binomial size tail (T02(i-sharp)) and the proof that the hoped-for sharper size cutoff is false (Prop E3, Prop D), the corrected n = 200 / finite-n disclosure threshold (1.2e5 replaced by about 2.1e6-2.5e6), the decision-theory **Prop 1 = T07 + T06(i)** with its sharp size-prior ceiling and the B5 ERROR on its data paragraph, the orthogonal-design **T05** benchmark gap proved by W7-SEC, and the literature verdicts of LIT-STAT. This theme is the statistical half ("the first term") of the thread's final decomposition of the reported-HPM error, in HQ's words at [pos 1142]: "P(reported ≠ S₀) ≤ P(the exact posterior's mode ≠ S₀) + P(S₀ is never scored)", where "the first term is pure statistics: T03♯ (Rossell 2022, Prop 1)" and the second is the discovery side (CJ118 (T38), TH334 (N200), ⟦LS0⟧). The exact inequality behind it is TH422 (T21 (C1)): $P(U\text{ or }\hat S\ne S_0)\le P(U)+2E_0\delta_1+P(\text{truth not scored})$ with $\delta_1=1-\pi(S_0)$ (W2-BOOK, Theorem "Composition for the reported HPM").

### TH121 — T01 (A0): contrast reduction and mixed-rate transfer  [theorem, locked, as used]
- Source (authoritative): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T01_T02_contrast_dimension/STATEMENT.md` §§1-2 (statement checked by the Opus xhigh statement checker, review/STATEMENT_CHECK_R2.md); proof `PROOF_v3.tex`; register row in `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/LOCKED_PROOFS.md` ("T01 and T02"); positions: [pos 119] (HQ inventory of the locked set), [pos 238] (W1-T03R task that cites it).
- Statement (verbatim; setting first, then T01):

> **Target (method §5).** K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋), Ω = {S ⊆ [p] : |S| ≤ K}. For S ∈ Ω, k = |S|: G_S = X_SᵀX_S = (n−1)R_S, z_S = X_Sᵀy, H_S = (n+1)G_S + I_k, D_S = det H_S / det(G_S + I_k), Q_S = yᵀy − n z_SᵀH_S⁻¹z_S (D_∅ = 1, Q_∅ = yᵀy), a₀ = b₀ = 0.01, ν = a₀ + n/2,
> m(S) = (2b₀)^{a₀}Γ(ν)/(π^{n/2}Γ(a₀)) · D_S^{−1/2}(2b₀ + Q_S)^{−ν};
> w(k) = ½/C(2p−1, k), W_K = Σ_{k≤K} C(p,k)w(k), ϖ(S) = w(|S|)/W_K; Z = Σ_Ω ϖ(S)m(S); π(S) = Π(S | y) = ϖ(S)m(S)/Z; BF(S) = m(S)/m(∅).
> The v3 joint posterior of (S, β_S, σ²) is the posterior of the working model
> y | β_S, σ², S ~ N_n(X_Sβ_S, σ²I_n), β_S | σ², S ~ N_k(0, nσ²(G_S+I_k)⁻¹), σ² ~ IG(a₀, b₀), S ~ ϖ on Ω,
> evaluated at the standardised y (its S-marginal is π). The **joint transformed posterior** is its image under the bijection (S, β_S, σ²) ↦ (S, θ_S, v) = (S, s_yβ_S, s_y²σ²).
>
> **Contrast model at rate b > 0** (fixed, i.e. not a function of the data, unless stated). For S ∈ Ω:
> y_c | θ_S, v, S ~ N_{n−1}(X_{c,S}θ_S, vI_{n−1}), θ_S | v, S ~ N_k(0, nv(G_S+I_k)⁻¹), v ~ IG(0.51, b), S ~ ϖ.
> (Note X_{c,S}ᵀX_{c,S} = G_S.) m^c_b(S) := the marginal density of y_c under model S at rate b. z_S^c = X_{c,S}ᵀy_c, Q_S^c = y_cᵀy_c − n (z_S^c)ᵀH_S⁻¹z_S^c. For a measurable parameter event E ⊆ ⋃_{S∈Ω} {S} × ℝ^S × (0,∞) with sections E_S:
> I_b(E) := Σ_{S∈Ω} ϖ(S) ∫∫_{E_S} N_{n−1}(y_c; X_{c,S}θ, vI) N_k(θ; 0, nv(G_S+I)⁻¹) IG(v; 0.51, b) dθ dv,
> Z^c_b := I_b(everything) = Σ_Ω ϖ(S)m^c_b(S), Π_b(E) := I_b(E)/Z^c_b (the contrast-model posterior at rate b).
>
> **Statistical model (for probabilistic parts).** Fixed design; y^r = α*1 + X^rβ* + ε, ε ~ N_n(0, σ*²I_n), σ*² > 0 fixed, α* ∈ ℝ arbitrary; μ = CX^rβ* = Xθ*, θ* = D_xβ*, S₀ = supp β*, s₀ = |S₀|. P₀, E₀ are over ε. Assumption **G** is this model. Assumption **R**: s₀ fixed; p ≤ n^A with A ≥ 1 fixed; ‖μ‖²/n ≤ M (fixed M ≥ 0); λ_min(R_{S₀}) ≥ φ₀² > 0 (void if s₀ = 0); s₀ ≤ K for all large n. Regime **R1**: n → ∞, s₀ fixed, p ≤ n^A. Assumption **SE**: λ_min(R_T) ≥ φ₀² for every nonempty T with |T| ≤ min(p, m_n + s₀), where m_n = m_n(½ log n).
> r_n = √(log n / n); m_n(ω) = ⌈(s₀ log(2p) + (s₀+1)(log n)/2 + ω)/log 2⌉.
>
> **Scale event and envelope rates.** b₋ := b₀σ*²/2, b₊ := b₀(2(σ*²+M)+1), κ := (b₊/b₋)^{0.51} (constants, not depending on n or the data). 𝓑_n := {σ*²/2 ≤ s_y² ≤ 2(σ*²+M)+1} = {b₋ ≤ b₀s_y² ≤ b₊}.
>
> ## 2. T01
>
> **(i) [identity; every valid input, deterministic].** The joint transformed posterior of (S, θ_S, v) equals Π_{b₀s_y²}, the posterior of the contrast model at rate b = b₀s_y² (the rate evaluated at the observed s_y), and for every S ∈ Ω
> m(S) = c_n(s_y) · m^c_{b₀s_y²}(S),  c_n(s) = s^{n−1}Γ(0.51)/(√(2πb₀)Γ(0.01)).
> Hence BF(S) = m^c_{b₀s_y²}(S)/m^c_{b₀s_y²}(∅), π(S) = ϖ(S)m^c_{b₀s_y²}(S)/Z^c_{b₀s_y²}, and Z = c_n(s_y) Z^c_{b₀s_y²}. Moreover z_S^c = s_y z_S, Q_S^c = s_y²Q_S, and under the joint transformed posterior
> v | S, y ~ IG(ν, b₀s_y² + Q_S^c/2),  θ_S | v, S, y ~ N_k(nH_S⁻¹z_S^c, nvH_S⁻¹).
>
> **(ii) [envelope; deterministic].** Let 0 < b₁ ≤ b ≤ b₂ be any numbers and κ₁₂ = (b₂/b₁)^{0.51}. For every S ∈ Ω and every y_c ∈ ℝ^{n−1}:
> κ₁₂⁻¹m^c_{b₂}(S) ≤ m^c_b(S) ≤ κ₁₂ m^c_{b₁}(S).
> For every measurable parameter event E: κ₁₂⁻¹I_{b₂}(E) ≤ I_b(E) ≤ κ₁₂ I_{b₁}(E); consequently Π_b(E) ≤ κ₁₂² I_{b₁}(E)/Z^c_{b₂}. (The original writes b₋, b₊, κ here; the letters are changed only because b₋, b₊, κ denote the specific constants of §1 elsewhere. With b₁ = b₋, b₂ = b₊ one has κ₁₂ = κ.)
>
> **(iii) [scale event].** Under G and R: s_y² − (σ*² + ‖μ‖²/(n−1)) = O_{P₀}(n^{−1/2}) and P₀(𝓑_n) → 1. Also ε_c := Uᵀε ~ N_{n−1}(0, σ*²I_{n−1}) exactly, and y_c = X_cθ* + ε_c.
>
> **(iv) [rate derivative; fixed contrast data].** For S, S′ ∈ Ω and b > 0:
> ∂_b log[m^c_b(S)/m^c_b(S′)] = 2ν(Q_S^c − Q_{S′}^c)/((2b + Q_S^c)(2b + Q_{S′}^c)).
>
> **(T) [transfer rule].**
> (a) *Mixed-endpoint transfer.* With b₋, b₊, κ, 𝓑_n as in §1: on 𝓑_n, for every measurable parameter event E,
> Π(E | y) ≤ κ² I_{b₋}(E)/Z^c_{b₊} ≤ κ² I_{b₋}(E)/(ϖ(S₀) m^c_{b₊}(S₀))
> (the last step when S₀ ∈ Ω), where Π(· | y) is the joint transformed v3 posterior and the right-hand sides are computed from y_c at the fixed rates b₋ (numerator) and b₊ (denominator). Consequently, under G and R, if I_{b₋}(E_n)/Z^c_{b₊} ≤ ε_n with P₀-probability → 1 (resp. = O_{P₀}(ε_n)), then Π(E_n | y) ≤ κ²ε_n with P₀-probability → 1 (resp. = O_{P₀}(ε_n)).
> (b) *Same-rate bounds do not transfer (a worst case over inputs, not a statement about P₀).*
> (b1) For any fixed rates 0 < r₁ < r₂ there are valid inputs (n → ∞, p = 1) with Π_{r₁}({S = {1}}) → 1 and Π_{r₂}({S = {1}}) → 0 (so Π_{r₁}({S = ∅}) → 0 and Π_{r₂}({S = ∅}) → 1). Hence, for distinct fixed rates b ≠ b′, there is no function g with g(x) → 0 as x ↓ 0, independent of n and the data, such that Π_{b′}(E) ≤ g(Π_b(E)) for all valid inputs and all events E. (Its inputs have s_y² → 0, so they lie outside 𝓑_n for large n; (b2) is the version on 𝓑_n.)
> (b2) Fix any σ*² > 0 and M ≥ 0 (hence b₋, b₊), and any s² with σ*²/2 < s² < 2(σ*²+M)+1. There are valid inputs with p = 2 and s_y² = s² for every n ≥ 4 (so 𝓑_n holds for every n) such that, for E = {S = {1}}, Π_{b₋}(E) → 0 while Π(E | y) → 1 as n → ∞; and there are valid inputs with the same properties such that, for E′ = {S = {1,2}}, Π_{b₊}(E′) → 0 while Π(E′ | y) → 1. Hence, for b ∈ {b₋, b₊}, there is no constant C, independent of n and of the data, such that Π(E | y) ≤ C·Π_b(E) for all valid inputs in 𝓑_n and all events E.
> (Proof discipline, not a mathematical claim: the proofs never treat ε or ε_c as N(0, σ*²I) conditionally on s_y or on 𝓑_n.)

### TH123 — T03 (A2): selection, screening, PIPs and the global HPM (locked form, with H-T02 and the full SE)  [theorem, locked]
- Source (authoritative for the original): `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T03_A2_selection_consistency/STATEMENT.md` §§2-4; proof `PROOF_v2.tex`; theorem file `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/T03_A2_selection_consistency.md`; positions [pos 119], [pos 238].
- Statement (verbatim; hypotheses, then conclusions, then "not claimed"):

> ## 2. Hypotheses
>
> - **G.** Fixed design; $\varepsilon\sim N_n(0,\sigma_\star^2I_n)$, $\sigma_\star^2>0$ fixed.
> - **R.** $s_0$ fixed; $p\le n^A$ with fixed $A\ge1$; $\|\mu\|^2/n\le M$ (fixed $M$); $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0})\ge\varphi_0^2>0$ (fixed $\varphi_0$); eventually $s_0\le K$.
> - **SE.** $\lambda_{\min}(R_T)\ge\varphi_0^2$ for every nonempty $T\subseteq[p]$ with $|T|\le\min(p,m_n+s_0)$.
> - **Constants.** $j_*=\lceil(2A+1)s_0\rceil+1$; $C_*=2s_0+3[Aj_*+s_0+\log(j_*+1)+1]$; $L_*=\max\{4C_*,\,32[s_0(A+1)+2]\}$; $M_*=2L_*+1$.
> - **BM-C.** $\min_{j\in S_0}\theta^{\star2}_j\ge M_*\sigma_\star^2\log n/(n\varphi_0^2)$.
> - **BM-∞.** The same inequality with a sequence $M_n\to\infty$ in place of $M_*$.
> - **H-T02 (= T02(i), unproved v3 conjecture, used as hypothesis).** Under G and R, for each deterministic integer sequence $m=m(n)$,
>   $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\le2^{-m}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\,\Theta_{n,m}$, with $\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_n\sup_mP_0(\Theta_{n,m}>L)=0$.
>
> Convention: a minimum over the empty set is $+\infty$ (so BM-C and BM-∞ hold when $s_0=0$).
>
> ## 3. Conclusions (in R1)
>
> Under G, R, SE, H-T02 and BM-C (or BM-∞):
>
> - **(i)** $1-\pi(S_0)=O_{P_0}(r_n)$.
> - **(ii)** $\max_j|\mathrm{PIP}_j-\mathbf 1\{j\in S_0\}|\le1-\pi(S_0)$ for every data set (deterministic); and $P_0(\mathrm{MPM}=S_0)\to1$.
> - **(iii)** $P_0(S^\dagger\ne S_0)\le2E_0[1-\pi(S_0)]\to0$; on the event $\{\pi(S_0)>\tfrac12\}$, $S_0$ is the strict global maximiser of $F$ on $\Omega$ (the tie rule is not invoked).
>
> Under G, R, SE and H-T02 only (no beta-min):
>
> - **(iv)** With $J_n=\{j\in S_0:\theta^{\star2}_j\ge M_*\sigma_\star^2\log n/(n\varphi_0^2)\}$: $\Pi(\{S:S\not\supseteq J_n\}\mid y)=O_{P_0}(r_n)$, and $\min_{j\in J_n}\mathrm{PIP}_j\to1$ in $P_0$-probability (with $1-\min_{j\in J_n}\mathrm{PIP}_j=O_{P_0}(r_n)$; the minimum over $\emptyset$ is $1$).
>
> Deterministic remarks:
>
> - **(v)** If $s_0=0$, BM-C and BM-∞ hold vacuously. For every $c>0$, replacing $(\theta^\star,\sigma_\star^2)$ by $(\theta^\star/c,\sigma_\star^2/c^2)$ (in particular $c=s_y$) leaves the BM-C and BM-∞ inequalities and the set $J_n$ unchanged.
>
> ## 4. Not claimed
>
> The theorem file's sentences "No frequentist $O(r_n)$ selection-error rate follows from the posterior $O_{P_0}(r_n)$ rate" and "$M_*$ is conservative, not sharp; the sharp general-design constant is open" are interpretive remarks. They are not part of the claim and are not proved.

- Earlier versions / repairs: this is the version REPLACED by TH128. What changed (W1-T03R REPORT section 2 table, summarised): H-T02 removed (T02(i-sharp) used instead); the full SE ("all $T$, $|T|\le\min(p,m_n+s_0)$") replaced by two anchored conditions SE_lambda(j0), SE_w(m#_n; g0); the provisional constant $M_*$ replaced by BM-inf or BM(c), $c>c_0$ with $c_0=L_*=\max\{4C_*,32[s_0(A+1)+2]\}$; the proof steps that change are listed in W1-T03R REPORT section 2 and the unchanged ones cited by label.

### TH124 — T04 (A3): contraction without beta-min (locked, as used with H-T02)  [theorem, locked]
- Source: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T04_A3_contraction/STATEMENT.md` §§2-3 (wave 3); positions [pos 119], [pos 238]. T04 is a consumer of H-T02 and was not part of the campaign's repairs.
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## 2. Assumptions
>
> - **R1:** n → ∞, s₀ fixed, p = p_n ≤ n^A with a fixed A ≥ 1.
> - **G:** the fixed design and Gaussian errors above.
> - **R:** s₀ fixed; p ≤ n^A with A ≥ 1; ‖μ‖²/n ≤ M; λ_min(R_{S₀}) ≥ φ₀² > 0 (vacuous if s₀ = 0); eventually s₀ ≤ K.
> - **SE** (only where stated): λ_min(R_T) ≥ φ₀² for every nonempty T ⊆ [p] with |T| ≤ min(p, m_n + s₀).
> - **DX** (only for (iv)): every diagonal entry of D_x is ≥ d₋ > 0.
> - **H-T02** (= T02(i), an explicit hypothesis because it is unproved): in R1 under G and R, Π(|S| > m_n(ω_n) | y) = O_{P₀}(e^{−ω_n}) for every deterministic ω_n → ∞ with ω_n = O(log n). It is used only with ω_n = ½ log n, in the form Π(|S| > m_n | y) → 0 in P₀-probability.
> - No beta-min condition is assumed.
>
> ## 3. Conclusion
>
> "→ 0" means convergence to 0 in P₀-probability as n → ∞. There is a constant C < ∞, depending only on (σ*², M, φ₀, A) (b₀ = 0.01 is fixed), such that, in R1 under G, R and H-T02:
>
> - **(i) [fallback; secondary]** Π†(‖Xθ − μ‖²/n > C ε_{2,n}² | y) → 0.
> - **(ii) Under SE in addition:**
>   - Π(|S| > d_* | y) → 0;
>   - Π†(‖Xθ − μ‖²/n > C ε_{1,n}² | y) → 0;
>   - Π†(‖θ − θ*‖² > C ε_{1,n}²/φ₀² | y) → 0.
> - **(iii)** For every deterministic sequence u_n → ∞: Π†(|v/σ*² − 1| > C[ε_n² + u_n/√n] | y) → 0. Here ε_n = ε_{2,n} under G, R, and ε_n = ε_{1,n} under SE in addition (the "applicable ε_n"). v is on the contrast scale.
> - **(iv) Under SE and DX:** Π†(‖D_x⁻¹(θ − θ*)‖² > C ε_{1,n}²/(φ₀² d₋²) | y) → 0. This is the rate of (ii) multiplied by d₋⁻².
>
> **Not claimed:** beta-min; out-of-sample, intercept-posterior or empirically centred random-design Hellinger results.

### LM101 — Lemma E1 (exact BB(1,p) tail)  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §1 (Lemma E1), `W1-T03R/REPORT.md` §1; verified in `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` rows 1-4 and `A-REV2/REVIEW.md` §3.1; positions: launch [pos 233]/[pos 238]; result [pos 296], [pos 342]; verification [pos 337], [pos 370]; cross-family [pos 565], [pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim; definitions first):

> Throughout: $N=n-1$, $K=\min(p,\lfloor n/2\rfloor)$, $w(k)=\tfrac12/\binom{2p-1}{k}$, $\varpi(S)=w(|S|)/W_K$, $r_n=\sqrt{\log n/n}$, $m_n(\omega)=\lceil(s_0\log(2p)+(s_0+1)(\log n)/2+\omega)/\log 2\rceil$ (00_COMMON). We assume $p\ge2$ (for $p=1$ every statement below is trivial or void).
>
> Put $q_k:=\binom pk w(k)$ ($0\le k\le p$) and, for every integer $m$ and $0\le s_0\le K$,
> $$R_m:=\frac{\varpi(\{S\in\Omega:|S|>m\})}{\varpi(S_0)}=\sum_{k=m+1}^{K}\frac{q_k}{w(s_0)}\qquad(\text{empty sum}=0;\ W_K\text{ cancels}).$$
> $R_m$ is a data-free number (it depends on $p$, $s_0$, $K$, $m$ only), and $R_m=0$ for $m\ge K$.
>
> ### Lemma E1 (exact tail; PROVED)
> Let $\rho_i:=\dfrac{p-i}{2p-1-i}$ for $0\le i\le p-1$.
>
> **(a)** $\rho_i=\tfrac12\Big(1-\dfrac{i-1}{2p-1-i}\Big)$, and for $s_0\le k\le p$: $\ q_k/w(s_0)=\binom p{s_0}\prod_{i=s_0}^{k-1}\rho_i$.
>
> **(b)** For every integer $m\ge s_0$:
> $$R_m\le\binom p{s_0}\,2^{-(m-s_0)}\,e^{-\gamma_m},\qquad \gamma_m:=\frac{m(m-1)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)}{4(p-1)} .$$
>
> **(c)** If $s_0\ge1$ and $s_0\le m\le K-1$:
> $$R_m\ \ge\ \frac{q_{m+1}}{w(s_0)}\ \ge\ \binom p{s_0}\,2^{-(m+1-s_0)}\exp\Big\{-\frac{m(m-1)-(s_0-1)(s_0-2)}{4(p-m)}\Big\}.$$
>
> **(d)** (comparison with the locked bound) The locked proof of T02(i) bounds the same ratio by $4(2p)^{s_0}2^{-m}$ ([P1] `lem:prior`(c),(d)). For $m\ge s_0\ge 1$, (b) improves this by the factor at least $4\,s_0!\,e^{\gamma_m}$, since $\binom p{s_0}2^{s_0}\le(2p)^{s_0}/s_0!$.
>
> **Reading.** By (a) the size marginal of BB(1,p) is geometric with ratio $\rho_i\approx\frac12$; the per-*model* ratio $w(k+1)/w(k)=(k+1)/(2p-1-k)\approx k/(2p)$ is cancelled by the multiplicity $\binom p{k+1}/\binom pk=(p-k)/(k+1)$. The exact tail therefore improves the locked one only by the factor $4\,s_0!\,e^{\gamma_m}$ ($\approx 36$ bits at $s_0=14$, plus $m^2/(4p)$ nats), not by a factor $p^{-(m-s_0)}$.

- Earlier versions / repairs: replaces the locked treatment in [P1] `lem:prior`(c),(d), which bounded $\varpi(|S|>m)\le 2^{1-m}$ and $\varpi(S_0)\ge\frac12(2p)^{-s_0}$ separately (hence the locked factor $4(2p)^{s_0}2^{-m}$). W6-FIXREV2 §1.1 restates the objects with the sum starting at $\max(m+1,0)$: "$R_m := \sum_{k=\max(m+1,0)}^{K} q_k / w(s_0)$ (empty sum = 0; so $R_m=0$ for $m\ge K$)". A first W1 headline reading of the improvement ("saves about 180 sizes") is RF121.
- Status history: PROVED (W1-T03R; candidate pending cross-family review) -> VERIFIED (W2-VT03R: exact-rational check of E1(a)-(d) on 2,779 $(p,n,s_0)$ triples; "max $R_m$/ub = 0.998") -> VERIFIED (A-REV2 section 2: "Exact BB size-marginal recurrence and both tail bounds, including s0=0 in the upper bound").
- Proved by / checked by: W1-T03R (Opus 5.5) / W2-VT03R (same family, exact rationals + independent script) / A-REV2 (Astra, cross-family). A-REV2 qualifications (Summary:): the bound E1(d) is a lower bound on the improvement factor, not an exact expression; the geometric sum starts at $m+1$ and gives $2^{s_0-m}$; the lower bound (c) is legitimate only for $s_0\ge1$, $m\le K-1$.
- Depends on: ⟦00_COMMON prior w(k)=1/[2C(2p-1,k)]⟧ (BB(1,p) capped at K); TH101 (T01) not needed (pure prior algebra).
- Feeds: TH125, TH126, LM102; final card S-T (K93, K04: "size masses decay geometrically with ratio <= p/(2p-1)").
- Notes: the exact class (size-marginal) ratio is $\rho_i=(p-i)/(2p-1-i)\approx\tfrac12$; the per-model ratio $w(k+1)/w(k)\approx k/(2p)$ is cancelled by the multiplicity $\binom p{k+1}/\binom pk=(p-k)/(k+1)$ (this is exactly why RF122 is false). LIT-STAT later proved the same fact independently as LM107.

### LM102 — Lemma E2 and the cutoff $m^\sharp_n$ (location of the exact-tail cutoff)  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §1 (Definition, Lemma E2); numerics `W1-T03R/REPORT.md` §3; verified `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` rows 5-7, 27; `A-REV2/REVIEW.md` §3.1; positions [pos 296], [pos 370], [pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ### Definition (new size cutoff)
> For $s_0\le K$ and real $\omega$:
> $$m^\sharp_n(\omega):=\min\{m\in\mathbb Z:\ m\ge s_0,\ R_m\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}\},\qquad m^\sharp_n:=m^\sharp_n(\tfrac12\log n).$$
> The minimum exists and $m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le K$, because $R_K=0$. It is computable exactly (`scripts/tail_bound.py`).
>
> ### Lemma E2 (location of $m^\sharp_n$; PROVED)
> Assume $s_0\le K$, $\omega\ge0$, and $s_0\ge1$ in (ii)–(iii) ($n\ge5$ if $s_0=0$ in (i)).
>
> **(i)** $s_0\le m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le\min\{K,\ m_n(\omega)\}$.
>
> **(ii)** $m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le\min\Big\{K,\ s_0+\Big\lceil\dfrac{\log\binom p{s_0}+\frac{s_0+1}2\log n+\omega}{\log2}\Big\rceil\Big\}$.
>
> **(iii)** If $m^\sharp:=m^\sharp_n(\omega)\le K-1$, then
> $$m^\sharp-s_0\ \ge\ \frac{\log\binom p{s_0}+\frac{s_0+1}2\log n+\omega}{\log2}-1-\frac{m^\sharp(m^\sharp-1)}{4(p-m^\sharp)\log2}.$$

- Numerical companion (verbatim from `W1-T03R/REPORT.md` §3, re-derived exactly by W2-VT03R row 27):

> ### Thresholds at ω = ½ log n, s₀ = 14
>
> Source: `scripts/tail_bound.py`, output in `tail_bound_output.txt`.
>
> | n | p | K | m_old (locked) | m♯ (exact, capped) | m♯ uncapped | old SE size m_old + s₀ | new SE_w size min(m♯,K) + s₀ |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | 200 | 500 | 100 | 201 | **100 (cap binds)** | 146 | 215 | 114 |
> | 200 | 1000 | 100 | 215 | **100 (cap binds)** | 168 | 229 | 114 |
> | 10³ | 500 | 500 | 220 | 161 | 161 | 234 | 175 |
> | 10³ | 1000 | 500 | 234 | 184 | 184 | 248 | 198 |
> | 10⁴ | 1000 | 1000 | 260 | 207 | 207 | 274 | 221 |
> | 10⁶ | 1000 | 1000 | 313 | 251 | 251 | 327 | 265 |
> | 10⁴ | n^{1.17} = 49,177 | 5000 | 339 | 302 | 302 | 353 | 316 |
> | 10⁶ | n^{1.17} ≈ 1.1·10⁷ | 5·10⁵ | 501 | 465 | 465 | 515 | 479 |
> | 10⁸ | n^{1.30} ≈ 2.7·10¹⁰ | 5·10⁷ | 712 | 676 | 676 | 726 | 690 |
>
> - For p = n^A the saving is ≈ 36 sizes. This equals log₂(14!) = 36.3, as Lemma E1(d) predicts.
> - For fixed p the saving grows with n (65–100), because of the Gaussian factor e^{−m²/4p}.
> - m♯ − s₀ grows like s₀ log n everywhere, as Prop. E3 predicts.
>
> ### Prior ratio R_m (log₁₀) at n = 200, p = 500
>
> | m | exact | E1(b) upper bound | E1(c) lower bound | locked bound 4(2p)^{s₀}2^{−m} |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | 14 | 26.75 | 26.76 | 26.46 | 38.39 |
> | 40 | 18.60 | 18.63 | 18.31 | 30.56 |
> | 80 | 5.40 | 5.56 | 5.00 | 18.52 |
> | 99 | −1.44 | −0.90 | −1.71 | 12.80 |
>
> - The locked bound overstates R_m by 10^{11.6}–10^{14.2}. Of this, 10^{11.6} = 4·14!, and the rest is the Gaussian factor.
> - Bounds (b) and (c) bracket the exact value within 10^{0.6}.
> - The full T02(i♯) prefactor, minimised over m < K, is 10^{15.8} (p = 500) and 10^{21.3} (p = 1000). It is vacuous at n = 200.
> - The cutoff first falls below K at n = 342 (exact) versus n = 464 (locked), for p = n^{1.17}.

- Earlier versions / repairs: the locked cutoff is $m_n(\omega)=\lceil(s_0\log(2p)+(s_0+1)(\log n)/2+\omega)/\log 2\rceil$ (00_COMMON); E2(i) shows $m^\sharp_n\le\min(K,m_n)$. Note the two equivalent normalisations in the sources: PROOF/W6 define $m^\sharp_n(\omega)$ with $R_m\le n^{-(s_0+1)/2}e^{-\omega}$ and $m^\sharp_n:=m^\sharp_n(\tfrac12\log n)$; the REPORT headline and card C9 write the same cutoff as $R_m\le n^{-(s_0+2)/2}$ (identical, since $e^{-\frac12\log n}=n^{-1/2}$).
- Status history: PROVED (W1-T03R) -> VERIFIED (W2-VT03R: E2(i)-(iii), exact check on 129 cases; "needs s0 >= 1, or s0 = 0 with n >= 5") -> VERIFIED (A-REV2, keep the stated $s_0\ge1$ restrictions and the $n\ge5$ null-truth exception).
- Proved by / checked by: as LM101.

### TH125 — Theorem T02(i-sharp) (sharpened size tail with the exact BB(1,p) tail)  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative, latest repaired version): `W6-FIXREV2/STATEMENTS.md` §1.2 (statement of record) with constants from `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §2; positions: launch [pos 233]/[pos 238], result [pos 296]; verification [pos 337]/[pos 370]; Astra [pos 565]/[pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim, W6-FIXREV2 §1.2 and the size-tail objects of §1.1):

> - **Size tail objects (data-free).** q_k := C(p,k)w(k). For every integer m,
>   R_m := Σ_{k = max(m+1, 0)}^{K} q_k / w(s₀)  (empty sum = 0; so R_m = 0 for m ≥ K).
>   For real ω, m♯_n(ω) := min{m ∈ ℤ : m ≥ s₀, R_m ≤ n^{−(s₀+1)/2}e^{−ω}} (it exists and is ≤ K); m♯_n := m♯_n(½ log n).
>   m♯_n is a deterministic function of (n, p, s₀); it is never selected from the response.
>
> **Theorem T02(i♯) (exact Beta-Binomial size tail; no eigenvalue condition beyond R).** Status: PROVED (S03 §2);
> A-REV2: VERIFIED. Assume G, R, s₀ ≤ K. Define Θ♯_{n,m} ≥ 0 by Π(|S| > m | y) = R_m(n+1)^{s₀/2}√n·Θ♯_{n,m} if R_m > 0, and
> Θ♯_{n,m} := 0 if R_m = 0. With c♯ := κ²/(c_IG σ*²) (constants of S03 §2), for every L > (c♯)² and every n,
>
>   sup_m P₀(Θ♯_{n,m} > L) ≤ (8 + 24M/σ*²)/(n − 1) + L^{−1/2} + C_Λ / log(√L/c♯).
>
> The quantifier is sup_m P₀(·), **not** P₀(sup_m ·). Consequently, for every **deterministic** real sequence ω_n,
> Π(|S| > m♯_n(ω_n) | y) ≤ (1 + 1/n)^{s₀/2} e^{−ω_n} Θ♯_{n, m♯_n(ω_n)} = O_{P₀}(e^{−ω_n}).

- Constants (verbatim, W1-T03R PROOF §2):

> Constants (as in [P1] §1 and `lem:den`): $b_-=b_0\sigma_*^2/2$, $b_+=b_0(2(\sigma_*^2+M)+1)$, $\kappa=(b_+/b_-)^{0.51}$, $\mathcal B_n=\{b_-\le b_0s_y^2\le b_+\}$, $c_{\rm IG}=\min_{v\in[\sigma_*^2,2\sigma_*^2]}\mathrm{IG}(v;0.51,b_+)$, $C_\Lambda=\frac1{\sqrt2}+\frac12+\mathbf 1\{s_0\ge1\}\frac{(1+\frac1{2\varphi_0^2})(M+\sigma_*^2)}{2\sigma_*^2}$, and
> $$c^\sharp:=\kappa^2/(c_{\rm IG}\sigma_*^2).$$

- Earlier versions / repairs: the locked T02(i) (TH122) reads $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)=2^{-m}(2p)^{s_0}(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\,\Theta_{n,m}$ with $\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_n\sup_m P_0(\Theta_{n,m}>L)=0$. Changed step (W1-T03R): the prior factor $2^{-m}(2p)^{s_0}$ is replaced by the exact ratio $R_m$ (LM101), using Lemma den-prime (LM103) before $\varpi(S_0)$ is bounded. A-REV2 (verbatim): "The quantifier is `sup_m P(Theta_nm>L)`, **not** `P(sup_m Theta_nm>L)`. ... It is not permission to select a cutoff from the response. For negative m, define `R_m` through the prior-mass ratio, or truncate its summation lower index at 0." (W6 §1.2 repeats the quantifier warning.) A-REV5 noted that Card 1 already has $\sup_m P$, "contrary to R2 REPORT".
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) (W1-T03R, "non-asymptotic: holds at every n with s0 <= K") -> SF VERIFIED (W2-VT03R row 10: "E₀Θ⁽¹⁾ = 1 exactly; P₀(𝓑ₙᶜ) ≤ (8+24M/σ*²)/(n−1) re-derived; pointwise chain checked numerically") -> XF VERIFIED (A-REV2 §2: "Explicit constant and pointwise-in-m uniform tail-probability bound are correct") -> A-REV5 VERIFIED core.
- Proved by / checked by: W1-T03R (Opus 5.5) / W2-VT03R (Opus 5.5, 60 stress designs incl. near-collinear) / A-REV2 and A-REV5 (Astra).

### TH126 — Proposition E3 (the exact-tail route cannot give $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)$)  [proposition]
- Source: `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §1; verified `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` row 8; `A-REV2/REVIEW.md` §2, §3.1; positions [pos 296], [pos 342], [pos 370], [pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ### Proposition E3 (the exact-tail route cannot give $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)$; PROVED)
> In R1 with $s_0\ge1$ fixed and $n^{a}\le p_n\le n^A$ for some fixed $0<a\le A$: either $m^\sharp_n=K$ or
> $$m^\sharp_n-s_0\ \ge\ \frac{s_0\log(p/s_0)+\frac{s_0+2}2\log n}{\log2}-1-o(1)\ \ge\ \frac{(s_0a+\frac{s_0+2}{2})\log n-s_0\log s_0}{\log 2}-1-o(1).$$
> Since $s_0\log n/\log p\le s_0/a=O(1)$, the brief's target scale $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)$ is not reached by any bound of the form "Markov numerator over $S_0$-denominator" (the form of the locked T02(i) and of Theorem T02(i♯) below): such a bound is at least $R_m(n+1)^{s_0/2}\sqrt n\cdot c$ with $R_m$ two-sided-controlled by E1.
>
> *Remark (not a claim about the true posterior).* E3 is a barrier for the proof technique. Whether the *true* posterior needs $m_n-s_0\asymp s_0\log p$ under G and R is **OPEN**. Proposition D below shows that *some* growth, $m_n\ge(\tfrac12-o(1))\log_2 n$, is necessary in general.

- Earlier versions / repairs: none to the statement. The W6-FIXREV2 scope sentence (verbatim): "Prop. E3 (S03, PROVED): for this route — a Markov numerator over an S₀-denominator with the exact-tail cutoff — the cutoff cannot be s₀ + O(s₀ log n/log p). It is a barrier for this proof route only, not a lower bound for the posterior." A-REV2: "A barrier for the defined exact-tail cutoff and the specified numerator/denominator envelope; not a posterior lower bound or a universal impossibility theorem for other proof techniques."
- Status history: PROVED (W1-T03R) -> VERIFIED (W2-VT03R: "as a statement about m♯. 'Any bound of this form' is a correct reading for bounds of the type Markov numerator / S₀-denominator") -> VERIFIED* (A-REV2: barrier only).
- Proved by / checked by: W1-T03R / W2-VT03R / A-REV2.
- Depends on: LM101, LM102.
- Feeds: scope sentence of S-T (K93).
- Notes: under the T03-sharp hypotheses the posterior concentrates on size $s_0$ (TH129), so the $\Theta(s_0\log n)$ cutoff is a property of the SE-free route only. Whether the true posterior needs $m-s_0\asymp s_0\log p$ is CJ131.

### CE111 — Prop D: duplicated-column counterexample (hoped-for $m_n$ is false without SE)  [counterexample]
- Source (authoritative): `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §3 (design, claim and proof); `W1-T03R/REPORT.md` §3 and §1 item 1; reproduced in `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` row 11 and §4.2; verified `A-REV2/REVIEW.md` §3.5; positions [pos 296], [pos 342], [pos 370], [pos 570].
- Construction and claim (verbatim):

> ## 3. Proposition D: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the target scale without SE (COUNTEREXAMPLE, reproducible)
>
> **Design.** $n\ge3$, $2\le p$ (e.g. $p=n$, so $A=1$), $x\in\mathbb R^n$ fixed with $\|Cx\|^2=n-1$, $X^r=[x,\dots,x]$ ($p$ identical columns), $\beta^*=(\beta_1,0,\dots,0)$ with fixed $\beta_1\ne0$, any $\alpha^*$, $\sigma_*>0$. Then $s_0=1$, $S_0=\{1\}$, $\tilde x:=Cx$ is every standardised column, $\|\mu\|^2/n=\beta_1^2(n-1)/n\le\beta_1^2=:M$, $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0})=1$: **G and R hold** (SE fails at size 2).
>
> **Claim.** With $E_n:=\{m(\emptyset)\le m(\{1\})\}$, $P_0(E_n)\to1$, and on $E_n$, for every integer $0\le m\le K-1$,
> $$\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\ \ge\ 2^{-(m+4)}\exp\Big\{-\frac{m(m-1)}{4(p-m)}\Big\}.$$
> Consequently, for any deterministic $m_n\le\sqrt p$ with $\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)=O_{P_0}(n^{-1/2})$, necessarily $m_n\ge\frac12\log_2n-O(1)$; in particular no cutoff $m_n=s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)=1+O(1)$ (here $p=n$) works, and more generally $\Pi(|S|>m_n\mid y)=O_{P_0}(e^{-\omega_n})$ forces $m_n\ge\omega_n/\log2-O(1)$.
>
> **Reproduction:** `scripts/duplicate_counterexample.py` (output in `duplicate_counterexample_output.txt`): $2^m\,\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\in[0.70,1.00]$ for $m\le16$, $n\in\{200,\dots,2\cdot10^5\}$; the smallest $m$ with $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\le n^{-1/2}$ is $4,6,8,9$ for $n=200,2000,20000,200000$ ($\approx\frac12\log_2n$); 200/200 replicate data sets at $n=p=2000$ satisfy $\Pi(|S|>m\mid y)\ge2^{-m}/8$ for all $m\le12$.

- Earlier versions / repairs: W1 headline 1 read more broadly ("The brief's premise about m_n is false"); W2-VT03R R2 replaced it with: "The brief's premise about m_n is false for the SE-free size-tail route (T02(i)); under G and R alone it is false outright (Prop. D)." and W2-VT03R Prop D-prime (TH129) fixes the scope.
- Status history: COUNTEREXAMPLE (reproducible) (W1-T03R) -> VERIFIED (W2-VT03R row 11: "every constant re-derived: √(2/3)/(½+e^{1.01}) = 0.25157 ≥ ¼ (margin 0.0016); ((n+1)N+1)(N+0.02) ≤ 2nN² ⇔ n²−3.02n+2 ≥ 0"; brute-force over all models $n=8$-16 agrees with the closed form to $1.1\times10^{-13}$; $P(E_n)=1.000$ at every tested $n$ up to $2\times10^5$; required cutoff $\lceil\tfrac12\log_2 n\rceil$) -> VERIFIED (A-REV2 §2: "Duplicate-design counterexample under G and R, outside the SE hypotheses"; §3.5 below).
- Proved by / checked by: W1-T03R (Opus 5.5) / W2-VT03R (independent script `propD_independent.py`) / A-REV2 (Astra: "The rank-one formulas for `D_k` and `Q_k` are correct. ... The necessity statement uses `m<=min(sqrt(p),K-1)`; a zero tail beyond K is not a counterexample to its restricted claim.").
- Depends on: LM101 (E1(a) with $s_0=0$ and E1(c)), TH101 (T01) `lem:spec`(b), ⟦00_COMMON⟧ score.
- Feeds: refutes RF121; related card PropD-T03 in S-LIM (K100 duplicates clause: "PropD-T03 XF-VERIFIED").
- Notes: A-REV2 §3.5 (verbatim, first paragraphs):

> The rank-one formulas for `D_k` and `Q_k` are correct. For `k>=1`, the comparison with `m_1`
> is bounded below by `sqrt(2/3)` and above by `exp(1.01)`. The tail constant is safe:
> `sqrt(2/3)/(1/2+exp(1.01))>1/4`. Multiplying by the E1 lower bound gives the stated `2^(-m-4)`.
> The squared sample correlation tends to the positive signal fraction when the fixed coefficient
> is nonzero, so the event `m_empty<=m_1` has probability tending to one. The necessity statement
> uses `m<=min(sqrt(p),K-1)`; a zero tail beyond K is not a counterexample to its restricted claim.
>
> This example satisfies G and R but violates even size-two SE. It does not contradict T03♯.
> Under T03♯, the posterior tail above `s0` itself is at most `1-pi(S0)=O_P(r_n)`.
