### RF121 — "The exact BB(1,p) tail cuts $m_n$ to $s_0+O(s_0\log n/\log p)$, so SE is meaningful at n = 200"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim (verbatim):

>   - Replace T02(i)'s geometric tail 2^−m with the exact BB(1,p) tail. This cuts m_n from about 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p), so SE on sets of size ≤ m_n + s₀ ≤ K becomes meaningful at n = 200 (Fable).
>
> - **Thm 1, T03 (+T01, T02).** Replace the 2^{−m} geometric size tail in T02(i) by the exact BB(1,p) tail (ratio ≈ k/2p, not ½); m_n drops from ≈ 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p), which makes SE on sets of size ≤ m_n + s₀ ≤ K meaningful at n = 200. Replace M_* by an unnamed C in θ² ≥ C σ² (log n + log p)/n, or use BM-∞. s₀ fixed, p ≤ n^A, K_n = ⌊n/2⌋. Failure point: uniform Gaussian-maximum control over C(p, k) subsets with the (n+1)^{−1/2} determinant penalty. Optional upgrade if T03 closes fast: s₀ → ∞ with s₀ log p = o(n), statistical half only.
>
>   - replace T02(i)'s 2^−m size tail by the exact BB(1,p) tail, which cuts m_n from about 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p);
>
> ## TASK
> 1. T02(i): replace the 2^{-m} model-size tail by the EXACT BB(1,p) tail; this should cut the size threshold m_n from ~200 to s0 + O(s0 log n / log p). Prove the sharpened tail bound with explicit constants.
> 2. T03 restatement: restrict SE (sparse eigenvalue condition) to the comparison unions actually used in the proof (not all subsets); replace the provisional constant M* by BM-inf or an unnamed constant; s0 fixed, p_n <= n^A, triangular array. Re-derive: posterior mass outside S0 is O_P(sqrt(log n / n)); PIPs within that of the 0/1 truth; HPM and MPM of the true posterior = S0 w.p.->1; without beta-min, large signals still get PIP -> 1.
> 3. Identify exactly which steps of the locked proofs change; write the new proofs of changed steps in full; cite unchanged steps by label.
> 4. n=200 honesty paragraph: at n=200 SE is impossible (rank <= 199 vs subsets of 215-229 columns) and beta-min fails by ~100x in squared signal. Write the precise disclosure paragraph; give any finite-n statement that survives.
> 5. Evaluate the new tail bound numerically at (n,p,s0) = (200,500,14), (200,1000,14) and larger n; compare with the old bound.
> Read first: 00_COMMON.md, the T01/T02/T03 statements and proofs, METHODOLOGY_v3.md prior sections.

- Refutation (verbatim, W1-T03R REPORT headline 1 and §4 first bullet):

> 1. **The brief's premise about m_n is false. The exact BB(1,p) tail does not bring m_n down to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p).** The BB(1,p) size marginal is exactly geometric with ratio ρ_i = ½(1 − (i−1)/(2p−1−i)) (Lemma E1(a)). The per-model ratio w(k+1)/w(k) ≈ k/(2p), quoted in FABLE_REVIEW and FROZEN_LIST, is cancelled by the multiplicity C(p,k+1)/C(p,k) ≈ p/k. The exact tail improves the locked bound by the factor 4·s₀!·e^{γ_m}: about 36 bits at s₀ = 14, plus m²/(4p) nats. It cannot do more:
>    - **PROVED (Prop. E3):** the two-sided bound E1 shows that any bound of the T02(i) form needs m − s₀ ≥ log₂C(p,s₀) + ((s₀+2)/2)log₂n − O(1).
>    - **COUNTEREXAMPLE (Prop. D, reproducible):** under G and R alone, a design with duplicated columns has Π(|S|>m | y) ≥ 2^{−(m+4)}e^{−m²/(4(p−m))} with probability → 1. So *no* cutoff s₀ + O(1) gives an O_P(n^{−1/2}) tail; at least ½log₂n − O(1) is necessary.
>
> - **The frozen-plan sentence "cuts m_n from about 200 to s₀ + O(s₀ log n / log p), so SE on sets of size ≤ m_n + s₀ ≤ K becomes meaningful at n = 200" is wrong on both counts.**
>   - The exact tail saves ~36–55 sizes, not ~180. The reason is in Lemma E1(a): the size marginal is geometric(½), so the truth's prior cost log C(p,s₀) ≈ s₀ log p must be repaid at log 2 nats per extra size.
>   - Prop. D shows that, without eigenvalue conditions, even the true posterior can need m_n ≳ ½log₂n.
>   - What does make SE meaningful at n = 200 is the **cap**: m♯ ≤ K always.

- Counterexample: CE111 (Prop D); proved barrier: TH126 (Prop E3); proved structure: LM101.
- Replacement result: TH125 (T02(i-sharp)), whose cutoff is $m^\sharp_n\le\min(K,m_n)$ (LM102) of order $s_0\log n$; the only thing that makes SE finite-sized at $n=200$ is the cap $K=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ (LM102 notes). W1-T03R "Needs escalation" 1 asks HQ to correct the FROZEN_LIST sentence; the suggested text (verbatim): "Use the exact BB tail R_m (saves log₂ s₀! ≈ 36 sizes); the cap K binds at n = 200, so the anchored SE ranges over ≤ K + s₀ = 114 columns."
- Status: REFUTED. SF: W2-VT03R VERIFIED (with scope R2: false for the SE-free route, outright false under G and R alone). XF: A-REV2 VERIFIED (Prop D, E1-E3). HQ acted on it at [pos 342] ("The planned sharper size cutoff in T02 can't hold: a counterexample with duplicated columns rules it out.") and [pos 370].
- Origin of the claim: FABLE_REVIEW and FROZEN_LIST (paper selection of 2026-10-28, "Restatement notes — T03 / T02"), THEORY_PRIORITIES, and the HQ-written W1-T03R task BRIEF items 1 and 4 (all quoted above); the Fable review names as failure point "uniform Gaussian-maximum control over C(p, k) subsets with the (n+1)^{−1/2} determinant penalty".

### LM104 — Lemma I (interlacing) and Lemma B (B1)-(B3), with the anchored hypotheses SE_lambda(j0), SE_w(m;g0)  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §4; verified `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` row 13 (9,000 random pairs), row 12 (implied by the locked SE); `A-REV2/REVIEW.md` §3.3; positions [pos 296], [pos 370], [pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim; hypotheses first):

> ## 4. Restricted eigenvalue hypotheses and bookkeeping
>
> **Hypotheses (new).** Let $j_0:=\lceil(2A+1)s_0\rceil+1$ (this is $j_*$ of [P3]; it depends only on $s_0,A$) and $g_0>0$ a fixed constant.
>
> - **SE$_\lambda(j_0)$** [anchored, normalised, bounded size]: $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0\cup J})\ge\varphi_0^2$ for every $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $|J|\le j_0$ and $S_0\cup J\ne\emptyset$.
> - **SE$_w(m;g_0)$** [anchored, unnormalised]: $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S_0\cup J})\ge g_0$ (equivalently $\lambda_{\min}(R_{S_0\cup J})\ge g_0/(n-1)$) for every $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $|J|\le m$ and $S_0\cup J\ne\emptyset$.
>
> These are restrictions of SE to the **comparison unions** $S\cup S_0$ used by the proofs. The locked SE (all $T$ with $|T|\le\min(p,m_n+s_0)$, constant $\varphi_0^2$) implies SE$_\lambda(j_0)$ (as $j_0\le m_n$ for large $n$) and SE$_w(m^\sharp_n;\varphi_0^2)$ (as $m^\sharp_n\le m_n$ by E2(i), and $(n-1)\varphi_0^2\ge\varphi_0^2$). So the new hypotheses are weaker.
>
> **Lemma I (interlacing; standard).** If $\emptyset\ne T\subseteq T'$, then $\lambda_{\min}(G_T)\ge\lambda_{\min}(G_{T'})$. *Proof.* For $v\in\mathbb R^T$, $v^\top G_Tv=\tilde v^\top G_{T'}\tilde v$ with $\tilde v$ the zero-padding, and $\|\tilde v\|=\|v\|$. $\square$
>
> **Lemma B (what the proofs need; PROVED).** Assume R, SE$_\lambda(j_0)$ and SE$_w(m^\sharp_n;g_0)$.
> - **(B1)** For $J\subseteq[p]\setminus S_0$ with $1\le|J|\le m^\sharp_n$: $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S_0\cup J})\ge g_0>0$, so $X_{c,S_0\cup J}$ has full column rank, $P_{S_0\cup J}-P_{S_0}$ is an orthogonal projection of rank $|J|$, and under G, $\chi^2_J:=\sigma_*^{-2}\|(P_{S_0\cup J}-P_{S_0})e\|^2\sim\chi^2_{|J|}$ exactly; and $D_{S_0\cup J}/D_{S_0}\ge[(n+1)(1+1/g_0)^{-1}]^{|J|}$.
> - **(B2)** For underfitting $S$ (i.e. $S_0\not\subseteq S$) with $|J'(S)|\le j_0$, $S'=S\cup S_0$: $\lambda_{\min}(G_{S'})\ge N\varphi_0^2$; if $S\ne\emptyset$, $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge N\varphi_0^2$; $P_{S'}-P_S$ is an orthogonal projection of rank $|J(S)|$; under G, $N_S/\sigma_*^2\sim\chi^2_{|J(S)|}$.
> - **(B3)** For $S\subseteq T$, $T\ne\emptyset$, with $S=\emptyset$ or $\lambda_{\min}(G_S)\ge N\varphi_0^2$, and every $u\in\mathbb R^N$: $u^\top(M_T-M_S)u\le\frac n{n+1}\big[\|(P_T-P_S)u\|^2+\eta_n\|P_Su\|^2\big]$. (Upper half of [P3] `cor:diff`, with the eigenvalue condition on $S$ only.)

- Earlier versions / repairs: the locked SE was "$\lambda_{\min}(R_T)\ge\varphi_0^2$ for every nonempty $T$ with $|T|\le\min(p,m_n+s_0)$" (TH121 setting). W1-T03R replaced it by these two anchored conditions; the locked SE implies both (W2-VT03R row 12: "for n with j0 ≤ m_n; SE_w with g0 = φ0²"). W6-FIXREV2 §1.1 keeps both and adds: "g₀ > 0 is a **fixed constant** (a sequence g₀,n → 0 is not covered)".

### LM105 — Lemma A1 (anchored = unanchored up to $s_0$ columns)  [lemma]
- Source: `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` §2 (new in the verification run) and §3 R2; restated in `W6-FIXREV2/STATEMENTS.md` §1.1 ("Equivalent forms"); `A-REV2/REVIEW.md` §3.3; positions [pos 337], [pos 370], [pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Lemma A1 (anchored = unanchored up to s₀ columns; PROVED).** Let g > 0 and m ≥ 0. The following are equivalent:
> - (a) λ_min(G_{S₀∪J}) ≥ g for every J ⊆ [p]∖S₀ with |J| ≤ m and S₀ ∪ J ≠ ∅;
> - (b) λ_min(G_T) ≥ g for every nonempty T ⊆ [p] with |T∖S₀| ≤ m.
>
> The same holds with R in place of G and φ₀² in place of g.
>
> *Proof.* (b) ⇒ (a): T = S₀ ∪ J has T∖S₀ = J. (a) ⇒ (b): T ⊆ S₀ ∪ (T∖S₀) with J := T∖S₀, |J| ≤ m. By Cauchy interlacing (W1 Lemma I), λ_min(G_T) ≥ λ_min(G_{S₀∪J}) ≥ g. ∎
>
> Consequences:
> - SE_w(m; g₀) implies the unanchored non-degeneracy λ_min(G_T) ≥ g₀ for **all** T with |T| ≤ m.
> - In particular, every m columns of X are linearly independent: spark(X) > m.
> - At n = 200 with m♯ = K = 100, SE_w requires every 100 columns of X to be linearly independent with λ_min(XᵀX) ≥ g₀, and every 114-set that contains S₀ likewise.
> - SE_λ(j₀) requires normalised conditioning φ₀² on **every** set of ≤ j₀ columns, null columns included. So SE_λ(j₀) fails for every fixed φ₀ > 0 once n > 1/φ₀² if a single pair of null columns has correlation 1 − 1/n. Such a pair constrains SE_w only to g₀ ≤ λ_min(G_{{a,b}}) = (n−1)(1−r) = (n−1)/n, so it is compatible with SE_w for any fixed g₀ < 1/2 (n ≥ 2).

- W6-FIXREV2 §1.1 version (verbatim):

>   *Equivalent forms* (V03 Lemma A1, PROVED; interlacing): SE_λ(j₀) ⇔ λ_min(R_T) ≥ φ₀² for every nonempty T with
>   |T∖S₀| ≤ j₀; SE_w(m♯_n; g₀) ⇔ λ_min(G_T) ≥ g₀ for every nonempty T with |T∖S₀| ≤ m♯_n. In particular SE_w(m♯_n; g₀)
>   forces every m♯_n columns of X to be linearly independent. "Anchoring" is therefore not a restriction to a hand-picked
>   list of sets; the substantive savings are the size cutoff m♯_n and the unnormalised constant for large sets.

- Earlier versions / repairs: none; it is the correction of the W1-T03R wording RF128 ("restricted to the comparison unions actually used"). W2-VT03R R2 supplies the replacement paper sentence (quoted in RF128).
- Status history: PROVED (W2-VT03R, author = verifier; no second same-family check) -> A-REV2 §3.3 (verbatim): "Anchoring is not a restriction to a small handpicked list of matrices. By interlacing it is equivalent to the same bound on every nonempty T with `|T\S0|<=m` (and analogously for j0). The substantive savings are the cutoff and the normalization for the larger sets." (no verdict row).
- Proved by / checked by: W2-VT03R (Opus 5.5); statement independently noted by A-REV2 and by LIT-STAT (H3: "close to Rossell's v̄ over sizes in [p_t, p̄]").
- Depends on: LM104 (Lemma I).
- Feeds: TH128 scope; the paper must not advertise anchoring as the main relaxation (W2-VT03R escalation 2).
- Notes: consequences listed in the quote: SE_w(100) at n = 200 forces spark(X) > 100; SE_lambda(j0) fails for every fixed $\varphi_0>0$ once $n>1/\varphi_0^2$ if one pair of null columns has correlation $1-1/n$.

### TH128 — Theorem 1 = T03-sharp (T03♯): posterior target consistency under anchored, size-restricted eigenvalue conditions  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative, latest repaired version): `W6-FIXREV2/STATEMENTS.md` §1.1-§1.2 ("statement of record"); original `W1-T03R/REPORT.md` §1 and `W1-T03R/PROOF.md` §6; positions: launch [pos 233]/[pos 238]; result [pos 296]/[pos 342]; verification launched [pos 334]/[pos 337], reported [pos 370]; Astra [pos 570]; repair pushed [pos 736]/[pos 742]; synthesis [pos 796]; literature verdict [pos 1009]/[pos 1142].
- Statement (verbatim, W6-FIXREV2 §1.1 hypotheses, then §1.2 theorem and the scope that must accompany it):

> ### 1.1 Setting and hypotheses
>
> - **R1.** Triangular array, n → ∞; X = X_n fixed (non-random); s₀ ≥ 1 fixed; p = p_n ≤ n^A with A fixed; s₀ ≤ K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋) for all large n.
> - **G.** y^r = α*1 + X^rβ* + ε, ε ~ N_n(0, σ*²I), σ*² > 0 fixed; μ = Xθ*, S₀ = supp β*.
> - **R.** ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn and λ_min(R_{S₀}) ≥ φ₀² > 0, with M, φ₀ fixed.
> - **Size tail objects (data-free).** q_k := C(p,k)w(k). For every integer m,
>   R_m := Σ_{k = max(m+1, 0)}^{K} q_k / w(s₀)  (empty sum = 0; so R_m = 0 for m ≥ K).
>   For real ω, m♯_n(ω) := min{m ∈ ℤ : m ≥ s₀, R_m ≤ n^{−(s₀+1)/2}e^{−ω}} (it exists and is ≤ K); m♯_n := m♯_n(½ log n).
>   m♯_n is a deterministic function of (n, p, s₀); it is never selected from the response.
>
> - **SE_λ(j₀)** (normalised, anchored, bounded size): j₀ := ⌈(2A+1)s₀⌉ + 1, and λ_min(R_{S₀∪J}) ≥ φ₀² for every
>   J ⊆ [p]∖S₀ with |J| ≤ j₀.
> - **SE_w(m♯_n; g₀)** (unnormalised, anchored): g₀ > 0 is a **fixed constant** (a sequence g₀,n → 0 is not covered), and
>   λ_min(G_{S₀∪J}) ≥ g₀ for every J ⊆ [p]∖S₀ with |J| ≤ m♯_n.
>   *Equivalent forms* (V03 Lemma A1, PROVED; interlacing): SE_λ(j₀) ⇔ λ_min(R_T) ≥ φ₀² for every nonempty T with
>   |T∖S₀| ≤ j₀; SE_w(m♯_n; g₀) ⇔ λ_min(G_T) ≥ g₀ for every nonempty T with |T∖S₀| ≤ m♯_n. In particular SE_w(m♯_n; g₀)
>   forces every m♯_n columns of X to be linearly independent. "Anchoring" is therefore not a restriction to a hand-picked
>   list of sets; the substantive savings are the size cutoff m♯_n and the unnormalised constant for large sets.
> - **Beta-min** (for (i)–(iii)): **BM-∞**: min_{j∈S₀} θ*_j² ≥ M_nσ*² log n/(nφ₀²) with M_n → ∞; or **BM(c)**: the same with a
>   fixed c > c₀(s₀, A) := L_* = max{4C_*, 32[s₀(A+1)+2]} (C_* of the locked T03 proof; a proof artefact, not sharp).
>
> **Theorem T03♯.** Status: PROVED (S03 §6; changed steps C1–C10 written in full there); V03 and A-REV2: VERIFIED under exactly
> these hypotheses. Assume R1, G, R, SE_λ(j₀) and SE_w(m♯_n; g₀); for (i)–(iii) also BM-∞ or BM(c) with c > c₀(s₀, A).
> 1. 1 − π(S₀) = O_{P₀}(r_n).
> 2. For every data set, max_j |PIP_j − 1{j ∈ S₀}| ≤ 1 − π(S₀); hence P₀(MPM = S₀) → 1.
> 3. P₀(S† ≠ S₀) ≤ 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)] → 0, where S† is the global HPM. (Only convergence is claimed: boundedness of 1 − π(S₀)
>    turns convergence in probability into convergence of the expectation, not into an O(r_n) bound on it.) On the event
>    {π(S₀) > ½}, S₀ is the strict global maximiser of F, so no tie rule is used.
> 4. (No beta-min.) For fixed c > c₀(s₀, A) let J_n(c) := {j ∈ S₀ : θ*_j² ≥ cσ*² log n/(nφ₀²)}. Then
>    Π(S ⊉ J_n(c) | y) = O_{P₀}(r_n) and 1 − min_{j∈J_n(c)} PIP_j = O_{P₀}(r_n), with the convention min_∅ := 1 (the claim is
>    vacuous when J_n(c) = ∅). The same holds for J_n^∞ = {j : θ*_j² ≥ M_nσ*² log n/(nφ₀²)} with any M_n → ∞.
> 5. Scale invariance as in the locked T03.
>
> **Scope (must accompany the theorem).**
> - This is posterior / global-HPM theory. It says nothing about the reported HPM Ŝ (discovery by the sampler).
> - Prop. E3 (S03, PROVED): for this route — a Markov numerator over an S₀-denominator with the exact-tail cutoff — the
>   cutoff cannot be s₀ + O(s₀ log n/log p). It is a barrier for this proof route only, not a lower bound for the posterior.
> - Prop. D (S03, COUNTEREXAMPLE): under G and R alone (duplicate columns), Π(|S| > m | y) ≥ 2^{−(m+4)}e^{−m(m−1)/(4(p−m))}
>   on an event of probability → 1, so some growth m_n ≳ ½ log₂ n is needed in general. It violates size-2 SE and does not
>   contradict T03♯ (under T03♯, Π(|S| > s₀ | y) ≤ 1 − π(S₀) = O_P(r_n), V03 Prop. D′).
> - **Finite-n disclosure (corrected; replaces S03's "≈ 1.2·10⁵").** With s₀ = 14, p = round(n^A), 1/g₀ → 0 (most
>   favourable) and exact m♯_n, the proof as written needs δ_n ≤ ½ (first n = 115,150 / 130,328 for A = log 500/log 200 /
>   log 1000/log 200), the geometric-series condition q_n ≤ ½ (first n = **2,116,048 / 2,457,025**), and, only to fix the
>   displayed constant c_q, e^{2ε_n} ≤ 4 (first n = 25,571,897 / 29,755,302). At S03's n = 130,328, q_n ≈ 5.53·10²² (A = 1.17)
>   and 7.86·10²⁸ (A = 1.30). These are checks of named conditions, **not a universal n₀**: other thresholds involve the signal,
>   variance and eigenvalue constants and the BM sequence. At (n, p) = (200, 500) and (200, 1000), m♯_n = K = 100 (the cap
>   binds; uncapped m♯_n would be 146 and 168, locked m_n = 201 and 215); the cap removes the dimension-tail term there but
>   does not verify SE_λ, SE_w or BM, and the O_P rate is not numerically informative.
>   Replacement sentence for the disclosure: "…and the proof's own deterministic thresholds (as written) hold only from
>   n ≈ 2×10⁶ (p = n^{1.17}) to 2.5×10⁶ (p = n^{1.30}); the O_P constants are unspecified."
>   (Independent recomputation: `scripts/t03_thresholds.py`, `results/t03_thresholds.txt`; it agrees with V03 R1 and A-REV2 §3.5
>   to the integer.)

### TH130 — Proposition W (SE_lambda is needed only for the signal)  [proposition, PROOF SKETCH]
- Source: `W2-VT03R/REPORT.md` §2 and §6 item 3; positions [pos 337], [pos 370].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Proposition W (SE_λ is needed only for the signal; PROOF SKETCH).** Define, for c > 0:
>
> > **SIG(c):** for all large n, every underfitting S with |S| ≤ m♯_n and |J′(S)| ≤ j₀ has Δ_S = ‖(I−P_S)μ_c‖² ≥ cσ*² log n.
>
> Assume R1, G, R (including λ_min(R_{S₀}) ≥ φ₀²), SE_w(m♯_n; g₀) and SIG(c) with c ≥ L*. Then T03♯(i)–(iii) hold.
>
> SE_λ(j₀) + BM(c) implies SIG((1−1/n)c), by [P3] `lem:signal`. So Prop. W contains T03♯(i)–(iii).
>
> *Sketch.* SE_λ(j₀) enters W1's proof in exactly three places: (C3) = `lem:ongood`(c), the lower half of `cor:diff` inside (C6)(b), and `lem:signal` in (C10). Each is handled as follows.
>
> 1. **`lem:ongood`(c).** Take S ≠ ∅ underfitting with |J′(S)| ≤ j₀. SE_w and interlacing give λ_min(G_S) ≥ g₀. [P1] `lem:spec`(c) then gives I − M_S ⪯ (I−P_S) + (1+1/g₀)(n+1)^{−1}P_S. So 2b + Q^c_S ≤ E′_n + V_S, where:
>    - E′_n := 2b + ‖e‖² + (1+1/g₀)(n+1)^{−1}‖y_c‖²;
>    - on 𝒢_n, Nσ*²(1−δ_n) ≤ E′_n ≤ Nσ*²(1+δ‴_n);
>    - δ‴_n := 3√(log n/N) + (12b₀ + 4(1+1/g₀))(M+σ*²)/(Nσ*²) → 0.
>
>    (Checked numerically as [OGc′], §4.3.)
> 2. **Lower half of `cor:diff` with an eigenvalue bound g₀ on T = S′ only.** M_{S′} − M_S ⪰ (n/(n+1))[(P_{S′} − P_S) − η′P_{S′}], with η′ = 1/((n+1)g₀). (Checked as [CDl′].) In `lem:SvsSp` the subtracted term is
>
>    ν(n/(n+1))η′‖y_c‖²/E′_n ≤ 8n²(M+σ*²)/((n²−1)g₀σ*²) ≤ ρ′ := 9(M+σ*²)/(g₀σ*²),
>
>    a constant. The second inequality of `lem:SvsSp` holds once δ‴_n ≤ 1.
> 3. **`lem:signalgain`.** Use Δ_S ≥ L*σ*² log n directly from SIG, and (G4), which needs no eigenvalue condition. This gives κ_n(𝒰) ≤ e^{ρ′}n^{−2} on 𝒢_n. The constant e^{ρ′} does not affect any rate. The rest is T03♯ verbatim.
>
> Status PROOF SKETCH: the verbatim parts were not re-typeset line by line, and (iv) needs a per-coordinate version of SIG that I did not write.

### TH131 — Prop 1 (T07 + T06(i)): decision rules and the sharp size-prior ceiling  [proposition]
- Source (authoritative, latest version): `W5-LOCKBOOK/STATEMENTS.tex` (Proposition "Decision rules and the size-prior ceiling; Prop. 1"), with proofs of the new clauses in `W2-BOOK/PROOF.md` §3 and the tie-aware amendment of `A-REV6/BOOK.md` R3; positions: W2-BOOK launched [pos 334]/[pos 342], reported [pos 358], [pos 424]; W5-LOCKBOOK launched [pos 509]/[pos 510], pushed 19:00 [pos 736]; A-REV4 launched [pos 677]/[pos 678]; A-REV6 launched [pos 807]; HQ statements [pos 550], [pos 1238]; literature [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim, W5-LOCKBOOK STATEMENTS.tex):

```tex
\begin{proposition}[Decision rules and the size-prior ceiling; Prop.~1]\label{prop:decision}
Let $\pi$ be the target posterior on $\Omega=\{S:|S|\le K\}$, $m$ the marginal likelihood, $\prec$ the method's tie
order (smaller size, then lexicographic), and $S^*_k$ the $\prec$-least maximiser of $m$ among models of size $k$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] The HPM is a Bayes rule for $0$--$1$ loss on supports; the median probability model
  $\{j:\mathrm{PIP}_j>\tfrac12\}$ is a Bayes rule for Hamming loss over all subsets, unique iff no
  $\mathrm{PIP}_j=\tfrac12$ (over $\Omega$: keep the $\min(K,N_+)$ largest PIPs above $\tfrac12$).
\item[(ii)] For any PIP estimate $\hat p$, the plug-in Hamming rule has excess posterior risk at most
  $2\|\hat p-\mathrm{PIP}\|_1$.
\item[(iii)] If $s_0\le K$, some positive size-only prior has global HPM $S_0$ if and only if $S^*_{s_0}=S_0$. Hence a
  within-size ranking error ($S\ne S_0$, $|S|=s_0$, $m(S)\ge m(S_0)$) is exactly the error that no re-tuning of the
  size prior, including any truncated beta-binomial, can repair; the repairing prior in the converse depends on the data.
\item[(iv)] (Certificate.) If a scored model $S'\ne S_0$ with $|S'|=s_0$ has an exactly computed score above that of
  $S_0$, then no positive size-only prior recovers $S_0$ on those data.
\item[(v)] Two supports have equal score for every response iff $X_SX_S^\top=X_{S'}X_{S'}^\top$ (equal outer
  products, not merely equal spans); they then have equal size and nothing in the data or in a size-only prior
  separates them.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}
% Hypotheses: none beyond m > 0 (finite, deterministic). Used for data: (iv) needs the score gap to exceed numerical
% error (the engine's error bound is heuristic).

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

- Earlier versions (verbatim):
  - (a) Locked T07 (wave 3, `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/STATEMENT.md` §2):

> ## 2. T07: size-only ranking ceiling and Bayes decisions
>
> Setting. m is the marginal likelihood (only m > 0 is used). ≺ is the tie order above; any fixed total order on subsets of [p] works. For a positive size-only prior on Ω, w̃(k) > 0 for 0 ≤ k ≤ K and ϖ_w̃(S) = w̃(|S|)/Σ_{k≤K} C(p,k) w̃(k). S†_w̃ is the ≺-least element of argmax_{S∈Ω} ϖ_w̃(S)m(S). For 0 ≤ k ≤ p, S*_k is the ≺-least element of argmax_{|S|=k} m(S).
>
> **(i) Ceiling.** For every response and every positive size-only prior w̃, {S†_w̃ = S₀} ⊆ {S*_{s₀} = S₀}. Here s₀ ≤ K on the left event, which is empty when s₀ > K. Equivalently: on {S*_{s₀} ≠ S₀} (a within-size ranking error, S₀ beaten or ≺-preceded within its size by m), S†_w̃ ≠ S₀ for every positive size-only prior. No size-only prior repairs it.
>
> **(ii) Bayes decisions.** π is the target posterior on Ω. J₊ = {j : PIP_j > ½} and N₊ = |J₊|. The posterior risk of an action a under a loss L is ρ_L(a) = Σ_S π(S) L(a, S).
>
> (a) For the 0–1 loss on supports, L(a, S) = 1{a ≠ S} with a ⊆ [p]: ρ(a) = 1 − π(a) (with π(a) = 0 for a ∉ Ω). The minimisers over all a ⊆ [p] are exactly argmax_Ω F, and S† is one of them.
>
> (b) For the Hamming loss, L(a, S) = |a △ S| with a ⊆ [p]: MPM = J₊ minimises ρ_H over all subsets of [p]. It is the unique minimiser if and only if no PIP_j equals ½.
>
> (c) Capped. Put ℓ = min(K, N₊). Let a* ⊆ J₊ be the ℓ elements of J₊ with the largest PIPs, with ties at the boundary broken by a fixed deterministic rule. Then a* minimises ρ_H over Ω = {a : |a| ≤ K}.
>
> **(iii) Target versus reported decisions.** (i)–(ii) concern S†, π and PIP. (Interpretation, not a separate claim: for the reported objects they hold only through scoring and estimation events.)
>
> (a) Ŝ = S† if and only if S† ∈ 𝒮. Ŝ minimises the posterior 0–1 loss if and only if 𝒮 ∩ argmax_Ω F ≠ ∅.
>
> (b) {Ŝ = S₀} ∩ {S*_{s₀} ≠ S₀} ⊆ {S*_{s₀} ∉ 𝒮}. (Interpretation, not a separate claim: the ceiling of (i) is a statement about S†; for Ŝ the corresponding event depends on 𝒮.)
>
> (c) Let p̂ ∈ [0,1]^p be any PIP estimate and 𝒜 the action class: all subsets for the MPM rule, Ω for the capped rule. Let â minimise Σ_{j∈a}(1 − 2p̂_j) over 𝒜 (MPM̂ = {j : p̂_j > ½}, or the capped rule of (ii)(c) applied to p̂). For any minimiser a_opt of ρ_H over 𝒜,
>
>   0 ≤ ρ_H(â) − ρ_H(a_opt) ≤ 2 Σ_{j ∈ â △ a_opt} |p̂_j − PIP_j| ≤ 2‖p̂ − PIP‖₁.
>
> MPM̂ = MPM if and only if, for every j, p̂_j > ½ ⇔ PIP_j > ½.
>
> Interpretation (not a separate claim): the scoring events and estimation errors in (a)–(c) are not controlled by (i)–(ii). Their control is the subject of computational results (T21, T23, T26), which this document neither uses nor proves.

  - (b) Locked T06(i) (same file §1):

> **(i) Exact ties.**
>
> (a) For S, S′ ∈ Ω: F_S = F_{S′} on 𝕊 if and only if X_SX_Sᵀ = X_{S′}X_{S′}ᵀ. If X_SX_Sᵀ = X_{S′}X_{S′}ᵀ then |S| = |S′|, and moreover F(S) = F(S′) for every response vector put into the formulas.
>
> (b) Hence if span(X_S) = span(X_{S′}) but X_SX_Sᵀ ≠ X_{S′}X_{S′}ᵀ, the score functions differ somewhere on 𝕊. Such feasible pairs exist for some valid input at every n ≥ 4 (with p = 4); they never exist when K = 1 (in particular when n = 3).
>
> (c) Under G, P₀-almost surely, every exact tie F(S) = F(S′) at the observed y between models S ≠ S′ in Ω has X_SX_Sᵀ = X_{S′}X_{S′}ᵀ. Consequently, under G and NIS,
>
>   P₀(∃ S ≠ S′ in Ω with F(S) = F(S′)) = 0.

  - (c) W2-BOOK REPORT form of the restated proposition ("PROVED (locked T07(i)-(iii) and T06(i)(a); (i-prime) and (iii-prime) new, PROVED)"):

> ### Proposition 1 (T07 + T06(i)). PROVED (locked T07(i)–(iii) and T06(i)(a); (i′) and (iii′) new, PROVED).
> Let π be the target posterior. Let S*_k be the ≺-least maximiser of the marginal likelihood m among models of size k.
> 1. **Bayes rules.** Under 0–1 loss on supports, the posterior risk of a is 1 − π(a). The HPM S† = argmax π is a
>    Bayes rule for exact recovery. Under Hamming loss, the MPM {j : PIP_j > ½} is a Bayes rule, unique iff no
>    PIP_j = ½. With the size cap K, keep the min(K, N₊) largest PIPs above ½.
> 2. **Estimated PIPs.** For any estimate p̂, the plug-in Hamming rule â has excess posterior risk at most
>    2Σ_{j ∈ â Δ a_opt}|p̂_j − PIP_j| ≤ 2‖p̂ − PIP‖₁.
> 3. **Size-prior ceiling (sharp).** For s₀ ≤ K: some positive size-only prior has global HPM S₀ if and only if
>    S*_{s₀} = S₀. So a within-size ranking error, that is an S ≠ S₀ with |S| = s₀ and m(S) ≥ m(S₀) (ties by ≺), is
>    exactly the error that no re-tuning of the size prior can fix. This covers every truncated BB(a, b), including the
>    dropped BB(1,1) arm. Errors between different sizes are fixable for those data by some (data-dependent) size prior
>    iff S*_{s₀} = S₀.
> 4. **Certificate.** If a scored model S′ with |S′| = s₀ has F(S′) > F(S₀), then no positive size-only prior has global
>    HPM S₀ on these data.
> 5. **(T06(i))** Two supports have equal posterior score for every response iff X_SX_Sᵀ = X_{S′}X_{S′}ᵀ. They then have
>    equal size, and nothing in the data or in a size-only prior separates them.
>
> *Tie to the data* (preliminary ANALYSIS-H2 working tables, THEORY_PRIORITIES §5).
> - Every completed wrong HPM is a posterior miss (F(S₀) ≤ F(HPM)).
> - At c = 0.5 these are mostly same-size swaps and subsets.
> - By (4), each strict same-size swap is certified: on those data **no** size-only prior recovers S₀. That part of the
>   c = 0.5 error is a ceiling of the target (look-alike swaps), not of the prior or the sampler.
> - Subset misses are different-size errors, and the ceiling does not cover them.
> - *HQ to fill from ANALYSIS-H2:* the count of strict same-size posterior misses out of the posterior misses at
>   c = 0.5, by scenario. The data do not say whether the remaining (subset) misses satisfy S*_{s₀} = S₀; the scored set

> **(i′) Sharpness of the ceiling. PROVED.** Assume s₀ ≤ K. Then there is a positive size-only prior w̃ with
> S†_w̃ = S₀ if and only if S*_{s₀} = S₀.
>
> *Proof.*
> - (⇒) This is T07(i), locked.
> - (⇐) Let M := max_{S∈Ω} m(S) and m₀ := m(S₀) > 0. Put w̃(s₀) = 1 and w̃(k) = ε for k ≠ s₀, 0 ≤ k ≤ K, where
>   0 < ε < m₀/M. The normaliser Σ_k C(p,k)w̃(k) is common to all S, so S†_w̃ is the ≺-least maximiser of
>   w̃(|S|)·m(S).
> - If |S| ≠ s₀, then w̃·m(S) ≤ ε·M < m₀ = w̃(s₀)·m(S₀).
> - If |S| = s₀, then m(S) ≤ m₀, because S₀ = S*_{s₀} maximises m at size s₀. If m(S) = m₀ and S ≠ S₀, then
>   S₀ ≺ S, because S₀ is the ≺-least such maximiser.
> - So the maximum value m₀ is attained only at models of size s₀ with m = m₀, and S₀ is ≺-least among them. Hence
>   S†_w̃ = S₀. ∎
>
> *Reading.* The event "some size prior recovers S₀" is exactly the event "no within-size ranking error". The prior in
> the proof is data dependent (ε < m₀/M). So (i′) says nothing about one fixed prior repairing all different-size errors
> at once. It is a per-data-set statement.
>
> **(iii′) A certificate from a fitted run. PROVED.** If some scored model S′ ∈ 𝒮 satisfies |S′| = s₀, S′ ≠ S₀ and

> conclusion holds if F(S′) = F(S₀) and S′ ≺ S₀.
>
> *Proof.* |S′| = |S₀| gives ϖ(S′) = ϖ(S₀), so m(S′) > m(S₀), or m(S′) = m(S₀) with S′ ≺ S₀. In both cases S₀ is not
> the ≺-least maximiser of m at size s₀. Then apply T07(i). ∎
>
> *Corollary for the study.* A completed fit is a "posterior miss" (F(S₀) ≤ F(Ŝ), Ŝ ≠ S₀). If such a fit has
> |Ŝ| = s₀ and the inequality is strict, then S′ = Ŝ is a certificate. So every strict same-size posterior miss is a
> data set on which no size-only prior (BB(1,p) or any retuning, including the dropped BB(1,1) arm) makes the
> global HPM equal S₀. Under G and NIS, exact ties have P₀-probability 0 (T06(i)(c), locked), so "strict" holds almost
> surely. Subset and superset misses carry no such certificate. Whether S*_{s₀} = S₀ holds on them is not decidable from
> the scored set alone.
>
> **T06(i) sentence** (locked T06(i)(a)). F_S = F_{S′} as functions of the response iff X_S X_Sᵀ = X_{S′} X_{S′}ᵀ.
> Then |S| = |S′|, and the two supports have equal posterior probability for every response. No data and no size-only
> prior can separate them under this target. The added clause "no size-only prior" follows from |S| = |S′|.
> **Caution on wording.** THEORY_PRIORITIES writes "projections agree". The locked condition is equality of the outer
> products X_S X_Sᵀ, which is not equality of the projection matrices P_S (T06(i)(b): equal spans with different outer
> products give different score functions). The paper must use "outer products".

> ## R3. Tie-aware size-prior certificate (Astra candidate proof)
>
> On finite Ω with positive marginal likelihood m, let S*_k be the tie-order-first maximiser among size k. A positive size-only prior can select S0 as global tie-broken HPM iff S*_(s0)=S0. Necessity follows because the size multiplier cancels within that layer, including tie order. For sufficiency give size s0 multiplier 1, all others ε>0 smaller than `m(S0)/max_Ω m`; all other layers then score strictly below S0, and the within-layer tie rule selects S0.
>
> An equal-likelihood same-size competitor does not defeat S0 when S0 precedes it. Hence replace W5's `m(S)≥m(S0)` paraphrase by “strictly larger likelihood, or equal likelihood and a competitor preceding S0 in the prescribed tie order.” In data use a validated interval: if `Fhat(S')−Fhat(S0)>e(S')+e(S0)` for same-size S', with actual rigorous envelopes e, the exact score is strictly larger and no size-prior retuning recovers S0. A heuristic engine error field is not such an envelope. Completion alone supplies no posterior-miss certificate: a scored set containing only a lower-scoring wrong support can miss a uniquely optimal S0.

### LM106 — Lemma T05-R (exact representation under ORTH) and Corollary T05-R1 (top-k structure)  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `W7-SEC/PROOF_T05.md` §§0-1; `W7-SEC/REPORT.md` §2; positions: W7-SEC task written/launched [pos 711], [pos 716], [pos 717]; branch listed [pos 751], [pos 756]; A-REV9 [pos 821]/[pos 843] (review incomplete).
- Setting and symbols (verbatim, PROOF_T05 §0):

> ## 0. Setting and new symbols
>
> **Hypotheses.** G (fixed design, ε ~ N_n(0, σ*²I), σ*² > 0) and ORTH-design: XᵀX = (n−1)I_p (so p ≤ n − 1), columns
> centred. S₀ = supp θ*, 1 ≤ s₀ := |S₀| < p, s₀ ≤ K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋), n ≥ 3. Equal magnitudes and b_n²/σ*² bounded
> are used **only** where stated (Theorem T05-L, case c = +∞). No beta-min, no SE.
>
> **New symbols** (all defined from ε and θ*; P₀ is over ε):
> - e_j := x_j/√(n−1), j ∈ [p] (orthonormal, ⊥ 1). Complete them to an orthonormal basis e_1..e_p, f_1..f_{n−1−p} of 1^⊥.
> - ξ_j := e_jᵀε/σ*, η_i := f_iᵀε/σ*. λ_j := (n−1)θ*_j²/σ*², and T_j := √(n−1)θ*_j/σ* + ξ_j (so T_j ~ N(±√λ_j, 1)).
> - R′ := Σ_i η_i² (R′ ≡ 0 if p = n − 1); Ξ := R′ + Σ_{j∉S₀}ξ_j²; d := n − 1 − s₀; M := p − s₀ ≥ 1.
> - V_S := R′ + Σ_{j∉S}T_j² + n⁻¹Σ_{j∈S}T_j²; V_tot := V_∅ = R′ + Σ_jT_j²; c_n := 0.02·V_tot/(n−1).
> - τ := τ_n = log n + 2 log((2p − s₀)/s₀) (as in the theorem file); τ^{(i)} := log n + 2 log((2p−1−i)/(i+1)), so τ^{(s₀−1)} = τ.
> - ν′ := 2ν(1 − 1/n) = (n−1)(n+0.02)/n.
> - Global HPM S† (00_COMMON §1). Known-size selector Ŝ_or := the s₀ indices with the largest |z_j|.
>
> Facts used without proof (standard): (F1) Laurent–Massart: for X ~ χ²_D and x > 0, P(X ≤ D − 2√(Dx)) ≤ e^{−x} and
> P(X ≥ D + 2√(Dx) + 2x) ≤ e^{−x}. (F2) 2Φ̄(s) ≤ e^{−s²/2} for s ≥ 0 (log 2Φ̄ has derivative −φ/Φ̄ ≤ −s by the
> Mills ratio). (F3) Hoeffding's inequality for sums of independent [0, q]-valued variables. (F4) C(M, i) ≤ (eM/i)^i.

- Statement (verbatim):

> ## 1. Lemma T05-R (exact representation). **PROVED.**
>
> Under G and ORTH-design:
> (a) ξ_1, …, ξ_p, η_1, …, η_{n−1−p} are iid N(0,1); hence (ξ_j)_{j∈S₀}, (ξ_j)_{j∉S₀} and R′ ~ χ²_{n−1−p} are
> independent, and Ξ ~ χ²_d is independent of (ξ_j)_{j∈S₀}.
> (b) D_S = n^{|S|} and Q_S = (n−1)V_S/V_tot for every S ∈ Ω.
> (c) F(S) = κ + log ϖ(|S|) − (|S|/2) log n − ν log(c_n + V_S), where κ := log C_n + ν log(V_tot/(n−1)) does not depend on S.
> (d) The exact addition log-odds of T05(i) hold: for S of size k < K and j ∉ S,
> F(S+j) − F(S) = log[(k+1)/(2p−k−1)] − ½ log n + ν log[(0.02+Q_S)/(0.02+Q_S−z_j²/n)].
>
> **Corollary T05-R1 (top-k structure). PROVED.** Since V_S = V_tot − (1 − 1/n)Σ_{j∈S}T_j², for each k the maximum of F
> over {|S| = k} is attained exactly at the k-subsets with the largest T_j² (a.s. unique). Write top_k for it and
> g(k) := F(top_k). Then S† = top_{k̂}, k̂ = the smallest maximiser of g; and **S† = S₀ ⇔ top_{s₀} = S₀ and g(s₀) > g(k)
> for all k ≠ s₀** (up to a P₀-null set of ties). (Checked by enumeration: `results/t05_representation_check.txt`.)

- Earlier versions: the pre-campaign T05(i) (one-pager/theorem file) states the identities $D_S=n^{|S|}$ and $Q_S=y^\top y-n^{-1}\sum_{j\in S}z_j^2$ and the exact addition log-odds without proof; Lemma T05-R(d) gives them with proof.
- Status history: T05 CONJECTURED (not proved) at campaign start (one-pager; Sol check J11 single-seed numerical evidence n = 40, p = 6) -> PROVED (W7-SEC, own line-by-line check; brute-force enumeration $n\in\{13,25,40,60\}$, $p\le12$, relative error $\le5\times10^{-15}$, HPM equals the top-k set in 70/70 data sets) -> XF: A-REV9 "GAP in this review: deferred detailed proof/code audit, no mathematical rejection asserted" (verbatim in TH132).

### TH135 — Proposition T05-O and Theorem T05-G (the oracle gap, T05(iii))  [theorem]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T05.md` §4; `W7-SEC/REPORT.md` §2 (including the proposed paper sentence); positions [pos 717], [pos 751], [pos 957].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## 4. Proposition T05-O (the known-size selector) and Theorem T05-G (the gap). **PROVED.**
>
> **Proposition T05-O.** Under G and ORTH-design, for every x > 0,
>   P₀(Ŝ_or ≠ S₀) ≤ e^{−x} + Σ_{j∈S₀} Φ(√(2 log M + 2x) − √λ_j).
> *Proof.* |z_j| ∝ |T_j| with a common positive factor (Lemma T05-R), so Ŝ_or = S₀ iff min_{S₀}|T_j| > max_{j∉S₀}|ξ_j|.
> With t := √(2 log M + 2x): P(max_{j∉S₀}|ξ_j| ≥ t) ≤ M·2Φ̄(t) ≤ Me^{−t²/2} = e^{−x} (F2), and
> P(|T_j| ≤ t) ≤ P(ξ_j ≤ t − √λ_j) = Φ(t − √λ_j). ∎ (Knowledge of σ* is not used: the selector is scale-free.)
>
> **Corollary.** If ω_n := √λ_min − √(2 log M) → ∞ then P₀(Ŝ_or = S₀) → 1: take x = ω_n²/8, so that
> √(2 log M + 2x) ≤ √(2 log M) + ω_n/2 and the bound is ≤ e^{−ω_n²/8} + s₀Φ(−ω_n/2).
>
> **Theorem T05-G (= T05(iii)).** Under G, ORTH-design and equal magnitudes, every sequence with
> √λ_n − √(2 log M_n) → ∞ and √τ_n − √λ_n → ∞ has P₀(Ŝ_or = S₀) → 1 and P₀(S† = S₀) → 0 (Prop T05-O, Cor T05-U∞;
> for the reported HPM, also P(Ŝ = S₀) → 0 whenever P(final local_limit) → 0, Cor T05-Ŝ). Such sequences exist
> whenever log n → ∞, because τ_n − 2 log M_n = log n + 2 log((2p − s₀)/(p − s₀)) − 2 log s₀ ≥ log n − 2 log s₀,
> so √τ_n − √(2 log M_n) ≥ (log n − 2 log s₀)/(2√τ_n) → ∞ (τ_n ≤ 3 log n + 2 log 2); take √λ_n halfway. E.g. p ≍ n^a,
> λ_n = (1−ε)τ_n with 0 < ε < 1/(1+2a).
> At p = n^a (a > 0), √τ_n − √(2 log M_n) = [√(1+2a) − √(2a)]√log n + o(1) (`results/t05_mc.txt` part C). **PROVED.**

- Proposed paper sentence (verbatim, W7-SEC REPORT §2):

>   oracle succeeds in 74% of replicates and the HPM in 2%."

- Source of the claim (verbatim):

(b) One sentence of T06(i) next to Prop 1: exact ties and near-duplicates are a ceiling for every method (S4).
>
> Status: CONJECTURED (not proved)  | Rank: secondary | Paper role: Supplement remark (restored by both reviewers: the g-prior + BB(1,p) HPM loses a sqrt(log n) factor to the oracle under orthogonal design; disclose before a referee finds it)

- Refutation (verbatim, W7-SEC PROOF_T05 §4 "Wording correction for the paper remark (important)"):

⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.90; best match `A-REV6/sources/W7-SEC__PROOF_T05.md`). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
> **Wording correction for the paper remark (important).** The gap is **additive on the amplitude scale √λ**
> (equivalently b_n√(n−1)/σ*): about [√(1+2a) − √(2a)]√log n standard errors. On the energy scale λ, or for the minimal
> detectable |b_n|, it is a **constant factor**: the HPM needs λ ≳ (1+2a) log n and the oracle λ ≳ 2a log n, a ratio
> (1+2a)/(2a) (= 2 at a = ½, 1.5 at a = 1). Both thresholds scale as √(log n / n) in b_n. So "loses a √log n factor" is
> wrong if read multiplicatively; it is right only as "an additive √log n in standardised amplitude". The
> multiplicative loss is unbounded only when log p = o(log n) (e.g. p fixed: oracle needs λ → ∞, HPM needs λ > log n).
>
> (W7-SEC REPORT §5, verbatim:) 
> - **"Loses a √log n factor"** is false as a multiplicative statement at p = n^a, a > 0. It is true additively in
>   amplitude, and multiplicatively only when log p = o(log n).

- Counterexample: CE113 (the computation at $p=n^a$).
- Replacement: TH135 (T05-G) in additive-amplitude form, with the paper sentence quoted there.
- Status: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the multiplicative reading (W7-SEC, author-only; registry `T05-wording`); XF none; the HQ summary of the campaign still lists it as "T05 (the disclosed √log n negative)" [pos 717] and "T05 (a disclosed negative)" [pos 957] (the wording was never re-edited in HQ messages).

### LIT-STAT — literature verdicts on the statistical target (LM107, LM108, RF130, RF131, RF132, CJ138)
Source: `LIT-STAT/REPORT.md` (branch `theory/LIT-STAT`, run 2026-11-02, Opus, API credit, $8 cap; "a literature audit. It contains no new theorem of record"); working notes `LIT-STAT/notes/00-05`; positions: launched [pos 986]/[pos 988] (23:26), reported [pos 1009] ("Thm 1 (posterior concentration): a modest extension of Rossell (2022, *Bayesian Analysis*). The bound P(S† ≠ S₀) ≤ 2E[1 − π(S₀)] is his Proposition 1 word for word, so Thm 4 and Thm 5 must credit him. What remains ours is narrow: handling a model-size cap of order n under the BB(1,p) prior."), used again at [pos 1142] ("The first term is pure statistics: T03♯ (Rossell 2022, Prop 1)"). Status words of this section are the author's "assessment" unless marked PROVED (elementary) or UNVERIFIED; no cross-family check of LIT-STAT exists in the archive.

Headline (verbatim, `LIT-STAT/REPORT.md` §1):

> 1. **Thm 1 (T03♯) is a modest extension of known results, not a new phenomenon.** Its architecture (dimension bound, then no strict
>    supersets, then beta-min recovery) is the field's standard template (CSvdV 2015; BCG review 2026). The closest prior art is
>    **Rossell (2022, Bayesian Analysis)**. He proves concentration for Zellner priors with τ = 1 (unit information), a **non-complexity
>    Beta-Binomial** model prior, polynomial p, and eigenvalue quantities anchored at the true model, with L¹ rates. **Moreno–Girón–Casella
>    (2015)** prove g = n plus a hierarchical-uniform model prior consistent for k = O(n^b), b ≤ 1. Several things are genuinely ours:
>    - BB(1,p) rather than BB(1,1);
>    - the cap K = ⌊n/2⌋, which is not o(n) (Rossell needs p̄ ≪ n);
>    - the ridge slab;
>    - the size-cutoff device m♯_n of T02(i♯), which lets SE be imposed only up to size m♯_n ≈ s₀ + O(log n).
> 2. **T03♯(3), P(S† ≠ S₀) ≤ 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)], is KNOWN.** It is Rossell (2022) Proposition 1 verbatim, and Rossell states that it also holds
>    for the MPM. Thm 4 (T21) and Thm 5(0) inherit this term, so the paper must cite it.
> 3. **Prop 1 (T07):**
>    - (ii)(a), the HPM as the Bayes rule under 0–1 loss, is textbook.
>    - (ii)(b), the MPM as the Bayes rule under Hamming loss, is folklore; it is the same coordinate-wise algebra as the proof of
>      Barbieri–Berger (2004) Thm 1.
>    - (ii)(c), the capped version, is a trivial variant that I did not find stated.
>    - (i), the within-size ceiling, is a one-line observation. After targeted searches I found it **not stated** anywhere, including
>      Berger–García-Donato–Pericchi (2026), a paper devoted entirely to size-only model priors.
>
>    Prop 1 is correct bookkeeping, not novelty.
> 4. **The exact BB(1,p) tail (T02(i♯)) is the most distinctive statistical piece.** Under BB(1,p) the dimension prior has ratio
>    (p−s+1)/(2p−s) ≈ ½ (PROVED; `scripts/bb_ratios.py`). So BB(1,p) violates CSvdV's exponential-decrease condition (2.2) for every fixed
>    A4 > 0, and CSvdV's Thm 1 and Cor 1 do not cover it. CSvdV's own example needs Beta(1, p^u) with u > 1, and Cor 1 needs A4 > 1. I found
>    no published dimension or tail bound for the BB(1,p) / g = n pair in which the Occam factor of the slab, not the prior, carries the size
>    penalty. Rossell's §5.2 is the nearest result: BB(1,1), with p̄ ≪ n.
>    **Correction after a later check (§12):** per model, BB(1,p) and BB(1,1) penalise each added variable at the same order (ratios
>    (k+1)/(2p−1−k) vs (k+1)/(p−k)). BB(1,p) ≈ BB(1,1) × ((p+1)/2)·2^{−k}, i.e. BB(1,1) tilted by a Geometric(½) size law. So the gap is
>    narrow: it is "Rossell's BB(1,1) spurious-model analysis does not reach a cap K ≍ n; the geometric size tilt of BB(1,p) plus T02(i♯)
>    does". The novelty of T02(i♯) is **modest**, not a new mechanism.
> 5. **The naive-merge proposition (A-DRAFT Prop M) formalises a known phenomenon.** That phenomenon is omitted-variable bias in block-wise
>    or marginal fits. Papaspiliopoulos–Rossell (2017) state that block-local exactness requires a block-diagonal Gram matrix and is only a
>    heuristic otherwise. Prop M is a clean COUNTEREXAMPLE for motivation, not a contribution.
> 6. **What the literature lacks.** Nothing I read proves anything about the **reported** (best-scored) HPM of a finite-budget algorithm when
>    the posterior is fine but the start is masked. The papers that couple statistics with computation (YWJ 2016, Zhou et al. 2022,
>    Hou–Atchadé) assume local Bayes-factor monotonicity ("Condition 1"), complexity priors with κ₀ ≥ 2, and g ≥ p. Our masked-regime results
>    (Thms 2, 3, 5) sit outside all of that. API-POS already showed that the LH posterior itself satisfies Condition 1(b), so the novelty is
>    the start-law analysis, not posterior multimodality.

Gaps (verbatim, §3 G1 and G4, and §9 escalations):

> - **G1. Concentration under BB(1,p) with a g = n slab and a cap of order n.**
>   - Every concentration theorem I read uses one of three things to beat the multiplicity of large models: a complexity or exponentially
>     decreasing dimension prior (CSvdV, YWJ, Hou–Atchadé, Ročková–George), a slab variance growing like p^{2+δ} (Narisetty–He; YWJ's
>     g = p^{2κ₁}), or a maximum size p̄ ≪ n (Rossell; Shin et al.).
>   - T03♯ uses none of these. BB(1,p) has dimension ratio ≈ ½ (PROVED, §6), g = n < p, and K = ⌊n/2⌋.
>   - The device that makes this work is T02(i♯)'s exact tail. It bounds Π(|S| > m | y) by the prior tail ratio R_m times
>     (n+1)^{s₀/2}√n, with a tight factor Θ♯, and so moves the SE requirement down to sizes ≤ m♯_n ≈ s₀ + O(log n). Prop. D (duplicate
>     columns) shows that some log n growth of the cutoff is necessary without SE.
>   - I found no published analogue of either the upper bound (exact BB(1,p) tail) or the lower bound (Prop. D) for a non-complexity BB prior.
>   - **This is the defensible statistical novelty of Thm 1. It is modest.** It is narrowed further by §12: BB(1,p) is BB(1,1) times a
>     Geometric(½) size tilt, so Rossell's per-model accounting carries over up to constants. What remains new is handling a cap of order n
>     (Rossell's (B1) needs p̄ ≪ n) through the geometric tail and the exact cutoff m♯_n, together with Prop. D's matching lower bound.
>
> - **G4. Finite-n relevance at n = 200.**
>   - No asymptotic theorem in the table has force at n = 200, p ∈ {500, 1000}.
>   - YWJ's (E) already fails for every s₀ ≥ 1 (§2 row 3). Rossell's (B1) fails for our cap. T03♯'s own thresholds are about 2·10⁶.
>   - The only explicit finite-sample posterior bound found (Hou–Atchadé Thm 2) is for a complexity prior and an approximate posterior,
>     with constants c₁ and c₂ that are not computable from the design alone.
>   - Nobody has a usable finite-n selection theorem for designs like the study's. API-N200's measured-Π(X) route is a different kind of
>     object (a composition plus measurement), not a competitor to any paper here.
>
> ## 9. Needs escalation
>

>   with u ≤ 1 combined with a unit-information slab? Candidates to check: the Rossell (2022) supplement (Lemmas S15–S16, Section S3),
>   Castillo–vdV 2012 §2 (lower bounds), and Martin, Mess & Walker (2017), whom Rossell cites on p̄ ≤ n. I did not read these.

### LM107 — BB(1,p) is not a complexity prior in the sense of Castillo-Schmidt-Hieber-van der Vaart (2.2)  [lemma, elementary]
- Source: `LIT-STAT/REPORT.md` §6 "Evidence" (script `bb_ratios.py`, exact rational arithmetic, run via `owls_run -j 2`; the script and results are not in the snapshot); position [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim):

> - `scripts/bb_ratios.py` → `results/bb_ratios.txt`. Exact rational arithmetic, deterministic, run via `owls_run -j 2`. It checks three
>   things:
>   1. w(k) = ½/C(2p−1,k) = B(k+1, 2p−k)/B(1,p), for k ≤ min(p, 60) and p ∈ {20, 500, 1000}.
>   2. The dimension ratio is π_p(s)/π_p(s−1) = (p−s+1)/(2p−s), asserted exactly. The implied CSvdV exponent is A4 = −log(ratio)/log p,
>      which is 0.1003–0.1080 at p = 1000 and 0.111–0.130 at p = 500 for s ≤ 100, and tends to 0 as p → ∞ for fixed s.
>   3. The per-model ratio is w(s)/w(s−1) = s/(2p−s).
>
>   **PROVED** (elementary algebra, with exact numerical confirmation): BB(1,p) satisfies CSvdV (2.2) for no fixed A4 > 0 uniformly in p,
>   so CSvdV Thms 1, 4 and Cor 1 do not apply to our size prior.

- Earlier versions: none (first appearance as headline 4 of the same report; see RF132 for the later narrowing).
- Status history: PROVED (elementary algebra with exact numerical confirmation; LIT-STAT, single author; no verifier, no cross-family check). Consistent with LM101(a) (the dimension prior ratio is $\pi_p(s)/\pi_p(s-1)=(p-s+1)/(2p-s)$, the per-model ratio $w(s)/w(s-1)=s/(2p-s)$).
- Proved by / checked by: LIT-STAT only.
- Depends on: ⟦00_COMMON prior⟧; compares with CSvdV (2015) condition (2.2).
- Feeds: the positioning sentence in S-T ("BB(1,p) is not a complexity prior in the sense of Castillo et al. (2015, (2.2)), since its dimension ratio is (p−s+1)/(2p−s) → ½": LIT-STAT §5 proposed wording).

### LM108 — BB(1,p) equals BB(1,1) times a geometric size tilt (LIT-STAT addendum §12)  [lemma, elementary]
- Source: `LIT-STAT/REPORT.md` §12 (script `bb11_vs_bb1p.py`, exact rationals); position [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## 12. Addendum: BB(1,p) versus Rossell's BB(1,1) (checked after the first draft)
>
> `scripts/bb11_vs_bb1p.py` → `results/bb11_vs_bb1p.txt` (exact rationals, deterministic, run via `owls_run -j 2`). It shows:
>
> - The per-model ratios are w(k+1)/w(k) = (k+1)/(p−k) for BB(1,1) and (k+1)/(2p−1−k) for BB(1,p), both asserted exactly. They agree to
>   within a factor of about 2.
> - w_{BB(1,p)}(k)/w_{BB(1,1)}(k) = (p+1)C(p,k)/(2C(2p−1,k)). This equals ((p+1)/2)·2^{−k}·(1 + o(1)) for k ≪ √p. The bracketed
>   correction is 1.000 at k = 0 and 0.96 at k = 14 (p = 1000), and only 0.0045 at k = 100 (p = 500), where BB(1,p) is even lighter.
>
> **PROVED** (elementary): BB(1,p) is BB(1,1) multiplied by a size-only factor that is at most ((p+1)/2)·(2p/(2p−1))·2^{−k} for k ≥ 1.
> The reason is that C(p,k)/C(2p−1,k) = ∏_{i<k}(p−i)/(2p−1−i). The i = 0 factor is p/(2p−1) = ½·2p/(2p−1), and every factor with i ≥ 1
> is ≤ ½. This also explains the 1.0010 = 1000/999 entry at k = 1, p = 500. A first draft of this line said "≤ ½ for every i ≥ 0", which
> is false at i = 0; corrected here.
>
> Consequences for this audit:
> - **Spurious models.** Rossell's (2022) §5.2 accounting of spurious models (per-model prior ratio times a Bayes-factor bound) transfers to
>   BB(1,p) up to the constant (p+1)/2 at the denominator S₀ and an extra 2^{−(k−s₀)} that only helps.
> - **Cap.** His requirement p̄ ≪ n comes from summing a flat size law up to p̄. The geometric tilt is exactly what lets T02(i♯) live with
>   K = ⌊n/2⌋.
> - **Revised verdicts.** T03♯ is a **modest extension of Rossell (2022)** to a geometric-size-tilted BB prior, a cap of order n and a
>   ridge slab, rather than a different mechanism. H2's severity rises from Medium to **Medium–High**. G1 narrows to the cap and the exact
>   cutoff, with Prop. D's lower bound.
> - **E1 updated.** Rossell's supplement (Lemma S15, Lemma S21, read in the same arXiv PDF) treats BB(1,1), uniform and Complexity
>   priors only. It has no BB(1,p) and no cap of order n. A stronger reviewer should still check Martin, Mess & Walker (2017), which I did
>   not read.

- Earlier versions / repairs: the first draft of this line said "≤ ½ for every i ≥ 0", false at $i=0$ (RF131); the headline-4 reading "the gap is a new mechanism" was narrowed (RF132).
- Status history: PROVED (elementary; LIT-STAT, single author).
- Proved by / checked by: LIT-STAT only; reproduces `C(p,k)/C(2p−1,k)=∏_{i<k}(p−i)/(2p−1−i)` which is LM101(a).
- Depends on: LM101.
- Feeds: the "modest extension" verdict on TH128 (RF130, RF132).

## Theme 2: START-LH — the start in the favourable and masked regimes, the linked-hub (LH) family and its iid p ≫ n version

**Summary:** This theme is the campaign's proof programme for paper Theorem 2 ("the start"): the block-product start law $\pi_0$ of v3 and when it concentrates near the truth (favourable regime, locked T22(iii)) or assigns it vanishing mass (masked regime, locked T27(i)). It starts from two locked-but-conditional pre-campaign results whose premises were unverified: T22(iii) assumed EXP′, VIS, NL$_\eta$, NL$_{\rm avg}(\kappa)$ and T27(i) assumed H2 (a joint ratio law) and H3 (a normalised reference-mass lower bound) TH116 (T22(iii)) TH119 (T27(i)) CJ121 (EXP′) (statements are owned by Theme 0). The branches and timeline (positions are transcript positions):

- **W1-EXP** (Wave 1, Opus 5.5 routine, launched 2026-11-02 16:04Z [pos 233], [pos 238]; report [pos 351], [pos 355]): EXP′ as a theorem (Thm 1), favourable-regime consequences (Props 2.1/2.2, Lemma 2.3, Thms 2 and 6), the chain-leakage condition CL(L) replacing H2 (Thms 3, 4), the linked-hub family LH (Lemmas 4.1/4.2, Thm 5, exact Gram, $p\le n-1$).
- **W3-VEXP** (Wave 3 same-family referee of W1-EXP, [pos 355]; verdict [pos 363], [pos 370]): "No mathematical ERROR in any W1 theorem"; adds the finite-$n$ certificate R1, a fixed-partition-surrogate sketch R3 for LH-iid, wording repairs R4, and Proposition D (dilution ceiling), which refutes W1's "weak-signal masking" conjecture.
- **W3-PXN** (Wave 3, [pos 355]; result read [pos 423], [pos 425], [pos 430], [pos 474]): the $p\gg n$ family LH-iid with P1–P8, Lemma B (exact Beta laws), Lemma Tr (truncated moment), Lemma U, Lemma $\Lambda$, Props Q and W, Conj. W′.
- **W5-VMASK** (Wave 5 same-family referee of W3-PXN and W4-T38FULL, launched [pos 510]; pushed by [pos 742]): VERIFIED with cosmetic repairs R2–R7, a new proof R1 of D2-d (no-tweak route, $c=1$), and the sharp LH-LAT margin $m_0^\sharp$.
- **A-REV2** (Astra, cross-family; relaunched [pos 465], [pos 474]; result [pos 568], [pos 570]): EXP′, Thms 3–4 VERIFIED; constant 0.52/c$_*$ ERROR (0.51/c$_*$); Thm 4 "iff" ERROR. **A-REV5** (re-review, [pos 807], [pos 919]) confirms the corrected constant.
- **A-REV3** (Astra, launched ~[pos 676], [pos 696]; landed by [pos 742]; used [pos 796]): W3-PXN P1–P5, P8, Lemmas B, Tr VERIFIED; P6 (lattice/TD′) GAP, P7 GAP, joint LS0 route GAP. **A-REV6** (re-review [pos 807], [pos 919]) and **A-REV8** (launched [pos 843], result [pos 919]) retain the P6/P7 GAP.
- **W7-PART** (Wave 7, launched [pos 717]; running [pos 742], [pos 748]; listed [pos 796]): partition-recovery lemma (Theorems A, B, C, counterexamples CE1–CE3); A-REV6 VERIFIED Theorem B in restricted scope, ERROR in Lemma 3 and in the CE2 header.
- **API-PXNGAP** (API credit, Fable, $25 cap, launched [pos 911]; result [pos 978]): Thm 5(b1) with LS0 on LH-iid for every polynomial $p\le n^A$, every premise discharged on the random design; PROVED (candidate), no cross-family review in the archive.

The recurring facts of the theme: (i) the n = 200 study masking is **dilution** (Theme 3), not the cancellation masking of LH; (ii) LH masking needs the method's own partition to put the two cancelling hubs in *different* blocks, i.e. $g\le B<2g$, so the study's groups of five are outside the family; (iii) the final paper-1 list (M3 START) cites EXP′ (as a hypothesis of T22(iii)), Thms 3/4-EXP and Thm 5-LH, and S-BLOCKS cites PART-ThmA; the $p\gg n$ results (W3-PXN, W5-VMASK, API-PXNGAP) are **not** in the final list (see Notes).

### Common setting and hypotheses (W1-EXP; used by the whole theme)

Source: `W1-EXP/REPORT.md` section "Refined statements"; `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` header. Notation of `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md`.

> Common setting: G (fixed design, `eps ~ N(0, sigma^2 I)`), triangular array, blocks = the v3 partition (any partition with `|C_b| <= 16` where stated), `nu = 0.01 + n/2`. Hypotheses:
>
> | Name | Statement | Checkable? |
> |---|---|---|
> | R-lite(A,M) | `p <= n^A`, `||mu||^2 <= Mn` | given truth |
> | SE-blk(phi0) | `min_b lambda_min(R_{C_b}) >= phi0^2` | yes, from X |
> | BO | `X_{C_b}'X_{C_b'} = 0`, `b != b'` | yes, from X |
> | BM-blk | `min_{j in S0} theta_j^2 >= M_n(sigma^2+2M) log n/(phi0^2(n-1))`, `M_n -> inf` | given truth |
> | ZL(S°) | `lambda_b(S°) := ||(P_{C_b} - P_{S° ∩ C_b}) mu||^2 = 0` for all b | given truth (exact) |
> | NL_C(S°) | `max_b lambda_b(S°) <= C sigma^2 log n` | given truth |
> | SPREAD(Delta_0) | `min_b ||(I - P_{C_b}) mu||^2/(n-1) >= Delta_0 > 0` | given truth |
> | VIS-lin(S°, c_V) | `min_b min_{U ⊆ C_b, S°∩C_b ⊄ U} ||(P_{U ∪ S°_b} - P_U) mu||^2 >= c_V n` | given truth |
> | H1 | fixed chain `S^(0) ⊂ … ⊂ S^(c) = S0` of single additions, s, c fixed | definition |
> | CL(L_n) | `max_{i<c} |delta_{T_i,l_i}| <= L_n sigma`, `T_i = S^(i) ∩ C_{b_i}` | given truth |
> | H3 | `P(pi0(S^(0)) >= c0) -> 1` | — (discharged by Thm 6) |

Notation in the proof file: $y=Y/s_y$, $\|y\|^2=\|x_j\|^2=n-1$; blocks $C_b$ deterministic in $X$ with $|C_b|\le B\le16$; $P_T$ the orthogonal projection on ${\rm span}\,X_T$; for a within-block addition $(b,T,l)$ ($T\subseteq C_b\setminus\{l\}$) $x_{T,l}=({\rm RSS}_T-{\rm RSS}_{T+l})/{\rm RSS}_T=(\delta_{T,l}+\sigma Z_{T,l})^2/{\rm RSS}_T$; $r_b(U)=m(U)/m(\varnothing)$ the block table. Also in the proof file: **G**, and
> * **SE-blk(phi0)**: `lambda_min(X_U'X_U/(n-1)) >= phi0^2` for every nonempty `U ⊆ C_b`, every b. *Checkable*: by Cauchy interlacing SE-blk(phi0) holds iff `min_b lambda_min(R_{C_b}) >= phi0^2` (J eigenvalue computations on the actual blocks).

Pre-campaign EXP′ as locked-conditional (Theme 0) was: "EXP' (log[r_b(T+l)/r_b(T)] = -(1/2) log(n+1) - nu log(1 - x_{T,l}) + R with max |R| = O_P(1))" (`main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T22.md`), listed in the register as "Not proved" (`LOCKED_PROOFS.md`, "EXP' ... Decision Point 2 D1"). T27(i)'s H2 was "sequential ratio law, jointly two-sided $O_P(1)$ remainders; assumed statistical input" and H3 "normalised reference-mass lower bound" (`one_pagers/T27.md`).

### TH136 — EXP′ (W1-EXP Theorem 1; "Thm 1 (EXP′; any regime)")  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative, latest repaired version): `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §1 "Theorem 1 (EXP′)"; `W1-EXP/REPORT.md` "Thm 1"; constant corrected by `W6-FIXREV1/CONSOLIDATED.md` §7 and `W6-FIXREV2/REPORT.md` row 8 (see RF134). Positions: launch [pos 233]; report [pos 351], [pos 355]; SF [pos 363], [pos 370]; XF A-REV2 [pos 568], [pos 570]; A-REV5 [pos 807], [pos 919].
- Statement (verbatim, `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §1):
  > **Theorem 1 (EXP′).** Status: **PROVED** (complete; checked line by line below).
  > Assume G, R-lite(A, M), SE-blk(phi0). Put `c_* = sigma^2 / (8(M + 2 sigma^2))` and
  > `kappa_EXP = (1 + phi0^{-2})/(2 phi0^2 (n-1)) + (n/2 + 0.01)(1.02 + 1/(n phi0^2))/(c_* n)`.
  > On an event `E_n` with `P_0(E_n) -> 1`, *every* within-block addition `(b, T, l)` satisfies
  >
  >     log[ r_b(T+l) / r_b(T) ] = -(1/2) log(n+1) - nu log(1 - x_{T,l}) + R_{n,b,T,l},
  >     |R_{n,b,T,l}| <= kappa_EXP  (-> 0.52/c_* = 4.16 (M + 2 sigma^2)/sigma^2 + o(1)).
  >
  > In particular EXP′ holds in its strict form, `rho_n = max |R| = O_{P_0}(1)`, with an explicit deterministic bound on `E_n`.
- Earlier versions / repairs: (1) The displayed limit "$\to0.52/c_*=4.16(M+2\sigma^2)/\sigma^2$" and Remark (b) "$|R|\le0.52/c_*+o(1)$" were found wrong by A-REV1 §3.4 and A-REV2 §5.1: the limit is $0.51/c_*=4.08(M+2\sigma^2)/\sigma^2$; $0.52/c_*+o(1)$ is only a valid looser upper bound; the finite bound is unaffected (see RF134). (2) $\kappa_{\rm EXP}$ is vacuous at the study scale ($\approx100$–$125$ nats at $c=1$, $\approx1{,}700$ at $c=4$, W3-VEXP REPAIRS R1); replaced for finite-$n$ use by the data-computable certificate TH137. (3) Pre-campaign, EXP′ was an assumed hypothesis of T22(iii) (Decision Point 2 D1, "Not proved").
- Status history: proposed as locked-conditional hypothesis (pre-campaign, Theme 0) → PROVED (W1-EXP, "complete; checked line by line", candidate) → SF **VERIFIED** (W3-VEXP, verdict rows 1–5: "Composition of 1–4 ... max|R| → 0.67 ≠ 0 (repro) ... κ_EXP is loose") → XF **VERIFIED*** (A-REV2 §2 "SEX Theorem 1 EXP′, exact remainder and stated bound — VERIFIED: Fixed-X actual blocks, uniform SE-blk, bounded B and polynomial family. Its displayed limiting constant needs the arithmetic correction"; "It requires no cross-block orthogonality, beta-min, VIS, or NL") → constant corrected (W6-FIXREV1, W6-FIXREV2; A-REV5: "Correct constant ... EXP′ VERIFIED fixed-design core. Does not supply all of locked T22(iii)'s inputs"). Registry: `EXP′` author PROVED; SF VERIFIED; XF VERIFIED*.
- Proved by / checked by: W1-EXP (Opus 5.5); W3-VEXP (Opus, own code, reproduced $p=8$–24, $n$ up to $1.6\cdot10^6$); A-REV2 (Astra, 696 additions on $p=8$ AR(.5), max decomposition error $1.39\cdot10^{-13}$, largest $|R|=0.9213$); A-REV5.
- Proof route (Summary:) Lemmas 1.1–1.4 (LM109–LM112): exact decomposition of the log-ratio into a determinant part ($\log(n+1)+\eta_D$) and a ridge-$Q$ part; probability enters only through the RSS floor (Lemma 1.4).
- Depends on: LM109, LM110, LM111, LM112; CJ130 (G), CJ130 (R) (00_COMMON).
- Feeds: M3 START (K16, as hypothesis of T22(iii): "Cite T22(iii) ... with G, R, within-block SE, EXP′, VIS, NL$_\eta$, NL$_{\rm avg}(\kappa)$ retained"); REGISTRY_PAPER1 card L-MASK (K15, K17, K18); K16 is "a supplementary conditional lemma".
- Notes: Remark (c) of the proof: the remainder is genuinely $O(1)$, not $o(1)$ ("its main part is $\nu[a_T/{\rm RSS}^y_T-a_{T+l}/{\rm RSS}^y_{T+l}]$"). Only G, $p\le n^A$, $\|\mu\|^2\le Mn$, $|C_b|\le16$ and SE-blk are used — no BO, no $s_0$, no beta-min, no VIS/NL. Lemmas 1.1, 1.2, 1.4 never use block membership (W5-VMASK row 6), which is how W3-PXN uses them on general small sets.

### LM109 — W1 Lemma 1.1 ($Q_S$ versus RSS)  [lemma]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §1. Positions: as TH136.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 1.1 (Q_S versus RSS). For nonempty S with `lambda_min(G_S) >= phi^2 (n-1)`:
  > `Q_S = RSS^y_S + c_S` with `0 <= c_S <= 1 + 1/(n phi^2)`; and `c_empty = 0`.
- Status: PROVED; SF VERIFIED (W3-VEXP row 1); XF VERIFIED (A-REV2 §5.1: "τ ... nonnegative and at most ε/φ²; ... the stated upper bound c_S ≤ 1+1/(nφ²) is valid"). Depends on: ⟦00_COMMON score Q⟧. Feeds: TH136. Also re-proved self-contained as PXNGAP Lemma E (E2) (LM123).

### LM110 — W1 Lemma 1.2 (determinant ratio)  [lemma]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §1.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 1.2 (determinant ratio). Let `T ⊆ C_b`, `l ∈ C_b \ T` and `lambda_min(G_{T+l}) >= phi^2(n-1)`.
  > Then `log D_{T+l} - log D_T = log(n+1) + eta_D` with `|eta_D| <= (1 + phi^{-2})/(phi^2 (n-1))`.
- Status: PROVED; SF VERIFIED (row 2); XF VERIFIED (A-REV2 §5.1). Note: the statement says $T\subseteq C_b$ but the proof uses only the Schur complement and $\lambda_{\min}$ (W5-VMASK row 6). Feeds: TH136. Depends on: —.

### LM111 — W1 Lemma 1.3 (exact decomposition of the EXP′ remainder)  [lemma]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §1.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 1.3 (exact decomposition). Under SE-blk(phi0), for every within-block addition, if all `RSS^y_U > 0`:
  >
  >     R_{n,b,T,l} = -(1/2) eta_D - nu [ log(1 + a_{T+l}/RSS^y_{T+l}) - log(1 + a_T/RSS^y_T) ],
  >     a_U := 0.02 + c_U ∈ [0.02, 1.02 + 1/(n phi0^2)].
  >
  > Hence `|R_{n,b,T,l}| <= (1+phi0^{-2})/(2 phi0^2 (n-1)) + nu (1.02 + 1/(n phi0^2)) / min_{U ⊆ C_b} RSS^y_U`.
- Status: PROVED; SF VERIFIED (row 3; bound holds on 300 adversarial small designs, max ratio 0.77); XF VERIFIED (A-REV2: "no factor two is missing"). Deterministic. Feeds: TH136, TH137. Depends on: LM109, LM110.

### LM112 — W1 Lemma 1.4 (RSS floor)  [lemma]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §1.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 1.4 (RSS floor). Under G and R-lite(A, M), with `|C_b| <= 16`:
  > `P_0( min_{b, U ⊆ C_b} RSS^y_U >= c_* n ) -> 1`, `c_* = sigma^2/(8(M + 2 sigma^2))`.
- Status: PROVED; SF VERIFIED (row 4); XF VERIFIED (A-REV2: "dimension at most 17 ... union over at most 2^16 n^A sets"). Notes: PXNGAP replaces it by Lemma E with $c_E=\sigma^2/(12(M+\sigma^2))$ (LM123); A-REV3/W5 R2 show that using $c_*$ in "$\le1$" is false (RF138). Feeds: TH136.

### TH137 — R1-cert (W3-VEXP "EXP′ remainder certificate", Corollary R1)  [corollary]
- Source: `W3-VEXP/REPAIRS.md` §R1. Positions: SF [pos 363], [pos 370] ("at most 1.52 nats on study-like designs").
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Corollary R1.** Fix any data set and any partition. Suppose SE-blk(φ) holds on the realised blocks, that is, min_b λ_min(R_{C_b}) ≥ φ² > 0, and suppose y ∉ span X_{C_b} for every b. Then every within-block addition (b, T, l) satisfies
  >
  >     |R_{n,b,T,l}| ≤ cert := (1 + φ^{-2}) / (2 φ² (n-1)) + ν (1.02 + 1/(n φ²)) / min_b RSS^y_{C_b},
  >
  > where R is the exact EXP′ remainder, log r_b(T+l)/r_b(T) = −½ log(n+1) − ν log(1 − x_{T,l}) + R.
- Status history: PROVED (W3-VEXP; author is the verifier) → XF VERIFIED (A-REV2 §2 "VEX R1 data-computable EXP′ certificate — VERIFIED: Deterministic; no high-probability event is necessary once realized SE and positive full-block RSS are checked"). Values: $0.59$–$1.52$ nats in every simulated study design ($S1$–$S6$, $c\in\{0.5,1,4\}$); actual $\max|R|\le0.145$ at $n=200$.
- Proof (Summary:) For $U\subseteq C_b$, $P_U\preceq P_{C_b}$, hence ${\rm RSS}^y_U\ge{\rm RSS}^y_{C_b}$; Lemma 1.3 is deterministic. A-REV2 caveat: neither the asymptotic theorem nor $\kappa_{\rm EXP}$ proves a given $n=200$ data set lies on the probabilistic floor event; the certificate is the finite-$n$ statement.
- Depends on: LM111. Feeds: none in paper-1 list (finite-$n$ certificates belong to Theme 9; see TH137 (R1-cert)). Notes: replaces $\kappa_{\rm EXP}$ in the n = 200 disclosure.

### TH138 — Thm2-BO (W1-EXP Theorem 2: favourable regime, block-orthogonal benchmark; T22(iii) unconditional in BO)  [theorem]

### LM113 — W1 Lemma 2.3 (leakage bounds the discrepancy; visibility from block gain)  [lemma]

  with `lambda_b(S°) = ||(P_{C_b} - P_{U_b°}) mu||^2` ("in-block signal not carried by S°") and `g_b(S°) = min_{U ⊆ C_b, U_b° ⊄ U} ||(P_{U ∪ U_b°} - P_U) mu||^2` ("visibility gain").

### TH140 — Thm6-EXP (W1-EXP Theorem 6: direct start concentration under exact zero leakage)  [theorem]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §2 "Theorem 6". Positions: [pos 351], [pos 355]; SF [pos 363], [pos 370].
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Theorem 6 (direct start concentration under exact zero leakage; no truncation, no locked-proof transfer).** Status: **PROVED**. Let `S°` be deterministic, feasible, `|S°| = s` fixed. Assume G, R-lite(A, M), SE-blk(phi0), and
  > * **ZL(S°)** (exact zero leakage): `lambda_b(S°) = 0` for every block, i.e. `P_{C_b} mu ∈ span X_{U_b°}`;
  > * **SPREAD(Delta_0)**: `min_b ||(I - P_{C_b}) mu||^2/(n-1) >= Delta_0 > 0` (no single block carries all the signal);
  > * **VIS-lin(c_V)**: `min_b g_b(S°) >= c_V n` with fixed `c_V > 0` (empty minimum = +inf).
  > Then `1 - pi_0(S°) = O_{P_0}(2^B n^{-1/2})` (in particular `pi_0(S°) -> 1`), and `e_n° = O_P(e^{-c n})` for some c > 0.
  (Report form: "either regime — S° = S0 is favourable, S° ≠ S0 is masked".)
- Status history: PROVED (W1-EXP) → SF VERIFIED (W3-VEXP row 11: "Steps 0–3 rechecked: a < ½ makes E e^{aZ²} finite; telescoping lower bound; T22(i-a,b). Repro: flat √n(1−π₀(S°)) ≈ 1.6 for n = 100…102400, with no √(log n)") → XF none. W3-VEXP §7.2: the "uniform RSS event (ii)" deserves review.
- Proof route (Summary:) Step 1 bounds $u_n^\circ$ via EXP′ and $x/(1-x)=\sigma^2Z^2/{\rm RSS}_{T+l}$ with $a<1/2$; Step 2 bounds $e_n^\circ$ by the telescoped lower bound $(n/2)(c_V/2)/C_R$; Step 3 is wave-1 T22(i-a,b).
- Depends on: TH136, LM113, TH116 (T22(i)). Feeds: TH144 (Thm 5(a)); none directly in paper-1 list.
- Notes: SPREAD excludes the case where one block carries the whole signal (then the exponent hits the non-integrable $1/2$; the locked truncation route covers it at the price of $\sqrt{\log n}$). Remark 2 (source): in BO with $S^\circ=S_0$, ZL is automatic; SPREAD holds whenever the true variables meet $\ge2$ blocks; under fixed beta-min Thm 6 gives the favourable statement $1-\pi_0(S_0)=O_P(2^Bn^{-1/2})$ without the locked T22(iii).

### TH141 — Thm3-EXP (W1-EXP Theorem 3: two-sided chain ratio law under chain leakage CL(L))  [theorem]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §3 "Theorem 3"; `W3-VEXP/REPAIRS.md` R4 (deterministic chain). Positions: [pos 351], [pos 355], [pos 363], [pos 568], [pos 570].
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Hypotheses.**
  > * **H1** (fixed chain): as in the T27(i) STATEMENT: deterministic `S^(0) ⊂ … ⊂ S^(c) = S0`, `S^(i+1) = S^(i) + l_i`, fixed s = |S^(0)|, c >= 1, all feasible; `b_i = b(l_i)`, `T_i = S^(i) ∩ C_{b_i}`.
  > * **SE-chain(phi0)**: `lambda_min(R_{T_i + l_i}) >= phi0^2` for i < c (implied by SE-blk).
  > * **CL(L_n)** (chain leakage): `max_{i<c} |delta_{T_i, l_i}| <= L_n sigma`. Fixed `L_n = L` is the *bounded-leakage* case; `L_n -> inf` is allowed in part (b).
  > * **H3** (unchanged): `P_0(pi_0(S^(0)) >= c0) -> 1`; or **H3-T22**: the hypotheses of Prop. 2.2 with `S° = S^(0)`.
  >
  > **Theorem 3 (two-sided ratio law).** Status: **PROVED**. Under G, R-lite, SE-chain, H1, CL(L_n): w.p. -> 1, for all i < c,
  >
  >     -1 - kappa_EXP <= E_{n,i} := log[r_{b_i}(T_i+l_i)/r_{b_i}(T_i)] + (1/2) log n
  >                    <= kappa_EXP + nu sigma^2 (L_n + |Z_i|)^2 / RSS_{T_i+l_i},
  >
  > with `Z_i = Z_{T_i,l_i} ~ N(0,1)` and `RSS_{T_i+l_i} >= sigma^2 (n-1)/2` on the event, so the upper bound is `<= kappa_EXP + 1.01 (L_n + |Z_i|)^2` for n >= 400. (a) If `L_n = L` is fixed, `max_i |E_{n,i}| = O_{P_0}(1)`: **H2 holds**. (b) In general `E_{n,i} ∈ [-O_P(1), O_P(1) + 1.01(L_n + O_P(1))^2]` — a two-sided law with multiplier `e^{O(L_n^2)}` on the upper side only.
- Earlier versions / repairs: W3-VEXP R4: "W1's H1 requires a **deterministic** chain, whereas T27(i)'s H1 allows data-measurable chains. Theorem 3's 'Z_i exactly N(0,1)' needs the deterministic version (or a chain chosen independently of ε)"; "1.01 valid for n ≥ 103". A-REV2 §5.2 "Quantifier boundary: the locked T27(i) allows a data-measurable chain but assumes H2 for that selected chain. SEX Theorem 3 discharges H2 only for its more restrictive deterministic chain ... Do not apply this theorem to a selected trajectory without a uniform bound."
- Status history: PROVED (W1-EXP) → SF VERIFIED (W3-VEXP row 12, "needs a deterministic chain (R4)") → XF **VERIFIED** (A-REV2 §2: "SEX Theorem 3, deterministic fixed-length chain — VERIFIED: No response-selected chain; 1.01 upper multiplier is valid for the stated n≥400"). Registry `Thm3-EXP`: author PROVED; SF VERIFIED; XF VERIFIED.
- Depends on: TH136 (restricted to chain pairs), LM109–LM112; CJ125 (H2) (replaced), TH119 (T27(i)).
- Feeds: M3 START (K17, masked law; "T27(i) retains a fixed feasible completion chain, jointly two-sided tight successive log-table ratios and a normalized reference-mass lower bound"); L-MASK; cited in status lines of M2 Theorem WS.

### TH142 — Thm4-EXP (W1-EXP Theorem 4: T27(i) from bounded chain leakage; includes growing-leakage bound "Thm4-growL")  [theorem]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §3 "Theorem 4"; `W3-VEXP/REPAIRS.md` R4; A-REV2 §5.3. Positions as TH141.

### TH143 — LimitLaw (limit law of the masking statistic, W1-EXP §3 "Limit law (refinement)")  [proposition]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §3 end; `W1-EXP/REPORT.md` headline 3.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Limit law (refinement).** Status: **PROOF SKETCH**. If moreover `delta_{T_i,l_i} = 0` exactly, `T_i = ∅` for all i, `pi_0(S^(0)) -> 1` in probability, and the chain directions `x_{l_i}` are mutually orthogonal, then
  >
  >     log pi_0(S0) + c log p + (c/2) log n  ->_d  sum_{i<c} log((s+i+1)/2) + sum_{i<c} (sigma^2/(2 v_∅)) chi^2_{1,i},
  >
  > `v_∅ = sigma^2 + ||mu||^2/(n-1)` (independent chi-squares).
  Report form: "A limit law `log pi0(S0) + c log p + (c/2)log n -> sum log((s+i+1)/2) + sum (L_i+Z_i)^2 sigma^2/(2v)` is a PROOF SKETCH and matches exact computation to two decimals."

Wording fix W3-VEXP R4: at fixed $p$ the constant is $\sum\log((s+i+1)p/(2p-s-i-1))$ (what W1's numerics use), the $p\to\infty$ form is $\sum\log((s+i+1)/2)$. Registry `LimitLaw`.

### LM114 — W1 Lemma 4.1 (LH population algebra)  [lemma]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §4.1. (LH family definition quoted here.)
- Definition (verbatim):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.993) from `A-REV1/sources/W1-EXP/PROOF.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > Population correlation `Sigma` on `p = G g` variables, `G` groups `C_1..C_G` of size `g`:
  > * within group h: equicorrelation `rho_h ∈ [rho_-, rho_+] ⊂ (0,1)` (S3: 0.7; S4: 0.85; S6: 0.4–0.9);
  > * each group has a hub `j_h` (the position of its potential true variable);
  > * groups independent (S3/S4/S6) **except** c disjoint *linked pairs* `(a_i, b_i, psi_i)`, `|psi_i| <= psi_+ < 1`, with the rank-one cross-covariance through the hubs:
  >
  >       Sigma[C_a, C_b] = psi Sigma[C_a, j_a] Sigma[j_b, C_b]
  >       (corr(j_a, j_b) = psi; corr(j_a, k) = psi rho_b, k ∈ C_b \ j_b; corr(k, k') = psi rho_a rho_b off-hub).
  >
  >   Equivalently the two groups are conditionally independent given the hub pair: a two-node "tree" link.
  > * truth: `theta_{j_{a_i}} = beta_i != 0`, `theta_{j_{b_i}} = -psi_i beta_i` (the **suppressor**), and `theta_{j_h} = beta_h != 0` for a fixed set of further unlinked "visible" groups; all other coefficients 0. `s0 = 2c + #visible`, fixed. `S° := S0 \ M`, `M = {j_{b_1}, …, j_{b_c}}` (the masked set), `s = s0 - c`.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Lemma 4.1 (population algebra).** Status: **PROVED**.
  > (a) `lambda_min(Sigma) >= (1 - psi_+)(1 - rho_+)`.
  > (b) `Cov(X_{C_{b_i}}, mu) = 0`: every masked group is orthogonal to the signal.
  > (c) `Cov(X_{C_{a_i}}, mu) = beta_i (1 - psi_i^2) Sigma[C_{a_i}, j_{a_i}]`, so the block projection of mu on `C_{a_i}` is `beta_i(1 - psi_i^2) x_{j_{a_i}}`; on a visible group h it is `beta_h x_{j_h}`; on any other group it is 0. Hence the population block-projection support is exactly `S°` (when blocks = groups).
- Status: PROVED; SF VERIFIED (W3-VEXP row 16; Config A: $0.242\ge0.15$). Note (W5-VMASK 23″): the pair unit is positive definite iff $\psi^2<1$ (see CJ143). Feeds: TH144, TH150. Origin of the name: in S3/S4/S6 the "hub" $j_h$ is the position of a possible true variable.

### TH144 — Thm5-LH (W1-EXP Theorem 5: masked regime on the linked-hub family, exact Gram, $p\le n-1$; "joint masked-regime family LH")  [theorem]
- Source: `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §4.2 "Theorem 5"; `W1-EXP/REPORT.md` "Thm 5". Positions: [pos 351], [pos 355] ("one explicit family carries masking and near-truth start mass at the same time"); SF [pos 363], [pos 370].
- Statement (verbatim; report form and proof form combined):
  ⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.94; best match `A-REV1/sources/W1-EXP/PROOF.md`). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
  > Realisation: `X'X = (n-1) Sigma` exactly for every n (any centred orthonormal frame), so all population statements hold in-sample *exactly*. Regime R1 with `p = p_n <= n - 1` (G may grow; c, s0, the betas, psis and rhos fixed; `g <= B_n < 2g` for all large n).
  >
  > **Theorem 5 (masked regime on LH; input for T38(b)).** Status: parts (a), (b), (c), (e): **PROVED** here from Theorems 1, 3, 4, 6, Lemmas 2.3, 4.1, 4.2 and the locked wave-1 T22(i), T22(ii-a), T22(iv-b); part (d) by citation of the locked T03 (its hypotheses verified below); the limit-law refinement in (b) is a PROOF SKETCH. Under G, `sigma^2 > 0` fixed:
  >
  > (a) **Near-truth start mass (T22(i) at S° ∈ R_0).** `1 - pi_0(S°) = O_{P_0}(2^B n^{-1/2})`; hence `pi_0(R_d) >= pi_0(R_0) >= pi_0(S°) = 1 - O_P(2^B n^{-1/2})` for every `d >= 0`: `b_n -> 1`.
  > (b) **Masking (T27(i)).** `pi_0(S0) = p^{-c} n^{-c/2} e^{O_P(1)}`, with the limit law of §3 (the masked hubs are mutually independent and orthogonal).
  > (c) **Regime.** VIS fails at reference S0 (block `C_{b_i}`, `U = ∅`: gain `||P_{x_{j_{b_i}}} mu||^2 = 0`), so the favourable branch T22(iii) does not apply — consistently, (b) gives `pi_0(S0) -> 0`.
  > (d) **Posterior.** `1 - pi(S0) = O_P(sqrt(log n/n))` (locked T03 under G, R, SE, BM-∞: SE from Lemma 4.1(a), `lambda_min(R_{S0}) >= lambda_min(Sigma)`, fixed nonzero betas give BM-∞, `||mu||^2/n <= theta'Sigma theta`).
  > (e) **Bridge endpoints.** The start is masked, the target is not: `pi_0(S0) -> 0`, `pi(S0) -> 1`, while `pi_0(R_0) -> 1`. By T22(iv-b) `inf_phi q_phi(S0) >= pi_0(S0)` only — the bridge must transport mass from `S° ∈ R_0` to `S0` (c missing-true additions), which is what T38(b) has to handle.
  >

### TH145 — R3-LHiid(VEXP) (W3-VEXP R3: LH, iid Gaussian realisation, part (a), fixed-partition surrogate)  [proposition]
- Source: `W3-VEXP/REPAIRS.md` §R3; `W1-EXP/PROOF.md` §4.3 (the gap). Positions: SF [pos 363], [pos 370]; XF A-REV2 [pos 568].

  > **R3. LH-iid (a).** Rows iid N(0, Σ_LH), |ψ_i| < min ρ, g ≤ B < 2g, p ≤ n^A, fixed betas. Then 1 − π₀(S₀∖M) = O_P(2^B √(log n) n^{−1/2}), and (b) holds as in W1. PROOF SKETCH; the only unwritten step is a routine uniform LLN for VIS-lin.

- Earlier version: W1-EXP §4.3 PROOF SKETCH left open "the conditioning argument for the leakage family uniformly over the X-dependent partition"; W1 also asserted $\delta_{\emptyset,j_b}\sim N(0,\|\mu\|^2/(n-1))$ exactly, which A-REV2 §5.4 corrects: "after normalizing a Gaussian column, its direction is spherical, not Gaussian ... The needed δ=O_P(1) follows from its conditional second moment".
- Status: PROOF SKETCH (W3-VEXP) → XF **GAP** (A-REV2 §2 "VEX random-design / actual-packing extensions — GAP. Preserve sketch status. Fixed-surrogate argument is sound in its restricted regime; general adaptive packing is not resolved"). Registry `R3-LHiid(VEXP)`: [APPLIED] W6-FIXREV2 keeps PROOF SKETCH; B ≥ 2g packing GAP stands. Superseded by TH150 (W3-PXN P3, rate $\sqrt{\log n/n}$, no $2^B$).
