### TH294 — Theorem T32(i): the score-evaluation ceiling of the SMC branch (and Corollaries T32(i-lit), T32(c))  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `W5-LOCKBOOK/PROOF.md` section "T32. Theorem T32(i): the score-evaluation ceiling of the SMC branch. PROVED"; re-count `W7-SEC/REPORT.md` (theme 9); referee `A-REV6/BOOK.md` rows "W5 T32-a" and "W5 T32(c)", R5; positions [pos 463] (launch), [pos 510], [pos 711] (W7-SEC launch), [pos 742].
- Pre-campaign statement (verbatim, `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T32.md`; status "CONJECTURED (not proved)"):
> ## Statement (as conjectured)
> Source: theorems/T32_T23C_resource_counts.md (repo paths under `Docs/Theory/`). Faithful condensation; the source file is authoritative.
> - (i) Score ceiling on the SMC branch: C_score <= sum_b 2^|C_b| + sum_{e=0}^{1} (1+4l) H_e [1 + 2m(T_e+L+4)] + 4 N_1 [1 + 2m(T_1+L+4)] + (8l+3)(l+1)[p + k*(p-k*)], with m = p + B + 2, sum_b 2^|C_b| <= p 2^B / B. (ii) Convolution O(pK); iid-sampler work <= O(Q_all p 2^B); at most 2(l+1) grid constructions with O(60 T_e) log-sum-exp calls each; Gram O(n p^2); total arithmetic work polynomial in (n, p). (iii) Storage O(np + p^2 + p 2^B + pK + N_1 K^2 + nK) words on the SMC branch (a streaming exact implementation uses O(np + pK + nK + K^2) words); implementation contracts, not lower bounds; the method's scan bound K(p-K) is corrected to max_{k<=K} k(p-k).
>

- Statement as proved (verbatim, W5-LOCKBOOK):
> **Theorem T32(i).** Assume EX-A (used only in step 2(a): the pilot has at most T_e stages). For every valid input on
> the SMC branch, every seed and every realisation of the streams and of the clock, the fit makes
>
>   C_eval ≤ Σ_b 2^{|C_b|}
>         + Σ_{e∈𝔈} { (1 + 4ℓ)·H_e·[1 + m(T_e + L + 4)] + (ℓ + 1)·[1 + (ℓ + 1)M_p] + (ℓ + 1)(40p + 1) }
>         + 4N_{e*}·[1 + m(T_{e*} + L + 4)] + (80p + 1) + [1 + (ℓ + 1)M_p],
>
> where 𝔈 ⊆ {0, 1} is the set of calibration tiers run and e* the final tier (the last two lines are absent if the
> fit stops before the final run). In particular, with 𝔈 = {0, 1}, e* = 1,
>
>   C_eval ≤ Σ_b 2^{|C_b|} + Σ_{e=0}^{1}(1 + 4ℓ)H_e[1 + m(T_e + L + 4)] + 4N₁[1 + m(T₁ + L + 4)]
>         + (2ℓ + 3)[1 + (ℓ + 1)M_p] + 2(ℓ + 1)(40p + 1) + 80p + 1,                                     (T32-a)
>
> with Σ_b 2^{|C_b|} ≤ p·2^B/B. The bound is deterministic (a sure bound). Counting logical score events instead,
> C_log satisfies the same bound with every m(T_e + L + 4) replaced by (m + p)(T_e + L + 4) ≤ 2m(T_e + L + 4).
>
> The pieces: **per particle-round ≤ m evaluations**; **per stage one round per particle**; per island N[1 + m(T + L + 4)]
> with T ≤ T_e; the pilot and ≤ 4ℓ diagnostic islands of H_e particles per tier; 4 final islands of N_{e*}; **at most
> 2ℓ + 3 local searches, each ≤ 1 + (ℓ + 1)M_p evaluations**; plus the table scores, the V rescorings and the inherited
> rescoring, which T32's conjectured form omits.
>
> **Corollary T32(i-lit). PROVED.** The conjectured right-hand side of T32(i) (theorem file
> `theorems/T32_T23C_resource_counts.md`),
>   Σ_b2^{|C_b|} + Σ_{e=0}^{1}(1 + 4ℓ)H_e[1 + 2m(T_e + L + 4)] + 4N₁[1 + 2m(T₁ + L + 4)] + (8ℓ + 3)(ℓ + 1)M_p,
> is ≥ the right side of (T32-a); so the conjectured inequality holds for C_eval (hence for C_score). It is **not**
> established for C_log by this argument (see Remark 3).
>
> **Corollary T32(c) (cost corollary of Thm 5(c)). PROVED.** With p ≤ n^A (A ≥ 1 w.l.o.g.) and n ≥ 3,
> C_eval ≤ c_A · n^{2A} · log²n for an absolute-in-n constant c_A; in general C_eval = O(max(n, p)·p·log²(n + p)
> + p²log²(n + p)). So the number of score evaluations is polynomial in (n, p), deterministically. (The arithmetic
> cost per evaluation, O(nK² + K³) per score under the fallback route, is T32(ii) and is not claimed here.)
>

### CJ208 — Corrected T32(c) rate with the calibration log^3 factor (Astra candidate R5)  [conjecture]
- Source: `A-REV6/BOOK.md` "R5. T32 count and corrected asymptotic corollary (Astra candidate proof)"; `T38-RECORD/T38_STATEMENT.md` V19; positions [pos 802] (A-REV6 launch), [pos 807], [pos 919] ("T38's cost rate should be log³, not log². It's still polynomial").
- Statement (verbatim, A-REV6 R5):
> ## R5. T32 count and corrected asymptotic corollary (Astra candidate proof)
>
> W5's T32-a adds the identifiable costs: block tables; one pilot and at most 4ℓ diagnostic islands per tier; at most two tiers; four final islands; ≤2ℓ+3 local searches; V rebuild and inherited-model rescores. A round evaluates at most m=p+B+2 new/proposed models; held Gibbs states are logical events, not additional evaluations. At most ℓ+1 full local-search scans follow from scanning before the move-limit test. These arguments support the count in the exact-arithmetic scope stated by W5. They neither give wall-time bounds nor adopt arithmetic/storage claims.
>
> But its asymptotic proof drops `(1+4ℓ)` in the island term. Put q=n+p+1 and M=max(n,p), absorbing the fixed lower budget 2500 into constants. Then H_e=O(M), m=O(p), T_e=O(log²q), L=O(log q), ℓ=O(log q). Therefore
>
> `Σ_e(1+4ℓ) H_e [1+m(T_e+L+4)] = O(M p log³q)`.
>
> Final islands cost O(Mp log²q). Local searches cost O(p²log²q), because their number and scans per search each contribute one log factor; rebuilds cost O(p log q), tables O(p) since B≤16. Thus the directly proved corollary is
>
> `C_eval = O(M p log³q + p²log²q)`.
>
> Under p≤n^A, A≥1, this is O(n^(2A)log³n), still polynomial. The smaller log² claim is not proved by this count; an additional amortisation argument, absent from W5/W7, would be needed to improve it. Also fix W5's slack step `1+4ℓ≥5ℓ` to `1+4ℓ≥4ℓ`; W7 correctly detects that slip. W7's fp pilot addendum has additional floating-step hypotheses and is not needed for this EX-A corollary.

- Status history: W5-LOCKBOOK's T32(c): "C_eval = O(max(n, p)·p·log²(n + p) + p²log²(n + p))" PROVED -> W7-SEC confirms without detecting the calibration-iteration factor -> A-REV6: GAP in the stated rate proof; Astra candidate repair R5 (Astra-authored, pending Claude verification, not adopted); v3 V19: "The displayed order ... carries an XF GAP ... Polynomiality survives."
- Depends on: TH294. Feeds: dropped (only polynomiality is claimed).
- Notes: "The smaller log² claim is not proved by this count; an additional amortisation argument, absent from W5/W7, would be needed to improve it." (A-REV6 R5).

- Source: false citation in `W1-T38E/PROOF.md` section 7 step (1), repeated in the W4-T38FULL dependency row C1; repair v2 change S6 and v3 text; positions [pos 570], [pos 807].

Therefore U ∪ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀} ⊆ U ∪ {δ₁ ≥ ½} ∪ (Uᶜ ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝒮⁺}), and Markov gives P(δ₁ ≥ ½) ≤ 2E₀δ₁. Adding LS0 scores cannot hurt: they only enlarge 𝒮⁺.

- Repair (verbatim, v2 change S6): "The "T11(vii)" citation is replaced by the direct set argument (locked T21(C1)). The two-sided form "P(𝒪, Ŝ⁺ = S₀) − (1 − P(U)) → 0" is added." (`W6-FIXREV1/T38_STATEMENT.md`, S6; source [AR] §8). v3 II.1 row C1: "strict maximiser on {π(S₀) > ½} ∩ {S₀ scored}; Markov | locked T21(C1); T38_PROOF §1".
- Status: incorrect citation (A-REV5: "T38 citation and cap | GAP/incorrect citation | VERIFIED"), the mathematics is unaffected; also K = min(p, floor(n/2)) (S3).

### RF223 — the brief's limit form "P(S-hat = S0) -> 1 - limsup P(U)"  [refuted claim]
- Source: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T38.md` ("Conclusion: P(S-hat = S0) -> 1 - limsup P(U)") and the W1-T38E brief; correction in `W1-T38E/PROOF.md` section 7; verified by `W3-VT38E/REPORT.md` ("Brief's limit form ... is ill-posed | VERIFIED | trivial"); positions [pos 201], [pos 370].
- The claim (verbatim, T38 one-pager):
> - Conclusion: P(S-hat = S0) -> 1 - limsup P(U). Not claimed: evidence or PIP accuracy in the masked regime (T26(i)-(ii), favourable only); any result about fits selected for having completed; comparative superiority.

- Correction (verbatim, W1-T38E section 7 conclusion, last sentences): "(The brief's "P(Ŝ = S₀) → 1 − limsup P(U)" is not a well-formed limit; this is the correct form.)" with the correct form liminf_n P(Uᶜ ∩ {Ŝ⁺ = S₀}) ≥ 1 − limsup_n P(U); and if P(U) → u then P(Uᶜ, Ŝ⁺ = S₀) → 1 − u (v0, TH241). In v2/v3 the strong form is the two-sided P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ = S₀}) − (1 − P(U)) → 0 (TH281).
- Status: malformed statement, repaired.

### RF224 — the brief's cost formula O(N T (p+B+2) + l p)  [refuted claim]
- Source: `main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T38.md` ("(c) cost corollary: expected score evaluations O(N_n T_n (p + B + 2) + l_n p), arithmetic from T32"); correction `W1-T38E/PROOF.md` section 7 corollary (c), `W5-VMASK/REPAIRS.md` R7; positions [pos 201], [pos 370], [pos 463].
- Correction (verbatim, W1-T38E):
> **Corollary (c), cost (PROVED given T32(i), which is itself an unlocked conjecture).** The total number of score evaluations is deterministically bounded by T32(i)'s ceiling, Σ_b 2^{|C_b|} + Σ_{e=0}^{1}(1+4ℓ)H_e[1 + 2m(T_e+L+4)] + 4N₁[1 + 2m(T₁+L+4)] + (8ℓ+3)(ℓ+1)[p + k_*(p−k_*)], plus (ℓ+1)[p + k_*(p−k_*)] for LS0. With N_e ≤ 4(2500 + n + p), T_e ≤ 4·max(1000, ℓ²), m = p + B + 2, ℓ = O(log n) and 2^B ≤ 2^16, this is O((n+p)(p+B)log²n + p²log²n) = poly(n). The brief's form O(N T(p+B+2) + ℓp) omits the scan's k(p−k) swaps and the number of local searches.

- Repair of the LS0 term (verbatim, W5-VMASK R7): "The local search evaluates its centre once when the centre is emitted, plus at most ℓ + 1 scans, each of ≤ p + k(p−k) neighbours. The LS0 term in T38 (c) and W1-T38E E3 should therefore read 1 + (ℓ+1)·max_{k≤K}[p + k(p−k)]. This is immaterial asymptotically."
- Status: incorrect formula, replaced (TH289, TH294).

### Dead ends and corrections (Theme 7)

- **The literal GUARD claim** "every reported output equals the guard-free output" is false (RF215, CE176): allocation, timing, peak memory and guard-record fields differ even when no guard fires (A-REV4 B1, A-REV8 E2). The transfer holds only for statistical outputs, scored sets, decisions and status; a stopped fit returns an incomplete HPM, so Theorems 4 and 5 need the convention "a stopped fit is no output" (G in U) (LM191 G1) [pos 696], [pos 843].
- **Conditioning on completion** breaks unbiasedness (RF221, CE175): "A guard that stops 0.22% of runs makes E[Z-hat | output] = 0.974 Z", and the direction of the bias can be upward under the engine-faithful cost rule [pos 328], [pos 742]. Never state results given completion; use P(O, .).

Label clash "(e') = Theorem B" versus "(e') = T37" resolved by (d+) = T37 (TH279). The "T37 as route (e)" was "a category error: the local search is a scan route".

### TH295 — W2-T26 Theorem A (T26 (i)-(ii) premise form; Thm 6A; `T26-ThmA`)  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative, latest repaired version): `W2-T26/PROOF.md` section 1 (Theorem A), section 0 for the definitions, `W2-T26/REPORT.md` section 2; paper form with the realised stage count in `W5-LOCKBOOK/STATEMENTS.tex` (Thm 6). Positions: launch [pos 334], wave report [pos 342, 424], referee launch [pos 507], A-REV4 launch [pos 677], synthesis [pos 796], re-reviews [pos 802, 806, 915, 919].
- Statement (verbatim, `W2-T26/PROOF.md` section 0 definitions needed):
  > **Δ_n := 1 − inf_{φ∈[0,1]} q_φ(S₀)** (the bridge's worst-case deficit at the truth, as in the T26 theorem file).
  > **ρ̄ := whole-round departure probability at the truth**: the probability that one φ = 1 round K₁ started at S₀ has a state ≠ S₀ on its path X⁽¹⁾,…,X⁽ᵐ⁾ (the ρ of T23's BASIN; T23 STATEMENT §5 reading 1).
  > Conventions off Ω: if S₀ ∉ Ω put Δ_n := 1, ρ̄ := 1, u_π := ∞.
  > **𝒢_n** = the event that the SMC branch is taken and calibration succeeds (a grid is constructed at the final tier, so the status is not `schedule_limit` and the final run executes). It is the event 𝒜 of T12 STATEMENT; it is (data, 𝓒)-measurable.
  > **ℰ_n** = the exact-enumeration branch (deterministic in (n, p): Σ_{k≤K} C(p,k) ≤ (5H₀+4N₀)p).
  > **Potential uninterrupted run.** On 𝒢_n, under EX-A, EX-S, CAL, START, the final run (4 islands, T stages, L burn-in and 4 measured rounds) is a well-defined random object (T12's I(𝓒)), whether or not the real job would finish within its resource allocation. Its outputs: Ẑ°_r, Ẑ° = ¼Σ_rẐ°_r, PIP̂°_{rj}, primary PIP̂°_j = ¼Σ_r PIP̂°_{rj}, MPM̂° = {j : PIP̂°_j > ½}. W_r := Ẑ°_r/Z.
  > **𝒪_n (output-available)** = the event that the method returns evidence and PIPs (status `exact` or `completed`). The reported Ẑ, Ẑ_r, PIP̂, MPM̂ exist only on 𝒪_n.
  > **T^max_n := 4T₀ = 4 max(1000, ℓ²)**, ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉. A construction with more than T_e intervals fails (METHODOLOGY §6.7) and e ≤ 1, so T ≤ T^max on 𝒢_n (a deterministic cap).
  > **b(𝓒) := 2(T+1)Δ_n / (1 − Δ_n)**, finite because Δ_n < 1 when S₀ ∈ Ω (Lemma 1).
  > **OUT (output bookkeeping).** 𝒪_n ⊆ ℰ_n ∪ 𝒢_n; on 𝒪_n ∩ 𝒢_n the reported outputs equal the potential run's outputs (an interruption, e.g. `resource_limit`, can remove outputs but never alters a reported value); on 𝒪_n ∩ ℰ_n, Ẑ = Z and PIP̂_j = PIP_j (exact enumeration under EX-A). This is the potential-uninterrupted-run / output-available split. **Nothing below conditions on 𝒪_n.** Every probabilistic conclusion has the form P(𝒪_n ∩ {error > ε}) → 0, and P(𝒪_n) → 1 is not claimed.

  > ### Theorem A (T26(i)–(ii), premise form: composition of locked results)
  > *Hypotheses.* EX-A, EX-S, CAL, START, OUT, and
  > - **(Ω)** P₀(s₀ ≤ K_n) → 1;
  > - **(P1)** for every ε > 0, P(𝒢_n ∩ {(T_n + 1)Δ_n > ε}) → 0 (joint probability over data and calibration streams; T_n the realised stage count). Sufficient deterministic-budget form: (T^max_n + 1)Δ_n → 0 in P₀-probability.
  > - **(P1-ex)** P₀(ℰ_n ∩ {δ₁ > ε}) → 0 for every ε > 0 (the exact-branch twin of (P1); implied by the deterministic-budget form of (P1), by T03(i), and vacuous when ℰ_n eventually fails, e.g. p ≥ 18 and n ≥ 22).
  >
  > No statistical assumption (G, R, SE, BM, EXP, VIS, NL) is used in Theorem A. The frozen second premise (L_n + 4)ρ*_n → 0 is **not needed** (Lemma 3, Remark 3.2).
  >
  > *Conclusions.*
  > **(A-0) Finite n, calibration-conditional.** Fix n, the data with S₀ ∈ Ω, and 𝓒 ∈ 𝒢_n. For every island r:
  > - (a) E_𝓒|Ẑ°_r/Z − 1| ≤ b(𝓒) and E_𝓒|Ẑ°/Z − 1| ≤ b(𝓒).
  > - (b) For f = the fraction of island r's particles ≠ S₀ at the end of stage T, or at the start of any measured round (after L + h − 1 terminal rounds, h = 1..4): E_𝓒 f ≤ min{1, 2δ₁ + 2b(𝓒)}.
  > - (c) E_𝓒 max_j |PIP̂°_{rj} − 1{j∈S₀}| ≤ min{1, 2δ₁ + 2b(𝓒)} + ρ̄ + u_π ≤ min{1, 2δ₁ + 2b(𝓒)} + (B+4)u_π; the same bound holds for the primary PIP̂°_j.
  > - (d) P_𝓒(MPM̂° ≠ S₀) ≤ 2[min{1, 2δ₁ + 2b(𝓒)} + ρ̄ + u_π].
  > - (e) Δ_n = max{1 − π₀(S₀), δ₁} exactly, and ρ̄ ≤ Σ_e K_e(S₀, Ω∖{S₀}) ≤ (B+3)u_π.
  >
  > **(A-i) Evidence consistency.** For every ε > 0, each of P(𝒪_n ∩ {|Ẑ/Z − 1| > ε}), P(𝒪_n ∩ {max_r |Ẑ_r/Z − 1| > ε}), P(𝒪_n ∩ {|log Ẑ − log Z| > ε}) tends to 0; and for the potential run, P(𝒢_n ∩ {max_r |Ẑ°_r/Z − 1| > ε}) → 0.
  >
  > **(A-ii) PIP and MPM consistency.** For every ε > 0, P(𝒪_n ∩ {max_j |PIP̂_j − 1{j∈S₀}| > ε}) → 0 (also with max over islands r of the islandwise PIPs) and P(𝒪_n ∩ {MPM̂ ≠ S₀}) → 0. The same holds for the potential run on 𝒢_n.
  >
  > **(A-iii) Not claimed.** P(𝒪_n) → 1 (operational completion; OP-s); any statement in the masked regime; the secondary (Ẑ_r-weighted) PIP; the HPM (T38 replaces old T26(iii)); any uniform Monte Carlo rate in N (none of the bounds depend on N); anything about runs selected by their flags or by their completion; floating-point validity (EX-A).
- Earlier versions / repairs: (1) Pre-campaign T26 (CONJECTURED) required "(T_n + 1) Δ_n → 0 and (L_n + 4) ρ*_n → 0" (`main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T26.md`, FROZEN_LIST restatement); Theorem A removes the second premise (see LM200 (LM200) and RF235) and uses the exact-branch twin (P1-ex). ### LM198 — W2-T26 Lemma 1 (Delta identity)  [lemma]
- Source: `W2-T26/PROOF.md` section 2; `REPORT.md` section 3 item 1; positions as TH295.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 1 (Δ identity). PROVED.
  > If S₀ ∈ Ω then Δ_n = max{1 − π₀(S₀), 1 − π(S₀)} < 1.
  >
  > *Proof.* T22(iv-b) (locked, deterministic, assumes only S₀ ∈ Ω) gives sup_{φ∈[0,1]}[1 − q_φ(S₀)] ≤ max{1 − π₀(S₀), 1 − π(S₀)}. Conversely φ = 0 and φ = 1 belong to [0,1] and q₀ = π₀, q₁ = π, so the sup is at least each endpoint value. Both endpoint masses are > 0 (γ₀, γ₁ > 0 on Ω), so Δ_n < 1. ∎
  >
  > So (P1) ⇔ [(T_n+1)(1 − π₀(S₀)) → 0 and (T_n+1)δ₁ → 0] (on 𝒢_n): the bridge interior 0 < φ < 1 adds nothing.
- Status history: PROVED (W2-T26) -> SF CORRECT, grid check 66/66, $|\Delta_{grid}-\Delta|\le 1.1\cdot10^{-16}$ (W5-LOCKBOOK) -> XF VERIFIED (A-REV4: Hölder bound on the normaliser, $q_\varphi(S_0)\ge \min(q_0(S_0),q_1(S_0))$; "Feasibility and strict positive scores are essential"). Grid minimum over 201 values of $\varphi$ equalled the endpoint minimum in all 246 runs (REPORT 4.1).
- Depends on: TH116 (T22(iv-b)). Feeds: TH295, TH296; ⟦W5-FAVIID C2⟧.

### LM199 — W2-T26 Lemma 2 (departure from the truth; exact rho-bar)  [lemma]
- Source: `W2-T26/PROOF.md` section 2.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 2 (departure from the truth). PROVED.
  > Assume S₀ ∈ Ω. Let K_e, over the m = p + B + 2 labels (Gibbs j = 1..p, one uniform swap, B neighbour swaps, one independence proposal), be the elementary kernels at φ = 1. Then
  >
  >   ρ̄ ≤ Σ_e K_e(S₀, Ω∖{S₀}) ≤ Σ_{j=1}^p π(S₀Δ{j})/π(S₀) + (B+2)u_π ≤ (B+3)u_π;  in particular ρ̄ ≤ ρ*.
  >
  > *Exact form.* By the same Markov structure, P(no departure | σ) = ∏_{k=1}^m [1 − K_{σ(k)}(S₀, Ω∖{S₀})], which does not depend on σ. Hence ρ̄ = 1 − ∏_e [1 − K_e(S₀, Ω∖{S₀})] exactly (≤ Σ_e K_e(S₀, Ω∖{S₀}) by the union bound).
- Status history: PROVED (W2-T26) -> SF CORRECT ("Exact product form re-derived"; simulated departure frequency agrees with exact rho-bar within 1 s.e., REPORT 4.4: 0.1162 vs 0.1155) -> XF VERIFIED (A-REV4: "Invariance alone implies K_e(S0,y)<=pi(y)/pi(S0). Gibbs destinations for distinct labels are distinct one-flip states ... No union over all p unrestricted destinations is introduced"). A-REV9 notes that $\bar\rho\le\min(1,(B+3)u_\pi)$ is already T23(iii), so M1 does not depend on this lemma.
- Notes: the bound $(B+3)u_\pi$ overstates the true $\bar\rho$ by 4-8x in the designs tried; the exact product form is cheap and could replace $\rho^*$ in T24/T37-type statements (REPORT section 7). Depends on TH107 (T09(ii)), TH110 (T12 (R3)). Feeds: TH295, TH300, TH313.

### LM200 — W2-T26 Lemma 3 (round-start occupancy controls the bad-round fraction)  [lemma]
- Source: `W2-T26/PROOF.md` section 2 (Lemma 3, Remarks 3.1, 3.2).
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Lemma 3 (round-start occupancy controls the bad-round fraction). PROVED.
  > Fix data with S₀ ∈ Ω, 𝓒 ∈ 𝒢_n and an island r. Let B̄_r be the bad-round fraction of T23 STATEMENT §1 and g_{r,h} the fraction of island r's particles ≠ S₀ at the start of measured round h (= terminal round L + h). Then
  >
  >   E_𝓒 B̄_r ≤ ¼ Σ_{h=1}^{4} E_𝓒 g_{r,h} + ρ̄.
  >
  > **Remark 3.1 (what the frozen premise came from).** If occupancy is controlled only at the end of stage T (T23(ii-c)'s "initial occupancy" δ), one must also pay for departures in all L + h rounds: with 𝓡 = {S₀}, T23(ii-c) applies with BASIN({S₀}, r₀ = 1, a = 1 − ρ̄, η = ρ̄, ρ = ρ̄, δ) and gives δ + ρ̄^L + 2(L+4)ρ̄ + u_π; a direct union bound gives δ + (L + 5/2)ρ̄ + u_π. That is the origin of the premise (L_n+4)ρ*_n → 0.
  >
  > **Remark 3.2 (why it is not needed).** T15 is stated at every recording position τ ∈ 𝒯, including (b) "any fixed elementary prefix within the L + 4 terminal rounds", because its hypothesis H-T12 is T12(i.b), which holds after any fixed finite sequence of φ = 1 rounds. So occupancy is controlled afresh at the start of each measured round, and only one round's departure ρ̄ is paid. This removes the (L+4) factor, and with it the premise.
- Status history: PROVED (W2-T26; flagged by the author for review: "T15 at position (b) ... exactly T12(i.b)") -> SF CORRECT, "Lemma 3: T15 at a terminal-round prefix (T12(i.b)): CORRECT ... W_r is unchanged after stage T", redundancy "CORRECT, and material" (At n = 40,960 median $(L+4)\rho^*$ = 2.4-3.9 vs $\bar\rho+u_\pi$ = 0.05-0.07) (W5-LOCKBOOK) -> XF VERIFIED (A-REV4: "T12(i.b) explicitly includes every fixed terminal prefix ... each finite-n application is legitimate"; "This removes the old accumulated burn-in departure factor; it does not assert that trajectories never departed during burn-in"). Independently re-derived by A-DRAFT (D5, D8) using only locked identities (A-REV6: "A-DRAFT's sharper occupancy proof is independent").

### RF225 — "the exact branch fails whenever p >= 18 and n >= 22" (`T26-exact-branch-paren`)  [refuted claim]
- Source: false claim in `W2-T26/PROOF.md` (P1-ex parenthesis in Theorem A, and the proof of (A-i),(A-ii), "at p ≥ 18 and n ≥ 22, ℰ_n fails") and `W2-T26/REPORT.md` section 4 ("That is the smallest p at which v3 takes the SMC branch for n ≥ 22, because 2¹⁸ > 12,560·18."); refutation A-REV4 `REVIEW.md` section 7 (verdict table ERROR), reconfirmed A-REV5 `REVIEW.md` section 4 and A-REV6 `BOOK.md` row 28. Positions: claim [pos 342, 424]; verdict first used by HQ [pos 796] and in W8-SYNTH; summary of Astra errors [pos 1233, 1238].
- Statement of the false claim (verbatim): "(P1-ex) ... vacuous when ℰ_n eventually fails, e.g. p ≥ 18 and n ≥ 22" and "(…) it is vacuous when ℰ_n eventually fails (p_n → ∞ fast enough; at p ≥ 18 and n ≥ 22, ℰ_n fails)." (`W2-T26/PROOF.md`).
- Refutation (A-REV4 section 7, verbatim): "The repeated parenthetical assertion that the exact branch fails whenever p>=18 and n>=22 is false under the actual budgets. Counterexample: p=18, n=2^18. Then K=p, the state count is 2^18, N0=n, and the threshold (5H0+4N0)p is at least 4*2^18*18, strictly larger than the entire state count. The exact branch is therefore taken. More generally fixed p eventually enumerates, as common regime R2 explicitly says. Remove this parenthetical and replace it with the exact combinatorial inequality, or a genuinely sufficient growth condition. This does not invalidate Theorem A's fully written statement because P1-ex is retained, nor Theorem B because T03 supplies it." See CE180.
- Replacement: none written (registry: "[PENDING] none written (A-REV4: replace by the exact combinatorial inequality or a genuinely sufficient growth condition)"); W5-LOCKBOOK `STATEMENTS.tex` simply states (P1-ex) with no example; A-REV6 `BOOK.md`: "ERROR remains; use actual combinatorial branch criterion". The fixed-p fact "the exact branch is eventually taken" is recorded as N12-eventual dispatch (K76, seat-proved, unchecked).
- Status: **ERROR** (XF, A-REV4 / A-REV5 / A-REV6). Affects only the supporting remark; Theorem A (P1-ex retained) and Theorem B (T03 supplies it) unaffected. Lesson: the premise scan at p = 18 used n up to 163,840, where the exact branch is not excluded at all n.

### TH298 — Proposition 2 (c): pooled Ẑ x primary PIP has bias -3/4 Cov (`Prop2(c)`)  [proposition]
- Source: `W2-BOOK/REPORT.md` section 2 (c); proof `W2-BOOK/PROOF.md` section 1 (c); data `scripts/frozen_run_exact.py`, `results/frozen_run_exact.txt`; locked T12 (iv.b). Positions as TH297.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > - (c) **Not claimed, and false in general.** Pooled × pooled: E[Ẑ·P̄_j | 𝓒] = Z·PIP_j − ¾·Cov(PIP̂_1j, Ẑ₁ | 𝓒). The normalised P̄_j is not unbiased: E[P̄_j | 𝓒] − PIP_j = −Cov(PIP̂_1j, Ẑ₁ | 𝓒)/Z. Both biases are non-zero in an explicit component instance: < −0.17 for P̄₁, and < −0.1275·Z for Ẑ·P̄₁.

  and (`PROOF.md` section 1 (c)): "E[Ẑ·P̄_j | 𝓒] = Z·PIP_j − ¾·Cov(PIP̂_{1j}, Ẑ₁ | 𝓒) = Z·{PIP_j + ¾(E[P̄_j | 𝓒] − PIP_j)}. In the T12(iv.b) component instance, E[Ẑ·P̄₁] − Z·PIP₁ < −0.1275·Z, so pooled × pooled is not an identity." Proof: the 4 diagonal terms each equal Z·PIP_j; the 12 off-diagonal terms factorise by conditional island independence (locked T12(iv.c)) to Z·μ_j with μ_j := E_𝓒 PIP̂_{1j}, so E_𝓒[Ẑ·P̄_j] = (Z/16)(4·PIP_j + 12·μ_j). "With I islands the factor ¾ becomes (I − 1)/I."
- Status history: PROVED (W2-BOOK) -> SF CORRECT: "Reproduced: ¾Cov/Z = 0.130481, relative bias −0.131716, closed form = convolution to 10⁻⁵⁸" (W5-LOCKBOOK; its paper form: "in an explicit instance the two biases are −0.1305 Z and −0.174") -> XF **VERIFIED** (A-REV4: "bias −¾Cov_C(PIP̂₁ⱼ, Ẑ₁)"; Owls 50-digit finite-law reproduction (mpmath 1.3.0) matched −0.1739741778 (primary PIP bias) and −0.1317163950 (pooled relative bias), residuals ~10^-50, "numerical check, not an interval certificate"; A-REV6: "never pooled-product unbiasedness").
- Proved by / checked by: W2-BOOK; W5-LOCKBOOK; A-REV4, A-REV6.
- Depends on: TH110 (T12(iv.b)), TH110 (T12(iv.c)), TH297. Feeds: M1 ⟦Theorem V/H⟧ (K50: "The product Ẑ̄·PIP^eq is not unbiased: E[Ẑ̄·PIP^eq_j] − Z·PIP_j = −(1−1/R)·Cov(Ẑ₁, PIP̂_1j | 𝓒)"), S-POOL, L-T12. Replaces the false claim RF226; the instance is CE182.

### CE181 — stylised resource guard: conditioning on completion biases Ẑ (`CEX-guard`)  [counterexample]
- Source: `W2-BOOK/PROOF.md` section 0.3; `REPORT.md` section 4; reproduced `W5-LOCKBOOK/REPORT.md` section 4.1 and verdict table.
- Construction (verbatim, section 0.3): "**Instance.** The T12(iv.b) component instance: n = 20, p = 2, with the appendix data of the T12 STATEMENT; T = 1, N = 1, L′ = L = 5, M = 4, flag unset. Its scope is that of T12(iv.b). The full method would take the exact branch at p = 2, and N = 1 is not a production budget. **Stylised guard.** The cost of scoring a model of size k is 1 + k³ units. Under SR, a Gibbs step scores both configurations, a swap scores its proposal, and an independence step scores its proposal. The stage-0 start draw is also scored. The guard is checked after the stage-1 bridge stage, as in the engine. The output is available iff the accumulated cost is at most h. Then Ẑ/Z₀ = e^{D·B} with B = 1{X₀ = {1,2}} and D = 8.1468, and the run that would take the big model (the large weight) is also the expensive run."
- Table (verbatim): h = 8: P(𝒪_h) = 0.5468, E[Ẑ | 𝒪_h]/Z = 0.0103; h = 30: 0.9614, 0.0112; h = 32: 0.9907, 0.7978; h = 33: 0.99783, 0.9739; h = 40: 0.9999995, 0.99998. Summary (REPORT section 4): stopped share 0.22% gives 0.974, 0.93% gives 0.798, 3.9% gives 0.011. "At h = 33 the guard stops 0.22% of runs, close to the 0.25% observed in PROD-H. Yet the output-conditional evidence is 2.6% low."
- Same-family reproduction (W5-LOCKBOOK): the both-configurations-paid convention reproduces 0.01123 / 0.79784 / 0.97392; the engine-faithful "flip only" convention gives E[Ẑ | 𝒪]/Z = 1.00136 (h = 16, P(𝒪) = 0.970286) and 0.97524 (h = 19, P(𝒪) = 0.996830): "0.32% stops give E[Ẑ | 𝒪] = 0.975Z; 3.0% stops give 1.0014Z", so the bias can be upward.
- Status: COUNTEREXAMPLE (exact enumeration, 50 digits; registry `CEX-guard`); XF VERIFIED* (A-REV4: stylised, "cannot quantify actual engine bias"). Refutes RF227. Feeds M1 and S-POOL, S-OUT, L-RO.

### TH300 — F-MASKPIP Proposition M1 (evidence-weighted PIP bound; `FMP-M1`)  [proposition]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 (Proposition M1); positions: launch [pos 675], finished [pos 748], A-REV9 launch [pos 830, 843], results [pos 915, 919]. Helper simulation `F-MASKPIP/results/SIM_NOTES.md` (Opus 5.5 helper).
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Proposition M1 (evidence-weighted PIP bound). PROVED.
  > For every data set, every successful 𝓒 (any frozen grid, any N ≥ 1), every island r and every s ∈ {0, …, L+3}:
  >   (M1-a) E_𝓒[W_r f_{r,s}] = δ₁ and E_𝓒[W_r] = 1;
  >   (M1-b) E_𝓒[W_r B̄_r] ≤ δ₁ + ρ̄;
  >   (M1-c) E_𝓒[W_r err_r] ≤ δ₁ + ρ̄ + u_π.

  with (from section 2 of the report) W_r := Ẑ_r/Z, terminal positions τ_s ("after s terminal rounds", τ₀ = end of stage T), f_{r,s} the fraction of island r's particles outside S₀ at τ_s, B̄_r the T23(ii) bad-round fraction, err_r := max_j |PIP̂_rj − 1{j∈S₀}|, "Masked regime: π₀(S₀) → 0 while δ₁ → 0 (F-DRAFT §0). Throughout S₀ ∈ Ω; if S₀ ∉ Ω then u_π = ∞ and all bounds are trivial."
- Proof route (Summary:): (a) is locked T12(i.b) at the position τ_s with f = 1_{Ω∖{S₀}}; (b) is W2-T26 Lemma 3 multiplied by W_r ≥ 0, with the conditional departure step from T12 (R3) and H-measurability of W_r; (c) is T23(ii-a,b) pathwise (err_r ≤ B̄_r + u_π) times W_r. Remarks in the report: "No independence across particles, no union bound over coordinates, no premise on π₀(S₀), no bound on T, no condition on N"; "It is **not** an identity: E_𝓒[W_r f_{r,s}] = δ₁ is, and the rest is the T23 pathwise step."

### TH302 — F-MASKPIP Proposition M3 (no conditional evidence theorem from first moments; `FMP-M3`)  [proposition]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 (Proposition M3); review `A-REV9/REVIEW.md` ("Masked PIPs and evidence variance: proof checks") and `A-REV9/MASKED_PW2_CHECK.md`. Positions as TH300.
- Statement (verbatim, as printed):
  > ### Proposition M3 (no conditional evidence theorem from first moments). PROVED.
  > Let C = C_{r,s} be any crossing event with P_𝓒(C) =: κ > 0. Then
  >   E_𝓒[W_r | C] ≥ (1 − 2δ₁)/κ  and  E_𝓒[W_r | Cᶜ] ≤ 2δ₁/(1−κ).
  > Moreover, for every κ ∈ (0,1) and δ₁ ∈ (0, ¼) there is an abstract instance of T15's setting (W_r > 0, f_r ∈ [0,1], E W_r = 1, E[W_r f_r] ≤ δ₁) in which P(W_r < c | C) = 1 for some c < 1 (take W_r = c on a subset of C of mass κ − κ′ and W_r = (1 − c(κ−κ′))/κ′ on the rest, with f_r = 0 on C and f_r = 1, W_r = 0 on Cᶜ; the identity constraints are all satisfied).
- Earlier versions / repairs: the clause "Moreover ... P(W_r < c | C) = 1" is **false as printed** (RF229, instance repaired in CE184); the conditional-mean inequalities are retained but need 0 < κ < 1 (A-REV9: "As written M3 assumes only kappa>0, so its second conditional expectation is undefined at kappa=1; omit that clause there or restrict kappa. The first inequality alone does not assert overestimation for every kappa: its lower bound exceeds one only when kappa<1-2delta"). The report's reading: "Conditioning on delivery does not restore Ẑ: on average over crossing realisations the island overestimates by 1/κ, and the dispersion of W_r on C is unconstrained by every first-moment identity we have ... Any masked-regime evidence statement needs a second-moment input (PW2 → T25(iv)) or a different estimator. The one thing that survives everywhere is T31(i)".
- Status history: PROVED (F-MASKPIP) -> XF (A-REV9): **ERROR** on the printed probability-one instance, conditional means **VERIFIED** for 0 < κ < 1 (A-REV9: LOCKABLE list: "M3 conditional means restricted to 0<kappa<1 ... Exclude original M3 counterexample"). Registry: `PROVED (SF: none; XF: ERROR (A-REV9))`. Because the registry row for `FMP-M3` records only the ERROR code, the ID TH302 records the valid conditional-mean part and RF229 the refuted clause.
- Depends on: TH301 ((M2-e)), TH110 (T12), TH113 (T15).
- Feeds: SYNTHESIS M7; K53 row of R0_DIFF (`FMP-M3: PROVED (SF: none; XF: ERROR (A-REV9))`); final S-Z uses only the exception-probability form (see Dead ends).

### RF229 — F-MASKPIP M3 printed instance: "P(W_r < c | C) = 1 for some c < 1"  [refuted claim]
- Source: false clause quoted in TH302; refutation A-REV9 `REVIEW.md` (verdict "F-MASKPIP M3: ERROR probability-one counterexample"), `MASKED_PW2_CHECK.md` ("ERROR candidate: M3's claimed lower-tail example").
- Refutation (verbatim, A-REV9): "The assertion `P(W<c | C)=1` for some `c<1`, for every `kappa in (0,1), delta in (0,1/4)`, is false. For example, `kappa=1/2, delta=1/10` forces `E[W|C]>=1.6`, incompatible with `W<c<1` almost surely on C. The proposed example itself puts a very large W on a positive-probability subset of C, directly contradicting its claimed probability one. It also sets `W=0` on C-complement despite assuming `W>0`."
- Replacement: CE184 (the intended moment non-implication, P(W<c|C) → 1 as κ′ → 0). Status: ERROR (XF). Lesson: do not state a probability-one lower tail from first moments.

### CE184 — repaired abstract moment instance for M3  [counterexample]
- Source: `A-REV9/MASKED_PW2_CHECK.md` ("Repair preserving the intended first-moment obstruction"); also `REVIEW.md`.
- Construction (verbatim): "fix `0<kappa<1`, `0<delta<1/4`, and choose `0<a<min(c,(1-delta)/kappa)` for a chosen `0<c<1`. For small `0<kappa'<kappa`, partition C into masses `kappa-kappa'` and `kappa'`, set `f=0` there, and set W respectively to `a`, and `b=[1-delta-a(kappa-kappa')]/kappa'`. On C-complement set `f=1`, `W=delta/(1-kappa)`. All weights are strictly positive, `E W=1`, `E Wf=delta`, and C is exactly `{f<=1/2}`. For sufficiently small kappa', b exceeds c and `P(W<c | C)=1-kappa'/kappa -> 1`. Thus no useful universal conditional lower-tail guarantee follows from these first moments alone ... This is an abstract moment counterexample, not a construction of a v3 BVS dataset/run."
- Status: referee-authored (A-REV9); not realised by an actual BVS run.

### TH303 — F-MASKPIP Theorem R (restart theorem for the PIPs; `FMP-ThmR`)  [theorem]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 (Theorem R and "Where the inputs come from"). Positions as TH300.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Theorem R (restart theorem for the PIPs; no evidence input). PROVED as a composition.
  > Fix data, a successful 𝓒 and an island r. Let 𝔛 ⊆ Ω be fixed given 𝓒 with S₀ ∈ 𝔛 (a *repair basin*), and H ∈ {1, …, L}. Define
  > - δ_𝔛 := E_𝓒[N⁻¹Σ_i 1{X_{i,0} ∉ 𝔛}] (expected fraction outside 𝔛 at the end of stage T; "late delivery");
  > - β_H := sup_{x∈𝔛} P_x(X_h ≠ S₀ for all h = 1, …, H) under H rounds of the φ = 1 kernel (uniform entrance failure).
  > Then
  >   (R-a) E_𝓒 err_r ≤ δ_𝔛 + β_H + (L+4)ρ̄ + u_π, and the same for err_prim;
  >   (R-b) P_𝓒(MPM̂ ≠ S₀) ≤ 2[δ_𝔛 + β_H + (L+4)ρ̄ + u_π].
- Notes on inputs (verbatim): "β_H: W1-T24G Theorem B (candidate) bounds P_x(S₀ not *scored* within H rounds) ≤ v(1−c_*)^{⌊H/v⌋} + Hη. Scoring is weaker than entering; the gap is closed by the acceptance step ... So β_H ≤ [Theorem B bound] + u_π once u_π ≤ 1/B." "What Theorem R does not use. Any evidence quantity; any bound on T; any ESS; the start mass π₀(S₀). It is the masked-regime analogue of Theorem A's PIP clause with the evidence lower tail (T15) replaced by delivery + repair. Note the price: the (L+4)ρ̄ term is back (W2-T26 Lemma 3 removed it only through T15's re-control at each round start, which needs the evidence lower tail that the masked regime lacks)." Escalation (report section 6): the "entrance vs scored" acceptance argument "should be written against the method's exact Hastings factor for neighbour swaps".
- Status history: PROVED as a composition, CONDITIONAL on two masked-regime inputs: DELIV-POP (OPEN, CJ217) and REP (W1-T24G Theorem B, PROVED candidate; ⟦Theorem B (T24)⟧ SF VERIFIED* (W2-VT24G), XF VERIFIED* (A-REV1)). No review of Theorem R itself: registry `PROVED (SF: none; XF: none)`; A-REV9 explicitly excludes it ("no approval of F-MASKPIP N-b/N-c or Theorem R").
- Depends on: TH117 (T23(ii-a,b)), TH110 (T12 (R3)), ⟦Theorem B (T24)⟧, LM199, CJ217. Feeds: R0_DIFF K58 ("Masked PIP/MPM consistency of the equal-weight estimator reduces to population delivery and repair"), final disposition FUTURE_WORK FW7 ("Reduces to population delivery; FMP-DELIVPOP is OPEN").
- Notes / UNCERTAIN: at n = 200 with median π₀(𝓡₂) ≈ 0.8 the bound is ≥ 0.2 before repair and departure terms (report section 7): it "explains the mechanism, not the study's numbers".

### CJ217 — DELIV-POP (population delivery into the repair basin; `FMP-DELIVPOP`)  [open problem]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 ("Where the inputs come from") and section 6 item 4; registry `FMP-DELIVPOP` OPEN; SYNTHESIS: "Masked-regime accuracy of Ẑ and the PIPs. It needs population delivery, DELIV-POP (`F-MASKPIP`)".
- Statement (verbatim): "δ_𝔛: this is the **population** version of T38(b2)'s DELIV ("at least one particle in 𝔛_n after the last resampling"). It is OPEN. Mechanism (CONJECTURE): once a W-particle exists at a stage t < T, the next resampling amplifies it by e^{Δ_{t+1}(d(W) − d(outsiders))} = e^{Θ(n)/T_e} ≫ N (Prop. NM gap, Δ_t ≥ 2^{−60} is not enough but the method's grid has Δ_t ≥ 1/T_e at the pilot), so the population collapses onto W (W4-SHARE Lemma PD, Prop. SH threshold); if the arrival is at stage T itself, only the arriving particles are in W and the rest must be in the repair basin already (𝔛 ⊇ Lat(S°) in the LH family, where the whole start basin is downhill to S₀ at φ = 1 by W4-SHARE Prop. M). So DELIV-POP ⇐ DELIV ∧ (an amplification stage remains, or 𝔛 ⊇ start basin)." Escalation: "the amplification mechanism (one resampling after arrival collapses the population onto W) deserves a lemma of its own (W4-SHARE's branching envelope is the right tool)."
- Status: OPEN (medium cost via an amplification lemma from W4-SHARE D4); stronger than T38's one-particle DELIV. Note the dependency on RF203 (SHARE-M(b)), which has an A-REV3 ERROR (Prop. M(b): expansion ERROR; "vanishing crossing temperature under all T03 hypotheses" ERROR), restricted by A-REV6 candidate M-star; theme 6. Final disposition: FUTURE_WORK FW7 (K58); also FW6.

### TH305 — F-MASKPIP Proposition N (a): evidence collapse on non-crossing realisations (`FMP-Na`)  [proposition]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 (Proposition N (a)); review A-REV9 `REVIEW.md`, `MASKED_PW2_CHECK.md` ("VERIFIED candidate / precision GAP: N-a"). Positions as TH300.
- Statement (verbatim, as printed):
  > **(N-a) PROVED (general).** Let (data, 𝓒) be any sequence with δ₁ → 0 and liminf P_𝓒(f_{r,0} > ½) ≥ κ > 0 (the terminal population misses S₀ with probability ≥ κ). Then
  >   P_𝓒(f_{r,0} > ½ ∧ W_r < √δ₁) ≥ κ − 2√δ₁ → κ:
  > on the non-crossing realisations the island underestimates Z by a factor ≥ δ₁^{−1/2} → ∞; under T03's rate the factor is ≥ (n/log n)^{1/4}(1+o(1)). T31(i) still holds (P_𝓒(Z ≥ 0.05Ẑ_r) ≥ 0.95), with the true Z above the reported bound by a factor ≥ 20δ₁^{−1/2}. If κ → 1 this holds with probability → 1. *Proof:* (M2-a). ∎
- Earlier versions / repairs (A-REV9, verbatim): "The exact finite-index consequence is `P(f_0>1/2, W<sqrt(delta)) >= P(f_0>1/2)-2sqrt(delta)`. Consequently `delta_n->0` and `liminf P(f_0>1/2)>=kappa` give liminf of the left side at least kappa. They do not imply the report's literal finite-n lower bound `kappa-2sqrt(delta_n)` without the stronger premise `P(f_0>1/2)>=kappa` at each index. Replace it by the displayed probability or `kappa-o(1)-2sqrt(delta_n)`." And: "T03 states only `delta_n=O_P(sqrt(log n/n))`; it does not imply the report's unit-constant factor `>= (n/log n)^(1/4)(1+o(1))`. It yields an inverse-order-in-probability lower scale ... factor `>= C^(-1/2)(n/log n)^(1/4)`." A-REV9 LOCKABLE: "N-a's corrected finite-index inequality. Exclude ... unit-constant rate claim."
- Status history: PROVED (F-MASKPIP) -> XF **GAP** (A-REV9) on the literal finite-index/rate wording; the finite-index inequality with the actual non-crossing probability VERIFIED. Registry: `PROVED (SF: none; XF: GAP (A-REV9))`.
- Depends on: TH301 (M2-a), TH103 (T03). Feeds: R0_DIFF K40 and S-Z (masked lower tail, exception-probability form only: P(Ẑ_r > √δ₁·Z on a terminal-off island) ≤ 2√δ₁, ÷κ if conditioned on an off event of probability κ); SYNTHESIS: "N-a ... PROVED".

### TH306 — F-MASKPIP Proposition N (b): reflected comparator (`FMP-Nb`)  [proposition]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 (N-b).
- Statement (verbatim): "**(N-b) The reflected comparator (what W_r actually is on a non-crossing realisation). PROOF SKETCH.** If the population stays in a set M ∌ S₀ through stages 0, …, T−1 and at each stage is approximately distributed as q_{t−1}(·|M), then q̂_{t−1}(G_t) ≈ Z̄_t(M)/Z̄_{t−1}(M), the product telescopes, and W_r ≈ π(M)/π₀(M) = r_M (the comparator mean Z·r_W of `00_COMMON.md` §2) ≤ δ₁/π₀(M). So the underestimation is by the ratio of the posterior mass to the start mass of the region the bridge actually explored, ≈ δ₁ when the start basin M carries almost all of π₀. (N-a) is the rigorous, weaker form (√δ₁ instead of δ₁)."
- Status: PROOF SKETCH (author); no review (A-REV9: "no approval of F-MASKPIP N-b/N-c"). Superseded in rigour by API-MASKZPIP E1/E2 (TH308, TH309).

### TH307 — F-MASKPIP Proposition N (c): explicit split family, evidence and PIPs separate (`FMP-Nc`)  [proposition]
- Source: `F-MASKPIP/REPORT.md` section 3 (N-c) and section 4.1 (helper simulation). Positions as TH300; empirical corroboration in W4-SHARE headline 4 (PB design).
- Statement (verbatim):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.997) from `A-REV6/sources/F-MASKPIP__REPORT.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > **(N-c) An explicit split family. PROOF SKETCH (deterministic core PROVED; family-level claims rest on candidates).** Take the one-stage grid T = 1, φ = (0, 1) (admissible: T ≥ 1; all locked results hold for any frozen grid). Then exactly W_r = q̂₀(e^d)/E_{π₀}[e^d] (T14(i-a)). Let M_D := {x ∈ Ω : d(x) ≤ d(S₀) − D}. On the event A := {all N initial draws lie in M_D}, W_r ≤ e^{−D}/π₀(S₀)  (PROVED: E_{π₀}e^d ≥ π₀(S₀)e^{d(S₀)} and q̂₀(e^d) ≤ e^{d(S₀) − D} on A), and P_𝓒(Aᶜ) ≤ Nπ₀(Ω∖M_D). On the LH exact-Gram family of W1-EXP §4 (omission masking of c ≥ 1 hubs M; start mode S° = S₀∖M), take M_D := {x : x ∩ M = ∅} (hub-free models) and D := d(S₀) − max_{x∩M=∅} d(x). The claim needed is D = Θ(n): d(S₀) − d(S°) = Θ(n) (Prop. NM: the hubs' signal is visible to the full posterior and invisible to the tables), and a hub-free x gains over S° at most the extras' O_P(log n) discrepancies each (the dilution term of F-DRAFT Lemma W1 is already in d(S°)), so max_{hub-free} d ≤ d(S°) + O_P(K log n) — PROOF SKETCH. Then π₀(Ω∖M_D) = π₀(some hub present) = c·p^{−1}n^{−1/2}e^{O_P(1)} (W1-T38E E1, O-BGIBBS Prop. LH), and with N = N_e = O(n + p) the event A has probability → 1 whenever p/(√n log² n) → ∞ (the T38(b1-LH) c = 1 condition; p ≤ n − 1 on exact-Gram LH). Hence **W_r ≤ e^{−Θ(n)}·p^{c}n^{c/2} = e^{−Θ(n)} with probability → 1**: the 95% bound is off by e^{Θ(n)}. Meanwhile the whole start basin Lat(S°) is downhill to S₀ at φ = 1 (W4-SHARE Prop. M(b), PROOF SKETCH), so 𝔛 = Lat(S°) has δ_𝔛 ≤ 1 − π₀(Lat(S°)) → 0 by W1-EXP Thm 6 at S° (candidate), and Theorem B / Prop. LH give β_L → 0; Theorem R then gives PIP and MPM consistency on the same family, with the same output.
  > *Caveat on the grid.* Whether the method's calibration produces T = 1 on such data is OPEN ... With any grid, (N-a) applies as soon as non-crossing at stage T has positive probability. The empirical instance is W4-SHARE headline 4: on the PB design, delivery to 𝓡₀ succeeded in 200/200 islands while the median log Ẑ/Z was −67.
- Numerical evidence (report section 4.1, helper): p = 18, 24 settings, 3,840 island-runs, designs `masked` (corr(x₃,x₀) = 0.6, β₃ = −0.6) and `masked8` (corr 0.8). With the one-stage grid G1 the median log W_r is −4.32 (n = 640, N = 2500), −5.88 (n = 5120, N = 2500), −11.7 (n = 5120, N = 50), −10.8 (masked8, n = 5120); the island PIP error equals the exact-posterior PIP error to four digits (e.g. 0.0067 vs 0.0067) and the MPM is correct in 100%. Blind restricted-ESS grid G3 (pilot of Nπ₀ draws; S₀ ∉ V in every setting): median log W_r −5.13 to −10.8, PIP error exact. Full-space ESS grid G2: |median log W_r| < 0.03. "Unbiasedness is carried by rare islands: in collapsed settings the top 5% of islands hold 99-100% of ΣW_r". The 95% lower bound 0.05·Ẑ_r is valid in every run, off by about 20·e^{5…11}. Not shown: a non-crossing population at the end of stage T (so (M2-a) untested) and anything about p ≫ n or the method's actual calibration.
- Status history: PROOF SKETCH, deterministic core PROVED (F-MASKPIP) -> no review (A-REV9 excludes N-b/N-c). Family claims rest on TH140 (W1-EXP Thm 6), TH259 (O-BGIBBS Prop LH) and RF203 (SHARE-M(b)) (PROOF SKETCH; **A-REV3 ERROR**, see CJ217); "whether calibration realises T = 1 is OPEN".
- Depends on: TH112 (T14(i-a)), TH303, RF203 (W4-SHARE Prop M(b)), ⟦Prop NM⟧. Feeds: SYNTHESIS row "Masked-regime meaning of Ẑ and PIPs"; superseded for the method's own grid by RF231's caveat (API-MASKZPIP).

Setting (PROOF section 0, verbatim): "Fixed data, a successful frozen calibration 𝓒 (EX-A, EX-S, CAL, START), one island with N particles, frozen grid 0 = φ_0 < φ_1 < … < φ_T = 1. ... γ₀ = unnormalised start law, γ₁ = γ = unnormalised posterior, d := log γ₁ − log γ₀ on Ω (finite), so the bridge is γ_φ = γ₀ e^{φd} = γ₀^{1−φ}γ₁^φ ... W := W_T = Ẑ_r/Z ... New symbols: S° := argmax π₀ (start mode); for x°, x* ∈ Ω, a(x°,x*) := log π₀(x°)/π₀(x*), Λ(x°,x*) := log π(x*)/π(x°), φ* := a/(a+Λ) (the **crossing temperature**: q_φ(x*) = q_φ(x°) iff φ = φ*, when a, Λ > 0); d_max := max_Ω d, x_m ∈ argmax_Ω d; for A ⊆ Ω, D_A := d_max − max_{Ω∖A} d; E_s(A) := {q̂_s(A) = 0}". ### TH308 — API-MASKZPIP Theorem E1 (two-phase sandwich; `MZ-E1E2`)  [theorem]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part E. Positions: [pos 909, 978].
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Theorem E1 (two-phase sandwich). PROVED (deterministic, any kernel, any grid, any N).
  > Let 1 ≤ t ≤ T, M, M′ ⊆ Ω, x° ∈ M, x* ∈ M′, η := max_{x∈M}|d(x)−d(x°)|, η′ := max_{x∈M′}|d(x)−d(x*)| (η′ := 0 if t = T). On F := {supp q̂_k ⊆ M for k = 0,…,t−1; supp q̂_k ⊆ M′ for k = t,…,T−1},
  >   | log W − Ψ_t | ≤ φ_t η + (1−φ_t) η′,   Ψ_t := log[q_t(x°)/π₀(x°)] + log[π(x*)/q_t(x*)].
  > Moreover Ψ_t = (1−φ_t)a − φ_tΛ + log π(x*) − log π₀(x°) = (a+Λ)(φ* − φ_t) + log π(x*) − log π₀(x°).
  >
  > **Corollary E1a (late switching = underestimation by the log-odds overshoot).** With x° = S°, x* = S₀ and the population frozen at S° before stage t and at S₀ from stage t on (η = η′ = 0): log W = (a+Λ)(φ* − φ_t) + log π(S₀) − log π₀(S°) exactly. If π(S₀), π₀(S°) → 1, the island underestimates Z by e^{(a+Λ)(φ_t−φ*)} when it switches after the crossing temperature, and overestimates (at most by 1/π₀(S₀)) when it switches before. PROVED.
  > **Corollary E1b (island agreement is uninformative).** On F, log W is determined by (x°, x*, t) up to φ_tη + (1−φ_t)η′. Hence four islands that switch at the same stage report log Ẑ_r within 2(φ_tη + (1−φ_t)η′) of each other *whatever* the value of log Ẑ − log Z. PROVED. (Explains F-MASKPIP's masked8/G1 row: q05–q95 of log W_r = (−10.8, −10.8).)
  > **Corollary E1c (one-sided relaxation).** If supp q̂_k ⊆ M for k < t and q̂_k(x*) ≥ 1 − f_k for k ≥ t, then log W ≥ Ψ_t − φ_tη + Σ_{k=t}^{T−1} log(1−f_k).
- Proof route (Summary:): on a frozen phase every increment is e^{Δd(x)} and the products telescope to tempered-mass ratios (algebra).
- Status: PROVED (candidate, author); no same-family or cross-family review. Limit stated by the author: "E1 is exact but needs a near-frozen path. When the populations are diffuse (δ₁ ≈ 0.05-0.1 at p = 18), the visited sets have a d-spread of 20+ nats and the sandwich is uninformative (median width ≈ 24 nats in the masked8/n=640 jump grids). The rigorous content in the diffuse case is the one-sided E2."
- Depends on: TH110 (T12) (via O-PW2 Lemma 2). Feeds: R0_DIFF K40 ("In the masked regime Ẑ underestimates Z by the log-odds overshoot of a late crossing"), K79 (island agreement certifies nothing), S-Z (Proposition Z (iii): "E1/E2 path-tail clause imported with its full hypotheses (A, x_m, τ_A, D_A, exceptions) or omitted"), FUTURE; the PC1 proof check lists the E1/E2 path-tail formula as AMBIGUOUS until A, x_m, τ_A, D_A and exceptions are defined.

### TH309 — API-MASKZPIP Theorem E2 (miss bound: evidence lost by a blind step; `MZ-E1E2`)  [theorem]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part E. Positions as TH308.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Theorem E2 (miss bound: the evidence lost by a blind step). PROVED (any kernel, any grid, any N).
  > For A ⊆ Ω and 1 ≤ t ≤ T,
  >   (a) E_𝓒[W·1{E_{t−1}(A)}] ≤ κ_t(A) := q_{t−1}(1_{Ω∖A} h_{t−1,T}) ≤ e^{(1−φ_t)d_max} γ_{φ_t}(Ω∖A)/Z ≤ [π₀(Ω∖A)/π₀(x_m)]·e^{−φ_t D_A};
  >   (b) for η ∈ (0,1): P_𝓒(W > κ_t(A)/η) ≤ η + P_𝓒(E_{t−1}(A)ᶜ); for t = 1, P_𝓒(E_0(A)ᶜ) ≤ N π₀(A);
  >   (c) (arrival-temperature form) let τ_A := min{s ≥ 0 : q̂_s(A) > 0} and τ′ := min(τ_A, T). Then P_𝓒( W > (T/η)·[π₀(Ω∖A)/π₀(x_m)]·e^{−φ_{τ′} D_A} ) ≤ η + N π₀(A).
  > For t = T the bound in (a) is exactly π(Ω∖A) (h_{T−1,T} = g_T).
- Proof route (Summary:): one Feynman-Kac martingale step (O-PW2 Theorem A1) on the miss event, then h ≤ e^{(1−φ_t)d_max}Z̄_t/Z; union bound over t for (c). Reading (author): "Whatever happens later in the bridge, the island evidence carries at most the start-mass-weighted fraction e^{−φ D_A} of Z, where φ is the temperature at which the population first touches A. ... This generalises F-MASKPIP (N-c) (T = 1, W ≤ e^{−D}/π₀(S₀)) to every grid and every kernel ... Note that E W = 1 is not contradicted: the event Eᶜ has probability ≤ Nπ₀(A) and carries the mean (F-MASKPIP M3)."
- Status: PROVED (candidate); no review. Depends on: LM202, TH316 (A1), TH110 (T12). Feeds: R0_DIFF K40; S-Z (see TH308). Escalation (author): an independent check that A1 holds for v3's exact stage order (resample, mutate, record); later confirmed for the O-PW2 martingale by A-REV9.

### LM203 — API-MASKZPIP Lemma J (a full-space ESS grid cannot jump a crossing)  [lemma]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part E.
- Statement (verbatim): "### Lemma J (a full-space ESS grid cannot jump a crossing). PROVED. If χ²(q_t‖q_{t−1}) ≤ χ̄ then q_t(A)² ≤ (1+χ̄) q_{t−1}(A) for every A ⊆ Ω. *Proof.* q_t(A) = q_{t−1}(g_t1_A) ≤ q_{t−1}(g_t²)^{1/2}q_{t−1}(A)^{1/2} (Cauchy–Schwarz) and q_{t−1}(g_t²) = 1+χ². ∎ With the method's threshold (ESS ≥ 0.9 ⇔ χ̄ = 1/9): a single step can raise the mass of a set from ε only to ≤ (10ε/9)^{1/2}; so the blind step of E2 ... is impossible on the full space and possible only when the ESS is computed on a set that misses A (T13(iii); the candidate set V of METHODOLOGY §6.7, or a particle population with no particle in A)."
- Status: PROVED (candidate); no review. Depends on TH111 (T13). Feeds: TH311 (E4), diagnostic remark C4 (blind-crossing flag, "no theorem").

### TH310 — API-MASKZPIP Proposition E3 (exact pair refresh gives W → 1)  [proposition]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part E.
- Statement (verbatim): "### Proposition E3 (positive side: exact pair refresh gives W → 1). PROVED in the stated idealisation; the perturbation to a pair-dominated bridge is a PROOF SKETCH. (a) (O-PW2 Thm C with λ = 0, candidate) If every round kernel is an exact refresh, K_t(x,·) = q_t, then E_𝓒(W−1)² = ∏_t(1 + χ²_t/N) − 1, χ²_t := χ²(q_t‖q_{t−1}). (b) (pair) Let x°, x* differ in exactly one coordinate j and suppose q_t({x°,x*}) = 1 for all t (pure pair). Then the v3 round is an exact refresh: the Gibbs step on j is a draw from q_t(·|{x°,x*}) = q_t, and every other elementary step proposes a state of q_t-mass 0, which is never accepted (heat-bath probability 0; MH ratio 0). So (a) applies, and with a grid satisfying χ²_t ≤ 1/9, E(W−1)² ≤ e^{T/(9N)} − 1. (c) PROOF SKETCH (pair-dominated): if q_t({x°,x*}) ≥ 1 − ε_t, couple the island with the pure-pair island; the coupling fails with probability ≤ N Σ_t (m·ε_t·ḡ-type leakage) and on success W equals the pure-pair W up to factors ∏(1 ± O(ε_t ḡ_t)). This is the "two-state analysis, V11" that METHODOLOGY §6.7 attributes to Fable-T3 (unproved). Not completed here: the leakage constant needs sup-norm control of h (O-PW2's H_{s,T}), which is the same obstruction O-PW2 reports."
- Status: (a),(b) PROVED in the idealisation; (c) PROOF SKETCH (author); no review. Caution: the exact-refresh product can under-estimate the truth by 5.4x (p = 6) and 20.7x (p = 8, corr .95, Gibbs-only) (O-PW2 §5, see RF228): "χ²-only reasoning (T13 alone) is not a bound". Feeds: CJ218 (c).

### TH311 — API-MASKZPIP Theorem E4 (evidence dichotomy on a pair-dominated masked bridge), blind half  [theorem]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part E (Theorem E4 and "LH consequence"); `REPORT.md` section 2 (E4) and section 5.
- Statement (verbatim):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.989) from `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > ### Theorem E4 (the evidence dichotomy on a pair-dominated masked bridge). PARTLY PROVED.
  > Let x° = S° and x* = S₀ (or the pair that dominates the bridge), A := the S₀ basin, φ* the crossing temperature.
  > - **(blind; PROVED by E2(c))** If the population first touches A at stage τ_A, then log Ẑ_r − log Z ≤ −φ_{τ_A}D_A + log(T/η) + log(1/π₀(x_m)) w.p. ≥ 1 − η − Nπ₀(A). On the frozen path the matching lower bound holds up to the sandwich width (E1, E1c).
  > - **(resolved; CONJECTURE, PROOF SKETCH E3(c))** If both members of the pair are in the candidate set V, the grid's restricted ESS controls the pair's χ²_t (Lemma J on the pair), and the pair is exactly refreshed (E3(b)); then log Ẑ_r − log Z = O_P(√(T/N)) + leakage.
  > So the honest two-sided statement is: **upper tail always O_P(1) (Markov, T31(i)); lower tail O_P(√(T/N)) if the grid resolves the crossing, and −φ_{τ_A}D_A + O_P(log T + log 1/π₀(x_m)) if it does not.** Which case occurs is decided by whether any calibration run scored the S₀ basin (V includes the top 20p *scored* models by γ₁, METHODOLOGY §6.7).
  > **LH consequence (PROOF SKETCH).** ... If the final grid is blind (no calibration run scored a hub-containing model) and its first step is φ₁, then log Ẑ_r − log Z ≤ −Θ(n)φ₁ + O_P(log n) → −∞ (assuming log 1/π₀(x_m) = O_P(log n), hypothesis XM). But O-BGIBBS BG1/BG3 (candidates) say the pilot scores S₀ at stage 1 w.p. → 1 on LH, so V ∋ S₀ and the method's grid is expected to be in the *resolved* case on LH c = 1 ... For c ≥ 2 the pair differs in c coordinates; exact pair refresh fails and the resolved case is OPEN.
- Status: blind half PROVED (candidate); resolved half CONJECTURE (CJ218); LH consequence PROOF SKETCH. No review. Depends on TH309, LM203, ⟦O-BGIBBS BG1/BG3⟧ (theme 6).
- Feeds: R0_DIFF K40; SYNTHESIS row "masked-regime meaning" (author claim "Ẑ underestimates by exactly the log-odds overshoot of a late crossing", [pos 978]).
- Numerics (report section 5/9): at p = 18 the engine's log W equals an exact-refresh SMC's log W on the same grid in every setting ("the evidence loss is a grid effect, not a kernel effect"); method-like V always contained S₀ (9/9 pilots) with |median log Ẑ_r/Z| ≤ 0.04, a blind V gave −10.8 to −11.7 nats. ### RF231 — API-MASKZPIP first-draft claim: method-level evidence collapse on LH by the floor φ₁ ≥ 1/T_e  [refuted claim]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/REPORT.md` section 5 (verbatim): "**A method-level evidence collapse on LH.** My first draft claimed that on LH the method's Ẑ underestimates by e^{−Θ(n)/T_e} via the floor φ₁ ≥ 1/T_e. That is **wrong for the method**, for two reasons. The floor 1/T_e belongs to the *pilot* (METHODOLOGY §6.6), not to the final grid. ### TH312 — API-MASKZPIP Theorem P1 (RB PIP bias <= TV distance of the delivered population; `MZ-P1P2`)  [theorem]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part P. Positions as TH308.
- Statement (verbatim): "### Theorem P1 (RB PIP bias ≤ TV distance of the delivered population). PROVED. For every j, |E_𝓒[PIP̂_rj] − PIP_j| ≤ TV(ν̄_r P^{L}, π) ≤ TV(ν̄_r, π) ≤ E_𝓒 f_{r,0} + δ₁, where P is the φ = 1 round kernel. Conditionally: |E[PIP̂_rj | 𝓕_T] − PIP_j| ≤ TV(q̂_T, π) ≤ f_{r,0} + δ₁; in particular on the locked event {q̂_T = δ_{S₀}}, |E[PIP̂_rj | 𝓕_T] − PIP_j| ≤ δ₁ (no L, no B, no ρ̄)." (ν̄_r := E_𝓒[q̂_T], TV(μ,ν) := ½Σ|μ−ν|.)
- Proof route (Summary:): the terminal rounds are π-invariant with fresh randomness, so E[PIP̂_rj | 𝓕_T] = q̂_T(F̄) with F̄ ∈ [0,1] and π(F̄) = PIP_j; hence the difference is at most the TV distance.
- Status: PROVED (candidate); no review. R0_DIFF K57 / card S-POOL "TV error" (supplement): "(a) |E[PIP̂_rj] − PIP_j| ≤ TV(law of delivered population, π) (MZ-P1 PROVED)". Final: the recording-marginal bias comparison ships in S-POOL; "general accuracy" is FUTURE_WORK FW8 (K57). Depends on TH110 (T12 (R3)), TH117 (T23(ii)).

### TH314 — API-MASKZPIP Proposition P3 and Corollary P3' (top-store evidence and PIPs; `MZ-P3`)  [proposition]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part P.
- Statement (verbatim): "### Proposition P3 (top-store evidence and PIPs: deterministic two-sided bounds). PROVED. For any reported set 𝒯 of exactly scored models: Z_𝒯/Z = π(𝒯) and |PIP^𝒯_j − PIP_j| ≤ π(Ω∖𝒯) for every j. If S₀ ∈ 𝒯: 1 − δ₁ ≤ Z_𝒯/Z ≤ 1, |PIP^𝒯_j − PIP_j| ≤ δ₁ and |PIP^𝒯_j − 1{j∈S₀}| ≤ 2δ₁. ... **Corollary P3′ (PROVED as a composition, CONDITIONAL).** If P(𝒪 ∩ {S₀ ∉ 𝒯}) → 0 (S₀ scored, e.g. O-BGIBBS BG3 on LH, and the top store keeps the best scored models, so S₀ ∈ 𝒯 once S₀ is scored and is the HPM, T03) and δ₁ → 0 (T03), then on 𝒪: Z_𝒯/Z → 1 and max_j|PIP^𝒯_j − PIP_j| → 0 in probability, both at rate δ₁ = O_P(√(log n/n)), with no grid, ESS, mixing or second-moment hypothesis. **This is the only two-sided evidence consistency statement on the masked family that does not need the bridge to resolve the crossing.**" (Proof: write J := {S ∋ j}, a := π(𝒯∩J), b := π(𝒯); PIP^𝒯_j − PIP_j = a(1−b)/b − π(J∖𝒯), both terms in [0, 1−b].)
- Status: P3 PROVED (deterministic), P3' PROVED as a composition, CONDITIONAL (author, candidate; "AUTHOR-ONLY" in the meeting registry). Depends on ⟦O-CERT⟧ top store (theme 9), TH103 (T03). Feeds: M4 ⟦Theorem Z_T⟧ (K43: "If S₀ ∈ 𝒯 then 1−δ₁ ≤ Z_𝒯/Z ≤ 1 and |PIP^𝒯_j − PIP_j| ≤ δ₁, two-sided and deterministic"), with LS0/eviction wording (R3_B R3-1: "𝒯_new = top_c(𝒯_old ∪ 𝒮_added)"). The split between Ẑ and PIPs is again "Prop W4 made concrete": Z_𝒯 and the PIPs are first-moment/occupancy objects while Ẑ is a product of importance-sampling steps.

### TH315 — API-MASKZPIP Propositions C1-C3 (per-fit certificates; `MZ-C1`)  [proposition]
- Source: `API-MASKZPIP/PROOF.md` Part C.
- Statement (verbatim): "### Proposition C1 (certified upper bound on the evidence ratio). PROVED (deterministic). Ẑ/Z ≤ Ẑ/Z_𝒯 on every run (Z ≥ Z_𝒯). If Ẑ < Z_𝒯, the run **certifies underestimation** of Z by at least Z_𝒯/Ẑ. Same for each island: Ẑ_r/Z ≤ Ẑ_r/Z_𝒯. ### Proposition C2 (the per-fit evidence band). PROVED (O-CERT Thm C1 + C1 above). With probability ≥ 0.95, simultaneously for all models: log Z ≥ max(log Z_𝒯, log Ẑ − log 20). No finite-n upper bound on Z (equivalently no lower bound on W) follows from the run alone (O-CERT; T31(c,d)); E1b shows that island agreement cannot supply one. ### Proposition C3 (per-fit PIP gap). PROVED. For every j: |PIP̂_rj − PIP_j| ≤ |PIP̂_rj − PIP^𝒯_j| + π(Ω∖𝒯). The first term is computable from the output; the second is not certifiable from above, but w.p. ≥ 0.95 π(Ω∖𝒯) ≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(0.05Ẑ) (a certified *lower* bound on the missing mass, O-CERT)."
- Status: PROVED (deterministic, candidate); registry-style status in the meeting: `MZ-C1: PROVED (C1-C3 per-fit, deterministic)`. Feeds: M4 (K42: "Z ≥ Z_𝒯 = Σ_{S∈𝒯}ϖ(S)m(S) deterministically for any scored set 𝒯, so max{Z_𝒯, 0.05·Ẑ} is a valid 95% lower bound and Ẑ < Z_𝒯 certifies underestimation"). Application: in the 4 study fits re-scored by O-CERT, Ẑ/Z_𝒯 = e^{0.18…0.59}, so no underestimation is certified (not proof of Ẑ ≈ Z). Theme 9 owns the certificate card; this entry records the evidence-meaning content. At n = 200 the posterior itself is diffuse: "O-CERT's sure bound π(Ŝ) ≤ e^{F(Ŝ)}/Z_𝒯 gives π(S₀) ≤ 0.37 even on exactly correct fits. So δ₁ ≥ 0.63 and every bound involving u_π is vacuous at the study's n" (report section 7).

Pre-campaign context (`main@c4ef0dc/Docs/Theory/one_pagers/T25.md`): T25(iv) "variance of the evidence ratio under PW2: let W_t = Z-hat_t/Z_t for one island and suppose, for t = 1..T, E_c[W_{t-1}^2 {(q-hat_{t-1}(g_t))^2 - 1}] <= (a_t/N) E_c[W_{t-1}^2] + nu_t (PW2). Then Var_c(W_T) <= B_T := prod_{t=1}^T (1 + a_t/N) - 1 + sum_{s=1}^T nu_s prod_{t>s} (1 + a_t/N); the pooled four-island evidence has variance at most B_T/4"; "The theorem is equivalent to the PW2 recursion: it adds no control of the evidence beyond PW2 (audit finding E5)"; PW2 was "assumed ... NOT proved". Notation (O-PW2 section 2, verbatim): "q_t, G_t, c_t, g_t = G_t/c_t (so q_{t−1}(g_t) = 1), Ẑ_t, W_t = Ẑ_t/Z_t and W_0 = 1 ... 𝓕_t: the σ-field of the island's randomness up to and including q̂_t. λ_{t−1} := G_t q̂_{t−1} / q̂_{t−1}(G_t), the weighted parent law. μ_t := λ_{t−1}K_t for t ≥ 1, and μ_0 := q_0. **Fact F**: given 𝓕_{t−1}, the N particles of q̂_t are iid μ_t. ... Q_t f(x) := g_t(x)(K_t f)(x). h_{s,T} := Q_{s+1}⋯Q_T 1 for 0 ≤ s ≤ T, with h_{T,T} = 1, so h_{T−1,T} = g_T and h > 0. σ²_{s,T} := Var_{q_s}(h_{s,T}). H_{s,T} := max_Ω h_{s,T}. σ²_T := Σ_{s=0}^{T−1} σ²_{s,T}. V_t := Var_c(W_t), v_t := E_c W_t² = 1 + V_t. χ²_t := q_{t−1}(g_t²) − 1 = χ²(q_t‖q_{t−1}); δ²_t := q_t((g_t − 1)²) = q_{t−1}(g_t³) − 1 − 2χ²_t ≤ ḡ_t χ²_t; ḡ_t := max_Ω g_t; λ_t := ‖K_t − Π_t‖_{L²(q_t)→L²(q_t)}, where Π_t f = q_t(f); ε_t := ε_{φ_t} of T09(iv), so K_t(x,·) ≥ ε_t q_t(·)." Setting: "fixed data, a successful frozen calibration c, one island, and N = N_e. ... K_t is the v3 round kernel at φ_t: a uniformly random order, q_t-invariant and q_t-reversible (T09(iii)). EX-A, EX-S, CAL."

### LM201 — O-PW2 Lemma 1 (q_{t-1}(Q_t f) = q_t(f))  [lemma]
- Statement (verbatim): "**Lemma 1.** q_{t−1}(Q_t f) = q_t(f). Hence q_s(h_{s,T}) = 1 for every s ≤ T. *Proof.* q_{t−1}(g_t ·) = q_t(·) as measures, because q_{t−1}G_t/c_t = γ_{φ_t}/Z̄_{φ_t}. Then q_t K_t = q_t. Induct downward from h_{T,T} = 1. ∎"
- Status: PROVED (candidate); XF VERIFIED (A-REV9 helper `MASKED_PW2_CHECK.md`: "target invariance gives q_(t-1) Q_t=q_t, hence q_s h_(s,T)=1"). Feeds TH316. Depends on TH107 (T09(iii)).

### LM202 — O-PW2 Lemma 2 and Fact F (weighted unbiasedness; conditional iid children)  [lemma]
- Statement (verbatim): "**Lemma 2.** For t ≥ 1, W_t = W_{t−1} q̂_{t−1}(g_t), and W_t μ_t(f) = W_{t−1} q̂_{t−1}(Q_t f) = E[W_t q̂_t(f) | 𝓕_{t−1}]. Also E_c[W_t q̂_t(f)] = E_c[W_t μ_t(f)] = q_t(f)." (Proof: Ẑ_t/Z_t = (Ẑ_{t−1}/Z_{t−1})·q̂_{t−1}(G_t)/c_t; the conditional expectation follows from Fact F since W_t is 𝓕_{t−1}-measurable; "This is the product-form unbiasedness of T12(i.a), re-derived here.")
- Status: PROVED (candidate); XF VERIFIED (A-REV9 helper: "Conditional on the preceding population, multinomial ancestors and independent mutation randomness produce iid children with law mu_s. ... Shared random mutation orders across particles would invalidate Fact F, but the inspected methodology explicitly prescribes fresh orders per particle."). Feeds TH316-TH317 and API-MASKZPIP E2 (TH309). Depends on TH110 (T12(i.a)).

### TH316 — O-PW2 Theorem A (exact variance identity; `OPW2-ThmA`)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-PW2/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem A. Positions as the block header.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Theorem A (exact identities). PROVED (candidate).
  > Set Γ_s(f) := W_s q̂_s(f), M_s := Γ_s(h_{s,T}) for 0 ≤ s ≤ T−1, and M_{−1} := 1. Then:
  > (A1) (M_s)_{s=−1}^{T−1} is an (𝓕_s)-martingale with M_{T−1} = W_T. Moreover W_s μ_s(h_{s,T}) = M_{s−1}.
  > (A2) Var_c(W_T) = (1/N) Σ_{s=0}^{T−1} E_c[W_s² Var_{μ_s}(h_{s,T})].
  > (A3) Var_c(W_T) = (1/N) Σ_{s=0}^{T−1} (1−1/N)^{T−1−s} (e_s − 1), where e_s := E_c[W_s² μ_s(h²_{s,T})] and e_0 = q_0(h²_{0,T}).
  > (A4) PW2's left side is exactly a variance increment: E_c[W²_{t−1}{(q̂_{t−1}g_t)² − 1}] = V_t − V_{t−1}.
  Headline form (report section 1): "N·Var_c(W_T) = Σ_{s<T} (1−1/N)^{T−1−s} (E_c[W_s² μ_s(h²_{s,T})] − 1); equivalently, N·Var_c(W_T) = Σ_{s<T} E_c[W_s² Var_{μ_s}(h_{s,T})]. Here h_{s,T} is the future-weight function and μ_s is the conditional child law. No mixing assumption is used." and "(A4) shows that PW2 is precisely a hypothesis on the growth v_t ≤ (1+a_t/N)v_{t−1} + ν_t. Theorem A computes that growth instead of assuming it."
- Proof route (Summary:): Γ_{T−1}(h_{T−1,T}) = W_T; martingale increments D_s = W_s(q̂_s(h_{s,T}) − μ_s(h_{s,T})) are orthogonal; E[D_s²|𝓕_{s−1}] = W_s² Var_{μ_s}(h_{s,T})/N by Fact F; m_s − 1 = (1−1/N)(m_{s−1} − 1) + (e_s − 1)/N gives (A3).
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) (O-PW2) -> same-family: none -> cross-family: **VERIFIED** (A-REV9: "O-PW2 A1-A4 VERIFIED"; helper: "No mixing or reversibility beyond target invariance is used"; for N = 1 the exponent-zero coefficient is 1). Numerical: (A3) holds to 1e−9 relative accuracy at every N ∈ {10,…,2500} in every exact-enumeration case (p ≤ 10). Registry: `PROVED (SF: none; XF: VERIFIED (A-REV9))`.
- Depends on: LM201, LM202, TH107 (T09(iii)), TH110 (T12(i.a)). Feeds: S-Z (Proposition Z (ii): "exact variance identity (OPW2 Thm A, as a specialisation of CDG 2011 Thm 1.4 in kind); the exact-refresh product never substituted (OPW2-cex)"), R0_DIFF K39 (`N·Var(W_T|𝓒) = Σ_s(1−1/N)^{T−1−s}(E[W_s²μ_s(h²_{s,T})]−1)` holds for invariant kernels), K53, K59.
- Notes / UNCERTAIN: literature: "O-PW2 Theorem A may be a known result of Cérou–Del Moral–Guyader (2011); the reader didn't check this by derivation" (LIT-SMC, [pos 1009]); registry text "Novelty of (i) vs Cérou–Del Moral–Guyader Thm 1.4 unchecked (LIT-SMC §3A: needs escalation)". Remark (O-PW2 section 8): the identity W_s μ_s(h_{s,T}) = M_{s−1} "also gives an unbiased-type handle for lower bounds on Var (two-sided evidence control). It may matter for T26."

### TH317 — O-PW2 Theorem B (two-sided non-asymptotic bound; `OPW2-ThmB`)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-PW2/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem B and section 1 item 2.
- Statement (verbatim):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.987) from `A-REV9/sources/O-PW2_REPORT.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > ### Theorem B (two-sided non-asymptotic bound). PROVED (candidate).
  > (B1) For every T ≥ 1:
  >   |N·V_T − Σ_{s=0}^{T−1} (1−1/N)^{T−1−s} σ²_{s,T}| ≤ Σ_{s=1}^{T−1} (1−1/N)^{T−1−s} H²_{s,T} √(V_s(1+V_s)).
  > There is no s = 0 error term; in particular V_1 = χ²_1/N exactly.
  > (B2) Define U_0 := 0 and, recursively,
  >   U_t := (1/N) Σ_{s=0}^{t−1} (1−1/N)^{t−1−s} [σ²_{s,t} + 1{s≥1} H²_{s,t} √(U_s(1+U_s))].
  > Then V_t ≤ U_t for every t ≤ T. Under the four final islands (T12(iv.c): independent given c), Var_c(Ẑ/Z) ≤ U_T/4.
  > (B3) Closed form. Put x := max_{t≤T} σ²_t/N and y := max_{t≤T} (1/N) Σ_{s=1}^{t−1} H²_{s,t}. If 2y²(1+2x) ≤ x, then for every t ≤ T: V_t ≤ U_t ≤ 2x, and V_T ≤ σ²_T/N + y√(2x(1+2x)) = σ²_T/N + O(N^{−3/2}).
  Headline (report section 1): "It delivers T25(iv)'s **conclusion** directly, including the /4 for pooling, with PW2 removed as a hypothesis. It also gives PW2 itself with explicit a_t and ν_t (Corollary B2)."
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) -> XF **VERIFIED*** (A-REV9: "B1-B3 VERIFIED; the O(N^{-3/2}) remainder only for fixed inputs/grid or uniform constants"; "The /4 is conditional on frozen calibration. The constants can be huge along growing n,p,T; this review does not establish study-scale precision"; helper: "Conditional independence of the four final island streams gives precisely Var(Wpool)=V_T/4, bounded by U_T/4; this does not imply the same unconditional variance formula across shared random calibration"). Numerical: at N = 2500 Theorem B is within 6-35% of the truth (16% in the hardest Gibbs-only case). Registry: `PROVED (SF: none; XF: VERIFIED* (A-REV9))`.
- Proof route (Summary:): split e_s = E[W_sμ_s(h²)] + E[W_s(W_s−1)μ_s(h²)]; the first equals q_s(h²_{s,T}) = 1 + σ²_{s,T}; the second is at most H²_{s,T}√(V_s v_s) by Cauchy-Schwarz.
- Depends on: TH316, LM201, LM202. Feeds: K39, K53, K59 (`MA-CorV`); S-Z. Related: TH118 (T25(iv)) (conclusion without PW2).

### TH318 — O-PW2 Corollary B2 (PW2 holds with a_t = (S_t − S_{t−1})_+)  [corollary]
- Source: `O-PW2/REPORT.md` section 3 (Corollary B2).
- Statement (verbatim): "**Corollary B2 (PW2 itself, explicit).** Write η_t := Σ_{s=1}^{t−1} H²_{s,t} √(U_s(1+U_s)) and S_t := Σ_s (1−1/N)^{t−1−s} σ²_{s,t}. By (B1) and (A4), N(V_t − V_{t−1}) ≤ S_t − S_{t−1} + η_t + η_{t−1}. So PW2 holds with a_t := (S_t − S_{t−1})_+ and ν_t := (η_t + η_{t−1})/N. This uses v_{t−1} ≥ 1. The slack ν_t = O(N^{−3/2}), and a_t → (σ²_t − σ²_{t−1})_+ as N → ∞. So PW2 is **true with O(1) rate constants** in the finite-state v3 setting. The rate constant is the increment of the asymptotic variance, **not** χ²_t. T25(iv) fed with these constants is weaker than (B2) used directly; we recommend (B2)."
- Status: PROVED (candidate), "done modulo item 7.2" (author escalation: "the a_t uses S_t − S_{t−1} with the (1−1/N) weights. Check that the sign handling is right when σ²_t < σ²_{t−1}"). A-REV9 helper: "VERIFIED candidate with scope GAP ... Sign handling remains correct even if the variance increment is negative. Define S_0=eta_0=0 explicitly. The O(N^(-3/2)) slack and bounded limiting a_t conclusions hold for fixed finite input, fixed frozen grid/T, and fixed kernels as N grows ... They are not uniform claims along the actual growing n,p,T budgets." Registry: no separate row; included under `OPW2-ThmB` (B1-B3). Final: SYNTHESIS row "PW2 holds with a_t = (S_t − S_{t−1})₊".
- Depends on TH316, TH317. Feeds: S-Z / T25(iv).

### TH319 — O-PW2 Theorem C (constants from stage primitives; `OPW2-ThmC`)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-PW2/REPORT.md` section 3 (Theorem C) and section 4.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > ### Theorem C (primitive constants: T13's χ², T09's ε, an L² mixing defect). PROVED (candidate).
  > (C1) σ²_{T−1,T} = χ²_T. For 1 ≤ t ≤ T−1: σ²_{t−1,T} ≤ χ²_t + 2δ_tλ_t σ_{t,T} + ḡ_tλ_t² σ²_{t,T} ≤ χ²_t + λ_tδ²_t + λ_t(1 + ḡ_tλ_t) σ²_{t,T}. Here σ_{t,T} := (σ²_{t,T})^{1/2}.
  > (C2) H_{T,T} = 1, and H_{t−1,T} ≤ ḡ_t(ε_t + (1−ε_t)H_{t,T}).
  > (C3) Suppose for all t: χ²_t + λ_tδ²_t ≤ c̄ and κ_t := λ_t(1 + ḡ_tλ_t) ≤ κ < 1. Then σ²_{s,T} ≤ c̄/(1−κ) and σ²_T ≤ Tc̄/(1−κ). If also ḡ_t(1−ε_t) ≤ θ < 1, then H_{s,T} ≤ ḡ*/(1−θ), where ḡ* := max_t ḡ_t.
  > (C4) Exact refresh (K_t = Π_t, so λ_t = 0 and ε_t = 1): h_{s,T} = g_{s+1}, σ²_{s,T} = χ²_{s+1}, and Theorem A gives exactly V_T = Π_t(1+χ²_t/N) − 1.
  > T13(ii)(b) and (iii): under COVER(V, ε_C), 1 + χ²_t ≤ 10/(9(1−ε_C)²); with ε_C = 0 this is χ²_t ≤ 1/9.
- Status: PROVED (candidate); no review (A-REV9: "no ... review of O-PW2 Theorem C beyond reading it for context"). **Not non-vacuous with locked inputs only (author, section 4):** "T09 gives λ_t ≤ 1−ε_t, and ε_t is exponentially small in n for realistic data (T09(v)). Then κ_t ≈ 1 + ḡ_t > 1: the recursion (C1) grows like Π ḡ_t, and (C2) likewise. **Verdict: with only locked T09/T13 inputs, the bound is valid but vacuous at study scale.**" Registry: `OPW2-ThmC ... PROVED (SF: none; XF: none)`; "L² mixing condition ... NOT implied by the locked T09 constant". Numerics: at N = 2500 Theorem C is within a factor of 3.5; "σ²_T can be 20× Σχ²_t" so a realised-grid ESS condition alone (T13) cannot control σ²_T.
- Depends on: TH316, TH317, TH111 (T13), TH107 (T09(iv)). Feeds: nothing as a card; related CJ219. In the masked regime the route is "vacuous unless the crossing is resolved" (API-MASKZPIP §5).

- Source: `O-PW2/REPORT.md` section 6 (verbatim): "**The one-step, parent-uniform route** (OPTIONAL_PW2 (A)–(C)) requires sup_x K_{t−1}g_t(x) ≤ 1 + O(1/N). Source for the block: `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md` section 2 ("What convergence of posterior expectations means for v3"); branch `theory/A-DRAFT` head `dbf47f7` (GPT-6 Astra high, Codex; task "novelty + E[h] consistency + naive-merge failure"); launch [pos 493], completion [pos 494] (19:03 UTC), early HQ note [pos 563] ("§13.1, E[h(θ)] estimates converge: Same gap as Prop 2.
