The report's own caveat (verbatim, header): "**PROVED** below means a complete argument is supplied here or an explicitly identified source labels its result PROVED; campaign results remain candidates. ... No source result is upgraded by this report." and "The draft's §13.1 is correct if "ground truth" means the exact working posterior expectation and its limit is specified. It is false for arbitrary bounded functions if "ground truth" means the value at the generating parameter."

Targets and estimators (A-DRAFT section 2.1, Summary: plus quote): working posterior $\Pi(dS,d\beta,dv|y)=\pi(S|y)\kappa_S(d\beta,dv)$, $v=\sigma^2$; for bounded measurable $h$, $|h|\le M$, $f_h(S)=\int h(S,\beta,v)\kappa_S(d\beta,dv)$ and $\mu_h=\Pi h=\pi f_h$. Estimators: (1) self-normalised terminal particle estimate $\widetilde\mu_{r,N}(h)=\sum_iG_T(S^i_{r,T-1})f_h(S^i_{r,T-1})/\sum_iG_T(S^i_{r,T-1})$; (2) joint draws from $\kappa_{S^i}$; (3) Rao-Blackwell estimate $\widehat\mu^{RB,j}_{r,N}(h)=\frac1{4N}\sum_{u=1}^4\sum_i(K_jf_h)(Y^i_{r,u,j})$ with $(K_jf_h)(S)=o_j(S,1)f_h(S^+)+(1-o_j(S,1))f_h(S^-)$; "For $h_j=1\{j\in S\}$, $K_jf_{h_j}=o_j$; this is **exactly v3's recorded island PIP**." Also: "v3 currently specifies HPM, evidence and PIPs, **not an implemented general-purpose h-estimator**."

### TH320 — A-DRAFT Theorem A (fixed-data particle consistency; `ADRAFT-ThmA`)  [theorem]
- Source: `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md` section 2.2. Positions as the block header.
- Statement (verbatim):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.984) from `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > ### 2.2 Theorem A — fixed-data particle consistency (PROVED, candidate)
  > Assume EX-A, EX-S, START (locked T09(i)) and CAL. Condition on a successful calibration `c`, fixing the finite grid, move kernels, tier, `L`, four measured rounds and four islands, but let the final particle count `N→∞`. Consider the **potential uninterrupted run** (guards removed, otherwise identical).
  > For every bounded measurable h, all the estimators in §2.1 converge in probability and in `L²` to `μ_h`, islandwise and under primary pooling. The terminal weighted support law and every fixed terminal/prefix support law converge to `π` in total variation. Also `Zhat_r/Z→1` and `Zhat/Z→1`. In particular max_{j≤p}|PIP_j-hat − PIP_j| → 0.
  > For fixed `(data,c)` the mean-square errors are `O_{data,c,h}(N^{-1})`. This is an idealised particle family, not an accuracy rate claimed for the two production tiers. On the exact branch, posterior sums are already exact for the support law and any exactly evaluated `f_h`.
- Proof route (Summary:): on the finite simplex $\Psi_t(\eta)(f)=\eta(G_tf)/\eta(G_t)$ is Lipschitz (constant $2\max G_t/\min G_t$ in $\ell^1$), $\Phi_t(q_{t-1})=q_t$ by T09, conditional on the previous population the new particles are iid from $\Phi_t(\eta^N_{t-1})$ so variance is at most $\|f\|^2_\infty/N$; induct over the finitely many stages; terminal transitions $R$ with $\pi R=\pi$ (the recorded RB position uses the mixture $R_j$ over uniform orders). Calibration scope (verbatim): "An N-independent random calibration may be averaged out by dominated convergence. ... The bound can be enormous and is **not** uniform in growing n,p. Without a bounded-stage or other uniform-control hypothesis, conditional convergence at each fixed calibration does not imply a triangular-array limit."
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) (A-DRAFT, Astra) -> Astra-on-Astra: **VERIFIED*** (A-REV4 `REVIEW.md` verdict table "A-DRAFT §2 Theorem A and A1: VERIFIED. Fixed-data bounded-functional LLN/MSE and unnormalised identities; no CLT upgrade") -> A-REV6: "VERIFIED LLN/MSE and islandwise numerator identities; no T16 CLT/status upgrade". Registry: `PROVED (SF: VERIFIED* (A-REV4); XF: none)` ("ASTRA-ONLY"; REGISTRY_PAPER1: "ADRAFT-ThmA ASTRA-ONLY (Astra-on-Astra; citing a standard fixed-grid lemma does not upgrade it)").
- Depends on: TH107 (T09(i)), TH107 (T09(ii)), CJ130 (CAL), TH110 (T12). Relation (author): "T16(i), in `theorems/T16_T9_frozen_limits.md`, already states the evidence/PIP fixed-calibration limits and a CLT, but is marked **CONJECTURE** and is not a locked entry. Theorem A proves the bounded-functional consistency/MSE portion directly; it does **not** prove or upgrade T16's joint CLT."
- Feeds: M1 ⟦Theorem V/H⟧ (K47: "At a fixed grid and R, Ẑ_r, PIP̂_rj and H_r(h) converge to Z, PIP_j, π(h) as N → ∞", ASTRA-ONLY; final fixed-grid limit lemma card L-PROPP and S-POOL).

### TH321 — A-DRAFT Corollary A1 (exact finite-N identities for marked RB rewards; `ADRAFT-CorA1`)  [corollary]
- Source: `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md` section 2.3.
- Statement (verbatim):
  ⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.95; best match `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md`). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
  > **Corollary A1 (PROVED from locked T12).** At a fixed admissible terminal boundary, a pre-label recording position, or for a fixed convex average of the marked RB rewards above, E_c[Zhat_r muhat_r(h)] = Z mu_h, E_c Zhat_r = Z.  (I)
  > For the terminal pre-resampling estimator this also holds: multiply its ratio by `Zhat_T` to cancel its denominator, then apply T12(i.a) at stage T−1 to `G_T f_h`. For the other positions use T12(i.b,c) with `f_h` or `K_j f_h`; T09 gives `πK_j f_h=πf_h`. Conditional expectation over any optional coefficient draws preserves (I). Thus the numerator `Zhat_r muhat_r` is unbiased; the self-normalised or RB estimate itself generally is not.
  > In particular, for identically distributed islands given c, E_c muhat_r − mu_h = −Cov_c(Zhat_r, muhat_r)/Z. The unbiased pooled numerator is `(1/4)Σ_r Zhat_r muhat_r`. Independence of the four islands conditional on c gives E_c[Zhat · overline mu] − Z mu_h = −(3/4) Cov_c(Zhat_1, muhat_1).
  > The primary PIP in v3 is `overline mu`, not an evidence-weighted ratio. At fixed four islands both poolings are consistent as N grows by Theorem A. At fixed N and an increasing number of independent frozen islands, only the evidence-weighted ratio is guaranteed consistent by (I) and the iid law of large numbers; equal pooling converges to the generally biased mean. This is the distinction already anticipated by T16(ii), not a reason to silently change the production estimator.
  > T31's `0.05 Zhat` bound follows by Markov from `E Zhat=Z`; unbiasedness alone does **not** imply concentration or fixed-N accuracy.
- Status history: PROVED from locked T12 (A-DRAFT) -> Astra-on-Astra **VERIFIED*** (A-REV4: "A1 VERIFIED (pre-resampling identity; pooled product bias −¾Cov)"); A-REV6 VERIFIED. This is the general-h version of TH298 (the −3/4 Cov formula); registry `PROVED (SF: VERIFIED* (A-REV4); XF: none)`.
- Depends on: TH110 (T12(i.a,i.b,i.c)), TH107 (T09), TH298. Feeds: M1 ⟦Theorem V/H⟧ via K46 (`E[Ẑ_r·H_r(h)] = Z·π(h)` for bounded h measurable in (X, y, 𝓒); "A1new: PROOF SKETCH (NEW-SYNTH)... N1"), K47, K50; L-PROPP. The meeting's N1 ("E[W_r ĥ_r] = π(h)") remained a premise.

### TH322 — A-DRAFT Theorem D (n-indexed budgets, conditional on T26's premise), with uniform PIPs without (L+4)rho* -> 0 (`ADRAFT-ThmD`, `ADRAFT-uniPIP`)  [theorem]
- Source: `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md` section 2.4. Positions as the block header.
- Statement (verbatim):
  ⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.96; best match `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md`). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
  > ### 2.4 Theorem D — n-indexed budgets, conditional on T26's premise (PROVED, candidate)
  > Let n increase, with p, the design, true support, working posterior and budgets indexed by n. Use the actual four islands, `N_e=4^e max(2500,n,p)`, `T≤4 max(1000,ceil(log2(n+p+1))²)`, `L=max(4,ceil(log2(n+1)))`, and four measured rounds. Let `G_n` denote successful SMC calibration and `E_n` the exact branch. Assume EX-A, EX-S, START, CAL and **OUT**: whenever estimates are reported they equal their potential uninterrupted-run values; exact-branch output equals the exact posterior calculation. Let `O_n` be the output-available event. Assume
  > P_0(S_{0,n} ∉ Ω_n) → 0,  Δ_n = sup_{0≤φ≤1}{1 − q_{n,φ}(S_{0,n})},
  > P{G_n ∩ [(T_n+1)Δ_n > ε]} → 0,  P_0{E_n ∩ [1 − π_n(S_{0,n}) > ε]} → 0  (ε>0).  (P1)
  > These are W2-T26's premise form, including its exact-branch clause. For any data-measurable sequence `h_n` bounded by one fixed M, independent of final-run randomness, put `μ_n=Π_n h_n`.
  > Then for the integrated terminal self-normalised, endpoint and fixed-label RB estimators of §2.1, islandwise and primary pooled, P{O_n ∩ [|μhat_n − μ_n| > ε]} → 0.  (D1)
  > The same holds with the optional independent exact conditional parameter draws. Evidence satisfies `P{O_n∩[|Zhat/Z−1|>ε]}→0`, and the actual production PIPs satisfy P{O_n ∩ [max_{j≤p_n}|PIPhat_{n,j} − 1{j∈S_{0,n}}| > ε]} → 0  (D2) and hence also uniform convergence to the full posterior PIPs, and `P(O_n, MPMhat≠S0,n)→0`. No assertion that `P(O_n)→1` is included. For an unconditional successful-output guarantee add that operational assumption. Conditional-on-completion consistency can be deduced if `liminf P(O_n)>0`, by division of the displayed joint-error bounds, but no conditional unbiasedness or calibration identity follows.
  The proof gives explicit bounds (Summary: and verbatim key lines): (D3) `Δ=max{1−π_0(S_0), 1−π(S_0)}`; (D4) `E_c|W_r−1| ≤ b_c := 2(T+1)Δ/(1−Δ)`; the sharpening (D5) "E_c η_r(S_0^c) = δ + E_c[(1−W_r)η_r(S_0^c)] ≤ δ + E_c|W_r−1| ≤ δ + b_c. This uses 0≤η_r(S_0^c)≤1; it is not a lower-tail conditioning argument."; (D6) `E_c|η_r f − π f| ≤ 2M(2δ + b_c)`; (D7) `ρ̄ ≤ (B+3)u_π`; and the uniform PIP bound (D8) **E_c max_j|PIPhat_{r,j} − 1{j∈S_0}| ≤ min{1, δ+b_c} + ρ̄ + u_π** with the remark "Notice that no factor L appears: the evidence identity re-controls occupancy at every measured-round start. This independently justifies W2-T26's removal of the older `(L+4)ρ*→0` premise, using only locked identities." For weighted augmentation: Σ_i w_i² ≤ 1/m_0 + v_out² → 0. A sufficient deterministic version of (P1) is `(T_n^max+1)Δ_n→0` (T03 for the posterior endpoint, T22(iii) for the start endpoint under EXP′/visibility/leakage). Scope (author): "This is a favourable-start theorem, not a general theorem about correction from a badly distorted product law." "Neither T16 nor T26 alone asserts `Π_n h→h(θ*)` for all bounded h."
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) (A-DRAFT) -> Astra-on-Astra **VERIFIED*** (A-REV4 verdict table "A-DRAFT §2 Theorem D and D1: VERIFIED. Explicit favourable-start premise and bounded-function/continuity qualifications retained"; registry: "Theorem D and D1 VERIFIED with the explicit favourable-start premise (P1) and bounded-function/continuity qualifications; no masked-start or completion guarantee"; "D7 checked (elementary detailed balance; no p-union-bound loss); does not prove output availability → 1") -> A-REV6 "VERIFIED conditionally; explicit favorable premise, contraction/continuity, exact branch and output scope" and "A-DRAFT's sharper occupancy proof is independent". Registry rows: `ADRAFT-ThmD`, `ADRAFT-uniPIP` both `PROVED (SF: VERIFIED* (A-REV4); XF: none)`.
- Depends on: TH295 (Theorem A / (P1), (P1-ex)), LM198-LM200, TH112 (T14(i)), TH110 (T12(i.b)), TH116 (T22(iv-b)). Feeds: M1 ⟦Theorem V/H⟧ via K51 ("For any bounded h the Ẑ-weighted estimate is within 2δ₁ + c_h(ρ̄+u_π) of h(S₀) in W-weighted mean on every island, regime and frozen grid", classed DRAFT-ONLY; the meeting's "A1new" is "M1 + Prop P(iii) with h in place of the PIP"); the premise (P1) is unproved on masked designs.

### TH323 — A-DRAFT Corollary D1 (generating-value consistency under continuity; `ADRAFT-CorD1`)  [corollary]
- Source: `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md` section 2.5.
- Statement (verbatim):
  ⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.98; best match `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md`). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
  > **Corollary D1 (PROVED, conditional statistical implication).** Suppose, in addition to Theorem D, the full posterior concentrates about a generating parameter `θ*_n` in a specified metric after back-transformation, and `h_n` is uniformly locally continuous there: for every ε>0 there is r>0 with sup_n sup_{d(ϑ,ϑ_n^*)<r} |h_n(ϑ) − h_n(ϑ_n^*)| ≤ ε. Then `Π_n h_n−h_n(θ*_n)→0` in data probability, because its absolute value is at most `ε+2M Π_n{d≥r}`. Add (D1) to obtain generating-value consistency on the output event. Appropriate statistical contraction, e.g. a correctly matched T04 conclusion, is an additional input; T03 supplies support concentration alone. For support indicators and bounded support functions, T03 suffices directly: `|π_n f_n−f_n(S0,n)|≤2Mδ_n`. For inclusion indicators, (D2) is the sharper simultaneous statement.
  > **Suggested replacement for draft §13.1.** "For each fixed data set and successful independently calibrated final schedule, the SMC particle estimates and the recorded Rao–Blackwell inclusion estimates converge to their exact working-posterior expectations as the number of final particles increases. Under the stated favourable-start, posterior-concentration and operational conditions, the actual n-indexed budgets also give posterior-functional consistency and uniform inclusion recovery. Convergence of general parameter functionals to their generating values requires an additional posterior-contraction and continuity argument."
- Status history: PROVED, conditional (A-DRAFT) -> Astra-on-Astra **VERIFIED*** (A-REV4: "D1 VERIFIED (uniform local continuity and posterior contraction needed)"); A-REV6 VERIFIED with "continuous generating-value claims additionally need contraction and uniform local continuity". Registry `ADRAFT-CorD1`.
- Replaces the over-claim RF230. Depends on TH322, TH103 (T03), TH104 (T04). Feeds: none in paper-1 (K47-K51 cover the fixed-grid and h-estimator statements; this corollary is not carried).

### RF233 — "in the masked regime Ẑ can only fail downward" (THM-SYNTH A2 plain sentence)  [refuted claim]
- Source: `THM-SYNTH` THEOREM_LIST A2 as quoted in `MEET-v31/evidence/2026-11-03_PC1_proof_check.md` Claim 4 (this belongs to the theorem-meeting phase, theme 12 for THM-SYNTH; recorded here because it concerns the masked evidence tail of TH311). Also listed in R1_C item 7 (Seat C, Astra).

It does not apply to A2's formal statement (iii) ("P(W > (T/η)[π₀(Aᶜ)/π₀(x_m)]e^{−φ_{τ_A}D_A}) ≤ η + Nπ₀(A)").
- Refutation (PC1 claim 4, verbatim): "Suppose Ẑ ≤ Z almost surely and E[Ẑ | 𝓒] = Z. Then Z − Ẑ ≥ 0 with mean 0, so Ẑ = Z almost surely. A2(iii) says that in the masked regime P(Ẑ < Z | 𝓒) > 0, and in fact close to 1. Hence P(Ẑ > Z | 𝓒) > 0. More precisely, E[(W−1)⁺ | 𝓒] = E[(1−W)⁺ | 𝓒], so the rare upward excursions carry all the missing mass." Instance CE187. Corrected wording (verbatim): "In the masked regime Ẑ underestimates Z with high probability: P(W_r > t_*) ≤ η + Nπ₀(A) with t_* = (T/η)[π₀(Aᶜ)/π₀(x_m)]e^{−φ_{τ_A}D_A}. Because E[W_r | 𝓒] = 1, the complementary rare event carries compensating overestimates of the same total mean ... Markov caps them: P(Ẑ > 20Z) ≤ 0.05. The run certificate Ẑ < Z_𝒯 detects underestimation only."
- Status: PROVED false for the plain-language sentence (PC1 claim 4: "PROVED (C's COUNTEREXAMPLE is valid)"); the formal tail statement (TH311/TH309) is untouched. In S-Z (Proposition Z (iii)) only the exception-probability form P(Ẑ_r > √δ₁Z on a terminal-off island) ≤ 2√δ₁ ships ("PC1 §15 COUNTEREXAMPLE conceded"). **UNCERTAIN (placement):** also belongs to the THM-SYNTH owner (theme 12).

## Theme 9: FINITE-N-CERT (finite-n theory and certificates)

Summary: this theme collects what the campaign proved, refuted or measured about what can be said at a *finite* n (in particular the study's n = 200, p in {500, 1000}, s0 = 14), as opposed to the asymptotic theorems of the other themes. It has four strands.

1. **Per-fit certificates.** Branch `theory/O-CERT` (Opus 5.5 high, laptop; launched [pos 575] 2026-11-02 18:49 UTC; result reported to the user at [pos 706]); same-family referee `theory/O-VCERT` (launched [pos 729] 19:29 UTC; result reported [pos 763]); cross-family review inside A-REV9 (Astra; launched [pos 830] 21:15 UTC; verdicts folded into the registry and reported at [pos 917]-[pos 919]). Contents: Lemma M (Q_S decreasing and D_S increasing in S), C1 the one-sided global certificate, C2 the PW2-conditional two-sided band, C3 exact relative certificates, C4 the box certificate, C5 the posterior-miss certificate, C6 the per-fit card, and the repairs R1 and R2 written by the referee.
2. **Predicted miss rates.** Branch `theory/O-SWAP` (Opus 5.5 high; launched [pos 577]; mid-run note [pos 578]; finished by [pos 742]): finite-n laws of the three one-move posterior-miss modes under a projection approximation PA, the first-order bracket, the swap ceiling, the predictors T1/T2, and their comparison with the observed misses.
3. **Theorem N200.** Branch `theory/API-N200` (Fable 5.1 on the API credit, cap $25; launched [pos 906], announced [pos 911], result reported [pos 978] 23:22 UTC): the composition inequality for the reported HPM valid at every n, with the posterior-miss probability Pi(X) as its middle term, and the 24-cell table (predicted 558.1 vs observed 571 wrong fits of 2,400; RMS z 1.08).
4. **Numerics and data.** `theory/W7-SEC` (cloud credits; launched [pos 711]; HQ description [pos 717]; still working [pos 742] and [pos 748]; all reports in by [pos 754]): T33 floating-point margins, the engine `error_bound()` counterexample, the T32(i) recount and a floating-point addendum (the T05 half of that branch belongs to theme 1). `theory/S-ELS` (E_LS ledger extraction, Claude Work on the laptop; launched [pos 715]; reported [pos 763]) and `theory/O-LS0` (LS0 post hoc on the 2,400 fits; data run launched [pos 399]-[pos 400], relaunched light [pos 465]-[pos 467], report written by O-LS0-WRAP launched [pos 760] 20:24 UTC; outcome reported [pos 774] and [pos 796]) are **data facts** and are entered as CJ entries labelled "data fact". Finally the n = 200 disclosure paragraph of W8-SYNTH `SYNTHESIS.md` section 1 (W8-SYNTH launched [pos 756], reported [pos 763], brief corrected [pos 793]) with its numerical-inconsistency table in section 4.13.

Status vocabulary. Everything in strands 1-3 is a "candidate" in the authors' own words; nothing in this theme was adopted. Cross-family (XF) verdicts exist only for the certificates (A-REV9 on O-CERT and O-VCERT) and, negatively (GAP), for the O-SWAP predicted rates; for W7-SEC A-REV9 says "GAP in this review: deferred", meaning unreviewed, not rejected; N200 is author-only. Final-card mapping (MEET-THM): Lemma M and C4 feed the supplement S-CERT (K73, K05); the deterministic inequality Z >= Z_T of C1 feeds M4 (K42); N200 feeds M5 Theorem HPM (K72), with the Pi(X) upper bound relegated to FUTURE_WORK FW14 (K94); the validated-arithmetic obligation and the T33-errbound counterexample feed FUTURE_WORK FW16 (K107); the O-SWAP rates and the data facts feed no final card (campaign-only).

### Common setting of the O-CERT results (quoted once; the items below refer to it)

- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 2, head 332bf3e (verbatim).
- Setting (verbatim):
  > Notation of `00_COMMON.md` and the T12/T31 statements. Standardised (X, y), ‖x_j‖² = ‖y‖² = n − 1, K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋),
  > Ω = {S ⊆ [p] : |S| ≤ K}. For S ∈ Ω, M_S := X_SX_Sᵀ (n × n),
  >
  >   F(S) := log ϖ(S) + log m(S) = log w(|S|) − log W_K + log C_n − ½ log D_S − ν log(2b₀ + Q_S),
  >
  > so π(S) = e^{F(S)}/Z and Z = Σ_Ω e^{F}. New symbols:
  > - 𝒮̄ is the scored set of the potential uninterrupted run R̄ (W2-BOOK). 𝒯 is any *reported* set of distinct scored
  >   models with their scores; the engine reports the top store `top_store`, the 40p + 1 best scored models, and
  >   `local_search`. Z_𝒯 := Σ_{S∈𝒯} e^{F(S)}.
  > - Ŝ is the reported HPM, and Ẑ = ¼Σ_rẐ_r is the reported pooled evidence.
  > - g := F(Ŝ) − max_{S∈𝒯∖{Ŝ}} F(S) ≥ 0 is the best-of-scored gap (the engine's top store gives it as top[1] − top[2]).
  > - 𝒩(c) is the feasible flip-or-swap neighbourhood (T20 §1), and N̄(c) := {c} ∪ 𝒩(c).
  > - For L ⊆ U ⊆ [p], the box [L, U] := {S ∈ Ω : L ⊆ S ⊆ U}, and
  >   - Φ(L, U) := log w(|L|) − log W_K + log C_n − ½ log D_L − ν log(2b₀ + Q_U);
  >   - M(L, U) := log Σ_{k=|L|}^{min(|U|,K)} C(|U|−|L|, k−|L|) w(k) − log W_K + log C_n − ½ log D_L − ν log(2b₀ + Q_U).
  > - 𝒪 is the output-available event, 𝒪_E ⊆ 𝒪 the event that an evidence value is reported, and 𝒜 the calibration
  >   success event (W2-BOOK, Prop 2).
  >
  > Hypotheses (all named in locked results or W2-BOOK): EX-A, EX-S, CAL, START, (H-T12) = T12(iii), GUARD (stop-only
  > coupling, W2-BOOK). Floating point enters only through VAL-FP(η, ε) (W2-BOOK) and, for the deterministic items, the
  > score contract SC(η_F) below.
  >
  > **SC(η_F)** (new code). Every score used by the card, whether computed by the engine or post hoc, is within η_F of
  > its exact value. This is the deterministic analogue of VAL-FP, and it is checkable by replay in higher precision.

- Lemma M: VERIFIED in exact arithmetic. The push-through identity gives Q=y'y/(n+1)+n/(n+1)y'(I+(n+1)XX')^-1 y. Inversion reverses PSD order. For a column addition D'/D=h(n+1)/h(1), h'(c)=x'(I+cM)^-2 x>=0. BB weight ratio is (k+1)/(2p-1-k)<=1.

**(RV-3) A-REV9 repairs and explicit counterexamples** (same file, section "Certificate repairs and explicit counterexamples", verbatim):

C1(a): take any two scored models with strict gap g>0 and set S=HPM. The displayed inequality becomes 1<=exp(-g). Exclude HPM; define g only when a competitor exists (or specify the empty-maximum convention).

R1: let a positive finite posterior have all states scored, let Zhat=Z, and choose a reported subset T with pi(T)<alpha. Unscored mass is zero, whereas 1-Z_T/(alpha Z)>0. The corrected statement is about Omega minus T. O-VCERT's optional unscored bound also requires a genuine upper bound on the entire logical scored set: a final-run fresh-score count that omits calibration is insufficient. Use a full store and Nbar covering every phase, with unreported scores bounded by F_min.

C5: identical predictor columns 1 and 2 give F({1})=F({2}). Let the truth be {1}, the reported/scored alternative be {2}, and restrict the verified box to U={1,2} with singleton models maximizing (choose a response fit where one inclusion beats empty but redundant inclusion is penalized). The lexicographic rule prefers {1}. Weak score domination alone cannot exclude a tie-related search miss. The C5 event inclusion only concerns strict score superiority and survives unchanged.

C3/C6 local identity: v3_engine.h local_search marks A.returned as certified when its frozen-centre scan has no strict improvement. The ledger can update the HPM on an equal-score neighbour without moving the centre (explicit code comment and strict best.F>C.F test). Therefore check returned==HPM, certify the returned support by name, or rescan HPM. Local flags alone cannot be silently transferred across distinct supports.

C4/C6 floating point: SC bounds computed complete scores F(S). Phi(L,U) combines log D_L and log(2b0+Q_U); errors in complete scores do not separately bound these mixed ingredients. Require interval bounds for each ingredient (including summation) and prune only when an upper bound for Phi is below a lower bound for F(HPM). R2 then correctly supplies

    u_fp(S)=exp(F_fp(S)+eta_F)/max(exp(-eta_F) Z_T_fp, alpha Zhat_fp),
    outside-store lower bound = 1-exp(eta_F) Z_T_fp/(alpha Zhat_fp).

The statistical failure probability is at most alpha exp(eta) P(A)+epsilon under VAL-FP. This is a conditional validation contract, not a measured production guarantee. Local and region claims must only be emitted after their own checks. Under exact arithmetic, those checks plus R1 give the C6 union bound directly from the single bad event Z<alpha Zhat. We do not upgrade the original GAP card or GUARD's broader implementation claims.

Reference audit: methodology sections 5 and 6.13 match the common Q,D definitions; expanding the scorer's nonnegative fallback with beta=n H^-1 z gives y'y-z'beta, the same Q. v3_ledger.h stores distinct models by deterministic score/support and uses size then lexicographic HPM ties. v3_engine.h:202-216 draws each particle's round separately; the final loop uses multinomial resampling before independent mutations. These support the exact component model, not a universal floating-point assertion.

**(RV-5) O-VCERT repairs R1 and R2** (`O-VCERT/REPORT.md` section 4, verbatim):

- **R1 (C1(b) last sentence, C6 G3, C1 remark).**
  - Replace "unscored and unreported" with "**not in 𝒯**". The claim π(Ω ∖ 𝒯) ≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ) is then exactly right.
  - If an *unscored*-mass statement is wanted: let N̄ be any reported upper bound on the number of distinct scored
     models (the engine's score counter is one), and F_min := min_𝒯 F. Then, on the same event,
     π(unscored) ≥ 1 − [Z_𝒯 + (N̄ − |𝒯|)₊·e^{F_min}]/(αẐ).
  - Proof of the bound: every scored model outside a full store has F ≤ F_min. If the store is not full, every scored
     model is in 𝒯 and the correction is 0.
  - Change the remark to "the reported store holds less than α of the posterior".
- **R2 (C6 FP clause).**
  - Under SC(η_F), VAL-FP(η, ε), and a de-duplication of 𝒯 by model before summing, report
    u_α^fp(S) := exp(F^fp(S) + η_F) / max(e^{−η_F}·Z_𝒯^fp, α·Ẑ^fp).
  - The G claims then fail only on 𝒪_E ∩ {Z < αẐ^fp}, whose probability is ≤ α·e^η·P(𝒜) + ε (W2-BOOK Prop 2(f)).
  - The same inflation applies to the "outside 𝒯" item: 1 − e^{η_F}Z_𝒯^fp/(αẐ^fp). (The log-sum-exp rounding is
    absorbed into η_F.)

  in a non-singleton leaf: it double-counts e^{F(Ŝ)}, which is conservative. Confirmed numerically.
- **S2.** §1 item 1, §5 first bullet and C6 "cannot certify confidence … without PW2 or enumeration" overstate C1(c).
  - C1(c) is a non-implication from the 𝓛(Z) properties only.
  - Any certified upper bound on Z gives a sure lower bound on π(Ŝ): the inventory's UB, a Lemma-M box cover of all of Ω
    (impractical at p = 500, as O-CERT §5 says), or T31's own remark Ẑ ≥ e^{−Δ}Z with Δ = max_Ω d − min_Ω d.
  - Reword as: "not from unbiasedness; it needs an upper bound on Z (PW2, UB, enumeration, or a bound on Δ)".
- **S3.** In C5, "posterior miss" needs F(S₀) < F(Ŝ), or F(S₀) = F(Ŝ) with Ŝ ≺ S₀. Under an exact tie with S₀ ≺ Ŝ,
  scoring S₀ would have changed the report, which makes it a search miss in the tie sense. Certify Φ(leaf) < F(Ŝ)
  strictly, or carry the HPM order. Exact ties are non-generic (T06). Also add |S₀| ≤ K.
- **S4.** §4 is empty and `results/cards.txt` is not committed. Every numeric claim of O-CERT (tree sizes, "cost grows
  like 2^{#ambiguous}", P(S₀ ⊄ U) "measured") is therefore unsupported as it stands. The "2^{#ambiguous}" sentence is a
  heuristic remark, not part of C4.
  - My small-p B&B used a natural variable order and visited a median of 272 nodes for |U| = 13 (8,192 leaves).
  - I did not reproduce the p = 500 runs: R and the study datasets are not on this laptop.
- **S5.** C1 and C6 inherit the unreviewed status of W2-BOOK (Lemma RO, GUARD, Prop 2). Lemma RO(1)–(4) are elementary
  inclusions, and I re-checked them. GUARD itself is a code fact that I did not audit.


### LM204 — Lemma M (OCERT-LemmaM; "Lemma M (Q_S decreasing, D_S increasing in S)"; proposed paper label Lemma MON)  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3, "Lemma M (monotonicity of the score ingredients). PROVED."; reviews RV-1, RV-2. Positions: launch of O-CERT [pos 575]; result reported [pos 706] ("A new monotonicity lemma gives a box certificate"); O-VCERT launch [pos 729] (brief asked to check "whether Lemma M's monotonicity holds for the ACTUAL score"), result [pos 763]; A-REV9 [pos 830], [pos 917]-[pos 919].
- Statement (verbatim, `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3):
  > For S ⊆ S′ ⊆ [p]: (a) Q_S ≥ Q_{S′}; (b) D_S ≤ D_{S′}; (c) w(k + 1) ≤ w(k) for 0 ≤ k ≤ p − 1, so w is non-increasing on
  > {0, …, K}. Moreover (d) Q_S = yᵀy/(n+1) + (n/(n+1))·yᵀ(I_n + (n+1)M_S)⁻¹y and
  > D_S = det(I_n + (n+1)M_S)/det(I_n + M_S).
- Earlier versions / repairs: none to the statement. O-VCERT adds a free corollary (RV-1, Lemma M (d) row and section 3 item 2): Lemma M(d) gives Q_S >= y'y/(n+1), so the engine trigger Q < 10^-8 y'y can never fire in exact arithmetic when n + 1 < 10^8 (the non-negative branch is a pure floating-point safeguard); the same fact is proved independently by W7-SEC as LM207.
- Status history: proposed and proved by O-CERT (PROVED, candidate, "checked line by line") -> SF VERIFIED by O-VCERT: (a) Q_S decreasing VERIFIED, (b) D_S increasing VERIFIED (derivative re-derived; log D rises by >= 5.6e-3 per addition in every test, duplicates included), (c) w decreasing VERIFIED, (d) both n x n forms VERIFIED (agree with the k x k definitions to 8e-13); "0 violations in 476,160 exhaustive (S, S+j) pairs" on 150 designs (n in {5,6,12,30,40}, p in {8,9,10}, so p > n included) -> XF VERIFIED in exact arithmetic (A-REV9: "Lemma M: VERIFIED in exact arithmetic"). Registry: `OCERT-LemmaM` PROVED / VERIFIED / VERIFIED; on `T38-RECORD/LOCKABLE_v2.md` (strict lockable; A-REV9 LOCKABLE: "O-CERT Lemma M"). A-REV8 also VERIFIED Lemma M as used by Prop GU (registry conflict C25: A-REV9 called GU a GAP only because the imported Lemma M was not re-audited there).
- Proved by / checked by: O-CERT (Opus 5.5); O-VCERT (Opus 5.5, same family); A-REV9 (Astra, cross-family).
- Proof route (Summary:) push-through identity gives Q_S = y'y/(n+1) + (n/(n+1)) y'(I + (n+1)M_S)^-1 y; Loewner order reverses under inversion; determinant ratio via the matrix determinant lemma with h(c) = 1 + c x'(I + cM)^-1 x, h' = x'(I + cM)^-2 x >= 0; w(k+1)/w(k) = (k+1)/(2p-1-k) <= 1.

### TH327 — Theorem C2 (OCERT-C2; "two-sided band, conditional on PW2")  [theorem]
- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem C2, "PROVED (candidate), CONDITIONAL"; reviews RV-1, RV-2. Positions as TH326.

  > T25(iv), so that Var_c(Ẑ/Z) ≤ B_T/4. Then for ε ∈ (0, 1):
  >
  >   P(𝒪_E, ∃S ∈ Ω : π(S) < (1 − ε)e^{F(S)}/Ẑ) ≤ E[1_𝒜·B_T/(B_T + 4ε²)],
  >
  > and jointly with C1, π(S) ∈ [(1 − ε)e^{F(S)}/Ẑ, e^{F(S)}/max(Z_𝒯, αẐ)] for every S simultaneously, except on an event
  > of probability ≤ α·P(𝒜) + E[1_𝒜 B_T/(B_T + 4ε²)].
  > *Corollary (conditional global-HPM certificate).* On the good event, if (1 − ε)e^{F(Ŝ)}/Ẑ > ½, then π(Ŝ) > ½. So Ŝ is
  > the unique global HPM of π and the Bayes rule for exact recovery (Prop 1), and the event E_n of T20(ii) holds with S₀
  > replaced by Ŝ.

  > from ESS) nor the empirical 4-island SD (T31(d2): conditioning on E2 not raised can push coverage below any γ)
  > supplies them. C2 is a *what-if* statement: "if the run's relative variance were at most v, then π(Ŝ) ≥ …".

### TH328 — Theorem C3 (OCERT-C3; "exact relative certificates on fully scored regions")  [theorem]
- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem C3, "PROVED."; reviews RV-1 to RV-3. Positions as TH326.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > Assume EX-A (or SC(η_F), with the stated changes). Let R ⊆ Ω be any finite region with Ŝ ∈ R whose scores are all
  > available (scored by the run, or recomputed post hoc from (X, y)). Then exactly
  > π(Ŝ | R) = e^{F(Ŝ)}/Σ_{S∈R} e^{F(S)}, and π(S)/π(Ŝ) = e^{F(S)−F(Ŝ)} for all S ∈ R. In particular:
  > - (a) **Local** (T20(i)). If `local_certified`, then F(S) ≤ F(Ŝ) for all S ∈ 𝒩(Ŝ). The local share
  >   ρ_loc := π(Ŝ | N̄(Ŝ)) and the type gaps
  >   - g_add := F(Ŝ) − max_j F(Ŝ ∪ {j}),
  >   - g_del := F(Ŝ) − max_i F(Ŝ ∖ {i}),
  >   - g_swap := F(Ŝ) − max_{i,j} F(Ŝ ∖ {i} ∪ {j})
  >
  >   are exact. They need p + |Ŝ|(p − |Ŝ|) scores, the same as one scan.
  > - (b) **Subset class.** For the 2^{|Ŝ|} − 1 proper subsets of Ŝ, g_sub := F(Ŝ) − max_{S⊊Ŝ} F(S) and
  >   Σ_{S⊊Ŝ} π(S)/π(Ŝ) are exact (enumeration; 16,383 scores at |Ŝ| = 14).
  > - (c) **Best-of-scored.** For every S ∈ 𝒮̄ ∖ {Ŝ}, π(S) ≤ e^{−g}π(Ŝ) with g the top-store gap.
  >
  > Under SC(η_F), each exact equality becomes a two-sided bound with factor e^{±2η_F}, and each certified inequality
  > F(S) ≤ F(Ŝ) needs the computed gap to be ≥ 2η_F.
- Application to S0-type alternatives (verbatim, same section):
  > *What these give the S₀-type alternatives (task item iii).* The study's misses are supersets at c = 1, and same-size
  > swaps and subsets at c = 0.5 (THEORY_PRIORITIES §5). If S₀ = Ŝ ∪ {j} or Ŝ ∖ {i}, or a one-swap of Ŝ, then S₀ ∈ N̄(Ŝ),
  > and the card's g_add, g_del, g_swap bound π(S₀)/π(Ŝ) exactly. If S₀ ⊊ Ŝ (a superset miss at any depth), (b) bounds it
  > exactly. In each case the bound is computable without knowing S₀, because it holds uniformly over the whole class.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none to the statement. A-REV9 requires an identity check (see status).
- Status history: O-CERT "PROVED" -> SF O-VCERT "VERIFIED (with S-bar read as the SR logical scored set; code-checked)"; scope note: no region other than T has its scores in the run output, so local, subset and box certificates are post-hoc rescoring, which C3 allows -> XF A-REV9 "C3: VERIFIED ratios and fully rescored regions in exact arithmetic. Apply local certification to the returned/scanned centre; identifying it with the reported HPM requires checking identity, especially under exact ties" (the engine `v3_engine.h` local_search can update the HPM on an equal-score neighbour without moving the centre; "check returned==HPM, certify the returned support by name, or rescan HPM"). Registry `OCERT-C3`: VERIFIED / VERIFIED*; on LOCKABLE_v2 with qualification "any fully scored region".
- Proved by / checked by: O-CERT; O-VCERT (code audit of `TopStore::offer`, `offer_stores`, calibration export); A-REV9.

### TH329 — Theorem C4 (OCERT-C4; "box certificate", box monotonicity)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem C4, "PROVED."; reviews RV-1 to RV-3. Positions as TH326.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > Assume EX-A. For L ⊆ U ⊆ [p] with |L| ≤ K, and every S ∈ [L, U]:
  >
  >   F(S) ≤ Φ(L, U),  and  Σ_{S∈[L,U]} e^{F(S)} ≤ e^{M(L, U)}.
  >
  > Let 𝔗 be a finite family of boxes partitioning [∅, U] (for example the leaves of a binary tree in which a node [L, U′]
  > splits into [L ∪ {j}, U′] and [L, U′ ∖ {j}] for some j ∈ U′ ∖ L). Then:
  > - (a) *Optimality.* If every leaf [L, U′] ∈ 𝔗 satisfies Φ(L, U′) ≤ F(Ŝ), or is a singleton {S} with F(S) ≤ F(Ŝ),
  >   then F(Ŝ) = max_{S∈[∅,U]} F(S) (when Ŝ ⊆ U). Equivalently, π(S) ≤ π(Ŝ) for all 2^{|U|} supports S ⊆ U with |S| ≤ K.
  > - (b) *Conditional mass.* With Ŝ ⊆ U, π(Ŝ | [∅, U]) ≥ (1 + Σ_{leaves ≠ {Ŝ}} e^{M(leaf) − F(Ŝ)})⁻¹, where a
  >   singleton leaf {S} contributes e^{F(S)−F(Ŝ)}.
  > - (c) *Refutation.* If some S ∈ [∅, U] evaluated in the tree has F(S) > F(Ŝ), then Ŝ is not the HPM of π. If moreover
  >   S ∉ 𝒮̄, the run made a **search miss** relative to S. The certificate is constructive.
  >
  > Under SC(η_F), replace F(Ŝ) by F(Ŝ) − 2η_F in (a).
- Remarks of the author (verbatim; the cost sentence "grows like 2^(number of ambiguous variables)" is a heuristic, see CJ248):
  > *Remarks.*
  > - C4 needs only (X, y, Ŝ), not the run. It can certify **any** reported model, including SuSiE's or SSL's, and is
  >   valid for every choice of U, including a data-dependent one. So there is no selection or multiplicity issue.
  > - **Cost.** The bound is loose at the root, where the prior factor w(|L|) is evaluated at |L| = 0. Pruning happens
  >   once L has absorbed the decisive variables. So the tree's size grows like 2^{(number of ambiguous variables in U)},
  >   not 2^{|U|}. Measured sizes are in §4.
- Earlier versions / repairs: O-VCERT S1: C4(a) should state that leaves with |L| > K are empty and vacuously fine; C4(b) double-counts e^F(S-hat) when S-hat lies in a non-singleton leaf, which is conservative (confirmed numerically). A-REV9: the floating-point clause "Under SC(eta_F), replace F(S-hat) by F(S-hat) - 2 eta_F in (a)" is a GAP (RV-3 "C4/C6 floating point": SC bounds complete scores F(S), whereas Phi(L,U) combines log D_L and log(2 b0 + Q_U); interval bounds for each ingredient are needed).
- Status history: O-CERT "PROVED." -> SF O-VCERT "VERIFIED: 0 Phi-violations and 0 M-violations over all 285,712 boxes on 48 designs (including p > n, duplicate and factor designs, and the binding cap K). B&B agrees with brute force 80/80, and the mass lower bound is valid 40/40" -> XF A-REV9 "C4: VERIFIED exact-arithmetic box inequalities ... The displayed mass lower bound is conservative even if the HPM leaf is not isolated. FP clause remains GAP". Registry `OCERT-C4`: VERIFIED / VERIFIED*; on LOCKABLE_v2 ("exact boxes"). O-VCERT also records: endpoint evaluation max(F(L), F(U)) underestimates the box maximum in 2,764 of 6,561 boxes, so the split into three separately monotone factors is essential (see RF251/CE196).
- Proved by / checked by: O-CERT; O-VCERT; A-REV9.
- Proof route (Summary:) Lemma M (a)-(c) bound each factor of F(S) on the box; sum the exact size weights for the mass bound; the split rule partitions the box.
- Depends on: LM204 (Lemma M), EX-A. The trial of a global box at p > n fails: "Q_[p] ~ y'y/(n+1) when p > n, so Phi(empty, [p]) is astronomically large" (O-CERT section 5).
- Feeds: S-CERT K73 ("Branch-and-bound over a declared region with a certified upper bound on subtree scores is exact when it completes, 'unresolved' on budget exhaustion, and certifies nothing outside the region"); MEET-THM status cell "OCERT-C4: PROVED (SF: VERIFIED (O-VCERT); XF: VERIFIED* (A-REV9))". The operational region-certification clause was withdrawn at the theorem meeting (R3-8; `REGISTRY_PAPER1.md` S-CERT note).


### TH330 — Corollary C5 (OCERT-C5; "posterior-miss certificate")  [corollary]
- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3 Corollary C5, "PROVED."; reviews RV-1 to RV-3. Positions as TH326.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > In the setting of C4(a), on the event {S₀ ⊆ U}: Ŝ ≠ S₀ implies F(S₀) ≤ F(Ŝ). So the miss is a **posterior** miss in
  > the classification of THEORY_PRIORITIES §5, and by Prop 1 it cannot be repaired by any search, and (for same-size
  > S₀) by no size-only prior. Hence, for every data-measurable rule U = U(X, y, Ŝ),
  >
  >   P(𝒪, Ŝ ≠ S₀, F(S₀) > F(Ŝ)) ≤ P(𝒪, C4(a) fails for U) + P(𝒪, S₀ ⊄ U).
  >
  > *Proof.* Immediate from C4(a). ∎ The last term is a screening probability. It is the only place where statistics (and
  > hence asymptotics) re-enters. At n = 200 it is measured, not proved, in §4.
- Earlier versions / repairs: O-VCERT S3: "in C5, 'posterior miss' needs F(S0) < F(S-hat), or F(S0) = F(S-hat) with S-hat before S0 [in the HPM order]. Under an exact tie with S0 before S-hat, scoring S0 would have changed the report, which makes it a search miss in the tie sense. Certify Phi(leaf) < F(S-hat) strictly, or carry the HPM order. ... Also add |S0| <= K." A-REV9: tie-insensitive prose is an ERROR (RF239, CE191); the displayed strict-score event inclusion is VERIFIED.
- Status history: O-CERT "PROVED." -> SF O-VCERT "VERIFIED, with a tie caveat" -> XF A-REV9 "C5: ERROR if interpreted as a tie-aware posterior-miss certificate from a weak score inequality ... The C5 event inclusion only concerns strict score superiority and survives unchanged." Registry `OCERT-C5`: VERIFIED* / ERROR. A-REV9 LOCKABLE: "C5 strict-score event inclusion" only.
- Proved by / checked by: O-CERT; O-VCERT; A-REV9.
- Depends on: TH329 (C4(a)), TH131 (Prop 1 (T07)), the HPM total order (TH115 (T21) section 1).
- Feeds: none directly (campaign-only); the posterior-miss / search-miss trichotomy is carried by TH334 (Theorem N200) (TH334) in its order-exact form.


### TH331 — Theorem C6 (OCERT-C6; "the per-fit certificate card"), with Remark C6' (deterministic regime)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem C6 and Remark C6' (head 332bf3e); repairs R1, R2 in `O-VCERT/REPORT.md` section 4; reviews RV-1 to RV-4. Positions as TH326.
- Statement (verbatim, "Theorem C6 (the per-fit certificate card). PROVED (candidate)."):
  > The **card** of a fit with output is the list of claims:
  > - **L (local, deterministic):** `local_certified` ⇒ F(S) ≤ F(Ŝ) on 𝒩(Ŝ); the exact values g_add, g_del, g_swap,
  >   ρ_loc (C3(a)); g_sub and the subset ratio (C3(b)); the best-of-scored gap g (C3(c)).
  > - **R (region, deterministic):** for the reported U, "Ŝ = argmax_{[∅,U]} F" and π(Ŝ | [∅, U]) ≥ ρ_U (C4), or a
  >   refutation (C4(c)).
  > - **G (global, one-sided, level α):** π(Ŝ) ≤ u_α(Ŝ) = e^{F(Ŝ)}/max(Z_𝒯, αẐ); π(S) ≤ u_α(S) for every model; the
  >   unscored mass is ≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ) (C1).
  > - **C (conditional, flagged as such):** the C2 band for a stated hypothetical B_T. It is not counted as certified.
  >
  > Under EX-A, EX-S, CAL, START and GUARD:
  >
  >   P(𝒪 and some L, R or G claim on the card is false) ≤ α·P(𝒜) ≤ α,
  >
  > for every n, p and data set, with no asymptotics, and without conditioning on completion. Given completion, only the
  > bound α·P(𝒜)/P(𝒪) is claimed. Under VAL-FP(η, ε) and SC(η_F), with the L and R claims checked at margin 2η_F, the bound
  > becomes α·e^{η} + ε.
- Remark C6' (verbatim, "deterministic regime; PROVED", added after O-VCERT's review; unreviewed):
  > *Remark C6′ (deterministic regime; PROVED).* Every L, R and G claim on the card is true **surely** on the
  > data-observable event 𝒟_α := {Z_𝒯 ≥ αẐ}. On 𝒟_α, max(Z_𝒯, αẐ) = Z_𝒯 ≤ Z, so u_α(S) = e^{F(S)}/Z_𝒯 ≥ π(S) by C1(a).
  > The unscored-mass line reads "≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ)", whose right side is ≤ 0, so it is vacuous. The L and R claims are
  > deterministic. Hence {card false} ⊆ 𝒟_αᶜ ∩ {Z < αẐ}, and a fit whose card shows Z_𝒯 ≥ αẐ carries a card that is true
  > with certainty, not merely with probability 1 − α. This is legitimate even though 𝒟_α is selected after the fact,
  > because the claim holds pointwise on 𝒟_α. The price is that the G bound is then only as good as the top store. All
  > four fits in §4 are in this regime.
- What the card does not say, and the paper sentence (verbatim):
  > *What the card does **not** say.*
  > - It does not say that π(Ŝ) is large. That needs C2 (PW2) or enumeration.
  > - It does not say Ŝ = S₀. That needs Thm 1 (asymptotic) and the screening term of C5.
  > - It does not say that the global HPM was found. That needs [∅, U] = Ω, impossible at p = 500.
  >
  > The paper sentence: "*Each fit reports a certificate card whose claims hold simultaneously with probability at least
  > 95%, at the actual n, whether or not the run completes.*"

### TH334 — Theorem N200 (finite-n composition, two-sided, every term explicit)  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `API-N200/PROOF.md` sections 0 and 2; `API-N200/REPORT.md` sections 1-2; branch head 453117a. Positions: launch [pos 906] (21:29 UTC; brief says the simulated JRSS-B referee's point 1 and W8-SYNTH's "still open: anything quantitative at n = 200" motivate it), [pos 911] (API-N200 "A finite-n theorem for n = 200, checked cell by cell against the observed miss counts. It answers the referee's biggest objection"), [pos 929], result [pos 978] ("Predicted 558 wrong reports vs 571 observed across 2,400 fits (24 cells, RMS z ~ 1.1)"), later use [pos 1009], [pos 1028], [pos 1059], [pos 1142], author-only flag [pos 1361].
- Setting (verbatim, `API-N200/PROOF.md` section 0):
  > Fix n ≥ 3, p ≥ 1, the standardised design X, the truth S₀ ∈ Ω, θ* and σ*² (hypothesis G: ε ~ N(0, σ*²I); P₀ is the law of y given X). Ω = {S ⊆ [p] : |S| ≤ K}, K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋). F(S) = log[ϖ(S)m(S)] is the exact score (EX-A). Let ≻ be T21's **total order** on Ω: S ≻ S′ iff F(S) > F(S′), or F(S) = F(S′) and |S| < |S′|, or F and size equal and S is lexicographically smaller. S† := max_≻ Ω is the global HPM (unique, by totality).
  >
  > The run: 𝒪 is the output-available event, U := 𝒪ᶜ. On 𝒪 the run has a nonempty scored set 𝒮 ⊆ Ω and reports Ŝ := max_≻ 𝒮 (the same total order; T21 §1). P is the joint law of data and algorithm randomness (EX-S), with data marginal P₀. Nothing below uses anything about *how* 𝒮 is produced: tables, pilot, final run, rejected proposals, scans. In particular no coupling, no SR, no CAL is needed for Theorem N200 itself; they enter only through the discovery bounds of T21 that one may plug into its last term.
  >
  > Three classes of fit with output (the S-ELS classification, made order-exact):
  > - **exact recovery:** Ŝ = S₀;
  > - **posterior miss:** Ŝ ≠ S₀ and Ŝ ≻ S₀;
  > - **search miss:** S₀ ≻ Ŝ.
  >
  > Since ≻ is total, on 𝒪 exactly one of the three holds. (With continuous noise, F-ties have P₀-probability zero, so "posterior miss" is a.s. the event {Ŝ ≠ S₀, F(Ŝ) ≥ F(S₀)} used by S-ELS, and "search miss" is a.s. {F(S₀) > F(Ŝ)}.)
- Statement (verbatim, section 2; proof paragraph omitted, see "Proof route"):
  > For every n, p, X, S₀, θ*, σ*², and every law of the algorithm's randomness:
  >
  > **(i) Identity.** P(U ∪ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) = P(U) + P(𝒪, posterior miss) + P(𝒪, search miss).
  >
  > **(ii) Upper bound.**
  >   P(U ∪ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≤ P(U) + P(𝒪, S† ≠ S₀) + P(𝒪, S₀ ∉ 𝒮) ≤ P(U) + **Π(X)** + P(𝒪, S₀ ∉ 𝒮),
  > where **Π(X) := P₀(S† ≠ S₀ | X)** is the *posterior-miss probability of the design*: a function of (X, θ*, σ*²) only, free of the algorithm.
  >
  > **(iii) Lower bound.**
  >   P(U ∪ {Ŝ ≠ S₀}) ≥ P(U) + P(𝒪, S† ≠ S₀) − P(𝒪, S† ∉ 𝒮).
  >
  > **(iv) Comparison with T21 (C1).** P(𝒪, S† ≠ S₀) ≤ P(𝒪, π(S₀) ≤ ½) ≤ P(π(S₀) ≤ ½) ≤ 2E₀δ₁, with δ₁ = 1 − π(S₀). So (ii) implies T21's C1 term by term, and is strictly sharper whenever P₀(S† ≠ S₀) < 2E₀δ₁. (At n = 200 the right side exceeds 1, see §4; the left side is 5–75% per cell.)
  >
  >
  > *Remarks.*
  > 1. The theorem is exact at every n and needs no hypothesis beyond EX-A (exact scores) and the definition of Ŝ as the ≻-maximum of the scored set. Floating point enters through O-CERT's score contract SC(η_F): under SC(η_F) replace "Ŝ ≻ S₀" by a margin 2η_F; S-ELS's smallest observed margin is 0.0049 nats, about 10⁶ times the measured η_F ≈ 3·10⁻¹².
  > 2. The three terms of (ii) are of different natures. P(U) is operational (resource limits); it is **measured**, not bounded. Π(X) is **statistical**: it is what Thm 1 (T03) drives to zero as n → ∞, and at n = 200 it is a computable quantity (§3). The discovery term is **algorithmic**: T21's routes (a)–(f) bound it a priori; at n = 200 those bounds are vacuous (§5) and the term is **measured per fit** (S-ELS: 0 of 2,394) and **certifiable per fit without S₀** (O-CERT C5).
  > 3. (iii) is new relative to T21 and is what justifies reading the observed miss rate as an estimate of Π(X): the observed rate is sandwiched between Π(X) − P(𝒪, S† ∉ 𝒮) − P(U) and Π(X) + P(𝒪, S₀ ∉ 𝒮) + P(U) (both correction terms are discovery terms).
  > 4. Nothing is claimed about PIPs or Ẑ.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none recorded; the theorem replaces the middle term 2 E0[delta1] of T21 (C1) by Pi(X). Floating point: "under SC(eta_F) replace 'S-hat after S0' by a margin 2 eta_F; S-ELS's smallest observed margin is 0.0049 nats, about 10^6 times the measured eta_F ~ 3e-12" (remark 1). The author's paper wording is quoted in CJ240.
- Status history: proposed and proved by API-N200 (Fable 5.1) "PROVED, elementary, every n"; Pi(X) upper bound "OPEN". No same-family verification and no cross-family review ("Self-checked flag: N200 author-only", `MEET-THM/REGISTRY_PAPER1.md` M5; registry row for N200 absent from `REGISTRY_v2.md`; `MEET-THM` status cell "N200: PROVED (elementary, every n); Pi(X) upper bound OPEN"). Author recommendation: "Independent check of Lemma 1 / Theorem N200 (elementary; a Lean formalisation next to T21HPM.lean is the natural check)".
- Proved by / checked by: API-N200 (Fable 5.1) only; the score contract SC(eta_F) was measured by O-CERT/O-VCERT (agreement 3e-12) and by W7-SEC (TH343).
- Proof route (Summary:) trichotomy of the total order gives (i); Lemma 1(a),(b) give (ii); Lemma 1(c) gives (iii); Lemma 1(d) with Markov gives (iv).
- Depends on: LM205, TH115 (T21) (total order and C1), EX-A, EX-S, G (Gaussian noise); LM188 (Lemma RO) not needed ("no coupling, no SR, no CAL is needed for Theorem N200 itself").
- Feeds: **M5 Theorem HPM** (K72, "composition at every n, N200": `MEET-THM/THEOREM_LIST_FINAL.md` card M5 (0) uses the order-exact composition; status cell "N200 author-only"); FUTURE_WORK **FW14** (K94 "finite-n bound on the posterior-miss probability Pi(X)": Envelope GAP) and **FW26** (finite-n Gibbs discovery, "ThmB-T24 vacuous at n = 200; no route").
- Notes / UNCERTAIN: the term the paper can compute is a *lower* bracket of Pi(X) (TH335); the data sandwich (iii) is what lets the observed miss rate be read as an estimate of Pi(X). T21's 2 E0 delta1 is vacuous at n = 200: "O-CERT (4 regenerated study fits): pi(S-hat) <= 0.37 even when S-hat = S0 ... so delta1 >= 0.63 on those fits and 2 delta1 >= 1.26" (PROOF section 4) while Pi(X) is 5-75% per cell; the exact p = 12 enumeration (CJ244) shows, in its nine tabulated rows, 2 E0 delta1 between 0.934 and 1.812 against Pi between 0.077 and 0.789 (the c = 0.35 rows of the results file have 2 E0 delta1 = 1.85-1.95 and Pi = 0.89-0.96).


### TH335 — Proposition 2 of API-N200 (brackets for the posterior-miss probability Pi(X))  [proposition]
- Source (authoritative): `API-N200/PROOF.md` section 3; `API-N200/REPORT.md` section 2. "This is O-SWAP's Theorem 4 with the chain of Hamming balls added" (TH340). Positions as TH334.
- Statement (verbatim, with the definitions that precede it):
  > Let 𝒩(S₀) be the one-move neighbourhood of S₀ (p − s₀ adds, s₀ drops, s₀(p − s₀) swaps), L := {∃S′ ∈ 𝒩(S₀): F(S′) > F(S₀)} the **one-move posterior-miss event**, and p_e := P₀(F(S_e) > F(S₀) | X) for each one-move event e. For d ≥ 1 let L_d := {∃S′ ≠ S₀, |S′ Δ S₀| ≤ d : F(S′) > F(S₀)}; L_1 ⊆ L = L_1 ∪ {swaps} ⊆ L_2.
  >
  > **Proposition 2 (brackets). PROVED (exact score, no PA).**
  >   max_e p_e ≤ P₀(L | X) ≤ P₀(L_2 | X) ≤ … ≤ Π(X),   and   P₀(L | X) ≤ Σ_e p_e.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none.
- Status history: author "PROVED (exact score, no PA)"; no external check. The evaluation of Pi(X): the lower bracket by exact-score Monte Carlo is "rigorous up to a binomial Monte Carlo error"; the closed forms p_e are "PA-exact, not rigorous" (an anti-concentration margin for the score gap at 0 is unwritten, CJ236); an upper bound on Pi(X) at n = 200 is OPEN (CJ230).
- Proved by / checked by: API-N200 only.
- Proof route (Summary:) every S' that beats S0 strictly gives S' above S0 in the total order, so S0 is not the global mode; monotonicity and the union bound.
- Depends on: TH334, TH340 (O-SWAP Theorem 4), TH336-TH339 for the closed forms.
- Feeds: FW14 (K94).


### O-SWAP block: common material (quoted once)

- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` (branch `theory/O-SWAP`, head 5b9b506), "Run: O-SWAP (Opus 5.5) ... Everything here is a **candidate**: not reviewed, not adopted." Positions: launch [pos 577] 18:49 UTC (brief: "GOAL: a finite-n quantitative theory that PREDICTS the posterior-miss rates"), mid-run [pos 578] ("T1 overpredicts S5 badly at c = 0.5 (84 against 49), so I'm waiting on the T2 test"), HQ framing [pos 594], finished by [pos 742].
- Headline status line (verbatim):
  > **Status:** Props 1–3 PROVED under the projection approximation PA (Lemma 0, PROVED; its error is O(10⁻³) nats). Thm 4, Prop. 5 and Prop. 6 PROVED. Cor. 2.1 PROOF SKETCH. Predictor T2 is an approximation. The SuSiE/SSL link is a CONJECTURE.
- Setting and notation (verbatim, `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 2):
  > Notation is that of `Docs/Theory/theorems/00_COMMON.md`. We fix the design X (standardised, ‖x_j‖² = n − 1), the truth S₀ (s₀ = |S₀|), and the coefficients θ on the X scale. In the study θ = c·β, where β has the pattern (1.4, −1, 1.8, −1.2, 0.8, −1.6) cycled over the 14 truths, c ∈ {1, 0.5}, and the noise sd is σ = 1. We write ỹ = C y^r = μ + Cε with μ = X_{S₀}θ and ε ~ N(0, σ²I). All probabilities are **conditional on X** and are over ε.
  >
  > F is invariant under y ↦ a·y except through the constant 2b₀ = 0.02. So we work on the raw contrast scale with b̃ := 2b₀ s_y². In every formula b̃ is replaced by its design-level value 2b₀ s̄_y², where s̄_y² = (‖μ‖² + (n − 1)σ²)/(n − 1). The resulting error in a log-score difference is at most ν·2b₀|s_y² − s̄_y²|/Q, which is below 10⁻³ nats here.
  >
  > New symbols (all deterministic given X):
  >
  > - For T ⊂ [p] and k ∉ T: r_{k|T} = (I − P_T)x_k. For a truth j, T_j := S₀ − j and r_j := r_{j|T_j}.
  > - For a swap pair (j, l): ρ_{jl} := cor(r_{j|T_j}, r_{l|T_j}), the partial correlation of x_j and x_l given the other truths.
  > - δ_j := θ_j‖r_j‖/σ = θ_j √((n−1)(1 − R²_{j|T_j}))/σ, the signal-to-noise of truth j given the other truths.
  > - Log determinant ratios use D_S = det H_S / det(G_S + I) exactly:
  >   - adding l: κ⁺_l := log(w(s₀)/w(s₀+1)) + ½ log(D_{S₀+l}/D_{S₀}) = log((2p−1−s₀)/(s₀+1)) + ½ log(D_{S₀+l}/D_{S₀});
  >   - dropping j: γ_j := log(w(s₀−1)/w(s₀)) + ½ log(D_{S₀}/D_{S₀−j}) = log((2p−s₀)/s₀) + ½ log(D_{S₀}/D_{S₀−j});
  >   - swapping j for l: κ_{jl} := ½ log(D_{S₀−j+l}/D_{S₀}). The size prior cancels exactly.
  > - λ := e^{κ/ν} for each κ, and ν = a₀ + n/2.
  > - Residual sums: E_A := ‖(I − P_A)ỹ‖², W_A := ‖P_A ỹ‖². The pseudo-observation terms are Ω₀ := E W_{S₀}/(n+1) + b̃ and Ω_j := E W_{T_j}/(n+1) + b̃, with ω = Ω/σ².
  > - **First-order (one-move) posterior-miss event:** L := {∃ S' ∈ 𝒩(S₀) : F(S') > F(S₀)}, where 𝒩(S₀) holds the p − s₀ adds, the s₀ drops and the s₀(p − s₀) swaps.
  >
  > At c = 1, Ω₀/σ² ≈ ‖μ‖²/(n+1) ≈ 24; at c = 0.5 it is ≈ 6. The τ = 1 pseudo-observation in H_S = (n+1)G_S + I leaves a fraction 1/(n+1) of the fitted sum of squares in Q_S. This acts as an **SNR-dependent extra size penalty** (Prop. 2).
- Cross-family review of all O-SWAP rates (A-REV9, verbatim):
  > O-SWAP rates: GAP. Its projection remainder formula is an exact algebraic identity, but replacing the fitted energy W_S0 by its expectation is an additional approximation beyond PA. In Proposition 2 the exact PA event uses E+W_S0/(n+1)+btilde, whereas the displayed law uses deterministic Omega0. W_S0 is a nondegenerate noncentral chi-square quantity; varying the Gaussian component in span(X_S0) changes the exact threshold while keeping the orthogonal residual components fixed. Thus the displayed event identity is ERROR if asserted under PA alone. Restore the random fitted-energy term and integrate it, or explicitly label the extra approximation. A random Gaussian quadratic-form error is not uniformly bounded by 10^-3 nats merely because a typical error is small. The predicted aggregate rates and regenerated-data agreement require a separate saved-output/data-provenance audit; they are not LOCKABLE here.
- Registry (`T38-RECORD/REGISTRY_v2.md` section B, "finite-n theory of posterior misses (O-SWAP; unverified)"): `OSWAP-L0` PROVED / none / none; `OSWAP-P1`, `OSWAP-P2`, `OSWAP-P3` PROVED-UNDER / none / **GAP** (A-REV9: "predicted rates GAP (additional approximations and data reproduction remain; PA alone does not give the displayed add law)"); `OSWAP-T4` PROVED / none / none; `OSWAP-P5` PROVED / none / none. `LOCKABLE_v2.md` section 3e ("Headline items with NO verification at all (author only)") lists `OSWAP-L0`, `OSWAP-T4`, `OSWAP-P5`; `OSWAP-P1/P2/P3` are in the GAP list. No O-SWAP item has an SF verification (no O-V* branch was launched for it).
- Label note: the report numbers Lemma 0, Props 1, 2, 3, Theorem 4, Props 5, 6 and Corollary 2.1 (there is no Proposition 4); the registry uses OSWAP-L0, -P1, -P2, -P3, -T4, -P5; Prop. 6 has no registry row.


### LM208 — Lemma 0 of O-SWAP (OSWAP-L0; projection approximation PA)  [lemma]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3, "Lemma 0 (projection approximation PA). PROVED." Positions as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > Write G_S = VΛVᵀ and X_S = U Λ^{1/2} Vᵀ, where UᵀU = I and P_S = UUᵀ. Then
  >
  >   Q_S = Q̃_S + η_S,  with Q̃_S := E_S + W_S/(n+1) and η_S = Σ_i n (u_iᵀỹ)² / ((n+1)((n+1)λ_i + 1)) ∈ [0, n W_S/((n+1)((n+1)λ_min(G_S)+1))].
- Following text (verbatim; defines what "under PA" means for the later results):
  > To first order, η_S ≈ ‖θ̂_S‖²·n/(n+1)², where θ̂_S is the OLS coefficient vector. The error it induces in a one-move log-score difference is ν(η_{S'} − η_{S₀})/Q ≈ (θ̂²_{in} − θ̂²_{out})/(2σ²(n−s₀)), which is O(10⁻³) nats in this study. Every analytic statement below is exact for the score with Q replaced by Q̃ (call it F̃). The conditional Monte Carlo of §4 uses the **exact** F, so the PA is checked empirically.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none. A-REV9 notes that PA replaces Q by Q-tilde and is exact algebra, but "replacing the fitted energy W_S0 by its expectation is an additional approximation beyond PA" (see TH337) and "A random Gaussian quadratic-form error is not uniformly bounded by 10^-3 nats merely because a typical error is small".
- Status history: author PROVED; no SF check; no XF verdict on the lemma itself (A-REV9: "Its projection remainder formula is an exact algebraic identity"). Registry `OSWAP-L0`: PROVED / none / none.
- Proved by / checked by: O-SWAP only.
- Proof route (Summary:) spectral form n X_S H_S^-1 X_S' = U diag(n lambda_i/((n+1) lambda_i + 1)) U'.
- Depends on: ⟦00_COMMON score⟧.
- Feeds: none (campaign-only).
- Notes: the engine-level cross-check of the score is `scripts/check_score_local.py`: "max |difference| = 8.5e-13 over 60 comparisons" (O-SWAP section 4.4).


### TH336 — Proposition 1 of O-SWAP (OSWAP-P1; within-size swap)  [proposition]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3 Proposition 1, "PROVED under PA". Positions as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof paragraph omitted):
  > Fix a truth j and a null l. Set A := r_jᵀỹ/‖r_j‖ and B := r_{l|T_j}ᵀỹ/‖r_{l|T_j}‖. Then (A, B) ~ N(σ(δ_j, ρδ_j), σ²[[1, ρ],[ρ, 1]]) with ρ = ρ_{jl}. Let U = S₀ ∪ {l}, E_U ~ σ²χ²_{n−2−s₀}, and W_{T_j}. These three are mutually independent and independent of (A, B). Then
  >
  >   {F̃(S₀ − j + l) > F̃(S₀)} = { (n/(n+1))(λ B² − A²) > (λ − 1)(E_U + ‖v‖² + W_{T_j}/(n+1) + b̃) },  where λ = e^{κ_{jl}/ν} and ‖v‖² = (A² − 2ρAB + B²)/(1 − ρ²).
  >
  > In particular, when κ_{jl} = 0 (to first order κ_{jl} = O(1/n); see the remark),
  >
  >   **P_swap(j, l) = Φ(−d₋)Φ(d₊) + Φ(d₋)Φ(−d₊),  d∓ := |δ_j| √((1 ∓ ρ)/2)**,
  >
  > and Φ(−d₋)Φ(d₊) ≤ P_swap ≤ Φ(−d₋) + Φ(−d₊). For ρ > 0 and δ_j → ∞, P_swap ~ Φ(−d₋).
- Quadrature, remark and margin link (verbatim):
  > The general-λ probability is computed exactly by a Gauss–Hermite integral over the s-coordinate and a closed-form interval in the d-coordinate (`scripts/analytic.py::p_swap`; it agrees with direct MC to 3 decimals in `scripts/test_analytic.py`). There E_U is replaced by its mean. The error this causes is at most |λ − 1|·σ²√(2(n−2−s₀)) ≈ 0.03σ².
  >
  > *Remark (κ_{jl} is small but not negligible).* In this study |κ_{jl}| ≲ 0.3 nats. That moves P_swap by up to about 15 % relative (e.g. δ = 4, ρ = 0.85: 0.137 at λ = 1 versus 0.116 at λ = 1.002), so the predictions use the exact κ_{jl}.
  >
  > *Margin link to W1-T37R.* The mean log-score gap is M_{jl} := E[A² − B²]/(2σ²) = δ_j²(1 − ρ²)/2 = (n−1)θ_j²(1 − R²_{j|T_j})(1 − ρ²)/(2σ²). This is T37R's margin, with the partial R² factor added. The miss probability is governed by d₋² = M_{jl}/(1 + ρ), not by M_{jl}: **P_swap ≈ Φ̄(√(M_{jl}/(1+ρ)))**.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none. A-REV9: GAP on the predicted rates built from Props 1-3; the independent second reader requested by O-SWAP (section 7 item 1: "Prop. 1, step 2 (the decomposition of Q-tilde_{T+k} through the 2-dimensional projection v), and the general-lambda quadratic in analytic.py::p_swap") has not happened.
- Status history: author "PROVED under PA" -> no SF -> XF A-REV9 "GAP". Registry `OSWAP-P1`: PROVED-UNDER / none / GAP.
- Proved by / checked by: O-SWAP only; numerical validation: "P_swap (general lambda) against direct MC (400,000 draws), to within 0.001 in all 5 test points; for example delta = 4, rho = 0.85, lambda = 1.002 gives 0.1160 by quadrature and 0.1163 by MC".
- Depends on: LM208 (PA), TH106 (T07) ("Prop. 1 contains no size-prior term: the size prior cancels exactly in a within-size swap. This is T07's Prop. 1 in quantitative form"), ⟦W1-T37R margin⟧ (the mean log-score gap M_jl = delta_j^2 (1 - rho^2)/2 is T37R's margin with the partial R^2 factor added).
- Feeds: none (campaign-only).


### TH337 — Proposition 2 of O-SWAP (OSWAP-P2; superset by one null)  [proposition]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3 Proposition 2, "PROVED under PA". Positions as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof omitted):
  > For a null l, let u_l = r_{l|S₀}/‖r_{l|S₀}‖ and B_l := u_lᵀỹ. B_l ~ N(0, σ²) exactly, for every design and every θ. Let E := E_{S₀} ~ σ²χ²_{n−1−s₀}. Then
  >
  >   {F̃(S₀ + l) > F̃(S₀)} = { B_l² / (E + Ω₀) > τ_l },  τ_l := (n+1)(1 − e^{−κ⁺_l/ν})/n.
  >
  > Hence, with E' := E − B_l² ~ σ²χ²_{n−2−s₀} independent of B_l,
  >
  >   **P_add(l) = P( χ²₁ (1 − λ_l/(n+1)) > (λ_l − 1)(χ²_{n−2−s₀} + ω₀) )**,  λ_l = e^{κ⁺_l/ν}.
  >
  > Under the same PA, the union over nulls is exactly {max_l B_l²/τ_l > E + Ω₀}, where (B_l/σ)_l ~ N(0, Γ) with Γ_{ll'} = u_lᵀu_{l'}.
- Consequences (verbatim):
  > *Consequences.*
  > - (i) P_add(l) depends on the design only through κ⁺_l. For every l, κ⁺_l ≈ ½ log(n+1) + log((2p−1−s₀)/(s₀+1)), which is 6.83 at p = 500 and 7.54 at p = 1000. It depends on the signal only through ω₀ ≈ ‖μ‖²/((n+1)σ²).
  > - (ii) **The superset rate is essentially scenario-free.** For nearly orthogonal u_l, P(superset) ≈ 1 − (1 − q)^{p−s₀}, where q = P_add: 1.5–3.0 × 10⁻⁴ at p = 500 and 0.7–1.5 × 10⁻⁴ at p = 1000 (Cor. 2.1). Correlated nulls (S2–S6) lower the effective count.
  > - (iii) Lowering the SNR from c = 1 to c = 0.5 lowers ω₀ from ≈ 24 to ≈ 6. That lowers the effective χ²₁ threshold by about 9 % and raises q by about 2× (Cor. 2.1).
- Earlier versions / repairs: A-REV9 identifies a defect in the *displayed* event (RF242, CE193): "In Proposition 2 the exact PA event uses E + W_S0/(n+1) + b-tilde, whereas the displayed law uses deterministic Omega0. W_S0 is a nondegenerate noncentral chi-square quantity; ... Thus the displayed event identity is ERROR if asserted under PA alone. Restore the random fitted-energy term and integrate it, or explicitly label the extra approximation." The statement above defines Omega_0 := E W_S0/(n+1) + b-tilde (expectation of W_S0), which is the extra approximation; the O-SWAP headline ("Props 1-3 PROVED under PA") does not label it.
- Status history: author "PROVED under PA" -> no SF -> XF A-REV9 "GAP" (and ERROR for the displayed identity under PA alone). Registry `OSWAP-P2`: PROVED-UNDER / none / GAP.
- Proved by / checked by: O-SWAP only; P_add: "3.10e-4 against 2.65e-4 +- 0.26e-4 (MC SE), which is 1.7 SE".
- Depends on: LM208; the user-visible quantity kappa_plus = log(w(s0)/w(s0+1)) + (1/2) log(D_{S0+l}/D_{S0}).
- Feeds: none (campaign-only).


### TH338 — Corollary 2.1 of O-SWAP (superset rate is p-free and rises as the signal falls)  [corollary]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3 Corollary 2.1, "PROOF SKETCH (expansion); the numbers are exact evaluations of Prop. 2". Positions as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim, including the table):
  > Let t_add be the root of P_add: the event of Prop. 2 is |B_l|/σ > t_add·√((E + Ω₀)/(σ²(n − 2 − s₀ + ω₀))) ≈ t_add, with
  >
  >   t_add² = (λ − 1)(n − 2 − s₀ + ω₀)/(1 − λ/(n+1)) = 2κ⁺(1 + η)(1 + O(κ⁺/n)),  η := (ω₀ − s₀ − 2)/n.
  >
  > With κ⁺ = ½ log(n+1) + log((2p − 1 − s₀)/(s₀ + 1)) + O(1/n),
  >
  >   log[(p − s₀)q] ≈ log[(p − s₀)·2φ(t_add)/t_add] = −η log(2p) − ½(1+η) log(n+1) + (1+η) log(s₀+1) − log t_add − ½ log(2π) + o(1).
  >
  > The step uses log(p − s₀) − log(2p − 1 − s₀) = −log 2 + o(1), which cancels the factor 2 of the two-sided tail.
  >
  > So the family-wise superset rate 1 − (1 − q)^{p−s₀} depends on p only through p^{−η}/t_add, with |η| < 0.05 here. **The BB(1, p) term log((2p−k−1)/(k+1)) cancels the multiplicity of the nulls almost exactly.** The SNR enters through ω₀ ≈ ‖μ‖²/((n+1)σ²): the pseudo-observation's share of the fitted sum of squares raises the threshold when the signal is strong.
  >
  > | | κ⁺ | γ (drop) | t_add (σ units) | q per null | 1 − (1 − q)^{p−s₀} | t_drop |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  > | p = 500, c = 1 (ω₀ ≈ 24.6) | 6.84 | 6.91 | 3.85 | 1.51 × 10⁻⁴ | 0.071 | 3.88 |
  > | p = 500, c = 0.5 (ω₀ ≈ 6.2) | 6.84 | 6.91 | 3.68 | 3.03 × 10⁻⁴ | 0.137 | 3.71 |
  > | p = 1000, c = 1 | 7.54 | 7.61 | 4.05 | 6.88 × 10⁻⁵ | 0.066 | 4.08 |
  > | p = 1000, c = 0.5 | 7.54 | 7.61 | 3.87 | 1.48 × 10⁻⁴ | 0.136 | 3.90 |
  >
  > (ω₀ is the design average, and the κ's here are the leading-order values; the cell predictions in §4 use the exact per-design values.) The independence value 1 − (1 − q)^{p−s₀} is an upper-type approximation: correlated nulls (S2–S6) lower the effective number of independent competitors.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none.
- Status history: author "PROOF SKETCH"; no review. Inherits the A-REV9 GAP of the Prop. 2 event (TH337). Registry has no separate row (grouped with OSWAP-P2).
- Proved by / checked by: O-SWAP only.
- Depends on: TH337.
- Feeds: none (campaign-only). The "superset rate is scenario-free" reading reproduces the observed extra-only counts at c = 1 (3-6 per 100 everywhere except S5) in the author's section 5.

### TH341 — Proposition 5 of O-SWAP (OSWAP-P5; the swap ceiling is information-theoretic)  [proposition]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3 Proposition 5, "PROVED (standard two-point bound)". Positions as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof omitted) and the connection to T07 (verbatim):
  > Fix (j, l) and let μ' := P_{S₀−j+l} μ be the closest mean supported on S' = S₀ − j + l. Then ‖μ − μ'‖ = σ|δ_j|√(1 − ρ²), and for **any** selector Ŝ (any prior, any method),
  >
  >   ½[P_μ(Ŝ ≠ S₀) + P_{μ'}(Ŝ ≠ S')] ≥ Φ(−|δ_j|√(1 − ρ²)/2).
  >
  > The HPM's own swap error is P_swap ≈ Φ(−|δ_j|√((1−ρ)/2)). The squared exponents differ by a factor (1 + ρ)/2, which tends to 1 as ρ → 1.
  > *Connection to T07.* Prop. 1 contains no size-prior term: the size prior cancels exactly in a within-size swap. This is T07's Prop. 1 in quantitative form. The swap probability also changes with g only through κ_{jl} = O(1/n). Prop. 5 says more: for look-alikes (ρ ≈ 0.85, as in S4), no method can push the averaged swap error much below the HPM's. The numbers are δ = 5.4, ρ = 0.85: the HPM gives Φ(−1.49) = 0.068 and the two-point bound gives Φ(−1.43) = 0.076.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none. The quantitative qualification the author states: "It is a pairwise floor and lies far below the whole-model miss rate. A whole-model floor (Assouad/Fano over the 14 truths and their look-alikes) is OPEN" (CJ233).

T07 proves that no size-only prior can fix this ... a ceiling for every method using this posterior").

### TH342 — Proposition 6 of O-SWAP (conditional representation of a truth's competitor cluster) and predictor T2  [proposition]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3 Proposition 6, "PROVED (exact, no PA). Predictor T2: approximation." Positions as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof omitted):
  > Fix a truth j and write A_j := r_jᵀỹ/‖r_j‖ and B_{jl} := r_{l|T_j}ᵀỹ/‖r_{l|T_j}‖ (Prop. 1). Then, for every null l,
  >
  >   B_{jl} = ρ_{jl} A_j + √(1 − ρ²_{jl}) Z_{jl},  with Z_{jl} ~ N(0, σ²) independent of A_j,
  >
  > and the Z_{jl} are **central**: their mean is 0 whatever θ is.
- Consequence and the predictor T2 with its three approximations (verbatim):
  > *Consequence (the cluster event).* Under PA and with λ ≡ 1, the event that truth j is lost to a one-move competitor (a drop or any swap (j, l)) is
  >
  >   {A_j² < t_j²(E)} ∪ {max_l |ρ_{jl}A_j + √(1−ρ²_{jl})Z_{jl}| > |A_j|}.
  >
  > Conditional on A_j, its probability is driven by the signs and sizes of the ρ_{jl}, and the large-|ρ| competitors (the group-mates in S3–S6) dominate. For a single competitor this reduces to Prop. 1.
  >
  > **Predictor T2** evaluates P(L) as E_E[ Π_l (1 − q_l(E)) · Π_j (1 − P_j(E)) ]. Here E is the common residual χ²_{n−1−s₀}, q_l(E) is the add probability of Prop. 2 given E, and
  >
  >   P_j(E) = 1 − E_{A_j}[ 1{A_j ∉ drop region(E)} · Π_l P(B_{jl}² ≤ thr_{jl}(A_j) | A_j) ],
  >
  > with the exact κ's (`scripts/t2.py`). T2 makes three approximations:
  > - (a) the Z_{jl} are taken as independent across l given A_j (they are correlated through the partial correlations of the nulls);
  > - (b) the clusters (the add block and each truth) are taken as independent given E;
  > - (c) inside the O(λ − 1) terms, ‖v‖² ≈ A² + σ², the swap thresholds use E at its mean, and E_U, E', E_{S₀} are identified (each error is O(10⁻³) in probability).
  >
  > It is an approximation, not a bound. A Šidák/Royen-type inequality does not apply directly: the slabs in (a) are not centred, and E is not independent of the B_l. Its accuracy is measured against the exact-score MC in §4.
- Earlier versions / repairs: T2 repairs the T1 overshoot (RF248). A rigorous version of T2 is OPEN (CJ232).
- Status history: Prop. 6 author PROVED (no registry row, no review); T2 explicitly "an approximation, not a bound". - Hypotheses, notation and cited lemmas (verbatim, `PROOF_T33.md` section 0):
  > - **Stored data.** X̂ (n×p) and ŷ (n) are the doubles the C++ context holds after `v3_preprocess`. All "exact"
  >   quantities below are computed **exactly from these doubles**: G := X̂ᵀX̂, z := X̂ᵀŷ, y′y := ŷᵀŷ, H_S, A_S := G_S + I,
  >   Q_S, log m(S), F(S), with the method's exact constants (a₀ = b₀ = 1/100, exact lgamma). Preprocessing error (the
  >   map raw → stored) is a separate data perturbation; it is not bounded here (see §6).
  > - **Computed.** Ĝ, ẑ, ŷtŷ (`data_init`), and log m̂(S), F̂(S) from `Scorer::score` (route `chol` unless stated).
  >
  > **New symbols.** u := 2⁻⁵³; γ_j := ju/(1 − ju); γ′_j := γ_j/(1 − γ_j). For S with |S| = k ≥ 1:
  > g_S := max_{a∈S} G_aa (= n − 1 for standardised columns); h_S := (n+1)g_S + 1; a_S := g_S + 1;
  > λ_H := λ_min(H_S), λ_A := λ_min(A_S), κ_H := λ_max(H_S)/λ_H, κ_A likewise; ν = 0.01 + n/2.
  >
  > **Hypotheses (named).**
  > - FP: IEEE-754 binary64 with round-to-nearest; the standard model fl(a ∘ b) = (a ∘ b)(1 + δ), |δ| ≤ u, for
  >   +, −, ×, /, √ (true for the production flags; FMA contraction is off). NOUF: no overflow or underflow occurs.
  > - LIB(c_L): `std::log` satisfies fl(log x) = log(x)(1 + δ), |δ| ≤ c_L u (glibc documents ≤ 1 ulp, so c_L = 2 is safe).
  > - SMALL: (n + 3K + 4)u ≤ 10⁻³ (so every γ_j used is ≤ 1.001ju and every product of (1 + γ) factors is ≤ 1.003).
  > - The constants log C_n and log ϖ(k) computed once in `data_init` have errors η_C := |log Ĉ_n − log C_n| and
  >   η_π(k) := |log ϖ̂(k) − log ϖ(k)|. They are not bounded a priori (lgamma accuracy is not specified by IEEE); they are
  >   measured once per (n, p) (≤ 1.8·10⁻¹² at n = 4000 and ≤ 1.1·10⁻¹³ at p ≤ 60 in `results/t33_fp_check.txt`).
  >
  > **Cited lemmas** (standard; statements as in Higham, *Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms*, 2nd ed., 2002).
  > - (H1) Thm 10.3: if Cholesky runs to completion on a symmetric A of order k, the computed factor satisfies
  >   L̂L̂ᵀ = A + ΔA, |ΔA| ≤ γ_{k+1}|L̂||L̂ᵀ|. (Holds for any order of evaluating the inner products; `chol_inplace` is the
  >   inner-product (jik/Crout) form.)
  > - (H2) Thm 8.5: substitution for a triangular system gives (L̂ + ΔL)ŵ = b, |ΔL| ≤ γ_k|L̂|.
  > - (H3) Thm 10.7 (Demmel): if A is SPD, D = diag(a_ii)^{1/2} and λ_min(D⁻¹AD⁻¹) > kγ_{k+1}/(1 − γ_{k+1}), Cholesky
  >   runs to completion (barring underflow/overflow).
  > - (H4) Recursive summation of k terms has absolute error ≤ γ_{k−1}Σ|terms|; an inner product of length n has
  >   |fl(xᵀy) − xᵀy| ≤ γ_n|x|ᵀ|y|.
