### LM206 — Lemma T33-M (= T33(i), generalised)  [lemma]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T33.md` section 1. Positions as the W7-SEC block.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Lemma T33-M (= T33(i), generalised).** For every S with |S| = k ≥ 1 and any real data,
  > I ≼ A_S ≼ (1 + tr G_S)I and I ≼ H_S ≼ (1 + (n+1)tr G_S)I. With standardised columns, tr G_S = (n−1)k, which is
  > T33(i): I ≼ H_S ≼ [1 + (n+1)(n−1)k]I. Hence κ_H ≤ 1 + (n+1)k g_S and κ_A ≤ 1 + k g_S, **also with duplicate columns**,
  > and exact Cholesky never fails.
  >

- Earlier versions / repairs: generalises the pre-campaign T33(i) (conjectured) to arbitrary data and to duplicate columns (the lower bound I <= A_S, H_S and explicit condition numbers).
- Status history: W7-SEC "PROVED" (author's check only; registry `T33-M`: PROVED / none / A-REV9 deferred). Proof: G_S >= 0 and lambda_max(G_S) <= tr G_S.
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEC only.
- Depends on: CJ113 (T33) (i).
- Feeds: none (supplement remark); used in TH343 and TH344.


### LM207 — Lemma T33-Q (Q_S >= y'y/(n+1))  [lemma]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T33.md` section 1. Positions as the W7-SEC block.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **Lemma T33-Q (new).** For every S and any real data, Q_S ≥ y′y − (n/(n+1))‖P_Sŷ‖² ≥ y′y/(n+1), where P_S is the
  > orthogonal projection onto col(X̂_S).
  >
  > **Consequences.** (a) y′y/Q_S ≤ n + 1: the cancellation in Q_S = y′y − n z′H⁻¹z costs at most a factor n + 1.
  > (b) The engine's switch to the non-negative form (`v3_score.h:219`, Q < 10⁻⁸y′y) is never triggered in exact
  > arithmetic when n + 1 < 10⁸; in floating point see Corollary T33-NF. (c) Checked: min_S Q_S(n+1)/y′y ranges from
  > 1.0099 (D4, y almost in the span) to 233 over all tested models (`results/t33_fp_check.txt`).
- Earlier versions / repairs: none. The same inequality is the free corollary of O-CERT Lemma M(d) found by O-VCERT (LM204): Q_S >= y'y/(n+1), so "the trigger Q < 10^-8 y'y can never fire in exact arithmetic when n + 1 < 10^8; the branch is a pure floating-point safeguard". Two independent derivations (push-through identity in LM204; Loewner comparison B >= A in LM207) of the same bound.
- Status history: W7-SEC "PROVED" (author's check only). Registry `T33-M` covers "Lemmas T33-M, T33-Q: PROVED / none / A-REV9 deferred". Numerical check: "min over models of (n+1) Q_S / y'y ranges from 1.0099 (D4, y almost in the span) to 233 over all tested models".
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEC only (agreement with O-VCERT's corollary noted here, not in either report).
- Depends on: Loewner order only.
- Feeds: none directly; used in TH343 (r_Q, theta_Q) and TH344.
- Notes: `q_nonneg` fallback is "dead code for n + 1 < 10^7 under the hypotheses of Cor T33-NF" (W7-SEC section 7).


### TH343 — Theorem T33-S (deterministic floating-point error bound for one score, Cholesky route)  [theorem]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T33.md` section 2 (statement) and `W7-SEC/REPORT.md` section 2 (summary). Positions as the W7-SEC block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof steps 1-8 omitted):
  > ## 2. Theorem T33-S (deterministic error bound for one score, Cholesky route). **PROVED** (given H1–H4, FP, NOUF, LIB, SMALL).
  >
  > Fix S with |S| = k ≥ 1. Define
  > - ε_H := 1.01·k·h_S·(n + k + 3)u,  ε_A := 1.01·k·a_S·(n + k + 2)u,  ε_Q := 1.02·k·h_S·(n + 3k + 3)u;
  > - ρ_H := ε_H/λ_H, ρ_A := ε_A/λ_A, ρ_Q := ε_Q/λ_H;
  > - ω := γ_n·√(n·k·g_S/λ_H);
  > - r_Q := γ_n + 2.03u + [(ρ_Q + γ_k)/(1 − ρ_Q)](1 + ω)² + 2ω + ω²;  θ_Q := (y′y/Q_S)·r_Q;
  > - ℓ_H := log(1.01h_S) + 1, ℓ_A := log(1.01a_S) + 1; L_S := |log(2b₀ + Q_S)|; log D_S = log det H_S − log det A_S.
  >
  > Assume ε_H, ε_A, ε_Q ≤ ½ and θ_Q ≤ ½. Then:
  > (a) both Cholesky factorisations in `try_chol` (stored-Gram route) run to completion, so `score` returns on route
  >     `chol` (no refactor, no QR, no numerical_failure);
  > (b) |l̂dH − log det H_S| ≤ η_H := kρ_H/(1 − ρ_H) + 1.01(k − 1 + c_L)k u ℓ_H, and likewise η_A for A_S;
  > (c) |Q̂_S − Q_S| ≤ y′y·r_Q, so |Q̂_S/Q_S − 1| ≤ θ_Q ≤ (n+1)r_Q;
  > (d) |log m̂(S) − log m(S)| ≤ η_m(S) := ½(η_H + η_A) + η_Q + η_asm + η_C, where
  >     η_Q := ν[θ_Q/(1 − θ_Q) + 1.01u] + 1.01(c_L + 2.01)u·νL_S and η_asm := 1.01u(2|log C_n| + 2 log D_S + νL_S);
  > (e) |F̂(S) − F(S)| ≤ η_F(S) := η_m(S) + η_π(k) + 1.01u(|log ϖ(k)| + |log m(S)|).
  > For k = 0, |log m̂(∅) − log m(∅)| ≤ η_C + ν(γ_n + 2.03u)(y′y/(2b₀+y′y)) + 1.01(c_L + 2.01)uνL_∅ + 1.01u|log m(∅)|.
  >
  > **Condition-number form.** Since h_S ≤ λ_max(H_S) and a_S ≤ λ_max(A_S),
  > ρ_H ≤ 1.01k(n+k+3)u·κ_H, ρ_A ≤ 1.01k(n+k+2)u·κ_A, ρ_Q ≤ 1.02k(n+3k+3)u·κ_H, so to first order in u
  >   |log m̂(S) − log m(S)| ≲ ½k²(n+k)u(κ_H + κ_A) + ν(y′y/Q_S)[k(n+3k)uκ_H + nu(1 + 2√(nkg_S/λ_H))] + u(2|log C_n| + 2 log D_S + νL_S) + η_C.
  > **Universal (data-free) form.** λ_H, λ_A ≥ 1 and y′y/Q_S ≤ n + 1 (Lemmas T33-M, T33-Q) give a bound depending on
  > (n, k, g_S) only. At n = 200, k = K = 100 it allows η_Q ≈ 4.6·10⁻³ nats (the worst case needs κ_H = kn² and
  > y′y/Q = n + 1 at once); at n = 1000, K = 500 it is vacuous (≈ 80 nats) (`results/t33_valfp_budget.txt`). The
  > a-posteriori form with the model's λ_H and y′y/Q_S is the useful one (≈ 10⁻⁹–10⁻⁸ on the tested models, observed
  > errors ≈ 10⁻¹³–10⁻¹¹; `results/t33_fp_check.txt`).
- Earlier versions / repairs: none. Cited lemmas H1-H4 are from Higham (2002); W7-SEC section 6 item 1: "I used it [Demmel's criterion, Higham Thm 10.7] from memory. A reader with the book should confirm the statement and its constant; if the constant differs, only the factor in Cor T33-NF moves."
- Status history: W7-SEC "PROVED (given H1-H4, FP, NOUF, LIB, SMALL)"; registry `T33-S`: PROVED-UNDER ("Higham H1-H4 (cited from memory), FP, NOUF, LIB, SMALL"); XF none (A-REV9 deferred: "I did not audit PROOF_T05, PROOF_T33, the floating-point library hypotheses, or the complete cost recount").
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEC only. Numerical validation (verbatim table, `REPORT.md` section 4.2): the production scorer compiled from the unmodified `v3_score.h` against a 60-digit reference:
  > - `results/t33_fp_check.txt`: the production scorer (compiled from the unmodified `v3_score.h` with the production
  >   flags) against a 60-digit reference with an exact integer Gram, on the stored doubles. Designs: iid (n = 200),
  >   near-collinear pairs (ρ ≈ 1 − 10⁻¹⁴), exact duplicates, y almost in the span (y′y/Q = 100 = n), and n = 4,000.
  >
  >   | design | max \|Δlog m\| | max \|Δlog m\| / η_m (rigorous) | / η_eng (heuristic) | route / Q-recompute |
  >   |---|---|---|---|---|
  >   | D1 iid n=200 | 1.3·10⁻¹³ | 7.6·10⁻³ | 5.9·10⁻³ | chol only / 0 |
  >   | D2 near-collinear | 1.0·10⁻¹¹ | 7.3·10⁻³ | 6.3·10⁻³ | chol only / 0 |
  >   | D3 duplicates | 4.9·10⁻¹³ | 9.3·10⁻⁶ | 1.3·10⁻⁵ | chol only / 0 |
  >   | D4 y′y/Q = n | 7.3·10⁻¹³ | 8.4·10⁻³ | 3.9·10⁻³ | chol only / 0 |
  >   | D5 n = 4000 | 1.3·10⁻¹⁰ | 2.6·10⁻³ | 4.2·10⁻² | chol only / 0 |
  >
  >   The constants have errors |log Ĉ_n − log C_n| ≤ 1.8·10⁻¹² and |log ϖ̂ − log ϖ| ≤ 1.1·10⁻¹³. Lemma T33-Q held in
  >   every case (min (n+1)Q/y′y = 1.0099).
- Depends on: LM206, LM207, TH299 (VAL-FP) (W2-BOOK Prop 2(f)).
- Feeds: FUTURE_WORK FW16 (K107) as the exact-arithmetic-versus-machine caveat: "exact-arithmetic bounds do not validate rounded production computations".
- Notes / UNCERTAIN: the data-free (universal) form allows eta_Q ~ 4.6e-3 nats at n = 200, k = K = 100 and is vacuous (~80 nats) at n = 1000, K = 500; the a-posteriori form is about 1e-9 to 1e-8 against observed errors 1e-13 to 1e-11 ("~10^2 x above the observed errors. That is the usual price of worst-case (n u) dot-product bounds").


### TH344 — Corollary T33-NF (numerical_failure and the Q fallback are impossible at moderate sizes, including n = 200)  [corollary]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T33.md` section 2; `REPORT.md` section 1 item 2. Positions as the W7-SEC block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof omitted):
  > ### Corollary T33-NF (numerical_failure and the Q fallback are impossible at moderate sizes). **PROVED.**
  > Under FP, NOUF, LIB, SMALL, suppose for every feasible S (|S| ≤ K) that ε_H, ε_A, ε_Q ≤ ½ and (n+1)r_Q ≤ ½, and that
  > n + 1 ≤ 10⁷. Then every call of `Scorer::score` returns on route `chol` with `q_recomputed = false`. In particular
  > **the status numerical_failure can never occur** (the scorer is its only source: `v3_core.cpp` setup tables, V,
  > inherited and final-run rescoring, and `Engine::eval` all call `Scorer::score`).
- Earlier versions / repairs: reformulates pre-campaign T33(iii)'s requirement ("no probability-zero statement for numerical_failure") as an impossibility statement under FP/LIB: "under FP/LIB it is not probability zero but impossible, for these sizes".
- Status history: W7-SEC "PROVED" (author only). A-REV9 (verbatim): "In particular I do not endorse 'numerical_failure impossible for every p,y' without its stated FP/NOUF/LIB/SMALL domain."
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEC only. Largest n for the a-priori hypotheses (`t33_valfp_budget.txt`): 1,286 (K = n/2), 4,575 (K = 10), 8,149 (K = 1).
- Depends on: TH343, LM207.

### TH345 — Proposition T33-H (HPM decisions and ties on a common scored set)  [proposition]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T33.md` section 3. Positions as the W7-SEC block.
- Statement (verbatim; proof omitted):
  > ## 3. Proposition T33-H (HPM decisions and ties on a common scored set). **PROVED.**
  >
  > Let 𝒮 be a set of models scored with the same computed values in both runs being compared, S* its exact HPM
  > (00_COMMON tie rule) and η̄′ := max_{S∈𝒮}[η_F(S) − η_C]. (The constant log Ĉ_n is the same double in every score, so
  > its error cancels from every difference F̂(S) − F̂(S′).)
  > (a) The computed HPM Ŝ^fp over 𝒮 lies in the near-tie set 𝒩 := {S ∈ 𝒮 : F(S) ≥ F(S*) − 2η̄′}.
  > (b) If F(S*) − max_{S∈𝒮∖S*}F(S) > 2η̄′ then Ŝ^fp = S*.
  > (c) Exact ties: if F(S*) = F(S′) for some S′ ≠ S* (e.g. T06 ties, X_SX_Sᵀ = X_{S′}X_{S′}ᵀ), the computed winner is
  >     decided by rounding, not by the tie rule, unless F̂(S*) and F̂(S′) are bitwise equal. The tie rule is implemented
  >     faithfully only among bitwise-equal computed scores (the cache and the deterministic scorer guarantee that the
  >     same model always gets the same bits, `v3_score.h:252–254`).
  > (d) If S₀ ∈ 𝒮 and F(S₀) − max_{S≠S₀}F(S) ≥ m_n with m_n > 2η̄′, then Ŝ^fp = S₀. T03's candidate margin is
  >     ½log n − ½log log n − O_P(1). At n = 200 even the data-free bound gives 2η̄′ ≲ 10⁻² for every |S| ≤ 100, and the
  >     a-posteriori bound gives ~10⁻⁸; so T33(ii)'s requirement η = o(log n) is met with a lot of room wherever
  >     Theorem T33-S applies with its a-posteriori constants.
- Earlier versions / repairs: none; this is the quantitative form of pre-campaign T33(ii). The remark that follows in the source (R9 `global_certified` and the heuristic eta_eng) is RF244/CE194.
- Status history: W7-SEC "PROVED" (author only); registry `T33-H`: PROVED / none / A-REV9 deferred. The statement "exact ties are decided by rounding unless the computed scores are bitwise equal" agrees with A-REV9's tie caveats on C3/C5 (TH328, TH330).
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEC only.
- Depends on: TH343, TH103 (T03) (candidate global margin), HPM total order of TH115 (T21).
- Feeds: none as a card; the neighbouring deterministic perturbation lemma K108 (S-CERT: "If every log mass is perturbed by at most epsilon then Z-tilde/Z in [e^-eps, e^eps], TV <= tanh eps, a winner with gap > 2 eps is unchanged") is credited by R0_DIFF to the seat's T29, not to W7-SEC.


### TH346 — Proposition T33-Z (the floating-point evidence and VAL-FP)  [proposition]
- Source: `W7-SEC/PROOF_T33.md` section 4. Positions as the W7-SEC block.
- Statement (verbatim; proofs omitted):
  > ## 4. Proposition T33-Z (the floating-point evidence and VAL-FP). Deterministic part **PROVED**; the a-priori ε part **PROVED but vacuous at the study's budgets**.
  >
  > Fix a calibration output 𝓒 computed in floating point. 𝓒 is a function of the data and streams 0–9 only (the fp
  > arithmetic is deterministic), so **T12's frozen-run identities apply to the exact-arithmetic final run R^ex on 𝓒**
  > (exact scores, exact π₀ and Z̄₀, same grid, same streams 10–13). Calibration agreement between fp and exact runs is
  > therefore **not** needed; W5-LOCKBOOK's "the exact run shares 𝓒" holds by construction. Let R^fp be the production
  > final run on the same 𝓒 and streams.
  >
  > **Agreement event.** G_fp := {every discrete decision of R^fp equals that of R^ex}: each π₀ draw (categorical draws by
  > inverse cdf), each Gibbs inclusion (u < o_j), each MH acceptance (u < α), each resampling ancestor (inverse cdf on
  > cumulative weights), and the local-search moves. On G_fp both runs visit, score and resample the same states.
  >
  > **(Z1) Deterministic part.** On G_fp, for every island r,
  >   |log Ẑ_r^fp − log Ẑ_r^ex| ≤ η_Z := η_{m0} + η_{Z̄0} + η_d + 2.01u·D_max + T·ρ_stage,
  > where η_{m0} is the k = 0 bound of Theorem T33-S; η_d := max over states of |d̂ − d| ≤ (J_S + 2)·max η′_m over the
  > model and its block sub-models (η′_m := η_m − η_C; J_S ≤ |S| = number of blocks met; the common log Ĉ_n cancels in
  > log m − log m(∅)); η_{Z̄0} ≤ J(2η′_tab + 2ρ_LSE) + max_k η_π(k) + ρ_LSE with η′_tab := max over table models of
  > η′_m and J the number of blocks; D_max := max |d| over visited states; ρ_LSE(N) := (N/e + 4)u + 1.01Nu_L + 2u·Λ
  > (u_L = 2⁻⁶⁴ the long-double unit, Λ the largest |value| entering or leaving the log-sum-exp); ρ_stage := ρ_LSE(N) + u·Λ_Z
  > (Λ_Z := max_t |log Ẑ_{r,t}|). The pooled Ẑ adds one log-sum-exp of 4 terms.
  >
  > **(Z2) A-priori ε (union bound).** Under EX-S (the uniforms of streams 10–13 are i.i.d. on the 2⁻⁵³ grid of [0,1)),
  >   P(G_fp^c | 𝓒) ≤ C_dec·(η_γ + 2⁻⁵³ + 4u) + 2N²η_d + T·N·(Nγ_N + 2⁻⁵³) + Q_all·(2η_{π0} + 2⁻⁵³)
  > where C_dec is the number of Gibbs/MH/independence decisions of the final run (≤ 4N_{e*}m(T + L + 4), T32), η_γ bounds
  > the error of each decision's log-ratio (≤ 2(max η′_m-based error of log γ_φ) — each log-ratio involves two states),
  > Q_all is the number of π₀ draws (each draw makes ≤ J + 1 categorical choices; η_{π0} bounds the error of their log
  > probabilities, ≤ η_{Z̄0} + 2η′_tab), and the resampling term uses Σ_tΔ_t = 1.
  >
  > **(Z3) VAL-FP and Prop 2(f).** On G_fp, |log Ẑ^fp − log Ẑ^ex| ≤ η_Z. So VAL-FP(η_Z, ε) holds with ε = the bound of (Z2),
  > and W2-BOOK Prop 2(f) gives P(𝒪_E ∩ {αẐ^fp > Z}) ≤ α·e^{η_Z}·P(𝒜) + ε. **PROVED** (as an implication).
  >
  > **What the numbers say** (`results/t33_valfp_budget.txt`; n = 200, p ∈ {500, 1000}, both tiers, T ∈ {10, 100, T_e}):
  > η_Z is 6·10⁻¹¹–4.5·10⁻⁹ with **measured** per-score errors (1.3·10⁻¹³) and ≈ 10⁻⁶ with the **rigorous** per-score
  > bound of a well-conditioned model (10⁻⁸), so e^{η_Z} − 1 is negligible either way. But the union bound ε is dominated
  > by C_dec·η_γ, and the final run makes 10⁸–10¹¹ decisions: ε ranges from 2·10⁻³ (tier 0, T = 10) to > 1 (tier 1,
  > T = 4000) with measured per-score errors, and is ≫ 1 (vacuous) with the rigorous ones. So **ε cannot be certified a
  > priori** at the study's budgets. It must be measured by replay (W2-BOOK's position stands), or replaced by a
  > path-free argument (§5, OPEN).
  >
  > ---
- Earlier versions / repairs: none. The W2-BOOK/W5-LOCKBOOK contract VAL-FP(eta, epsilon) is unchanged; W7-SEC supplies eta_Z explicitly and shows why epsilon cannot be supplied a priori (RF250).
- Status history: W7-SEC "Deterministic part PROVED; the a-priori epsilon part PROVED but vacuous at the study's budgets"; registry `T33-Z`: PROVED / none / A-REV9 deferred ("deterministic part; the a priori epsilon part is PROVED but vacuous at study budgets; epsilon must be measured by replay (OPEN)").
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEC only. What the open items are (verbatim, section 5): path-free (perturbed Feynman-Kac) argument stalls because "the MH self-loop probability 1 - alpha is not multiplicatively stable under score perturbations when alpha ~ 1, and fp kernels are not exactly invariant for any target"; preprocessing error (raw to stored doubles) is not bounded (CJ235).
- Depends on: TH343, TH110 (T12) frozen-run identities, TH299 (W2-BOOK Prop 2(f)).

- Source: `W7-SEC/REPORT.md` sections 2 (T32(i)), 3 (T32(i) and 3.3), 4.3; `W7-SEC/NOTES.md` section 1. The statement being recounted is W5-LOCKBOOK's CJ112 (T32(i)) (theme 7).   > forced step gives fl(φ + fl(1/T_e)) ≥ φ + 1/T_e − 2u, then a snap to 1 above 1 − 10⁻¹². So, until it reaches 1,
  > φ_k ≥ k(1/T_e − 2u).
  > - After T_e steps, φ ≥ 1 − 2T_e u > 1 − 1/T_e, because 2T_e²u < 1.
  > - From any φ > 1 − 1/T_e the next step ends at exactly 1: either the ESS test at 1 passes, or the bisection gap is

  > - Hence T_pilot ≤ T_e + 1. If T_e ≤ 4,503, a forced last step is snapped, so T_e + 1 needs a non-forced step landing in
  >   [1 − 2T_e u, 1).
  > - Diagnostic and final grids keep T ≤ T_e in fp: the integer check at `v3_calib.h:94`. ∎

| quantity | S-ELS | O-LS0 | API-N200 | agrees |

| stopped (resource_limit) | 6 (p500 c1: 1; p1000 c0.5: 2; p1000 c1: 3; all S5) | "3 of the 6 resource-limit fits (all S5, c = 1)" certify S0 under LS0 | U = 6 (1 + 3 + 0 + 2) | yes |

| posterior misses | 565 = 40 + 37 + 230 + 258 | "prod misses" 81 (c = 1) and 490 (c = 0.5) = 77 + 4 stopped and 488 + 2 stopped, total 571 = 565 + 6 | 565 | yes |
| search misses | 0 | "production has 0 search misses (S-ELS)" | 0 | yes |
| 6 + 1,829 + 565 | 2,400 | 2,400 | 2,400 | yes |
| 541 centres in R_2 minus {S0} | 541 (434 with S0 a one-move neighbour) | used as given | "434 of the 541" | yes |

### CJ222 — ELS-1 (data fact): the final local search made 0 moves in 2,394/2,394 completed fits; S0 was scored in every completed fit  [data fact]
- Source: `S-ELS/REPORT.md` sections 1, 3, 6; registry D2 row `ELS-1` ("data from production ledgers"). Positions: [pos 715], [pos 717], [pos 763] item 2, [pos 937] ("The final local search never moves ... It works purely as a certificate"), [pos 1111].
- Claim (verbatim, `S-ELS/REPORT.md` section 1):
  > - In **all 2,394 completed fits the final local search made 0 moves**: E3 never fired, the HPM never changed, and every search ended `no_improvement`, `local_certified = TRUE`, `local_limit = FALSE`. So Ŝ = S_c = returned model in every completed fit.
  > - **S₀ was scored by the fit in all 2,394 completed fits**: it is in the 20,001-model top store, and the store's F(S₀) equals the offline F(S₀) to 1e-12. The event E_LS (S₀ not scored before the search and better than the best scored model) is **empty in the data (0 of 2,394)**.
- Registry D2 (verbatim): | `ELS-1` | Final local search made 0 moves in 2,394/2,394 completed PROD-H fits; S₀ scored in every completed fit | S-ELS · REPORT.md §1, §3 (head 90423b1) | data from production ledgers |
- Checks (verbatim, `S-ELS/REPORT.md` section 6):
  > 1. S₀ in the ledger equals H2's S₀ in all 2,400 fits; H2's `F_smc_hpm` equals the ledger's F(Ŝ) (max diff 2e-12).
  > 2. S_c = `hpm_before_local` model and F(S_c) = its F, in all 2,394.
  > 3. F(Ŝ) ≥ F(S_c) everywhere; S_hat = returned model everywhere; E3 ⇔ F(Ŝ) > F(before local) (both never); moves > 0 ⇔ E3 (both never).
  > 4. **F(S₀) cross-check:** the offline `F_truth` equals the fit's own top-store F(S₀) in 2,394/2,394 (max diff 1e-12), and equals F(Ŝ) on the 1,829 exact recoveries (max diff 1e-12). So F(S₀) is the same score the fit used, and S₀ was in the fit's top-20,001 store every time.
- Limits (verbatim, section 7):
  > - I did not recompute F(S₀) from the data matrix. I took the H2 scoring output and validated it against the fit's own store (check 4). The store holds the top 20,001 scored models, so that check covers S₀ only because S₀ scored high enough to be kept, which it always was.
  > - The ledger is for the final local search only. The pilot and calibration searches (iteration ≥ 0) are not in the per-fit record fields I read; they only matter for how S_c was reached, not for E_LS at the end.
  > - I could not see the referee's sample, so I cannot say why they saw F(S₀) > F(S_c). §1 lists what I ruled out.
  > - The 6 stopped fits have no final search; they are described, not classified.
  > - The whole result is for the PROD-H design (n = 200, p ∈ {500, 1000}, S1–S6, c ∈ {1, 0.5}) at ℓ = 10 with the v2.2.1 engine. It says nothing about weaker regimes where the HPM is not already a local maximum.
- Status history: data extracted by S-ELS (Claude Work); no independent re-extraction; independently *consistent* with O-LS0 (LS0 changes the HPM in 0 of 2,394, CJ226) and with the per-cell counts of O-SWAP/API-N200 (CJ241, CJ243). It is the data input to Theorem N200's discovery term ("0 of 2,394; exact 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound 1 - 0.05^(1/2394) = 0.125% per fit").
- Proved by / checked by: S-ELS; consistency checks listed above.
- Depends on: ⟦E_LS⟧ (S0 unscored before the search and better than the best scored model), TH281 (Lemma 0), TH114 (T20) (`local_certified`).
- Feeds: M5 Theorem HPM notes (HQ summary "S-ELS: the final local search never moved"); n = 200 disclosure paragraph (CJ239). Consequence recorded by the author: "PROD-H says nothing about whether a greedy repair *works*, because the repair never operated. The production search is, empirically, a **pure certificate** that S-hat is a 1-flip/swap local maximum (2,394/2,394)".

### CJ230 — Finite-n upper bound on the posterior-miss probability Pi(X) = P0(S-dagger != S0 | X) at n = 200  [open problem]
- Source: `API-N200/REPORT.md` sections 1 item 2, 5, 6 item 2; `API-N200/PROOF.md` section 3; FUTURE_WORK FW14 (K94: "finite-n bound on the posterior-miss probability Pi(X)": "Envelope GAP"). Positions: [pos 978], [pos 929] ("a predicted miss-rate formula that's only approximate").
- Statement (verbatim, `API-N200/REPORT.md` section 1 item 2):
  > 2. **Where rigor stops in Π(X).** PROVED: max_e p_e ≤ P₀(L | X) ≤ P₀(L₂ | X) ≤ Π(X) and P₀(L | X) ≤ Σ_e p_e (one-move event L; Hamming-2 event L₂). P₀(L | X) is computed by exact-score Monte Carlo on the study's own designs (rigorous up to MC error); the closed-form p_e are **PA-exact** (O-SWAP Props 1–3), not rigorous. **An upper bound on Π(X) at finite n is OPEN**: the remainder Π − P₀(L) is measured (≤ 1.1 points per cell by exact-score MC with double drops; ±1 fit per cell by the realised hill-climb; 0.2–1 point at c = 1 in exact p = 12 enumeration) but not bounded. A union bound over Hamming balls provably cannot close it (PROOF.md §3).
- Statement (verbatim, `PROOF.md` section 3, on what is computable):
  > - **An upper bound on Π(X)** at n = 200: **OPEN**. Π(X) = P₀(L) + P₀(Lᶜ, S† ≠ S₀), and the second term has no proved bound. The evidence that it is small is (a) exact-score MC with double drops: ≤ 1.1 points per cell (O-SWAP; column "excess" in the table); (b) the realised one-move + double-drop + hill-climb check on the study's own y reproduces the observed SMC count in all 24 cells to ±1; (c) exact enumeration at p = 12 (`results/small_p_exact.txt`): the excess P_post − P(L) is 0.2–1 point at c = 1, 0.3–3 points at c = 0.75, and up to 8 points at c = 0.35–0.5, where the Hamming-2 event L_2 leaves at most 2 points. This is **empirical, not a theorem**.
- Escalation request (verbatim, `REPORT.md` section 6 item 2): 2. **A finite-n upper bound on Π(X)** of the form P₀(L | X) + r_n(X) with explicit r_n: the shell argument generalised to correlated nulls and to drops/swaps at distance 2, and a tail over distance ≥ 3. Stronger prover.
- Status: OPEN. Failed route: union bound over Hamming balls (RF249, CE195). Evidence only, not a theorem: remainder Pi - P0(L) at most 1.1 points per cell by exact-score MC with double drops; 0.2-1 point at c = 1 and up to 8 points at c = 0.35-0.5 in the exact p = 12 enumeration (CJ244).
- Feeds: FUTURE_WORK FW14 (K94).


### CJ231 — SuSiE/SSL effective-threshold conjecture ("a higher effective inclusion threshold wins at c = 1 and loses at c = 0.5")  [conjecture]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 5, subsection "SuSiE and SSL: only what the theory supports", and section 9 (confidence card row "SuSiE / SSL (goal 5)"). Positions: [pos 578]/[pos 742] (O-SWAP finished); HQ [pos 937] (same-size swaps: "the paper can say so with a theorem behind it"; supersets at c = 1: "the g-prior plus BB(1,p) model at n = 200 doesn't penalise extras quite enough").
- Statement (verbatim):
  > The theory **does** support the following:
  > 1. **At c = 1 the HPM's misses are prior-driven supersets, and a selector with a higher effective inclusion threshold avoids them for free.** Every truth has |δ_j| ≥ 11·√(1 − R²) ≳ 8 at c = 1. A selector that admits a null only when its standardised partial score exceeds t′ has superset rate ≈ (p − s₀)·2Φ̄(t′) and drop rate ≈ Φ(t′ − |δ|_min). For t′ between ≈ 4.5 and ≈ 6, both are below 1 %. The HPM's t_add ≈ 3.9 sits at a 7 % superset rate.
  > 2. **At c = 0.5 the same higher threshold costs subset misses.** The weakest truths have |δ| ≈ 5.6 (less in S5). The drop rate Φ(t′ − 5.6) is 16 % at t′ = 4.6 and 50 % at t′ = 5.6 per weak truth, against ≈ 4–8 % at t_drop ≈ 3.9.
  > 3. **Pairwise swaps have a floor for everyone** (Prop. 5). No method can be uniformly much better than the HPM on S4-type look-alikes.
  >
  > So "more conservative than BB(1, p) + g = n" is predicted to win at c = 1 and lose at c = 0.5. That is the observed SuSiE and SSL pattern: SuSiE goes from 585/600 to 220/600, SSL from 569 to 303, and SMC-BVS from 559 to 370.
  >
  > The theory does **not** support the following: that SuSiE's or SSL's effective threshold actually is t′ ≈ 4.5–6. Their thresholds come from SuSiE's estimated prior variance and purity filter, and from SSL's λ₀/θ adaptation, and are not derived here (CONJECTURE). It also does not support any explanation of SuSiE's collapse on S5 at c = 0.5 (3/100 and 0/100). That is plausibly a single-effect/credible-set failure under the global 0.3 equicorrelation, which is outside this score-based theory.
- Status: CONJECTURE (author: "their actual thresholds are not derived"; section 7 item 4: deriving the effective inclusion thresholds of SuSiE with estimated prior variance and purity filter, and of SSL with adaptive lambda_0, theta, at n = 200 "would turn the CONJECTURE of section 5 into a statement"). The observed counts quoted: "SuSiE goes from 585/600 to 220/600, SSL from 569 to 303, and SMC-BVS from 559 to 370" (c = 1 to c = 0.5; no campaign run re-derived them). Unreviewed; A-REV9 gives a GAP for the O-SWAP rates generally (TH337).
- Feeds: none (campaign-only).

### CJ233 — Whole-model (Assouad/Fano) lower bound over the 14 truths and their look-alikes  [open problem]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 4/5 ("Connection to T07") and section 9. Position: as the O-SWAP block.
- Statement (verbatim): 
  > Prop. 1 is T07 in quantitative form. In F(S₀ − j + l) − F(S₀) the size prior cancels identically, and the swap probability depends on the prior only through κ_{jl} = ½ log(D_{S₀−j+l}/D_{S₀}) = O(1/n) (|κ_{jl}| ≤ 0.3 nats here). So no size-only prior and no g can move the dominant c = 0.5 failure mode. Prop. 5 adds that **no selector at all** can push the two-point averaged swap error much below the HPM's own: the exponents are δ²(1−ρ²)/8 against δ²(1−ρ)/4, whose ratio (1+ρ)/2 is 0.93 at ρ = 0.85. The per-design Le Cam floor max_{(j,l)} Φ(−|δ_j|√(1−ρ²_{jl})/2) is reported in §4: ≤ 0.4 % at c = 1 and up to ≈ 9 % (S4) at c = 0.5. It is a **pairwise** floor and lies far below the whole-model miss rate. A whole-model floor (Assouad/Fano over the 14 truths and their look-alikes) is OPEN.
- Status: OPEN (author: "medium" cost: "multi-hypothesis lower bound"). The pairwise Le Cam floor (TH341) is "<= 0.4 % at c = 1 and up to ~9 % (S4) at c = 0.5. It is a pairwise floor and lies far below the whole-model miss rate".

### CJ234 — A data certificate of confidence (pi(S-hat) >= c, or "S-hat is the global HPM"): an upper bound on Z that is computable per fit  [open problem]
- Source: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 1 item 1 and C1(c) (TH326); `O-VCERT/REPORT.md` S2. Positions: [pos 706] item 1, [pos 763].
- Statement of the obstruction as claimed by O-CERT (verbatim, section 1 item 1): 
  > 1. **Direction (task item ii): PROVED.** The locked Markov bound P(Z ≥ 0.05Ẑ) ≥ 0.95 is a *lower* bound on Z, so it
  >    gives an **upper** bound on π(Ŝ) = e^{F(Ŝ)}/Z, never a lower one. It holds *simultaneously for every model*
  >    (the bad event is {Z < 0.05Ẑ}, whatever Ŝ is), so selecting Ŝ from the same run costs nothing (Thm C1).
  >    Combined with the deterministic Z ≥ Z_𝒯 (the sum over the reported top store) it reads
  >    π(Ŝ) ≤ e^{F(Ŝ)}/max(Z_𝒯, 0.05Ẑ). A *lower* bound on π(Ŝ) needs an upper bound on Z. That does **not** follow from
  >    unbiasedness (locked T31(c)), and the 4-island spread cannot supply it (T31(d), T12(iv.e)). Under PW2 (T25(iv)),
  >    Cantelli gives a two-sided band (Thm C2, PROVED but CONDITIONAL on PW2, which is not data-checkable). T13's
  >    restricted ESS does not give a lower bound on π(Ŝ) without PW2.
- Referee's correction (verbatim, O-VCERT S2): 
  > - **S2.** §1 item 1, §5 first bullet and C6 "cannot certify confidence … without PW2 or enumeration" overstate C1(c).
  >   - C1(c) is a non-implication from the 𝓛(Z) properties only.
  >   - Any certified upper bound on Z gives a sure lower bound on π(Ŝ): the inventory's UB, a Lemma-M box cover of all of Ω
  >     (impractical at p = 500, as O-CERT §5 says), or T31's own remark Ẑ ≥ e^{−Δ}Z with Δ = max_Ω d − min_Ω d.
  >   - Reword as: "not from unbiasedness; it needs an upper bound on Z (PW2, UB, enumeration, or a bound on Δ)".
- Status: OPEN as a practical per-fit item. What is proved: no lower bound follows from unbiasedness alone (C1(c), VERIFIED non-implication by O-VCERT and A-REV9: "it does not exclude deterministic upper bounds on Z"); a two-sided band follows under PW2 (TH327); a global box cover is impractical at p = 500 ("Q_[p] ~ y'y/(n+1) when p > n, so Phi(empty, [p]) is astronomically large", O-CERT section 5). Even a correct fit carries little posterior mass at n = 200: "At c = 1, S-hat = S0, and yet pi(S-hat) <= 0.37 surely" (CJ245).
- Feeds: none (K95 odds certificate is in S-TARGET, theme outside).

### CJ237 — A finite-n discovery bound for the Gibbs route (T38(b)); a priori discovery bounds are vacuous at n = 200  [open problem]
- Source: `API-N200/REPORT.md` sections 1 item 3, 5; `API-N200/PROOF.md` section 5; FUTURE_WORK FW26 ("Finite-n Gibbs discovery (HPM residual): Existing asymptotic or vacuous bounds do not supply useful finite-n discovery (ThmB-T24 vacuous at n = 200; no route)").
- Statement (verbatim, `REPORT.md` section 5, third bullet):
  > - **A priori discovery bounds at n = 200.** Route (a) is vacuous by six orders of magnitude (σ²-dilution). Route (d) does not apply to S₀ as a whole. Routes (b), (c), (e) are open at every n. No restatement of the existing routes changes this; a finite-n bound for the Gibbs-flip route (which empirically delivers S₀ in every fit) would be new theory (T38(b), O-BGIBBS-type).
- Supporting computation (verbatim, `PROOF.md` section 5, route (a)):
  > **A priori (T21 routes), rigorous but vacuous.**
  > - Route (a), fresh iid draws: P(S₀ ∉ 𝒮) ≤ P(F_cal^c, S₀ ∉ 𝒮_cal) + E[1_{F_cal}1{S₀ ∉ 𝒮_cal}(1 − π₀(S₀))^{Q_f}]. At the study budgets N₀ = 2500, L = 8, Q_f ≥ 4N_e(L + 6) = 1.4·10⁵ (e = 0), and π₀(S₀) has per-cell median 10^{−11}–10^{−26} (O-DILUTE, 480 regenerated fits; the study's H2 tables say ≈ 10^{−12} or smaller; 1 favourable fit of 2,394). So Q_fπ₀(S₀) ≲ 10⁻⁶ and the bound is ≥ 1 − 10⁻⁶: **vacuous**. The deficit is σ²-dilution (O-DILUTE Thm E: −log π₀(S₀) = V + C − log A, V ≈ 83% of it), so no restatement of (a) helps at this n.
  > - Route (d), tables and scans: S₀ is not inside one block (14 truths over blocks of size ≤ 14 with proxies), so table scoring does not apply. The final scan's centre S_c = Ŝ had S₀ ∈ N(S_c) in 434 of the 541 near-truth misses and in all 1,829 recoveries trivially; a completed scan from such a centre scores S₀ (T20(ii)), which is a **per-fit certificate** of the (already observed) scoring, not an a-priori bound.
  > - Routes (b), (c), (e): E_G, PX, H24 are open at every n.
  > So the best rigorous a-priori discovery bound at n = 200 is 1.
- Status: OPEN; the discovery term is measured, not proved (0 of 2,394, CJ222).
- Feeds: FW26.

  >    > At the study's size (n = 200, p ∈ {500, 1000}, s₀ = 14) the theorems describe mechanism, not the reported numbers.

  >    > (ii) The start is masked by *dilution* (each block's table treats the other blocks' signal as noise): the median start mass on S₀ is 10⁻¹¹–10⁻²⁶ per cell, while about 0.8 of the start mass lies within two extras of a subset of S₀.
  >    > (iii) Theorem 1's proof thresholds hold only from n ≈ 2·10⁶, its beta-min constant exceeds the executed signals by at least 43×, and its eigenvalue premise is unverified on the realised designs.
  >    > (iv) The start-rate bounds carry a 2^B factor that is ≥ 10³ at B = 14.
  >    > (v) The HPM at this size is delivered by Gibbs flips during the bridge.
  >    > We bound P(reported and wrong), not P(wrong | reported).
  >
  >    **Where the numbers come from.**
  >    - (i): S-ELS.
  >    - (ii): O-DILUTE §7.
  >    - (iii): W2-VT03R R1 and F-REFINE ARCHITECTURE §7.
  >    - (iv): F-REFINE.
  >    - The last sentence: W5-LOCKBOOK STATEMENTS.tex.
  >
  >    **What Felipe must decide.**
  >    - Whether to quote a "favourable from n ≈ …" threshold at all. The sources disagree: 590–730 (O-DILUTE, c → ∞ ceiling), 800–1,600 (W3-VEXP), and 1,050–3,200 (W5-FAVIID). I recommend omitting it, or quoting the W5-FAVIID empirical first-n with its source.
  >    - Whether to say "dilution" in the main text.
  >    - Whether to keep the "98% of fresh scores come from Gibbs flips" figure. It is from THEORY_PRIORITIES §5, preliminary, and no campaign run re-derived it.
- Consistency check of the draft (clerk's arithmetic; Summary:): (i) 6 + 1,829 + 565 = 2,400 (CJ223); the 6 stopped fits are all S5 (1 at p = 500, c = 1; 5 at p = 1000: 3 at c = 1 and 2 at c = 0.5; Wilson 95% interval [0.11%, 0.54%] in W5-LOCKBOOK). (ii) "the median start mass on S0 is 1e-11 to 1e-26 per cell" is the O-DILUTE per-cell range (10^-11.1 for p500 S1 c1 to 10^-25.6 for p1000 S5 c0.5; 480 numpy-regenerated fits; pooled median 10^-15.7); "about 0.8 of the start mass lies within two extras of a subset of S0" is the pooled median pi0(R2) = 0.794, whereas the per-cell medians run from 0.20 (p500 S4 c1) to 0.96 (p1000 S1 c0.5), so "0.8" is not a per-cell value (S4 cells are 0.20-0.40). (iii) the numbers 43x and 2e6: W2-VT03R R1 and F-REFINE ARCHITECTURE section 7. (iv) 2^B >= 1e3 at B = 14 (F-REFINE internal conflict: ARCH section 7(iv) ">= 10^3 at B = 14 for n <= 10^4" vs CARDS 2.7e3 / 497 / 61, W8-SYNTH digest G5). (v) "The HPM at this size is delivered by Gibbs flips" rests on the preliminary "98% of fresh scores come from Gibbs flips" (THEORY_PRIORITIES section 5), which no campaign run re-derived (W8-SYNTH). The sentence in SYNTHESIS section 1 decision 1 "That check has not landed" is stale (RF247).
- Status: proposed wording (W8-SYNTH, an Opus 5.5 synthesis run on API credits); later final lists carry only the scale disclosure of M2 (`THEOREM_LIST_FINAL.md`, "Scale disclosure (not a theorem)"), FW22. Not a theorem.
- Depends on: CJ222-CJ223, CJ243, TH103 (T03 thresholds), TH171 (O-DILUTE Thm E), ⟦F-REFINE ARCHITECTURE⟧ (themes 1, 3).


### CJ240 — API-N200's draft paragraph for the paper's n = 200 section  [proposed target]
- Source: `API-N200/REPORT.md` section 9 (candidate), and PROOF section 6 "Assembled statement for the paper". Position: [pos 978].
- Draft (verbatim, `REPORT.md` section 9):
  > > **What the theory says at the study's n = 200.** Theorem 4 holds at every n. In the form used here it reads, for each design, P(no output or Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≤ P(no output) + P₀(S† ≠ S₀ | X) + P(output, S₀ never scored), where S† is the global mode of the posterior, and conversely P(output, Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≥ P(output, S† ≠ S₀) − P(output, S† never scored). The three terms are of different natures. The first is operational: 6 of 2,400 fits stopped at the resource limit. The third is a scoring event: in all 2,394 completed fits S₀ was scored and no reported model was beaten by S₀ (0 search misses; exact 95% upper bound 0.13% per fit); the a-priori bounds of Theorem 4's routes are vacuous at this n because the start mass π₀(S₀) is 10⁻¹¹–10⁻²⁶ (σ²-dilution, Proposition DM), so this term is measured, not proved. The second is the posterior-miss probability of the design: it does not involve the sampler, it is what Theorem 1 drives to zero as n → ∞, and at n = 200 it is bounded below by the probability that a one-move neighbour of S₀ beats S₀, a Gaussian/χ² computation in the residual projections of X (Propositions 1–3 of the supplement). Summed over the study's own 1,200 designs this lower bound predicts 552 posterior misses in 2,394 completed fits against 565 observed (RMS z = 1.08 over the 24 cells), and it predicts the type: supersets at c = 1, same-size swaps and dropped truths at c = 0.5. We do not have a proved upper bound on the posterior-miss probability at finite n; the multi-move remainder is measured to be at most about one point per cell. In short, at n = 200 every observed error is a posterior miss, and the posterior-miss rate is the quantity the finite-n inequality isolates and the one-move theory computes; the asymptotic theorems describe where that quantity goes, not its value at n = 200.
- Wording of the theorem for the paper (verbatim, `PROOF.md` section 6):
  > **Theorem (finite-n composition).** For every n, p, design, truth and noise level, and for the method as run,
  >   P(no output or Ŝ ≠ S₀) = P(no output) + P(output, Ŝ ≻ S₀) + P(output, S₀ ≻ Ŝ)
  >   ≤ P(no output) + P₀(S† ≠ S₀ | X) + P(output, S₀ never scored),
  > and P(output, Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≥ P(output, S† ≠ S₀) − P(output, S† never scored). The posterior-miss probability P₀(S† ≠ S₀ | X) depends only on (X, θ*, σ*²); it is bounded below by the one-move event P₀(L | X), which is a Gaussian/χ² computation in the residual projections of X (O-SWAP Props 1–3), and above by nothing proved at finite n.
  >
  > Status: Theorem PROVED (elementary; a candidate for Lean after T21HPM.lean, where `hpm_eq_truth`, `t21_event_subset` already carry the ≤ ½ version). The evaluation of Π(X) at n = 200 is a computation (rigorous lower bracket, PA closed forms, empirical remainder); the discovery term is measured.
- Consistency check (clerk's arithmetic; Summary:): "552 posterior misses in 2,394 completed fits against 565 observed" uses the sum 552.1 of the Monte-Carlo P0(L | X) over the 2,400 designs (`n200_table.md`: 40.5 + 37.3 + 228.3 + 246.0 = 552.1) against 565 = 40 + 37 + 230 + 258; the headline "558 vs 571" adds the observed U = 6 to both sides (552.1 + 6 = 558.1; 565 + 6 = 571). "6 of 2,400 fits stopped at the resource limit" is consistent with CJ223. The draft says the stated lower bound "is computable" but also "We do not have a proved upper bound ... the multi-move remainder is measured to be at most about one point per cell" (CJ230).
- Status: proposed wording, candidate; the theorem it states is TH334 (author-only).

### CJ242 — O-SWAP prediction claim: the design-averaged predictor T2 gives 43/40 misses per 600 at c = 1 against 40/37 observed, and 251/271 at c = 0.5 against 230/259  [data fact]
- Source: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 1 (third bullet) and section 4.3 items 3-5. Position: as the O-SWAP block.
- Claim (verbatim, section 1 bullets):
  > - **Each posterior-miss mode has an exact finite-n law** given X: Gaussian/χ² events in residual projections, under PA.
  >   - Swap: Prop. 1, P ≈ Φ(−|δ_j|√((1−ρ_{jl})/2)), with no size-prior term (T07).
  >   - Superset: Prop. 2, a χ²₁ tail at a p-free threshold t_add ≈ 3.7–4.1σ that **rises with the SNR** through the τ = 1 pseudo-observation (Cor. 2.1).
  >   - Subset: Prop. 3, Φ(t_drop − |δ_j|).
  > - **The observed misses match the one-move posterior misses.** On the study's own data (regenerated in Python with R's RNG ported exactly), the exact-score one-move check reproduces the observed SMC-BVS miss count in all 24 cells to within ±1: 39 / 37 / 227 / 257 against 40 / 37 / 230 / 259.
  > - **The theory predicts the rates.** The design-averaged predictor T2 (Props 1–3 + 6) gives 43 / 40 misses per 600 at c = 1 against 40 / 37 observed, and 251 / 271 at c = 0.5 against 230 / 259. It reproduces the scenario ranking (S4 ≫ S5 > S6 ≈ S3 > S1 ≈ S2) and the type split: supersets at c = 1, swaps and drops at c = 0.5.
  > - **Why the modes switch with c.** Supersets face a nearly fixed prior threshold (it falls only slightly with ω₀), so their rate only doubles from c = 1 to c = 0.5. Swaps and drops are exponential in δ² ∝ c². A higher-threshold selector (SuSiE/SSL-like) is predicted to win at c = 1 and lose at c = 0.5 (CONJECTURE as applied to those methods).

  > RMS z (obs vs T2) = 1.38; RMS z (obs vs MC) = 1.22 over 12 cells.

Conflict of numbers inside the claim: "RMS z (obs vs T2) = 0.86" (c = 1) and "1.38" (c = 0.5) in O-SWAP against API-N200's "RMS z = 1.08 over the 24 cells" for observed posterior misses vs the exact-score MC (a different predictor and standard deviation; the per-cell z of the two reports agree to within 0.1 where compared, e.g. p1000 S5 c1: +1.8 in both).

  > | **C** under PW2, B_T = 0.25: π(Ŝ) ≥ 0.5e^{F}/Ẑ except w.p. ≤ 0.2 | 0.150 | 0.157 | 0.029 | 0.044 |
  > | F(S₀) − F(Ŝ) (uses S₀) | 0 | 0 | −1.19 | −1.89 |
- Text of the findings (verbatim, items 1-6): 
  > **What the illustration shows.**
  > 1. **The score contract holds to ~10⁻¹² nats.** Two independent implementations (the engine's C++ and my R) agree
  >    to within 3·10⁻¹² nats on every top-store score checked. This is a cross-implementation check, not a
  >    high-precision replay, but it makes SC(η_F) with η_F = 10⁻⁹ comfortable. Every certified gap above is ≥ 0.5 nats,
  >    about 10⁹ times the margin 2η_F.
  > 2. **The global claim was deterministic on every fit.** Z_𝒯 > 0.05Ẑ in all four cases, by 2.4–3.0 nats: the
  >    reported top store already contains more than 5% of the estimated evidence. So max(Z_𝒯, αẐ) = Z_𝒯, and the G bound
  >    π(Ŝ) ≤ e^{F(Ŝ)}/Z_𝒯 holds **surely** (C1(a)), with no probability at all. The Markov factor of T12/T31 adds nothing
  >    at α = 0.05 here. It would become active only for a run whose top store sees less than 5% of Ẑ, the
  >    exploration-failure case, which is exactly when the "unscored mass ≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ)" line becomes non-vacuous.
  >    Here that line is 0 on all four fits.
  > 3. **Even a correct fit carries little posterior mass at n = 200.** At c = 1, Ŝ = S₀, and yet π(Ŝ) ≤ 0.37 surely.
  >    The binding alternatives are supersets (g_add = 2.3–2.9 nats ≪ g_del, g_swap ≈ 20–38 nats). This is the
  >    finite-n face of the "superset misses at c = 1" finding (THEORY_PRIORITIES §5): exact recovery is the posterior
  >    mode, but not with posterior probability ½. No certificate can say π(Ŝ) ≥ ½, and here even the truth fails it.
  > 4. **The two c = 0.5 misses are certified posterior misses.** In both, S₀ = Ŝ ∖ {FP} is a one-deletion of Ŝ. The
  >    card's g_del (1.19 and 1.89 nats) is exactly F(Ŝ) − F(S₀), so π(S₀) ≤ e^{−g_del}π(Ŝ) = 0.30π(Ŝ) and 0.15π(Ŝ)
  >    respectively. The box certificate independently confirms that S₀ ∈ 2^U and that Ŝ = argmax over 2^U (C5). Both
  >    are posterior misses: no amount of extra search would have returned S₀. The card certifies this **without
  >    knowing S₀**, because it bounds every model in N̄(Ŝ) and in 2^U uniformly. A reader who suspects that "the truth is
  >    Ŝ minus one variable" is told by the card that every such model has posterior ratio ≤ e^{−1.19}.
  > 5. **The box certificate is cheap.** The optimality B&B over 2^U with |U| = 30–31 (10⁹ models) closed in
  >    2·10³–8·10⁴ nodes and at most 38 s, consistent with the "2^{#ambiguous variables}" remark under C4. The mass
  >    version is costlier (it must bound the whole tail to e^{−12}). It closed on three of the four fits, with
  >    π(Ŝ | 2^U) ≥ 0.70, 0.73 and 0.28. Note that π(Ŝ | 2^U) ≥ 0.70 > 0.37 ≥ π(Ŝ) is not a contradiction. Conditioning on 2^U
  >    removes at least 1 − 0.37/0.70 ≈ 47% of the mass of the models that compete with Ŝ (for example, supersets that
  >    add a variable outside U).
  > 6. **Ẑ's island spread is small (SD of log Ẑ_r 0.02–0.08), but is not used.** By T31(d2), conditioning on a
  >    small spread can destroy coverage. The C row is printed only as a what-if.
- UNCERTAIN (source conflict): O-VCERT (reviewing 17e7f15): "S4. §4 is empty and results/cards.txt is not committed. Every numeric claim of O-CERT (tree sizes, 'cost grows like 2^{#ambiguous}', P(S0 not in U) 'measured') is therefore unsupported as it stands." The snapshot (332bf3e) contains §4 and A-REV9's source copy is the same text, but nobody re-ran or re-reviewed it ("Historical numerical claims were not independently reproduced", A-REV9). The registry W8-SYNTH sentence "O-CERT §4 illustration is empty and no results were committed" is therefore stale for the final head but still the last review record.
- Internal arithmetic check (clerk's; Summary:): log Z_T minus log(0.05 Zhat) = 2.79, 2.82, 2.40, 2.44 nats in the four columns, within the stated "2.4-3.0 nats"; pi(S0) <= e^-1.19 pi(S-hat) = 0.30 pi(S-hat) and e^-1.89 = 0.15 pi(S-hat); consistent with the table.
- Status: candidate illustration; not feeds. Used by API-N200 section 4 ("O-CERT (4 regenerated study fits, production engine): pi(S-hat) <= 0.37 even when S-hat = S0").


### CJ246 — W7-SEC numerical margins at the study's sizes: universal bounds, measured scorer errors, eta_Z and the vacuous epsilon  [data fact]
- Source: `W7-SEC/REPORT.md` sections 1 items 2-4 and 4.2; `PROOF_T33.md` sections 2 and 4. Position: as the W7-SEC block.

  >    of λ_min(H_S), κ(H_S), κ(A_S) and y′y/Q_S. It rests on two new exact facts:
  >    - Q_S ≥ y′y/(n+1) (Lemma T33-Q), so the cancellation in Q costs at most a factor n + 1;
  >    - I ≼ H_S, A_S (Lemma T33-M).

  >    - on path agreement, |log Ẑ^fp − log Ẑ^ex| ≤ η_Z ≈ 10⁻¹⁰–10⁻⁶ (Prop T33-Z, combined with W2-BOOK's VAL-FP).
  > 3. **T33: the a-priori VAL-FP ε is vacuous at the study's budgets.** The union bound over 10⁸–10¹¹ final-run decisions
  >    is ≥ 10⁻³ even with measured per-score errors and ≫ 1 with rigorous ones. ε must be measured by replay, as W2-BOOK
  >    said. A path-free argument is OPEN.
  > 4. **COUNTEREXAMPLE: the engine's `error_bound()` (`v3_score.h:242`) is not a bound** at large n. Actual error / η_eng
  >    reaches 1.17 at n = 10⁵ and 6.2 at n = 4·10⁶ when y is highly correlated with the model. It held with about 25×
  >    room at n ≤ 4,000. The R9 "global_certified" flag on the exact branch inherits this.
- Measured values (verbatim, `REPORT.md` section 4.2, budget bullet and engine stress):
  > - `results/t33_engine_bound_stress.txt`: n ∈ {10⁴, 10⁵, 10⁶, 4·10⁶}, y = x₁ + noise. The ratio to η_eng reaches
  >   1.17 (n = 10⁵), 3.5 (n = 10⁶) and 6.2 (n = 4·10⁶). The rigorous bound holds wherever its hypotheses hold
  >   (n ≤ 10⁵ here); beyond that it is ∞.
  > - `results/t33_valfp_budget.txt`:
  >   - worst-case a-priori quantities at n = 200, K = 100: ε_H = 1.4·10⁻⁷, (n+1)r_Q = 4.6·10⁻⁵, universal
  >     η_Q = 4.6·10⁻³;
  >   - largest n for Cor T33-NF: 1,286 (K = n/2), 4,575 (K = 10), 8,149 (K = 1);

Not reviewed (A-REV9 deferred). Constants: |log C_n-hat - log C_n| <= 1.8e-12 (n = 4000) and |log varpi-hat - log varpi| <= 1.1e-13.

### Refuted and retired claims, with their counterexamples (RF237-RF251, CE189-CE196)

Each RF entry quotes the claim verbatim and names the entry that replaces it. A CE entry quotes the concrete counterexample. Paired IDs: RF237/CE189, RF238/CE190, RF239/CE191, RF240/CE192, RF242/CE193, RF244/CE194, RF249/CE195, RF251/CE196.


### RF237 — O-CERT C1(b)/C6: "the posterior mass of the unscored and unreported models is at least 1 - Z_T/(alpha Zhat)"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` C1(b), the Remark after C1, and Theorem C6 item G (verbatim):
  > In particular, with probability at least 1 − α (output-level, unconditional): π(Ŝ) ≤ e^{F(Ŝ)}/max(Z_𝒯, αẐ), and the
  > posterior mass of the *unscored and unreported* models is at least 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ).
  > - The lower bound on unscored mass is a finite-n *exploration* diagnostic: it is positive exactly when
  >   Z_𝒯 < αẐ, i.e. when the evidence estimate says the run has seen less than α of the posterior.
  > - **G (global, one-sided, level α):** π(Ŝ) ≤ u_α(Ŝ) = e^{F(Ŝ)}/max(Z_𝒯, αẐ); π(S) ≤ u_α(S) for every model; the
  >   unscored mass is ≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ) (C1).
- Refutation: CE189 (O-VCERT section 2.1; `vcert_check.py` section 4). The inequality is a bound on the mass outside the reported store T, not on the unscored mass; T is only the top-(40p + 1) store, so scored-but-unreported models carry mass. A-REV9 (verbatim): "Original unscored-mass wording: ERROR; O-VCERT R1 correctly replaces it with mass outside T. This does not upgrade the original statement." and "O-VCERT's optional unscored bound also requires a genuine upper bound on the entire logical scored set: a final-run fresh-score count that omits calibration is insufficient."
- Replaced by: TH332 (R1: "not in T"; optional unscored bound with a reported upper bound Nbar on the number of distinct scored models and F_min). Registry `OCERT-C1`: "[APPLIED] O-VCERT R1 (written by the referee; O-CERT's text not edited)"; O-CERT's own `cert_run.R` already prints "posterior mass outside the top store" (O-VCERT: "The REPORT text disagrees with its own code").
- Who found it: O-VCERT (same family) [pos 763]; confirmed by A-REV9 (cross-family).


### CE189 — Counterexample to the "unscored mass" sentence: factor design, n = 40, p = 10, all models scored  [counterexample]
- Source: `O-VCERT/REPORT.md` section 2.1 (verbatim):
  > On {Z ≥ αẐ}, C1 gives π(Ω ∖ 𝒯) ≥ 1 − Z_𝒯/(αẐ). But Ω ∖ 𝒯 contains the models that were **scored but not reported**,
  > because 𝒯 is only the top-(40p+1) store. The *unscored* mass can be 0 while the claim is positive.
  >
  > Instance (`vcert_check.py` §4): factor design, n = 40, p = 10. Every model is scored, so the unscored mass is 0, and
  > Ẑ = Z, so the good event holds. 𝒯 = the top-m models:
  >
  > | m | α | claimed "unscored" mass ≥ | true unscored mass | true mass outside 𝒯 |
  > |---|---|---|---|---|
  > | 3 | 0.5 | 0.590 | 0 | 0.795 |
  > | 10 | 0.5 | 0.007 | 0 | 0.504 |
  >
  > C1 allows any reported 𝒯, so this refutes the sentence as worded. With the engine's 𝒯 the same failure needs a
  > posterior that is diffuse beyond 40p+1 models, which is plausible at p = 500 under weak signals. O-CERT's own
  > `cert_run.R` prints the correct phrase ("posterior mass outside the top store"). The REPORT text disagrees with its own
  > code.
- Cross-family restatement (A-REV9 verbatim):
  > R1: let a positive finite posterior have all states scored, let Zhat=Z, and choose a reported subset T with pi(T)<alpha. Unscored mass is zero, whereas 1-Z_T/(alpha Z)>0. The corrected statement is about Omega minus T. O-VCERT's optional unscored bound also requires a genuine upper bound on the entire logical scored set: a final-run fresh-score count that omits calibration is insufficient. Use a full store and Nbar covering every phase, with unreported scores bounded by F_min.
- Refutes: RF237. Concrete values: unscored mass 0 against claimed lower bounds 0.590 (m = 3, alpha = 0.5) and 0.007 (m = 10, alpha = 0.5); true mass outside T 0.795 and 0.504.


### RF238 — O-CERT C1(a): "For every scored S in T, pi(S)/pi(S-hat) = e^{F(S)-F(S-hat)} <= e^{-g}"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` C1(a) (verbatim):
  > (a) *Deterministic.* On 𝒪: for every S ∈ Ω, π(S) ≤ e^{F(S)}/Z_𝒯. For every A ⊆ 𝒯, π(A) ≤ Σ_A e^{F}/Z_𝒯. For every
  > scored S ∈ 𝒯, π(S)/π(Ŝ) = e^{F(S)−F(Ŝ)} ≤ e^{−g}.
- Refutation: CE190. The statement holds for S in T other than S-hat; as quantified it includes S = S-hat. O-CERT's C3(c) already writes it correctly ("For every S in S-bar minus {S-hat}").
- Replaced by: the same statement with S-hat excluded (A-REV9 repair; g defined only when a competitor exists, or an empty-maximum convention). The deterministic normaliser inequality Z >= Z_T is untouched ("The Z_T bound itself is VERIFIED").
- Who found it: A-REV9 (cross-family). O-VCERT's verdict for (a) was "VERIFIED" (a self-inclusive reading was not noticed by the same-family referee).


### CE190 — Counterexample to the self-inclusive gap inequality  [counterexample]
- Source: `A-REV9/REVIEW.md` "Certificate repairs and explicit counterexamples" (verbatim):
  > C1(a): take any two scored models with strict gap g>0 and set S=HPM. The displayed inequality becomes 1<=exp(-g). Exclude HPM; define g only when a competitor exists (or specify the empty-maximum convention).
- Refutes: RF238.


### RF239 — O-CERT C5 (tie-insensitive prose): "Hence ... Ŝ ≠ S0 implies F(S0) <= F(S-hat). So the miss is a posterior miss ... and by no search"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` Corollary C5 (verbatim):
  > In the setting of C4(a), on the event {S₀ ⊆ U}: Ŝ ≠ S₀ implies F(S₀) ≤ F(Ŝ). So the miss is a **posterior** miss in
  > the classification of THEORY_PRIORITIES §5, and by Prop 1 it cannot be repaired by any search, and (for same-size
  > S₀) by no size-only prior. Hence, for every data-measurable rule U = U(X, y, Ŝ),
  >
  >   P(𝒪, Ŝ ≠ S₀, F(S₀) > F(Ŝ)) ≤ P(𝒪, C4(a) fails for U) + P(𝒪, S₀ ⊄ U).
  >
  > *Proof.* Immediate from C4(a). ∎ The last term is a screening probability. It is the only place where statistics (and
  > hence asymptotics) re-enters. At n = 200 it is measured, not proved, in §4.
- Refutation: CE191. A weak score inequality F(S0) <= F(S-hat) does not exclude a *tie-related search miss*: S0 can win the lexicographic/size tie-break. What survives (A-REV9): "The C5 event inclusion only concerns strict score superiority and survives unchanged."
- Replaced by: C5 with strict inequality F(S0) < F(S-hat), or carry the total HPM order, and |S0| <= K (O-VCERT S3; A-REV9 repair). Kept as TH330.
- Who found it: O-VCERT (caveat S3, "tie caveat", verdict VERIFIED) and A-REV9 (ERROR).


### CE191 — Counterexample: identical predictor columns give equal-size, equal-score models  [counterexample]
- Source: `A-REV9/REVIEW.md` "Certificate repairs and explicit counterexamples" (verbatim):
  > C5: identical predictor columns 1 and 2 give F({1})=F({2}). Let the truth be {1}, the reported/scored alternative be {2}, and restrict the verified box to U={1,2} with singleton models maximizing (choose a response fit where one inclusion beats empty but redundant inclusion is penalized). The lexicographic rule prefers {1}. Weak score domination alone cannot exclude a tie-related search miss. The C5 event inclusion only concerns strict score superiority and survives unchanged.
- Refutes: RF239. (Exact ties are non-generic, O-VCERT cites T06; the point is logical.)


### RF240 — O-CERT C6 floating-point clause: "with the L and R claims checked at margin 2 eta_F, the bound becomes alpha e^eta + eps"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` Theorem C6 (verbatim):
  > for every n, p and data set, with no asymptotics, and without conditioning on completion. Given completion, only the
  > bound α·P(𝒜)/P(𝒪) is claimed. Under VAL-FP(η, ε) and SC(η_F), with the L and R claims checked at margin 2η_F, the bound
  > becomes α·e^{η} + ε.
  >
  > *Proof.* The L and R claims are deterministic functions of (X, y, Ŝ, 𝒯), true surely on 𝒪 under EX-A (C3, C4).
  > Under SC(η_F), every computed inequality with margin ≥ 2η_F implies the exact one. The G claims fail exactly on
  > {Z < αẐ} (C1(b)), whose output-level probability is ≤ α·P(𝒜). With floating point, VAL-FP gives
  > P(𝒪_E, Z < αẐ^{fp}) ≤ P(𝒪_E, Z < αe^{η}Ẑ̄) + ε ≤ αe^{η} + ε, by W2-BOOK Prop 2(f). ∎
- Refutation: CE192 (O-VCERT section 2.2) -- the clause omits the SC(eta_F) inflation of the G items: the deterministic Z >= Z_T no longer holds for the computed Z_T^fp. A-REV9: SC bounds complete scores, not the mixed ingredients of Phi(L,U) (see TH329).
- Replaced by: TH333 (R2). About the dropped factor: the O-CERT form "alpha e^eta + eps" is the weaker (valid) STATEMENTS.tex form of W2-BOOK Prop 2(f); R2 uses the PROOF.md form "alpha e^eta P(A) + eps" (see TH331 item (iii)). The RF is the missing inflation, not the P(A) factor.
- Who found it: O-VCERT [pos 763]; A-REV9 ("C6: GAP pending R1, FP inflation R2").


### CE192 — Counterexample (logical instance): Z_T^fp can exceed Z  [counterexample]
- Source: `O-VCERT/REPORT.md` section 2.2 (verbatim):
  > SC(η_F) allows F^fp(S) = F(S) + η_F on every S ∈ 𝒯. If most of the posterior sits in 𝒯 (Z_𝒯 ≈ Z), then
  > Z_𝒯^fp ≈ e^{η_F}Z > Z, and the "deterministic" bound π(Ŝ) ≤ e^{F^fp(Ŝ)}/Z_𝒯^fp can be false on every run. That leaves
  > an event outside the claimed α·e^η + ε. This is a logical gap, not an observed failure: η_F is tiny in practice.
- Refutes: RF240. (O-VCERT: "This is a logical gap, not an observed failure: eta_F is tiny in practice"; measured 3e-12 nats, TH334 remark 1.)


### RF241 — O-CERT overstatement: "It cannot certify confidence ... out of reach without PW2 or exact enumeration"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim: `O-CERT/REPORT.md` section 1 item 4 (verbatim) and section 5 first bullet:
  > 4. **Certificate card (item v): PROVED (candidate).** The run reports local, region and global one-sided items. Then
  >    P(output and some item on the card is false) ≤ 0.05·P(𝒜) ≤ 0.05 at every n, with no asymptotics and no conditioning
  >    on completion (Lemma RO). This is the right finite-n statement for n = 200 (Thm C6). The card certifies
  >    **optimality and uncertainty**: "Ŝ beats every model in an explicit region" and "π(Ŝ) is at most u". It cannot
  >    certify **confidence**: "π(Ŝ) ≥ ½" or "Ŝ is the global HPM" are out of reach without PW2 or exact enumeration.
  > - **A lower bound on π(Ŝ) from Ẑ alone.** It is impossible (C1(c)). The Markov direction is fixed: unbiased
  >   non-negative estimators only give lower bounds on Z, hence upper bounds on every posterior probability.
- Refutation (O-VCERT S2, verbatim in RV-6): C1(c) is only a non-implication from the properties of the law of Zhat; "Any certified upper bound on Z gives a sure lower bound on pi(S-hat): the inventory's UB, a Lemma-M box cover of all of Omega (impractical at p = 500, as O-CERT section 5 says), or T31's own remark Zhat >= e^{-Delta} Z with Delta = max_Omega d - min_Omega d."
- Replaced by: O-VCERT's wording: "not from unbiasedness; it needs an upper bound on Z (PW2, UB, enumeration, or a bound on Delta)". No CE (the alternatives are bounds that exist in principle). Tracked as the open item CJ234.
- Who found it: O-VCERT (S2). A-REV9 agrees with the corrected scope of C1(c).

- Source of the claim: `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` headline status line and Proposition 2 (verbatim):

  > For a null l, let u_l = r_{l|S₀}/‖r_{l|S₀}‖ and B_l := u_lᵀỹ. B_l ~ N(0, σ²) exactly, for every design and every θ. Let E := E_{S₀} ~ σ²χ²_{n−1−s₀}. Then
  >
  >   {F̃(S₀ + l) > F̃(S₀)} = { B_l² / (E + Ω₀) > τ_l },  τ_l := (n+1)(1 − e^{−κ⁺_l/ν})/n.
  >
  > Hence, with E' := E − B_l² ~ σ²χ²_{n−2−s₀} independent of B_l,
  >
  >   **P_add(l) = P( χ²₁ (1 − λ_l/(n+1)) > (λ_l − 1)(χ²_{n−2−s₀} + ω₀) )**,  λ_l = e^{κ⁺_l/ν}.
  >
  > Under the same PA, the union over nulls is exactly {max_l B_l²/τ_l > E + Ω₀}, where (B_l/σ)_l ~ N(0, Γ) with Γ_{ll'} = u_lᵀu_{l'}.
- Refutation: CE193.

Registry `OSWAP-P2` (and P1, P3): XF GAP; "predicted rates GAP (additional approximations and data reproduction remain; PA alone does not give the displayed add law)".

### CE193 — Counterexample construction: varying the Gaussian component in span(X_S0) changes the exact PA threshold  [counterexample]
- Source: `A-REV9/REVIEW.md` "Additional requested items and remaining work" (verbatim):
  > O-SWAP rates: GAP. Its projection remainder formula is an exact algebraic identity, but replacing the fitted energy W_S0 by its expectation is an additional approximation beyond PA. In Proposition 2 the exact PA event uses E+W_S0/(n+1)+btilde, whereas the displayed law uses deterministic Omega0. W_S0 is a nondegenerate noncentral chi-square quantity; varying the Gaussian component in span(X_S0) changes the exact threshold while keeping the orthogonal residual components fixed. Thus the displayed event identity is ERROR if asserted under PA alone. Restore the random fitted-energy term and integrate it, or explicitly label the extra approximation. A random Gaussian quadratic-form error is not uniformly bounded by 10^-3 nats merely because a typical error is small. The predicted aggregate rates and regenerated-data agreement require a separate saved-output/data-provenance audit; they are not LOCKABLE here.
- Refutes: RF242. Note: this is an analytic construction (A-REV9: "No experiments were executed; all counterexamples below are explicit analytic constructions"), not numerical parameters.

### RF244 — The engine heuristic error_bound() (v3_score.h:241-246, eta_eng) bounds the floating-point error of a score; R9 `global_certified` is a rigorous certificate  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim (implicit in the code, as described by W7-SEC, verbatim):
  > **Remark (exact-branch certificates, R9).** `v3_exact.R` certifies "global" when F̂(HPM) − η_eng(HPM) >
  > max_{S≠HPM}[F̂(S) + η_eng(S)], with the engine's heuristic η_eng (`v3_score.h:241–246`). This is a valid certificate
  > of the exact HPM whenever η_eng(S) ≥ |F̂(S) − F(S)| − η_C for all S; replacing η_eng by η_F − η_C of Theorem T33-S makes
  > it rigorous. **COUNTEREXAMPLE: η_eng is not a bound.** With y = x₁ + noise (y′y/Q ≈ 10²–10⁴), k ∈ {1, 2},
  > |log m̂ − log m| / η_eng reaches 1.17 at n = 10⁵ and 6.2 at n = 4·10⁶ (`scripts/t33_engine_bound_stress.py`,
  > `results/t33_engine_bound_stress.txt`, seed 20261104). The cause: η_eng's Q term ν(y′y/Q)(1 + k cond_H)·64ε has no
  > factor growing with n, while the rounding of the length-n dot products z_j and y′y in `data_init` grows like √n (in
  > these tests) relative to y′y and is multiplied by ν·y′y/Q. At n = 200 the heuristic held in every test with
  > ≥ 24× room (`results/t33_fp_check.txt`). Fixes (implementation, not done here): add a term
  > 64ε·ν·(y′y/Q)·√n (or ·n for a worst-case bound) to η_eng, or accumulate the dot products in long double or with
  > compensated summation.
- Refutation: CE194.
- Replaced by: Theorem T33-S (TH343): "replacing eta_eng by eta_F - eta_C of Theorem T33-S makes it rigorous"; implementation fixes recommended (add a term 64 eps nu (y'y/Q) sqrt(n), or accumulate the dot products in long double or with compensated summation). Registry: `T33-errbound` COUNTEREXAMPLE ("implementation fix recommended (not a method change)"); `REGISTRY_v2` section D `error_bound`; FUTURE_WORK FW16 (K107). The n = 200 study is not affected (the heuristic held with >= 24x room).
- Outside-scope consequence (verbatim, W7-SEC section 7): - **`error_bound` feeds R9's `global_certified`** (`v3_exact.R`) on the exact branch. With large n and small p (the exact branch's typical regime), a certificate can be issued with an η that underestimates the true error by up to 6×. A wrong certificate needs a near-tie within ~10⁻³ nats, so it is rare but possible.
- Who found it: W7-SEC (author's own check; A-REV9 deferred).

### RF248 — O-SWAP predictors T1 (independence across all one-move events) and T1-lo (clusters perfectly dependent)  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim (verbatim, `O-SWAP/REPORT.md` section 3 Theorem 4 paragraph and section 6):
  > The **predictor T1** is P̂_T1(X) = 1 − Π_e(1 − p_e): independence across events, with p_e from Props. 1–3 and the exact κ's. It is an approximation, not a theorem; its accuracy is reported in §4. The **lower bracket T1-lo** treats each cluster as perfectly dependent and the clusters as independent. The clusters are: the adds of the nulls in one generator group of 5; and, for each truth j, {drop_j} ∪ {swap_{jl} : all l}. The per-cell prediction is the average of P̂(X) over the 100 actual study designs of that cell.
  > - **Independence across all one-move events (T1) overshoots at c = 0.5** (§4). For a fixed truth j, the s₀(p − s₀) swap events all share A_j: when A_j comes out low, every swap (j, ·) and the drop of j become likely together. Treating them as independent double-counts. T1 is fine at c = 1, where all events are rare. Prop. 6 / T2 repairs this by conditioning on A_j and E.
  > - **The cluster-max lower bracket (T1-lo) is far too low** (§4). Inside a truth's cluster the events are not perfectly dependent: different group-mates l compete through independent Z_{jl}.
- Refutation (data; section 4.3 item 4): "T1 overshoots by 40-50% (326 / 383), and T1-lo undershoots by half (118 / 141)" at c = 0.5 (observed 230 / 259); fine at c = 1 (46 / 43 against 40 / 37). Mid-run note [pos 578]: "T1 overpredicts S5 badly at c = 0.5 (84 against 49)".
- Replaced by: Prop. 6 / predictor T2 (TH342), itself an approximation (CJ232).
- Who found it: O-SWAP (self-correction).


### RF249 — A union bound over Hamming balls closes an upper bound on Pi(X)  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim (implicit route; recorded as a failed route, `API-N200/PROOF.md` section 3, verbatim):
  > **Why a union bound over Hamming balls cannot close it (recorded as a failed route).** The distance-2 supersets alone number C(p − s₀, 2) ≈ 1.2·10⁵ at p = 500. Under PA with orthonormal residualised nulls, the two-add gain is g(B_l² + B_{l′}²) − 2κ⁺ with g convex, g(0) = 0, and (B_l, B_{l′}) ~ N(0, I): the union bound Σ P(χ²₂ > 4κ⁺(1+η)) ≈ 1.2·10⁵·e^{−2κ⁺(1+η)} ≈ 0.07 at p = 500, c = 1, the same size as the whole one-add rate. The bound is loose because the two-add event is almost entirely contained in the one-add events: by convexity g(x + y) ≥ g(x) + g(y), so "two-add beats, neither single add beats" forces both B_l² and B_{l′}² into the shell [thr − c_n, thr] with c_n ≈ g(2·thr) − 2g(thr) ≈ ν(thr/Q)² ≈ 0.5 nats; the shell has probability ≈ 7·10⁻⁵ per null, so the two-add-only event has probability ≈ C(p − s₀, 2)(7·10⁻⁵)² ≈ 6·10⁻⁴ for orthogonal nulls. **PROOF SKETCH** for orthogonal nulls only; for correlated nulls the quadratic form (B_l, B_{l′})Γ⁻¹(B_l, B_{l′})ᵀ ~ χ²₂ remains exact (central) but the shell argument must be redone in the Γ-metric, and the drops/swaps at distance 2 are not covered. A rigorous upper bound on Π(X) via "L plus a controlled remainder" is the research item (needs escalation).
- Refutation: CE195.
- Replaced by: nothing yet (CJ230); the convexity "shell" argument is a PROOF SKETCH for orthogonal nulls only.
- Who found it: API-N200 (Fable 5.1). Not reviewed.


### CE195 — The distance-2 superset union bound is as large as the whole one-add rate: about 0.07 at p = 500, c = 1  [counterexample]
- Source: `API-N200/PROOF.md` section 3 and `API-N200/REPORT.md` section 5 (verbatim):
  > - **A rigorous finite-n upper bound on Π(X).** Union bounds over Hamming balls fail: the distance-2 superset union bound alone is ≈ 0.07 at p = 500, c = 1, as large as the entire one-add rate, because the two-add events are almost entirely inside the one-add events. The convexity "shell" argument bounds the two-add-only remainder by ≈ 6·10⁻⁴ for orthogonal nulls (PROOF SKETCH) but does not cover correlated nulls, drops or swaps at distance 2, or distance ≥ 3. This is the finite-n face of T03 and is the research item.
- Numbers: C(p - s0, 2) ~ 1.2e5 at p = 500; union bound ~ 1.2e5 x e^{-2 kappa+ (1+eta)} ~ 0.07 (same size as the whole one-add rate); the two-add-only event, by the convexity shell argument, has probability about 6e-4 for orthogonal nulls (shell probability ~ 7e-5 per null, c_n ~ 0.5 nats).
- Refutes: RF249.

### RF251 — HQ premise in the O-VCERT brief: "the size prior is NOT monotone in |S|; the marginal likelihood is"  [refuted claim]
- Source of the claim (verbatim, HQ brief to O-VCERT, [pos 729], `transcript/traces/traces_03_551-807.md`): "Be adversarial on: the direction of every inequality; whether Lemma M's monotonicity holds for the ACTUAL score (the size prior is NOT monotone in |S|; the marginal likelihood is; check the exact Phi(L, U) construction)".
- Refutation (verbatim, `O-VCERT/REPORT.md` section 3 item 2):
  > 2. **Lemma M against the actual score.**
  >    - HQ's premise needs a correction. Under BB(1,p), **both** the per-model weight w(k) and the size marginal
  >      C(p,k)w(k) are non-increasing in k: the marginal ratio is (p−k)/(2p−1−k) < 1. The object that is *not* monotone is
  >      the marginal likelihood m(S), and hence F. In the tests, m rises on 185,095 additions and falls on 291,065
  >      (`results/vcert_check.txt` §1).
  >    - Endpoint evaluation max(F(L), F(U)) underestimates the box maximum in 2,764 of 6,561 boxes. So the split into
  >      three separately monotone factors is essential, and O-CERT's Φ does it correctly.
  >    - Engine Q: the §6.13 branch Q = ‖y − X_Sβ̂‖² + (‖X_Sβ̂‖² + ‖β̂‖²)/n with β̂ = nH_S⁻¹z_S is algebraically the same
  >      function. Expanding gives yᵀy − 2zᵀβ̂ + β̂ᵀH_Sβ̂/n = yᵀy − zᵀβ̂.
  >    - Lemma M(d) gives Q_S ≥ yᵀy/(n+1). So the trigger Q < 10⁻⁸yᵀy can never fire in exact arithmetic when n + 1 < 10⁸;
  >      the branch is a pure floating-point safeguard. (A free corollary; it answers O-CERT §6's second escalation item.)
- Replaced by: Lemma M (LM204): Q_S decreasing, D_S increasing and w non-increasing; the marginal likelihood m(S), hence F, is *not* monotone, so the box bound must take w and D at L and Q at U (TH329).
- Who found it: O-VCERT (same family).


### CE196 — m(S) is not monotone, and endpoint evaluation under-bounds the box maximum  [counterexample]
- Source: `O-VCERT/REPORT.md` section 3 item 2 (verbatim, quoted above under RF251) and `results/vcert_check.txt` section 1-2.
- Numbers: "m rises on 185,095 additions and falls on 291,065"; "Endpoint evaluation max(F(L), F(U)) underestimates the box maximum in 2,764 of 6,561 boxes".

### Dead ends and corrections (Theme 9)

Certificates (O-CERT, O-VCERT, A-REV9)
- **"Unscored" versus "not in T".** O-CERT C1(b), the C1 remark and C6 item G3 claimed a lower bound on the *unscored* posterior mass; the reported store T is only the top-(40p + 1) set, so scored-but-unreported models carry mass. Refuted by O-VCERT with an exhaustive factor design (n = 40, p = 10; RF237, CE189); repaired by R1 (TH332); A-REV9 adds that an optional unscored bound needs a score count covering calibration as well as the final run [pos 763], [pos 917]-[pos 919]. O-CERT's own `cert_run.R` already printed the correct phrase.
- **Self-inclusive gap inequality.** C1(a) quantified over all scored S in T including the HPM; found only by the cross-family reviewer (RF238, CE190); the same-family referee had marked (a) VERIFIED.
- **Weak versus strict inequality in C5.** The posterior-miss certificate needs F(S0) < F(S-hat) (or the total HPM order) and |S0| <= K; duplicate columns give an equal-score search-miss instance (RF239, CE191). Exact ties are non-generic (T06), but the statement must carry them.
- **Floating-point clause of C6.** Missing SC(eta_F) inflation (RF240, CE192, R2 = TH333); A-REV9 further requires interval bounds for each ingredient of Phi(L,U), because SC controls complete scores only (TH329). **The P(A) factor:** O-CERT's FP clause is alpha e^eta + eps, O-VCERT's is alpha e^eta P(A) + eps; the discrepancy comes from W2-BOOK's two forms of Prop 2(f) (PROOF.md versus STATEMENTS.tex); the O-CERT form is weaker and valid, so this is not an error.
- **Overreach on "confidence".** "Cannot certify confidence without PW2 or enumeration" (RF241) overstated C1(c): any certified upper bound on Z gives a sure lower bound on pi(S-hat). Open item CJ234. Even a correct fit carried pi(S-hat) <= 0.37 at n = 200 (CJ245).
- **O-CERT section 4 conflict (registry C21).** O-VCERT reviewed head 17e7f15 where section 4 was empty and `results/` absent: "every numeric claim of O-CERT ... is therefore unsupported". Heads 0edc58f/332bf3e added the illustration on four study fits and Remark C6'. A-REV9 read the 332bf3e text but states that historical numbers were not reproduced. The W8-SYNTH sentence "O-CERT section 4 illustration is empty" is stale for the final head but is the last review record (CJ245).
- **HQ premise corrected.** The brief to O-VCERT said the size prior is not monotone and the marginal likelihood is; the opposite holds (RF251, CE196 [pos 729]). The box bound must use w and D at L and Q at U.
- **Cost heuristic.** "The tree grows like 2^(ambiguous variables)" is a heuristic remark, not part of C4 (CJ248).
- **GUARD scope.** C1/C6 inherit W2-BOOK's Lemma RO/GUARD; A-REV4 showed the full-output GUARD claim false (timing/allocation metadata) and the stop-only statistical reading valid; A-REV9 uses the latter.

Predicted miss rates (O-SWAP)
- **Independence predictor T1 overshoots at c = 0.5 (326/383 against 230/259), the cluster-maximum T1-lo undershoots by half (RF248).** T2 (TH342) is an approximation (+0 to +9 points per cell against the exact MC at c = 0.5).
- **PA is not enough (RF242, CE193).** The displayed superset law replaces the random fitted energy W_S0 by its expectation; A-REV9 calls the displayed identity an ERROR under PA alone and the predicted aggregate rates a GAP. Nobody checked O-SWAP's algebra independently (the second reader requested in its section 7).
- **"4 no-output fits" (RF243).** The true number of stopped fits is 6 (S-ELS); O-SWAP rescaled cells to 100, producing 259 where S-ELS has 258 posterior misses at p = 1000, c = 0.5.
- **Open:** rigorous bracket for T2 (CJ232), whole-model floor (CJ233), PA error to probability (CJ236), SuSiE/SSL thresholds (CJ231).

Theorem N200 (API-N200)
- **Union bound over Hamming balls fails** as a route to an upper bound on Pi(X): the distance-2 superset bound alone is about 0.07 at p = 500, c = 1 (RF249, CE195). The remainder Pi - P0(L) is only measured (<= 1.1 points per cell), not bounded (CJ230, FW14).
- **T21's middle term is vacuous at n = 200** (2 E0 delta1 > 1 because the p - s0 supersets with kappa+ about 7 nats make pi(S0) < 1/2 even when S0 is the mode; exact p = 12 enumeration gives 0.934-1.812 against Pi between 0.077 and 0.789 in the nine tabulated rows, CJ244). The finite-n content of N200 is replacing {pi(S0) <= 1/2} by {S-dagger != S0}.
- **A priori discovery bounds are vacuous** (Q_f pi0(S0) <= 1e-6 because of sigma^2-dilution); the term is measured, 0 of 2,394 (CJ237, CJ222).
- **Minor internal inconsistency** in the 24-cell text (the "four larger" cells include z = -1.5; CJ243); the "2,370 of 2,394" figure is not located in S-ELS (CJ222 note). Observed 571 against predicted 558.1 is an excess of about 13 fits that is not bounded by any theorem (the prediction is a lower bracket plus a measured term).
- **Author-only status.** No same- or cross-family check; the proposed check is a Lean formalisation next to `T21HPM.lean`.

Numerics (W7-SEC) and data (S-ELS, O-LS0)
- **Engine `error_bound()` is not a bound at large n** (RF244, CE194: ratio 1.17 at n = 1e5, 6.2 at n = 4e6); n = 200 unaffected (>= 24x room); R9 `global_certified` on the exact branch inherits it; fix recommended, not a method change; FW16.
- **A-priori epsilon of VAL-FP is vacuous at the study's budgets** (RF250); path-free argument stalls (MH self-loop probability 1 - alpha is not multiplicatively stable); epsilon must be measured by replay (CJ235).
- **Worst-case floating-point bounds are loose:** the data-free form allows eta_Q about 4.6e-3 nats at n = 200, K = 100 and is vacuous at n = 1000, K = 500; the a-posteriori form is about 100 times above the observed errors (TH343). Demmel's criterion (Higham Thm 10.7) was used from memory; LIB (glibc log/lgamma) is measured for one container only.
- **A-REV9 did not review W7-SEC** ("GAP in this review: deferred"); it explicitly declines to endorse "numerical_failure impossible for every p, y" without the FP/NOUF/LIB/SMALL domain (TH344). T32(i) remains SAME-FAMILY-ONLY with a slip in W5's corollary proof (RF245) and an fp-pilot addendum (+1,320,960 on 2.676e11, TH347).
- **S-ELS versus O-LS0 numbers agree** (cross-check table in the data block); the only discrepancies are the move cap (RF246), the quoted F(S0) agreement (1e-12 versus 5e-8 for different data copies) and API-N200's 2,370 figure. O-LS0's pairing compares F(LS0 best) on Owls with F(S-hat) on NOTS; its margins (>= 0.002) are far above the 5e-8 agreement but the production HPM was not rescored on the Owls data. The in-engine integrated LS0 test remains unrun (CJ229).
- **ELS-3** cannot reproduce W3-VT37R's sampled F(S0) > F(S_c); this settles Lemma 0(b) on the study data only, not as logic (theme 4).
- **W8-SYNTH read the branches too early** (RF247) and its n = 200 disclosure draft needs the corrections listed under CJ239: "about 0.8" is the pooled median pi0(R2) (per-cell 0.20-0.96); the 98% Gibbs-flip figure is preliminary; the favourable-n thresholds (590-730, 800-1,600, 1,050-3,200) disagree and are best omitted (CJ247).
- **Lesson.** At n = 200 every observed error is a posterior miss (565 of 2,400; 0 search misses; 6 stopped); the finite-n content that survives review is the deterministic part (Lemma M, Z >= Z_T, exact ratios, strict-score C5 inclusion, exact boxes), the one-sided Markov part with R1, and the order-exact composition N200; everything that predicts the observed rates is an approximation or a measurement.
