## Part A. The seven theoretical targets of Felipe's first draft and their fates

The draft ("Local-to-Global Bayesian Computation", pdf attached at [pos 482]; text extracted at [pos 485]) proposes local block posteriors, a merge, and a correction toward the global posterior by importance sampling, Metropolis-Hastings or SMC tempering. The draft itself is not in the archive. Its theoretical targets are known verbatim from the brief HQ gave to F-DRAFT (traces_02, tool input at [pos 489]):

⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.00; best match the cited source). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
> Its theoretical targets are:
> - Prop 1: MH exactness;
> - Prop 2: SMC consistency for a local-to-global path;
> - §5.3 Theorem 1: weight stability under weak cross-block dependence (the divergence between the product-of-blocks proposal and the full posterior is controlled by cross-block covariance; bounded importance-weight variance);
> - §5.4: approximation error (KL, TV, PIP and joint-inclusion error);
> - §3.2: naive union merge distorts uncertainty;
> - §13: convergence of estimates of E[h(θ)], and the partition as a random variable to be inferred ("stochastic scheduling").

(§13 contains two targets, so there are seven: Prop 1, Prop 2, §5.3, §5.4, §3.2, §13.1 and §13.3.) HQ's first mapping table is at [pos 563] (rows for these seven plus "Risk 2, novelty"); F-DRAFT's final classification is in `F-DRAFT/CROSSWALK.md` §1 (classes (a) already covered, (b) partly, (c) compatible but absent, (d) incompatible) and HQ's relay of it at [pos 616]. The one-sentence verdict of F-DRAFT:

> ## 0. The one-sentence verdict
>
> The draft's design is realised by v3 exactly: π₀ is the merged product of block-local tables, the bridge
> γ_φ = γ₀ e^{φ d} is the draft's eq. (2) with L̃ = ∏_b m(S ∩ C_b)/m(∅)^{J−1}, and the correction is SMC with Gibbs, swap and
> an independence (= the draft's MH) move. Every validity target of the draft (Prop 1, Prop 2, the frozen-run estimates) is
> locked. The draft's one substantive theory target, §5.3 "weight stability under weak cross-block dependence", is
> **not** covered and, as drafted, is **false for v3's tables**: under *exact* block orthogonality the composite start still
> differs from the posterior by a Θ(n) term coming from the per-block integration of σ² against the full response
> (the "dilution" that W3-VEXP found to mask the start at n = 200). The right statement (NEW_TARGETS Theorem W) is a
> dilution theorem: in the favourable block-orthogonal regime the one-step importance weights have
> log(1 + χ²(π‖π₀)) ≈ R²_pop · log p − ½ log n, with R²_pop the population R², so one-shot importance correction fails for
> p ≫ n even when the start is right, while the adaptive ESS grid needs only a bounded number of stages. That theorem,
> a rigorous "naive merge fails" proposition (NM) and a partition remark (P) are the three things worth adding.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/CROSSWALK.md`)*

Lemma W1 (PROVED, trivial): under exact BO, d(S) = ν[Σ_b log(1−ξ_b) − log(1−Σ_b ξ_b)] ≥ 0 (ξ_b the block's shrunken R²), zero iff one block carries all the R²; with a *known* σ² the same tables give d ≡ 0 and π₀ = π exactly. So the BO discrepancy is entirely the shared-σ² coupling ("dilution"), of size Θ(n) on signal-bearing models (254 nats at n = 800 in the check). What matters for weights is its *dispersion* over the bulk: Lemma W2 gives log[π(S₀+l)/π(S₀)] − log[π₀(S₀+l)/π₀(S₀)] = κ_b·G_l with κ_b = Δ_{T_b}/v_{T_b} the dilution fraction (00_COMMON's leakage quantities) and G_l the posterior gain; checked to two decimals. **Theorem W** (two-sided rate; lower bound PROVED, upper bound PROOF SKETCH): favourable BO regime ⇒ log(1+χ²(π‖π₀)) = [R²_pop log p − ½ log n]₊ + O_P(log log p). O-WSTAB's own regime dichotomy (WS5.3, TH353/TH354) and WS6(d) (TH356) say: weights are stable when the start already sees the truth; the one-step $\chi^2$ can nevertheless diverge (zero cross-block correlation). ## Part B. F-DRAFT's own statements (NEW_TARGETS.md) and their fates

### CJ256 — F-DRAFT Theorem W (a)(b)(c): one-step weight stability in the favourable BO regime  [conjecture (proposed theorem); partly refuted]
- Source (authoritative): `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` section "W. One-step weight stability in the favourable block-orthogonal regime"; summary table at the end; positions: [pos 489-491 (launch), 616 (reported)].
- Statement (verbatim):
> ## W. One-step weight stability in the favourable block-orthogonal regime
>
> **Theorem W.** Assume G, BO, SE-blk(φ₀), BM-blk, R-lite (p ≤ n^A, ‖μ‖² ≤ Mn), s₀ fixed, the v3 blocks (|C_b| ≤ B ≤ 16), and
> that the signal occupies at most s₀ blocks (automatic). Let R² := R²_pop ∈ (0, 1) be fixed. Then:
>
> (a) [lower bound, PROVED modulo W2] For every ε > 0, with P₀-probability → 1,
>     1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≥ p^{R² − ε} n^{−1/2}.
>
> (b) [upper bound, PROOF SKETCH] For every ε > 0, with P₀-probability → 1,
>     1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ 1 + p^{R² + ε} n^{−1/2} + o(1).
>
> (c) [expected sharp form, CONJECTURE] log(1 + χ²(π‖π₀)) = [R² log p − ½ log n]₊ + O_P(log log p).
>
> Equivalently the one-step ESS fraction ρ_Ω(0, 1) → 1 if R² log p − ½ log n → −∞ and → 0 if it → +∞. KL(π‖π₀) and
> TV(π, π₀) are O_P(n^{−1/2}·polylog) throughout (Prop W4), so the dichotomy is invisible to KL and TV.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Proof route (Summary:) in F-DRAFT: layer decomposition of $1+\chi^2=\sum_S\pi(S)^2/\pi_0(S)$; single-null layer via Lemma W2 and extreme values; multi-extra layers via a "second-moment aggregation lemma" (T22(i) with squared odds) — the crux, which F-DRAFT left as a skeleton.
- Status history: F-DRAFT summary table: W(a) "PROVED modulo W2"; W(b) "PROOF SKETCH (crux: second-moment aggregation)"; W(c) "CONJECTURE" (REGISTRY_v2 rows `FD-W(a)` PROVED-UNDER, `FD-W(b)` PROOF SKETCH, `FD-W(c)` CONJECTURE; no SF, no XF). Because W(a) rests on Lemma W2 (ERROR per A-REV4, RF254), its "PROVED modulo W2" is moot. O-WSTAB then proved the ORTH version: the lower bound is TH362 (d) lower half; the **upper bound W(b) and the sharp form W(c) are FALSE on the divergent side** (RF252, RF253, CE197); they hold on the convergent side ($2Ar<1$) in the form TH362(d). The threshold $2Ar\lessgtr1$ of F-DRAFT is correct (O-WSTAB headline item 4: "The threshold of W (Ar ≶ ½) is correct, and so are W(a) and, on the convergent side, W(b)").
- Depends on: TH350, LM212, TH116 (T22(i)), TH138 (W1-EXP Thm 2). Feeds: replaced by TH362 (card M2 uses H-ORTH only); FW: none.

### CJ257 — F-DRAFT Conjecture W' (ideal grid stage count)  [conjecture; resolved under ORTH by TH363, conditional corollary TH367]
- Source: `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` section "W′. Stage count of the ideal adaptive grid"; positions: [pos 616, 733 (O-STAGES brief)].
- Statement (verbatim):
> ## W′. Stage count of the ideal adaptive grid (favourable BO regime)
>
> **Conjecture W′.** Under the hypotheses of Theorem W, let the ideal grid be: from u, take the largest v ≤ 1 with
> ρ_Ω(u, v) ≥ 0.9 (60 halvings), until v = 1. Let g := log(√n/9)/(R² log p). Then w.p. → 1 the number of stages is
>
>     T_ideal = ⌈log₂(1 + 1/g)⌉ + O(1)   if g > 0,   and T_ideal = 1 if g ≥ 1;
>
> in particular T_ideal = O(1) whenever p ≤ n^A (since 1/g ≤ 2AR²/(1 − 2 log 9/log n)).
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Status history: F-DRAFT: "CONJECTURE (PROOF SKETCH for the recursion given the χ² law)"; obligations (1) monotonicity of $v\mapsto\rho_\Omega(u,v)$ (closed by O-STAGES Lemma 1, LM217), (2) ideal vs V-restricted grid (still OPEN, CJ265). O-WSTAB: **Theorem W' proved under ORTH** with $T_{\rm ideal}\in\{1,2\}$ (TH363), which is consistent with, but sharper than, "$\lceil\log_2(1+1/g)\rceil+O(1)$". O-STAGES: Corollary W' conditional on (LL) (TH367). Numerical check by F-DRAFT: "T_ideal = 1 in all BO runs at n = 800 (p = 12, g ≫ 1), 6 at n = 200 with one truth per block, 2 with both in one block."
- UNCERTAIN: F-DRAFT's $g=\log(\sqrt n/9)/(R^2\log p)$ vs O-WSTAB's $G_n=\log n/(2r\log p)$; they agree to $O(\log\log p/\log p)$ in the regime $p=n^{A+o(1)}$ (both are $\approx1/(2Ar)$); not a conflict.

### CJ258 — F-DRAFT Lemma W3 (cross-block covariance term)  [conjecture / PROOF SKETCH]
- Source: `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` section W3. Statement (verbatim):
> ## W3. The cross-block covariance term (the draft's mechanism)
>
> **Lemma W3 (PROOF SKETCH).** Drop BO. Let R_S = D_S + E_S with D_S block diagonal and E_S the cross-block correlations
> among the members of S, and β̂_b := D_{S_b}⁻¹ρ_{S_b} the block-local standardised LS coefficients (ρ = correlations with
> y). Then
>
>     d(S) = d_BO(S) + (n/2) · Σ_{b≠b′} β̂_bᵀ E_{bb′} β̂_{b′} / (1 − R²_S) + O(n ‖E_S‖² ‖β̂‖²) + O(|S|/(nφ₀²)),
>
> where d_BO is the expression of Lemma W1 evaluated at the block R²'s R²_{S_b} = ρ_{S_b}ᵀD_{S_b}⁻¹ρ_{S_b}, and the
> last term is the determinant non-additivity (W1-EXP Lemma 1.2). The table side also acquires leakage: for a null l with
> δ_{T,l} ≠ 0 the table gain is (δ_{T,l} + σZ)²/(2v_T) instead of σ²Z²/(2v_T) (T22(iii)'s family; CL(L) of W1-EXP).
> *Sketch:* Neumann expansion of (D + E)⁻¹ in ρᵀ(D+E)⁻¹ρ, then −ν log(1 − R²) − Σ_b[−ν log(1 − R²_b)] as in W1.
> **Status: PROOF SKETCH.** This is the draft's "divergence controlled by cross-block covariance", now a second additive
> term beside dilution, first order in E_S and scaled by n.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Status history: PROOF SKETCH (registry `FD-W3`, no SF, no XF). O-WSTAB never proved it: REPORT §5: "Uniform perturbation in the cross-block Gram ([PF] WS4) controls |d − d_σ| only when ε_S = o(1/n)... So W3 (the cross-block term) stays at [FD]'s PROOF SKETCH level, and Theorem W is stated for ORTH." Its role was taken by TH351 (WS4, PROVED, perturbative scale only) and, in the theorem meeting, by M2(a1) ($|d_X|\le b_X$, K11, a PROOF SKETCH of Seat C).

### CJ259 — F-DRAFT Proposition W4 (KL and TV small while χ² large)  [conjecture / PROOF SKETCH; A-REV4 GAP]
- Source: `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` section W4. Statement (verbatim):
> ## W4. Divergence versus weight variance
>
> **Proposition W4 (PROOF SKETCH).** In the favourable BO regime of Theorem W,
>     KL(π‖π₀) ≤ (1 − π₀(S₀))(1 + o(1)) + Σ_{l∉S₀} π(S₀+l)·LR_l = O_P(2^B√(log n) n^{−1/2}·polylog p),
>     TV(π, π₀) ≤ (1 − π(S₀)) + (1 − π₀(S₀)) = O_P(2^B√(log n) n^{−1/2}),
> while log(1 + χ²(π‖π₀)) = [R² log p − ½ log n]₊ + O_P(log log p). *Sketch:* W0(iii) with E_{π₀}e^d ≥ π₀(S₀)e^{d(S₀)}; the
> null layer of E_π[d − d(S₀)] has summands p^{−1}n^{−1/2}e^{Z²/2}·κZ²/2 whose sum is p^{0}n^{−1/2}·L(p) (tail index 1: no
> polynomial growth). Thus the draft's "divergence small ⇒ weights stable" is false in the χ² sense that matters for
> importance sampling; the content of §5.3 is entirely in the step from KL/TV to χ².
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Status history: PROOF SKETCH (`FD-W4`). A-REV4 DRAFTS_CHECK: "F-DRAFT W4: VERIFIED TV bound; GAP for KL rate and chi-square assertion" (full text in the Part C quote). O-WSTAB then **proved** the replacement: TH362(f): $TV(\pi,\pi_0)\le\ell^*=O_P(\sqrt{\log p/n})$ and $KL(\pi\|\pi_0)=O_P((\log p)^{3/2}/\sqrt n)$ in all cases (VERIFIED, A-REV9 W(f)); the exact KL bound of A-REV4 is TH379; the abstract separation of KL/TV from $\chi^2$ is CE203. The "polylog" in F-DRAFT's KL rate is $(\log p)^{3/2}$ in O-WSTAB.

### TH377 — F-DRAFT W'' (two-state part): path length $\int_0^1 sd_{q_\phi}(d)\,d\phi\le\pi$  [proposition]
- Source: `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` section "W″"; positions: [pos 616 (implicitly)]; later [pos 1038 area, O-STAGES].
- Statement (verbatim):
> ## W″. A masked-regime crossing costs a bounded number of stages
>
> **Proposition W″ (two-state part).** Let the bridge be restricted to two states {S°, S₀} with log-odds
> log[q_φ(S₀)/q_φ(S°)] = c₀ + φD, D = d(S₀) − d(S°). Then Var_{q_φ}(d) = D²a_φ(1−a_φ) with a_φ = q_φ(S₀), and
>
>     ∫₀¹ sd_{q_φ}(d) dφ → π   as D → ∞   (exactly ∫_{a_0}^{a_1} da/√(a(1−a)) ≤ π),
>
> independent of D. With small steps, χ²(q_{φ+Δ}‖q_φ) = Δ²Var_{q_φ}(d)(1 + o(1)), so the ESS-0.9 rule (Δ·sd ≤ 1/3) needs
> ≈ 3π ≈ 9.4 stages across the crossing whatever the size of the odds gap D (Θ(n) in Prop NM; c log p + (c/2) log n +
> Θ(n) under T27). **PROVED** (calculus; d²/dφ² log Z̄_φ = Var_{q_φ}(d)). Check: 14 and 16 stages in the proxy-split
> runs, where the window is not exactly two-state.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Status history: **PROVED** (calculus) for the two-state integral $\int_{a_0}^{a_1}da/\sqrt{a(1-a)}\le\pi$ (`FD-W″-two`, no SF, no XF). The inference "so the ESS-0.9 rule needs ≈ 3π ≈ 9.4 stages whatever the odds gap" is NOT proved and is false at the production level: O-STAGES Theorem L(iii) holds only as $c\to0$, and the two-state family has $L\le\pi$ while $T^*\to\infty$ (RF255, RF258, CE201). A-REV4: "The O(1) discrete ideal-grid assertion is not established by W″'s thermodynamic-length calculation: a local small-step approximation and finite integral do not prove a uniform finite-threshold discrete stage bound."
- Depends on: TH111 (T13). Feeds: none (superseded by TH365, TH368); the path-length fact itself is K28 (CONFIRMED-D, KNOWN, cite Syed et al. 2024).

### TH375 — F-DRAFT Proposition P (the partition as a random variable)  [proposition]
- Source: `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` section "P. The partition as a random variable"; positions: [pos 616]. Statement (verbatim):
> ## P. The partition as a random variable
>
> **Proposition P.** (i) [validity is partition-free; PROVED] For any partition 𝒫 of [p] into blocks of size ≤ K and any
> positive tables, T09, T12, T13, T21, T22(i)(ii)(iv) and T31(i) hold with 𝒫 in place of the method's partition
> (their proofs use only the product form of γ₀, γ₀ > 0 and the move definitions; T22(i)'s statement already quantifies
> over all partitions and positive tables). Hence if 𝒫 is drawn from any law Λ measurable with respect to (X, y) and
> streams 0–9, all of them hold conditionally on 𝒫 and E[Ẑ] = Σ_𝒫 Λ(𝒫)E[Ẑ | 𝒫] = Z. The target π does not depend on 𝒫.
> Therefore "the partition as a random variable to be inferred" is not an inference about the model; it is an adaptation
> of the start (like the schedule), and its objects are π₀^𝒫(S₀) (delivery), the dilution fractions κ_b(𝒫) and the
> leakages δ_{T,l}(𝒫) (weight stability; Theorem W, Lemma W3), and Z̄₀^𝒫.
>
> (ii) [mixture start; PROVED, elementary] For partitions 𝒫₁..𝒫_m and weights λ_i > 0, Σλ_i = 1, let
> π₀^{mix} := Σ_i λ_i π₀^{(i)}. Then: π₀^{mix} is exactly samplable (draw i, then the backward sampler of T09(i));
> its density is π₀^{mix}(S) = Σ_i λ_i γ₀^{(i)}(S)/Z̄₀^{(i)} (m table lookups and the m exact normalisers); the bridge
> γ_φ := (π₀^{mix})^{1−φ}(ϖBF)^{φ}·const with d^{mix}(S) = log(ϖ(S)BF(S)) − log π₀^{mix}(S) ends at π, and every move of
> T09(ii) with the independence proposal from π₀^{mix} is q_φ-invariant (T09's proof uses only exact sampling and an
> evaluable density). Moreover π₀^{mix}(S₀) ≥ max_i λ_i π₀^{(i)}(S₀) and sup_S π/π₀^{mix} ≤ min_i λ_i⁻¹ sup_S π/π₀^{(i)}, so
> one favourable partition in the mixture bounds the iid discovery budget of T11(iii) by that partition's budget times
> 1/λ_i, and the independence-sampler rate (W0(iv)) likewise. Cost: m times the table and convolution work of §6.3.
> This is the draft's "multiple random partitions" (§8.4) and a method extension not in the 2,400 fits (investment rule);
> it is the natural companion of T39 and of W3-VEXP's finding that packing both hubs of a linked pair into one block
> removes the LH masking.
>
> (iii) [stochastic scheduling; PROVED by T12] An adaptive schedule is valid iff it is frozen before the final run's
> randomness (CAL); T12(iv) shows that a state-dependent stopping rule inside the final run breaks E[Ẑ] = Z. v3's
> calibration plus frozen final run is exactly this.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Status history: PROVED (registry `FD-P`: "PROVED"; no SF, no XF; part (ii) is "elementary" and is a method extension not in the 2,400 fits: "investment rule"). A-REV6 did not list it. HQ [pos 616]: "Validity doesn't depend on the partition, so the partition is a design choice of the start, not a parameter to infer."
- Depends on: TH107 (T09), TH110 (T12), TH111 (T13), TH115 (T21), TH116 (T22(i)(ii)(iv)), TH120 (T31(i)). Feeds: none (campaign-only); mixture start (ii) developed as O-MIX (theme 3).

A-REV4 (Astra, GPT-6; launched [pos 677-678]; covers W2-T26, W2-BOOK, F-DRAFT, A-DRAFT §2) summary line: "**Overall: GAP.** ... F-DRAFT contains two explicit false formulas, and its sharp weight-divergence claims are not proved." Verdict table rows for F-DRAFT (`A-REV4/REVIEW.md`): "F-DRAFT NM | ERROR", "F-DRAFT W1 | VERIFIED", "F-DRAFT W2 | ERROR", "F-DRAFT W4 | GAP" (full rows: NM "Population-rate expansion has a false O_P(1) remainder; further normalisation/mode/repair claims have gaps."; W1 "BO algebra and known-common-variance comparison; source remains candidate."; W2 "Ordinary partial R² is not the exact v3 score fraction; uniform asymptotic claim also has a gap."; W4 "TV implication verified; KL omits positive layers; sharp chi-square rate imports a conjecture."). The F-DRAFT part of `A-REV4/DRAFTS_CHECK.md` in full:

> ## F-DRAFT W1: VERIFIED
>
> Under BO both G and H are block diagonal. Thus D multiplies, t adds, and the displayed expression for d follows exactly from methodology §5. Set a_b=t_{S_b}/c. Positivity and the ridge bound give a_b≥0 and Σa_b<1. Inductively ∏(1−a_b)≥1−Σa_b, strictly when at least two a_b are positive. This proves the sign and equality case. With known common variance, the log marginal BF is −log(D_S)/2+t_S/(2σ²), so it is additive and the *globally prior-coupled* start equals the posterior, including the cap. This does not identify the start with a product of local posterior probabilities. Source status remains PROVED candidate.
>
> ## F-DRAFT W2: ERROR in the purported exact identity; GAP in the uniform conclusion
>
> The source explicitly defines x_{T,l}=(RSS_T−RSS_{T+l})/RSS_T. This is ordinary least-squares partial R². The exact v3 marginal score uses Q, not RSS, and additionally 2b0. Consequently the displayed exact identities using x are false, even for orthogonal singleton columns. For a singleton with G=n−1, its v3 explained quantity is n(n−1)/n²=(n−1)/n times its ordinary LS explained quantity; 2b0 supplies another discrepancy. The determinant cancellation under BO is correct.
>
> Repair: define a separate regularised fraction
>
>     h_{T,l} := (t_{T+l}−t_T)/(2b0+Q_T).
>
> Then BO gives exactly h_{S°,l}=h_{T,l}(2b0+Q_T)/(2b0+Q_{S°}), and LR_l=ν[log(1−h_{T,l})−log(1−h_{S°,l})]. These are algebraic statements needing no Gaussian assumption. Require S°+l feasible; it is otherwise outside Ω and its posterior odds are undefined.
>
> The asymptotic leading mechanism κ_b Z²/2 is plausible for fixed null comparisons, but not proved by declaring a common remainder cancels. The regularised increments contain signal-dependent ridge corrections; uniform *relative* o_P(1) errors are particularly stronger than additive errors when the smallest |Z_l| tends to zero. The source's expansion hypotheses are candidates, and an O_P(1) additive expansion does not imply G_l=(Z_l²/2)(1+o_P(1)) uniformly. Supply an additive uniform error with its rate and prove it suffices for each subsequent layer bound, or state explicit lower bounds on |Z_l| on the selected extreme-value subset. Also raw-scale v_T must be compared to working-scale Q after response standardisation; the scale cancels in their ratio but cannot be omitted for individual residual limits. Source conditional PROVED label is not independently verified as written.
>
> ## F-DRAFT W4: VERIFIED TV bound; GAP for KL rate and chi-square assertion
>
> For any probability laws P,Q and state a, TV(P,Q)≤P(a^c)+Q(a^c), by inserting δ_a. Therefore the displayed TV bound follows conditional on the two cited concentration-rate inputs. No weight-moment premise is needed for this part.
>
> There is an exact useful KL bound, from E_{π0}e^d≥π0(S0)e^{d(S0)}:
>
>     KL(π||π0) ≤ −log π0(S0) + Σ_{S≠S0}π(S)[d(S)−d(S0)].
>
> The source replaces this whole sum by the single-null layer without controlling positive terms from multiple extras or mixed deletion/addition states. Under BO d increases on adding explained signal in a distinct block, so positive multi-extra terms cannot simply be discarded for an upper bound. That is a proof gap. The asserted sharp chi-square law is W(c), explicitly CONJECTURE, and remains such here; W4 cannot promote it to a proved consequence. Preserve W4's PROOF SKETCH status.
>
> Small KL and TV alone indeed do not force stable importance weights. An explicit abstract construction establishes that point independently: take π0=(1−ε, εe^{−1/√ε}), normalised by its coordinate sum, and π=(1−ε,ε). Then TV→0 and KL→0 while χ² diverges. This does not prove the claimed v3 rate or its sharp threshold.
>
> ## F-DRAFT NM: ERROR/GAP as a general proposition; valid fixed-p repair
>
> 1. The claimed precise expansion log BF({l})=nc/2−(log n)/2+O_P(1), with c the *population* log residual ratio, is false for fixed nonzero proxy correlation: empirical correlation fluctuates by O_P(n^{−1/2}), giving a nondegenerate O_P(√n) fluctuation in log BF. Use n^{-1}log BF→c/2, or nc/2−(log n)/2+O_P(√n). The displayed BF formula with ordinary x=r_{ly}² is also not exact for ridge/IG scores (W2 issue); it suffices for the exponential rate after an O_P(1) log correction in fixed dimension.
>
> 2. The exact odds identity in (ii) verifies π0({j})→0. By itself it does **not** verify π0(j,l∈S)→1, nor that the start mode is exactly {j,l}; all other states must be bounded. Likewise singleton evidence in each block alone does not prove the entire naive union equals exactly {j,l} when other columns/blocks are arbitrary. The assumptions do not explicitly provide uniform global SE/BM hypotheses of locked T03. Saying eigenvalues are bounded on 'sets used' is insufficiently specified for its growing-p application. A correct minimal repair is the identifiable p=2 family in A-DRAFT Proposition M, whose four-state direct comparison supplies all missing normalisation arguments.
>
> 3. With that repair, (iii), TV separation, and exponential start truth-mass decay follow directly; the polynomial iid-discovery obstruction follows. An exponential lower bound on M yields a poor *worst-case* independence-sampler rate; do not infer failure for every initial state (starting at truth is an immediate exception). State precisely the initial law and success event before claiming all algorithms fail at every polynomial budget.
>
> 4. Part (v) needs occupancy of the stated mode when its Gibbs label is executed. SR scores {j} if the current state at label l is {j,l}; merely starting a round there does not ensure that. The cited candidate's actual lower-bound hypotheses must be retained. The O(1) ideal-grid conclusion is also not established by W″'s thermodynamic-length calculation: a local small-step approximation and finite integral do not prove a uniform finite-threshold discrete stage bound. It remains a separate obligation. No masked-regime estimator-consistency theorem follows.
*(verbatim from `A-REV4/DRAFTS_CHECK.md`)*

### TH348 — WS1 (exponential-family identities for the bridge; Theorem WS1)  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §1; registry `OWS-WS1`; positions: [pos 492 (launch), 659/666 (laptop), 748 (finished)].
- Statement (verbatim):
> **Theorem WS1.** For all real u, v, with Δ := v − u and w := 2v − u:
>
> (a) **Singleton identity.** 1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u) = exp{Λ(w) − 2Λ(v) + Λ(u)} = q_v(S)² / (q_u(S) q_w(S)) for **every** S ∈ Ω.
>
> (a′) **Rényi version.** For every real α and every S ∈ Ω,
>  Σ_Ω q_v^α q_u^{1−α} = exp{Λ(u+αΔ) − αΛ(v) − (1−α)Λ(u)} = q_v(S)^α q_u(S)^{1−α} / q_{u+αΔ}(S).
>
> (b) **Set bounds.** For ∅ ≠ A ⊊ Ω,
>  q_v(A)²/q_u(A) + q_v(Aᶜ)²/q_u(Aᶜ) ≤ 1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u) ≤ cosh²(|Δ| osc_A(d)/2) · q_v(A)²/(q_u(A) q_w(A)).
> (The upper bound also holds for A = Ω.)
>
> (c) **Variance representation.** KL(q_v‖q_u) = ∫ |t − u| Λ''(t) dt over the segment between u and v, and
>  log(1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u)) = ∫_{v−|Δ|}^{v+|Δ|} (|Δ| − |t − v|) Λ''(t) dt.
> Hence KL(q_v‖q_u) ≤ (Δ²/2) sup_{t between u,v} Var_{q_t}(d) and log(1+χ²(q_v‖q_u)) ≤ Δ² sup_{t between u,w} Var_{q_t}(d).
>
> (d) **TV.** For every S ∈ Ω: TV(q_u, q_v) ≤ max{1 − q_u(S), 1 − q_v(S)}; and TV(q_u, q_v) ≥ |q_v(A) − q_u(A)| for every A.
>
> (e) **Log-concavity in the temperature.** For every S ∈ Ω, φ ↦ log q_φ(S) is concave on ℝ. Hence
> q_φ(S) ≥ min{q_a(S), q_b(S)} for φ ∈ [a, b], and sup_{φ,φ'∈[0,1]} TV(q_φ, q_φ') ≤ max{1 − π₀(S), 1 − π(S)}.
> (For S = S₀ the first claim on [0,1] is locked T22(iv-b); here it is extended to every S and every interval.)
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Remark (verbatim): relation to locked T13.
> **Remark (relation to locked T13).** (a) is locked T13(i) with V = {S} (then ρ_V ≡ 1); (b)'s upper bound is
> T13(i)+(iii) with V = A, plus Kantorovich. The point of (a) is that it holds *for every S simultaneously*: the
> bridge's χ² is controlled exactly when one model dominates q_u, q_v **and the over-tempered law q_w**.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status history: PROVED (author; SF none; XF none; "FLAG AUTHOR-ONLY" in MEET-THM index). CHECK_SEP_W re-used (a) at $S=S^\circ$ ("WS1(a) at S = S° (seen, proof checked)"). Proof route (Summary:) cumulant/Taylor identities, Cauchy-Schwarz, Kantorovich. 
- Depends on: TH111 (T13)(i)(iii), TH116 (T22(iv-b)) (WS1(e) extends it from $S_0$ to every $S$). Feeds: M2 Theorem WS (K102, K104 as used; (b2) uses "WS1(a) cumulant identity").

### TH349 — WS2 (one importance step; ESS, evidence variance, PW2 at the first stage)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §2; registry `OWS-WS2`. Statement (verbatim):
> **Theorem WS2.** Fix real u < v, Δ = v − u, w = 2v − u, g := e^{Δd}/E_{q_u}e^{Δd} = dq_v/dq_u. Let S₁,…,S_N be iid q_u.
> (a) (1/N)Σg(S_i) has mean 1 and variance χ²(q_v‖q_u)/N.
> (b) ESS_N/N := (Σg(S_i))²/(NΣg(S_i)²) → ESS_∞ := 1/(1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u)) almost surely as N → ∞.
> (c) **ESS sandwich.** ESS_∞ = q_u(S)q_w(S)/q_v(S)² for every S ∈ Ω, and ESS_∞ ≤ q_u(A)/q_v(A)² for every A.
> For the start-to-target step (u, v) = (0, 1):
>  π₀(S)·q₂(S)/π(S)² = ESS_∞(π₀ → π) ≤ π₀(S)/π(S)²  for every S, in particular S = S₀.
> (d) **PW2 at the first stage.** In a final island of the v3 run (iid exact π₀ start, W₀ = 1; setting of locked
> T25(iv)), PW2 holds at t = 1 **with equality** for a₁ = χ²(q_{φ₁}‖π₀) and ν₁ = 0:
> E_c[(q̂₀g₁)² − 1] = χ²(q_{φ₁}‖π₀)/N. If the frozen grid has T = 1 (φ₁ = 1), Var_c(Ẑ_r/Z) = χ²(π‖π₀)/N exactly
> and Var_c(Ẑ/Z) = χ²(π‖π₀)/(4N).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (SF none, XF none). Depends on: TH348, TH118 (T25(iv)), TH110 (T12). Feeds: M2(b3) states the same first-stage identity $1+N_e{\rm Var}=1+\chi^2(q_{\phi_1}\|\pi_0)$ ("W2PC1 B.R3(b)(1)-(4)").

### TH350 — WS3 = F-DRAFT Lemma W1 = O-WSTAB REPORT Lemma W1 (block orthogonality: the whole discrepancy is σ²-sharing)  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §3 (Theorem WS3); F-DRAFT `NEW_TARGETS.md` W1; REPORT.md "Lemma W1 (= [PF] WS3; PROVED)". Aliases: OWS-WS3, FD-W1, Lemma W1, "d is pure noise-variance sharing". Positions: [pos 616 (F-DRAFT), 748 (O-WSTAB)].
- Statement (verbatim, O-WSTAB WS3):
> **BO** (00_COMMON): X_{C_b}ᵀX_{C_c} = 0 for b ≠ c.
>
> **Theorem WS3.** Assume BO. For every S ∈ Ω (write S_b = S ∩ C_b):
> (a) D_S = ∏_b D_{S_b}, t_S = Σ_b t_{S_b}, hence x_S = x̄_S < 1.
> (b) **d is pure noise-variance sharing:** d(S) = d_σ(S) := ν[Σ_b log(1 − x_b(S)) − log(1 − x̄_S)].
> (c) 0 ≤ d_σ(S) ≤ ν Σ_{b<c} x_b(S)x_c(S)/(1 − x̄_S); d_σ is nondecreasing in each x_b; d_σ(S) = 0 iff at most one
> block has x_b(S) > 0.
> (d) **Mean-field representation.** Let λ be the Gamma law with shape ν and rate Q̄/2 for the precision τ = 1/σ²
> (the posterior of τ under the null model ∅ in the working model), and f_b(U; τ) := D_U^{−1/2} exp(τ t_U/2). Then
>  BF(S) = E_λ[∏_b f_b(S_b; τ)],  r_b(U) = E_λ[f_b(U; τ)].
> So π(S) ∝ ϖ(S)E_λ∏_b f_b(S_b; τ) while π₀(S) ∝ ϖ(S)∏_b E_λ f_b(S_b; τ): **π₀ is π with the single shared noise
> precision replaced by an independent copy per block.** In the fixed-variance version of the model (τ known,
> tables built the same way) d ≡ 0 and π₀ = π exactly.
> (e) The size prior (BB(1,p), cap K) enters π₀ and π identically; π(S)/π₀(S) = e^{d_σ(S)}/E_{π₀}e^{d_σ}. So the
> BB(1,p) coupling across blocks produces **no** discrepancy; all of it is the noise-sharing term d_σ.
> (f) For T ⊆ C_b, l ∈ C_b ∖ T: δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀμ_b with μ_b := X_{S₀∩C_b}θ_{S₀∩C_b}: no out-of-block signal leaks
> into any table comparison.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Statement (verbatim, F-DRAFT Lemma W1, earlier, same content, different notation $\xi_b=x_b$):
> **Lemma W1.** Assume BO. For S ∈ Ω write S_b = S ∩ C_b, c := 2b₀ + yᵀy = 2b₀ + n − 1, ξ_b := t_{S_b}/c ∈ [0, 1). Then
> D_S = ∏_b D_{S_b}, t_S = Σ_b t_{S_b}, and
>
>     d(S) = ν [ Σ_b log(1 − ξ_b) − log(1 − Σ_b ξ_b) ]  ≥ 0,
>
> with d(S) = 0 iff at most one block has ξ_b > 0. Moreover, if the tables and the posterior are computed with a known
> noise variance σ² (g-prior slab N(0, nσ²(G_S + I)⁻¹), no IG integration), then d ≡ 0 and π₀ = π exactly.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- Remarks (verbatim, O-WSTAB): FKG view and scale.
> **Remark (FKG view).** All f_b(·; τ) are increasing in τ, so d ≥ 0 is the Harris–FKG inequality
> E∏f_b ≥ ∏E f_b. Under BO the start always **under-rewards** models that fit in several blocks: each table measures its
> block's fit against a residual that still contains the other blocks' signal.
>
> **Remark (scale).** For a model fitting several blocks, d_σ is of order n: with block R²'s x_b, d_σ ≈ (n/2)Σ_{b<c}x_bx_c/(1 − x̄).
> This does **not** make π₀ far from π — d enters only through its *variation* over the region that carries mass
> (WS1(c)). Near S₀ (adding a null l in a truth-free block) the increment is d_σ(S₀+l) − d_σ(S₀) ≈ ω Z_l²/2 with
> ω := 1 − RSS_{S₀}/yᵀy (computed exactly in §6): bounded in n, but *unbounded over the p nulls*.
>
> ---
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*

### TH351 — WS4 (perturbation in the standardised cross-block Gram)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §4; registry `OWS-WS4`. Statement (verbatim, definitions and theorem):
> **Definitions.** For S ∈ Ω with |S| ≥ 2: R_S = G_S/(n − 1); A_S := the block-diagonal part of R_S (entries (j,k) with
> j, k in the same block; zero otherwise); E_S := R_S − A_S (the cross-block Gram). Assume A_S ≻ 0 (implied by
> SE-blk(φ₀): λ_min(R_{C_b}) ≥ φ₀² for every b, by interlacing). The **cross-block dependence measures**
>  ε_S := ‖A_S^{−1/2}E_SA_S^{−1/2}‖_op,  F_S := ‖A_S^{−1/2}E_SA_S^{−1/2}‖_F² ≤ |S|ε_S².
> (For |S| ≤ 1 put ε_S = F_S = 0.) Sufficient: ε_S ≤ ‖E_S‖_op/φ₀² ≤ |S| max_{cross pairs}|r_jk|/φ₀².
> Decomposition (from Lemma 0, any X): d = d_det + d_fit + d_σ with
>  d_det(S) := −½[log D_S − Σ_b log D_{S_b}],  d_fit(S) := −ν log[(1 − x_S)/(1 − x̄_S)],  d_σ as in WS3(b)
> (d_σ and d_fit are defined when x̄_S < 1).
>
> **Theorem WS4.** Let S ∈ Ω with A_S ≻ 0 and ε := ε_S < 1. Then
> (a) (1 − ε)A_S ⪯ R_S ⪯ (1 + ε)A_S; in particular λ_min(R_S) ≥ (1 − ε) min_b λ_min(R_{S_b}) (global SE on S from
> SE-blk plus weak cross-block dependence).
> (b) |t_S − Σ_b t_{S_b}| ≤ (ε/(1 − ε)) Σ_b t_{S_b}, i.e. |x_S − x̄_S| ≤ ε x̄_S/(1 − ε).
> (c) |d_det(S)| ≤ F_S/(4(1 − ε)).
> (d) If x̄_S < 1 − ε: |d_fit(S)| ≤ ν ε x̄_S/(1 − ε − x̄_S), hence
>  |d(S) − d_σ(S)| ≤ η_S := ν ε x̄_S/(1 − ε − x̄_S) + F_S/(4(1 − ε)).
> (e) **Transfer.** Let W ⊆ Ω be nonempty with (a)–(d) applicable on W and η_W := max_W η_S. Let q^σ_φ ∝ γ₀e^{φd_σ} be the
> *BO-equivalent bridge* (same start, discrepancy d_σ). Then for every real v,
>  e^{−4|v|η_W} ≤ [1 + χ²(q_v^W ‖ π₀^W)] / [1 + χ²(q_v^{σ,W} ‖ π₀^W)] ≤ e^{4|v|η_W},  TV(q_v^W, q_v^{σ,W}) ≤ 1 − e^{−2|v|η_W}.
> With W = Ω this compares (π₀, π) with (π₀, π^σ) globally; for W ⊊ Ω combine with WS1(b).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Scale warning (verbatim):
> **Scale of the perturbation regime (important).** η_S ≈ (n/2)ε_S x̄_S/(1 − x̄_S). For a model explaining a fixed
> fraction of yᵀy this is o(1) only when **ε_S = o(1/n)**. Sample cross-correlations of unrelated columns are of order
> n^{−1/2}, so the uniform perturbation route covers only near-orthogonal designs ("near-BO" benchmarks). The relevant
> weak-dependence notion at the n^{−1/2} scale is the leakage of §5, which acts on log-odds through δ²/(2v) = O(1).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (SF none); CHK_INHERITED "OWS-WS4 VERIFIED (PC1, cross-family, line by line)"; final card line: "OWS-WS3, OWS-WS4: PROVED (SF: none; XF: none) + CHK 'VERIFIED (PC1, cross-family, line by line)'". Depends on: LM209, LM223, TH350. Feeds: M2(a3), (b2) four-normaliser transfer (K11 "OWS-WS4 in cards").

### LM211 — Lemma WS5.1 and the truth-dependent leakage quantities  [lemma]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §5. Definitions and statement (verbatim):
> **Truth-dependent cross-block quantities** (deterministic given X and θ*; 00_COMMON μ = Xθ*). For each block b:
> U*_b := S₀ ∩ C_b; μ_b := X_{U*_b}θ*_{U*_b}; μ_{−b} := μ − μ_b = X_{S₀∖C_b}θ*_{S₀∖C_b}; and
> - **cross-block coefficient shift** α_b := G_{U*_b}⁻¹X_{U*_b}ᵀμ_{−b} ∈ ℝ^{U*_b} (the regression of the out-of-block signal on
>   the block's own truths; empty if U*_b = ∅);
> - **effective block coefficient** θ̃_b := θ*_{U*_b} + α_b;
> - **leakage remainder** Λ_b := ‖(P_{C_b} − P_{U*_b})μ_{−b}‖² (= [E]'s λ_b(S₀));
> - total visible leakage κ_b := ‖P_{C_b}μ_{−b}‖² = Λ_b + ‖X_{U*_b}α_b‖².
> Under BO: α_b = 0, θ̃_b = θ*_{U*_b}, Λ_b = κ_b = 0.
>
> **Lemma WS5.1.** P_{C_b}μ = X_{U*_b}θ̃_b + ρ_b with ρ_b := (P_{C_b} − P_{U*_b})μ_{−b} ⊥ span(X_{U*_b}), ρ_b ∈ span(X_{C_b}),
> ‖ρ_b‖² = Λ_b.
> *Proof.* P_{C_b}μ = μ_b + P_{U*_b}μ_{−b} + (P_{C_b} − P_{U*_b})μ_{−b}, P_{U*_b}μ_{−b} = X_{U*_b}α_b, and P_{C_b} − P_{U*_b} is the projection
> onto span(X_{C_b}) ⊖ span(X_{U*_b}) (U*_b ⊆ C_b). ∎
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (proof in file). Feeds: TH352.

### TH352 — Proposition WS5.2 (leakage formulas)  [proposition]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §5; registry `OWS-WS52`. Statement (verbatim):
> **Proposition WS5.2 (leakage formulas; PROVED).** Assume SE-blk(φ₀). For b, T ⊆ C_b, l ∈ C_b ∖ T:
> (a) δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀ(I − P_T)X_{U*_b∖T}θ̃_{b,U*_b∖T} + u_{T,l}ᵀρ_b.
> (b) *Null comparisons* (l ∉ S₀, U*_b ⊆ T): δ_{T,l} = u_{T,l}ᵀρ_b and |δ_{T,l}| ≤ √Λ_b. **NL quantities of T22(iii) are pure
> cross-block leakage.** In particular NL_η holds if CBL(η): max_b Λ_b ≤ ησ*² log n.
> (c) *Block-completing truth addition* (l ∈ U*_b, T = U*_b ∖ {l}): δ_{T,l} = θ̃_{b,l}‖(I − P_T)x_l‖ **exactly**, and
> ‖(I − P_T)x_l‖ ≥ φ₀√(n−1).
> (d) *Visibility*: for T ⊆ C_b with U*_b ⊄ T, ‖(P_{T∪U*_b} − P_T)μ‖ ≥ φ₀√(n−1)‖θ̃_{b,U*_b∖T}‖ − √Λ_b. Hence VIS (with
> M_n^V = M_n) holds if
>  EBM(M_n): min_{b, j∈U*_b} |θ̃_{b,j}| ≥ [√(M_n(σ*² + 2M) log n) + √Λ_b] / (φ₀√(n−1)), M_n → ∞.
> (e) With c_b := max_{j∈C_b, k∈S₀∖C_b}|r_jk|: κ_b ≤ (n−1)|C_b| c_b² ‖θ*_{S₀∖C_b}‖₁²/φ₀² and
> ‖α_b‖₂ ≤ √|U*_b| c_b ‖θ*_{S₀∖C_b}‖₁/φ₀².
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (SF none, XF none). Depends on: LM211, ⟦W1-EXP⟧ leakage quantities (NL, VIS, EBM). Feeds: TH353, TH354; final cards: none directly (M2 card removed "the m-form of (S) and (F) (to the leakage corollary, R3-5)").

### TH353 — WS5.3 (F) weak leakage implies a favourable start, and (N) the necessity form  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §5 Theorem WS5.3 (F), (N); registry `OWS-WS53F`, `OWS-WS53N`. Statement (verbatim, (F) and (N); (M) is TH354):
> **Theorem WS5.3 (regime dichotomy in cross-block terms).**
>
> (F) *Weak leakage ⇒ favourable start.* Assume G, R (with A, M, φ₀), SE-blk(φ₀), EBM(M_n), and CBL(η) with
> 0 ≤ η < η_A := (√(2A+1) − √(2A))². Then VIS and NL_η hold deterministically (WS5.2(b),(d)); EXP′ holds by [E] Thm 1
> (candidate); NL_avg(κ) is supplied by NL_η for every 0 < κ < ½ − η/2 − √(2Aη) (κ = ½ if η = 0), as stated in
> locked T22(iii). Hence, by locked T22(iii),
>  1 − π₀(S₀) = O_{P₀}(2^B √(log n) n^{−κ}).
> Under BO, α ≡ 0 and Λ ≡ 0, so EBM reduces to a block beta-min and η = 0 ([E] Thm 2).
> **Status:** the reduction (VIS, NL_η ⇐ EBM, CBL) is **PROVED**; the conclusion is a direct composition with locked
> T22(iii) and inherits the candidate status of [E] Thm 1.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
> (N) *Necessity form of (F).* Along any sequence satisfying G, R, SE-blk on which π₀(S₀) ↛ 1 in probability, for every
> M_n → ∞ and every η < η_A, infinitely often either some |θ̃_{b,j}| < [√(M_n(σ*²+2M)log n) + √Λ_b]/(φ₀√(n−1))
> (**coefficient cancellation**, which needs ‖α_b‖ ≳ θ_min) or max_b Λ_b > ησ*² log n (**large leakage remainder**). Both

*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*

### TH354 — WS5.3 (M): masking needs order-one cross-block cancellation  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §5; registry `OWS-WS53M`. Statement (verbatim):
> (M) *Masking needs order-one cross-block cancellation.* Let S^{(0)} ⊂ … ⊂ S^{(c)} = S₀ be any chain of single
> additions (T27's H1), c ≥ 1, T_i := S^{(i)} ∩ C_{b(l_i)}. For every block b that receives an addition, the **last**
> addition l in b has T = U*_b ∖ {l}, so (WS5.2(c))
>  |δ_{T,l}| = |θ*_l + α_{b,l}| · ‖(I − P_T)x_l‖ ≥ φ₀√(n−1) |θ*_l + α_{b,l}|.
> Hence [E]'s chain-leakage condition CL(L) (which yields T27(i)'s masking law, [E] Thms 3–4) forces
>  |θ*_l + α_{b,l}| ≤ Lσ*/(φ₀√(n−1)):
> the out-of-block signal, regressed on block b's truths, must cancel θ*_l up to O(n^{−1/2}). Consequently:
> (M1) under BO (α ≡ 0) and |θ*_j| ≥ θ_min > Lσ*/(φ₀√(n−1)), CL(L) fails for every chain: no T27-type masking
>  without cross-block dependence;
> (M2) by WS5.2(e), CL(L) requires c_b ≥ φ₀²(|θ*_l| − Lσ*/(φ₀√(n−1)))/(√|U*_b| ‖θ*_{S₀∖C_b}‖₁): a cross-block correlation
>  bounded away from zero (it does not vanish with n).
> **Status: PROVED** (deterministic).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Remarks (verbatim):
> **Remark (the LH family of [E]).** corr(x_{j_a}, x_{j_b}) = ψ, θ*_{j_b} = −ψθ*_{j_a}: α_{b,j_b} = ψθ*_{j_a}, so θ̃_{j_b} = 0 exactly,
> Λ_b = 0. Masking is exact coefficient cancellation, with zero leakage remainder. If instead θ*_{j_b} is fixed and ψ
> varies, θ̃_{j_b} = θ*_{j_b} + ψθ*_{j_a} vanishes at a single ψ: masking is **not monotone** in the cross-block correlation
> (numerics N2).
>
> **Remark (random designs).** In iid Gaussian designs with population BO (S1, S3, S4, S6), the sample α_b and ρ_b are
> O_P(n^{−1/2}) and O_P(1)·√(Bσ_μ²) respectively, so θ̃ → θ* (EBM holds) but max_b Λ_b is O_P(log p): CBL(η) with small
> η is not automatic; the average route NL_avg is needed there ([E] §4.3, PROOF SKETCH). WS5.3(F) is the fixed-design
> statement.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (deterministic; SF none, XF none). Depends on: TH352, TH119 (T27(i)), ⟦W1-EXP Thms 3-4⟧ (CL(L)). Feeds: none directly; the statement "no T27-type masking without cross-block dependence" supports the START card (M3, K17) narrative.

### TH355 — WS6(a)-(c) (deterministic weight identities; KL needs less tilt control)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §6; registry `OWS-WS6abc`. Statement (verbatim, items (a)-(c); (d) is TH356; (e) is CJ261):
> **Theorem WS6.**
> (a) (*deterministic*) For every S ∈ Ω: 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) = π(S)²/(π₀(S)q₂(S)), and
>  1/q₂(S) − 1 = Σ_{S'≠S}[π₀(S')/π₀(S)] e^{2(d(S')−d(S))} = Σ_{S'≠S}[π(S')/π(S)] e^{d(S')−d(S)}.
> For α > 1: e^{(α−1)D_α(π‖π₀)} = π(S)^απ₀(S)^{1−α}/q_α(S), 1/q_α(S) − 1 = Σ_{S'≠S}[π(S')/π(S)]e^{(α−1)(d(S')−d(S))}.
> (b) (*stable weights ⇐ start sees the truth + tilt control*) χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ 1/(π₀(S₀)q₂(S₀)) − 1, and for **every** grid
> 0 = φ₀ < … < φ_T = 1, max_t χ²(q_{φ_t}‖q_{φ_{t−1}}) ≤ 1/m² − 1 with m := min{π₀(S₀), q₂(S₀)}.
> (c) (*KL needs less tilt control*) For every θ ∈ (0, 1]:
>  KL(π‖π₀) ≤ log(π(S₀)/π₀(S₀)) + (π(S₀)/θ)(1/q_{1+θ}(S₀) − 1),
>  KL(π₀‖π) ≤ log(π₀(S₀)/π(S₀)) + (π₀(S₀)/θ)(1/q_{−θ}(S₀) − 1).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (deterministic; SF none, XF none). Depends on: TH348. Feeds: M2(b) (via WS6(b): $\max_t\chi^2\le1/m^2-1$) and TH358(b).

### TH356 — WS6(d): noise-chasing obstruction (zero cross-block correlation, χ² diverges)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §6; registry `OWS-WS6d`; amendment `MEET-THM/evidence/CHK_INHERITED/REPORT.md` §1. Statement (verbatim):
> (d) (*noise-chasing obstruction; ORTH, zero cross-block correlation*) Assume G; ORTH (XᵀX = (n−1)I_p, so BO holds for
> **every** partition); s₀ ≥ 1 fixed; θ*_{S₀} fixed and nonzero; S₀ ∈ Ω; let N₀ be the null predictors lying in blocks
> that contain no true predictor, with |N₀| → ∞ and log|N₀| = O(log n). Put R̄² := ‖θ*‖²/(‖θ*‖² + σ*²) (population R²).
> Then for every fixed α > 1, with probability → 1,
>  1/q_α(S₀) − 1 ≥ [(s₀+1)/(2p)] · n^{−1/2} · |N₀|^{1+(α−1)R̄²} · (log|N₀|)^{−(1+(α−1)R̄²)/2} · e^{−O_P(1)}.
> Consequently e^{(α−1)D_α(π‖π₀)} ≥ π(S₀)^α × [the same bound]. If |N₀| ≥ p/2 and
> p^{(α−1)R̄²}/[√n (log p)^{(1+(α−1)R̄²)/2}] → ∞, then D_α(π‖π₀) → ∞ in probability; for α = 2, **χ²(π‖π₀) → ∞ and the
> population ESS fraction → 0**, while TV(π, π₀) → 0 (π(S₀) → 1 by locked T03; π₀(S₀) → 1 by [E] Thm 6 when the truth
> meets ≥ 2 blocks, or by WS5.3(F) with η = 0). With p = n − 1 this happens for every R̄² > ½.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status and amendment: author PROVED (SF none, XF none; "lower bound self-contained; the divergence and TV consequences cite locked T03 and [E] Thm 6 / WS5.3(F)"). CHK_INHERITED (theorem meeting, after pos 1110; Sol checker PC1): verdict table row (verbatim):
> | OWS-WS6(d) | VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT | The lower bound and divergence argument check. For the accompanying TV conclusion, make the bounded-block setting explicit, or separately assume start concentration. The shipped block cap supplies this setting. |
*(verbatim from `MEET-THM/evidence/CHK_INHERITED/REPORT.md`)*
  Final card: "(c1) Zero-dependence obstruction (WS6(d) with CHK amendment)... Instance: p = n−1, one coefficient 2, σ² = 1" (CE199).
- Depends on: TH355, TH348, TH103 (T03), TH140 (W1-EXP Thm 6). Feeds: M2(c1) = Proposition ONE-SHOT. This is the rigorous form of "the draft's claim that weak cross-block dependence bounds the weight variance is false as stated for χ²" (see the Interpretation paragraph quoted at RF256).
- Notes: the ORTH hypothesis only, "No H-ORTH restriction p log p=o(n) is used" (CHK); distinct from TH362 which needs $p\log p=o(n)$.

### TH357 — WS7: weights in the masked regime; "reweighting cannot create the truth"  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §7; registry `OWS-WS7`; amendments CHK_INHERITED §2. Statement (verbatim):
> **Theorem WS7.**
> (a) ESS_∞(π₀ → π) ≤ π₀(S₀)/π(S₀)², and ≤ π₀(A)/π(A)² for every A ⊆ Ω; KL(π‖π₀) ≥ π(S₀)log(1/π₀(S₀)) − log 2;
> TV(π, π₀) ≥ π(S₀) − π₀(S₀).
> (b) Under the conclusions of T27(i) [π₀(S₀) = p^{−c}n^{−c/2}e^{O_P(1)}; available from CL(L) + H3 by [E] Thm 4] and of T03
> [π(S₀) → 1]: ESS_∞(π₀ → π) ≤ p^{−c}n^{−c/2}e^{O_P(1)}, KL(π‖π₀) ≥ (c log p + (c/2)log n)(1 − o_P(1)) − O_P(1), TV → 1.
> (c) *Reweighting cannot create the truth.* Any scheme that starts from N iid π₀ draws and then only reweights and
> resamples holds S₀ in some particle with probability 1 − (1 − π₀(S₀))^N ≤ Nπ₀(S₀). In the v3 final run the 4N_e initial
> particles contain S₀ with probability ≤ 4N_eπ₀(S₀); every other route to S₀ is a move (independence proposals —
> the iid budget Q_f of T11(iii)/T27 — Gibbs flips, swaps, neighbour swaps, local search).
> (d) *Accepted grids need only log-log many stages.* Let V ∋ S₀ and let every interval of a grid be accepted at level
> ρ̄ ∈ (0,1] (ρ_V(φ_{t−1}, φ_t) ≥ ρ̄; the method uses ρ̄ = 0.9). With ℓ_t := −log q^V_{φ_t}(S₀) and c_ρ := log(1/ρ̄):
>  ℓ_t + c_ρ ≥ (ℓ_{t−1} + c_ρ)/2, hence T ≥ log₂[(ℓ₀ + c_ρ)/(ℓ_T + c_ρ)].
> Under masking ℓ₀ = log(π₀(V)/π₀(S₀)), so at ρ̄ = 0.9 and ℓ_T ≈ 0, T ≳ log₂(9.5 ℓ₀) ≈ log₂(9.5(c log p + (c/2) log n)). The bound is
> attained up to O(1) by two-state families, so restricted-ESS control by itself does not force a long bridge.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Reading (verbatim):
> **Reading.** Under masking the importance weights between neighbouring tempered laws can be kept stable with few
> stages, but the population holds S₀ with probability ≤ Nπ₀(S₀): what the sampler must supply is **transport**
> (moves), not reweighting. This is the T38(b) delivery/repair problem.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: author PROVED (SF none, XF none); CHK_INHERITED row (verbatim): "OWS-WS7 | VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT | Clarify initial versus subsequent particle presence; qualify the restricted-set stage-count approximation and its degenerate endpoint. The ESS/KL/TV obstruction is unchanged." Final card M2(c2): "the initial population holds S₀ with probability 1 − (1−π₀(S₀))^N ≤ Nπ₀(S₀), later stages only '≤'; restricted-grid lower bounds with the set-mass... and singleton-endpoint amendments."
- Depends on: TH348, TH349, TH119 (T27(i)), TH103 (T03), TH111 (T13)(iii), TH109 (T11(iii)). Feeds: M2(c2); M6 Theorem SEP + Lemma KL (K105: "KL(π‖π₀) ≥ (1−δ₁)log(1/π₀(S₀)) − log 2", REGISTRY "KL: PROOF SKETCH (NEW-SYNTH)", the checked form with $\pi(S_0)$ is WS7(a)); M7(d) (WS7(d): $T\gtrsim\log_2(9.5\ell_0)$).

### CJ261 — WS6(e): the Rényi-order threshold $\alpha^*=1+1/(2A\omega^*)$  [conjecture]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §6(e); registry `OWS-WS6e`. Statement (verbatim):
> (e) **CONJECTURE (threshold).** Under ORTH (more generally BO + SE-blk + favourable), with p = n^A and
> ω* := max over truth-free blocks of the limit of 1 − RSS_{S₀}/RSS_{S₀∩C_b} (= R̄² under ORTH):
> D_α(π‖π₀) → 0 if A(α−1)ω* < ½ and → ∞ if A(α−1)ω* > ½. KL (α ↓ 1) always vanishes in the favourable regime;
> the χ² (α = 2) vanishes iff Aω* < ½. Equivalently the critical Rényi order is α* = 1 + 1/(2Aω*).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
- Status and fate: CONJECTURE (SF none, XF none). Resolved for $\alpha=2$ under ORTH and $p\log p=o(n)$ by TH362 (convergent side $2Ar<1$ and divergent side $2Ar>1$; equality unresolved, CJ267). For general $\alpha$, "not used" (final card M2: "OWS-WS6e: CONJECTURE; OWS-WS8d: OPEN (neither used)"). Status paragraph with the heuristic for the upper side:
> **Status.** (a)–(c) **PROVED** (deterministic). (d) **PROVED** (lower bound self-contained; the divergence and TV
> consequences cite locked T03 and [E] Thm 6 / WS5.3(F)). (e) **CONJECTURE**; heuristic for the upper side: under BO,
> 1/q_α(S₀) − 1 ≈ Σ_{N}∏_{l∈N}c_l + (subset terms), and Σ_N∏c_l ≤ exp(Σ_l c_l) − 1 with
> Σ_lc_l ≍ n^{−1/2}p^{−1}Σ_le^{(1+(α−1)ω)Z_l²/2} ≍ n^{−1/2}p^{(α−1)ω} (stable-law scaling of a sum of heavy-tailed terms with
> index 1/(1+(α−1)ω) < 1); the missing piece is uniform control of large models and of subset terms, where the per-null
> expansion fails (a T02-type argument for the doubled-likelihood law q₂ ∝ ϖD^{−1/2}(Q̄ − t)^{−2ν}∏_b(1 − x_b)^ν).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*

### TH359 — Proposition W0 ("three faces of π/π₀": χ², sup ratio, value at $S_0$) = F-DRAFT W0  [proposition]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2 and §3.1 (self-contained re-proof); `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` W0. Aliases: Prop W0, FD-W0. Positions: [pos 616, 748].
- Statement (verbatim, O-WSTAB REPORT, later and self-contained):
> **Proposition W0 (three faces; deterministic; EX-A). PROVED.** With r(S) := π(S)/π₀(S) = e^{d(S)}/E_{π₀}e^{d} and
> M := max_Ω r:
> (i) 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) = E_{π₀}e^{2d}/(E_{π₀}e^{d})² = Z̄₀Z̄₂/Z̄₁² = 1/ρ_Ω(0,1) = π(S)²/(π₀(S)q₂(S)) for every S ∈ Ω.
> (ii) π(S)²/π₀(S) ≤ 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ M for every S; KL(π‖π₀) ≤ log(1+χ²(π‖π₀)); TV ≤ √(KL/2).
> (iii) (independence move at φ = 1 = Metropolised independence sampler with proposal π₀, T09(ii)) Its kernel K satisfies
> K(x, ·) ≥ π(·)/M for every x, so ‖K^t(x,·) − π‖_TV ≤ (1 − 1/M)^t for all x, t. Conversely, for x* ∈ argmax r,
> ‖K^t(x*,·) − π‖_TV ≥ (1 − 1/M)^t − π(x*). So, from the worst state, the move needs ≍ M steps.
> (iv) (iid discovery, T11(iii)) P(S absent from Q iid π₀ draws) = (1 − π₀(S))^Q ≥ 1 − Qπ₀(S), and π(S)/π₀(S) ≤ M.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Earlier version (F-DRAFT W0, verbatim):
> ## W0. Three faces of the start discrepancy (deterministic; EX-A)
>
> **Proposition W0.** For every data set and partition:
>
> (i) π(S)/π₀(S) = e^{d(S)}/E_{π₀}[e^{d}] for all S ∈ Ω, with E_{π₀}[e^d] = Z̄₁/Z̄₀.
>
> (ii) 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) = E_{π₀}[e^{2d}]/(E_{π₀}[e^d])² = Z̄₀Z̄₂/Z̄₁² = 1/ρ_Ω(0, 1). It is the reciprocal of the population ESS
> fraction of one-step importance sampling from π₀ to π, and equals 1 + Var_{π₀}(w̄) for the normalised weight
> w̄ = e^d/E_{π₀}e^d. (T13(i) with V = Ω, u = 0, v = 1.)
>
> (iii) KL(π‖π₀) = E_π[d] − log E_{π₀}[e^d] ≤ log(1 + χ²(π‖π₀)); TV(π, π₀) ≤ √(KL/2). Lower bounds: for every S,
> 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≥ π(S)²/π₀(S); in particular ≥ π(S₀)²/π₀(S₀).
>
> (iv) Let M := sup_S π(S)/π₀(S) = e^{max_Ω d}/E_{π₀}e^d < ∞. The independence move at φ = 1 (T09(ii)) is the Metropolised
> independence sampler with proposal π₀; its second-largest eigenvalue is 1 − 1/M (Liu 1996, Thm 1) and
> ‖K^t(x, ·) − π‖_TV ≤ (1 − 1/M)^t (Mengersen and Tweedie 1996). In particular 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ M and M ≥ π(S₀)/π₀(S₀).
>
> (v) (T11(iii)) P(S₀ absent from Q iid π₀ draws) = (1 − π₀(S₀))^Q; and π(S₀)/π₀(S₀) ≤ M.
>
> So the draft's three correction mechanisms (importance weighting, MH, iid/SMC discovery) are the L², L^∞ and pointwise
> norms of one ratio. **Status: PROVED** (definitions, T13(i), T09(ii), T11(iii), Liu 1996). Check: in the proxy-split run,
> 1 + χ² = 4.9·10⁴⁰ against the single-term lower bound π(S₀)²/π₀(S₀) = 4.4·10⁴⁰.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- What changed: F-DRAFT (iv) cites "second-largest eigenvalue is 1 − 1/M (Liu 1996, Thm 1)" and Mengersen-Tweedie; O-WSTAB (REPORT §3.1): "The spectral statement 'second eigenvalue 1 − 1/M' of Liu (1996) is not used; I have not seen that source", replaced by a Doeblin minorisation argument giving a two-sided rate $(1-1/M)^t-\pi(x^*)\le\|K^t(x^*,\cdot)-\pi\|_{TV}\le(1-1/M)^t$.
- Status: PROVED (F-DRAFT `FD-W0`; O-WSTAB). SF: not in CHECK_SEP_W's scope. XF: none. Depends on: TH111 (T13)(i), TH107 (T09)(ii), TH109 (T11)(iii). Feeds: M6 / S-IDENT (K19 iid miss, K103 "Doeblin/minorisation constants", K104); F-DRAFT recommended adding it as clause (v) of the T13 supplement lemma ("three faces").

## Part E. O-WSTAB REPORT.md: Theorem W under ORTH, Theorem W', and the counterexample to F-DRAFT

Headline of the REPORT (verbatim, items 1-5):

> ## 1. Headline
>
> 1. **One function governs everything.** For any reference model S° let ℓ(φ) := −log q_φ(S°). It is convex, and
>    **log(1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u)) = ℓ(u) + ℓ(2v−u) − 2ℓ(v) exactly** (T13(i) with V = Ω, in second-difference form). In the
>    favourable regime every stage's χ² equals ℓ(2v−u) + o_P(1). The ideal ESS-0.9 grid's stage count is pinned between
>    ⌈log₂(1+1/g₊)⌉ and ⌈log₂(1+1/g₋)⌉, where g± are read off the sublevel sets of ℓ. (Prop L, Prop G: **PROVED**, deterministic.)
> 2. **W0** (three norms of π/π₀) **PROVED**. It is self-contained: a Doeblin argument replaces the unseen Liu (1996)
>    citation and gives a two-sided rate for the independence move. **W1** **PROVED** ([PF] WS3). **W2** **PROVED** in an
>    *exact* finite-n form, κG ≤ LR ≤ κG/(1−y), with no EXP′ needed.
> 3. **Theorem W under ORTH** (X′X = (n−1)I, any partition, s₀ and θ* fixed, p log p = o(n)), with r := R²_pop:
>    if p^r√(log p)/√n → 0, then p^{r−ε}/√n ≤ χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ p^{r+ε}/√n w.p. → 1, both sides **PROVED**. If
>    L_n := r log p − ½ log n − ((1+r)/2) log log p → ∞, then **c·e^{L_n/r} ≤ log(1+χ²) ≤ C·e^{L_n/r}(log p)^{5(1+r)/(2r)}**,
>    i.e. log log(1+χ²) = L_n/r + O(log log p): polynomial in n (both sides **PROVED**, the upper one via an integral
>    form of the separable bound).
>    KL(π‖π₀) and TV(π, π₀) → 0 throughout (**PROVED**). The proof never takes an expectation of a heavy-tailed weight.
> 4. **COUNTEREXAMPLE to [FD] Theorem W(c)** ("log(1+χ²) = [R² log p − ½ log n]₊ + O_P(log log p)"). On the divergent side,
>    multi-extra models dominate: with p = n^A and Ar > ½, log(1+χ²) ≥ n^{A−1/(2r)−o(1)}, not O(log n). Exact large-p
>    numerics agree: at n = 10¹⁶, p = n^{0.95}, r = 0.9 the exact lower bound is 8.8·10³ nats, while W(c) predicts 13.
>    The *threshold* of W (Ar ≶ ½) is correct, and so are W(a) and, on the convergent side, W(b).
> 5. **W′ under ORTH**: the ideal ESS-0.9 grid has **T_ideal ∈ {1, 2}** w.p. → 1. T = 1 if 2Ar < 1, T = 2 if 2Ar > 1
>    (with p = n^{A+o(1)}). This is the [FD] formula ⌈log₂(1+1/g)⌉ with g → 1/(2Ar) (**PROVED** for the ideal full-space
>    grid; the method's V-restricted pilot grid is a separate, stated obligation). General BO with correlated blocks, and
>    p ≍ n: **PROOF SKETCH** / **OPEN**.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*

Standing notation of the REPORT (verbatim):

> Standing notation. g(z) := −log(1 − z) on [0, 1) (a function; not the design code G). Fit fractions x_S := t_S/Q̄,
> Q̄ = 2b₀ + yᵀy ([PF] §0; Lemma 0: log BF(S) = −½ log D_S + ν g(x_S), 0 ≤ x_S < 1). Bridge q_φ ∝ γ₀e^{φd}, φ ∈ ℝ.
> For a reference model S° ∈ Ω: **ℓ(φ) = ℓ_{S°}(φ) := −log q_φ(S°)** and **O(φ) := 1/q_φ(S°) − 1 = e^{ℓ(φ)} − 1** (the
> off-reference odds). ℓ* := max{ℓ(0), ℓ(1)} = max{−log π₀(S°), −log π(S°)}. c := log(10/9) (the ESS-0.9 threshold:
> ρ ≥ 0.9 ⇔ log(1+χ²) ≤ c). Favourable regime: ℓ_{S₀}* → 0 in probability; masked: ℓ_{S₀}(0) → ∞ (00_COMMON, T22, T27).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*

### LM212 — Lemma W2 (exact dilution form): $\kappa G\le LR\le\kappa G/(1-y)$; replaces F-DRAFT Lemma W2  [lemma]
- Source (authoritative): `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2 Lemma W2, proof §3.2; F-DRAFT `NEW_TARGETS.md` W2 (earlier, ERROR). Positions: [pos 616, 748].
- Statement (verbatim, O-WSTAB):
> **Lemma W2 (exact dilution form; PROVED).** Assume BO. Let S° ∈ Ω, l ∉ S° in block b, S° + l ∈ Ω, T := S° ∩ C_b.
> Put x̄ := x_{S°} (and x_T the fit fraction of T), y := (t_{T+l} − t_T)/(Q̄ − t_{S°}) ∈ [0, 1), **κ := (x̄ − x_T)/(1 − x_T) ∈ [0, 1)** (the
> fraction of block b's table residual that is other blocks' fit: the realised dilution fraction), and
> G := log[BF(S°+l)/BF(S°)] + ½ log(D_{T+l}/D_T) = ν g(y) (the posterior's fit gain). Then
>  LR := log[π(S°+l)/π(S°)] − log[π₀(S°+l)/π₀(S°)] = d(S°+l) − d(S°) = ν[g(y) − g((1−κ)y)],
>  **κ G ≤ LR ≤ κ G/(1 − y)**,
> and the table's fit gain is ν g((1−κ)y) = G − LR. *Statistical reading* (ORTH, S° = S₀, l a null in a truth-free block):
> T = ∅, κ = x_{S₀} = r + O_P(n^{−1/2}), G = (Z_l²/2)(1 + O_P(n^{−1/2})) and y = O_P(log p/n), uniformly over nulls
> (§3.6). So LR_l = r·Z_l²/2·(1 + O_P(n^{−1/2} + log p/n)) uniformly. Under general BO, identifying G with
> Z²_{T,l}/2 is EXP′ (W1-EXP Thm 1, candidate).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Earlier version (F-DRAFT Lemma W2, verbatim):
> ## W2. The null log-odds gap is the dilution fraction times the posterior gain
>
> **Lemma W2.** Assume BO and G. Fix S° ∈ Ω and l ∉ S° in block b, T := S° ∩ C_b. Then exactly
>
>     LR_l := log[π(S°+l)/π(S°)] − log[π₀(S°+l)/π₀(S°)] = d(S°+l) − d(S°)
>           = ν [ log(1 − x_{T,l}) − log(1 − x_{S°,l}) ],   x_{S°,l} = x_{T,l} · (2b₀ + Q_T)/(2b₀ + Q_{S°}),
>
> (the determinant parts cancel under BO and the explained increment t_{S°+l} − t_{S°} = t_{T+l} − t_T). With
> (2b₀ + Q_T)/(2b₀ + Q_{S°}) = v_T/v_{S°}·(1 + O_P(n^{−1/2})) and, at S° = S₀, v_{S₀} = σ²(1 + o_P(1)):
>
>     LR_l = κ_b · G_l · (1 + o_P(1)),   G_l := −ν log(1 − x_{S₀,l}) = Z_{S₀,l}²/2 · (1 + o_P(1)),
>
> uniformly over l ∉ S₀ on the EXP′ event of W1-EXP Thm 1 / W2-PREM Lemma U (the remainder of the expansion is the same
> R on both sides and cancels up to the RSS-ratio term). **PROVED** up to the two uniform expansions, which are candidate
> theorems. Check (n = 800): LR = 0.620 vs κG = 0.621; 1.050 vs 1.050; 0.429 vs 0.437; with κ = 0 (same block as all the
> signal) LR = 0.000 exactly.
>
> Sign and size: the posterior rewards a chance correlation Z² of a null with the full exponent Z²/2; the diluted table
> rewards it with (1 − κ_b)Z²/2. Hence π/π₀ on S₀ + l is e^{κ_b Z²/2}·(1 + o(1)) relative to its value at S₀.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md`)*
- What changed and why: F-DRAFT defines $x_{T,l}=(RSS_T-RSS_{T+l})/RSS_T$ (ordinary partial $R^2$) and claims "exactly" $LR_l=\nu[\log(1-x_{T,l})-\log(1-x_{S^\circ,l})]$. A-REV4 found this false for the v3 score (RF254, CE198: ridge-adjusted $Q$ and the $2b_0$ offset). O-WSTAB's version works with the exact v3 quantities $t_S$, $\bar Q=2b_0+y^\top y$, $y:=(t_{T+l}-t_T)/(\bar Q-t_{S^\circ})$ and the realised dilution fraction $\kappa:=(\bar x-x_T)/(1-x_T)$, and gives two-sided bounds (an exact formula $LR=\nu[g(y)-g((1-\kappa)y)]$ plus $\kappa G\le LR\le\kappa G/(1-y)$), not an equality with $\kappa G$. A-REV4's repair $h_{T,l}:=(t_{T+l}-t_T)/(2b_0+Q_T)$ is the same kind of quantity as $\delta/(1-x_T)=(1-\kappa)y$ in O-WSTAB's proof.
- Status history: F-DRAFT "PROVED modulo EXP′ (candidate)" -> A-REV4 ERROR (identity) and GAP (uniformity) -> O-WSTAB Lemma W2 PROVED (exact finite-$n$ under BO, "with no EXP′ needed"); SF: CHECK_SEP_W "Lemma W2 (§3.2), exact form and ORTH reading: verified" (F5 exposition: $y\ge0$ needs the Woodbury monotonicity line; 138 pairs, 6 BO designs, 0 violations); XF: A-REV6 W2-R (TH378) is the Astra-authored parallel repair, "GAP pending Claude".
- Depends on: LM209, TH350, CJ121 (EXP′) (only for the general-BO identification of $G$ with $Z^2_{T,l}/2$). Feeds: LM213 (via (S2)), TH362.

### TH360 — Proposition L ($\ell$-form of T13: $\log(1+\chi^2)=\ell(u)+\ell(w)-2\ell(v)$)  [proposition]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2, §3.3; the same identity is O-STAGES Lemma 0 (LM216). Statement (verbatim):
> **Proposition L (ℓ-form of T13; deterministic; PROVED).** For every S° ∈ Ω:
> (i) ℓ is real-analytic and convex on ℝ, and ℓ ≥ 0.
> (ii) For all real u, v, with w = 2v − u: log(1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u)) = ℓ(u) + ℓ(w) − 2ℓ(v), i.e. ρ_Ω(u, v) = exp{−[ℓ(u) + ℓ(w) − 2ℓ(v)]}.
> The same holds for the V-restricted bridge with ℓ_V(φ) := −log q^V_φ(S°), S° ∈ V, and ρ_V (T13(iii)).
> (iii) For 0 ≤ u, v ≤ 1: ℓ(u), ℓ(v) ≤ ℓ*, hence ℓ(w) − 2ℓ* ≤ log(1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u)) ≤ ℓ(w) + ℓ*.
> (iv) 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) = π(S°)² e^{ℓ(2)}/π₀(S°), and ℓ(2) − 2ℓ* ≤ log(1 + χ²(π‖π₀)) ≤ ℓ(2) + ℓ*.
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (author); SF: CHECK_SEP_W "Prop L (i)-(iv): verified (V-restricted part checked from 00_COMMON's ρ_V definition, T13(iii) not seen)"; numerics: identity to $3.6\cdot10^{-12}$ over 1400 random $(u,v)$ in 7 ORTH designs. XF: no separate A-REV9 row (it underlies W and W′). Connection to locked TH111 (T13) (REPORT, "Connections"): "T13(i) with V = Ω and T13(iii) with W = V are Prop L(ii)... T13(ii)'s coverage bound 10/(9(1−ε_C)²) is the statement that the second differences of ℓ_Ω and ℓ_V agree up to log(1−ε_C) terms."

### TH361 — Proposition G (ideal-grid sandwich $\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(1+1/g_+)\rceil\}\le T\le\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(1+1/g_-)\rceil\}$)  [proposition]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2, §3.4. Statement (verbatim, already carrying the review's F4 correction $\max\{1,\cdot\}$):
> **Proposition G (ideal-grid sandwich; deterministic; PROVED).** Fix S° with 2ℓ* < c. Let g₋ := sup{g ≥ 0 : ℓ(1+g) ≤ c − ℓ*}
> and g₊ := sup{g ≥ 0 : ℓ(1+g) ≤ c + 2ℓ*}, both in (0, ∞]. The *ideal grid* is φ₀ = 0,
> φ_t := max{v ∈ (φ_{t−1}, 1] : ρ_Ω(φ_{t−1}, v) ≥ 0.9}, until φ_T = 1. It is well defined, and
>  max{1, ⌈log₂(1 + 1/g₊)⌉} ≤ T ≤ max{1, ⌈log₂(1 + 1/g₋)⌉} (with 1/∞ := 0).
> Moreover, along any grid with every interval accepted: 2ℓ(φ_t) ≥ ℓ(φ_{t−1}) − c (the masked-regime halving of [PF] WS7(d)).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Remark on the method's grid (verbatim from the proof): "The method bisects only 60 times and appends the largest tested passing point... The method also uses ρ_V on pilot temperatures, not ρ_Ω... Closing the gap between the ideal and the method's grid is OPEN (a pilot-sampling statement)." (CJ265.)
- Status: PROVED; SF: CHECK_SEP_W "Prop G (§3.4): verified, with the upper bound read as max{1, ⌈log₂(1+1/g₋)⌉} (F4 exposition)". Overlaps O-STAGES Theorem G/F (TH364, TH366) but is derived independently from the second-difference form. Feeds: TH363.

### LM213 — Lemma SEP (separable domination under ORTH)  [lemma]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2, §3.5. Statement (verbatim):
> **Lemma SEP (separable domination under ORTH; deterministic; PROVED).** Assume ORTH (XᵀX = (n−1)I_p), any partition, any
> S₀ ∈ Ω (here only a reference model). Put x_j := x_{{j}}, s := Σ_{j∈S₀} x_j, N := [p] ∖ S₀, ū := Σ_{j∈N} x_j/(1 − s), and
> suppose ū < 1. For w ∈ [0, 2] let β(w) := 1/((1−s)(1−ū)) if w ≤ 1 and β(w) := w/((1−s)(1−ū)) − (w − 1) if 1 ≤ w ≤ 2;
> c_j(w) := n^{−1/2}e^{β(w)νx_j}, q(w) := p^{−1}Σ_{j∈N} c_j(w). If q(w) < 1 then
>  **ℓ_{S₀}(w) ≤ Σ_{j∈S₀} log(1 + 2p√n e^{−νx_j}) − (s₀ + 1) log(1 − q(w)).**
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Status: PROVED; SF: CHECK_SEP_W "Lemma SEP (§3.5) (crux 1): verified" (F7 exposition; numerics: 30 cases, 0 violations; display reproduces direct scores to $3.4\cdot10^{-11}$). XF: A-REV9 "Convexly moving each deletion interval rightward proves SEP's F2; the prior ratios are bounded by (2p)^m(s0+e)!/(s0! p^e). Summation yields the separable geometric bound." Proof route (Summary:) convex telescoping (F2) of the fit-fraction sums, prior-ratio bound, elementary symmetric polynomials $e_e(c/p)\le q^e/e!$. Feeds: TH362(b)(d).

### LM215 — (HT) heavy-tail lemma (no infinite expectations)  [lemma]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §3.6. Statement (verbatim):
> **(HT) Heavy-tail lemma (no infinite expectations).** E[e^{Z²/2}1{Z² ≤ τ}] = 2∫₀^{√τ}(2π)^{−1/2}dz = √(2τ/π), so by
> Markov, Σ_{j∈N} e^{Z_j²/2}1{Z_j² ≤ 2 log m} = O_P(m√log m). On {max_N Z² ≤ 2 log m}, for *every* a ≥ 1 simultaneously,
> Σ_N e^{aZ_j²/2} ≤ m^{a−1}Σ_N e^{Z_j²/2} = m^a·O_P(√log m).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (author; used inside the verified W(a),(b)). Note (CHECK_SEP_W F1 remark): at fixed exponent $a>1$ the truncated moment is $\asymp m^a/((a-1)\sqrt{\log m})$, not $m^a\sqrt{\log m}$, so the $\sqrt{\log p}$ loss is an artefact of uniformity in $a$ near 1. Feeds: TH362. See RF260.

### TH362 — Theorem W (ORTH; two-sided weight stability law and its divergent-side lower and upper bounds) = "Theorem WS"  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative, latest repaired version): `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2 Theorem W, proofs §3.6; independent check `O-WSTAB/review/CHECK_SEP_W.md`. Aliases: Theorem W (ORTH); H-ORTH; "Theorem WS" (REGISTRY_v2 §F rename); W(a)-(g). Positions: [pos 489-493 (launch), 659/666, 748 (finished), 1441, 1449 (later correction by HQ)].
- Statement (verbatim, hypotheses H-ORTH and parts (a)-(g)):
> **Theorem W (ORTH; two-sided).** Hypotheses **H-ORTH**: G; ORTH; s₀ ≥ 1 fixed and θ*_{S₀} fixed with all entries nonzero, so
> **r := R²_pop = ‖θ*‖²/(‖θ*‖² + σ*²) ∈ (0, 1)** is fixed; p → ∞ with p log p = o(n); any partition (it may depend on X)
> whose blocks have size ≤ B, with B fixed (or B ≤ 16, the method's cap). Let N₀ be the nulls in truth-free blocks
> (|N₀| ≥ p − s₀B), and ρ_n(w) := p^{(w−1)₊r}/√n. Then, with P₀-probability → 1:
> (a) **(both ends concentrate)** ℓ(0), ℓ(1) = O_P(√(log p/n)) for S° = S₀. So π₀(S₀) → 1 and π(S₀) → 1 (self-contained;
>  consistent with W1-EXP Thm 2/6 and locked T03).
> (b) **(uniform upper bound)** There is V_n = O_P(1), not depending on w, with q(w) ≤ V_n ρ_n(w)√(log p) for all w ∈ [0, 2].
>  Hence ℓ(w) ≤ o_P(1) − (s₀+1) log(1 − V_nρ_n(w)√log p) whenever V_nρ_n(w)√log p < 1. The o_P(1) is uniform in w and
>  equal to O_P(p√n e^{−c₀n}).
> (c) **(uniform lower bound)** For all w ∈ [1, 2]: O(w) ≥ ρ_n(w)(log p)^{−(1+(w−1)r)/2}e^{−U_n}, with U_n = O_P(1) not
>  depending on w.
> (d) **(convergent side)** If p^r/√n → 0, then for every ε ∈ (0, r): χ²(π‖π₀) ≥ p^{r−ε}/√n. If moreover
>  p^r√(log p)/√n → 0, then also χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ p^{r+ε}/√n. So the one-step ESS fraction 1/(1+χ²) → 1 at this polynomial rate.
>  (The window where p^r/√n → 0 but p^r√(log p)/√n does not is not covered on the upper side: review finding F1.)
> (e) **(divergent side, lower bound)** If L_n := r log p − ½ log n − ((1+r)/2) log log p → ∞, then log(1 + χ²(π‖π₀)) ≥ (1 − o_P(1))e^{(L_n − C₁ − 1)/r}
>  with the constant C₁ := 1 + log 2 + (1+r) log 4 + ((1+r)/2) log(4π). With p = n^{A+o(1)} and Ar > ½ this is
>  n^{A − 1/(2r) − o(1)}, and the ESS fraction is ≤ exp(−n^{A−1/(2r)−o(1)}).
> (g) **(divergent side, upper bound)** w.p. → 1, ℓ(2) ≤ (s₀+1) log 2 + o(1) + K_r(1 + o_P(1))·[p^r(log p)^{2(1+r)}/√n]^{1/r}
>  with K_r := (r/2)(2π/((1+r) sin(π/(1+r))))^{(1+r)/r}. Together with (e), when L_n → ∞:
>  c e^{L_n/r} ≤ log(1+χ²(π‖π₀)) ≤ C e^{L_n/r}(log p)^{5(1+r)/(2r)}.
> (f) **(KL and TV)** TV(π, π₀) ≤ ℓ* = O_P(√(log p/n)) and KL(π‖π₀) = O_P((log p)^{3/2}/√n) in all cases, including (e).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Earlier versions / repairs: (1) F-DRAFT Theorem W (CJ256) had (a) lower bound, (b) upper bound, (c) sharp form; (b),(c) are false on the divergent side (RF252, RF253). ### TH363 — Theorem W' (ORTH; ideal grid): $T_{\rm ideal}=1$ if $2Ar<1$, $=2$ if $2Ar>1$, always $\le2$  [theorem]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §2 and §3.7. Aliases: W'; Cor. WS-W' (registry rename); "W' ideal grid ≤ 2 stages". Statement (verbatim):
> **Theorem W′ (ORTH; ideal grid).** Under H-ORTH, with G_n := log n/(2r log p): w.p. → 1, g± (Prop G, S° = S₀) satisfy
> |g± − G_n| ≤ δ_n with δ_n = O_P(log log p/log p) whenever G_n + δ_n ≤ 1, and g₋ ≥ 1 when G_n − δ_n ≥ 1. Consequently
> T_ideal ∈ {⌈log₂(1 + 1/(G_n + δ_n))⌉, …, ⌈log₂(1 + 1/(G_n − δ_n))⌉} ∩ {1, 2}. In particular, with p = n^{A+o(1)}:
> **T_ideal = 1 if 2Ar < 1 and T_ideal = 2 if 2Ar > 1**, and always T_ideal ≤ 2 w.p. → 1 (ORTH forces p ≤ n − 1, so
> G_n ≥ 1/(2r) > ½).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md`)*
- Earlier version: F-DRAFT Conjecture W' (CJ257): $T_{\rm ideal}=\lceil\log_2(1+1/g)\rceil+O(1)$, "T_ideal = O(1) whenever p ≤ n^A". O-WSTAB proves the sharper statement under ORTH ("ORTH forces p ≤ n − 1, so G_n ≥ 1/(2r) > ½"). Numerics (REPORT §4, `orth_grid.py`): $2Ar<1$ gives $T_{\rm ideal}=1$; $2Ar>1$ gives 2; one finite-$n$ deviation: A = 0.45, n = 10^16 ($2Ar=0.81$) gives $T_{\rm ideal}=2$, "within the stated error δ_n".
- Status: PROVED (author); SF: CHECK_SEP_W "Theorem W′ (§3.7) (crux 3): verified" (F6 exposition, harmless; uses W(a),(b),(c) and Prop G only, so F1 does not reach it). XF: A-REV9 "O-WSTAB W prime | VERIFIED ideal full-space grid under H-ORTH; production-grid transfer remains GAP" ("equality is not resolved"). Relation to O-STAGES: O-STAGES Cor. W' (TH367) is conditional on the layer law (LL) and states $|T^*-\lceil\log_2(1+1/g)\rceil|\le1$; REGISTRY_v2 conflict C22 notes O-WSTAB's W' "is PROVED independently and is consistent".
- Depends on: TH361, TH362(a)(b)(c). Feeds: none (campaign-only); K29 "favourable stage law O(1)" is DRAFT-ONLY and routed to FUTURE_WORK FW23, with the (LL)/over-tilted $q_w$ input not a design condition.

### CE198 — A-REV4's explicit feasible counterexample to F-DRAFT W2  [counterexample]
- Source: `A-REV4/REVIEW.md` §3 ("W2 ERROR, explicit feasible counterexample"); reproduced on Owls (A-REV4 NUMERICS). Construction (verbatim):
> **W2 ERROR, explicit feasible counterexample.** Take n=20,p=4, centered orthogonal columns with G=19I, blocks {1,3},{2,4}, S°={1}, l=2, ||y||²=19, and squared z coordinates (100,30,0,0). Such a response exists because 130/19<19; the remaining energy can lie in an orthogonal contrast direction. K=4 so the addition is feasible. With nu=10.01, c=19.02, the actual v3 log-odds difference is
>
>     nu [log(1-1.5/19.02) - log(1-1.5/14.02)] = 0.310405538698...
>
> Ordinary RSS partial R² instead gives 0.353784569589..., a discrepancy 0.043379030891. This is not rounding. The source explicitly defines x from RSS, but v3 integrates a ridge-adjusted Q and .02 offset. Repair with h_{T,l}=(t_{T+l}-t_T)/(.02+Q_T); then h_S=h_T(.02+Q_T)/(.02+Q_S) and the displayed log identity holds with h. Require |S°|<K. Uniform multiplicative Gaussian-gain equivalence is a separate GAP: an O_P(1) additive remainder need not cancel and does not give uniform relative errors near Z_l=0. Prove an additive uniform remainder with sufficient rate, or restrict to controlled extreme-value comparisons.

In the large-deviation regime this gives halving rather than length-proportional steps, and the two-state family has L ≤ π with T* → ∞."

### RF256 — The draft's §5.3 premise: "weak cross-block dependence implies the divergence is controlled by cross-block covariance and importance-weight variance stays bounded" (for v3's tables)  [refuted claim]
- Source: false claim: draft §5.3 (quoted at CJ251); refutation: `F-DRAFT/CROSSWALK.md` §0 and §2.2 (via TH350), `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md` §6 Interpretation (TH356), REPORT "Connections"; positions: [pos 616, 748].
- False claim (verbatim from the O-WSTAB brief): "under weak cross-block dependence, the divergence between the product of block posteriors and the full posterior is controlled by cross-block covariance; hence importance-weight variance stays bounded."
- Refutation (verbatim, O-WSTAB PROOF §6 Interpretation):
> **Interpretation.** The importance weight of S₀ ∪ {l} relative to S₀ is e^{d_σ(S₀+l) − d_σ(S₀)} ≈ e^{ωZ_l²/2}: π₀ judges
> the null l against a residual variance inflated by the out-of-block signal (σ*² → σ*² + Δ), π judges it against σ*².
> Over p nulls the largest Z_l² is ≈ 2 log p, so a rare start draw S₀ + l carries weight ≈ p^ω. This is a
> **noise-variance-sharing** effect, present at zero cross-block correlation: the draft's claim that weak cross-block
> dependence bounds the importance-weight variance is false as stated for χ² (it is true for TV, and for KL by (c)
> whenever q_{1+θ}(S₀) → 1 for some θ > 0).
*(verbatim from `O-WSTAB/PROOF.md`)*
  and (F-DRAFT CROSSWALK §2.2, verbatim): "So the draft's premise 'zero cross-block covariance ⇒ product ≈ posterior' holds for a known-σ² table and fails for v3's integrated-σ² table by a Θ(n) term." It is true for TV (and for KL by TH355(c) when $q_{1+\theta}(S_0)\to1$) and for χ² only when $2Ar<1$ (TH362), "even at zero cross-block correlation".
- Replacement: TH350, TH356, TH362. Concrete instance: CE199. HQ's relay to Felipe [pos 616]: "the discrepancy between the start and the posterior is **not** driven by cross-block correlation, as the draft guessed. It is driven by each block table using its own estimate of σ², a 'dilution' term that grows linearly in n."

### CE204 — $E\,e^{aZ^2/2}=\infty$ for $a\ge1$ (the divergent expectation)  [counterexample]
- Source: `O-WSTAB/REPORT.md` §3.6 (HT) proof line: $E[e^{Z^2/2}1\{Z^2\le\tau\}]=2\int_0^{\sqrt\tau}(2\pi)^{-1/2}dz=\sqrt{2\tau/\pi}$, which grows without bound in $\tau$; so $E\,e^{Z^2/2}=\infty$ and a fortiori $E\,e^{(1+r)Z^2/2}=\infty$.

### TH378 — A-REV6 W2-R: exact regularised identity and an ORTH uniform additive expansion (Astra-authored repair of F-DRAFT W2)  [proposition]
- Source: `A-REV6/WEIGHTS.md` section "W2-R"; registry `REV6-cands(A6)`; positions: [pos 807 (launch), 919].
- Statement (verbatim):
> ## W2-R: exact regularised identity and an ORTH uniform repair
>
> **Astra-authored candidate; GAP for adoption pending Claude verification.**
>
> (a) For any data satisfying sample BO, any S with |S|<K, and l outside S in block b, set T=S intersect C_b and
>
>     h_{U,l}=(t_{U+l}-t_U)/(2b0+Q_U),  U=T,S.
>
> Then 0<=h<1 and, exactly,
>
>     h_{S,l}=h_{T,l}(2b0+Q_T)/(2b0+Q_S),
>     d(S+l)-d(S)=nu[log(1-h_{T,l})-log(1-h_{S,l})].
>
> Proof: BO makes the two explained increments equal and the determinant addition factors identical. Insert the exact score log BF(U)=-log D_U/2-nu log[(2b0+Q_U)/c]. Prior odds cancel between posterior and start. Positivity of the updated residual denominator gives h<1. No Gaussian assumption is needed. Ordinary RSS partial R-squared cannot replace h.
>
> (b) Consider deterministic centered ORTH designs X'X=(n-1)I_p with p<=n-1, raw contrast response Y=X theta+epsilon, epsilon isotropic N(0,sigma² I) on the contrast space, sigma>0, fixed support size s0 and fixed nonzero coefficients. Use v3 response standardisation, fixed a0=b0=.01, a deterministic partition, and |S0|<K. For l outside S0, define Z_l=x_l'epsilon/(sigma sqrt(n-1)); these are independent standard normals. Let T_b=S0 intersect C_b, Delta_b=sum_{j in S0 outside C_b}theta_j², and kappa_b=Delta_b/(sigma²+Delta_b). Then
>
>     max_{l outside S0}|d(S0+l)-d(S0)-kappa_{b(l)} Z_l²/2|
>       = O_P(log n/sqrt(n)+(log n)^2/n)=o_P(1).
>
> Proof: in ORTH, H=n²I, t_U=(n-1)/n times the ordinary explained sum of squares. Undoing response standardisation multiplies every residual denominator by the common sample variance s_Y²; its 2b0 offset becomes 2b0 s_Y²=O_P(1). Gaussian quadratic-form concentration and fixed s0 give, simultaneously over the at most 2^s0 different T_b,
>
>     (2b0+Q_{S0})s_Y²/n=sigma²+O_P(n^-1/2),
>     (2b0+Q_{T_b})s_Y²/n=sigma²+Delta_b+O_P(n^-1/2).
>
> The raw-scale null increment is sigma²(n-1)Z_l²/n, independent of the reference U. Since nu=n/2+.01, this yields
>
>     nu h_{S0,l}=Z_l²/2 [1+O_P(n^-1/2)],
>     nu h_{T_b,l}=(1-kappa_b)Z_l²/2 [1+O_P(n^-1/2)],
>
> with random error bounds common to all l. A Gaussian union bound gives max_l Z_l²=O_P(log n), hence max h=O_P(log n/n). Uniform Taylor expansion -log(1-h)=h+O(h²) in (a) proves the assertion. This is an additive error, sufficient to exponentiate the single-null discrepancy uniformly; it asserts neither a relative error near Z_l=0 nor control of multi-extra layers. It narrows BO to ORTH and does not certify the original W2.
*(verbatim from `A-REV6/WEIGHTS.md`)*
- Status: "Astra-authored candidate; GAP for adoption pending Claude verification" (A-REV6); registry: "REFEREE ... pending Claude verification"; no Claude verification recorded by pos 1110. Relation: (a) is the same kind of identity as O-WSTAB LM212's exact formula; (b) is narrower than F-DRAFT W2 ("It narrows BO to ORTH and does not certify the original W2").
- Depends on: TH350. Feeds: none. NM-R (same file) belongs to theme 11 (TH393 (NM-R)).

## Part F. O-STAGES: the stage count of the bridge (Lemma 0, Lemma 1, Theorem G, L, F, M, Corollaries W', W''')

Branch `theory/O-STAGES` (Opus 5.5 high, CP, laptop; started 19:29 UTC, head 8d3c142 at the registry cut, REPORT.md only). Task (HQ [pos 733]): "a theorem for the number of bridge stages the calibration actually produces. Two paper results rest on it: T26's last premise and T38's cost exponent." Headline of the REPORT (verbatim):

> ## 1. Headline
>
> 1. **PROVED (structure).** For any finite candidate set V, the ESS step criterion is monotone in both endpoints. So the
>    bisection finds the exact frontier, which settles W′'s open obligation (1) for every V. The greedy rule also produces
>    the **shortest** valid grid: no grid whose every step has ESS ≥ 0.9 has fewer intervals. The v3 construction, which
>    refines the pilot's points, is optimal among grids that refine those points, and max(T*_V, T_P) ≤ T_grid ≤ T*_V + T_P.
> 2. **PROVED (key identity).** For every state R, ρ(u, v) = q_u(R)·q_{2v−u}(R)/q_v(R)². The ESS of a stage is set by the
>    mass of one state at the extrapolated temperature w = 2v − u, and this produces a **halving law**. In the favourable
>    regime this gives a deterministic two-sided bound on T* through q_w(S₀), w ∈ [1, 2] (Theorem F). Given Theorem W's
>    layer law, that bound becomes **W′ with |T* − ⌈log₂(1 + 1/g)⌉| ≤ 1** (PROVED conditional on the layer law, which is
>    a PROOF SKETCH in F-DRAFT).
> 3. **COUNTEREXAMPLE to W″ as stated; corrected form PROVED (two-state) / PROOF SKETCH (families).** A masked crossing
>    costs **log₂ A₀ + O(1)** stages, where A₀ = log[π₀(S°)/π₀(S₀)] is the start's masking depth. It does not depend on the
>    posterior-side gap A₁. The 3π window count is only the O(1) part. Exact numerics give T* = log₂A₀ + 7.7 ± 0.4. That
>    reproduces F-DRAFT's proxy-split counts 14 and 16, and gives 18 at n = 3200. The proxy masking (A₀ = Θ(n)) costs
>    log₂n + O(1) stages. LH/T27 masking (A₀ = c log p + (c/2)log n) costs O(log log n) stages.
> 4. **Path length is the right quantity only for fine grids.** We PROVED √c·T*(c) → L = ∫₀¹ sd_{q_φ}(d)dφ as c → 0, with
>    two-sided κ-regularity bounds. At the production c = log(10/9), the two-state family has L ≤ π while T* → ∞, so the
>    length does not determine T_n.
> 5. **T26 and T38(c).** In the favourable regime, (T_n+1)Δ_n → 0 holds whenever Δ_n → 0 and the over-corrected law
>    q_{1+g₀} still puts mass 0.9/(1−Δ_n) on S₀. On BO with p ≤ n^A, T* = O(1), so P1 needs nothing beyond Δ_n → 0. In the
>    masked regime P1 fails anyway, because Δ_n → 1. The cost term N_nT_n(p+B+2) carries T_n = O(1) on favourable BO,
>    log₂n + O(1) on proxy masking, O(log log n) on LH masking, and ≤ T_e = O(log²(n+p)) always.
*(verbatim from `O-STAGES/REPORT.md`)*

The model of the grid rule it analyses (verbatim; `cpp/v3_calib.h`, METHODOLOGY_v3 §§6.6-6.7):

> ## 2. Model of the grid rule (from `cpp/v3_calib.h`, METHODOLOGY_v3 §§6.6–6.7)
>
> - F_V(t) := log Σ_{S∈V} γ₀(S)e^{t d(S)} for t ∈ [0, 2], with q^V_t ∝ γ₀e^{td} on V. Population version: V = Ω, F = log Z̄_t.
> - Φ_V(u, v) := F_V(u) − 2F_V(v) + F_V(2v − u) = −log ρ_V(u, v) = log(1 + χ²(q_v‖q_u)) = D₂(q_v‖q_u), the Rényi-2
>   divergence. A step is accepted iff Φ_V ≤ c := log(10/9) ≈ 0.10536, i.e. ρ ≥ 0.90.
> - **Pilot (population, H → ∞):** from u, take v = 1 if it passes; otherwise bisect on (u, 1]. The floor 1/T_e is
>   inactive in every case below. This is the greedy grid on Ω, and we write T*_Ω for its number of intervals.
> - **Candidate grid:** the pilot points P are the targets. From u, take b = min{P ∩ (u, 1]}; append b if Φ_V(u, b) ≤ c,
>   otherwise bisect on (u, b]. The construction fails beyond T_e intervals, so **T_n ≤ T_e on success** (deterministic).
> - T26's T_n and T38's T_n are the final run's interval count, which is T_grid of the last accepted construction.
*(verbatim from `O-STAGES/REPORT.md`)*

### TH365 — O-STAGES Theorem L (thermodynamic path length)  [theorem]
- Source: `O-STAGES/REPORT.md` §3; STG-L. Statement (verbatim):
> **Theorem L (path length). PROVED.** Let L := ∫₀¹ √F″(t) dt = ∫₀¹ sd_{q_t}(d) dt, the thermodynamic (Fisher–Rao) length.
> (i) For any valid step, Φ(u, v) = ∫₀^Δ∫₀^Δ F″(u+s+r) ds dr ∈ [Δ² inf_{[u,w]}F″, Δ² sup_{[u,w]}F″], with Δ = v − u.
> (ii) Let κ_G be the largest ratio sup/inf of F″ over the windows [u, 2v−u] of the greedy grid. Then
> T*(c) ≥ L/√(κ_G c). Let κ′ be the same ratio over the grid built with Δ(u) = sup{Δ : Δ² sup_{[u,u+2Δ]}F″ ≤ c}. Then
> T*(c) ≤ L√(κ′/c) + 1.
> (iii) If d is nonconstant on V, then √c·T*(c) → L as c ↓ 0.
> (iv) Worst case: T* ≤ ⌈D/(2√c)⌉ = ⌈1.54·D⌉, where D := max_V d − min_V d.
*(verbatim from `O-STAGES/REPORT.md`)*
  The caveat (verbatim):
> *Why this is not the answer at the production c:* in the approach to a crossing, F″ grows like e^{Dt} across a window
> of size Δ = Θ(1). Then κ_G = e^{Θ(D)} and (ii) is vacuous. See Theorem M.
*(verbatim from `O-STAGES/REPORT.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (SF none, XF none). KNOWN—CITE: Syed et al. 2024 Thm 3, Gelman–Meng 1998 (K28, CONFIRMED-D). Final card: M7(e) "[cited] √c·T*(c) → Λ_len := ∫₀¹ sd_{q_φ}(d)dφ ≤ √J as c → 0". Depends on: LM216. Feeds: K28 (cited); the "length governs T* only as c→0" is RF258.
