## Part G. API-T26BUD: Theorem G stage laws and the one-stage regime (Theorem 6 without a run premise)

Branch `theory/API-T26BUD` (Opus on the Agent SDK, $12 cap, API promotional credit; "task R5 (T26-BUDGET), Theorem 6 with a proved stage count", referee-response task R5 of F-REFEREE's RESPONSE_PLAN). HQ: launched in the API wave [pos 906, 911] ("Theorem 6 with a proved stage count"), result [pos 978]: "A proved stage count; in the one-stage regime T26 holds with no extra premise. Closes a premise of Theorem 6." The task (verbatim, `campaign/tasks/API-T26BUD.md`):

> ### R5. T26-BUDGET: Theorem 6 with a proved stage count
>
> **Paper role:** Theorem 6's premise (M5, m15).
>
> **Claim to prove.** On ORTH (and on FAV of W5-FAVIID if R6 verifies it), the calibration's ESS bisection rule produces a
> realised stage count T_n with T_n ≤ C₁ + C₂ log(1/Δ_n) (or any bound such that (T_n + 1)Δ_n → 0 in P₀-probability);
> hence (P1) holds and Theorem 6(A-i)(A-ii) follow with no premise on the run. Inputs: `v3_calib.h` (the bisection on the
> ESS of e^{(φ′−φ)d}), W2-T26 Lemmas 1–3, W1-EXP Thm 1/6, W2-T26 Prop. C (ORTH). If the bound fails because the grid can
> over-refine, state the weakest extra rule (e.g. a cap T^max_n = C log n) under which it holds and whether the cap is
> ever active in the study (it is not: realised T ∈ {1, 2}).
*(verbatim from `campaign/tasks/API-T26BUD.md`)*

Headline of the REPORT (verbatim):

> ## 1. Headline
>
> - **Theorem G (grid stage count). PROVED, deterministic.** This applies to `v3_calib.h::build_grid`. On any successful construction
>   with S₀ ∈ V, the realised count is T = N^pil + k^bis, with k^bis ≤ ⌈log₂(1/η_n)⌉. Here N^pil is the number of pilot
>   stages, and η_n is the largest η ≤ 1 with R(0) ≤ ε₀ and R(1+η) ≤ ε₀, where R(t) = (1 − q_t(S₀))/q_t(S₀) and
>   ε₀ = 0.9^{−1/2} − 1. The grid can over-refine only through the pilot, or when the bridge extrapolated past φ = 1 leaves S₀.
> - **Theorem 1 (one-stage regime). PROVED, given its inputs.** If 1 − π₀(S₀) → 0, 1 − π(S₀) → 0, χ²(π‖π₀) → 0 and the HPM of π
>   is S₀ w.p. → 1, then the pilot jumps 0 → 1 and the grid is {0, 1}: **T_n = 1 w.p. → 1**. So (P1) holds and Theorem 6
>   (A-i)(A-ii) follow with no premise on the run. The proof uses only the iid first pilot stage, so no occupancy control
>   is needed.
> - **ORTH (Proposition O). PROOF SKETCH.** R(1+η) = O_P(n^{−1/2+Aη(1−λ*)} polylog) with 1 − λ* ≤ R²₀. So χ²(π‖π₀) → 0, and
>   T_n = 1 w.p. → 1, when A·(1 − λ*) < ½ (in particular for p ≤ n^A with A < 1/(2R²₀)). Otherwise k^bis = O(1), but the
>   number of pilot stages is only CONJECTURED to be O_P(1) (Conjecture P). The missing piece is occupancy control under the
>   adaptive pilot.
> - **Rule CAP. PROVED.** Under the cap "more than min{T_e, T^cap_n} intervals → fail" with T^cap_nΔ_n →_P 0 (e.g. ⌈log₂ n⌉),
>   (P1) holds deterministically on 𝒢_n, and the cap costs nothing in Theorem A. The existing T_e = O(log²n) already gives
>   the asymptotic statement (W2-T26 Theorem B). Only its constant 1000 makes it vacuous at finite n.
> - **Numerics (exact p = 18, the actual pilot and grid rules).** [filled in §4]
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/REPORT.md`)*

Definitions (verbatim, PROOF.md §0):

> ## 0. New symbols
>
> | symbol | definition |
> |---|---|
> | r_S, e_S | r_S = γ₀(S)/γ₀(S₀) (start odds of S against S₀); e_S = d(S) − d(S₀) |
> | R(t) | Σ_{S ∈ Ω_K, S ≠ S₀} r_S e^{t e_S} = (1 − q_t(S₀))/q_t(S₀), for t ∈ ℝ (Ω_K = feasible models) |
> | R_V(t) | the same sum restricted to S ∈ V∖{S₀}; R_V ≤ R termwise when S₀ ∈ V |
> | ε₀ | 0.9^{−1/2} − 1 ≈ 0.05409, so that 2 log(1 + ε₀) = log(1/0.9) |
> | η_n | sup{η ∈ (0, 1] : R(0) ≤ ε₀ and R(1 + η) ≤ ε₀} (sup ∅ := 0) |
> | N^pil | number of pilot stages = number of distinct pilot temperatures in (0, 1] (the last one is 1) |
> | k^bis | number of grid intervals whose right endpoint came from the bisection branch of `build_grid` |
> | D_k | for pilot stage k with population d₁, …, d_H: max_i d_i − (the ⌈0.02H⌉-th smallest d_i) (2 %-trimmed range) |
> | a | 0.5125 ≤ 2 arccosh(0.98/√0.9) (≈ 0.51249…; we use a = 0.5124 in proofs, 0.5125 in the script — immaterial) |
> | T^cap_n | an optional cap on the number of grid intervals (Rule CAP, §5) |
>
> Identity used throughout: R(1 + η) = Σ_{S≠S₀} r_S^{−η} (r_S e^{e_S})^{1+η}. Here r_S e^{e_S} = π(S)/π(S₀). So R(1 + η) is the
> order-(1+η) Rényi-type moment of the posterior odds against the start odds. In particular
> **R(2) = [π₀(S₀)/π(S₀)²]·Σ_{S≠S₀} π(S)²/π₀(S)**, and exactly 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) = [π(S₀)²/π₀(S₀)]·(1 + R(2)). So, when π(S₀), π₀(S₀) → 1,
> R(2) → 0 ⇔ χ²(π‖π₀) → 0.
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*

### LM220 — API-T26BUD Fact 1 (monotonicity of $\rho_V(u,\cdot)$ and of the pilot's population ESS)  [lemma]
- Source: `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §1. Statement (verbatim):
> **Fact 1 (monotonicity). PROVED.** For fixed u, v ↦ ρ_V(u, v) is non-increasing on [u, ∞). The same holds for the pilot's
> population ESS, δ ↦ ESS(δ) = (Σ_i e^{δd_i})²/Σ_i e^{2δd_i}, on [0, ∞).
> *Proof.* d/dv[−log ρ_V] = 2F′_V(2v − u) − 2F′_V(v) ≥ 0, because F_V is convex (it is a log-sum-exp of affine functions)
> and 2v − u ≥ v. For the pilot, d/dδ log ESS = 2Ē_δ[d] − 2Ē_{2δ}[d] ≤ 0. Here Ē_s is the mean under weights ∝ e^{sd_i}, which is
> non-decreasing in s (its derivative is a variance). ∎
>
> Consequence: in both bisections the set of passing points in (u, b] is an interval (u, v*] ∩ (u, b]. The invariant "lo
> passes or lo = u; hi fails" holds, so after 60 halvings lo ≥ v* − (b − u)2^{−60} whenever some tested point passed.
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (candidate; same fact as O-STAGES Lemma 1, LM217, proved independently for the as-coded pilot ESS). Feeds: TH370.

### LM221 — API-T26BUD Fact 2 (reference decomposition $-\log\rho_V=L_V(u)+L_V(2v-u)-2L_V(v)$)  [lemma]
- Source: `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §1. Statement (verbatim):
> **Fact 2 (reference decomposition). PROVED.** If S₀ ∈ V, then for u < v,
>  −log ρ_V(u, v) = L_V(u) + L_V(2v − u) − 2L_V(v) ≤ L_V(u) + L_V(2v − u),  L_V := log(1 + R_V) ≥ 0.
> *Proof.* F_V(t) = log γ₀(S₀) + t d(S₀) + L_V(t). The affine parts cancel in the second difference, because
> u + (2v − u) − 2v = 0. L_V ≥ 0. ∎
>
> R_V is a positive combination of exponentials in t, so it is convex. Hence sup_{[a,b]} R_V = max{R_V(a), R_V(b)}. Also
> R_V ≤ R, and R(0) = (1 − π₀(S₀))/π₀(S₀), R(1) = (1 − π(S₀))/π(S₀).
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (candidate); this is O-STAGES Lemma 0 (LM216) in the notation $L_V=\log(1+R_V)$. Feeds: TH370, TH371.

### TH370 — API-T26BUD Theorem G (grid stage count): $N^{\rm pil}\le T\le N^{\rm pil}+\lceil\log_2(1/\eta_n)\rceil$  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §2; registry-index `T26BUD-G` ("PROVED, deterministic (Theorem G)", FLAG AUTHOR-ONLY); positions: [pos 906, 911, 975, 978]. (Not to be confused with O-STAGES Theorem G, TH364.) Statement (verbatim):
> **Statement.** Take any data, any successful pilot with temperatures 0 < φ₁ < … < φ_{N^pil} = 1, and any frozen V with
> S₀ ∈ V. Let `build_grid` succeed with T intervals. Then:
> (a) T = N^pil + k^bis, and every pilot temperature is a grid point;
> (b) if η := η_n > 0, then k^bis ≤ ⌈log₂(1/η)⌉ (and k^bis = 0 when η = 1, i.e. when R(0) ≤ ε₀ and R(2) ≤ ε₀);
> (c) hence N^pil ≤ T ≤ N^pil + ⌈log₂(1/η_n)⌉.
> This holds for every construction in the rebuild loop, in particular for the final grid, because the targets (the pilot
> temperatures of the tier) do not change across rebuilds.
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
- Remark (verbatim): "The condition actually used is L_V(u) + L_V(2v − u) ≤ log(1/0.9). The ε₀ form is a convenient sufficient condition. The script also records the exact one-step quantity: on V = Ω, the one-step grid {0, 1} passes iff χ²(π‖π₀) ≤ 1/9, since ρ_Ω(0, 1) = 1/(1 + χ²(π‖π₀))." Scripts' summary of realised counts: favourable designs (fav_iid, fav_cor, orth): "realised T_V counts {1: 20, 3: 6, 2: 7}; runs 33. Violations of Theorem G / Lemma P: 0." Masked designs: $T_V=3,6$ (n=160), $3,20$ (n=320), 15, 16, 26, 20, 23 for n=640..10240.
- Status: PROVED, deterministic (candidate; SF none; XF none; in the final card M2 status: "T26BUD-G: PROVED, deterministic, AUTHOR-ONLY"). Needs "an independent check of Theorem G's count argument (it is short, but it is the main new claim)" (REPORT §6). Depends on: LM220, LM221, LM222. Feeds: M7 Theorem STG (K26; "T26BUD-G: PROVED, deterministic (Theorem G)"), FUTURE_WORK FW6 (K31: Conjecture P).

- Source: `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §3. Statement (verbatim):

### TH373 — API-T26BUD Rule CAP and Corollary 2: with a cap $T_n^{\rm cap}\Delta_n\to_P0$, (P1) holds deterministically  [corollary]
- Source: `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §5. Statement (verbatim, rule, corollary and remark):
> **Rule CAP.** Replace "more than T_e intervals → the construction fails" by "more than min{T_e, T^cap_n} intervals → the
> construction fails". Here T^cap_n is any deterministic sequence with T^cap_n Δ_n →_P 0. Under Theorem B's hypotheses
> Δ_n = O_P(r_n), with r_n = 2^B√(log n)n^{−κ} + e_n + √(log n/n). So any T^cap_n = o(1/r_n) works, for example T^cap_n = ⌈C log n⌉.
> On ORTH (κ = ½, e_n = o(n^{−m})), any T^cap_n = o(√(n/log n)) works.
> **Corollary 2.** Under Rule CAP, T_n ≤ T^cap_n on 𝒢_n deterministically. So (P1) holds whenever T^cap_nΔ_n →_P 0, with no
> premise on the run. The cap enters Theorem A only through 𝒢_n. Theorem A never claims P(𝒪_n) → 1, so a cap that fires
> only lowers P(𝒪_n) and costs nothing in (A-i) and (A-ii).
> *Remark.* The existing rule already gives T_n ≤ T_e = 4^e max(1000, ℓ²) = O(log²n). This is the deterministic form used by
> W2-T26 Theorem B, so on ORTH (P1) is **already** a theorem asymptotically (conditional on Prop. C). The defect is
> quantitative: the constant 1000 makes (T_e + 1)Δ_n ≥ 44 at n = 163,840. Rule CAP with T^cap_n = ⌈log₂ n⌉ (= 8 at n = 200,
> = 18 at n = 163,840) removes that constant. Corollary 1 and Theorem 1 show that the cap does not bind when their hypotheses
> hold. Numerically it never binds (§ evidence: realised T ∈ {1, 2} in the favourable designs).
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROVED (candidate). It is a one-line method change (an interval cap), "inactive in the study" (REPORT confidence card); not adopted in v3.1 per the sources read (no K-number found). Depends on: TH296 (W2-T26 Theorem B). Feeds: none.

### TH374 — API-T26BUD Proposition O (ORTH: grid inputs $R(1+\eta)\to0$ for $\eta(1-\lambda^*)A<\tfrac12$; $T_n=1$ if $A(1-\lambda^*)<\tfrac12$)  [proposition]
- Source: `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §6. Statement (verbatim, family, claim, unverified steps, converse):
> **Family.** ORTH-F of W2-T26 Prop. C: XᵀX = (n−1)I_p, p ≤ min(n − 1, n^A), fixed s₀, fixed nonzero θ, Gaussian errors, and
> the method's blocks. Let R²₀ ∈ (0, 1) be the population fraction of var(y) explained by S₀. Let A_b be the share explained
> by the signals in block b, and λ_b = (1 − R²₀)/(1 − A_b) ∈ [1 − R²₀, 1]. Put λ* = min_b λ_b over blocks containing a null
> (λ* = 1 − R²₀ as soon as some block has no signal).
> **Claim.** For every fixed η ∈ (0, 1] with η(1 − λ*)A < ½,
>  R(1 + η) = O_P(n^{−1/2 + Aη(1−λ*)}·polylog n) → 0.
> Consequently, together with 1 − π₀(S₀) →_P 0 (Prop. C), η_n ≥ η_A := min{1, 1/(4A(1 − λ*))} w.p. → 1, and
> k^bis ≤ ⌈log₂(1/η_A)⌉ = O(1). If A(1 − λ*) < ½ (e.g. p fixed, or A·R²₀ < ½), then R(2) →_P 0, and **Theorem 1 gives
> T_n = 1 w.p. → 1 on ORTH-F**.
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
> **Unverified steps (why this is a SKETCH):** (1) uniform second-order control of the h-expansions when a_E is not small;
> (2) the T02-type truncation for q_{1+η} (T02 is proved for q₁); (3) the cross-terms between M and E; (4) the σ̂₀ plug-in.
> Each step looks routine, but none was checked line by line.
> **Converse (shows the A-dependence is real).** If A(1 − λ*) > ½, the single-extra sum at η = 1 is ≍ n^{−1/2}p^{1−λ*} → ∞.
> Then R(2) → ∞, the one-step grid fails, and k^bis ≥ 1 for large n. T_n still stays bounded by N^pil + ⌈log₂(1/η_A)⌉.
> The heuristic is the same as above (PROOF SKETCH).
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: PROOF SKETCH (author: "Each step looks routine, but none was checked line by line"); the missing steps are subsumed under ORTH with $p\log p=o(n)$ by TH362(d),(e) and TH363 (verified under H-ORTH; O-WSTAB did not cite T26BUD): TH362 gives the sharp thresholds $2Ar\lessgtr1$ in terms of $r=R^2_{\rm pop}$, and $1-\lambda^*\le R^2_0$ here, so Prop O's threshold $A(1-\lambda^*)<\tfrac12$ matches ($1-\lambda^*=R_0^2=r$ when some block is signal-free). Feeds: none.

### CJ268 — API-T26BUD Conjecture P: on ORTH-F the number of pilot stages is $N^{\rm pil}=O_P(1)$  [conjecture]
- Source: `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md` §7; REPORT headline and §5. Statement (verbatim):
> ## 7. Conjecture P (pilot count on ORTH). CONJECTURE
>
> On ORTH-F, N^pil = O_P(1). More precisely, N^pil ≤ 1 + ⌈log₂(1/η_A)⌉ w.p. → 1. Hence T_n = O_P(1).
> *What is proved:* the first pilot stage. Its particles are iid π₀. The proof of Theorem 1 at a general δ ≤ 1 gives
> ESS(δ)/H →_P 1 whenever R(2δ) →_P 0. So φ₁ ≥ min{1, (1 + η_A)/2} w.p. → 1 (the condition is used at t = 2δ ≤ 1 + η_A).
> *What is missing:* at later stages the particles are resampled and moved under an adaptive schedule, so their law is not
> q_φ. The locked occupancy result T15 is stated for frozen grids, and T12's unbiasedness also needs a frozen grid. A proof
> needs either an adaptive-schedule occupancy bound, or a high-probability bound D̄_n = O_P(log n) on the trimmed d-range of
> every pilot population (Lemma P then gives N^pil = O_P(log n), which is enough for (P1)). The second route needs the pilot
> particles to stay on supersets of S₀ with O(1) extras. This is plausible, because every move is γ_φ-reversible and
> models missing a signal have q_φ-mass e^{−Θ(n)} for all φ ∈ [0, 1], but it is not proved.
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/PROOF.md`)*
- Status: CONJECTURE (author; registry-index "Conjecture P (pilot stage count O_P(1)) CONJECTURED [IDX 268]"). Final fate: the as-coded masked stage count is FUTURE_WORK FW6/K31: "Conjecture P OPEN; V's complement is never inspected (I9(d)); only T ≤ T_e and the coverage identity are provable". Why it fails to follow from the rules (REPORT §5, verbatim):
> ## 5. What fails and why
>
> - **A bound of the form T_n ≤ C₁ + C₂ log(1/Δ_n) does not follow from the rules alone.** The pilot advances by a/D_k, and
>   D_k is the d-range of an arbitrary particle population. One particle on a model with d − d(S₀) of order n forces a step
>   of order 1/n. Excluding this needs occupancy control of the adaptive pilot, which is not available: T15 and T12 need a
>   frozen grid. Theorem 1 avoids this by using only the iid first stage. Conjecture P is where it stays open.
> - **The bisection count is controlled by the bridge past φ = 1, not by Δ_n.** Δ_n controls R only on [0, 1], while the
>   last step from u to 1 evaluates F_V at 2 − u > 1. So the right quantity is η_n, i.e. R(1+η), a Rényi-type moment of π
>   against π₀. It is not a function of Δ_n. On ORTH it is bounded below by a constant depending on A and R²₀ (Prop. O),
>   which gives O(1) bisections, better than log(1/Δ_n).
*(verbatim from `API-T26BUD/REPORT.md`)*
- Evidence (scripts `results/realised_T_summary.md`, favourable designs fav_iid, fav_cor, orth; masked): realised $T_V\in\{1,2,3\}$ on favourable designs, 15-26 on masked designs at n = 640-2560 (columns include $N^{\rm pil}$, bisect$_V$ max, $(T_V+1)\Delta_n$ and Theorem G / Lemma P check "0 violations"). Depends on: TH370, LM222. Feeds: FW6 (K31).

## Part H. The plug-in-σ² method note and the final fate of the draft track

### CJ273 — F-DRAFT method note: "building every block table with one shared plug-in σ² would make the draft's §5.3 literally true" (and unmask the start at n = 200)  [hypothesis]
- Source: `F-DRAFT/CROSSWALK.md` §6 and confidence card; positions: [pos 616 (reported to Felipe as "a possible method change"), 666 (O-DILUTE brief includes it), 937 (HQ rejects it)]. Statement (verbatim):
> ## 6. Outside scope: a method note for HQ (not pursued; investment rule)
>
> Lemma W1 says the entire BO discrepancy between the composite start and the posterior is the per-block integration of σ²
> against the full-y residual; with a common noise scale (known σ², or a single plug-in σ̂² from a preliminary fit used
> in *all* tables) the tables would give d ≡ 0 under BO and π₀ = π exactly, and in general d would be first order in the
> cross-block covariance, i.e. the draft's Theorem 1 would hold literally. Such tables are "arbitrary positive tables"
> in the sense of T22(i), so T09, T12, T13, T21, T22(i)(ii)(iv), T31 hold verbatim; only the EXP′-dependent statistical
> results (T22(iii), W1-EXP) would need redoing. W3-VEXP identified dilution (v ≈ 25σ²) as the reason the start misses
> 6–12 of the 14 truths at n = 200 at *every* signal scale. A plug-in-σ² table is therefore the one cheap method change
> that attacks the n = 200 masking at its cause. It changes the start only, it is not in the 2,400 fits, and whether it
> performs is a pilot question (investment rule). I flag it; I do not recommend acting on it inside this campaign.
*(verbatim from `F-DRAFT/CROSSWALK.md`)*
- Status history: F-DRAFT confidence card: "Method note §6 helps at n = 200 | plug-in-σ² tables unmask the start | 0.6 | pilot question | performance under false inclusions | yes". HQ [pos 616]: "I'd fold it into the same decision as LS0, after O-DILUTE reports on the dilution mechanism." Outcome: **rejected**: HQ at [pos 919]: "Common-σ² start: reject. Two agents independently found it floods the start in study-like designs. If you ever want a different start, a residualised-table variant looks promising in a pilot (378 of 480 cases favourable)." and [pos 937]: "The shared-σ² fix is out (it floods the start in random designs)." The two agents are F-SIGMA (Fable) and O-MIX (Opus); their theorems belong to theme 3: ⟦F-SIGMA⟧, ⟦O-MIX⟧, ⟦O-DILUTE⟧.
- Feeds: none (campaign-only; rejected). Note that TH350's "with known σ² the same tables give $d\equiv0$, $\pi_0=\pi$" (and M2(a3) "with known σ² (tables recomputed under known precision) d ≡ 0") remains the true half of this idea.

### Dead ends and corrections (Theme 10)

- **The draft's §5.3 mechanism is wrong for v3's tables** (RF256, CE199): weak cross-block covariance does not control the importance-weight variance; the whole BO discrepancy is the per-block integration of σ² against the full response ("dilution", $d=d_\sigma\ge0$, TH350), and the χ² can diverge at zero cross-block correlation (TH356). First flagged by F-DRAFT [pos 616], proved by O-WSTAB [pos 748]. Lesson: KL and TV vanish (TH362(f)) while χ² need not (CE203 shows the abstract separation).
- **F-DRAFT Theorem W(c) and W(b) false on the divergent side** (RF252, RF253, CE197): the multi-extra layers sum like $\exp(\Theta(k^*))$, not a geometric series, once $q^{(2)}>1$. The threshold $2Ar\lessgtr1$ is right. The correct statement is TH362(e),(g): $c\,e^{L_n/r}\le\log(1+\chi^2)\le C\,e^{L_n/r}(\log p)^{5(1+r)/(2r)}$. Found by O-WSTAB [pos 748]; confirmed numerically in two independent implementations (8 770 vs 7 961 nats at $n=10^{16}$, A = 0.95).
- **F-DRAFT Lemma W2 "exact" identity false** (RF254, CE198): ordinary RSS partial $R^2$ is not the v3 score fraction; the ridge-adjusted $Q$ and the $2b_0$ offset matter (0.3104 vs 0.3538 at n = 20, p = 4). Repairs: LM212 (O-WSTAB, inequality form), TH378 (A-REV6, Astra-authored, pending Claude). ### 0. Setting, families, notation and imported inputs (not IDs)

Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §0 (verbatim below). Family definitions are copied from there.

> **Score, start, posterior.** F(S) = log ϖ(S) + log m(S) on Ω = {S : |S| ≤ K}, K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋); π ∝ e^F; the composite start π₀ ∝ ϖ ∏_b r_b(S ∩ C_b) on the v3 partition (00_COMMON §1). Budgets (00_COMMON): ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉, L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉), N₀ = max(2500, n, p), Q_f = 4N_e(T+L+5) with 4N_e(L+6) ≤ Q_f ≤ 4N_e(T_e+L+5). Population residual Δ(T) := ‖(I − P_T)μ‖²/(n−1) (μ = Xθ*, columns centred and standardised).
>
> **LH** (exact Gram) = the family of [T38] Cor. b1-LH: X′X = (n−1)Σ_LH, p ≤ n−1, groups of size g with equicorrelation ρ_h ∈ [ρ₋, ρ₊] ⊂ (0,1), c ≥ 1 linked pairs (a_i, b_i, ψ_i) with 0 < |ψ_i| < min(ρ_{a_i}, ρ_{b_i}), fixed nonzero coefficients θ_{a_i} = β_i, θ_{b_i} = −ψ_iβ_i, v ≥ 0 visible hubs, g ≤ B_n < 2g eventually, s₀ = 2c + v fixed, p ≤ n^A. Masked set M = {b_1, …, b_c}, reference S° = S₀ ∖ M.
>
> **LH-iid** = [PXN] §0: rows iid N(0, Σ_LH), 9 ≤ g ≤ 16, n^a ≤ p ≤ n^A (p ≫ n allowed).
>
> **Cancellation depth** := c = |M|, the number of masked hubs (the task's "c"). It equals the masking exponent of T27: π₀(S₀) = p^{−c}n^{−c/2}e^{O_P(1)}.

Notation: $Q^\star_n:=p^c n^{c/2}$; $M_{stat}:=\log\pi_0(S_0)+c\log p+(c/2)\log n$. EX-A (exact iid $\pi_0$ draws) is assumed throughout, as in every T38 route.

𝔐_IS(Q): one-shot importance correction: from the same Q draws, estimate π-expectations by weights w = γ/γ₀ (oracle-normalised w̄ = π/π₀, or self-normalised). 𝔐_LS(Q): 𝔐_iid(Q), plus the production local search (M §6.10) from each draw and from S̃₀ (LS0). v3: the method (with or without LS0)."

**The task spec W7-SEP (the claim to prove)**, `campaign/tasks/W7-SEP.md` (written [pos 711]):

> **Claim to prove.** On an explicit masked family (LH / LH-iid: branches `theory/W1-EXP`, `theory/W3-VEXP`, `theory/W3-PXN`; masking per CL(L), W1-EXP Thm 3/4), with cancellation depth c ≥ 2:
> - (a) **Start-only methods fail.** Q iid draws from π₀ followed by the production local search from each draw (and from the start mode S̃₀, i.e. LS0 alone without the bridge) score S₀ with probability → 0 for every polynomial budget Q = n^A — unless the greedy basin of S₀ contains S̃₀ (quantify exactly when LS0 alone suffices, using Theorem A/TD′ from `theory/W1-T37R` + `theory/W3-VT37R`). Use R-T20(i) in `Docs/Theory/DROPPED.md` (iid discovery fails for c ≥ 3 under the n^{−c/2} law) and W1-T38E's iid-miss numbers.
> - (b) **One-shot importance correction fails.** Importance weights π/π₀ from the start have χ² → ∞ (F-DRAFT Theorem W, branch `theory/F-DRAFT`; O-WSTAB in progress on `theory/O-WSTAB`), so the one-shot corrected estimator of 1{S = S₀} has relative variance → ∞ for p ≫ n.
> - (c) **v3 succeeds.** Cite T38(b) with LS0 (`theory/W4-T38FULL`, `theory/W3-PXN`) and, if available, the no-tweak routes (`theory/W4-SHARE`, `theory/O-BGIBBS`, `theory/W5-B2ENV`).
>
> Write (a)–(c) as one **Separation Theorem** with all hypotheses named, prove (a) and (b) in full (they are the new content), and state (c) as a citation with its premises. Give the budget exponents explicitly: the polynomial budget that v3 needs versus the super-polynomial budget that start-only discovery needs. Verify (a) numerically at small p on the LH family.

HQ's announcement of the task [pos 717]: "A **separation theorem**: on the masked family, start-only discovery (iid draws + local search) needs a super-polynomial budget, one-shot importance correction has infinite relative variance, and v3 succeeds with a polynomial budget. It's the paper's conceptual spine: proof that the bridge is *needed*, not just that it works."

### TH380 — SEP(A); SEP-A  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §1 (Theorem SEP (A)), §2 (proof); `W7-SEP/REPORT.md` §2; positions: [pos 717], [pos 763], [pos 796]; XF: `A-REV9/REVIEW.md` ("Separation, partition and stage counts"), reviewed [pos 843 launch], [pos 915 fetch], [pos 925].
- Statement (verbatim, PROOF.md §1):
  > **Theorem SEP.** Let (X, y) follow LH (exact Gram) with c ≥ 1 fixed, or LH-iid (parts (A), (B) only, through I7). Put Q*_n := p^c n^{c/2}.
  >
  > **(A) Start sampling cannot discover the truth below Q\*.** For every deterministic budget sequence Q_n,
  >
  >   P₀(S₀ is scored by 𝔐_iid(Q_n)) → 0 if Q_n/Q*_n → 0, and → 1 if Q_n/Q*_n → ∞.
  >
  > In particular, if p ≍ n^a, a polynomial budget Q_n = n^α fails when α < c(a + ½) and succeeds when α > c(a + ½). **PROVED** (LH exact Gram, from I2, I4; LH-iid from I7, which is unverified).
- Hypotheses: EX-A; LH; ⟦W1-EXP Thm 5(b)⟧, LM115 (W1-EXP Lemma 4.2).
- Earlier versions / repairs: the task-spec version (a) was "score S₀ w.p. → 0 for every polynomial budget"; see RF263. The meeting's final card restricts the claim to the specified iid start-only comparison (see "SEP vs M6" below).
- Status history: proposed as task clause (a) [pos 711/717] -> PROVED (candidate), author W7-SEP, no SF verification (registry: "PROVED (SF: none)") -> XF: A-REV9 "VERIFIED as implications from its imported tight start-mass and posterior-concentration premises" -> carried into M6 (K19) with status "PROVED; SF none; XF VERIFIED (A-REV9)".
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEP (proof §2: exact conditional miss probability $(1-\pi_0(S_0))^Q$; tables excluded on $\{$blocks = groups$\}$; bounded convergence with $M_{stat}=O_P(1)$ on both sides). A-REV9 (Astra): "SEP(A): conditional miss probability is (1-pi0(S0))^Q. With pi0(S0)=Qstar^-1 exp(O_P(1)), Q/Qstar tending to zero or infinity yields the two sides by bounded convergence; table discovery must be excluded by the imported partition event."
- Depends on: ⟦W1-EXP Thm 5(b)⟧ (I2), LM115 (W1-EXP Lemma 4.2) (I4).
- Feeds: M6 Theorem SEP + Lemma KL (K19; also cited as the lower bound used by M2); Lean: `T11Miss.lean` (`t11_miss_iid`) proves the iid-miss inequality but no source maps K19/SEP-A to it (REGISTRY_PAPER1 M6 "Lean" note).
- Notes: PROOF §2 Remark 2: R-T20(i) (DROPPED.md) is the fixed-$p$ special case: $Q^\star=\Theta(n^{c/2})$, a budget $Q\asymp n\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n$ succeeds for $c\le2$ and fails for $c\ge3$; with $p\to\infty$ the factor $p^c$ makes $c=2$ already fail against $v3$'s own $Q_f$ (since $Q_f\pi_0(S_0)=O_P((n+p)\log^2n\cdot p^{-2}n^{-1})\to0$). Remark 3: the same proof applies to any scheme that only reweights and resamples iid $\pi_0$ draws (I10(c)).

### TH382 — SEP(B); SEP-B  [theorem]
- Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §1 (B), §3; REPORT.md §2; XF `A-REV9/REVIEW.md`.
- Statement (verbatim):
  > **(B) One-shot importance correction fails below Q\*.** On LH (or LH-iid):
  > - (B1) 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≥ π(S₀)²/π₀(S₀) = Q*_n e^{−Mstat}(1 + o_P(1)) → ∞, and KL(π‖π₀) ≥ (c log p + (c/2) log n)(1 − o_P(1)) − O_P(1).
  > - (B2) The unbiased one-shot estimator Î_Q := Q⁻¹ Σ_{i≤Q} w̄(X_i) 1{X_i = S₀} of π(S₀) (oracle normalisation) has relative variance Var(Î_Q | data)/π(S₀)² = (1/π₀(S₀) − 1)/Q = (Q*_n/Q)e^{−Mstat}(1 + o_P(1)).
  > - (B3) If Q_n/Q*_n → 0, then Î_Q = 0 and the self-normalised estimator Ĩ_Q = 0 with probability → 1, while π(S₀) → 1: the absolute error tends to 1 in probability, not only the variance to ∞.
  >
  > **PROVED** (given I2, I3; LH-iid via I7).
- Status history: author W7-SEP "PROVED"; SF none; XF A-REV9 "SEP(B1–B3) VERIFIED as implications from imported premises" (A-REV9: "chi-square >= pi(S0)^2/pi0(S0)-1, KL >= pi(S0)log(1/pi0(S0))-log 2, and the iid truth-indicator relative variance is (1/pi0(S0)-1)/Q. On no truth draw, both normalized and unnormalized estimates vanish. These are VERIFIED conditional implications; they do not independently discharge the LH statistical premises or prove a PIP statement."). ### TH384 — SEP(C); SEP-C (start + one greedy search succeeds on LH)  [theorem]
- Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §1 (C), §4; REPORT.md §2; positions [pos 763], [pos 796].

  > **(C) Start + local search is NOT separated from v3 (negative part; replaces the task's (a) for search methods).** On LH (exact Gram), w.p. → 1 the production local search scores *and certifies* S₀ from every centre C ⊆ R, where R is the union of the non-null groups (Proposition GU, §4). ### TH386 — SEP(E); SEP-E (budget exponents)  [theorem]
- Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §1 (E); REPORT.md §2 (E).
- Statement (verbatim, PROOF.md):
  > **(E) Budget exponents.** With p ≍ n^a (0 < a < 1 on exact-Gram LH; a ≥ 1 allowed on LH-iid):
  >
  > | Method | Score evaluations needed to score S₀ w.p. → 1 | Exponent of n | Status |
  > |---|---|---|---|
  > | 𝔐_iid, 𝔐_IS | ≍ Q* = p^c n^{c/2} (sharp, two-sided) | c(a + ½) | PROVED |
  > | 𝔐_LS(1) (draw + local search), LS0 | ≤ (ℓ+1)(p + K(p−K)) | ≤ 2a (+ log) | PROVED (Prop. GU) |
  > | v3 with LS0 (T38(b1-LH)) | ≤ T32 ceiling + LS0 term = O((n+p)(p+B) log² n + p² log² n) | ≤ a + max(1, a) (+ log) | PROVED-UNDER I11 (CONJECTURE) |
  >
  > The iid exponent exceeds v3's ceiling exponent iff c(a+½) > a + max(1,a); for every a > 0 this holds **iff c ≥ 2**. It exceeds the 𝔐_LS / LS0 exponent iff c(a+½) > 2a, i.e. always for c ≥ 2, and for c = 1 only when a < ½. **No super-polynomial gap exists in R1:** c ≤ s₀ is fixed, so Q* is polynomial. A super-polynomial gap needs c = c_n → ∞, which is outside the frozen setting (s₀ fixed) and outside every proved v3 route.

### TH387 — Proposition BASIN; SEP-BASIN  [proposition]
- Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §4.1; REPORT.md §2.
- Statement (verbatim, PROOF.md §4.1):
  > Fix the data and the tie rule. Let M(C) be the production best-move map (the best strict improvement among feasible flips and swaps of C, or ⊥), and N̄(S₀) := {S₀} ∪ {feasible flip and swap neighbours of S₀}. The search from C visits C₀ = C, C_{t+1} = M(C_t) while M(C_t) ≠ ⊥ and t < ℓ, and scans each visited centre (including the last one, M §6.10). Define the **scoring basin**
  >
  >   𝔅_ℓ := {C ∈ Ω : some visited centre C_t lies in N̄(S₀)}.
  >
  > Then: (i) the search from C scores S₀ iff C ∈ 𝔅_ℓ (with the centre emitted); (ii) LS0 scores S₀ iff S̃₀ ∈ 𝔅_ℓ; (iii) 𝔐_LS(Q) scores S₀ with probability, given the data, 1{S̃₀ ∈ 𝔅_ℓ} ∨ [1 − (1 − π₀(𝔅_ℓ))^Q].
- REPORT.md summary: "This is the exact answer to 'when does LS0 alone suffice'; GU, Lemma LS-score and Theorem A are sufficient conditions for membership."
- Status: PROVED (deterministic) (author); SF none; XF none. Proof: a scan from centre $C_t$ scores exactly the feasible neighbours of $C_t$ (Summary).
- Depends on: LM189 (Lemma LS-score), TH199 (Theorem A) (sufficient conditions listed in PROOF 4.1: lattice $D_S$ events with $\ell\ge\Phi(C)-1$; $TD'_\infty(\mathcal R)\ni C$ uncapped; $TD'_P(R_{a,d})\ni C$ with $\ell\ge a+d$).
- Feeds: none (campaign-only). Positions: [pos 763].
- Notes: the scan-the-last-centre and "centre emitted" conventions are exactly the `emit_centre` issue of CJ128 (GUARD)/⟦LS0⟧ (theme 7).

### TH388 — Proposition GU (greedy universality); SEP-GU  [proposition]
- Source (authoritative): `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §4.2; REPORT.md §1 item 2, §2; positions [pos 763] (item 7: "it proved a 'greedy universality' proposition instead"), [pos 796], XF [pos 807 launch, 919 result].
- Statement (verbatim, PROOF.md §4.2):
  > **Hypotheses.**
  > - (G) Gaussian errors, fixed design, σ² fixed; columns centred and standardised.
  > - (XG) Exact Gram: X′X = (n−1)Σ, so Δ(T) is the population residual variance.
  > - (REL) There is R ⊇ S₀ with |R| ≤ r (r fixed) and Σ_{R, Rᶜ} = 0.
  > - (SE) λ_min(Σ_R) ≥ φ₀² > 0.
  > - (BM) θ₀ := min_{j∈S₀}|θ*_j| > 0 and θ*′Σθ* ≤ M, both fixed.
  > - (R-lite) p ≤ n^A, and p ≥ r + 1 (at least one variable outside R; if p = r the proof is the same with K ≥ r).
  >
  > **Proposition GU.** Under these hypotheses there is an event U_n with P₀(U_n) → 1 on which, for all n ≥ n₁ with ℓ_n ≥ τ_GU and K ≥ r + 1, the production local search started at **any** C ⊆ R reaches S₀ by strictly improving moves, scores it, and stops there with `local_certified`, after at most
  >
  >   τ_GU := 1 + ⌈(2s₀/φ₀²) log(M/(φ₀²θ₀²))⌉ + (r − s₀)
  >
  > moves. Since ℓ_n = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉ → ∞ and K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋), the side conditions hold for all large n. **Status: PROVED** (candidate; uses I5).
- Proof route (Summary:): $U_n=E_n\cap V_n$ with $E_n$ Lemma M's event ($k=r+1$) and $V_n=\{\max_{T\in\mathfrak F,l\notin T}W_{T,l}\le 2\log(2^rp)+\tfrac14\log n\}$, $P(V_n^c)\le n^{-1/8}$. Phase 1 ($\Delta>0$): each greedy step lowers $\Delta$ by a factor $(1-\phi_0^2/(2s_0))$ because the best truth addition reduces $\Delta$ by $\ge(\phi_0^2/s_0)\Delta$ (LM224) and Lemma M makes the greedy choice $\Delta$-optimal up to $m_n\to0$; nulls never enter. Phase 2 (supersets $S_0\cup E$ inside $R$): every deletion of an extra gains $\ge\tfrac14\log n$ and additions/swaps lose (LM225), so the search deletes the extras one by one and stops at $S_0$.
- Remarks (verbatim, PROOF §4.2): "1. **No PGD needed.** Prop. GU does not assume that greedy moves are progress moves (PGD fails under SE + BM-∞, [T37R] C3). It uses only the population descent of Δ (GU-1), which holds for every T ⊆ R under SE. Greedy may take look-alikes first; it never gets trapped, because every state with Δ > 0 has a Θ(1) Δ-reduction available and every superset with an extra has a Θ(log n) deletion gain. This proves a version of [T37R] Conjecture C4 in the exact-Gram, isolated-relevant-set case: TD′_∞ on all of 2^R (C4's region also allows null extras; not covered). 2. **Where the isolation (REL) is used.** Only to keep nulls out of the path (phase 1) and to make phase 2 a union over a fixed finite family 𝔉. ... 3. **Centres with nulls.** For a centre containing data-chosen nulls, phase 2 needs the deletion gain of each such null uniformly over data-chosen sets, which is the NA/LD issue of [T37R] C1. Not covered (OPEN)."
- Status history: proposed/proved by W7-SEP (single run) -> "needs cross-family check" (REPORT §6 item 1: especially GU-1(b), the determinant bound in GU-2 and the use of Lemma M with data-chosen pairs) -> **A-REV7**: "VERIFIED as a greedy-search theorem; GAP as a standalone no-LS0 growing-p theorem: the actual HPM search centre need not lie in its isolated finite relevant set." (A-REV7 §6: "**GU:** the Schur-complement lower bound and l1/l2 argument give best truth-addition reduction at least (lambda_min/s0)Delta. The score comparison then makes each greedy underfit move reduce Delta by a fixed factor, and isolates the path inside R. On supersets, the chi-square union over 2^r p directions makes additions unfavourable; deleting an extra beats swapping that extra for a new variable. The source report's casual phrase 'every swap loses' is stronger than needed: the proof correctly compares an extra swap to its corresponding deletion. This establishes the stated move bound and eventual certification under its hypotheses. It is a greedy best-neighbour argument, not a random Gibbs-round argument. For growing p the actual best-scored centre may include nulls outside R. Showing its eligibility, or adding a search from S° (LS0), is still necessary to use GU alone. For fixed p take R=[p], and remember that production eventually enumerates.") -> **A-REV9**: "GAP in this review: descent and superset argument checked, imported uniform score-comparison Lemma M not independently audited here" (A-REV8 VERIFIED Lemma M). Registry conflict C25: "Not a mathematical disagreement; recorded V* with both texts." Registry cell: "VERIFIED* — A-REV7 ...; A-REV9 ...: GAP in that review".
- Proved by / checked by: W7-SEP (Opus-class cloud run); XF Astra (A-REV7 VERIFIED*; A-REV9 GAP, scope only); Lemma M is XF-VERIFIED by A-REV8 and SF-VERIFIED by W5-VMASK.
- Depends on: LM224, LM225, LM190 (Lemma M) (I5), ⟦W1-T37R Conjecture C4⟧, ⟦W1-EXP Lemma 4.1(a)⟧ (I6).
- Feeds: none in the final list (campaign-only). T38 v3 Remark 6 and E-SPINE cite it; W8-SYNTH §3 lists it: "Prop. GU ... PROVED, candidate ... needs a start already inside the relevant set". HQ at [pos 919]: "Refuted: ... Prop GU as a standalone no-LS0 route" (wording stronger than A-REV7's GAP; see CJ278).
- Notes: this is the result that "changes the story" (REPORT §6.1): it is the basis of RF262, RF264, CE207.

- Statement (verbatim): "**Corollary GU-LH.** On LH (exact Gram) the hypotheses hold with R = the union of the 2c + v non-null groups (r = (2c+v)g), φ₀² = (1 − max|ψ_i|)(1 − ρ₊) (I6), θ₀ = min(|β_i|, |ψ_iβ_i|, |θ_h|), M = θ*′Σθ*. ### TH393 — NM-R (A-REV6 four-state replacement of F-DRAFT NM)  [proposition]
- Source: `A-REV6/WEIGHTS.md` §NM-R; `A-REV6/REVIEW.md` ("F-DRAFT Prop NM | ERROR | A-REV6 candidate NM-R | GAP pending Claude | Four-state normalizer solved; O_P(sqrt n) fluctuation retained; not production SMC at p=2."); positions: A-REV6 launched [pos 807], reported [pos 919].
- Statement (verbatim, A-REV6 WEIGHTS.md): 
  > **Astra-authored candidate; GAP for adoption pending Claude verification.** Let p=2, K=2, singleton blocks {j},{l}, deterministic centered columns with norms sqrt(n-1) and fixed correlation r satisfying 0<|r|<1. Let Y=theta x_j+epsilon with fixed theta!=0 and sigma>0 and isotropic Gaussian contrast noise. Use v3 preprocessing, exact scores and the capped BB(1,p) prior. Put
  >
  >     c_l = (1/2)log[(sigma²+theta²)/(sigma²+theta²(1-r²))] > 0.
  >
  > Then local singleton inclusion probabilities tend to one, the naive union is {j,l} with probability tending to one, pi0({j,l})->1, pi({j})->1, and
  >
  >     log pi0({j})=-n c_l+O_P(sqrt(n)+log n),
  >     TV(pi,pi0)->1,
  >     liminf (1/n)log[1+chi²(pi||pi0)] >= c_l
  >
  > where the last liminf is in probability (equivalently every smaller constant is an eventual probability-tending-to-one lower bound). This p=2 construction falls on the production exact-enumeration branch. It is a counterexample for naive union and abstract start-based schemes, not a production-SMC execution failure. A polynomial number of iid start draws misses {j} with probability tending to one. An independence-MH chain initialised from pi0 likewise fails to visit {j} in polynomially many proposals with probability tending to one.
- Proof route (Summary:): direct singleton scores $n^{-1}\log BF(\{l\})\to c_l$, $n^{-1}\log BF(\{j\})\to\tfrac12\log[(\sigma^2+\theta^2)/\sigma^2]>0$; the four start weights $w(0),w(1)BF(j),w(1)BF(l),w(2)BF(j)BF(l)$ give $\pi_0(j,l)\to1$ by dividing by the last weight; posterior: compare all three alternatives directly with $\{j\}$ (empty model exponentially small; proxy-only ratio $-(n/2)\log[1+\theta^2(1-r^2)/\sigma^2]+O_P(\sqrt n+\log n)$; pair-to-truth ratio $n^{-1/2}\exp[O_P(1)]$ times the fixed prior ratio). Independence-MH: "visiting truth requires either initial truth or a truth proposal, so the bound is $(Q+1)\pi_0(j)$. This proves the stated initial-law result without claiming failure from every initial state." Gibbs repair: "For a terminal Gibbs label l, **conditional on the actual pre-label state being {j,l}**, the flip scores {j} and deletes l with probability 1/(1+pi({j,l})/pi({j}))->1. This is a label-time statement. It does not infer that occupancy from the round-start mode. No O(1) ideal-grid stage count is claimed."
- Status history: Astra-authored (A-REV6) -> "GAP pending Claude" (A-REV6 table); no Claude verification recorded in the sources I read (registry row `REV6-cands(A6)`: "Astra-authored; pending Claude verification"). Original A-REV4 ERROR verdict on F-DRAFT NM preserved (RF265).

### LM224 — Lemma GU-1 (population descent); SEP-GU1  [lemma]
- Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §4.2.
- Statement (verbatim): "**Lemma GU-1 (population descent).** Under (SE) and (BM), for every T ⊆ R with Δ(T) > 0, writing M_T := S₀ ∖ T: (a) Δ(T) ≥ φ₀²‖θ*_{M_T}‖₂² ≥ φ₀²θ₀², and Δ(T) = 0 iff T ⊇ S₀; (b) red*(T) := max_{j∈M_T}[Δ(T) − Δ(T + j)] ≥ Δ(T)²/‖θ*_{M_T}‖₁² ≥ (φ₀²/s₀)Δ(T) ≥ φ₀⁴θ₀²/s₀. Moreover for every T ⊆ [p], Δ(T) = Δ(T ∩ R)."
- Proof route (Summary:): (a) Schur complement of $\Sigma_T$ in $\Sigma_{T\cup M_T}$ and interlacing; (b) $\|\tilde\mu\|^2\le\|\theta_{M_T}\|_1\max_j|\langle\tilde x_j,\tilde\mu\rangle|$ and $\|\tilde x_j\|^2\le1$, then Cauchy–Schwarz; last claim from (REL) and (XG). The source notes: "(Lemma GU-1(b) is a sharpened form of [SH] Prop. M(a) and of [T37R] Lemma 3.)"
- Status: PROVED (candidate), SF none; XF: contained in A-REV7's GU verdict (the Schur-complement lower bound and $\ell_1/\ell_2$ argument checked) and A-REV9 ("descent and superset argument checked").
- Depends on: TH253 (SHARE-M(a)) (TH253 (W4-SHARE Prop M(a))), ⟦W1-T37R Lemma 3⟧.
- Feeds: TH388.

### LM225 — Lemma GU-2 (one addition at a superset); SEP-GU2  [lemma]
- Source: `W7-SEP/PROOF.md` §4.2.
- Statement (verbatim): "**Lemma GU-2 (one addition at a superset).** Let 𝔉 := {S₀ ∪ E : E ⊆ R ∖ S₀}. Define for T ∈ 𝔉 and l ∉ T W_{T,l} := ⟨r_l, ε⟩²/(σ²‖r_l‖²), r_l := (I − P_T)x_l. Then W_{T,l} ~ χ²₁ for each fixed (T, l), and on Lemma M's event E_n (I5) with k = r + 1, for n ≥ n₀,
  F(T + l) − F(T) ≤ −½ log(n − 1) + log(1/φ₀) + log((r+1)/p) + ½ W_{T,l}(1 + η_n) + c₀,   (4.1)
  with η_n = O(n^{−1/3}) and c₀ = c₀(M, σ², φ₀) of Lemma M."
- Proof route (Summary:): three factors: prior ratio $w(t+1)/w(t)\le(r+1)/p$; determinant $D_{T+l}/D_T\ge(n-1)\phi_0^2$ by Schur complements; fit $RSS_T-RSS_{T+l}=\sigma^2W_{T,l}$ with Lemma M's $Q$-versus-RSS bounds.
- Status: PROVED (candidate); registry label `SEP-GU2` "Every deletion of an extra gains ≥ ¼ log n; every addition or swap loses" (A-REV7: the "every swap loses" phrase is stronger than needed; an extra swap is compared with its deletion).
- Depends on: LM190 (Lemma M) (I5).
- Feeds: TH388.

### RF262 — task clause (a): start-only methods with local search fail  [refuted claim]
- Source: false claim in `campaign/tasks/W7-SEP.md` (quoted above): "(a) **Start-only methods fail.** Q iid draws from π₀ followed by the production local search from each draw (and from the start mode S̃₀, i.e. LS0 alone without the bridge) score S₀ with probability → 0 for every polynomial budget Q = n^A — unless the greedy basin of S₀ contains S̃₀".
- Refutation (W7-SEP REPORT §1 item 1, verbatim): "**The task's claim (a), as written, is false on its own family.** Its iid-only part is true (item 3), but on LH 'start-only + production local search' does **not** fail: S̃₀ = S° and the search from it scores S₀ with probability → 1 (this is already T38(b1-LH)). The task's exception ('unless the greedy basin of S₀ contains S̃₀') is the generic case, not an exception. **COUNTEREXAMPLE** (by proof, Corollary GU-LH; and numerically in 100% of replicates)." W7-SEP early finding (NOTES.md): "On LH (exact Gram) and LH-iid this exception is exactly what happens: S~0 = S° w.p. -> 1 and LS from S° scores S0 in c moves (T38(b1-LH), W3-PXN P5-P6). So (a) with local search is FALSE on the task's own family."
- Replacement: TH384 (SEP(C)), TH388/TH389, CE207; the iid-only part survives as TH380. Registry row `SEP-taska` (COUNTEREXAMPLE; SF none; XF none).
- Who found it: W7-SEP (the assigned agent, against its own task). HQ reaction [pos 763] item 7: "the separation claim as I posed it is false on LH (start-only plus local search *does* reach S₀ there); it proved a 'greedy universality' proposition instead." W8-SYNTH §4.10 "Agents versus their own task specs": "the task's claim that start-only methods fail is false on LH (Prop. GU)".
- Final card: M6 "Scope boundary: ... SEP-taska remains a COUNTEREXAMPLE."

- Source (false/over-claimed statement), `F-DRAFT/NEW_TARGETS.md` §NM (verbatim):
  <!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.996) from `A-REV4/snapshots/F-DRAFT_NEW_TARGETS.md`; that file is authoritative -->
  > **Proposition NM.** Assume G with σ² > 0. Let the partition separate j and ℓ (b(j) ≠ b(ℓ)). Write BF_b for the block-b table law π_b(U) ∝ w(|U|)r_b(U) on U ⊆ C_b (the draft's local posterior). As n → ∞ with p ≤ n^A, with P₀-probability → 1:
  >
  > (i) [local analyses] π_{b(j)}(j ∈ U) → 1 and π_{b(ℓ)}(ℓ ∈ U) → 1; precisely log r_{b(ℓ)}({ℓ}) = (n/2) log[1/(1 − r²θ²/(σ²+θ²))] − ½ log n + O_P(1) → +∞ linearly in n. Hence the naive union Ŝ_∪ = {j, ℓ}.
  >
  > (ii) [the composite start inherits it] By T22(ii-a) exactly, π₀({j,ℓ})/π₀({j}) = [w(2)/w(1)]·r_{b(ℓ)}({ℓ}) = (2/(2p−2))·r_{b(ℓ)}({ℓ}) → ∞; so π₀({j}) → 0 and π₀(j, ℓ ∈ S) → 1 (double counting).
  >
  > (iii) [the posterior does not] π({j,ℓ})/π({j}) = (2/(2p−2))·(n+1)^{−1/2}e^{Z²/2 + O_P(1)} → 0, where Z is the standardised residual correlation of x_ℓ on x_j with ε (δ_{{j},ℓ} = 0 since (I − P_j)μ = 0), and π({ℓ})/π({j}) = exp{−(n/2) log(1 + θ²(1 − r²)/σ²)(1 + o_P(1))} → 0 (the look-alike margin; linearised it is T37's (n−1)θ²(1−r²)/(2σ²)). With T03 (or directly) π({j}) → 1, PIP_ℓ → 0.
  >
  > (iv) [uncertainty distortion] |π_{b(ℓ)}(ℓ ∈ U) − PIP_ℓ| → 1; |π₀(j,ℓ ∈ S) − π(j,ℓ ∈ S)| → 1; TV(π, π₀) → 1; 1 + χ²(π‖π₀) ≥ π({j})²/π₀({j}) = exp{(n/2) log[1/(1 − r²θ²/(σ²+θ²))] (1 + o_P(1))}, so by Prop W0 one-shot importance correction, independence-MH from π₀ and iid discovery from π₀ all fail at every polynomial budget.

P1; a₁ ≥ 0.14 at n = 200 in the p = 20 designs), and by W″ the ideal grid crosses from {j,ℓ} to {j} in O(1) stages.
  >
  > *Proof.* (i) r_{b(ℓ)}({ℓ}) = BF({ℓ}) = (n+1)^{−1/2}(1 + O(1/n))·(1 − x_{∅,ℓ})^{−ν}, x_{∅,ℓ} = r_{ℓy}² → r²θ²/(σ²+θ²) > 0; ... **Status: PROVED** modulo the cited candidates; a fully self-contained finite-n version is available because every quantity is a closed form in (r_{jy}, r_{ℓy}, r, n, p). Check: proxy-split runs give argmax π₀ = {1,7}, argmax π = {1}, π₀({1}) = 1.7·10⁻⁴¹ (n = 200) and 1.0·10⁻¹⁴⁶ (n = 800), π({1}) = 0.86 and 0.95, TV = 0.985 and 0.996, 1 + χ² = 4.9·10⁴⁰, T_ideal = 14 and 16.
  
  F-DRAFT's own status for it: "PROVED modulo T03/EXP′/Cor. P1" (summary table), CROSSWALK confidence "0.97", role "Prop 0: ... the paper's thesis 'easy merge, hard uncertainty' in one proposition".
- Refutation (A-REV4, `A-REV4/REVIEW.md` verdict table "F-DRAFT NM | ERROR", verbatim): "**NM ERROR and scope GAP.** Even the identifiable fixed-p two-column Gaussian family, b=sigma=1 and proxy correlation r=1/2, contradicts the stated O_P(1) remainder around the population linear rate. In orthonormal contrast coordinates the signal coordinate is sqrt(n-1)+E1, the proxy coordinate combines it with an independent E2, and the remaining noise energy is chi²(n-3). The empirical explained fraction has nondegenerate n^-1/2 fluctuations. The derivative of log(1/(1-x)) at x=r²/(1+1)=1/8 is nonzero. The delta method therefore gives a nondegenerate sqrt(n) fluctuation of log BF about n log(8/7)/2, not a tight remainder after adding log(n)/2. Repair to O_P(sqrt n), or simply n^-1 log BF->log(8/7)/2. The exponential local proxy-inclusion phenomenon survives this repair." and (REVIEW.md): "The odds pi0({j,l})/pi0({j})->infinity prove only pi0({j})->0. They do not control all other states, identify the exact start mode or show that the complete naive union contains exactly this pair for arbitrary remaining columns. Specify the sets covered by SE, control all normalisers, and retain actual label-time occupancy in the Gibbs repair claim. An iid-discovery obstruction from exponentially small start truth mass is valid. A worst-case independence-MH bound is not failure for every starting state: starting at truth is a counterexample to that interpretation. The O(1) discrete ideal-grid assertion is not proved by a thermodynamic-length heuristic. A safe repair is the explicit fixed-p two-column family with a direct four-state comparison (as in A-DRAFT §3); this is a component construction, since production enumerates at p=2." Detailed in `A-REV4/DRAFTS_CHECK.md` "F-DRAFT NM: ERROR/GAP as a general proposition; valid fixed-p repair" (4 points: remainder false; odds do not control normalisation or the mode; (iii) and TV separation survive with the p=2 repair, "State precisely the initial law and success event before claiming all algorithms fail at every polynomial budget"; part (v) needs label-time occupancy, and the $O(1)$ ideal-grid conclusion is not established by W″).
- Replacement / repairs: A-DRAFT Prop M (CE208) as the valid fixed-$p$ version, which A-REV4 uses ("A correct minimal repair is the identifiable p=2 family in A-DRAFT Proposition M, whose four-state direct comparison supplies all missing normalisation arguments"); A-REV6's NM-R (TH393, Astra-authored, GAP pending Claude); registry: "[PENDING] A-REV4's repair: use the identifiable p = 2 family of A-DRAFT Prop. M; not applied to F-DRAFT's text". Counterexample object: CE209.
- Status history: F-DRAFT (Fable) "PROVED modulo T03/EXP′/Cor. P1" -> A-REV4 (Astra): **ERROR** (+ scope GAP) -> A-REV6: "ERROR ... NM-R supplies a finite four-state candidate; growing-p normalisation and stage-count claims remain OPEN" -> meeting: dropped as K98 "KNOWN-FALSE (SHARE-M(b), FD-NM)" (RF266). Positions: F-DRAFT result [pos 616]; A-REV4 launched ~[pos 677], bundled in HQ's [pos 796]; repairs in [pos 807]; HQ list of results "already shown false (SHARE-M(b), FD-NM, ...)" [pos 1361]; proposal to feature NM as "Prop 0" [pos 957]; meeting [pos 1626].

### Song–Liang (2015) positioning

Sources: `THM-INV/digests/SL.md` (read from the JRSS-B PDF supplied by Felipe, put in the repo at [pos 1072]; digest file head states: "The supplementary material (proofs of Thms 1-4, SAMC details, Theorem S on MAP consistency, Lemma 1.2) is NOT in the text"), `THM-INV/REPORT.md` §3b and D10, `A-DRAFT/REPORT.md` §1.2, `LIT-SMC/REPORT.md`, `LIT-PAR/REPORT.md`, meeting files. All claims about Song–Liang below are labelled by who wrote them; none is a campaign result.

Summary: SL's algorithm: random split of the $P_n$ predictors into $K_n$ subsets of size $\le s$ ($s\ge500$ recommended); stage 1 Bayesian variable selection by SAMC in each subset (FDR-controlled threshold $\alpha_1$, iterated at most twice); merge $\tilde S=\cup_i\tilde s_i$; stage 2 Bayesian variable selection on $\tilde S$ with prior $(r_n/p_n)^{|\xi|}\cdots$ and FDR level $\alpha_2$; the output is the posterior restricted to models inside $\tilde S$ ("The subset data regression is equivalent to the use of a data-dependent prior, which sets the prior probability to 0 for any models containing predictors that have been screened out in stage 1").

SL's formal results (digest, types only): Thm 1, Thm 2, Cor 1 (Hellinger contraction, exact full posterior); Thm 3 (sure screening of identifiable true predictors, exact posterior); Thm S (supplement, MAP consistency, exact posterior); Thm 4 and Cor 2 (misspecified fixed subset concentrates on the KL projection; $\tilde s$ = support of $\beta_0$); eq. (19). Digest: "There is NO formal theorem for the composed SAM procedure (merged output)." Key verbatim conditions (digest): "Condition 5 (l.620), verbatim: **|cov(x_t, y)| > 0 for any true predictor x_t.** (Note: only strictly positive; no 'bounded away from 0', no uniformity in n or P_n, no explicit rate.)"; "Eq (19): beta_0 = Sigma_s^{-1} Sigma_{s,t} beta*_t = Sigma_s^{-1} cov(x_s, y), Sigma_s = var(x_s), Sigma_{s,t} = cov(x_s, x_t). So s~ depends on both the correlation structure and beta*; 'when t not subset of s, it is unclear whether beta_{0,t} is exactly 0 or not.'" SL on uncertainty (Sec 7, digest): "SAM is not a standard Bayesian approach, as it does not process all data altogether and thus only provides an approximate quantification of uncertainty for each predictor through marginal inclusion probabilities."

THM-INV verdicts (THM-INV/REPORT.md §3b, verbatim rows): Thm S: "**EXCEED**: SL never prove anything about the merged output ('SAM is consistent' is informal; SL digest §2)"; Thm 4/Cor 2: "**EXCEED** (we quantify the failure, and correctness does not depend on it); their Condition 5 (|cov(x_t, y)| > 0) is exactly what masking violates"; §6 complexity: "**LACK of a comparable parallel-cost statement**"; UQ: "**EXCEED at fixed data; LACK as n grows in correlated (masked) designs**"; Thms 1–2/Cor 1: "**MATCH for selection; LACK for contraction rates and p up to e^{Cn^α}**". D10: "Settled against the text (SL digest). Condition 5 ... justifies the iterative stage-1 step. Theorem 4 / Corollary 2 with eq. (19) is what retains a true predictor: it is retained only if its population projection coefficient β₀,t on the subset is nonzero. Masking can break both: cov(x_t, y) = 0 for a cancelled pair, and β₀,t = 0 when its partner sits in another split."

A-DRAFT on SL (verbatim): "Their method selects within predictor subsets, aggregates selected variables, then selects again on the aggregate. It already addresses misspecified local regressions; Theorem 3 gives sure screening, Theorem 4 concerns misspecified-posterior consistency, and the text identifies a supplementary MAP-consistency result. Thus it is inaccurate to describe their complete algorithm as merely a naive union." Papers not in `Papers/`: Song–Liang, Lindsten et al., Gutierrez–Guhaniyogi (A-DRAFT table; checked from primary sources online).

LIT-SMC (theme 12 owns; used here only for positioning): Woodard–Schmidler–Huber persistence "a published mechanism matching W7-SEP SEP(A) (start-only discovery fails) and O-STAGES Theorem M"; Mathews–Schmidler: "the literature handles multimodality only when every mode is visible throughout the path. Our masked results (T38 b-routes, W7-SEP) live where that fails."; gap G2: "Masked start = low persistence, with an exact cost ... a quantitative separation: iid start draws need Q* = p^c n^{c/2} (W7-SEP SEP(A), A-REV9 VERIFIED)". LIT-SMC does not itself contain a Song–Liang entry for the split-and-merge method (grep: only §1D relatives Lindsten et al. #23 and Kuntz–Crucinio–Johansen #24).

### A-DRAFT novelty audit (six works) — summary table of A-DRAFT §1.2

Summary: A-DRAFT §1 (the audit "is a comparison against the six specified works, not proof of worldwide priority"):

| Work | What it already establishes (A-DRAFT) | Where v3 differs / A-DRAFT's referee attack |
|---|---|---|
| Song–Liang 2015 (JRSSB 77, 947–972) | split, per-subset selection, aggregate, second selection; Thm 3 sure screening, Thm 4 misspecified posterior; not "merely a naive union" | v3 keeps all feasible supports through positive block tables and a global size prior and targets the specified full posterior; "the §3 counterexample below refutes naive union, not Song–Liang's second selection stage" (CJ275) |
| Zanella–Roberts 2019 | TGS, Prop 1 consistency of weighted estimator, Thm 1 asymptotic variance bound vs Gibbs, §4.4 RB PIPs, §4.5 complexity | v3's annealed particle bridge has target-invariant moves, not a modified stationary law; "No superiority over TGS follows from any v3 theorem" |
| Lindsten et al. 2017 (D&C-SMC) | recursive local populations, merging, importance correction; Prop 1 unbiased constants, Prop 2 consistency; §4.2 tempering bridge | "closest conceptual antecedent"; "a renamed framework alone will not survive this comparison" |
| Schäfer–Chopin 2013 | binary-space SMC, geometric bridge, ESS bisection, logistic-conditionals proposals | "the ordinary geometric bridge and even ESS bisection are not novel" |
| Del Moral–Doucet–Jasra 2006 | SMC samplers, normalising constants, CLTs (Prop 2), adaptive ESS | T12/T31 are specialisations; "re-proving the finite-state LLN is useful validation, but should not be sold as a main novelty" |
| Gutierrez–Guhaniyogi 2022 | dynamic feature partitioning, fixed-partition pseudo-posterior theory | exact finite-data target vs approximation; the draft's random/inferred partition (§13.3) is "not the deterministic X-dependent partition of v3 and has no theorem here" |

A-DRAFT referee verdict (verbatim): "Risk 2 is real. The most plausible substantial contributions are (i) the concrete start law with exact global prior/cap handling, (ii) a jointly verified family exhibiting poor truth mass at the start but successful budgeted correction/discovery, and (iii) quantitative weight/estimator control in regimes where correction is actually needed. Item (iii) in the masked regime remains OPEN in this report ... A safe paper claim is 'a BVS-specific construction and analysis within established SMC principles.' 'First local-to-global Bayesian correction,' 'new generic SMC consistency,' and 'all uncertainty estimates are unbiased' are not defensible claims." HQ relay [pos 616]. Other A-DRAFT results (Theorem A fixed-data consistency, Corollary A1, uniform PIPs, Theorem D, Corollary D1 and the bounded-$h$ counterexample) are in the theme 8 section: TH320 (ADRAFT-ThmA), TH322 (ADRAFT-ThmD), CE185 (ADRAFT-CEXh).

> ## 1. The spine: "moving off the start is needed", not "tempering is needed"
> ### The finding
> W7-SEP ... tested the planned claim that "start-only methods fail; the tempering bridge is needed". On the paper's own masked family LH, that claim is **false**.
> - **Proposition GU (greedy universality)** is PROVED (candidate; not XF reviewed; it uses W4-T38FULL Lemma M, which is same-family VERIFIED only). Its setting: exact-Gram designs with an isolated relevant set R, SE on R and fixed signals. Its conclusion: the production local search, started at **any** C ⊆ R, reaches, scores and certifies S₀ with probability → 1, in a bounded number of moves.
> - **Corollary GU-LH** (COUNTEREXAMPLE to the task's claim (a), by proof). On LH, start-only discovery plus the production local search (that is, LS0) scores S₀ with probability → 1. The same held numerically in 386/386 replicates.
> - W7-SEP §1 item 4: on LH there is **no separation between the tempering bridge and a single greedy search from the start mode**.
>
> ### What is still true, and is the defensible claim
> **Moving off the start is needed.**
> - iid start draws alone fail in the masked regime: T27(i); R-T20(i).
> - W7-SEP Theorem SEP(A)/(B) (PROVED, candidate) makes this sharp on LH. iid discovery, and one-shot importance reweighting, need Q* = p^c n^{c/2} draws.
>
> **v3's moves provide the move off the start.** Each of the following is a sufficient discovery route; none is shown to be uniquely necessary:
> - bridge Gibbs flips;
> - the terminal rounds (O-BGIBBS Theorem BG3: PROVED for the original method on LH with p fixed; Prop. LH-lock is a PROOF SKETCH);
> - the local search, including LS0 (W7-SEP Prop. GU; T38(b1-LH)).
>
> **The bridge's own role** is to produce calibrated evidence and PIPs (T12, T26) and the HPM ledger.

(Note: AMENDMENTS says "the production local search, started at any $C\subseteq R$" and "SEP(A)/(B) (PROVED, candidate)"; the registry/A-REV9 records SEP(A)/(B) as XF-VERIFIED as implications; the amendments predate A-REV9.)

## Theme 12: PARALLEL-LIT-METHOD — parallel / work-depth theory, literature-derived claims and the synthesis layers

Summary: This theme covers the part of the campaign that is not a new statistical theorem about the sampler but the layer around it: (a) the parallel execution layer and work/depth accounting (METH-AUDIT, 2026-11-03: Lemma S, Proposition W, W-cal, Corollary W-R, Proposition P, Corollary V, Proposition D); (b) the literature-derived positioning claims (API-POS, LIT-SMC, LIT-MCMC, LIT-STAT, LIT-VENUE, LIT-PAR), including the verdict on the gap claim "no BVS method is parallel + correlation-robust + guaranteed"; (c) the synthesis layers (F-REFINE believed versions and 8-target architecture, S-REGISTRY/S-PAPER bookkeeping, F-REFEREE referee objections M1-M8 and minor points m1-m20, W8-SYNTH BRIEF/SYNTHESIS with the three decisions and the next-10 task list, THM-INV theorem ledger and gaps, THM-SYNTH G1-G6 19-item theorem list with tiers); and (d) N9-KERNEL, the proof and exact check that every move of the production kernel is reversible, the random-order round self-adjoint, and the start sampler exact. Chronology (positions in brackets): F-REFINE relaunched at Fable xhigh [pos 474] and completed [pos 463]; S-REGISTRY and S-PAPER launched [pos 594], S-PAPER done [pos 620], S-REGISTRY done [pos 584]; F-REFEREE launched [pos 726, 733], major-revision verdict reported [pos 763, 796]; W8-SYNTH launched 20:14 UTC [pos 763] and its decisions reported [pos 796]; API-POS launched [pos 911], result [pos 978]; the four literature readers launched [pos 983], reported with a correction to API-POS [pos 1009]; Felipe's gap thesis [pos 1030], LIT-PAR launched with the task of falsifying it [pos 1038, 1044]; METH-AUDIT and THM-INV launched [pos 1068, 1072], METH-AUDIT's "3/3" headline flagged as an overclaim [pos 1085, 1103, 1107], HQ re-runs of two designs [pos 1105, 1175, 1241]; THM-SYNTH launched [pos 1099-1102], list delivered [pos 1177, 1185]; N9-KERNEL launched [pos 1467], passed [pos 1546, 1550, 1593], cross-family inherited-proof check VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT [pos 1626]. Headline facts: no theorem the paper relies on breaks under parallel execution (METH-AUDIT); the literal sentence "methods with guarantees are sequential" is false in the work/depth sense (LIT-PAR); no published BVS MCMC-slow/SMC-fast separation is known (OPEN, LIT-MCMC); the published rapid-mixing hypotheses (R > M) fail for the paper target at the study scale (12/12 study-like data sets); the depth factor p+B+2 per round is real and the claim "depth free of N, H, R" was struck for v3.1; referee recommendation was "major revision".

#### CJ311 detail 1: the story and the architecture (ARCHITECTURE.md §1, amended)

> > **Amended 2026-11-02 (E-SPINE, wording only; no status word changed).** This draft no longer implies that tempering,
> > or "the sampler", is *needed*. W7-SEP (858004e · `REPORT.md` · Prop. GU, Cor. GU-LH) shows that on LH, start-only
> > discovery plus the production local search scores S₀. What the theory supports is **"moving off the start is needed"**.
> > Also: LS0 is effective (O-LS0 02348e2: 0/2,394 HPM changes); S-ELS counts; no-LS0 masked candidates pending A-REV7;
> > the "favourable from n ≈ …" figure is dropped. See `main:Docs/Theory/AMENDMENTS_20261102.md` (branch `theory/E-SPINE`).

> ## 1. The story, as it can honestly be told now
>
> What SMC-BVS reports is consistent because the truth gets **scored** and the posterior **ranks** it first. The
> reported HPM is the best model ever scored (every scan, both Gibbs configurations, rejected proposals, LS0 if used).
> So the error decomposes, for every n and every data set, as
>
>   P(output and Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≤ 2E₀[1 − π(S₀)] + P(output-potential run never scores S₀)        (Thm 4, exact)
>
> and the paper proves the two terms vanish in two different ways:
> - the **posterior** term by Thm 1 (T03♯: anchored, size-restricted sparse eigenvalue conditions and beta-min);
> - the **discovery** term either because the start already finds the truth (Thm 2 favourable regime + iid draws:
>   Thm 5(a)), or because the start lands *near* the truth (Thm 2 masked regime, reference S°) and a deterministic
>   greedy repair from that reference scores it (Thm 3 + LS0: Thm 5(b1)).
>
> **What discovery needs (amended 2026-11-02).** In the masked regime the run must **move off its start**: iid start
> draws alone fail (Thm 2 masked start / T27; W7-SEP Theorem SEP(A), Q* = p^c n^{c/2}). v3's moves supply this: bridge
> Gibbs, the terminal rounds (O-BGIBBS BG3 on LH, p fixed) and the local search incl. LS0 (W7-SEP Prop. GU). The tempering
> bridge is one of several sufficient discovery routes, not the uniquely necessary one. Its own role is the calibrated
> evidence and PIPs (Prop 2, Thm 6) and the HPM ledger.
>
> Thm 6 (evidence and PIPs) and Prop 2 (frozen-run identities, 95% bound) say the *other* reported quantities are
> consistent in the favourable regime and unbiased for every n. Prop 1 says the HPM is the right decision and names the
> one error no size prior can fix.
>
> What the story can **not** say: anything numerical at n = 200. The study's start is dilution-masked (6–12 of 14
> truths missing at every signal scale), its misses are posterior misses, the sampler delivers the HPM through Gibbs
> flips (a route with no completed theorem), and the T03 proof thresholds begin near n ≈ 2·10⁶. The theorems explain
> the mechanism; the simulations are evidence in their own right.

#### CJ311 detail 3: the overstatement watch (ARCHITECTURE.md §6, 15 items), the with/without-LS0 section (§4), the n = 200 disclosure (§7) and the open items (§8) are in the source file; the retired statements among them are registered as RF279, RF280 and in Themes 4, 6, 7, 11

> ## 7. The n = 200 disclosure (consolidated; one paragraph for the paper)
>
> At the study's size (n = 200, p ∈ {500, 1000}, s₀ = 14) the theorems are statements about mechanism, not about the
> reported numbers: (i) the block start is masked by dilution (each truth is scored against the other 13 as noise), so
> the start mode misses 6–12 truths at every signal scale (no "favourable from n ≈ …" figure is quoted: the campaign's
> estimates disagree, W8-SYNTH §4.13); (ii) every completed wrong HPM has F(S₀) < F(HPM) (565 of 2,394 fits; 0 search
> misses; S₀ scored in every completed fit, and the final local search never moved: S-ELS; 6 resource stops, all in S5,
> counted as misses); (iii) the sparse-eigenvalue premise of Theorem 1 now ranges over ≤ 114 columns because the
> cap K = 100 binds, but it is unverified on the realised designs, the beta-min constant exceeds the executed signals
> by ≥ 43×, and the proof's deterministic thresholds hold from n ≈ 2·10⁶; (iv) the start rates carry a 2^B factor that
> is ≥ 10³ at B = 14 for n ≤ 10⁴; (v) the HPM at this size is found by Gibbs flips during the bridge and terminal
> rounds, a route for which the paper proves exact finite-n inequalities but no rate.

F-REFEREE read `S-PAPER:theory_section.tex` as "the theory as it stands tonight" (744 lines, Theorems 1-6, Propositions 1-2, the n = 200 disclosure); the S-PAPER draft was therefore the object of the first referee report.

### F-REFEREE — referee objections M1-M8 and m1-m20 as claims (CJ303-CJ310)

Summary: F-REFEREE (Fable 5.1, hostile JRSS-B referee; launched [pos 726, 733], reported [pos 748, 763, 796]) wrote `REFEREE_REPORT.md` (major points M1-M8, minor points m1-m20, verdict) and `RESPONSE_PLAN.md` (point-by-point honest response, "the one change", twelve ranked task specs R1-R12). HQ turned R1-R12 into the API-credit wave of 8 runs [pos 906, 911]. The state of each objection was tracked by T38-RECORD `REGISTRY_v2.md` §H ("Tags updated from W8-SYNTH §5 with O-LS0, E-SPINE and the in-flight reviews"). Each M is registered as a hypothesis-type claim (CJ303-CJ310); the minor points are listed once in the table below.

Object reviewed, summary verdict, and the recommendation (verbatim from `REFEREE_REPORT.md`):

> **Recommendation: major revision.** The theory section is unusually candid, internally consistent, and the
> composition inequality (Theorem 4) is exactly the right organising principle. But in its present form the section
> does not support the paper's empirical claims, and its headline theorem (Theorem 5(b1)) is about an algorithm
> (v3 + LS0) that the reported simulations did not run. Three structural problems decide the tier:
>
> 1. **Every statistical theorem is asymptotic with proof thresholds at n ≈ 2·10⁶, while the simulations are at
>    n = 200 with s₀ = 14, in a start regime (dilution) that no theorem describes.** The section says so itself, at
>    length (§6). A referee will not punish the honesty; a referee will ask what the theorems are *for*.
> 2. **The masked regime, which is the paper's reason to exist, is proved only with a method change (LS0), and the
>    routes for the method that was evaluated are hypotheses-as-conclusions** ((b1′), (b2): conditional on DELIV, REP,
>    NB′; in the draft none is proved on any family, the best instance being a PROOF SKETCH on LH with c = 1).
> 3. **The theory is not positioned against the rapid-mixing literature for Bayesian variable selection** (Yang,
>    Wainwright & Jordan 2016, AoS; Zhou, Yang, Vats & Roberts 2022, JRSS-B), which proves *more* (polynomial mixing to the
>    full posterior, hence HPM, PIPs and everything) under hypotheses of the same kind (sparse eigenvalues plus beta-min),
>    for simpler algorithms, with no method tweak. A Series B referee will raise this in the first paragraph. The novelty
>    audit on `theory/A-DRAFT` does not mention these papers.
>
> What survives and is publishable now: Theorem 4 (exact composition, every n, matched by the data: all 565 misses are
> posterior misses), Theorem 1 as a target-specific consistency result with an exact size tail, Proposition 2 (frozen-run
> identities, with the correct islandwise wording), Theorem 3's exact deterministic part (Theorem A, Lemma LS-score),
> and the two negative results (literal truth dominance is unsatisfiable; bridge mass does not imply delivery, C1).
>
> **The one change that most raises the tier** (details in `RESPONSE_PLAN.md` §2): state and prove the masked-regime
> half of the main theorem **for the algorithm that produced the tables**, on the explicit family LH, and show the
> predicted transition numerically with the production code at growing n. Three candidate routes already exist on
> in-flight branches (O-BGIBBS pilot-stage discovery, W5-B2ENV route (b2) under STAB-LH, O-MIX mixture start); one of
> them cross-family verified turns Theorem 5(b) from "a theorem about v3 + LS0" into "a theorem about v3", and the
> growing-n simulation turns "asymptotic with thresholds at 10⁶" into "the mechanism is visible from n ≈ 10³–10⁴".

Verdict and the one change that most raises the tier (verbatim):

> **Verdict.** Major revision. Not reject: the composition theorem, the exact size tail, the start law with its masking
> theorem, the explicit masked family LH, the negative results, and the frozen-run identities are correct, careful and
> useful, and the candour of §6 is a model. Not minor: the headline theorem is about an unrun algorithm, the masked regime
> for the run algorithm is open, the computational-guarantee literature is unaddressed, and the connection between the
> theorems and the tables is absent.

> **The one change.** *Make Theorem 5(b) a theorem about the algorithm that produced the tables, on the explicit family LH,
> and show its predicted transition with the production code at growing n.* Concretely: cross-family verify one of the
> three in-flight no-tweak routes (O-BGIBBS BG1, W5-B2ENV B2-LH under STAB-LH, W5-B2ENV D2-LH for c = 1) and run LH at
> n ∈ {400, 1600, 6400, 25600} with c ∈ {1, 2, 3}, reporting start-mode misses, first-scoring stage and P(Ŝ = S₀) with and
> without LS0. This single change answers M2 and M3 outright, answers the first half of M1 (the mechanism becomes
> visible at n ≈ 10³–10⁴ rather than 10⁶), gives M4 its separation (start-only fails on the same runs), and leaves LS0 as
> an optional robustness device. Everything else in this report is wording, positioning (M6), or a supplement.
>

> ## 3. Setting compared
>
> **LH** (`W1-EXP · PROOF.md §4`): G groups of size g, with within-group equicorrelation ρ_h. Groups are independent except
> for c linked hub pairs with corr(j_a, j_b) = ψ, and the truth is θ_{j_a} = β, θ_{j_b} = −ψβ (the suppressor), plus visible
> hubs. Two realisations:
> - **exact-Gram**: X'X = (n − 1)Σ, p ≤ n − 1;
> - **iid**: rows iid N(0, Σ_LH), p ≤ n^A, p > n allowed.
>
> The fixed facts used below are λ_min(Σ) ≥ (1 − ψ₊)(1 − ρ₊) =: φ₀² (W1-EXP Lemma 4.1(a)), fixed nonzero β, and fixed s₀.
>
> **Paper's target** (`00_COMMON.md`): β_S ~ N(0, nσ²(G_S + I)⁻¹), σ² ~ IG(0.01, 0.01), and BB(1, p),
> w(k) = ½/C(2p − 1, k), capped at K = min(p, ⌊n/2⌋). Neighbouring prior ratio: w(k+1)/w(k) = (k+1)/(2p−1−k).
>
> **YWJ / ZYVR target**: Zellner g-prior with g ≍ p^{2α} (ZYVR: 1 + g = p^{2κ₁}), π(φ) ∝ 1/φ, and π(γ) ∝ p^{−κ₀|γ|} 1{|γ| ≤ s₀}.
> Here s₀ is **their tuning cap** and must satisfy s₀ ≲ n/log p.

### TH402 — Proposition U (API-POS): underfitted models are never local modes of the paper target on LH-G  [proposition]

- Source (authoritative): `API-POS/REPORT.md` §5; evidence `API-POS/results/cond1_lh.md`; positions: [pos 911], [pos 978].
- Statement (verbatim, with the proof sketch):

> **Proposition U (underfitted models are never local modes of the paper's target on LH-G).**
> - **Hypotheses.** G (fixed design, Gaussian noise σ² > 0 fixed); LH-G with p = p_n ≤ δ n for a small fixed δ (δ < c_U/σ²
>   suffices, c_U below); s₀, β, ρ, ψ fixed; the paper's target on M(K).
> - **Claim.** There is c_U = c_U(φ₀, β, ψ) > 0 such that, with probability → 1, simultaneously for every γ ∈ M(K) with
>   S₀ ⊄ γ and |γ| < K, some j ∈ S₀ ∖ γ satisfies log π(γ ∪ {j})/π(γ) ≥ c n.
> - **Consequence.** ZYVR Condition (1b) holds on all of M(K) with c₁ ≍ n/log p.
> - **Status.** PROOF SKETCH.
>
> *Sketch.*
> 1. **Signal.** By RE on all of M(K) (Y5),
>    ‖(I − P_γ)μ‖² = ‖(I − P_γ)X_{S₀∖γ}θ_{S₀∖γ}‖² ≥ (n − 1)φ₀²‖θ_{S₀∖γ}‖² ≥ (n − 1)φ₀² min_j θ_j².
> 2. **Best single addition.** By YWJ's Lemma 8 argument, one j ∈ S₀∖γ has
>    ⟨(I − P_γ)x_j, μ⟩²/‖(I − P_γ)x_j‖² ≥ ‖(I − P_γ)μ‖²·φ₀²/s₀ ≥ c_U n.
> 3. **Noise.** The noise enters through ⟨u, ε⟩ for a unit vector u ∈ span X, and |⟨u, ε⟩| ≤ ‖P_X ε‖ = σ√p(1 + o_P(1))
>    uniformly over all (γ, j). So the RSS drop is ≥ (√(c_U n) − σ√p(1 + o(1)))² ≥ c n when p ≤ δ n.
> 4. **Ratio.** RSS_γ ≤ ‖y‖² = n − 1. Hence
>    ν log(RSS_γ/RSS_{γ+j}) ≥ (n/2)·c n/(n − 1) ≥ c n/2.
>    This dominates the remaining terms, −½ log(n+1) and the prior ratio ≥ 1/(2p).
> 5. **Not yet written out.** The constant bookkeeping, and the replacement of y by its standardised version (scale factor s_y).

- Earlier versions / repairs: none within the branch. Related statement made by LIT-PAR notes 04 ("ZYVR Condition 1(b) likely fails on masked LH") is superseded by this proposition (RF277).
- Status history: proposed PROOF SKETCH (API-POS, 2026-11-02) -> not checked; THM-INV row 1 lists "API-POS Prop U (no underfitted local modes on LH) PROOF SKETCH"; LIT-MCMC cites it as "API-POS Prop. U, PROOF SKETCH".
- Proved by / checked by: API-POS author only; supported by exact enumeration (table below), p <= 20.
- Depends on: ⟦LH⟧, ⟦W1-EXP Lemma 4.1(a)⟧, YWJ Lemma 8 argument (cited).
- Feeds: no final card (campaign-only positioning input); the positioning paragraph next to M5 in THEOREM_LIST_FINAL.
- Notes: Prop U is the property (1b) of ZYVR Condition 1 for the paper target; LIT-MCMC Prop OB shows the complementary property (1a/overfitted side, R > M) fails for the paper prior.

API-POS "What fails and why" and escalations (verbatim):

> ## 10. What fails and why (routes tried)
>
> - **"LH violates the mixing papers' design conditions"**: false. RE holds on LH-G for every model size, SI holds,
>   beta-min holds (β fixed) and ω(X) is bounded. The mismatches are all on the *prior* side (g, κ, cap) and the regime side
>   (p ≥ n). None is on the design side.
> - **"The masking makes the posterior multimodal, so MCMC is slow on LH"**: false. The masking lives in π₀ only (§6;
>   Prop. U). At S° = S₀ ∖ M, adding a masked hub j_b has population gain β²ψ²(1 − ψ²)n > 0, because the residual of μ on
>   S° is βψ(ψx_{j_a} − x_{j_b}). So the target sees j_b, while the block-wise start (which regresses y on block C_b alone)
>   does not: Cov(X_{C_b}, μ) = 0.
> - **"Their theorems apply verbatim to the paper's posterior"**: false (Y0, Y7, Y8, Z4(1a)). The (1a) failure is not
>   only slack in the proofs. Under BB(1,p) with g = n the best null addition to an overfitted model costs only about
>   n^{−1/2}, against their p^{−2}.
