### TH401 — Proposition OB (the overfitted-side bottleneck for the paper prior)  [proposition]

- Source (authoritative): `LIT-MCMC/REPORT.md` §2.2 (statement), §3.1 (sketch); positions: [pos 983], [pos 1009]; HQ relay [pos 1009] ("A new proof sketch (Prop OB) explains why").
- Statement (verbatim):

> ### 2.2 Proposition OB (the overfitted-side bottleneck for the paper's prior)
>
> **Setting.**
> - The paper's target (`METHODOLOGY_v3.md §5`) on M(s) for some s with s₀ < s ≤ K.
> - N = add/delete/swap, M := max_{γ ∈ M(s)} |N(γ)| ≥ p − s.
> - G (Gaussian noise) and fixed s₀. Let γ_e := S₀ ∪ {e} for a null e ∉ S₀, k := s₀ + 1.
> - T_e := (n − k)·[Q_{S₀} − Q_{γ_e}]/Q_{γ_e}, the partial F-type statistic of e given S₀.
>
> **Claim.**
> - (i) Exact prior factor: ϖ(S₀)/ϖ(γ_e) = w(k − 1)/w(k) = (2p − k)/k.
> - (ii) π(S₀)/π(γ_e) = [(2p − k)/k] · √(n + 1) · exp(−½T_e) · (1 + o_P(1)), uniformly in e.
> - (iii) Suppose further that max_{e ∉ S₀} T_e ≥ (2 − ε) log p with probability → 1. This holds, for instance, when the
>   null columns' residuals given S₀ are nearly orthogonal (S1-like). Then with probability → 1, R ≤ max_{y∈N(γ_{e*})}
>   π(y)/π(γ_{e*}) ≤ C·p^{ε/2}√n/s₀ for e* = argmax T_e.
> - Consequently R/M ≤ C p^{ε/2}√n/(s₀(p − s)) → 0 whenever p^{1−ε/2} ≫ √n.
>
> So the hypothesis R > M of Chang–Zhou Thm 1/4, Zhou–Smith Assumption 1 (ν > α), and the analogous c₀ = 2 in ZYVR's (1a)
> **cannot hold for the paper's prior when p ≫ √n**. The study (p ≥ 500 ≫ √200 ≈ 14) is far into this range.
>
> **Status.** (i) PROVED (from w(k) = ½/C(2p − 1, k)). (ii)–(iii) PROOF SKETCH: §3.1 below. The step "the best neighbour of
> γ_{e*} is S₀" is used only as an upper bound through max_y and needs the swap neighbours to be controlled too; that step is
> not verified.
>
> **What OB does NOT say.** It does not say the chain mixes slowly. R ≤ M is the failure of a *sufficient* condition. The
> measured hitting times on LH (API-POS §6: median ≈ 70–140 iterations, flat in n) show that discovery is fast anyway.
> What OB says is that **no published unimodal-ratio theorem can certify our target in the study's regime**, for a
> structural reason: per extra variable, the prior and g-penalty is ≍ p√n, only one power of p, and the noise maximum eats
> that power.

Proof route (Summary: LIT-MCMC §3.1): Schur-complement determinant ratio gives the factor sqrt(n+1); the residual term gives exp(-T_e/2) when T_e = O(log p) = o(sqrt(n)); under S1-like nulls max T_e >= (2-eps) log p; the best neighbour of gamma_{e*} is bounded neighbour by neighbour (deletion of e* dominates). Not verified: uniformity in e, ridge corrections in Q, and the neighbour step.

- Earlier versions / repairs: the heuristic log_p(2 sqrt(n)/k) is about 0.1 at n = 200, k = 15, but the measured log_p R_ub is 0.2-0.5 because at finite p the noise maximum T_{e*} is below 2 log p; the conclusion R << M is unaffected.
- Status history: proposed (LIT-MCMC) (i) PROVED, (ii)-(iii) PROOF SKETCH -> supported by CE215 (12/12) and CE216 -> used by THM-INV D1 and THM-SYNTH REPORT §4.1 -> FUTURE_WORK FW4.
- Proved by / checked by: author only.
- Depends on: ⟦paper target (METHODOLOGY_v3 §5)⟧, CJ130 (G), w(k) = (1/2)/C(2p-1,k).
- Feeds: FUTURE_WORK FW4; positioning paragraph next to M5.
- Notes: OB does NOT say the chain mixes slowly; "R <= M is the failure of a sufficient condition. The measured hitting times on LH (API-POS §6: median about 70-140 iterations, flat in n) show that discovery is fast anyway."

### CJ289, CJ290, CJ291 — LIT-MCMC positioning statements L1, L2, L3  [conjecture / open problem / proposition]

- Source: `LIT-MCMC/REPORT.md` §2.1; positions: [pos 983], [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ### 2.1 Positioning statements (literature claims; status = how sure I am that they are true of the literature)
>
> - **L1 (rapid-mixing hypotheses).** Every polynomial mixing-time theorem for BVS MCMC that I read (#1–#5, #14, #15)
>   assumes either
>   - (i) a unimodal-ratio landscape on a sparse space, R > M (RW-MH) or R > M² (informed), together with a sparse cap
>     s ≲ n/log p and a prior penalty per extra variable of order p^{κ}·g^{1/2} with κ + α large; or
>   - (ii) a warm start whose support contains the truth (#14, #15).
>
>   None assumes BB(1, p) with g = n and cap ⌊n/2⌋. Status: CONJECTURE (literature claim); high confidence for the works
>   listed, unknown for unread works.
> - **L2 (no BVS tempering separation).** I found no published BVS family on which standard BVS MCMC provably mixes slowly
>   while a tempering or SMC method provably succeeds. The only proved BVS slow-mixing example is YWJ App. A.2, which is
>   cured by a size cap, not by tempering. Status: OPEN (as a literature claim); medium confidence.
> - **L3 (SMC theory needs either global gaps or mode mass along the bridge).** The general SMC finite-sample theorems
>   (#18, #19, and Marion–Mathews–Schmidler as recalled in #19) need either a spectral gap γ > 0 for *every* kernel or
>   local mixing plus µ⋆ = min mode mass along the bridge, with cost ∝ 1/µ⋆. In the masked regime µ⋆ ≤ π₀(S₀-basin)
>   ≍ n^{−c/2} (T27 / Thm 2 masking law). Status: PROVED as a reading of the stated theorems (the hypotheses are quoted
>   in N3 and N12). Applying it to our masked start uses Thm 2's masking law (a candidate, not adopted).

- CJ289 (L1): CONJECTURE (literature claim); high confidence for the works listed, unknown for unread works. CJ290 (L2, no BVS MCMC-slow/SMC-fast separation): OPEN (as a literature claim), medium confidence. CJ291 (L3): PROVED as a reading of the stated theorems.

### CJ292 — LIT-MCMC G1: no published hitting/scoring time of S0 from (1b)/(1c) alone  [conjecture]

- Source: `LIT-MCMC/REPORT.md` §0 item 4, §5, §6; positions: [pos 983], [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim, §5 gaps and §6 threats):

> - **G1. Discovery or scoring guarantees from (1b)/(1c) alone, with no (1a), no sparse cap and a weak prior.**
>   - Every published result proves *mixing*, which needs the overfitted-side drain (1a) or R > M on the whole space.
>   - Our story needs only that S₀ is *scored*: T21/Thm 4 and N200 make the reported HPM right once S₀ is scored and
>     ranked first.
>   - Our repair theorems give this kind of statement for local search from a near-truth centre: T37 / Prop. GU
>     (W7-SEP), T38(b1-LH) with LS0, and (b2-LH) without LS0 under STAB-LH.
>   - Nothing in the literature I read states a hitting-time-of-S₀ theorem under (1b)/(1c) only.
>   - Gamarnik–Zadik Thm 2.7 is the closest: local search from any start, but for iid X and n ≥ C k log p.
>
>   Value: **real**. Our discovery-and-scoring decomposition (T21) is a different, weaker and more relevant target than
>   mixing, and OB shows mixing theorems cannot reach our prior in p ≫ n.

> - **Θ1 (strongest). Chang–Zhou Thm 4 together with API-POS Prop. U.** If the target is unimodal with a strong ratio,
>   any start costs only log(1/π(x₀)) extra. The masked start has log(1/π₀(S₀)) ≈ (c/2) log n, so the start's masking
>   costs a log factor. On LH-iid with the YWJ prior this makes "the masked regime is solvable" a corollary of known
>   results (API-POS headline 2).
>   - Defence: OB shows these theorems cannot be applied to our prior in p ≫ √n. Our theorems are for the target and
>     method actually used.
>   - That defence is a formal gap, not a substantive one, which is API-POS's own verdict.
>   - Wording advice: present the masked theorems as "the method's own start creates the masking, and the method's own
>     moves remove it". Do not present them as "MCMC fails here".
> - **Θ2. Gamarnik–Zadik Thm 2.7.** "Local search from any k-sparse start recovers the support when n ≥ C k log p" is
>   known for iid Gaussian X. It overlaps T37/GU in spirit. Our versions cover correlated (exact-Gram, block) designs and
>   the production search, and state a finite move bound. GZ is a citation we must make.

- Status history: CONJECTURE (literature), medium confidence (LIT-MCMC §0 item 4). Closest published: Gamarnik-Zadik Thm 2.7 (iid X, n >= C k log p), YWJ Lemma 4, Chang-Zhou Thm 4 (a bad start costs log(1/pi(x0))).

### CE216 — LIT-MCMC rz_lh: exact enumeration of R and M on LH  [counterexample]

- Source: `LIT-MCMC/REPORT.md` §4 (table) and `LIT-MCMC/results/rz_lh.md`; positions: [pos 1009].
- Construction and result (verbatim):

> **Exact enumeration** (`scripts/rz_lh.py`, output `results/rz_lh.md`, run via owls_run -j 2, a few minutes).
> - **Inputs.** The paper's exact target, exact-Gram LH, and the same LH settings as API-POS:
>   - c = 1: p = 16, ρ = 0.7, ψ = 0.5;
>   - c = 2: p = 20, ρ = 0.85.
> - **Quantities.**
>   - R = min_{x ≠ x*} max_{y∈N(x)} π(y)/π(x) and M = max|N(x)|, with N = add/delete/swap.
>   - Two spaces: M(K), the whole capped space, and M(s), the sparse space with s = 6 or 8.
> - **Columns.**
>   - log_p R and log_p M.
>   - The two published sufficient conditions: R > M (RW-MH, Chang–Zhou Thm 1) and R > M² (informed, Thm 2).
>   - x* = S₀?, the state attaining R, and the number of non-x* local modes.
>
> | LH | n | space | log_p R | log_p M | R > M | R > M² | x* = S₀ | flattest state | other local modes |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | c = 1 | 200 | M(K) | 0.95 | 1.58 | NO | NO | yes | full model (16) | 0 |
> | c = 1 | 200 | M(6) | 1.06 | 1.54 | NO | NO | yes | {0,4,5,6,8} ⊇ S₀ | 0 |
> | c = 1 | 1,600 | M(K) | 1.16 | 1.58 | NO | NO | yes | {0,4,7,8} ⊇ S₀ | 0 |
> | c = 1 | 12,800 | M(K) | 1.70 | 1.58 | yes | NO | yes | full model | 0 |
> | c = 1 | 102,400 | M(K) | 2.08 | 1.58 | yes | NO | yes | full model | 0 |
> | c = 2 | 200 | M(K) | 0.88 | 1.60 | NO | NO | yes | full model (20) | 0 |
> | c = 2 | 200 | M(8) | 0.92 | 1.57 | NO | NO | yes | {0,5,8,12,16} (underfitted swap) | 0 |
> | c = 2 | 1,600 | M(K) | 0.92 | 1.60 | NO | NO | yes | {0,4,7,8,12,16} ⊇ S₀ | 0 |
> | c = 2 | 12,800 | M(K) | 1.37 | 1.60 | NO | NO | yes | ⊇ S₀ (size 7) | 0 |
> | c = 2 | 102,400 | M(K) | 1.93 | 1.60 | yes | NO | yes | full model | 0 |
>
> What it shows:
> 1. **The target is unimodal on LH at every n**, including n = 200. This agrees with API-POS.
> 2. **The flattest direction is almost always on the overfitted side.** It is either a superset of S₀ or the saturated
>    model, which is YWJ App. A.2's trap, here not a mode but nearly flat. This is the side that matters for mixing, not
>    for discovery. It matches OB.
> 3. **The published sufficient conditions fail at the study's n**, and R > M² fails everywhere.
> 4. **Caveat.** p ≤ 20 is far from the study's p ≥ 500. OB predicts the failure is much worse there. Not checked beyond

- Status: COUNTEREXAMPLE to R > M (Chang-Zhou Thm 1) and R > M^2 (informed samplers) for the paper target on LH at n <= 1,600 (R > M also fails at n = 12,800 for c = 2); p <= 20 only.
- Replaces / refutes: RF274, RF275.

>   "holds true under no additional assumptions on the model … including … nonhomogeneous potential functions G_n and

>     uniform conditions G(x) ≤ δG(x′) and M^m(x,·) ≤ βM^m(x′,·).

Its only mathematics are two elementary computations about the BB(1,p) prior (LM227, LM228). Key findings are quoted in the items below.

### LM227 — BB(1,p) is not a complexity prior in the sense of Castillo-Schmidt-van der Vaart (2.2)  [lemma]

- Source: `LIT-STAT/REPORT.md` §6 (evidence, PROVED), §1 item 4; `scripts/bb_ratios.py` -> `results/bb_ratios.txt`; positions: [pos 983], [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim):

> - `scripts/bb_ratios.py` → `results/bb_ratios.txt`. Exact rational arithmetic, deterministic, run via `owls_run -j 2`. It checks three
>   things:
>   1. w(k) = ½/C(2p−1,k) = B(k+1, 2p−k)/B(1,p), for k ≤ min(p, 60) and p ∈ {20, 500, 1000}.
>   2. The dimension ratio is π_p(s)/π_p(s−1) = (p−s+1)/(2p−s), asserted exactly. The implied CSvdV exponent is A4 = −log(ratio)/log p,
>      which is 0.1003–0.1080 at p = 1000 and 0.111–0.130 at p = 500 for s ≤ 100, and tends to 0 as p → ∞ for fixed s.
>   3. The per-model ratio is w(s)/w(s−1) = s/(2p−s).
>
>   **PROVED** (elementary algebra, with exact numerical confirmation): BB(1,p) satisfies CSvdV (2.2) for no fixed A4 > 0 uniformly in p,
>   so CSvdV Thms 1, 4 and Cor 1 do not apply to our size prior.

- Earlier versions / repairs: none.
- Status history: PROVED (elementary, with exact numerical confirmation) by the LIT-STAT author; not reviewed.
- Proved by / checked by: author only (exact rational arithmetic script).
- Depends on: CE110 (BB(1,p)), TH125 (T02(i♯)).
- Feeds: none (novelty wording for S-T / Theorem 1).

### LM228 — BB(1,p) = BB(1,1) tilted by a geometric size factor  [lemma]

- Source: `LIT-STAT/REPORT.md` §12 (addendum, "checked after the first draft"); `scripts/bb11_vs_bb1p.py`; positions: [pos 1009].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## 12. Addendum: BB(1,p) versus Rossell's BB(1,1) (checked after the first draft)
>
> `scripts/bb11_vs_bb1p.py` → `results/bb11_vs_bb1p.txt` (exact rationals, deterministic, run via `owls_run -j 2`). It shows:
>
> - The per-model ratios are w(k+1)/w(k) = (k+1)/(p−k) for BB(1,1) and (k+1)/(2p−1−k) for BB(1,p), both asserted exactly. They agree to
>   within a factor of about 2.
> - w_{BB(1,p)}(k)/w_{BB(1,1)}(k) = (p+1)C(p,k)/(2C(2p−1,k)). This equals ((p+1)/2)·2^{−k}·(1 + o(1)) for k ≪ √p. The bracketed
>   correction is 1.000 at k = 0 and 0.96 at k = 14 (p = 1000), and only 0.0045 at k = 100 (p = 500), where BB(1,p) is even lighter.
>
> **PROVED** (elementary): BB(1,p) is BB(1,1) multiplied by a size-only factor that is at most ((p+1)/2)·(2p/(2p−1))·2^{−k} for k ≥ 1.
> The reason is that C(p,k)/C(2p−1,k) = ∏_{i<k}(p−i)/(2p−1−i). The i = 0 factor is p/(2p−1) = ½·2p/(2p−1), and every factor with i ≥ 1
> is ≤ ½. This also explains the 1.0010 = 1000/999 entry at k = 1, p = 500. A first draft of this line said "≤ ½ for every i ≥ 0", which
> is false at i = 0; corrected here.
>
> Consequences for this audit:
> - **Spurious models.** Rossell's (2022) §5.2 accounting of spurious models (per-model prior ratio times a Bayes-factor bound) transfers to
>   BB(1,p) up to the constant (p+1)/2 at the denominator S₀ and an extra 2^{−(k−s₀)} that only helps.
> - **Cap.** His requirement p̄ ≪ n comes from summing a flat size law up to p̄. The geometric tilt is exactly what lets T02(i♯) live with
>   K = ⌊n/2⌋.
> - **Revised verdicts.** T03♯ is a **modest extension of Rossell (2022)** to a geometric-size-tilted BB prior, a cap of order n and a
>   ridge slab, rather than a different mechanism. H2's severity rises from Medium to **Medium–High**. G1 narrows to the cap and the exact
>   cutoff, with Prop. D's lower bound.
> - **E1 updated.** Rossell's supplement (Lemma S15, Lemma S21, read in the same arXiv PDF) treats BB(1,1), uniform and Complexity
>   priors only. It has no BB(1,p) and no cap of order n. A stronger reviewer should still check Martin, Mess & Walker (2017), which I did
>   not read.

- Earlier versions / repairs: a first draft said "<= 1/2 for every i >= 0" for the factors of C(p,k)/C(2p-1,k); false at i = 0; corrected in §12 (RF281).
- Status history: PROVED (elementary) by the author; the revised verdict (T03 sharp modest extension; novelty of T02(i sharp) "Low-to-medium confidence in the novelty, pending E1") follows.
- Proved by / checked by: author only.
- Depends on: LM227 (LM227)-type ratios, TH125 (T02(i♯)).
- Feeds: none.

## Part C. The gap claim and the parallel layer (2026-11-03)

### Block — LIT-PAR: the gap claim "no BVS method is parallel + correlation-robust + guaranteed"

Summary: On 2026-11-03 Felipe restated the project's purpose: the point of SMC is parallel computing that does not break under correlation the way Song-Liang split-and-merge does, the big-picture goal is "to retire MCMC for BVS" [pos 1020, 1030, 1040]. HQ framed this as a gap claim and a thesis sentence [pos 1038, 1044] and launched LIT-PAR (Opus, cap $10, spent $5.47) to try to falsify it [pos 1038]. Felipe's statement of the claim [pos 1030] (verbatim):

> So, again, we can keep our current theoretical goals, my point is, to the best of my knowledge there is no highly parallelizable BVS that works well, has strong theoretical guarantees. There are a lot of BVS with theoretical guarantees - sequential, not parallel, there are parallel computing friendly methods with guarantees but that break under correlated designs, etc. The practical difference is unspoken but clear, if something can be broken into pieces we can in principle go for higher p. And also I'm assuming if the method is successful somebody will build on it, the rationale is: sequential sampling, regardless of how good it is is can only take you so far wrt to number of variables, we want to begin to solve that problem. It won't be fully solved in one paper, but the big picture goal is basically to retire MCMC for BVS, the next gen samplers must be parallel and with the same degree of theoretical guarantees, it is basically a change of schools of thought

HQ framing of the claim and the thesis sentence [pos 1038, 1044] (verbatim):

> **Framing.** Methods that come with guarantees are sequential, and parallel-friendly methods with guarantees break under correlated designs. Our method is meant to be both, and paper 1 is a first step toward replacing sequential MCMC for BVS.

> - **Sequential depth:** the only sequential part is the stage count, and O-STAGES already bounds it: about log₂A₀ stages (A₀ measures how badly the block start misses the truth) when the start is masked, and O(1) when it isn't. MCMC's sequential depth is its mixing time.

> ### Thesis sentence
> **In split-and-merge, correlation breaks correctness. In local-to-global SMC, correlation costs only sequential depth and particles, never correctness.**

### CJ282 — S-GAP: the three-part gap claim and its verdict TRUE WITH QUALIFICATIONS  [conjecture]

- Source (authoritative): `LIT-PAR/REPORT.md` §1, §3, §4.1, §7; notes `LIT-PAR/notes/01`-`09`; ledger "13:03 UTC 2026-11-03: objective clarified; LIT-PAR launched"; positions: [pos 1030], [pos 1038], [pos 1044], [pos 1070] (HQ reads the report), [pos 1072] (HQ relays the verdict), [pos 1107].
- Statement (verbatim, §4.1 refined statements for the paper):

> ### 4.1 Refined statements proposed for the paper (positioning claims, not theorems)
> - **S-GAP (CONJECTURE about the literature; evidence from §2).** Among published BVS methods, none simultaneously
>   - (a) targets the exact model posterior with an unbiased evidence estimate,
>   - (b) parallelises in communication-free width (islands), and
>   - (c) has a proved sequential-depth (stage-count) bound on a correlated design whose start is masked.
>
>   Every parallel BVS method with a theorem needs one of:
>   - cross-split faithfulness (SaM);
>   - weak correlation (DECO, BB-SSL, Ray–Szabó, Yang–Pati–Bhattacharya);
>   - block-diagonal Gram (Papaspiliopoulos–Rossell);
>   - large-n plug-in consistency (DFP);
>   - fixed-dimension shards (WASP, M-posterior, Zhang–Lam–Lin).
>
>   Exact parallel BVS samplers (Schäfer–Chopin, Ma, Jankowiak, Zanella–Roberts) have only qualitative or relative guarantees.
> - **S-COUNTER (from the literature).** Under ZYVR Condition 1, a single informed chain has a p-free iteration bound with
>   O(ps₀) parallel work per iteration. "Guarantees ⇒ sequential" is false as a general statement.
> - **S-DEPTH (to be carried by our theorems; status inherited).**
>   - v3 has depth D = T·L_r·(p + B + 2)·s(K) + O(2^B s(B)) + T·O(log RN) and width R·N.
>   - T obeys the O-STAGES bounds (PROVED / PROOF SKETCH there).
>   - Pooled error at fixed N decays as 1/R by T31(i) (standard; Whiteley–Lee–Heine).
>   - A single-island relative-variance bound in the masked regime is **OPEN**.

HQ relay of the verdict to Felipe at [pos 1072] (verbatim):

> ### LIT-PAR verdict: the gap claim holds, with qualifications
> - **The gap is real.** Every parallel BVS method with a theorem needs a design condition that strongly correlated designs violate: Song–Liang, DECO, the Bayesian-bootstrap spike-and-slab LASSO, Gutierrez–Guhaniyogi, and variational methods. None combines all three of: the exact model posterior with an unbiased Ẑ, communication-free parallel computation, and a proved bound on sequential depth under correlation.
> - **Don't print "methods with guarantees are sequential".** That's false in the work-versus-depth sense. Zhou–Yang–Vats–Roberts–Rosenthal's informed sampler has a mixing bound that doesn't grow with p, and each step's neighbour scoring is parallel.
> - **More ingredients are standard and must be cited.** Ẑ-weighted pooling of independent islands (T31(i)) is in Whiteley–Lee–Heine 2016 and Dai et al. 2022. Parallel tempered SMC on binary spaces is Schäfer–Chopin 2013. Exact enumeration of correlation-clustered blocks is Papaspiliopoulos–Rossell 2017.
> - **New evidence for us:** on a small masked design, the exact posterior recovers the true model in 20 of 20 datasets. Split-and-merge recovers it in only 5 of 318 random splits that separate the linked pair. This is a first numerical result for the separation theorem.
> - **What remains ours:**
>   - the stage-count laws: O(1) stages when the start is favourable, about log₂A₀ when it is masked;
>   - the guarantees for a masked start;
>   - the full composition (exact block start, exact-target SMC, unbiased Ẑ) with theorems.

Gaps that remain after the falsification attempt (verbatim, §3.1):

> ### 3.1 Gaps: what nobody has proved that we prove or could prove
> - **G1.** A guarantee for an exact-target parallel sampler for BVS whose start is *masked* (truth's basin has exponentially small
>   start mass), on an explicit correlated family.
>   - Generic theory (Mathews–Schmidler) needs μ⋆ ≥ 1/poly. Syed et al. assume efficient local exploration. pSMC (Liang et
>     al.) assumes uniform Doeblin mixing.
>   - Ours: T38 (b1-LH) with LS0, and (b2-LH) under STAB-LH (XF-VERIFIED by A-REV7 on an explicit subfamily). Candidates only.
> - **G2.** Stage-count laws at a *coarse, production* ESS threshold: T* = O(1) favourable, log₂A₀ + O(1) masked, O(log log n)
>   on LH masking (O-STAGES items 2–3).
>   - The literature has only dense-schedule asymptotics in Λ.
>   - The contrast "Λ = L ≤ π while T* → ∞" is a clean new observation (O-STAGES item 4 with [n08]).
> - **G3.** A theorem tying the depth of a parallel BVS sampler to a design-dependent quantity (A₀, a property of the start built
>   from correlation blocks). Nobody analyses correlation-clustered splitting. SaM and Coats et al. split arbitrarily or
>   anti-cluster; Papaspiliopoulos–Rossell cluster but give no guarantee off block-diagonality.
> - **G4. SaM-type splitting fails on a masked pair: COUNTEREXAMPLE (numerical) + PROOF SKETCH (analytic)** [n09],
>   `scripts/sam_lh_demo.py`, seed 20261103.
>   - Design: an LH-like design (our construction; p = 16, n = 200).
>   - Result at β = 1: the exact full posterior recovers S₀ in 20/20 datasets. SaM recovers S₀ in **5/318** random splits that
>     separate the linked pair (median Stage-I PIP of the masked variable 0.010), against 265/282 when the pair stays together.
>     At β = 0.6 the separated count is 0/318.
>   - The analytic sketch uses Song–Liang Thm 5: the masked variable has a zero within-split projection coefficient. The step
>     "PIP → 0" is not verified against the paper.

How to phrase the parallel-scaling claim so a referee accepts it (verbatim, §3.3):

> ### 3.3 How to phrase the parallel-scaling claim so a referee accepts it
> 1. **Define the cost model explicitly.** Unit = one score evaluation s(k).
>    - **Work** W = R·N·T·L_r·(p + B + 2)·s(K), plus tables Σ_b 2^{|C_b|}. Here L_r = move rounds per stage.
>    - **Depth** D = (table depth 2^B·s(B)) + T·L_r·(p + B + 2)·s(K) + T·O(log(RN)) for resampling.
>    - **Width** = R·N particles (and p/B blocks for the tables).
>    - State that D is **independent of R** and that R needs no communication. (Whiteley–Lee–Heine; Dai et al.)
> 2. **The carrying theorem.**
>    - "Depth = O(T·L_r·p)" combined with O-STAGES' T bounds gives D = O(p) on favourable BO, O(p log n) on proxy masking, and
>      O(p log log n) on LH masking (O-STAGES items 3 and 5). The constant L_r must be fixed by the method.
>    - T31(i) / Whiteley–Lee–Heine handles the error at fixed N as R → ∞: relative variance of pooled Ẑ = single-island
>      relative variance / R.
>    - What is **missing** is a bound on the single-island relative variance in the masked regime. Without it, "R → ∞ fixes
>      everything" may need exponential R (Whiteley et al.'s own warning).
> 3. **Do not claim depth O(T) unless the kernel changes.**
>    - Option A (no method change): phrase the claim as "depth = T stages of p-step rounds; T = O(1)–O(log n) by O-STAGES".
>    - Option B (method change): make rounds parallel within a particle, e.g. informed or tempered-Gibbs moves that score all
>      p neighbours at once. Then D = O(T·L_r·log p), and "depth = stage count up to log p" becomes true.
>    - Either way, compare with parallelised LIT-MH, whose depth is O(n log p).
> 4. **What to measure.**
>    - Strong scaling: wall time and error vs number of workers at fixed total work.
>    - Weak scaling: R grows with workers, error ∝ 1/R.
>    - Report T vs n and p for S1–S6. Report the critical path in score evaluations, not only wall time.
>    - Report single-island relative variance of Ẑ (the 1/R constant).
>    - Report the comparator ZYVR LIT-MH with parallel neighbour scoring: iterations × log p.
> 5. **Wording to avoid:**
>    - "methods with guarantees are sequential";
>    - "no analogue speed-up for MCMC";
>    - "first parallel exact BVS";
>    - "depth = T" without the per-round factor.
> 6. **Wording that survives:**
>    - "We know of no BVS method that targets the exact posterior, scales out in communication-free width with consistent
>      Ẑ-weighted pooling, and has a stage-count (depth) bound proved on a correlated design with a masked start.
>      Feature-splitting methods with guarantees require cross-split faithfulness or weak correlation."
>    - Plus the citations of §2.

- Earlier versions / repairs: the HQ framing at [pos 1038] stated "Methods that come with guarantees are sequential" (RF268) and "the only sequential part is the stage count" (RF269); LIT-PAR replaced them by the three-part S-GAP and the depth = T L (p+B+2) accounting. Single-island relative variance of Zhat in the masked regime is left open ("the theorem a referee will ask for", §6).
- Status history: proposed by Felipe/HQ as a thesis [pos 1030, 1038, 1044] -> LIT-PAR verdict "TRUE WITH QUALIFICATIONS" [pos 1070, 1107] -> input to THM-SYNTH D3 (Theorem CD) and Felipe's objective list [pos 1153] -> MEET-THM: Thesis CD is "a scoped remark" (K96); the Song-Liang analytic separation is FUTURE_WORK FW21.
- Proved by / checked by: LIT-PAR author (Opus 5.5) only; sources listed in §8 of the report (local PDFs, arXiv PDFs; Song-Liang JRSS-B text NOT read, only Liang's slides; later read by THM-INV from the PDF in `theory_campaign/inputs/`).
- Depends on: ⟦Song-Liang 2015⟧ (cited), TH120 (T31(i)), ⟦O-STAGES⟧, CJ118 (T38), TH417 (Theorem SL), TH399 (Prop D).
- Feeds: Thesis CD (K96, remark only); M8 Proposition D remark (K90); FUTURE_WORK FW21.

### RF269 — "Sequential depth: the only sequential part is the stage count" (depth = T)  [refuted claim]

- Source of the claim: HQ framing [pos 1038] (quoted above); refutation: `LIT-PAR/REPORT.md` §1 item 4 and `METH-AUDIT/REPORT.md` §7 first bullet; positions: [pos 1038], [pos 1070], [pos 1072], [pos 1107].
- Refutation (verbatim, LIT-PAR §1 item 4):

> 4. **Self-critique: v3's per-particle depth is Θ(p) score evaluations per move round, not O(1).**
>    - A round is p + B + 2 elementary steps run sequentially within each particle.
>    - So "depth = stage count T" holds only if a round counts as one unit. Counted in score evaluations, the depth is
>      T·L·(p + B + 2).
>    - That is worse in p than a parallelised ZYVR chain. Either state the depth honestly, or change the move kernel
>      (§3.3; method decision for HQ).

HQ relay of the self-critique at [pos 1072] (verbatim):

> ### The issue that matters most for the method decision
> In v3, each particle's move round is a Gibbs sweep through all p variables, one after another. So the sequential depth is not just T stages: counted in score evaluations it is T × rounds × (p + B + 2), which grows linearly in p. That cuts against the "go higher in p" thesis, and it is exactly the kind of real issue that would justify a change. Likely options are scoring flips in parallel within a particle (an informed or multiple-flip proposal), or stating the depth honestly. The first would change the move kernel, which is a workhorse change.

- Replacement: Prop D depth (I+2)(T+L+4)(p+B+2) score evaluations at island level (TH399, M8); the only fix (informed or tempered-Gibbs moves scoring all p neighbours, Option B / C10) was rejected as a WORKHORSE change that breaks the Gibbs-path theorems (METH-AUDIT §4). Cost: about 2-3 ms per round at p = 500 (METH-AUDIT §6, not committed).

### Block — METH-AUDIT: is v3 parallel-friendly enough to ship? (Opus 5.5, cap $15, spent $5.89)

Summary: METH-AUDIT (launched [pos 1068, 1072], 2026-11-03 13:32 UTC; reported [pos 1085, 1103, 1107]) was Felipe's "Track A": evaluate whether the methodology is as parallel-friendly as it has to be, with changes allowed only if they address real issues (theorems breaking down or parallel orientation) [pos 1051, 1055, 1061]. It produced a work/depth map (18 components), a theorem-robustness table under parallel execution, a candidate-change table C0-C11 (classes ADDITIVE, POST HOC, LAW-PRESERVING, WORKHORSE), a recommendation (ship v3 unchanged + a five-part parallel execution layer, "v3.1"), and `PROOFS.md` (Lemma S, Prop W, W-cal, Cor W-R, Prop P, Cor V, Prop D). HQ adopted the recommendation as the method decision [pos 1099, 1107, LEDGER 16:50 UTC] and Felipe's MEET-v31 meeting made it final (v3.1 approved 2026-11-04 02:05 UTC). The branch's `results/` folder was never committed and REPORT §6 stayed "[filled in after the runs; see results/]". Key statements are quoted in the items below.

HQ relay of the method decision, including what was decided against (verbatim, [pos 1107] §1):

> ## 1. Method: ship v3 unchanged, plus a parallel execution layer (call it v3.1)
> METH-AUDIT checked every theorem the paper relies on: none breaks under parallel execution, and none of the changes is a workhorse change. The study's 2,400 fits stand, and nothing needs to re-run now.
>
> The real problem is in the code, not the method. The production code is serial everywhere: islands, calibration islands, particles and local search all run one after another on one CPU. So as things stand, any parallel claim in the paper would describe code that doesn't exist.
>
> v3.1 adds:
> - **Islands run at the same time** as independent workers, for both the final run and calibration. The results are bit-for-bit identical to the serial run. That is proved by reading the code, and checked by running it on a small test problem and on one study design so far.
> - **Local-search scans run in parallel.**
> - **More islands, each at full particle count**, with the number fixed in advance. This can only improve results.
> - **The Ẑ-weighted PIP is reported.** Your methodology spec defines it, but the core code never computes it. It can be computed after the fact for all 2,400 fits. It is the PIP with a proved "more islands → correct" guarantee.
> - **The start-mode local search (LS0) is added to production.** It changed 0 of 2,394 study best models. It turns an already cross-checked selection theorem into one about the method we actually ship.
> - **A bug fix:** the evidence estimate (`log_Z`) on a stopped fit now shows NA instead of a misleading value.
>
> What I decided against:
> - **Splitting a fixed particle budget into many small islands.** It provably makes the equal-weight PIP worse.
> - **Shortening calibration.** It weakens three existing theorems.
> - **A new move kernel to cut the sequential cost per particle.** Each move round steps through all p variables in sequence, so its sequential cost grows with p. Changing that would break the move-path theorems. At p = 500 a round costs about 2–3 ms, so we keep the kernel and state the cost plainly.
>
> Against Song–Liang, measured in the same units, our sequential depth is of the same order in p, up to log factors. We need far more processors and total compute. In exchange, the output is correct under correlation. So the paper should not claim "faster than split-and-merge".
>
> For p well beyond the study, two further changes are planned for a later version. Per-particle random streams make depth independent of particle count. A scorer that doesn't store XᵀX handles p ≳ 30,000. Neither changes the target distribution or any theorem.
>
> **One correction.** The METH-AUDIT write-up says the bit-for-bit check passed on 3 of 3 study designs, but the run stopped after only one. On that design:
> - the bit-for-bit check passed;
> - running the 4 islands at once cut final-run time from 358 s to 189 s;
> - 32 small islands gave PIPs within 2×10⁻⁴ of the default.
>
> I'm re-running the other two designs on Owls now (about 30 minutes).

### LM226 — Lemma S (order independence of the bounded stores)  [lemma]

- Source (authoritative): `METH-AUDIT/PROOFS.md` "Lemma S"; positions: [pos 1085], [pos 1107], [pos 1177].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Statement.** Let `TopStore` have capacity c and strict total order ≺ on pairs (v, S), where v = v(S) is a deterministic
> function of S. Whatever the order in which a finite multiset M of pairs is offered, the final content is the set of the
> c ≺-best distinct pairs of M. Hence for any partition M = M₁ ∪ … ∪ M_R, top_c(M) = top_c(top_c(M₁) ∪ … ∪ top_c(M_R)).

Proof route (Summary: PROOFS.md): invariant after each offer, the store equals top_c(M_seen); duplicates rejected (v is a function of S); a full store rejects e if c seen pairs beat it (also for an evicted pair re-offered, since the worst stored element only improves); otherwise insert and erase the worst; the partition identity because top_c(M) is contained in the union of top_c(M_r). The running HPM (`offer_hpm`) is the case c = 1 under the order "larger F, then smaller |S|, then lexicographic" (`hpm_better`, `TopCmp`).
- Status history: PROVED (METH-AUDIT, candidate; code reference `v3_ledger.h:41-56`) -> used by Prop W (b) -> final MEET-THM K63 ("The HPM is the maximum of F under the strict total order (F, -|S|, lex) over the scored set, independent of scoring order, and top-c stores merge by union-then-truncate") -> S-OUT.
- Proved by / checked by: METH-AUDIT author; no independent check recorded; Lean-certifiable (THM-SYNTH V2).
- Depends on: none.
- Feeds: S-OUT (K63); M5 Theorem HPM (hypothesis K63).

### TH394 — Proposition W (worker equivalence of the final run; concurrent islands bitwise)  [proposition]

- Source (authoritative): `METH-AUDIT/PROOFS.md` "Proposition W"; REPORT §1 item 2; evidence `MEET-v31/evidence/2026-11-03_concurrency_runs.md` (copied from `METH-AUDIT/results/run_owls.log`); positions: [pos 1068], [pos 1085], [pos 1103], [pos 1107], [pos 1175], [pos 1241], [pos 1276].
- Statement (verbatim, setting and claims):

> **Setting.** Fixed data, seed s and 𝓒. The *serial run* is `cpp_final_run`: islands r = 1..R in order, one shared
> `ScoreCache` (capacity 500p, cleared when full) and one shared `Ledger` (tables ingested, then inherited models), then
> the final local search from the ledger's HPM. The *worker run* executes island r in worker r, in any order and with any
> overlap in time. Worker r uses stream σ_r, its own cache of the same capacity, and its own ledger with the tables ingested.
> Then it merges:
> - HPM := the ≻-maximum of the worker HPMs and the inherited HPM;
> - each store := top_c of the union of the worker stores and the inherited models;
> - the final local search runs from the merged HPM with `emit_centre = false`.
>
> **Claims.**
> (a) For every r, Ẑ_r, PIP̂_r·, the per-stage ESS, phi, log-increments, move counts and the terminal table are **bitwise**
> equal in the two runs.
> (b) The merged HPM and the merged stores (top 40p+1 by F, top 20p by log γ₀, top 20p by log γ₁) equal the serial
> ledger's just before the final local search. So the local-search path, the final HPM, the near-tie list, the MPM, the
> pooled Ẑ, the primary and Ẑ-weighted PIPs, and the final flags E1, E2, E3 and low_empirical_ESS are equal too.
> (c) Not equal: the cache counters, the fresh/logical score counters, and the time stamps. The HPM provenance is equal if
> the merge takes it from the inherited record when the HPM is inherited, and otherwise from the lowest-index worker whose
> HPM equals the merged HPM.

Proof route (Summary: PROOFS.md): (a) island r is `Engine::run_island_s`; its reads are the read-only setup, the grid and N, L, Hm, tier, uniforms from `E.vs` (a fresh `RngSource` seeded `seed_stream(s, 9+r)` per island in both runs), and `eval`, whose scorer is a deterministic function of the sorted model with no carried state, so the score sequence does not depend on the cache or on other islands; the ledger is write-only during an island and the runtime guard reads no RNG; so the whole island computation is the same function of the same inputs, bitwise given equal compiler flags (pinned by `Makevars.v3`). (b) A model is offered to a ledger iff it has a fresh evaluation in that ledger's run; by Lemma S the stores and HPM agree; the final local search is a deterministic function of its centre, l and the scores. (c) Provenance is the first running-best event, canonical as stated.

### TH396 — Corollary W-R (stacking)  [corollary]

- Source: `METH-AUDIT/PROOFS.md` "Corollary W-R"; PC1 claim 6; positions: [pos 1107], [pos 1242].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Corollary W-R (stacking).** Run R′ > 4 final islands, where islands 1–4 use streams 10–13 and island r > 4 uses a
> stream disjoint from 0–13, all with the same N_e and the same 𝓒. Then islands 1–4 are bitwise those of the R = 4 run. The
> scored set before the final local search contains that of the R = 4 run, and so the pre-local-search HPM is ⪰ the R = 4

> necessarily ⪰ the R = 4 run's *post*-local-search HPM. To make the reported HPM exactly monotone in R′, also run the
> local search from the R = 4 pre-local-search HPM (one extra search of ≤ (ℓ+1) scans). PROVED by Proposition W(a, b)
> and the definition of the HPM.

### RF272 and CE220 — post-search HPM is not monotone in the island count without the extra local search  [refuted claim; counterexample]

- Source: `MEET-v31/evidence/2026-11-03_PC1_proof_check.md` Claim 6; `MEET-v31/MINUTES.md` decision 5; positions: [pos 1242].
- The refuted claim: that nested pre-search scored sets give a post-search HPM monotone in R' (and "stacking never worsens the reported HPM"). Counterexample and refutation (verbatim, PC1):

> **Monotonicity without the extra search: FALSE. COUNTEREXAMPLE (`c6_ls.py`, `c6b_ls_downsets.py`).**
>
> Setup: the spec's m(S), the production local search (flips and swaps, centre frozen during each scan, best strict ≻-improvement, ≤ ℓ moves then one more scan, every evaluated model updates the best), seed 20261106. Data: n = 29, p = 8, K = 8, ℓ = 6, with y = x₀ + x₁ + noise and x₂ ≈ x₀ + x₁ (a proxy).
>
> Under flips and swaps there are exactly two local maxima:
> - {2}, with F = −34.843 (the proxy);
> - {0,1} = S₀ = S†, with F = −31.512.
>
> The two runs:
> - **R = 4 run.** Pre-search HPM c₄ = {0,1,2,3}, F = −35.789. The search path is {0,1,2,3} → {0,1,3} → {0,1}, so the post-search HPM is {0,1} = S₀.
> - **R′ run.** An extra island scores {2}, so c′ = {2}, with F = −34.843 and c′ ≻ c₄. {2} is a local maximum, so the search stops immediately and certifies it. {0,1} is not a flip or swap neighbour of {2}. The post-search HPM is {2} ≠ S₀.
>
> The counterexample survives the most generous nesting: the scored sets can be taken to be the whole down-sets {S ⪯ c₄} ⊂ {S ⪯ c′}. In that design, 3,813 of 32,640 ordered pairs (c₄ ≺ c′) give HPM(R′) ≺ HPM(4). Adding the search from c₄ restores {0,1}.
>
> This shows the deterministic implication "pre-search sets nested ⇒ post-search HPM monotone" is false. I did not prove that the actual SMC realises these particular scored sets with positive probability. It is plausible, given full-support π₀ proposals, but it is CANNOT DECIDE here. The same configuration also gives S₀ ∈ 𝒮⁺(4) but S₀ ∉ 𝒮⁺(R′), so the post-search scored set is not nested either.

- Replacement: Cor W-R (TH396) with the extra local search from c4; no listed theorem needs the post-search monotonicity (PC1: "The extra search is not needed for any listed theorem"); it matters only for monotonicity or transfer claims.
- Status: COUNTEREXAMPLE (PC1, same-family); "I did not prove that the actual SMC realises these particular scored sets with positive probability ... CANNOT DECIDE here".

### TH397 — Proposition P (pooling as R grows at fixed N; R fixed in advance)  [proposition]

- Source: `METH-AUDIT/PROOFS.md` "Proposition P"; positions: [pos 1107], [pos 1169] (Felipe-facing dossier plan), [pos 1177].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## Proposition P (pooling as R grows at fixed N). PROVED (elementary)
>
> **Setting.** Fixed data and 𝓒 fixed before the final streams. Islands are conditionally iid given 𝓒 (distinct streams,
> modelled as independent uniforms: EX-S). The island identities E[W_r | 𝓒] = 1 and
> E[W_r·PIP̂_rj | 𝓒] = PIP_j hold for every N ≥ 1 (P6/P7; W2-BOOK Prop. 2(a); the island identity of Prop. 2(c), VERIFIED
> by A-REV4). W_r ≤ c_N almost surely for a finite constant, because the state space is finite and the weights are bounded.
>
> (i) **Equal pooling does not improve its bias with R.** PIP^eq_j := R⁻¹ Σ_r PIP̂_rj → E[PIP̂_1j | 𝓒] a.s. as R → ∞
> (SLLN). So its limit error is the single-island bias b_j(N) := E[PIP̂_1j | 𝓒] − PIP_j. This bias depends on N and the
> regime, not on R.
>
> (ii) **Ẑ-weighted pooling is consistent in R.** PIP^zw_j := Σ_r W_r PIP̂_rj / Σ_r W_r → PIP_j a.s. as R → ∞ (SLLN on
> numerator and denominator). This is T31(i). [Literature: Whiteley–Lee–Heine 2016 §5.1; Dai et al. 2022 (4.8); cite as
> standard (LIT-PAR).]
>
> (iii) **Non-asymptotic form with a regime-free numerator.** Let e_r ∈ [0, 1] be any island error, for example
> e_r = max_j |PIP̂_rj − 1{j ∈ S₀}|, and let ε := E[W_r e_r | 𝓒]. Then for s ∈ (0, 1) and t > 0:
>
>   P(max_j |PIP^zw_j − 1{j∈S₀}| > t | 𝓒) ≤ exp{−R(1−s)²/(2E[W_1² | 𝓒])} + ε/(s t).
>
> *Proof.* max_j |PIP^zw_j − 1{j∈S₀}| ≤ Σ_r W_r e_r / Σ_r W_r, because a convex combination of deviations is bounded by
> the same combination of their maxima. On {W̄_R ≥ s} this is ≤ (R⁻¹ Σ W_r e_r)/s, and Markov's inequality gives
> P(R⁻¹ Σ W_r e_r > s t) ≤ ε/(s t). For the lower tail of W̄_R, use Maurer's (2003) inequality for iid nonnegative
> variables: P(E W − W̄_R ≥ u) ≤ exp{−R u²/(2 E W²)}, here with E W = 1 and u = 1 − s. ∎
>
> With F-MASKPIP M1, ε ≤ δ₁ + ρ̄ + u_π for every island, every regime and every frozen grid (VERIFIED by A-REV9). So the
> **Ẑ-weighted PIP is accurate in the masked regime once R ≳ 2 E[W²] log(1/η)/(1−s)²**. The number of islands needed
> scales with the single-island relative second moment E[W²] = 1 + Var(Ẑ_r/Z | 𝓒). This is the precise sense of
> "correlation costs islands, never correctness". For the equal-weight PIP no such statement holds: by (i), its limit
> keeps the single-island bias. In the masked regime that bias is bounded away from 0 whenever a non-crossing island has
> probability ≥ κ > 0 (F-MASKPIP N(a)).
>
> *Caveat (honest).* E[W²] can be exponentially large in the masked regime. Then the R needed is impractical, and
> Proposition P is a correctness statement, not an efficiency statement. It does not replace DELIV-POP.
>
> (iv) **Pooled-product bias with R islands.** E[Ẑ·PIP^eq_j | 𝓒] − Z·PIP_j = −(1 − 1/R)·Cov(Ẑ_1, PIP̂_1j | 𝓒). This
> is Prop. 2(c) with ¾ replaced by 1 − 1/R. *Proof:* expand E[(R⁻¹ Σ_r Ẑ_r)(R⁻¹ Σ_s PIP̂_sj)] over the R diagonal and
> R(R−1) off-diagonal terms, using independence and the island identity. ∎
>
> (v) **Unbiasedness, the 95% bound and fixed R.** Pooled Ẑ = R⁻¹ Σ Ẑ_r is conditionally unbiased for every R fixed
> before the final randomness, and P(0.05·Ẑ > Z | 𝓒) ≤ 0.05 by Markov. If R is chosen *adaptively* from final-run outputs,
> for example "add islands until the SE is small", unbiasedness can fail. This is the same mechanism as W2-BOOK's
> CEX-guard, where data-dependent stopping biases E[Ẑ | output]. **Rule: R (or the stacking schedule) must be fixed
> before any final-run randomness.**

- Earlier versions / repairs: the spec's secondary (Zhat-weighted) PIP of METHODOLOGY §6.11 is "not computed by the core (`v3_run.R`)" (gap found by METH-AUDIT §9); MEET-v31 decision 8 makes the Zhat-weighted PIP primary and the equal-weight PIP secondary, POST HOC ("the only PIP with a consistency-in-R theorem, Prop P(ii), T31(i)").
- Status history: PROVED (elementary) (METH-AUDIT) -> THM-SYNTH V3 (settles THM-INV D4: Verge for (i), WLH for (ii)) -> PC1 consulted only through quoted statements -> MEET-THM S-POOL / L-PROPP, flagged AUTHOR-ONLY (IDX 70).
- Proved by / checked by: METH-AUDIT; input F-MASKPIP M1 XF VERIFIED (A-REV9); Maurer (2003) cited.
- Depends on: TH300 (FMP-M1), ⟦island identity E[W_r PIPhat_rj | C] = PIP_j⟧ (P6/P7; W2-BOOK Prop. 2(a); A-REV4), CE175 (CEX-guard).

### TH398 — Corollary V (same total particles, R islands)  [corollary]

- Source: `METH-AUDIT/PROOFS.md` "Corollary V"; positions: [pos 1107].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## Corollary V (same total particles, R islands). PROOF SKETCH
>
> From O-PW2 Theorem A (exact; VERIFIED by A-REV9): N_r·Var(W | 𝓒) = Σ_{s<T} (1 − 1/N_r)^{T−1−s} (E[W_s² μ_s(h²_{s,T})] − 1)
> for an island of N_r particles. The pooled variance with R islands of N_r = N/R particles is Var(W)/R. Then:
> - To leading order in 1/N_r (O-PW2 Theorem B), N·Var(Ẑ_pooled/Z) = Σ_s (1 − R/N)^{T−1−s} σ²_{s,T} + O(R/N)^{1/2}·(…).
> - The leading constant does not increase with R.
> - The remainder grows as N_r shrinks.
> - In the exact-refresh idealisation, Var(W) = Π_t(1 + χ²_t/N_r) − 1, so R·N_r fixed is neutral while Σ_t χ²_t ≪ N_r.
>   With the grid's restricted χ²_t ≈ 1/9 and T ≈ 25, Σ χ²_t ≈ 3 ≪ 312 = 10,000/32.
>
> **Crux not verified:** the stage quantities V_s and H_{s,T} of O-PW2 Theorem B are not re-derived here. The
> full-space χ²_t can exceed the restricted value the grid controls (METHODOLOGY §6.7 "Limits"). The masked regime is
> outside the leading-order regime.

- Status history: PROOF SKETCH (METH-AUDIT; "Crux not verified") -> THM-SYNTH D4 tiered v2 -> FUTURE_WORK FW9 (K59). METH-AUDIT §8 item 2: "needs O-PW2 Theorem B's V_s and H_{s,T} written out, and a check that the full-space chi^2_t stays small at N_r about 300".

### TH399 — Proposition D (depth with particle-parallel islands; work / depth / width of v3.1)  [proposition]

- Source (authoritative): `METH-AUDIT/PROOFS.md` "Proposition D"; REPORT §2 (work/depth map, totals); LIT-PAR §3.3 (cost model); positions: [pos 1038], [pos 1072], [pos 1107], [pos 1177].
- Statement (verbatim):

> ## Proposition D (depth with particle-parallel islands). PROVED (counting, given the code's structure)
>
> Let m = p + B + 2, s̄ be the mean score cost, I_e ≤ ℓ the rebuild iterations, T_pil and T the pilot and final stage
> counts, and T^(i) the stage count of the grid used at rebuild i. Assume one worker per particle per island, with
> synchronisation only at reweight/resample, at the end of an island, and between calibration phases. Then the critical
> path, in score evaluations, is
>
>   D = D_setup + Σ_{tiers e} [ (T_pil + L + 4) + Σ_{i=1}^{I_e} (T^(i) + L + 4) ] m + (T + L + 4) m
>       + (number of local searches)·(ℓ + 1)·⌈scan / width⌉ + O((T_pil + Σ_i T^(i) + T) log N)
>
> plus the grid constructions (≤ 60 |V| T_e log-sum-exps each, scalar and sequential, or log-depth if parallelised over V).
> Here D_setup is the depth of the Gram, the clustering, the tables and the convolution. **D does not depend on N, H or R.**
> With T ≤ T_e = max(1000, ℓ²), I_e ≤ ℓ and L = O(log n), this gives D = O(m·ℓ·T_e) = O(p log³(n + p)) score evaluations
> as the worst case on success. The work W = O(N·m·(ℓ + 2)·T_e) matches the A-REV6 candidate cost bound
> O(max(n,p)·p·log³(n+p) + p² log²(n+p)) (V19) when N ∝ max(n, p).
>
> *Proof.* Within a stage the N particle rounds are independent given the resampled population and their uniforms
> (IND-T(a) / EX-S). Each round is m sequential elementary steps, each with at most one fresh score, plus a π₀ draw of
> O(J + K) operations. Reweighting is an N-term log-sum-exp, and multinomial resampling is a prefix sum plus N
> lookups: O(log N) depth each. The calibration phases are sequential by construction: the pilot schedule feeds V and the
> grid, and each rebuild's grid feeds the next diagnostics. A local-search scan's evaluations are independent given the
> centre. Summing the stages gives D. ∎
>
> *Remark (honest, after LIT-PAR §3.3).* Measured in score evaluations, the depth carries the factor m = p + B + 2 per
> round. Removing it needs a different kernel, which is a WORKHORSE change. In wall-clock terms m·s̄ ≈ 2–3 ms at p = 500
> (REPORT §6), so the factor is not a practical obstacle at study scale or far beyond it.

> R islands; T the final grid's stage count; T_pil the pilot's stage count; I_e ≤ ℓ the rebuild iterations; L burn-in rounds;
> 4 measured rounds; ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉; s(k) the cost of one score at size k (O(k³) from the Gram); s̄ its mean along the
> path; k̄ the typical model size.

> **Memory per worker** at n = 200, p = 500 (B = 14): X 0.8 MB, G 2 MB, tables ≈ J·2^B·8 B ≈ 5 MB, cache ≈ 250,000 entries
> × (29 + 4k̄) B ≈ 20 MB, population < 1 MB. That is about 30 MB, so dozens of workers fit on any node. Each worker needs
> the full G (or X), because every Gibbs round touches every coordinate. This is the price of targeting the exact
> posterior, against Song–Liang, where a worker holds n × p/K. Mitigation: G is read-only and shared by threads or by
> forked processes (copy-on-write), so a node holds one copy. Across nodes, 8p² bytes is 0.8 GB at p = 10⁴ and 80 GB at
> p = 10⁵. Beyond about p ≈ 3·10⁴ a Gram-free scorer (G_S from X at O(n k²) per score; the `chol_refactor` route already
> does this) would be needed. That change is LAW-PRESERVING up to floating point, and it is not needed at study size.

> ### 2.2 Totals
>
> Score-evaluation units:
>
> - **Work**: W ≈ J 2^B s(B) + Σ_e [H_e (T_pil + L + 4) + 4 H_e Σ_i (T^(i) + L + 4)] m s̄ + R N_e (T + L + 4) m s̄
>   + n_LS (ℓ+1)(p + k̄(p−k̄)) s̄ + O(np²) + O(p²)–O(p³).
> - **Depth, v3 as coded** (serial): D = W.
> - **Depth, v3.1 PEL** (islands, diagnostic islands and scans concurrent; particles serial within an island):
>   D_PEL ≈ D_setup + Σ_e [H_e (T_pil + L + 4) + H_e Σ_i (T^(i) + L + 4)] m s̄ + N_e (T + L + 4) m s̄ + n_LS (ℓ+1) s̄.
> - **Depth, particle-parallel** (Proposition D): D_PP ≈ D_setup + [(T_pil + L + 4) + Σ_i (T^(i) + L + 4) + (T + L + 4)] m s̄
>   + O(ΣT·log N). This is free of N, H and R. Worst case on success: O(p log³(n+p)).
>
> Measured at study size: §6 Table 6.2.
>
> **Comparison with Song–Liang §6.** Their wall-time bound, with K_n = √p processors, is O(p^{(1+α)/2}) + O(np). The first
> term comes from T = O((p/K)^α) SAMC iterations per subset, each costing O(p/K). That α is a *choice* (α = 1 in the paper),
> not a mixing guarantee: their sampler theory is "by citing SAMC convergence" (METHODOLOGY §11). Their total work is
> O(p^{1+α/2} + n p^{3/2}) on √p workers, and the output is a posterior restricted to the merged set. Ours, on width R·N:
> - depth O(p·(ℓ+2)(T+L+4)) score evaluations, with T bounded by proved grid results: O(1) favourable, log₂n + O(1) under
>   proxy masking, O(log log n) on LH (O-STAGES, Theorem G), and ≤ T_e always;
> - work O(N p (ℓ+2) T_e);
> - output: the exact posterior (Ẑ unbiased, Ẑ-weighted PIPs consistent in R).
>
> So **our depth is of the same order in p as theirs at α = 1, up to logarithmic factors**. We need far more width
> (R·N ≈ 10⁴ particles, against √p ≈ 22 subsets) and far more total work. What we gain is correctness under correlation.
> That is an honest trade, and the paper should state it in exactly these units. Do not claim "faster than SaM".

### TH400 — METH-AUDIT theorem robustness under parallel execution  [proposition]

- Source: `METH-AUDIT/REPORT.md` §3, §10; positions: [pos 1107].
- Statement (verbatim, introduction of §3 and the list of changing hypotheses; the per-result table is in the source):

> ## 3. Theorem robustness under parallel execution
>
> Columns:
> - (i) the final run uses R ≫ 4 islands. Two readings: (i-a) *stacked*, with N_e per island unchanged; (i-b) *split*, with
>   smaller N and R·N fixed.
> - (ii) islands run concurrently with independent streams.
> - (iii) calibration is shared or shortened.
> - (iv) Ẑ-weighted versus equal pooling.
>
> ✓ = holds verbatim. ✓R = holds with "4" read as R. ⚠ = a hypothesis changes (stated).

> **Which hypotheses change, in one list.**
> 1. Every "4 islands" becomes "R islands, R fixed before final randomness".
> 2. Prop 2(c)'s ¾ becomes 1 − 1/R.
> 3. VAL-FP's ε scales with total work.
> 4. Under a split, DELIV inside an island depends on N_r (OPEN).
> 5. A shortened calibration touches (b1′) (through H₀), Theorem G and (0_H) (through P(S₀ ∈ V) and 𝒮_cal), and nothing
>    else.
> 6. Particle-level parallelism (not needed for (i)–(iv)) would restate IND-T as "uniforms of distinct (island, stage,
>    particle) triples are independent". The REP product form uses exactly this, so the theorems are unaffected.

- Status: "medium-high (registry-level reading of T26 Theorem A and T38 parts; not re-proved)" (confidence card); bookkeeping.
- Proved by / checked by: METH-AUDIT only.
- Depends on: all rows of the table (T12, Prop 2, T26, T38, O-STAGES, MASKZPIP, F-MASKPIP M1/M2, O-PW2, Thm 4/N200, Lemma RO, IND-T).
- Feeds: none as a card; MEET-v31 grounds for rejecting C9 (shortened calibration) and C8 (splitting N_e).

The candidate-change table C0-C11 (classes ADDITIVE / POST HOC / LAW-PRESERVING / WORKHORSE) is in METH-AUDIT REPORT §4; recommendation, what fails and escalations (verbatim, METH-AUDIT §5, §7, §8):

> ## 5. RECOMMENDATION
>
> **Ship v3.1 = v3 (unchanged statistical method: start, bridge, kernel, schedule rule, budgets N_e = max(2500, n, p), H_e,
> T_e, HPM decision, flags) + a parallel execution layer.** The layer has five parts:
> - **(a)** final islands as concurrent workers, each with its own cache and ledger, merged by Lemma S before the final
>   local search (C1);
> - **(b)** the calibration's 4 diagnostic islands as persistent concurrent workers, merged before each local search and V
>   build (C2);
> - **(c)** local-search scans evaluated in parallel with the lexicographic max-reduction (C3);
> - **(d)** optional island stacking R′ = 4k at N_e. Islands 1–4 stay on streams 10–13 and define v3's flags. R′ is fixed
>   before final randomness, and an extra local search runs from the islands-1–4 centre (C4);
> - **(e)** the Ẑ-weighted PIP computed and reported next to the equal-weight PIP (C5). The R-scaling guarantee is
>   stated for it.
>
> Parts (a)–(c) are bitwise-neutral on completed fits, (d) is nested, and (e) is post hoc. So the 2,400-fit study stands
> as v3.1's study at R′ = 4, with no re-run. (A final run with stacked islands, re-run once at the end, can only improve
> it.) Per-particle streams (C6) and the Gram-free scorer (C7) are a declared v3.2 path for p well beyond the study. They
> preserve the law and change no theorem. Do not split N_e across more islands (C8), do not shorten calibration (C9), and
> do not change the kernel for depth (C10).

> ## 6. Evidence

> ## 7. What fails and why
>
> - **"Depth = T stages" without the round factor fails.** The kernel is a p-step random-order Gibbs round, so per-stage
>   depth is m = p + B + 2 sequential score evaluations at best (Proposition D; LIT-PAR §3.3). The only fix is a kernel
>   change (C10), which breaks the Gibbs-path theorems. Rejected. The honest statement is
>   depth = (I + 2)(T + L + 4)·m score evaluations with T bounded by O-STAGES/Theorem G.
> - **"More islands always helps" fails for the equal-weight PIP under a split.** Proposition P(i): its limit is the
>   single-island mean, so its bias is set by N per island. Shrinking N to add islands (C8) makes it worse. The measured
>   difference at R = 32 × 312 (§6) is small on these designs, but the theorem gives no protection.
> - **Island-level parallelism alone does not scale p.** Depth under C1–C4 is ∝ N_e, and N₀ = max(2500, n, p). So for
>   p > 2500 the depth grows like p²·T. Particle-level parallelism (C6) is needed there, and it cannot be bitwise-identical
>   to the serial stream map. This is why C6 is LAW-PRESERVING, not ADDITIVE.
> - **Shortening calibration is not a parallel fix.** Calibration depth is (1 + I_e) island-depths. C2 cuts it 4-fold
>   bitwise, and C6 makes it N-free. Cutting rebuilds or H would touch T38(b1′) (H₀ in NB′), Theorem G (S₀ ∈ V) and (0_H)
>   (𝒮_cal), so C9 is rejected.
> - **A per-fit adaptive R is not allowed.** "Stack islands until the SE is small" breaks conditional unbiasedness
>   (Prop. P(v)), so R′ must be declared in advance.
> - **Not done:** the bitwise replay of the calibration (W-cal is code reading only), the law check for C6, and the full
>   10-design test (NOTS script provided, not run).

> ## 8. Needs escalation
>
> 1. **Proposition W / W-cal** need an independent code check of the claim that "the ledger is write-only during an
>    island" and of the claim that the scorer has no state between calls. My evidence is code reading plus 4/4 bitwise
>    executions (smoke + 3 designs), and the calibration version is not executed. API-AUDIT-style referee: cheap.
> 2. **Corollary V** (split neutrality to first order) is a PROOF SKETCH. It needs O-PW2 Theorem B's V_s and H_{s,T} written
>    out, and a check that the full-space χ²_t stays small at N_r ≈ 300.
> 3. **DELIV under a split** (T38(b2) with smaller islands): OPEN. It is relevant only if C8 is ever adopted.
> 4. **Prop. P(iii)'s practical scope:** in the masked regime E[W²] can be exponentially large. A referee should judge
>    whether the paper may phrase the Ẑ-weighted PIP result as "correctness at a cost in islands" without a bound on E[W²].

## Part D. THM-INV: the component-to-theorem map, the theorem ledger and the gaps (2026-11-03)

Summary: THM-INV (Opus, cap $12, spent $7.99; launched [pos 1068, 1072]; reported [pos 1103, 1107]) was Felipe's "Track B" step 1: "you will understand all components of the methodology ... extract all information of the literature search ... then ... add / remove theorems" [pos 1055]. It built (§1) a component-to-theorem map (14 components x validity / accuracy / cost / failure modes), (§2) a theorem ledger (about 34 rows with status verbatim, "Run" = as run vs idealisation, and the literature verdict) with ten flagged disagreements D1-D10, (§3) coverage tables against the proposal targets, Song-Liang and Felipe's three objectives, (§4) a 10-work primary-source pass on composite likelihood and diagnostics, (§5) twelve properties with no guarantee yet, and digests of REG, API, AREV, LIT, SL and LITGAP. Statuses are copied from the sources; the digests were written by Sonnet workers and "spot-checked ..., not line-checked". The ledger rows are the registry of Themes 1-11 and are not repeated; this section keeps the headline, the observations, the disagreements, the coverage tables and the gaps, which are the claims of the branch itself. Key statements are quoted in the items below.

Observations on the component map and the ledger (verbatim):

> **Observations.**
> - Nearly every positive theorem about the *algorithm* (rows 5–12) is either idealised or about a design the study did not use. The idealisations are a frozen calibration, iid final draws, an ideal grid, LS0, exact-Gram LH and fixed p. The study's designs (groups of 5, p ≫ n) are uncovered.
> - The only results that hold for the algorithm exactly as run, at every n, are bookkeeping:
>   - T07, T21(C1), N200 Lemma 1 and Thm N200, Theorem G;
>   - the T12/T31 identities, given the frozen calibration;
>   - Lemma RO and the per-fit certificates.

Disagreements flagged by THM-INV (verbatim, §2):

> **Disagreements to resolve (flagged).**
> - **D1: API-POS vs LIT-MCMC on rapid mixing.** The two reports agree that no published rapid-mixing theorem covers *our* prior and target as stated. They differ on why:
>   - API-POS puts the obstruction on the prior side (g = n, κ, cap ⌊n/2⌋). It expects a YWJ-style proof for our prior to "very likely succeed", and calls the gap "formal, not substantive".
>   - LIT-MCMC computes that the sufficient condition R > M fails at n = 200 and 1,600 on LH, and at study scale in 12/12 data sets (by a factor ≥ p^0.87). It concludes the unimodal-ratio route *cannot* certify our target.
>   - LIT-VENUE §1.3 says "R > M … since on LH S₀ is the unique local mode". LIT-MCMC's computation contradicts this: unimodality (R > 1) does not give R > M.
>   - **Reading:** both can be right. LIT-MCMC refutes a *sufficient condition*, not fast mixing, and API-POS's claim is a CONJECTURE. The paper should not say either "covered" or "not coverable". It needs an independent check (§6).
> - **D4: LIT-SMC vs LIT-PAR on island pooling.** LIT-SMC cites Vergé et al. as covering our identities; LIT-PAR calls Vergé "plain averaging" and contrasts it with Ẑ-weighted pooling. Both call T31(i) standard.
> - **D5: the size of μ⋆ under a masked start.** LIT-SMC and LIT-MCMC say "polynomially small"; LIT-PAR says "exponentially small" (Mathews–Schmidler).
> - **D6: Thm 6 / T26 novelty.** LIT-SMC says "no analogue"; LIT-VENUE says "standard pattern".
> - **D9: citation details that differ across reports.**
>   - Shin–Bhattacharya–Johnson venue: JASA (LIT-STAT) vs Statistica Sinica (LIT-VENUE).
>   - Le Fay–Chopin–Vihola theorem number: Thm 3.2 vs Thm 3.4.
>   - YWJ's size-cap constant is quoted three ways.
>   - All of these should be checked against the primary sources before printing.
> - **D10: Song–Liang's correlation condition.**
>   - Settled against the text (SL digest). Condition 5 ("|cov(x_t, y)| > 0 for any true predictor") justifies the iterative stage-1 step. Theorem 4 / Corollary 2 with eq. (19) is what retains a true predictor: it is retained only if its population projection coefficient β₀,t on the subset is nonzero.
>   - Masking can break both: cov(x_t, y) = 0 for a cancelled pair, and β₀,t = 0 when its partner sits in another split.
>   - LIT-PAR's "Thm 5" label and "read from slides" caveat should be replaced by this citation.

Properties of the method with no guarantee yet (verbatim, §5) — the source of CJ298-CJ302:

> ## 5. Properties of our method with no guarantee yet (ordered by importance to the goal)
>
> 1. **Accuracy of posterior expectations E_π[h(S)] as n grows, in the masked (study) regime.** This covers joint inclusion probabilities, functionals, and PIPs at p ≫ n. Nothing exists beyond the favourable-regime CONJECTURE (T26) and LH at fixed p (P1–P3). This is proposal §13.1 and Felipe's objective (1).
> 2. **Two-sided relative accuracy of Ẑ in the masked regime.** Only the lower-tail mechanism is PROVED; the resolved-grid half is a CONJECTURE (OPEN for c ≥ 2). LIT-PAR calls the single-island relative variance "the theorem a referee will ask for".
> 3. **A parallel work/depth theorem.** We need depth as a function of p, correlation and masking, and an R-versus-N trade-off. This is the formal content of "correlation costs depth and particles, never correctness". Today we have only total work (T32(i)) and stage counts in the favourable or ideal-grid cases (Theorem G, STG-M). Note LIT-PAR's warning that per-round depth is Θ(p).
> 4. **Delivery of output: P(U) → 0.** No theorem bounds P(resource_limit), P(schedule_limit), P(numerical_failure) or P(grid_unconverged). Every consistency statement is joint with "output exists".
> 5. **Masked-regime selection consistency for the production method on non-LH or random designs, including the study's own generator** (groups of 5 packed by next-fit, p ≫ n). The verified routes are only (b1) with LS0, which is not in production, and (b2-LH), an exact-Gram subfamily.
> 6. **Finite-n guarantees.** These are an upper bound on Π(X) (OPEN) and a finite-n discovery bound for the Gibbs route (OPEN). All asymptotic results are vacuous at n = 200.
> 7. **Mixing of the φ = 1 move round (V10).** No published or project theorem covers our prior. The rapid-mixing route is blocked as stated (D1).
> 8. **Positive power of the diagnostics and flags.** Is there any condition under which a flag fires when the output is wrong? All theory is negative (V12, E1c).
> 9. **Calibration behaviour.** Nothing covers convergence of the rebuild loop, the probability that V contains the competing pair, or the stage count T_n in the masked regime (Conjecture P OPEN).
> 10. **Partition law for the actual adaptive packing**, and the effect of block construction (B, linkage, overlap or random partitions) on cost.
> 11. **Floating-point accuracy at production size.** VAL-FP was measured at p ≤ 40 only, and there is no floating-point theorem.
> 12. **Exactness of the composite start sampler, and reversibility and self-adjointness of the move round (V5).** These hold by construction and were consultant-checked, but I found no registry theorem (?). They are routine, but a paper claim needs a written proof or a citation.

## Part E. THM-SYNTH: the final theorem list for paper 1 (G1-G6, 19-item list, tiers) (2026-11-03)

Summary: THM-SYNTH (Fable, cap $25, spent $8.4; launched [pos 1099-1102] after METH-AUDIT, THM-INV and LIT-PAR; delivered [pos 1177, 1182, 1185]; re-read at the theorem meeting [pos 1343, 1441]) produced `THEOREM_LIST.md` (the list, fields (i) statement, (ii) plainly, (iii) status, (iv) novelty, (v) difficulty and route, (vi) Lean, (vii) dependencies, and a tier v1 = Biometrika paper / v2 = later), `HQ_PLAN.md` (seven v1 HQs, nine v2 HQs, dependency graph, Lean plan) and `REPORT.md`. The method assumed is v3.1 = v3 + the METH-AUDIT parallel layer + LS0. "No new proofs": every status is copied; three statements are NEW-SYNTH (proposed, PROOF SKETCH at most): Theorem H, Lemma KL, Theorem SL. The list has six groups: G1 validity under parallel execution (V1-V4), G2 posterior accuracy (A1-A4), G3 parallel work and depth (D1-D4), G4 why the bridge, why the merge alone fails (S1-S4), G5 correlation robustness versus split-and-merge (C1), G6 selection accuracy of the reported output (R1-R7). The REPORT headline counts "19 items in six groups ... of which 14 are theorems/propositions and 5 are cited lemmas or dropped"; the summary table in THEOREM_LIST has 23 rows (V1-V4, A1-A4, D1-D4, S1-S3, C1, R1-R7). **UNCERTAIN:** 19 (REPORT, ledger) versus 23 table rows; the REPORT does not say which rows are excluded (probably the limitation/v2 rows R6, R7 and the dropped S3 and the cited-lemma rows).

> ## 1. Headline

>    deterministic cap T ≤ T_e, not for the as-coded masked stage count (OPEN); selection is covered on exact-Gram LH, not on
>    the study's generator.
> 2. **What is KNOWN—CITE and becomes a cited lemma, not a theorem:** SMC invariance/consistency and unbiased Ẑ (Del Moral et
>    al.; T12), Ẑ-weighted island pooling (Whiteley–Lee–Heine; T31(i)), the Markov 95% bound, plain-averaging bias (Vergé),
>    greedy-schedule optimality G(i) (Štefankovič–Vempala–Vigoda), the fine-grid length law (Syed et al.), the exp(KL)
>    sample size (Chatterjee–Diaconis), the 2E₀δ₁ term (Rossell Prop. 1), the Bayes rules (Barbieri–Berger). The list
>    says so at every such item.
> 3. **The thesis sentence is a theorem in a stated scope (§3): fixed data for "never correctness"; ideal grid + T_e cap
>    for "costs depth"; a non-asymptotic island bound with E[W²|𝓒] for "costs particles"; exact-Gram LH for the selection
>    half and for the split-and-merge contrast.** Outside that scope the paper may use the wording in §3.3.

>    both right, different poolings), D5 (μ⋆: polynomially small on LH at fixed c; ≈ 10⁻¹² on the study designs, scaling with
>    the number of invisible truths, not "exponentially small" without saying in what), D6 (T26: standard pattern; its new

### TH411 — Theorem V (V1): fixed-data validity of v3.1 for any island count  [theorem]

- Source (authoritative): `THM-SYNTH/THEOREM_LIST.md` V1; `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §2-§3; positions: [pos 1099], [pos 1177], [pos 1185].
- Statement (verbatim; hypotheses named in the source):

> ### V1. Theorem V (fixed-data validity of v3.1 for any island count)
>
> **(i) Statement.** Fix data (X, y), a seed-independent calibration 𝓒 (grid 0 = φ₀ < … < φ_T = 1, L, N = N_e, V,
> tier) produced on streams 0–9 (CAL), and an island count R and stacking schedule declared before any final-run
> randomness. Assume EX-A and EX-S. Islands r = 1, …, R run N iid π₀ draws through the frozen bridge with multinomial
> resampling and the q_t-invariant round kernels K_t (reversibility of each elementary move and self-adjointness of the
> random-order round: METHODOLOGY_v3 §6.5, V5). Let W_r := Ẑ_r/Z and let ĥ_r be island r's measured-round estimate of a
> bounded h: Ω → ℝ (for h = 1{j ∈ S} the Rao–Blackwellised PIP̂_rj). Then, conditionally on 𝓒:
> (a) E[W_r] = 1 and E[W_r ĥ_r] = π(h) for every N ≥ 1 and every r (islandwise identities);
> (b) E[Ẑ] = Z for Ẑ = R⁻¹Σ_r Ẑ_r, and P(0.05·Ẑ > Z) ≤ 0.05;
> (c) for fixed N, Σ_r Ẑ_r ĥ_r / Σ_r Ẑ_r → π(h) a.s. as R → ∞; for fixed R, each ĥ_r → π(h) in probability as N → ∞;
> (d) the pooled product Ẑ·(R⁻¹Σ_r ĥ_r) is *not* unbiased: its bias is −(1 − 1/R)Cov(Ẑ_1, ĥ_1 | 𝓒).
> Hypotheses named: EX-A, EX-S, CAL, V5 (kernel invariance), R fixed in advance (Prop P(v)).

Status paragraph (verbatim):

### TH412 — Theorem H (A1): Zhat-weighted estimates of bounded functionals, including joint inclusion (NEW-SYNTH)  [theorem]

- Source (authoritative): `THM-SYNTH/THEOREM_LIST.md` A1; `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §2-§3; positions: [pos 1099], [pos 1177], [pos 1185], [pos 1242] (PC1).
- Statement (verbatim; hypotheses named in the source):

> ### A1. Theorem H (Ẑ-weighted estimates of bounded functionals, including joint inclusion) — NEW-SYNTH
>
> **(i) Statement (proposed).** Setting of V1. Let h: Ω → [0, 1] (any bounded h after an affine rescaling), and let ĥ_r be
> island r's estimate of π(h) built from the measured rounds (the plain population average, or the Rao–Blackwellised
> version when h is a product of inclusion indicators). Write δ₁ = 1 − π(S₀), ρ̄ and u_π as in 00_COMMON §2.
> (a) *Islandwise, every regime, every frozen grid:* E[W_r·|ĥ_r − h(S₀)| | 𝓒] ≤ 2δ₁ + c_h(ρ̄ + u_π), where c_h = 0 for
> the plain average and c_h ≤ 1 for the RB version (the RB-specific terms are those of M1).
> (b) *Pooled, non-asymptotic:* for ĥ^zw := Σ_r W_r ĥ_r/Σ_r W_r, s ∈ (0,1), t > 0,
> P(|ĥ^zw − h(S₀)| > t | 𝓒) ≤ exp{−R(1−s)²/(2E[W_1²|𝓒])} + (2δ₁ + c_h(ρ̄+u_π))/(st).
> A second-moment-free version replaces E[W²] by the truncation level M_𝓒(ε) := inf{M : E[W 1{W > M}] ≤ ε} and Maurer by
> Hoeffding on W ∧ M: P(W̄_R ≤ s) ≤ exp{−2R(1 − ε − s)²/M²}.
> (c) *Joint inclusion:* for A ⊆ [p], h_A(S) = 1{A ⊆ S}; (a)–(b) give the joint inclusion probabilities, with
> h_A(S₀) = 1{A ⊆ S₀}.
> (d) *n → ∞ (R1, T03♯ hypotheses):* with δ₁ → 0 in P₀-probability and R_n such that R_n(1−s)²/E[W²|𝓒_n] → ∞ in
> probability, ĥ^zw → h(S₀) in probability, jointly with "output exists". Since π(h) → h(S₀) under T03♯, this is
> proposal §13.1's "the estimate of E_π[h] converges to the truth".
> (e) *Fixed data:* ĥ^zw → π(h) a.s. as R → ∞ at fixed N (V1(c); cited).

Status paragraph (verbatim):

> **(iii) Status.** PROOF SKETCH (this run). The proof is M1's with h in place of 1{j ∈ S}: for the plain average,
> |ĥ_r − h(S₀)| ≤ (fraction of measured particles off S₀) because |h(S) − h(S₀)| ≤ 1 and the average is over particles,
> so E[W_r |ĥ_r − h(S₀)|] ≤ E[W_r · frac_off_r] = π(S ≠ S₀) = δ₁ by the island identity for the indicator 1{S ≠ S₀}
> (the factor 2 covers the rescaling of a general bounded h to [0,1]). For the RB version the measured-round drift terms
> are M1's. (b) is Prop P(iii) verbatim with e_r = |ĥ_r − h(S₀)|. (c) is a special case. (d) composes with T03♯ as M2 /
> Prop P do. **Crux not verified:** the island identity E[W_r ĥ_r] = π(h) for the *measured-round average* (T12(i.b)-type,
> W2-T26 Lemma 3: "T15 at a terminal-round prefix") must be checked for general h; and the RB terms. Components: THM-INV
> rows 9, 10 (A), the empty "joint inclusion" cell.

### TH413 — Theorem Z (A2): the evidence, what Zhat can and cannot do  [theorem]

- Source (authoritative): `THM-SYNTH/THEOREM_LIST.md` A2; `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §2-§3; positions: [pos 1099], [pos 1177], [pos 1185], [pos 1242] (PC1).
- Statement (verbatim; hypotheses named in the source):

> ### A2. Theorem Z (the evidence: what Ẑ can and cannot do)
>
> **(i) Statement.** Setting of V1, one island (pooling by V1).
> (i) E[Ẑ_r | 𝓒] = Z; E[log Ẑ_r] ≤ log Z; P(0.05Ẑ > Z) ≤ 0.05 (regime-free).
> (ii) *Exact variance identity* (O-PW2 Thm A): N·Var(W_T | 𝓒) = Σ_{s<T}(1 − 1/N)^{T−1−s}(E[W_s² μ_s(h²_{s,T})] − 1), for
> any q_t-invariant round kernels; pooled variance = this/R.
> (iii) *Masked regime, lower tail* (MASKZPIP E1/E2): for any kernel, grid and N, with A the truth's basin, τ_A the first
> stage with a particle in A and D_A the d-gap, P(W > (T/η)[π₀(Aᶜ)/π₀(x_m)]e^{−φ_{τ_A}D_A}) ≤ η + Nπ₀(A); on a frozen path
> log W = (a + Λ)(φ* − φ_τ) + O(1): Ẑ underestimates by the log-odds overshoot of a late crossing. F-MASKPIP N(a): if the
> terminal population is off S₀ at stage T with probability ≥ κ, Ẑ_r ≤ √δ₁·Z there.
> (iv) *Run certificate* (MASKZPIP C1): Ẑ/Z ≤ Ẑ/Z_𝒯 on every run, so Ẑ < Z_𝒯 certifies underestimation; island agreement
> certifies nothing (E1c).
> (v) *Favourable regime* (W2-T26 Thm A): under EX-A, EX-S, CAL, START, OUT and (P1) (T_n + 1)Δ_n → 0, Ẑ/Z → 1 in
> probability on the output event.

### TH414 — Theorem D (D1): work, depth and width of v3.1; comparison with Song-Liang s6  [theorem]

- Source (authoritative): `THM-SYNTH/THEOREM_LIST.md` D1; `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §2-§3; positions: [pos 1099], [pos 1177], [pos 1185].

> ### D1. Theorem D (work, depth and width of v3.1; comparison with Song–Liang §6)
>
> **(i) Statement.** Units: one score evaluation s(k) at model size k (s̄ its mean on the path). Let m = p + B + 2 (steps
> per round), ℓ = ⌈log₂(n+p+1)⌉, L = max(4, ⌈log₂(n+1)⌉), I_e ≤ ℓ rebuild iterations, T_pil, T^{(i)}, T the stage counts,
> T ≤ T_e = max(1000, ℓ²)·4^e on success (deterministic, Theorem G), N = N_e, R islands.
> (a) *Work:* W = J·2^B·s(B) + Σ_e[H_e(T_pil + L + 4) + 4H_e Σ_i(T^{(i)} + L + 4)]·m·s̄ + R·N·(T + L + 4)·m·s̄
> + n_LS(ℓ+1)(p + k̄(p − k̄))s̄ + O(np²) + O(p²)–O(p³). Under the v3 budgets W is polynomial in n (T32(i); the displayed rate
> is a GAP, Astra's candidate O(max(n,p)·p·log³(n+p) + p²log²(n+p))).
> (b) *Depth, island-parallel (layer (a)–(c)):* D_PEL = D_setup + Σ_e[H_e(T_pil + L + 4) + H_e Σ_i(T^{(i)} + L + 4)]·m·s̄
> + N(T + L + 4)·m·s̄ + n_LS(ℓ+1)s̄, with width R (islands) and p + k̄(p−k̄) (scans).
> (c) *Depth, particle-parallel (declared v3.2 path, law-preserving):* D_PP = D_setup + [(T_pil + L + 4) + Σ_i(T^{(i)} + L + 4)
> + (T + L + 4)]·m·s̄ + O(ΣT·log N) + local searches; **free of N, H and R**; worst case on success O(m·ℓ·T_e) =
> O(p log³(n+p)) score evaluations; width R·N.
> (d) *Comparison, same units:* Song–Liang §6 with K_n = √p processors has wall time O(p^{(1+α)/2}) + O(np) with
> T = O((p/K)^α) SAMC iterations per subset, α a choice (α = 1 in the paper), total work O(p^{1+α/2} + np^{3/2}), width √p,
> output = posterior restricted to the merged set. v3.1: depth O(p(ℓ+2)(T+L+4)) with T from D2, work O(N·p·(ℓ+2)·T_e),
> width R·N, output = π exactly (V1). At α = 1 the depths have the same order in p up to log factors; ours needs far more
> width and work; what is bought is correctness under correlation.
