### TH417 — Theorem SL (C1): an analytic separation from Song-Liang's split-and-merge on a masked LH family (NEW-SYNTH)  [theorem]

- Source (authoritative): `THM-SYNTH/THEOREM_LIST.md` C1; `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §2; `LIT-PAR/REPORT.md` §3.1 G4; positions: [pos 1177], [pos 1185]; meeting disposition `MEET-THM/FUTURE_WORK.md` FW21.
- Statement (verbatim, setting and (i)):

> ### C1. Theorem SL (an analytic separation from Song–Liang's split-and-merge on a masked family) — NEW-SYNTH
>
> **Setting (from the JRSS-B text; SL digest, THM-INV D10).** Song–Liang's procedure (SL §3.1): uniformly random
> partition of the P_n predictors into K_n subsets of size s_n = P_n/K_n (recommended K_n = O(√P_n), SL §6); Stage 1 per
> subset: BVS on D_n^{s} = (y, X_s) with priors σ² ~ IG(a₀,b₀), β_ξ | ξ ~ N(0, σ²V_ξ), π(ξ) ∝ λ_s^{|ξ|}(1−λ_s)^{|s|−|ξ|}1{|ξ| ≤ s̄},
> λ_s = |s|^{−γ}; selection of predictors whose marginal inclusion probability passes a threshold (FDR rule at level α₁);
> iterative re-selection on the remainder (justified by Condition 5: |cov(x_t, y)| > 0 for every true predictor; capped at 2
> iterations); merge S̃ = ∪ s̃_i; Stage 2: BVS on (y, X_S̃) with prior r_n/p_n. Theorem 4 / Corollary 2 with eq. (19): for a
> fixed subset s, the subset posterior concentrates on the KL projection f₀ with β₀ = Σ_s^{−1}cov(x_s, y), and a true
> predictor t ∈ s is asymptotically selected iff β_{0,t} ≠ 0 (the "only if" direction is stated in the text after Cor 2, not
> proved there; see crux (ii)). SL's output is the posterior restricted to S̃ (prior mass 0 outside S̃; SL §7).
>
> **Our family.** LH exact Gram (W1-EXP §4): independent equicorrelated groups of size g (correlation ρ), c linked pairs of
> hubs (j_{a_i}, j_{b_i}) with corr(j_{a_i}, j_{b_i}) = ψ_i, 0 < |ψ_i| < ρ, θ_{j_{b_i}} = −ψ_iθ_{j_{a_i}}, visible hubs
> θ_{j_h} = β_h, null groups; X′X = (n−1)Σ_LH, p ≤ n − 1. Masked hubs M = {j_{b_i}}; S° = S₀ ∖ M.
>
> **(i) Statement (proposed).** Let E_n be the event that, for some i, the masked hub j_{b_i} is *isolated* in its subset:
> its subset contains neither j_{a_i} nor any other member of j_{b_i}'s group.
> (a) *Isolation probability (finite combinatorics):* for a uniformly random equipartition, P(a given other column shares
> j_{b_i}'s subset) = (s_n − 1)/(P_n − 1), so P(E_nᶜ) ≤ c·g·(s_n − 1)/(P_n − 1) ≤ c·g/K_n, and P(E_n) → 1 whenever K_n → ∞
> (in particular under SL's K_n = O(√P_n)). Exactly, P(j_{b_i} isolated from g given columns) = C(P_n−1−g, s_n−1)/C(P_n−1, s_n−1); the union bound is vacuous at small K_n: at K_n = 2, P(isolated) = 0.53 for g = 1 (LIT-PAR's design, P = 16) but 0.05 for g = 4 (`scripts/check_lemmas.py`). So at fixed K_n the failure probability is bounded away from 0 but can be small; the "→ 1" needs K_n → ∞.
> (b) *Loss of the hub on E_n (exact-Gram orthogonal-null lemma):* on E_n, x_{j_{b_i}} is orthogonal to every other
> column of its subset and x_{j_{b_i}}′μ = (n−1)(θ_{j_{b_i}} + ψ_iθ_{j_{a_i}}) = 0 exactly, so in its subset x_{j_{b_i}}
> is an orthogonal null column: Condition 5 fails exactly (cov = 0), β_{0,j_{b_i}} = 0 in every iteration, and under SL's
> priors π(j_{b_i} ∈ ξ | D_n^{s}) = O_P(λ_s·n^{−1/2}) → 0. Hence P(j_{b_i} ∈ S̃ | E_n) → 0 and SL's output cannot contain
> j_{b_i}: P(SL output = S₀) ≤ P(E_nᶜ) + o(1).
> (c) *The exact posterior is not the problem:* on the same family 1 − π(S₀) → 0 (W1-EXP Thm 5(d) / T03♯), and SL's own
> Theorem 3 (sure screening of identifiable predictors) applies to the full posterior: the failure is the split.
> (d) *v3.1 on the same family:* the final stage targets π exactly and all of V1 holds; with LS0, P(𝒪 ∩ {Ŝ⁺ ≠ S₀}) → 0
> (R5 (b1-LH), XF VERIFIED); without LS0, the same on A-REV7's STAB-LH subfamily (R5 (b2-LH)); the Ẑ-weighted PIPs and joint
> inclusions satisfy A1.
> (e) *Remark (clustered splits):* if the split keeps j_{b_i} with its group, β_{0,j_{b_i}} = ψ_iθ_{j_{a_i}}([Σ_bb^{−1}]₁₁ − 1) ≠ 0
> (the members carry the marginal signal −ρψβ), so Stage 1 retains the hub: SL's theory does not analyse clustering, and
> a clustered split still loses power (LIT-PAR note 09: 3/20 at β = 0.6). Our blocks are used only for the start.

Status paragraph and tier note (verbatim):

> **(iii) Status.** COUNTEREXAMPLE (numerical, reproducible: LIT-PAR G4, p = 16, n = 200, 5/318 separated splits vs 20/20 for
> the exact posterior at β = 1; 0/318 at β = 0.6) + PROOF SKETCH (this run, (a)–(e) above; the isolation argument is new and
> differs from LIT-PAR's sketch, which did not consider the hub's group). The numerical seed used a singleton masked
> variable (g = 1) and Liang's slides; it should be re-run on the W1-EXP LH family with g ≥ 2 and K ∈ {2, 4, √p} to show
> (a)'s dependence on K (first step of HQ-SL). Components: THM-INV §3b rows "Thm 4/Cor 2" and "UQ of the merged output".

> **Group G5 tiering note.** v1: C1(a)–(e) on exact-Gram LH, with (b)'s PIP step as the one proof obligation; the numerical
> counterexample re-run on the LH family. v2: LH-iid; the study's dilution designs (where SL's Condition 5 holds but the
> within-split projection coefficients are small; no analytic statement yet).

### RF276 — LIT-PAR G4 analytic sketch: "SaM loses the masked variable whenever the split separates the linked pair"  [refuted claim]

- Source of the claim: `LIT-PAR/REPORT.md` §3.1 G4 and `LIT-PAR/notes/09_sam_lh_counterexample.md` ("whenever the random split separates the linked pair (probability ~ 1/2 for two halves, -> (K-1)/K for K groups)"); corrections: `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §1 item 6, `THM-INV/REPORT.md` §2 D10; positions: [pos 1070], [pos 1177].
- Corrections (verbatim):

> 6. **Two corrections to inherited claims found while writing:** (a) the Song–Liang failure on the W1-EXP LH family needs the
>    masked hub to be *isolated* in its split (from its partner *and* its own group), because its group members carry the
>    marginal signal −ρψβ and Stage 1 then retains the hub (THEOREM_LIST C1(e), checked numerically); LIT-PAR's 5/318 used
>    a singleton masked variable (g = 1), where isolation = separation. (b) F-MASKPIP M3 is recorded as XF ERROR in
>    THM-INV; the "R ≳ 1/P(crossing)" remark must not cite it (replaced by Cauchy–Schwarz + M2).

> - **D10: Song–Liang's correlation condition.**
>   - Settled against the text (SL digest). Condition 5 ("|cov(x_t, y)| > 0 for any true predictor") justifies the iterative stage-1 step. Theorem 4 / Corollary 2 with eq. (19) is what retains a true predictor: it is retained only if its population projection coefficient β₀,t on the subset is nonzero.
>   - Masking can break both: cov(x_t, y) = 0 for a cancelled pair, and β₀,t = 0 when its partner sits in another split.
>   - LIT-PAR's "Thm 5" label and "read from slides" caveat should be replaced by this citation.

- Refutation: the exact computation in CE214 (isolation probabilities 0.53 at K_n = 2, g = 1 versus 0.05 at g = 4) and Theorem SL (e). Replacement: TH417; the numerical counterexample CE213 stands as evidence for g = 1.

### LM230 — Lemma KL (NEW-SYNTH)  [lemma]

- Source (authoritative): `THM-SYNTH/THEOREM_LIST.md` S2(c); `THM-SYNTH/REPORT.md` §2; final card `MEET-THM/THEOREM_LIST_FINAL.md` M6; positions: [pos 1177].

> (c) *Lemma KL (NEW-SYNTH, elementary):* for any π, π₀ on Ω with δ₁ = 1 − π(S₀),
> KL(π‖π₀) ≥ (1 − δ₁)·log(1/π₀(S₀)) − log 2.
> Proof: data processing on the partition {S₀, Ω∖S₀} gives KL(π‖π₀) ≥ kl(1−δ₁ ‖ π₀(S₀)) ≥ (1−δ₁)log((1−δ₁)/π₀(S₀)) +
> δ₁ log δ₁ ≥ (1−δ₁)log(1/π₀(S₀)) − h(δ₁) with h ≤ log 2. ∎ (PROOF SKETCH only because unreviewed; the inequality is
> two lines.) Consequently, under T27(i), the Chatterjee–Diaconis sample size exp(KL(π‖π₀)) for importance sampling from
> π₀ to π is ≥ ½·Q*^{1−δ₁}·e^{O_P(1)}: the exp(KL) scale and SEP-B's Q* agree (THM-INV §4b B1 called this identification
> "my inference, unproved"; Lemma KL makes it a one-line corollary).

>
> **A2's exact wording** (`origin/theory/THM-SYNTH:…/THEOREM_LIST.md`):
> - Table row, line 26: "masked regime: Ẑ errs only downward, by the log-odds overshoot of a late crossing".
> - §A2 "(ii) Plainly", line 236: "in the masked regime it can only fail *downward*, by an amount the run can partly certify."
> - Formal (iii), "Masked regime, lower tail": P(W > (T/η)[π₀(Aᶜ)/π₀(x_m)]e^{−φ_{τ_A}D_A}) ≤ η + Nπ₀(A), and "on a frozen path log W = (a+Λ)(φ*−φ_τ) + O(1): Ẑ underestimates…".
>
> (iii) is a high-probability statement plus a statement conditional on a path. It does not assert P(W > 1) = 0, so the counterexample does not refute (iii). C's quote matches the "Plainly" sentence word for word, so it is not a paraphrase.
>
> **Proof that the literal sentence is false.**
> 1. Suppose Ẑ ≤ Z almost surely and E[Ẑ | 𝓒] = Z.
> 2. Then Z − Ẑ ≥ 0 with mean 0, so Ẑ = Z almost surely.
> 3. A2(iii) says that in the masked regime P(Ẑ < Z | 𝓒) > 0, and in fact close to 1.
> 4. Hence P(Ẑ > Z | 𝓒) > 0. More precisely, E[(W−1)⁺ | 𝓒] = E[(1−W)⁺ | 𝓒], so the rare upward excursions carry all the missing mass. Nonnegativity is not even needed. ∎
>
> **Explicit instance (`c24_twostate.py`).** π₀(a) = 0.01, π(a) = 0.99, one particle (the masked start). W = 99 with probability 0.01, and W = 0.0101 with probability 0.99. E W = 1, and E(W−1)⁺ = E(1−W)⁺ = 0.98. Ẑ overestimates by a factor of 99 with probability 0.01.
>
> **Corrected wording.**
> > "In the masked regime Ẑ underestimates Z with high probability: P(W_r > t_*) ≤ η + Nπ₀(A) with t_* = (T/η)[π₀(Aᶜ)/π₀(x_m)]e^{−φ_{τ_A}D_A}. Because E[W_r | 𝓒] = 1, the complementary rare event carries compensating overestimates of the same total mean, E[(W_r−1)⁺] = E[(1−W_r)⁺], which can be large when they occur. Markov caps them: P(Ẑ > 20Z) ≤ 0.05. The run certificate Ẑ < Z_𝒯 detects underestimation only."
>
> Line 26 should change the same way, for example: "errs downward with high probability; upward errors are rare and large (mean-compensating)".

- Status: FALSE as the literal sentence (PC1, Claude Opus 5.5, same-family: "PROVED (C's COUNTEREXAMPLE is valid)"); the formal lower-tail statement A2(iii) is not refuted. Replacement wording given in the quote above.

> ## 4. Disagreements

>   this refutes the *applicability of the unimodal-ratio route*, not fast mixing. LIT-VENUE's "R > M since S₀ is the unique
>   local mode" is wrong: unimodality gives R > 1, not R > M.
> - **What the paper may say:** "No published rapid-mixing theorem covers the paper's prior and cap; the standard
>   sufficient condition (a best-neighbour ratio exceeding the neighbourhood size) fails on our designs because the BB(1,p)
>   + g = n penalty per extra variable is ≍ p√n against a neighbourhood of size ≍ p (LIT-MCMC Prop. OB, PROOF SKETCH). We
>   make no mixing claim in either direction. Our output theorems (Thm 5) do not use mixing: the truth is scored, not
>   mixed to." Plus, as evidence not theorem: "On LH the exact posterior is unimodal at p ≤ 20 (API-POS enumeration); the

Objects and hypotheses (verbatim, PROOF §0):

> **The code's target.** `Engine::eval` (`v3_engine.h:89-101`) sets, for the sorted model S with k = |S|,
>
> ```
> c(S)   = Σ_b log r_b(S ∩ C_b)              Start::comp, v3_start.h:54-66 (blocks met by S, increasing block order)
> lg0(S) = logprior[k] + c(S)                v3_engine.h:97
> d(S)   = (log m(S) − log m(∅)) − c(S)      v3_engine.h:97
> log γ_φ(S) = lg0(S) + φ·d(S)               Particle::lgphi, v3_engine.h:14
> ```
>
> with logprior[k] = log w(k) − log W_K (`v3_score.h:61-70`), log r_b(U) = log m(U) − log m(∅) for U ≠ ∅ and exactly 0 for
> U = ∅ (`v3_start.h:95`). In exact arithmetic
>
>   γ_φ(S) = ϖ(S) · BF(S)^φ · ∏_b r_b(S∩C_b)^{1−φ} ∝ (ϖ(S) m(S))^φ · π₀(S)^{1−φ},  S ∈ 𝒮_K,
>
> which is M §6.3 ("γ_φ = γ₀ e^{φd}"). It equals π₀ at φ = 0 and the posterior of M §5 (up to the constant m(∅)) at φ = 1.

> **Hypotheses used throughout.**
> - **(H-U) ideal uniforms.** Every call `vs->u(·)` returns a fresh U[0,1) variable independent of everything drawn before.
>   In production the source is one xoshiro256** stream per island (`v3_engine.h:20-23`, `v3_util.h:44-60`) shared by all
>   particles of the island, and the number of uniforms a step consumes depends on the state (self-loops consume none, an
>   empty neighbour candidate set consumes one). Under (H-U) this is harmless: the index at which a step starts reading is a
>   stopping time of the iid sequence, so the uniforms it reads are iid U[0,1) and independent of the past (strong Markov
>   property of an iid sequence). The deviations of the real generator (53-bit grid) are quantified in §5.
> - **(H-A) exact arithmetic** for the proofs; floating-point effects are listed in §5 and measured in CHECK.md.
> - **(H-D) determinism of the score.** log m(S) is a function of the sorted S only. True in the code: `Scorer` is stateless
>   apart from scratch buffers that are fully overwritten (`v3_score.h:145-237`; route choice Cholesky → refactor → QR is
>   a deterministic function of S), and the cache returns the stored bits of the first evaluation (`v3_score.h:239-296`).
>   Table scores are computed by the same scorer (`v3_start.h:93`). Hence lg0, d and γ_φ are functions of S. A

### TH405 — N9 Claim G — Gibbs coordinate step (heat bath with cap rule)  [proposition]

> complement (heat bath; one of S⁺, S⁻ is S). If S⁺ ∉ 𝒮_K, i.e. j ∉ S and |S| = K, then `add_ok` is false, o_j = 0, and

### LM229 — N9 Claim R: a uniformly random order of reversible kernels is self-adjoint; the production round is gamma_phi-reversible  [lemma]

- Source (authoritative): `N9-KERNEL/PROOF.md` §2; `REPORT.md` §2 rows 5-6; CHK §5 (amendments); positions: [pos 1546], [pos 1593], [pos 1626].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Claim R.** Let K_1,…,K_m be γ-reversible Markov kernels on a finite set (repetitions allowed), and let σ be a random
> permutation, independent of the chain, whose law μ satisfies μ(σ) = μ(σ∘ϱ) where ϱ is the reversal i ↦ m+1−i. Then
> R = Σ_σ μ(σ) K_{σ(1)}K_{σ(2)}⋯K_{σ(m)} is γ-reversible (self-adjoint on L²(γ)). The uniform law on S_m satisfies the
> hypothesis, so the production round kernel is γ_φ-reversible.

> **The exact condition, and what would break it.** Self-adjointness needs (i) every K_i γ_φ-reversible (§1, all at the
> same φ: `one_round` passes one φ to all steps, `:202-211`), (ii) the law of the label sequence reversal-invariant, and
> (iii) the sequence independent of the state. A varying number of steps per type is harmless as long as the law of the
> whole label sequence (including its length) is reversal-invariant and state-independent, e.g. any exchangeable law. It
> fails if the order or the step counts depend on the state, or if the order law is not reversal-invariant (e.g. a fixed
> order; CHECK.md shows the canonical fixed order is γ_φ-invariant but not self-adjoint, as M §6.5 says). In the code m is
> fixed and the order is uniform, so (ii) and (iii) hold.

Proof route (Summary: PROOF §2): the adjoint of a product is the product of adjoints in reverse order, so R* = Sum_sigma mu(sigma) K_{sigma o rho(1)}...K_{sigma o rho(m)}, which equals R by reversal invariance of mu; the code draws the order by Fisher-Yates from m-1 fresh uniforms (m = p+B+2 fixed), a bijection of choices onto the m! permutations (verified for m <= 8), independent of the state.
- Earlier versions / repairs: three prose amendments by the cross-family check (RF278, CE218): the order conditions are sufficient, not necessary; "A fixed order is not self-adjoint" -> "need not be"; the RB consequence needs the round to start in q_phi.
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) (N9-KERNEL) -> CHK VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT [pos 1626].
- Proved by / checked by: author; numerical: round DB rel <= 5.6e-14, canonical fixed order fails at phi > 0 (rel 0.68-0.999), production `one_round` MC matches R (27 chi^2 tests); Sol line by line.
- Depends on: TH405-TH408.
- Feeds: S-KERNEL (K21).

### TH409 — N9 Claim Z: Zbar0 is exact (truncated size-profile convolution)  [proposition]

- Source: `N9-KERNEL/PROOF.md` §3; positions: [pos 1546], [pos 1593], [pos 1626].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Claim Z.** F_J(k) = Σ_{S: |S| = k} ∏_b r_b(S∩C_b) for k ≤ K, and Z̄₀ = Σ_{k≤K} ϖ(k)F_J(k) = Σ_{S∈𝒮_K} γ₀(S).

- Earlier versions / repairs: none; floating point: log-sum-exp with long-double accumulation, absolute error in log Zbar0 of order J (B+K) eps; checked against an independent long-double brute force.
- Status history: PROVED (candidate) -> CHK VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT (claim Z checks: "Block size profiles and nonnegative convolutions enumerate all feasible products. Truncation at K cannot affect any coefficient through K. The size prior is multiplied once").
- Proved by / checked by: author; Sol.
- Depends on: ⟦capped BB(1,p) prior⟧.
- Feeds: S-KERNEL (K08).

### TH410 — N9 Claim S: draw_pi0 draws exactly from pi0  [proposition]

- Source: `N9-KERNEL/PROOF.md` §3; positions: [pos 1546], [pos 1593], [pos 1626].
- Statement (verbatim):

> **Claim S.** `draw_pi0` returns S with probability exactly π₀(S) for every S ∈ 𝒮_K (and never a set outside 𝒮_K).

Proof route (Summary: PROOF §3): P(S) = [varpi(k)F_J(k)/Zbar0] prod_b [e_b(k_b)F_b(r_b - k_b)/F_{b+1}(r_b)] prod_{k_b>0} [r_b(U_b)/e_b(k_b)]; with r_b - k_b = r_{b-1} and r_{J-1} = k the middle product telescopes to prod_b e_b(k_b)/F_J(k); empty blocks contribute e_b(0) = r_b(empty) = 1; ties play no role in sampling (they matter only for `start_mode`, not part of N9).
- Earlier versions / repairs: none.
- Status history: PROVED (candidate); production-RNG chi^2 p = 0.51, 0.97, 0.33; DFS law vs gamma0/Zbar0 max rel <= 2.0e-13, TV <= 5e-16; CHK VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT ("Backward conditional probabilities telescope ... Thus the full probability is gamma0(S)/Zbar0").
- Proved by / checked by: author; Sol.
- Depends on: TH409, ⟦tables r_b⟧.
- Feeds: S-KERNEL (K08).

> **Answers to the specific questions.**
> - (a) Unequal degrees: handled, because the factor uses the available degrees |N(j)∖S|, |N(l)∖S′|. An asymmetric graph is
>   impossible (`v3_blocks.h:170` symmetrises). Capped degrees: the cap B acts before the union and does not matter for
>   the proof.
> - (b) The cap K and ∅: Gibbs excludes additions at K. Swaps preserve the size. π₀ has support 𝒮_K. No move ever proposes
>   a set outside 𝒮_K, so nothing needs to be rejected for leaving the support.
> - (c) Uniform swap at |S| = 0 or p: a self-loop that consumes no uniform.
> - (d) In the independence move, Z̄₀ cancels from the acceptance ratio. Z̄₀'s exactness matters for log Ẑ =
>   log m(∅) + log Z̄₀ + Σ log inc (`v3_engine.h:299`), not for the move.
> - (e) Data-dependent inputs: the blocks, tables and graph are built from (X, y) once per setup, before any island, and
>   never depend on particles. State-dependent inputs: only the Gibbs feasibility, the self-loop rules and |N(j)∖S|, all
>   covered by the proofs. The adaptive pilot φ depends on the population, but it is the schedule, not the kernel: each
>   round is γ_φ-reversible for the φ it is given.
> - The task text's "γ_φ ∝ prior·m^φ·π₀^{1−φ}" has an extra ϖ^{1−φ}. The spec and the code use γ_φ = ϖ·BF^φ·∏r_b^{1−φ}
>   ∝ (ϖm)^φ π₀^{1−φ}. The code's lgphi matches this spec formula to ≤ 2.3e-14 (CHECK §2). This is a notation point only.

- CE217 (negative controls): a neighbour swap without its Hastings factor, an independence step with symmetric acceptance and the canonical fixed-order product fail at O(1); they show the exact check has power. CE218: at phi = 0 the final independence step refreshes exactly from pi0, so the canonical fixed-order product is reversible: a counterexample to "a fixed order is not self-adjoint" (as recorded in CHECK.md and used by CHK).

- Refutation: not an algebraic error: the order conditions are sufficient (CE218); the stated RB consequence needs a stationary start of the round. Replacement: CHK wording, adopted by MEET-THM ("N9 with CHK amendments").

## Part G. Dead ends and corrections

### Dead ends and corrections (Theme 12)

- **"Methods with guarantees are sequential" (RF268, CE212).** Felipe's belief [pos 1030] and the HQ framing [pos 1038] were tested by LIT-PAR [pos 1070, 1072]; the literal sentence is false in the work/depth sense (ZYVR informed chain with parallel neighbour scoring: depth O(n log p)); the three-part S-GAP (CJ282) survives, with verdict "TRUE WITH QUALIFICATIONS", medium-high confidence, and a list of wordings never to print ("first parallel exact BVS", "no analogue speed-up for MCMC", "depth = T").
- **"Depth = stage count" (RF269).** HQ [pos 1038] said the only sequential part is the stage count; LIT-PAR [pos 1070, 1072] and METH-AUDIT showed a round is p+B+2 sequential steps, so depth is T L (p+B+2) in score evaluations (about 2-3 ms per round at p = 500). The only fix (parallel-within-particle moves, C10 / Option B) is a WORKHORSE kernel change that breaks the Gibbs-path theorems and was rejected.
- **METH-AUDIT "3/3 designs bitwise" (RF270).** Overclaim at report time (only smoke + design 1 completed; §6 unfilled; `results/` never committed); caught by HQ [pos 1085, 1103, 1107]; re-established by HQ re-runs [pos 1175, 1241]. Residual source CONFLICT (1/1 vs 3/3) still listed in MEET-THM REGISTRY_INDEX §5.B B1 (**UNCERTAIN** whether a reader of the final registry will see it resolved). W-cal (TH395) was never executed. Wall-clock figure: 1.9x on 2 cores; no 4-core number.
- **"Depth free of N, H, R" (RF271).** True only for a particle-parallel implementation that does not exist; struck for v3.1 by MEET-v31 decision 6; island-level depth only (Felipe, 2026-11-03); C6 (per-particle streams) and C7 (Gram-free scorer) are the declared v3.2 path with a stated trigger (a particle-depth claim or any fit with p > 2,500).
- **Post-search monotonicity in the island count (RF272, CE220).** Cor W-R needs the extra local search from the R = 4 centre; without it the post-search HPM can be worse (PC1 counterexample, n = 29, p = 8).
- **"More islands always helps" (RF273).** False for the equal-weight PIP under a split of a fixed budget (Prop P(i)); stacking at fixed N_e, declared in advance, and the Zhat-weighted PIP primary replace it; adaptive R breaks unbiasedness (Prop P(v), same mechanism as CEX-guard).
- **Rapid-mixing theorems and our target (RF274, RF275, CE215, CE216, TH401, CJ297, CJ301).** Three-step history: API-POS [pos 978] "apply to LH" (with their priors; PROOF SKETCH), LIT-MCMC [pos 1009] "R > M fails for our target, 12/12, factor >= p^0.87" (a failed sufficient condition, not slow mixing), THM-INV D1 / THM-SYNTH §4.1 "say both, claim neither". LIT-VENUE's "R > M since S0 is the unique local mode" is wrong (R > 1 only). The mixing/spectral-gap question for the phi = 1 round stays OPEN (FW4, FW5).
- **No published BVS MCMC-slow / SMC-fast separation (CJ290).** OPEN as a literature claim. Consequence for the paper: the masked theorems repair a problem created by the method's own start; they do not show the method beats MCMC; W7-SEP's "moving off the start is needed, not tempering" is consistent (spine correction, Theme 11).
- **Components that were already known (CJ284, CJ285, CJ286, CJ287, CJ293, CJ294).** O-STAGES G(i)+Lemma 1 = Stefankovic-Vempala-Vigoda 2009; O-STAGES item 4 = Syed et al. Lambda; O-PW2 Theorem A ~ Cerou-Del Moral-Guyader 2011 Thm 1.4 (unchecked); T12/T31(i) = Whiteley-Lee-Heine, Dai et al., Grosse et al.; T03 sharp (3) = Rossell 2022 Prop 1; T03 sharp a modest extension of Rossell 2022 / Moreno-Giron-Casella 2015; BB(1,p) is BB(1,1) tilted by a geometric size factor (LM228; RF281: first-draft novelty narrowed; the "<= 1/2 for every i >= 0" line was false at i = 0).
- **Song-Liang separation (CE213, CE214, RF276, TH417, RF277).** LIT-PAR's numerical 5/318 used a singleton masked variable (g = 1) and slides-based "Thm 5"; the failure needs isolation from partner and group; correct citation is Thm 4 / Cor 2 + eq. (19) + Condition 5; crux (PIP -> 0 under SL priors, FDR variant) is NOT REPAIRED (W2PC1) and the analytic separation went to FUTURE_WORK FW21; ZYVR Condition 1(b) "likely fails on LH" (notes 04) was superseded by API-POS.
- **THM-SYNTH Theorem Z gloss (RF233, CE219, RF282).** "Zhat errs only downward" is literally false (E[(W-1)^+] = E[(1-W)^+]); the R_n lower bound must not cite F-MASKPIP M3 (XF ERROR).
- **N9 amendments (RF278, CE218).** Order conditions are sufficient, not necessary; fixed order need not fail; the RB consequence needs a stationary round start; V5 had "no registry row" (THM-INV §5.12) until N9; registry status remains PROVED (candidate) with the cross-family code check VERIFIED WITH AMENDMENT.
- **F-REFINE (CJ311, RF279, RF280).** Believed versions were same-family only (T38-RECORD C14); Theorem W region form is not the general sufficient condition for (M2) (exact tie on LH with c >= 2, VPGD-PropT); "without LS0 there is no masked-regime theorem" was superseded by the no-LS0 LH candidates and A-REV7; F-REFINE and ARCHITECTURE were amended in place by E-SPINE (wording only).
- **F-REFEREE (CJ303-CJ310).** Registry §H marks M6 "open" because it was written before API-POS landed; the question was in fact answered by API-POS and LIT-MCMC. Referee recommendation "major revision"; the one change that raises the tier (a no-LS0 masked theorem for the run algorithm on LH, plus a growing-n experiment) became A-REV7 / B2-LH and remained partly open (LH-SCALE not run; M1 open).
- **THM-SYNTH counting.** **UNCERTAIN:** REPORT: "19 items in six groups"; THEOREM_LIST table: 23 rows. Not reconciled in the sources.
- **S-REGISTRY counts.** **UNCERTAIN:** 230 + 31 at report time [pos 584] versus 337 + 39 in the archived file header.
- **Lessons.** (1) Report evidence only when its files are committed (METH-AUDIT §6 and `results/` were missing). (2) State depth and cost at the level of the implementation. (3) Say which object a literature theorem is about: a sufficient condition failing is not slow mixing. (4) Plain-language glosses in a theorem list (e.g. "only downward") must be checked as carefully as the formal clause. (5) "VERIFIED" in F-REFINE / THM-SYNTH / METH-AUDIT is same-family or author-only unless a cross-family review is named.

### Lean definitions used in the statements (Theme 13)

All Lean text in this document is verbatim from `SmcBvs/SmcBvs/*.lean` (proofs elided as `…`). Namespaces: `SmcBvs` (Basic, T21HPM, T11Miss), `SmcBvs.T07`, `SmcBvs.Greedy`, `SmcBvs.Lattice`, `SmcBvs.T12`.

**Shared (`Basic.lean`).**

```lean
/-- Posterior `π(S) = e^{F(S)} / Σ_{T∈A} e^{F(T)}` on the finite model set `A`, and `0` off `A`. -/
noncomputable def post [DecidableEq M] (F : M → ℝ) (A : Finset M) (S : M) : ℝ :=
  if S ∈ A then Real.exp (F S) / ∑ T ∈ A, Real.exp (F T) else 0
```

```lean
/-- `S` maximises `g` over `A`. -/
def IsArgmax (g : M → ℝ) (A : Finset M) (S : M) : Prop :=
  S ∈ A ∧ ∀ T ∈ A, g T ≤ g S
```

```lean
/-- `S` is the `≺`-least element of `argmax_A g`, with `≺` given by the injective rank `rk`. -/
def IsLeastArgmax (rk : M → ℕ) (g : M → ℝ) (A : Finset M) (S : M) : Prop :=
  IsArgmax g A S ∧ ∀ T, IsArgmax g A T → rk S ≤ rk T
```


**T07 (`T07Bayes.lean`).** The section variables `(K : ℕ) (F : Finset (Fin p) → ℝ)` and `{p : ℕ}` are implicit arguments of every theorem below that mentions `K`, `F` or `p`.

```lean
/-- The feasible model space `Ω = {S ⊆ [p] : |S| ≤ K}`. -/
def Ωf (p K : ℕ) : Finset (Finset (Fin p)) := univ.filter fun S => S.card ≤ K
```

```lean
/-- The size class `{S : |S| = k}`. -/
def sizeClass (p k : ℕ) : Finset (Finset (Fin p)) := univ.filter fun S => S.card = k
```

```lean
/-- Normaliser `W̃ = Σ_{k ≤ K} C(p,k) w̃(k)` of a size-only prior. -/
noncomputable def normW (p K : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ k ∈ range (K + 1), (p.choose k : ℝ) * w k
```

```lean
/-- The size-only prior `ϖ_w̃(S) = w̃(|S|)/W̃`. -/
noncomputable def sizePrior (p K : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin p)) : ℝ :=
  w S.card / normW p K w
```

```lean
/-- Positivity of a size-only prior on `0..K`. -/
def PosSizePrior (K : ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ k ≤ K, 0 < w k
```

```lean
/-- Posterior `π` on `Ω = Ωf p K` from the log-score `F` (and `0` off `Ω`). -/
noncomputable abbrev π := post F (Ωf p K)
```

```lean
/-- Posterior inclusion probability `PIP_j = π({S : j ∈ S})`. -/
noncomputable def PIP (j : Fin p) : ℝ := ∑ S ∈ Ωf p K, if j ∈ S then π K F S else 0
```

```lean
/-- Posterior 0–1 risk `ρ(a) = Σ_{S∈Ω} π(S) 1{a ≠ S}`. -/
noncomputable def risk01 (a : Finset (Fin p)) : ℝ := ∑ S ∈ Ωf p K, π K F S * if a = S then 0 else 1
```

```lean
/-- Posterior Hamming risk `ρ_H(a) = Σ_{S∈Ω} π(S) |a △ S|`. -/
noncomputable def riskH (a : Finset (Fin p)) : ℝ :=
  ∑ S ∈ Ωf p K, π K F S * ((symmDiff a S).card : ℝ)
```

```lean
/-- `ψ_q(a) = Σ_{j∈a} (1 - 2 q_j)`. -/
def psi (q : Fin p → ℝ) (a : Finset (Fin p)) : ℝ := ∑ j ∈ a, (1 - 2 * q j)
```

```lean
/-- `J₊(q) = {j : q_j > 1/2}`; `MPM = J₊(PIP)`. -/
noncomputable def Jplus (q : Fin p → ℝ) : Finset (Fin p) := univ.filter fun j => 1 / 2 < q j
```


**T37 abstract (`T37Greedy.lean`).**

```lean
/-- `M` is a best strict-improvement map for neighbourhood `N` and score `F` (any tie rule). -/
structure IsBestImprovement (N : α → Finset α) (F : α → ℝ) (M : α → Option α) : Prop where
  none_iff : ∀ S, M S = none ↔ ∀ T ∈ N S, F T ≤ F S
  some_mem : ∀ S T, M S = some T → T ∈ N S
  some_lt : ∀ S T, M S = some T → F S < F T
  some_max : ∀ S T, M S = some T → ∀ T' ∈ N S, F T' ≤ F T
```

```lean
/-- One greedy move (identity at a state with no improving neighbour). -/
def step (M : α → Option α) (S : α) : α := (M S).getD S
```

```lean
/-- The greedy path from `S`. -/
def path (M : α → Option α) (S : α) (k : ℕ) : α := (step M)^[k] S
```

```lean
/-- **TD′_∞(R)** (W1-T37R PROOF.md, Definitions): (L) `S₀` has no strictly improving neighbour;
(N) every other state of `R` has a greedy move, and it lands in `R`. -/
def TDinf (M : α → Option α) (R : Finset α) (S₀ : α) : Prop :=
  M S₀ = none ∧ ∀ S ∈ R, S ≠ S₀ → ∃ T, M S = some T ∧ T ∈ R
```

```lean
/-- `r_R(S) = #{S' ∈ R : F S' > F S}`. -/
noncomputable def rankAbove (F : α → ℝ) (R : Finset α) (S : α) : ℕ :=
  ((R.filter fun S' => F S < F S').card)
```

```lean
/-- **TD′_P(R)** with potential `Φ` (W1-T37R PROOF.md, Definitions; closure of `R` under the
progress moves is part of the hypothesis here; for `R = R_{a,d}` it is Lemma 2(a), proved in
`SmcBvs.T37Lattice`). -/
def TDP (M : α → Option α) (Φ : α → ℕ) (R : Finset α) (S₀ : α) : Prop :=
  M S₀ = none ∧ ∀ S ∈ R, S ≠ S₀ → ∃ T, M S = some T ∧ T ∈ R ∧ Φ T < Φ S
```


**T37 lattice (`T37Lattice.lean`).** `S₀` is a section variable `(S₀ : Finset (Fin p))`, an explicit first argument of `mis`, `ext`, `Φ`, `Rad`, `Lat`, `TDP'`, `DS` and of the theorems that use them.

```lean
/-- `T` is a flip (addition or deletion) or a swap of `S`. -/
def IsFlipSwap (S T : Finset (Fin p)) : Prop :=
  (∃ j ∉ S, T = insert j S) ∨ (∃ i ∈ S, T = S.erase i) ∨
    (∃ i ∈ S, ∃ j ∉ S, T = insert j (S.erase i))
```

```lean
/-- Feasible flip-or-swap neighbourhood (size `≤ K`). -/
noncomputable def nbhd (K : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin p)) : Finset (Finset (Fin p)) := by
  classical exact univ.filter fun T => T.card ≤ K ∧ IsFlipSwap S T
```

```lean
/-- Number of missing truths `m(S) = |S₀ ∖ S|`. -/
def mis (S : Finset (Fin p)) : ℕ := (S₀ \ S).card
```

```lean
/-- Number of extras `e(S) = |S ∖ S₀|`. -/
def ext (S : Finset (Fin p)) : ℕ := (S \ S₀).card
```

```lean
/-- Potential `Φ(S) = |S △ S₀|`. -/
def Φ (S : Finset (Fin p)) : ℕ := (symmDiff S S₀).card
```

```lean
/-- The region `R_{a,d}`. -/
noncomputable def Rad (a d : ℕ) : Finset (Finset (Fin p)) := by
  classical exact univ.filter fun S => mis S₀ S ≤ a ∧ ext S₀ S ≤ d
```

```lean
/-- The lattice of a centre, `Lat(S) = {T : S ∩ S₀ ⊆ T ⊆ S ∪ S₀}`. -/
noncomputable def Lat (S : Finset (Fin p)) : Finset (Finset (Fin p)) := by
  classical exact univ.filter fun T => S ∩ S₀ ⊆ T ∧ T ⊆ S ∪ S₀
```

```lean
/-- **TD′_P(R_{a,d})** on the lattice (W1 Definitions): (L) and, at every other state of
`R_{a,d}`, the greedy move exists and strictly decreases `Φ`. -/
def TDP' (M : Finset (Fin p) → Option (Finset (Fin p))) (a d : ℕ) : Prop :=
  M S₀ = none ∧ ∀ S ∈ Rad S₀ a d, S ≠ S₀ → ∃ T, M S = some T ∧ Φ S₀ T < Φ S₀ S
```

```lean
/-- The one-state progress event `D_S` (W1 PROOF.md, Definitions): the best feasible progress
neighbour (`Φ` decreases) strictly improves on `S` and strictly beats every non-progress
neighbour. It is stated with a witness `T` for the best progress move. -/
def DS (K : ℕ) (F : Finset (Fin p) → ℝ) (S : Finset (Fin p)) : Prop :=
  ∃ T ∈ nbhd K S, Φ S₀ T < Φ S₀ S ∧ F S < F T ∧
    ∀ T' ∈ nbhd K S, ¬ Φ S₀ T' < Φ S₀ S → F T' < F T
```


**T12 (`T12Core.lean`).**

```lean
/-- Apply a (row-stochastic) kernel matrix to a test function: `(K f)(x) = Σ_y K(x,y) f(y)`. -/
def kapply (K : α → α → ℝ) (f : α → ℝ) (x : α) : ℝ := ∑ y, K x y * f y
```

```lean
/-- `γ`-invariance of a kernel: `Σ_x γ(x) K(x,y) = γ(y)`. -/
def Invariant (γ : α → ℝ) (K : α → α → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ y, ∑ x, γ x * K x y = γ y
```

The checkers were given these excerpts (`fidelity/packet2/SOURCES.md` §4, verbatim from `W1-T37R/PROOF.md` and `W3-VT37R/REPAIRS.md`). The informal results themselves belong to the REPAIR-GREEDY theme (TH199 (Theorem A), LM144 (Lemma0(a,c)), RF167 (Lemma0(b)), LM146 (Lemma2-T37), TH198 (Prop1-TD)).

<!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.997) from `A-REV3/snapshots/T37_PROOF.md`; that file is authoritative -->
> **Lemma 0 (monotonicity obstruction; Ŝ after a certified repair). Status: PROVED.**
> (a) F(S⁰) < F(S¹) < … < F(S^r); in particular S₀ ∈ {S¹,…,S^r} implies F(S₀) > F(S_c).
> (b) In production S_c is the running global best over the pre-search scored set 𝒮_pre. Hence the local search can make S₀ a centre, or make Ŝ = S₀ (up to exact ties), only on the event E_LS := {S₀ ∉ 𝒮_pre, F(S₀) > max_{𝒮_pre} F}. On the complement — in particular on every posterior miss F(S₀) ≤ F(Ŝ) — no local search, with any move cap, delivers S₀ (it may still *score* S₀ as a scanned neighbour, which changes nothing in Ŝ).
> (c) If the path reaches S₀ and the search stops there with local_certified (S₀ is the returned scanned centre with no improving neighbour), then every model scored during the search has F ≤ F(S₀), and Ŝ = S₀ after the search, except for exact score ties (then the tie rule decides). No condition π(S₀) > ½ is needed.

<!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 0.993) from `A-REV3/snapshots/T37_PROOF.md`; that file is authoritative -->
> **TD′_∞(𝓡)** (no spurious local maximum + closure): (L) M(S₀) = ⊥ (S₀ has no strictly improving feasible flip or swap); (N) for every S ∈ 𝓡∖{S₀}: M(S) ≠ ⊥ and M(S) ∈ 𝓡.
> **TD′_P(𝓡)** (progress): (L), and for every S ∈ 𝓡∖{S₀}: M(S) ≠ ⊥ and M(S) is a progress move (equivalently Φ(M(S)) < Φ(S); by the class table ΔΦ < 0 exactly on 𝒫).
> **D_S** (one-state progress event), S ∈ Ω∖{S₀}: max_{S′∈𝒫(S)} F(S′) > max{F(S), max_{S″∈𝒩(S)∪ℛ(S)} F(S″)}, where 𝒫(S), 𝒩(S), ℛ(S) are the feasible progress/neutral/regressive neighbours of S. (TD′_P(𝓡) ⟺ (L) ∧ ⋂_{S∈𝓡∖S₀} D_S, ties among top progress moves allowed.)
> **Lattice of a centre.** For S = U ∪ P (U ⊆ S₀, P ∩ S₀ = ∅): Lat(S) := {U′ ∪ P′ : U ⊆ U′ ⊆ S₀, P′ ⊆ P}, |Lat(S)| = 2^{Φ(S)}. R_{a,d} is a union of lattices.

<!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 1.000) from `A-REV3/snapshots/T37_PROOF.md`; that file is authoritative -->
> **Lemma 2 (lattice closure; superset reduction). Status: PROVED.** (a) Progress moves map Lat(S) into Lat(S); R_{a,d} is closed under progress moves; Φ ≤ m(S) + e(S) on Lat(S). (b) On NA_d ∩ TL_d: M(S₀) = ⊥, and for every S = S₀ ∪ P with 1 ≤ |P| ≤ d, M(S) is the deletion of an extra (so D_S holds and M(S) ∈ R_{0,d}).

<!-- fidelity: not byte-identical; notation transliterated (4-gram coverage 1.000) from `A-REV3/snapshots/T37_PROOF.md`; that file is authoritative -->
> **Theorem A (refined T37(i): deterministic greedy repair). Status: PROVED.** Assume EX-A; X, y fixed; ℓ the production move cap.
> (A1) *Characterisation.* TD′_∞(𝓡) holds iff for every S ∈ 𝓡 the uncapped greedy path from S stays in 𝓡 and terminates at S₀. Under TD′_∞(𝓡) the path from S has at most r_𝓡(S) := #{S′ ∈ 𝓡 : F(S′) > F(S)} moves.
> (A2) *Progress version.* Under TD′_P(R_{a,d}), from every S ∈ R_{a,d} the greedy path stays in Lat(S) ⊆ R_{a,d}, Φ strictly decreases at each move, and S₀ is reached after τ(S) = m(S) + e(S) − σ(S) ≤ Φ(S) moves, where σ(S) is the number of extra→truth swaps used (τ(S) ≥ max{m(S), e(S)}).
> (A3) *Production search.* If TD′_P(R_{a,d}) holds and ℓ ≥ a + d (or merely ℓ ≥ τ(S_c)), then from any centre S_c ∈ R_{a,d} the production local search returns S₀ with local_certified, without local_limit, and after it Ŝ = S₀ up to exact ties (Lemma 0(c)). The same holds with TD′_P(R_{a,d}) replaced by the *lattice* condition (L) ∧ ⋂_{S′∈Lat(S_c)∖S₀} D_{S′}, which involves 2^{Φ(S_c)} states only.
> (A4) *Necessity.* Each of the conclusions implies PD on the respective set (F(S₀) > F(S) for S ≠ S₀ in 𝓡, resp. in Lat(S_c) along the path); the conclusion of (A1) for all S ∈ 𝓡 implies TD′_∞(𝓡); the conclusion "every greedy path from R_{a,d} decreases Φ at each step and ends at S₀" implies TD′_P(R_{a,d}).
> (A5) *Relation to literal TD.* Literal TD(d,0) strict ⇒ TD′_P(R_d); for d ≥ 1 the premise is never satisfied (Prop 1), for d = 0 it is satisfiable. TD′_P(R_{a,d}) ⇒ TD′_∞(R_{a,d}); the converse fails (Exp 3).

⚠ **FIDELITY FLAG (archive check):** the quote below is not byte-identical to its source and differs beyond notation (content 4-gram coverage 0.93; best match `L-LEAN/fidelity/packet/SOURCES.md`). It may be abridged, reformatted or paraphrased. Use the source file as authoritative.
> **Repair R3 (W3-VT37R REPAIRS.md): "What is weakest". Status: COUNTEREXAMPLE to the prose; A4 itself VERIFIED.** [...] Correct prose: TD′_P is necessary and sufficient for "every greedy move from R decreases Φ" (A4). For "reach S₀ within Φ moves", TD′_P is sufficient but not necessary. [...] The phrase "the cap needs ℓ ≥ a + d" should also read "ℓ ≥ a + d suffices". The exact requirement is ℓ ≥ τ(S_c), and max(m, e) ≤ τ ≤ Φ.

The move-class table (Δm, Δe; ΔΦ): progress 𝒫 = add truth (−1,0; −1), delete extra (0,−1; −1), swap extra→truth (−1,−1; −2); neutral 𝒩 = swap truth→truth, swap null→null (0,0; 0); regressive ℛ = add null (0,+1; +1), delete truth (+1,0; +1), swap truth→null (+1,+1; +2).

### TH418 — hpm_eq_truth  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `L-LEAN/SmcBvs/SmcBvs/T21HPM.lean`; informal: `Docs/Theory/proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/STATEMENT.md` §3 (C1) and `PROOF_v3.tex` lines 52-86 (proof of C1, first paragraph); positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- Deterministic core of C1: if `π(S₀) > 1/2` and `S₀` has been scored, every maximiser of the
score over the scored set `𝒮 ⊆ A` is `S₀` (whatever the tie rule). -/
theorem hpm_eq_truth {F : M → ℝ} {A 𝒮 : Finset M} {S₀ Ŝ : M} (h𝒮 : 𝒮 ⊆ A)
    (hS₀ : S₀ ∈ 𝒮) (hπ : 1 / 2 < post F A S₀) (hŜ : IsArgmax F 𝒮 Ŝ) : Ŝ = S₀ := …
```


- Informal statement formalised (verbatim, PROOF_v3): "On \(\{\pi(S_0)>1/2\}\), every \(S\ne S_0\) satisfies \(\pi(S)\le1-\pi(S_0)<\pi(S_0)\). Thus \(S_0\) is the strict score maximum, with no tie. If it has also been scored and the output is usable, the method must return it."
- Assumptions/abstractions (ASSUMPTIONS A-T21-2, A-T21-3): `Ŝ` is *any* maximiser of `F` over the scored set (`IsArgmax`), so the result holds for every tie rule, in particular the method's (`IsLeastArgmax → IsArgmax`); the model space is an arbitrary `A : Finset M` and `F` an arbitrary real score (no regression structure is used by C1).
- Not formalised: the SMC-BVS score formula, the method's tie rule as such (not needed: "no tie"), the notion "usable output" (the event `U` is abstract), see CJ319.
- Status history: statement frozen in `frozen/v1/T21HPM.lean` before its proof; proved sorry-free; Fable GREEN; Astra r1 GREEN (table row `hpm_eq_truth` — T21HPM:42 "Uses precisely discovery, posterior majority, and scored-set maximisation"). Not re-run in Astra r2. `#print axioms`: audited (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).
- Proved by / checked by: L-LEAN lead (Opus 5.5); Fable 5.1 (same family), Astra (cross family), fidelity only.
- Depends on: LM234 (`strict_max_of_post_gt_half`), `IsArgmax.eq_of_strict` (Basic.lean).
- Feeds: M5 Theorem HPM (K72), via TH278 (Thm4-C1) / TH281 (T38-(0)).
- Notes: Lean needs `𝒮 ⊆ A` (h𝒮) and `S₀ ∈ 𝒮`; `S₀ ∈ A` is not assumed, it follows from `1/2 < post F A S₀`.

### TH419 — t21_decomposition  [theorem]
- Source: `T21HPM.lean`; informal: TH278 (Thm4-C1) proof, display "{U^c, Ŝ≠S₀} ⊆ {δ₁≥1/2} ∪ {U^c, S₀∉𝒮}"; positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean; the sharp form, no measurability needed because `P` is an outer measure):

```lean
/-- **T21 decomposition** (sharp form). No measurability is needed (outer measure). -/
theorem t21_decomposition (P : Measure Ω) (U : Set Ω) (A : Finset M) (𝒮 : Ω → Finset M)
    (F : Ω → M → ℝ) (Ŝ : Ω → M) (S₀ : M) (h𝒮 : ∀ ω ∉ U, 𝒮 ω ⊆ A)
    (hŜ : ∀ ω ∉ U, IsArgmax (F ω) (𝒮 ω) (Ŝ ω)) :
    P (U ∪ {ω | ω ∉ U ∧ Ŝ ω ≠ S₀}) ≤
      P U + P {ω | ω ∉ U ∧ S₀ ∉ 𝒮 ω} +
        P {ω | ω ∉ U ∧ S₀ ∈ 𝒮 ω ∧ post (F ω) A S₀ ≤ 1 / 2} := …
```


- Informal statement formalised (verbatim, from the L-LEAN brief, `fidelity/packet/SOURCES.md` §1): "For events U (no output), the scored set 𝒮, the truth S₀ and the reported Ŝ = argmax of F over 𝒮 with a fixed tie rule, P(U ∨ Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≤ P(U) + P(S₀ ∉ 𝒮) + P(Uᶜ ∧ S₀ ∈ 𝒮 ∧ π(S₀) ≤ ½)". The sharp form here keeps `Uᶜ` inside the discovery term; it implies the brief's form (TH420).
- Assumptions: as TH418; "U or Ŝ ≠ S₀" is the event `U ∪ {ω | ω ∉ U ∧ Ŝ ω ≠ S₀}`, so no output is needed on `U` (matches STATEMENT.md §1: "Expressions 'U or Shat != S0' mean U union {U^c, Shat != S0}").
- Status history: sorry-free; Fable GREEN ("Valid sharper form retaining `Uᶜ` in the discovery term", Astra r1 table, T21HPM:67); Astra r1 GREEN. Audited by `#print axioms`.
- Depends on: LM231 (`t21_event_subset`), TH418.
- Feeds: M5 Theorem HPM (K72).

### TH421 — markov_half  [theorem]
- Source: `T21HPM.lean`; informal: PROOF_v3 "\(\Pp(\delta_1\ge1/2)=P_0(\delta_1\ge1/2)\le2E_0\delta_1\)"; positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- Markov's inequality at level `1/2`: `P(δ ≥ 1/2) ≤ 2 E δ` for an integrable `δ ≥ 0`. -/
theorem markov_half (P : Measure Ω) (δ : Ω → ℝ) (hδ0 : ∀ ω, 0 ≤ δ ω)
    (hint : Integrable δ P) :
    P.real {ω | 1 / 2 ≤ δ ω} ≤ 2 * ∫ ω, δ ω ∂P := …
```


- Assumptions: real-valued measure `P.real`; `δ` integrable and nonnegative; `P` need not be a probability measure here.

### TH422 — t21_C1  [theorem]
- Source (authoritative): `T21HPM.lean`; informal TH278 (Thm4-C1) = locked T21 (C1): `Docs/Theory/proofs/T21_T14H_HPM_composition/STATEMENT.md` §3 and `PROOF_v3.tex` lines 52-86 (restated as (C1′) in `W2-BOOK/PROOF.md` §4.1); positions: [pos 714], [pos 796], [pos 929].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- **T21 (C1)**: `P(U or Ŝ ≠ S₀) ≤ P(U) + 2 E δ₁ + P(Uᶜ, S₀ ∉ 𝒮)`, with `δ₁ = 1 - π(S₀)`.
(STATEMENT.md §3 (C1); PROOF_v3 eq. (C1).) -/
theorem t21_C1 (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (U : Set Ω) (A : Finset M)
    (𝒮 : Ω → Finset M) (F : Ω → M → ℝ) (Ŝ : Ω → M) (S₀ : M)
    (hF : ∀ S, Measurable fun ω => F ω S) (h𝒮 : ∀ ω ∉ U, 𝒮 ω ⊆ A)
    (hŜ : ∀ ω ∉ U, IsArgmax (F ω) (𝒮 ω) (Ŝ ω)) :
    P.real (U ∪ {ω | ω ∉ U ∧ Ŝ ω ≠ S₀}) ≤
      P.real U + 2 * ∫ ω, (1 - post (F ω) A S₀) ∂P + P.real {ω | ω ∉ U ∧ S₀ ∉ 𝒮 ω} := …
```


- Informal statement formalised (verbatim): "**(C1)** For every such n and data law, P(U or Shat != S0) <= P(U) + 2 E0 delta1 + P(U^c, S0 not in Sscr). Under H03 the middle term tends to zero. If P(U)->0 and any applicable discovery bound below tends to zero, recovery probability tends to one." (STATEMENT.md §3); where `F(S)=log(varpi(S)m(S))`, `pi(S)=exp(F(S))/Z`, `delta1=1-pi(S0)`, "exactly equal scores are ordered by smaller size, then lexicographically smaller sorted index list", `U` = "no usable HPM output is produced", and "On U^c, Shat is the total-order maximum of the nonempty Sscr" (STATEMENT.md §1).
- Assumptions/abstractions (ASSUMPTIONS A-T21-1 to A-T21-5): (A-T21-1) `(Ω,P)` is an abstract probability space carrying the joint law of data and algorithm randomness; the paper's `E₀δ₁` is written `∫ δ₁ dP`; these coincide because `δ₁ = 1 − π(S₀)` depends on the data only and the data marginal of `P` is `P₀`; the Lean statement lets `F` depend on all of `ω`, so it is more general. (A-T21-2) Ŝ = any maximiser. (A-T21-3) `A : Finset M` arbitrary; `F` an arbitrary real score. (A-T21-4) the decomposition needs no measurability; `t21_C1` assumes each `ω ↦ F ω S` measurable so that `δ₁` is integrable. (A-T21-5) routes (a)-(f) and the asymptotic H03 consequences are not formalised.
- Not formalised: "Under H03, 2E₀δ₁→0" (only the finite step `integral_le_eps_add_prob`, LM232), routes (a)-(f) for the discovery term P(U^c, S₀∉𝒮), the conventions that `U` must contain every stopped fit and abort (REGISTRY_v2 row `Thm4-C1`: "needs the convention 𝒢 ⊆ U (stopped fits return an incomplete HPM, G1)"; the Lean `U` is arbitrary), SR/GUARD code facts. See CJ314, CJ326.
- Status history: informal TH278 (Thm4-C1) is PROVED (SF: VERIFIED* (W5-LOCKBOOK); XF: none) per REGISTRY_v2 row `Thm4-C1`, and the pre-campaign T21 is PROVED-LOCKED, CONDITIONAL (MEET-THM REGISTRY_PAPER1 K72 note citing THEOREM_LIST.md R4(iii)); registry flags it FLAG SAME-FAMILY-ONLY for the informal proof. REGISTRY_v2 §G row 1 maps `Thm4-C1` and `T38-(0)` to `t21_C1`, `t21_decomposition`, `t21_decomposition'`, `hpm_eq_truth`, `markov_half`.

### TH423 — ceiling  [theorem]
- Source: `T07Bayes.lean`; informal: T07(i) in `Docs/Theory/proofs/T06_T07_identifiability_size_prior/STATEMENT.md` §2 and `PROOF_v2.tex` (Theorem ceiling); positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- **T07(i), ceiling.** If `S₀` is the global HPM `S†_w̃` under a positive size-only prior, then
`s₀ ≤ K` and `S₀ = S*_{s₀}`, the `≺`-least maximiser of `m` within its size class. -/
theorem ceiling {K : ℕ} (rk : Finset (Fin p) → ℕ) (m : Finset (Fin p) → ℝ) {w : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hw : PosSizePrior K w) {S₀ : Finset (Fin p)}
    (h : IsLeastArgmax rk (fun S => sizePrior p K w S * m S) (Ωf p K) S₀) :
    S₀.card ≤ K ∧ IsLeastArgmax rk m (sizeClass p S₀.card) S₀ := …
```


- Informal statement formalised (verbatim): "**(i) Ceiling.** For every response and every positive size-only prior w̃, {S†_w̃ = S₀} ⊆ {S*_{s₀} = S₀}. Here s₀ ≤ K on the left event, which is empty when s₀ > K. Equivalently: on {S*_{s₀} ≠ S₀} (a within-size ranking error, S₀ beaten or ≺-preceded within its size by m), S†_w̃ ≠ S₀ for every positive size-only prior. No size-only prior repairs it." with "S†_w̃ is the ≺-least element of argmax_{S∈Ω} ϖ_w̃(S)m(S)" and "S*_k is the ≺-least element of argmax_{|S|=k} m(S)".
- Assumptions (A-T07-1, A-T07-2): the tie order ≺ is an injective rank `rk : Finset (Fin p) → ℕ` ("Every total order on a finite set has this form, and PROOF_v2's Remark 'the tie order' states that any fixed total order works"); `m` is an arbitrary real function (only `m > 0` is used, and only in TH425 and TH433); the positive size-only prior is `w` with `0 < w k` for `k ≤ K` and `sizePrior p K w S = w S.card / normW p K w`.
- Status history: statement frozen in `frozen/v1/T07Bayes.lean`; proof sorry-free in the live file; Fable GREEN; Astra r1 GREEN ("Preserves within-size ranking and ties, and explicitly obtains truth feasibility"); audited. Informal TH131 (Prop1-T07) is PROVED (SF: VERIFIED* (W5-LOCKBOOK); XF: VERIFIED* (A-REV4 BOOK_CHECK)); T07 pre-campaign PROVED-LOCKED (wave 3).
- Depends on: LM256 (`exists_isLeastArgmax`/uniqueness), `normW_pos`.
- Feeds: S-TARGET supplement (K60; registrar REGISTRY_PAPER1 line 844 notes "`T07Bayes.lean` covers Prop1-T07 (Bayes rules, size-prior ceiling; K60) — 39 declarations, 28 theorems, 0 `sorry`") and the cited-lemma card L-DEC.

- Source: `T07Bayes.lean`; informal: T07(i) "No size-only prior repairs it" and W2-BOOK (iii′) (strict same-size certificate); positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].

```lean
/-- **T07(i), "no size-only prior can repair a within-size ranking error"** (contrapositive of
the ceiling). If some model `S'` of the same size as `S₀` beats `S₀` in `m`, or ties it and
precedes it in `≺`, then for *every* positive size-only prior `S₀` is not the global HPM.
(This is also W2-BOOK (iii′), stated in terms of `m`.) -/

    {S₀ S' : Finset (Fin p)} (hcard : S'.card = S₀.card)
    (hbeat : m S₀ < m S' ∨ (m S' = m S₀ ∧ rk S' < rk S₀)) :
    ∀ w : ℕ → ℝ, PosSizePrior K w →
      ¬ IsLeastArgmax rk (fun S => sizePrior p K w S * m S) (Ωf p K) S₀ := …
```

### TH434 — excess_riskH_le  [theorem]
- Source: `T07Bayes.lean`; informal T07(iii)(c): "Let p̂ ∈ [0,1]^p be any PIP estimate and 𝒜 the action class: all subsets for the MPM rule, Ω for the capped rule. Let â minimise Σ_{j∈a}(1 − 2p̂_j) over 𝒜 [...]. For any minimiser a_opt of ρ_H over 𝒜, 0 ≤ ρ_H(â) − ρ_H(a_opt) ≤ 2 Σ_{j ∈ â △ a_opt} |p̂_j − PIP_j| ≤ 2‖p̂ − PIP‖₁."; positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- **T07(iii)(c)**: PIP error bounds the excess Hamming risk. For any PIP estimate `q̂`, action
class `𝒜`, `â ∈ 𝒜` minimising `ψ_q̂` over `𝒜`, and `a_opt ∈ 𝒜` minimising `ρ_H` over `𝒜`:
`0 ≤ ρ_H(â) - ρ_H(a_opt) ≤ 2 Σ_{j ∈ â △ a_opt} |q̂_j - PIP_j| ≤ 2 Σ_j |q̂_j - PIP_j|`. -/
theorem excess_riskH_le (qhat : Fin p → ℝ) (𝒜 : Finset (Finset (Fin p)))
    {ahat aopt : Finset (Fin p)} (hahat : ahat ∈ 𝒜) (hahat_min : ∀ a ∈ 𝒜, psi qhat ahat ≤ psi qhat a)
    (haopt : aopt ∈ 𝒜) (haopt_min : ∀ a ∈ 𝒜, riskH K F aopt ≤ riskH K F a) :
    0 ≤ riskH K F ahat - riskH K F aopt ∧
      riskH K F ahat - riskH K F aopt ≤ 2 * ∑ j ∈ symmDiff ahat aopt, |qhat j - PIP K F j| ∧
      2 * ∑ j ∈ symmDiff ahat aopt, |qhat j - PIP K F j| ≤ 2 * ∑ j, |qhat j - PIP K F j| := …
```


- Assumptions (A-T07-3): the action class `𝒜` is any finite set of subsets; `q̂` any real vector (more general than `[0,1]^p`, Fable remark 9: "The Lean version is strictly more general"). Status: sorry-free; Fable GREEN; Astra r1 GREEN ("Includes nonnegativity, the symmetric-difference bound, and the full ℓ₁ bound"); audited. Feeds: S-TARGET (K60) / L-DEC.

### TH436 — t11_miss_pi  [theorem]
- Source: `T11Miss.lean`; informal T11(iii) (pre-campaign PROVED-LOCKED, wave 1): `Docs/Theory/proofs/T11_LLED_scoring_ledger/STATEMENT.md`, Claim (iii); positions: [pos 714], [pos 796].

```lean
/-- **T11(iii), product-space form.** Under `Q` iid draws from `π₀`, the probability that the
fixed model `s` is never drawn is `(1 - π₀{s})^Q`. -/
theorem t11_miss_pi (π₀ : Measure M) [IsProbabilityMeasure π₀] (Q : ℕ) (s : M) :
    (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin Q => π₀) {x | ∀ i, x i ≠ s} = (1 - π₀ {s}) ^ Q := …
```


- Informal statement formalised (verbatim): "On Λ, almost surely, P(S* is not among the Q_f final iid draws | 𝓒) = (1 − π₀(S*))^{Q_f} ≤ exp(−Q_f π₀(S*))." with Setting item 5: "The **final iid draws** are these 4N_e initial draws and 4N_e(T + L + 4) independence proposals, in total Q_f := 4N_e(T + L + 5), a function of 𝓒." and the scope note "Nothing is asserted about the calibration's π₀ draws: their number is adaptive [...] so the identity is **not** claimed with the calibration draw count in place of Q_f." Original wording: "P(S* absent from the final iid draws | 𝓒) = (1 − π₀(S*))^{Q_f} ≤ e^{−Q_fπ₀(S*)}. The adaptive calibration draw count is never a fixed exponent."
- Assumptions (A-T11-1): given 𝓒, `Q = Q_f`, `S*` and `π₀` are fixed and the draws are iid with law `π₀` (EX-S, CAL, START); the Lean statements are the unconditional identity for fixed `Q`, `S*`, `π₀`, applied pointwise in 𝓒. Not formalised: the regular conditional probability given 𝓒 (CJ315), the sampler exactness (EX-A), stream separation, and the algorithm that produces the draws.
- Status history: sorry-free; Fable GREEN; Astra r1 GREEN, "scope-qualified": "T11's GREEN is scope-qualified. As expressly recorded in `A:23`, these are fixed-calibration iid identities. The conditional-law construction, launch event, and derivation of the final draw family from separated streams are not formalised." Audited.

### TH445 — theoremA3_hpm  [theorem]
- Source: `T37Greedy.lean`; added after Fable remark 1; informal LM144 (Lemma0(a,c))(c) "Ŝ = S₀ after the search, except for exact score ties".
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- **Lemma 0(c), HPM clause.** Under the hypotheses of `theoremA3`, suppose the production
centre `S_c` is the running best of the pre-search scored set `pre` (`F S ≤ F S_c` on `pre`). Then
`S₀ = path τ` is scored, and every model in the post-search scored set — `pre`, the centres
`path k` (`k ≤ τ`) and their scanned neighbourhoods — has score `≤ F(S₀)`. Hence the reported
HPM (a maximiser over that set) equals `S₀` up to exact score ties. -/
theorem theoremA3_hpm (hM : IsBestImprovement N F M) {Φ : α → ℕ} {R : Finset α} {S₀ : α}
    (hTD : TDP M Φ R S₀) (hS₀ : S₀ ∈ R) {Sc : α} (hSc : Sc ∈ R) (pre : Set α)
    (hpre : ∀ S ∈ pre, F S ≤ F Sc) :
    ∃ τ ≤ Φ Sc, path M Sc τ = S₀ ∧
      ∀ T, (T ∈ pre ∨ ∃ k ≤ τ, T = path M Sc k ∨ T ∈ N (path M Sc k)) → F T ≤ F S₀ := …
```


- Notes: Astra r2 minor remark: "`theoremA3_hpm` itself is a ledger score-bound theorem. The explicit reported-maximiser and tie conclusions occur in `lemma0c_hpm`. The package covers recovery, but that distinction should remain clear." Status: sorry-free; not in packet 1; Astra r2 GREEN ("Extends the score bound to previously scored models"); audited. Feeds: M5 (K65).

### TH447 — lemma0c_hpm  [theorem]
- Source: `T37Greedy.lean`; added after Astra r1 objection 2; informal LM144 (Lemma0(a,c))(c) and TH199 (Theorem A)(A3) "after it Ŝ = S₀ up to exact ties (Lemma 0(c))".
- Statement (verbatim, Lean; reported-HPM clause with the pre-search ledger `pre`, the post-search scored set `L` and an injective tie rank):

```lean
/-- **Lemma 0(c), reported-HPM clause** (general form). In addition to the hypotheses of
`lemma0c`, let `pre` be the pre-search scored set with `S_c` its running best (`F ≤ F(S_c)` on
`pre`; in production `S_c` is the HPM of `pre`). Let `L` be the post-search scored set:
`S₀ ∈ L`, and every element of `L` is in `pre`, is a centre `path k` (`k ≤ τ`), or is a neighbour
scanned at one. Then every maximiser `Ŝ` of `F` over `L` has `F Ŝ = F S₀` ("`Ŝ = S₀` up to
exact ties"), and `Ŝ = S₀` if no other model of `L` ties with `S₀`. With an injective tie rank
`rk`, if `Ŝ` is the `rk`-least maximiser and `S₀` precedes every model of `L` tying with it, then
`Ŝ = S₀`. -/
theorem lemma0c_hpm (hM : IsBestImprovement N F M) {Sc S₀ : α} {τ : ℕ}
    (hτ : path M Sc τ = S₀) (hL : M S₀ = none) (pre : Set α) (hpre : ∀ S ∈ pre, F S ≤ F Sc)
    (L : Finset α) (hS₀L : S₀ ∈ L)
    (hLsub : ∀ T ∈ L, T ∈ pre ∨ ∃ k ≤ τ, T = path M Sc k ∨ T ∈ N (path M Sc k))
    {Ŝ : α} (hŜL : Ŝ ∈ L) (hŜmax : ∀ T ∈ L, F T ≤ F Ŝ) :
    F Ŝ = F S₀ ∧ ((∀ T ∈ L, T ≠ S₀ → F T ≠ F S₀) → Ŝ = S₀) ∧
      (∀ rk : α → ℕ, Function.Injective rk →
        (∀ T ∈ L, (∀ U ∈ L, F U ≤ F T) → rk Ŝ ≤ rk T) →
        (∀ T ∈ L, F T = F S₀ → rk S₀ ≤ rk T) → Ŝ = S₀) := …
```


- Notes: Astra r2: "`lemma0c_hpm` explicitly connects the pre-search score bound, certified arrival, post-search ledger, and reported maximiser. It concludes equal score with `S₀`, equality of models without ties, and equality under an injective rank when the reporting rule and `S₀`'s tie preference agree. [...] No posterior-majority hypothesis appears." The absence of `Sc ∈ pre` and of an exact-union equation weakens the premises without excluding the production case. Status: sorry-free; Astra r2 GREEN; audited. Feeds: M5 (K65), card L-TA.

### TH451 — theoremA2_lattice_count  [theorem]
- Source: `T37Lattice.lean`; added after Astra r1 objection 1; informal TH199 (Theorem A) (A2): "τ(S) = m(S) + e(S) − σ(S) ≤ Φ(S) moves, where σ(S) is the number of extra→truth swaps used (τ(S) ≥ max{m(S), e(S)})".
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- **Theorem A (A2), move count.** Under the hypotheses of `theoremA2_lattice`, the number `τ` of
moves from `S ∈ R_{a,d}` to `S₀` satisfies `max(m(S), e(S)) ≤ τ ≤ Φ(S)`. Each move lowers `Φ`
by 1 or 2, and `τ + σ = m(S) + e(S)`, where `σ` is the number of moves that lower `Φ` by 2
(by the move-class table these are the extra→truth swaps). That is, `τ = m + e − σ`. -/
theorem theoremA2_lattice_count {K : ℕ} {F : Finset (Fin p) → ℝ}
    {M : Finset (Fin p) → Option (Finset (Fin p))}
    (hM : Greedy.IsBestImprovement (nbhd K) F M) {a d : ℕ} (hTD : TDP' S₀ M a d)
    {S : Finset (Fin p)} (hS : S ∈ Rad S₀ a d) :
    ∃ τ ≤ Φ S₀ S, Greedy.path M S τ = S₀ ∧ max (mis S₀ S) (ext S₀ S) ≤ τ ∧
      (∀ k < τ, Φ S₀ (Greedy.path M S (k + 1)) + 1 ≤ Φ S₀ (Greedy.path M S k) ∧
        Φ S₀ (Greedy.path M S k) ≤ Φ S₀ (Greedy.path M S (k + 1)) + 2) ∧
      τ + ((Finset.range τ).filter fun k =>
          Φ S₀ (Greedy.path M S k) = Φ S₀ (Greedy.path M S (k + 1)) + 2).card =
        mis S₀ S + ext S₀ S := …
```


- Notes: Astra r1 proposed fix: conclude "preferably without natural-number subtraction, τ + σ = mis(S) + ext(S), max(mis(S), ext(S)) ≤ τ"; the Lean statement follows that form (σ is the cardinality of the filter of steps dropping Φ by 2). Astra r2: "Its inequalities restrict every pre-τ potential drop to exactly 1 or 2, and its filter counts precisely the two-unit drops over steps 0,…,τ−1. `drop_two_swap` and `swap_extra_truth_drop_two` identify these drops, in both directions, with extra→truth swaps." Status: sorry-free; Astra r2 GREEN ("Exact swap-adjusted identity, lower/upper bounds, and drop sizes"); audited. Depends on LM244, LM245, LM252. Feeds: M5 (K65).

### TH456 — unbiased_of_step  [theorem]
- Source: `T12Core.lean`; informal T12(i.a): `Docs/Theory/proofs/T12_T8_frozen_run_identities/STATEMENT.md` §3 (i.a) (registry TH297 (Prop2(a,b,d,e)); T12 pre-campaign PROVED-LOCKED); positions: [pos 714], [pos 717] (HQ: "Formalising T12 (unbiased evidence) in Lean needs the Feynman–Kac structure in Mathlib; L-LEAN will write the plan but not attempt it today"), [pos 796].
- Statement (verbatim, Lean):

```lean
/-- **T12(i.a), reduction**: if the functionals `E t f` (standing for `E_c[Ẑ_t q̂_t(f)]`) are
given at stage 0 by `E 0 f = Σ γ₀ f` (stage 0: `Ẑ₀ = Z₀ = Σ γ₀` and the particles are iid
`π₀ = γ₀/Z₀`, so `E[Ẑ₀ q̂₀(f)] = Z₀ π₀(f) = Σ γ₀ f`; here `γ₀` includes the factor `m(∅)`) and satisfy the resample–move recursion
`E t f = E (t-1) (G_t · K_t f)`, with `γ_t = γ_{t-1} G_t` and `K_t` `γ_t`-invariant, then
`E t f = Σ_x γ_t(x) f(x)` (`= Z_t q_t(f)`) for every `t`. -/
theorem unbiased_of_step (γ : ℕ → α → ℝ) (G : ℕ → α → ℝ) (K : ℕ → α → α → ℝ)
    (hγ : ∀ t x, γ (t + 1) x = γ t x * G (t + 1) x) (hK : ∀ t, Invariant (γ (t + 1)) (K (t + 1)))
    (E : ℕ → (α → ℝ) → ℝ) (h0 : ∀ f, E 0 f = ∑ x, γ 0 x * f x)
    (hstep : ∀ t f, E (t + 1) f = E t (fun x => G (t + 1) x * kapply (K (t + 1)) f x)) :
    ∀ t f, E t f = ∑ x, γ t x * f x := …
```


- Informal statement (verbatim): "(i.a) For every c, t ∈ {0, …, T} and f : Ω → ℝ: E_c[Ẑ_t q̂_t(f)] = Z_t q_t(f). In particular E_c[Ẑ] = Z." Abstract setting of `T12_PLAN.md`: "State space: a finite type α (the feasible models Ω). Unnormalised targets: γ_0 > 0 with γ_t = γ_{t−1}·G_t (G_t = e^{Δ_t d}). Z_t q_t(f) = Σ_x γ_t(x) f(x). Round kernels: K_t is a row-stochastic kernel that leaves γ_t invariant [...]. Island I(c) with N particles: stage 0: N iid draws from π_0 = γ_0/Z_0, with Ẑ_0 = Z_0; stage t: Ẑ_t = Ẑ_{t−1}·(1/N)Σ_k G_t(X^k_{t−1}); multinomial ancestors; one K_t round per particle. Claim: E[Ẑ_t · (1/N) Σ_i f(X^i_t)] = Σ_x γ_t(x) f(x)."
- What is formalised: the induction only. The functionals `E t f` stand for `E_c[Ẑ_t q̂_t(f)]`; they enter as arbitrary reals with two explicit hypotheses: `h0` (stage-0 identity, with `γ₀` including the factor `m(∅)`) and `hstep` (the resample–move recursion `E (t+1) f = E t (G_{t+1} · K_{t+1} f)`). Docstring: "The recursion is the conditional-expectation form of (2); it enters `unbiased_of_step` as an explicit hypothesis, never as an axiom." REPORT: "`unbiased_of_step` is a reduction, not a full unbiasedness theorem." `unbiased_of_step` holds for all `t ∈ ℕ`, stronger than needed (Fable remark 11).
- NOT formalised: the probabilistic island model (multinomial resampling, conditionally independent rounds, tower property), `PMF` of populations; Mathlib has no `PMF.pi`; the invariance of the actual round kernel; see CJ312, CJ313.
- Status history: sorry-free but PARTIAL; Fable GREEN (remark 11: state the stage-0 convention in the docstring — adopted); Astra r1 GREEN ("T12 labels its remaining work honestly [...] `unbiased_of_step` is appropriately presented as a reduction, not a completed SMC unbiasedness theorem"); audited. Informal TH297 (Prop2(a,b,d,e)): PROVED (SF: VERIFIED (W5-LOCKBOOK); XF: GAP (A-REV4)).
- Depends on: LM248 (`invariance_step`), LM249 (`resample_move_step`).
- Feeds: M1 Theorem V/H (K35 "Ẑ_r unbiased"; registry card L-T12).

### LM231 — t21_event_subset  [lemma]
- Source: `T21HPM.lean`; informal PROOF_v3 display "{U^c, Ŝ≠S₀} ⊆ {δ₁≥1/2} ∪ {U^c, S₀∉𝒮}".
- Statement (verbatim, Lean; `omit [MeasurableSpace Ω] in` precedes it):

```lean
/-- The event inclusion behind C1:
```

### CJ312 — T12(i.a): derive the recursion `hstep` and the stage-0 identity `h0` from a probabilistic island model  [open problem]
- Source: `L-LEAN/T12_PLAN.md`, `REPORT.md` §3, docstring of `T12Core.lean`; positions: [pos 717] (parked idea), [pos 796], [pos 953] ("Extend the Lean proofs (T12) | Bounded").
- Statement (verbatim, T12_PLAN.md): "The recursion `hstep` is an explicit hypothesis of (3). It is the only probabilistic content of (i.a)." Plan: "1. Model the island as a `PMF` on populations. The state at stage `t` is `(x : Fin N → α, Ẑ : ℝ)`; the type is countable once `Ẑ` is restricted to a finite set of reachable values, or the evidence can be carried as a function of the history. Simplest route: carry the full history `Fin (t+1) → (Fin N → α)` and define `Ẑ_t` as a deterministic function of it, so that only `PMF (history)` is needed. 2. One step: given population `x`, the next population has law `PMF.pi`-style iid draws `i ↦ (ancestor ~ Categorical(G(x_k)/ΣG)) >>= K(x_ancestor, ·)`. Mathlib has no `PMF.pi`, so either build it as `Measure.pi` on a finite type or define the joint law by `Finset.univ.prod`. 3. Linearity of expectation over `PMF` (finite sums), plus the marginal of each coordinate of the product law, gives `E[(1/N)Σ_i f(Y_i) | x] = Σ_k (G_k/ΣG) (K f)(x_k)`. Then `resample_move_step` gives `hstep`. 4. Stage 0, iid `π_0`: `E[(1/N)Σ_i f(X_i)] = π_0(f)` and `Ẑ_0 = Z_0`, so `E_0 f = Σ γ_0 f`. With the stage-0 flag set, apply `invariance_step` with `G ≡ 1` once more." "Estimated effort: one focused session. The main cost is the product-law plumbing in step 2" (REPORT §3: "estimated at 300–600 lines").
- Status: OPEN (not started beyond the plan). THEOREM_LIST_FINAL (M1 Lean core): "T12Core `unbiased_of_step` with `hstep` discharged for multinomial resampling + an invariant kernel; detailed balance of the four kernels (finite matrices)".
- Feeds: M1 Theorem V/H (K35, K36), cited-lemma card L-T12.

### Dead ends and corrections (Theme 13)
- Statement-first process: all statements frozen in `frozen/v1/` before the proofs; the frozen copies of `T07Bayes.lean` (12 `sorry`) and `T37Lattice.lean` (8 `sorry`), and the identical `fidelity/packet/lean/` copies, are statement packets, not unfinished work; the registrar flagged them for readers who count `sorry` (REGISTRY_PAPER1 lines 31 and 844; registrar §3.3).
- 87 versus 101 declarations (RF283): stale W8-SYNTH snapshot at head `d9c2f2c`. **UNCERTAIN** attribution of the 14 added theorems (package section).
- "Astra did not finish" (RF284) versus Astra round 2 GREEN; first Astra codex call killed because codex waited on stdin (FAILED_ATTEMPTS item 2); `ASTRA_raw.md` empty in the intermediate state and non-empty in the final snapshot (**UNCERTAIN** how it was filled).
- Astra round 1 RED on T37 coverage (RF285, RF288, RF289, CE221): resolved by adding theorems only, never by changing a frozen statement; Astra r2's GREEN is expressly "faithful within the theorem's stated component scope and the combined coverage supplied by this packet", not "each core theorem independently contains all of A2 or A3".
- Fable remarks: 12 minor; adopted 1, 2, 3, 4 (doc), 5 (doc), 7, 11; rejected 6; no action 8, 9, 10, 12 (ADVISER_DECISIONS). Fable's remarks 1, 4 and 5 touched the T37 coverage points (A3 reported-HPM clause, the τ = m + e − σ count, the D_S variant) but graded them minor and returned GREEN; Astra graded the same points RED in round 1. The two checkers therefore disagreed on T37 round 1 (Fable GREEN, Astra RED), and the substantive coverage gap was classified as such only cross-family.
- Docstring overclaim in `exists_bestImprovement` (RF287).
- Tooling dead ends: `import Mathlib` (more than 30 min, 3.5 GB free RAM), `codex exec` without `< /dev/null`, several Lean blocks in one Git Bash heredoc (FAILED_ATTEMPTS 1-3). Deprecations noted in MATHLIB_NOTES (`push_neg` → `push Not at h`, `Set.mem_setOf_eq` → `Set.mem_ofPred_eq`, `Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic` → `Mathlib.Basic.Real.Basic`, `Finset.sum_div` needs `Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Field`).
- Mathematical limits of what Lean covers: `theoremA2`/`theoremA3` need TD′ hypotheses (the theorem's own assumptions); W3-VT37R R3 shows TD′_P is sufficient, not necessary, for "reach S₀ within Φ moves", and the Lean files respect this (they assume TD′_P as the premise, never claim necessity except via A1's converse and PD).
- HQ summaries versus Lean scope: [pos 1361] row 13 "Lean has no gaps (sorry-free)" and row 14 "composition in Lean, sorry-free" must be read with the scope limits in CJ314-CJ318 and CJ326 (the Lean T21 is the abstract inequality; A4 remainder, A5, B, C and the T38 composition with GUARD/SR conventions are not in Lean). The registrar's index (pos 1492) states the counts correctly.
- T12(i.a) is the only target the Lean track did not finish; HQ knew from the start ([pos 717]: "L-LEAN will write the plan but not attempt it today") and the final reports say PARTIAL ([pos 796] lists only T07, T21, T11(iii), Theorem A as machine-checked).
- Statuses: Lean/fidelity results never change an informal status word. In particular TH278 (Thm4-C1) keeps "FLAG SAME-FAMILY-ONLY" for its informal proof, TH297 (Prop2(a,b,d,e)) keeps XF GAP (A-REV4), and T11(iii) has no registry row.
